title: Greenhouse Gas Monitoring system, IoT enabled Improved Cookstove Technology locally design & Pilot testing, & Environmental Restoration and Climate Ch
body:
**Terms of Reference (ToR): Greenhouse Gas Monitoring system, IoT enabled Improved Cookstove Technology locally design & Pilot testing, & Environmental Restoration and Climate Change impact Awareness action**

**Study location: Puntland**

**Duration: 15 December - 15 January 2027**

**1. Background**

Islamic relief Somalia is an International Humanitarian Organization that has been working in Somalia since 2006, providing urgently needed humanitarian assistance to communities affected by conflict, natural disasters, and climate shocks in the country. Various of IRS’s humanitarian emergency and development projects are carried out in the South-Central, Somaliland and Puntland regions. The humanitarian operations are needs based, delivered according to core humanitarian standards, and well-coordinated with the Somalia cluster structures, and are aligned with the Somalia Humanitarian Response Plans. IRS is implementing projects across South-Central Somalia and Puntland to address the growing impacts of climate change on vulnerable communities.

IRS implements climate change related activities under WWIP II and BREAC II projects through integrating practical climate mitigation and environmental monitoring measures into community programming.

Under WWIP II, the project aims to establish a community-based GHG and environmental monitoring system through field-based biomass sampling and community level set up. This process is aimed at promoting practical climate mitigation and environmental restoration through local development and pilot testing of 300 pcs of Internet of Things (IOT) enabled improved cook stoves technologies; establishment of a community tree nursery and planting centers; distribution of and monitoring of 600 drought-resistant tree seedlings (various species), alongside climate and environmental awareness activities. In addition, a total of 5 environmental management committees with 20 members each from the community and local authorities will be trained on climate change, basic GHG monitoring, environmental protection and sustainable natural-resource management.

**2. Purpose of the Assignment**

- The purpose of this assignment is to engage a qualified consulting firm/individual to design, procure, establish a community-based GHG and environmental monitoring systems, while strengthening community awareness and practical climate-change mitigation actions. The consultant is expected to generate credible baseline and follow-up evidence on GHG emissions, environmental conditions, household energy use, improved cookstove performance and climate-mitigation outcomes. The firm will scientifically analyze the findings, estimate potential GHG emission reductions and carbon benefits, and submit a comprehensive technical report with datasets, key findings, lessons learned and evidence-based recommendations for future climate and environmental programming.

**3. General Objective**

- To establish and operationalize community-based GHG and environmental monitoring systems, assess the environmental and climate benefits of improved cookstove and ecosystem restoration activities, and strengthen community capacity and awareness on climate-change mitigation and sustainable natural-resource management.

**4. Specific Objectives:**

- Establish baseline household cooking practices, including stove type currently in use, fuel consumption, costs and climate awareness plans and policy.
- Assess traditional and improved cookstove performance through baseline and follow-up fuel-use, emissions and air-quality monitoring.
- Assess household adoption and use of improved cookstoves, including correct use, maintenance, acceptance and Behavioral changes.
- Estimate GHG emission reductions resulting from reduced biomass-fuel consumption from the 300 IoT improved cookstoves.
- Train 20 community and local-authority representatives on climate change, GHG monitoring and environmental management.
- Conduct climate-awareness and clean-cooking demonstrations for participating households and communities under both projects.
- Conduct baseline and follow-up monitoring and analysis to measure changes in household energy use, emissions and environmental indicators.
- Develop monitoring tools, datasets and GHG calculations and prepare a comprehensive technical report with findings and recommendations for IRS.
- Identify, train and set up champions within IR for future GHG monitoring/tracking
- Train government, partners, community on development of locally resourced Improved cook stove
- Develop dashboard that track various gases generated rom ICS through internet of things simulating emission projection/prediction.

5\*\*. Proposed Research Design\*\*

- The consultant shall propose and justify the most appropriate research design.

5.1. **Scope of Research**

- Inceptio**n and Methodology Development:** Review project documents and develop the methodology, sampling approach, monitoring tools, indicators, GHG calculation methods and implementation workplan.
- **Procurement and Operationalization of Monitoring Equipment:** Procure, supply, install, calibrate, test and commission all required GHG and environmental monitoring equipment and hand it over to IRS upon completion.
- **Baseline Assessment:** Establish baseline data on household cooking, fuel consumption, emissions and climate awareness, as well as vegetation, biomass, trees and livestock-related emissions
- **IoT enabled Improved Cookstove development: Support and train community members in the development of IoT-ICS, sow case real time emission tracking and documents on the** performance, fuel efficiency, utilization and household adoption of **the improved cookstoves**.
- **GHG and Environmental Assessment:** Conduct biomass, vegetation and tree measurements, GPS-referenced monitoring, carbon-stock assessment and livestock-related GHG emission estimation.
- **Environmental Restoration:** Support establishment of the community nursery and planting and monitoring of **600 drought-resistant tree seedlings**, including survival and growth.
- **Follow-up and Endline Monitoring:** Conduct follow-up assessments to measure changes in fuel use, stove performance, emissions, household practices and environmental indicators.
- **Data Analysis and Reporting:** Analyze findings and submit comprehensive technical reports, datasets, GHG calculations, monitoring tools, equipment records and recommendations.
- Develop Realtime dashboard system linked to ICS usage with real world data from the households on ICS usage, energy efficiency, greenhouse gas emission and its contribution to climate change

**5.2. Equipment requirements**

- The consultant/firm should be able to provide the basic equipment required for this assignment.

**6. Firm Roles and Responsibilities**

The selected consulting firm will be responsible for the following:

- **Methodology and Workplan:** Develop and submit a detailed methodology, sampling approach, monitoring protocols, data-collection tools, indicators and implementation workplan for IRS approval.
- Provide technical support for the community nursery and planting and monitoring of **600 drought-resistant tree seedlings**, including survival and growth monitoring.
- Train **5 committee on greenhouse gas monitoring** and conduct community awareness and practical demonstrations on climate change, GHG monitoring, clean cooking and environmental protection.
- Conduct follow-up/endline monitoring to assess changes in fuel consumption, cookstove performance, selected emissions, household practices and environmental indicators.
- Analyze collected data and estimate GHG emission reductions, carbon benefits and livestock-related emissions using appropriate and documented methodologies.
- Submit inception, baseline, progress and final technical reports, together with cleaned datasets, GHG calculations and monitoring tool
- Develop an interactive dashboard that captures and reports on Business-as-Usual fuel consumption and future scenario on the use of improved cooking technologies, plus corresponding greenhouse gas.
- Provide mobile/portable GHG monitoring equipment/gas analyzer that can be used in future monitoring of gas emission/reduction by the community members
- Provide training to IR and government team on the use, tracking and reporting on emission pathways.

**7. IRS Roles and Responsibilities**

Islamic Relief Somalia (IRS) will be responsible for the following:

- **Overall Coordination:** Provide overall supervision and coordination of the consultancy through the relevant Programme, Project and MEAL teams.
- **Technical Review and Approval:** Review and approve the consultant’s inception report, methodology, sampling approach, monitoring protocols, workplan and data-collection tools before implementation.
- **Equipment Approval:** Review and approve the proposed specifications, brands/models and quantities of GHG and environmental monitoring equipment before procurement by the consulting firm.
- **Community and Stakeholder Coordination:** Facilitate engagement with targeted communities, local authorities, environmental committees and other relevant stakeholders
- **Field Facilitation:** Support necessary project-level coordination and access arrangements to enable the firm to undertake field assessments, training, awareness and monitoring activities.
- **Monitoring and Quality Oversight:** Monitor implementation progress and verify that activities, equipment and deliverables comply with the approved ToR, methodology and contractual requirements.
- **Review of Deliverables:** Review and provide timely feedback on inception, baseline, progress and final reports, datasets, GHG calculations and other consultancy deliverables.
- **Equipment Verification and Handover:** Participate in inspection, verification and formal acceptance of procured monitoring equipment and ensure its handover to the appropriate IRS office/project team.
- **Contract and Payment Management:** Process payments to the consulting firm in accordance with the agreed contract, approved deliverables and payment schedule.
- Facilitate local travel within project sites

**8. Required Consultant Qualifications**

The consultant/firm should have:

- Academic qualifications: Advanced degree in one or more of: Environmental Science, social sciences, environmental engineering, or climate change related.
- Professional experience: At least 10 years of relevant experience in climate-change research; Household energy/clean cooking; Environmental research; Energy efficiency; and/or Applied field research.
- The consultant should demonstrate experience with: Combustion/emissions analyzers; Household emissions measurement; Improved cooking technologies; IoT, Quantitative research; Statistical analysis; and Research report preparation.
- Experience with Testo, Bacharach or equivalent emissions-monitoring equipment would be an advantage.

9\. **Duration**

- The study will run for TWO months (Nov–Dec 2026). This timeframe ensures baseline assessment, intervention, and endline monitoring are completed within the calendar period.

10\. Available Budget

- provide itemized cost based on your understanding of the TOR.

11\. **Financial resources**

Islamic Relief request the potential and interested consultant/firm to submit a detailed technical and financial proposal. Islamic Relief will facilitate internal logistical movements and security during the course of the assignment. The consultant should submit itemized quotation in the financial application.

**Requirements:**

For consideration, kindly submit the following documents.

1. Updated CV and cover letter explaining your strength and expertise.
2. Detailed and clear interpretation and analysis of the ToR (how the firm/consultant will undergo in executing the task)
3. Detailed implementation plan
4. Detailed budget and breakdown of what cost covers (IR will cover in-country logistical arrangements, organize for all field level facilitation required)
5. Professional Registration certificates.

title: Spécialiste en fragilité et résilience, et analyse des conflits
body:
**Contexte**

SDI Inc., organisme spécialisé dans les études socio-économiques en Afrique, recherche avec ses partenaires un(e) Spécialiste en fragilité et résilience, et analyse des conflits pour des études de faisabilité socio-économique dans le Bassin du lac Tchad. Ces études portent sur la vulnérabilité des femmes et des hommes, les systèmes de production agrosylvopastoraux et halieutiques et la place du secteur privé. Le recrutement est soumis à l’attribution du contrat.

**Rôle et tâches**

Le ou la Spécialiste en fragilité, résilience et analyse des conflits conduit l’étude des dynamiques de conflits.

- Analyser les causes profondes des conflits et de l’insécurité, y compris les conflits fonciers et intercommunautaires
- Étudier les liens entre insécurité, déplacements forcés et systèmes de production
- Identifier les mécanismes de médiation et de prévention
- Formuler les recommandations de paix et de cohésion sociale

**Durée et lieu**

La mission s’étend sur environ six (6) mois. Le travail s’effectue en partie à distance et en partie dans les pays du Bassin du lac Tchad : Cameroun, Niger, Nigeria, République centrafricaine et Tchad.

**Qualifications exigées**

- Diplôme Bac+5 minimum en études sur la paix et les conflits, sciences politiques, relations internationales, études du développement, sociologie, politiques publiques, études sur la sécurité, droit ou discipline connexe
- Au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans l’évaluation des dynamiques de conflit, des facteurs de fragilité, des capacités de résilience et des défis de gouvernance dans des environnements complexes
- Au moins deux (2) expériences en programmation sensible aux conflits, analyse de l’économie politique, consolidation de la paix, cohésion sociale et gestion des risques
- Deux (2) expériences en facilitation multipartite et élaboration de stratégies de résilience et de paix durable, avec des partenaires techniques et financiers
- Expérience d’identification d’opportunités de résilience, de cohésion sociale et de développement durable en milieu complexe et multiculturel
- Expérience dans le Bassin du lac Tchad ou en contexte sahélien
- Maîtrise du français, à l’écrit et à l’oral

**Atouts**

- Plusieurs missions dans le Bassin du lac Tchad
- Connaissance des approches d’évaluation de la fragilité des bailleurs internationaux
- Pratique de l’anglais

**Conditions**

Contrat de consultant. Les honoraires sont négociés selon le profil et l’expérience.

title: Expert en financement des risques climatiques / assurance catastrophe
body:
**Contexte**

SDI INC est un organisme établi à Québec (Canada). Il est chef de file d'un groupement présélectionné pour une étude sur le système d'alerte et la gestion des risques d'inondation dans huit villes du Bénin, financée par la Banque africaine de développement. Pour constituer son équipe, SDI INC recherche un(e) consultant(e) pour le poste ci-dessus. L'engagement ne deviendra effectif que si le contrat est attribué au groupement.

**Rôle et principales tâches**

- Analyser les mécanismes existants de financement des risques d'inondation au Bénin.
- Modéliser les pertes et proposer des instruments de transfert du risque adaptés (assurance paramétrique, fonds de catastrophe, financement anticipé).
- Chiffrer les options et formuler des recommandations de mise en œuvre.
- Contribuer au plan d'action et au rapport global.

**Durée et lieu**

La mission s'étend sur environ six (6) mois. Le travail s'effectue en partie à distance et en partie au Bénin (Cotonou et villes de l'étude). Le démarrage est prévu en 2027, à une date qui sera confirmée après l'attribution du contrat.

**Qualifications exigées**

- Diplôme universitaire (Bac + 5 au moins) en économie, en finance, en assurance, en gestion des risques ou dans une discipline connexe.
- Au moins sept (7) ans d'expérience professionnelle dans le financement des risques climatiques ou l'assurance catastrophe.
- Participation à au moins deux (2) missions liées à la modélisation du risque ou au développement d'instruments de transfert du risque (assurance catastrophe, assurance paramétrique, fonds de catastrophe, etc.).
- Bonne connaissance des mécanismes internationaux de financement du risque climatique, notamment l'assurance paramétrique et le financement anticipé.

**Atouts**

- Expérience en Afrique subsaharienne.
- Connaissance de mécanismes tels que l'African Risk Capacity (ARC).

**Conditions**

Contrat de consultant, rémunéré par jour de travail effectué. Les honoraires journaliers sont à négocier et couvrent les frais de séjour ; les billets d'avion internationaux nécessaires à la mission sont pris en charge par le groupement. Le candidat retenu s'engage à être disponible pour la durée de la mission.

**Dossier de candidature**

- Un curriculum vitæ détaillé et à jour, qui précise pour chaque mission le client, le bailleur de fonds, le pays, la période et le poste occupé.
- Les copies des diplômes.
- Les attestations de travail ou de bonne fin d'exécution qui justifient les missions citées.
- La disponibilité et les honoraires journaliers souhaités.

- Les copies des diplômes.
- Les attestations de travail ou de bonne fin d'exécution qui justifient les missions citées.
- La disponibilité et les honoraires journaliers souhaités.

title: Consortium Manager - Sudan
body:
**This position is based in Kosti, White Nile, Sudan. The position/program is funded by the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) from 1 December 2026 to 30 August 2027. Medical Teams is the prime grant holder for the HSF and will lead both International & local partners, including ACTED, HOPE, SAPA, Gonanyat, and others.**

**CONSORTIUM MANAGER - SUDAN**

The Consortium Manager - Sudan contributes to Medical Teams International’s calling by bringing together International and local partners to deliver humanitarian aid including health, nutrition, protection, WASH and MPCA for conflict-affected and displaced communities in White Nile, Sudan. This position leads the day-to-day coordination of the Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Consortium Steering Committee so all partners deliver a single, coherent program on time, on budget, and to donor and humanitarian standards. The Consortium Manager is the main link between partners, the donor, coordination bodies and authorities, and acts as a neutral convener for all members.

Medical Teams International is the lead agency and prime grant holder. The Consortium Manager heads the Consortium Management Unit (CMU) within Medical Teams, manages the prime award on behalf of the consortium, oversees sub-grants to partners and is accountable to Medical Teams and the donor for overall grant performance and compliance.

The role bearer will occasionally be required to support implementation and delivery of other SHF projects as required and guided.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Partner, donor, and stakeholder management**

- Serve as the principal consortium focal point for donors, maintaining clear, timely and solutions-focused communication and coordinating formal approvals, notifications and escalation of significant issues along with key functions at Country Office level
- In coordination with the Grants and Partnership team, oversee the development, amendment and management of partner agreements and sub-awards, and ensure partner due diligence, monitoring, reporting, spot checks, verifications and corrective action plans are completed to the required standard.
- Manage partner performance through clear expectations, regular review meetings, evidence-based feedback, agreed action plans, and proportionate escalation where performance or compliance remains below standard.
- Promote equitable partnership, mutual accountability, shared learning and capacity strengthening, including harmonization of tools and systems where this improves quality and efficiency.
- Represent Medical Teams and the consortium in relevant coordination, donor, government, research, advocacy and stakeholder forums at country, regional or international level, as delegated.
- Support the identification and development of funding opportunities and contribute consortium evidence, learning and analysis to program development, strategic positioning, and advocacy.
- Lead and support structured partner capacity strengthening initiatives, including mentorship, technical coaching, compliance support, and systems strengthening, to improve implementation quality, donor compliance, and long-term institutional capacity of consortium partners.

**Consortium leadership and governance**

- Facilitate the Consortium Steering Committee and technical working groups, including agendas, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
- Maintain and update the consortium's governance documents: memorandum of understanding, terms of reference, roles and responsibilities, and decision-making procedures.
- Build trust and a culture of equal partnership among members, and mediate disagreements fairly.
- Manage consortium-wide risks, challenges, and stakeholder relationships, resolving complex operational issues, driving corrective actions, and ensuring timely communication, compliance, and implementation of agreed decisions.
- Promote meaningful participation of national and local partners in decision-making, in line with localization commitments.
- Lead the Consortium Management Unit and supervise its staff, such as MEAL, grants, and finance roles.

**Program quality, deliver, and reporting**

- Hold overall accountability for delivery of consortium results, workplans, milestones, indicators and contractual commitments across Medical Teams and all consortium partners.
- Ensure integrated planning and coordination across program, technical, MEAL, finance, awards, operations, supply chain, human resources, security, safeguarding and other enabling functions.
- Lead project start up/close out; identify and lead modifications (realignments, NCEs) in coordination with relevant internal departments and partners.
- Ensure timely procurement planning and coordination with Supply Chain during project start-up and implementation
- Ensure timely, accurate and coherent donor reporting and that narrative, indicator and financial information is reconciled across partners before submission.
- Lead development of high-quality donor reports and consortium modification requests in coordination with relevant functions and partner teams. Ensure timely reporting to all relevant cluster 5W’s, results and support participation and communication of project results and challenges in cluster meetings/updates.
- Coordinate joint work plans, targeting and geographic coverage across partners to avoid gaps and duplication.
- Track progress against the logframe, budget and work plan, and lead quarterly review meetings with partners.
- Lead an integrated, multi-sector approach so that partners' activities reinforce each other.
- Support adaptive programming as access, security and needs change, including program modifications with the donor.

**Financial stewardship, compliance, and risk management**

- Provide overall stewardship of the consortium budget, including forecasting, expenditure monitoring, burn-rate analysis, cost allocation, partner spending, and timely action on financial variances.
- Oversee timely processing of partner sub-awards, partner funding requests and disbursement of approved funds to ensure uninterrupted implementation and compliance with consortium agreements
- Ensure implementation complies with donor requirements, Medical Teams policies, consortium and partner agreements, approved budgets.
- Collaborate with HQ Global Programs and Finance teams to ensure Medical Teams International minimum standards are followed and met across the consortium, including regular compliance check-ins with partners, timely resolution of gaps, and escalation of significant issues.
- Maintain an integrated consortium risk register and ensure programmatic, financial, compliance, safeguarding, security, operational and reputational risks are actively managed and escalated.
- Promote audit readiness by ensuring complete, reliable and accessible program and partner documentation and timely closure of audit, monitoring and compliance findings.
- Oversee sub grant agreements, partner capacity and due diligence assessments, budget monitoring, spending forecasts and audits on behalf of the prime award holder.

**MEAL, accountability and learning**

- Oversee a common MEAL framework, shared indicators and data quality across partners.
- Ensure community feedback and complaints mechanisms work across the consortium, and that feedback leads to action.
- Coordinate and facilitate donor, OCHA, AIT and third-party monitoring missions, ensuring partners are prepared, documentation is available, and agreed follow-up actions are implemented in a timely manner.
- Coordinate baseline, mid-term and endline evaluations, and capture lessons learned and good practice.
- Ensure accountability is integrated into country strategies, program design, monitoring and evaluations, recruitment, staff onboarding, training and performance management, partnership agreements, and highlighted in reporting.

**Representation and external coordination**

- Represent the consortium with SHF UN agencies, humanitarian clusters and sector working groups, and relevant Sudanese authorities, consortium line ministries, including the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC).
- Coordinate joint advocacy and communications and make sure partner contributions are visible and credited.
- Support partners with access negotiations and travel permissions where needed.
- Ensure SHF visibility and communication requirements are implemented consistently across Medical Teams and partners’ implementation sites in line with donor and Medical Teams’ branding guidelines.

**Other Duties**

- Ensure the safeguarding of program participants and employees through promoting an environment of awareness and upholding the code of conduct provisions of Medical Teams International Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse & Harassment, Child & Vulnerable Adult protection, and harassment-free workplace policies. Incumbents will remain alert and responsive to any child and adult safeguarding risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills which will enable you to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child and adult safeguarding policy and procedures, and conduct yourself in a manner consistent with the Safeguarding Code of Conduct and behavior expectations across all consortium members.
- Coordinate with partners' security focal points on context monitoring and safe program delivery.
- Follow Medical Team's security management plan and contribute to consortium-wide security information sharing.
- Utilize volunteers when appropriate.
- Additional duties as assigned.

**EDUCATION, LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, humanitarian action, public policy, management or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Valid passport

**Preferred:**

- Master's degree in international development, humanitarian action, public policy, management or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Professional certification in Project Management, Grants Management, Monitoring & Evaluation, or Humanitarian Coordination.

**EXPERIENCE**

**Required:**

- At least 6 years of experience managing humanitarian or development programs, including at least 4 years of coordinating consortia or multi-partner programs.
- Proven experience managing sub-awards, partner oversight, compliance monitoring, and capacity strengthening of national and local NGOs
- Proven experience managing or coordinating large institutional grants, with knowledge of SHF's rules and reporting requirements.
- Experience working in insecure, conflict-affected, or fragile settings.
- A proven track record leading consortia and advancing localization with national NGOs.
- Experience with multi-sector programming in Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection & Cash Programming.

**Preferred:**

- Experience living and communicating cross-culturally in a relief/development setting
- Working knowledge of Arabic, enough to work with partners, authorities, and communities.
- Previous experience in Sudan or the wider region.
- Lived experience of, or close community ties to, displacement-affected or conflict-affected areas, and an understanding of how this shapes program design and partnership
- Prior experience working in Sudan

title: Staff Attorney
body:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

***This position is open to candidates based in Montana who are currently authorized to work in the United States.***

***A cover letter is required for consideration. Applications submitted without one will not be reviewed.***

**IRC BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC is at work today in more than 40 countries and in 26 U.S. cities. The IRC’s Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) department creates opportunities for refugees and other vulnerable migrants to survive and thrive in the US. RAI serves nearly 50,000 individuals each year in the US through a diverse portfolio of programs aimed at achieving outcomes in five impact areas: Health, Safety, Economic Wellbeing, Education, and Power.

In 2016, IRC re-opened its doors in Missoula and has since supported nearly 1,000 individuals building a new life in Montana. Over nine years, the IRC in Montana has served refugees and immigrants from Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Iraq, Yemen, Burma, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Haiti, Venezuela, Central America, and Mexico.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

IRC seeks a Staff Attorney to join the Montana Legal team to represent refugees and other individuals with petitions before US Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS). The Staff Attorney will also conduct community-based Know Your Rights workshops. The position will be part of the IRC Immigration Legal Services Network led by IRC’s Immigration Technical Unit (TU) at IRC’s headquarters, which supports IRC’s 24 legal service programs across the US. The role will collaborate closely with the IRC team in Missoula, Montana, but the position may be based in another high-needs service area outside of Missoula. The position will require some travel within Montana.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

*Direct Legal Representation and Program Management*

- Conduct intakes and consultations with IRC clients and community members, and provide direct legal representation to individuals before USCIS, DOS, and possibly other governmental agencies.
- Coordinate closely within IRC’s multidisciplinary teams to identify needs and facilitate referrals to services offered in-house and through partnerships with external providers.
- Ensure client and program data is collected consistently, managed appropriately, and reported accurately in accordance with program reporting requirements set by IRC.
- Position may supervise legal assistants and/or interns.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge and expertise of changing immigration policies through independent research and analysis, regular trainings, and peer-to-peer consultation.
- Participate in community-based coalitions related to immigrant rights.
- Serve as a strong advocate for humanitarian immigrants.

*Community Partnerships and Workshops*

- Create and maintain a viable outreach strategy to cultivate and maintain strong relationships with community-based organizations, local immigration attorneys, and nonprofit legal providers.
- Collaborate with other IRC departments and partners to offer community-based workshops or information sessions when demand exceeds capacity to provide direct legal representation. This may include pro se workshops to complete requests under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) among others.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Law degree (JD or LLM) from an ABA-accredited U.S. institution and membership in good standing with any state bar;
- Ideally at least 1-3 years of experience providing direct representation in immigration court and/or before USCIS to asylum applicants and other immigrants seeking humanitarian relief; law school graduates with clinical legal experience may be considered;
- Excellent legal research, writing, analytical, and organizational skills;
- Ability to communicate clearly and effectively, both orally in a courtroom setting and in writing;
- Bilingual in one or more commonly spoken languages among IRC Montana’s client population preferred (eg, Spanish, Arabic, Swahili, Dari, Pashto);
- Deep commitment to immigrant rights and working with humanitarian immigrants;
- Trauma-informed and sensitive listening and communication skills; respect for diverse perspectives;
- Evidence of capacity to be a strong team member in a highly collaborative and fast-paced multidisciplinary environment;
- Must have ability to travel in and around the service area to engage with clients and community partners and attend USCIS interviews.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard office environment with occasional participation in community outreach and legal assistance events.
- Depending on location, remote work from within the state of Montana may be a possibility.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $65,000-$86,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Current Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**US Benefits effective Jan 1, 2027:** IRC offers a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-30 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $187 per month, dental starting at $7.70 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare, dependent care, and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Oficial WASH Shelter & Infrastructure - Maracaibo
body:
Oficial WASH Shelter & Infrastructure - Maracaibo

El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial WASH Shelter & Infrastructure** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de base, y acompañamiento técnico de especialista WASI (basada en Caracas) la/él Oficial WASH Shelter & Infrastructure (WASI) estará directamente involucrado y velará por la implementación diaria de las actividades de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene, especialmente en las áreas de intervención. También será responsable de la evaluación, planificación, la facilitación de las actividades de WASI mediante la participación directa de los organismos y autoridades asociados y la elaboración de materiales de información y comunicación asociadas a la higiene/saneamiento y sensibilización para personas con necesidades específicas (PDE), los desplazados internos y las comunidades de acogida las zonas seleccionadas, de conformidad con la cultura y las prácticas de la población.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Liderar las evaluaciones de necesidades relacionadas con el agua, el saneamiento y la higiene en las comunidades de acogida, instituciones y otros sitios de interés en Apure, con base en Guasdualito y en otras zonas aledañas, según las instrucciones del Gerente de Base y bajo la gestión técnica del especialista de WASI.
- Ayudar en la identificación y selección de las comunidades, beneficiarios o centros de intervención con la ayuda de las autoridades locales y en conjunto con los equipos de protección, RecEc y DP.
- Preparar el plan de trabajo y los materiales de información, educación y comunicación (IEC) para las actividades de promoción de higiene en consulta con el Gerente de Base y del Especialista WASI.
- Administrar de manera efectiva la ejecución física y financiera de los proyectos de WASH utilizando las herramientas adecuadas para garantizar que estos se entreguen a tiempo, dentro del presupuesto y cumpliendo con la calidad y otros requisitos técnicos esperados.
- Garantizar que las comunidades y grupos vulnerables y/o con riesgos de protección, incluidas las mujeres, participen en cada una de las etapas del ciclo de los proyectos de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Facilitar todas las capacitaciones/campañas sobre agua, saneamiento e higiene en terreno mediante el uso de un enfoque participativo y orientado al cambio de comportamiento.
- Planificar y coordinar la ejecución de las campañas de saneamiento, gestión de residuos en las comunidades, asegurando la participación y apoyo de autoridades y entes locales relacionados, socios locales, comunidades, otros equipos dentro de DRC y demás interesados, asegurando estrategias de sostenibilidad de las acciones.
- Planificar en conjunto con los socios locales de DRC la ejecución de las actividades de los programas de agua, saneamiento e higiene, garantizando el fortalecimiento de capacidades y la transferencia de capacidades a los socios, con las orientaciones del Gerente de Base y el Especialista WASI, siguiendo los lineamientos de cada proyecto.
- Documentar los resultados y las lecciones aprendidas de la implementación del programa de agua, saneamiento e higiene, considerando la retroalimentación de las comunidades y de otros equipos técnicos de DRC y partes interesadas.
- Servir de enlace con otros actores/ONG relevantes y representantes de las personas de interés y líderes comunitarios para los esfuerzos de colaboración, incluyendo la participación en las reuniones de coordinación local de grupos temáticos sobre agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Realizar las gestiones para la obtención de los permisos necesarios ante las autoridades y entes necesarios para la ejecución de obras, campañas y servicios de saneamiento en los lugares de intervención, en conjunto con el Gerente de Base y con el apoyo técnico del Especialista WASI.
- Participar en los espacios de coordinación dentro de DRC con los equipos de otros sectores programáticos como Recuperación Económica (seguridad alimentaria y los medios de vida), Protección y Preparación para Desastres, para garantizar la implementación integrada con una planificación adecuada de las actividades.
- Garantizar que todas las partes interesadas relevantes tengan información sobre los antecedentes, el programa, los objetivos, las áreas de trabajo, la duración de los programas y las actividades en el campo de la organización.
- Completar los formularios y la documentación adecuada del sector WASH para los proyectos de intervención, como: levantamiento de necesidades, propuestas de proyectos, cómputos métricos, cronogramas, planos, diseños esquemáticos, manejo de coordenadas GPS, mapeo de las actividades/áreas del proyecto, especificaciones y diseño del contenido de kits WASH, entre otras.
- Hacer las solicitudes de compras de bienes y contrataciones de servicios para las actividades de agua, saneamiento e higiene de manera oportuna, y asegurarse de que tienen los acuerdos y contratos con los proveedores para el inicio de las actividades.
- Hacer un seguimiento e inspección adecuados de las obras de agua y saneamiento en terreno, así como el seguimiento de la ejecución física y financiera y las gestiones para el pago a las empresas de servicios y obras.
- Garantizar la recopilación de datos de los beneficiarios, documentar historias de éxito y otra información que sea requerida para el reporte de las actividades e indicadores de cada proyecto, y suministrar aportes para los informes de progreso o finales que son enviados a los donantes u otras partes interesadas.
- Contribuir a la planificación de contingencias para la preparación y una posible respuesta de emergencia en materia de agua, saneamiento e higiene, si es necesario.
- Garantizar la correcta presentación de la organización y la ética profesional en el control de los movimientos y garantizar la seguridad de todos los documentos.
- Realizar un seguimiento y preparar semanalmente, mensualmente, trimestralmente, todos los planes de compras de bienes y servicios necesarios para el programa de agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- En ausencia del Gerente de base, apoyar el proyecto de WASH con la estrecha coordinación del Gerente de Programa y el Especialista WASI.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el equipo de agua, saneamiento e higiene.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- 2 años de experiencia en el campo de WASH y en la implementación de proyectos humanitarios.
- Sólida comprensión de la capacitación básica en programación de agua, saneamiento e higiene, métodos de promoción participativa, movilizaciones comunitarias y creación de redes.
- Buen manejo de normas, estándares y prácticas sobre obras de construcción y/o rehabilitación de sistemas básicos esenciales de agua, saneamiento e higiene en instituciones o comunidades, incluyendo sistemas de agua, sistemas de disposición de excretas, manejo de residuos, entre otros.
- Conocimiento sobre las prácticas adecuadas de gestión de residuos y saneamiento, métodos de tratamiento de agua a nivel domiciliario y otras prácticas de higiene para evitar riesgos de salud pública.
- Experiencia en la implementación de actividades de formación, promoción de higiene y formación de comités en temas relacionados con agua, saneamiento e higiene.
- Título en Ingeniería en Salud Pública/Ingeniería Civil/Ingeniería Mecánica/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente con experiencia en WASH.
- Conocimientos informáticos y gestión de datos estadísticos.
- Implementación efectiva y oportuna de todas las intervenciones descritas en el producto y cualquier otra actividad programática relacionada con el agua, el saneamiento y la higiene.
- Experiencia laboral y conocimiento del lugar de destino local.
- Capacidad de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.

*Deseable:*

- Maestría o especialización en Ingeniería de Salud Pública, Ingeniería Hidráulica, Ingeniería Ambiental, Ingeniería Civil, Ingeniería Mecánica, Arquitectura o campo directamente relacionado;
- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de protección;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de crear buen ambiente de equipo y trabajo con socios locales implementadores;
- Manejo del inglés;
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

- Título en Ingeniería en Salud Pública/Ingeniería Civil/Ingeniería Mecánica/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente con experiencia en WASH.

**Idiomas:**

- Fluidez en inglés ( Deseable )escrito y hablado

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

title: Program Manager - International Hire
body:
**Project HOPE** is an international humanitarian and global health organization working alongside communities and health workers to strengthen health systems, respond to emergencies, and expand access to quality, lifesaving services.

**Code of Conduct**

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and disclose potential or actual violations of our Code of Conduct, including Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination, or Harassment. Together we reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Program Manager provides senior programmatic leadership and hands-on oversight of Project HOPE’s integrated humanitarian health, nutrition, WASH, and protection programming in Gaza. Working under the Gaza Mission Lead, the position translates program strategies, approved proposals, work plans, and budgets into coordinated, safe, high-quality, and accountable service delivery across field locations.

The position leads multidisciplinary program teams, drives program strengthens performance-management systems, and coordinates with technical advisers and support departments to address implementation gaps. The Program Manager is expected to combine strategic program leadership with practical field implementation experience and to strengthen national teams rather than create parallel management structures.

**PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Strategic Leadership & Program Management**

• Lead program planning and delivery across Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection, rehabilitation, and community-based services, ensuring coherence with mission priorities and the humanitarian context.

• Translate approved program objectives into integrated operational work plans with clear deliverables, milestones, owners, resource requirements, dependencies, and follow-up mechanisms.

• Lead regular program review meetings and oversee departmental action trackers, implementation schedules, risk logs, corrective actions, and adaptive management decisions.

• Provide technical and programmatic direction to designated sector managers and program teams; support evidence-informed program design and improvements to current and future interventions.

• Ensure coordination and appropriate complementarity across multiple awards and operational platforms, Coordinate program implementation across Project HOPE's different funded projects to ensure complementary service delivery, clearly defined project responsibilities, and identification of service gaps or duplication

**Integrated Program Delivery & Technical Quality**

• Oversee integrated service delivery across six fixed primary healthcare clinics (PHCCs) in Gaza City, the Middle Area, and Khan Younis, linking facility-based care with community outreach and referral services.

• Coordinate with Health and Nutrition teams to support quality primary care, child and maternal health, SRH, communicable and noncommunicable disease management, nutrition screening and management, and IYCF-E/Mother-Baby Area services.

• Support planning and performance oversight of two community-based rehabilitation outreach teams, including referral coordination, follow-up, functional rehabilitation, and linkage with specialized services.

• Ensure WASH activities respond to identified community and PHCC needs, including safe water delivery, water-quality monitoring, sanitation, hygiene promotion, IPC, waste management, and appropriate infrastructure improvements.

• Ensure Protection and MHPSS interventions are safely integrated, including child protection, violence prevention and response, psychosocial support, safe spaces, and confidential and survivor-centered referral pathways.

• Coordinate the deployment and performance monitoring of cross-sector community health promoters, including community engagement, screening, health and hygiene messaging, referral tracking, and beneficiary feedback.

• Work with technical leads to ensure interventions meet applicable clinical protocols, humanitarian quality standards, protection principles, and relevant sector coordination guidance.

**Program Start-Up, Scale-Up & Operational Readiness**

• Lead integrated readiness planning for new and expanded sites, ensuring that staffing, premises, accessibility, commodities, equipment, referral arrangements, WASH/IPC measures, registration tools, and safeguarding provisions are in place.

• Coordinate with Human Resources, Finance, Supply Chain, Administration, Security, Compliance, and MEAL to resolve constraints that threaten safe and timely service activation.

• Oversee site-readiness checklists and monitor facility set-up, outreach schedules, training plans, stock availability, and implementation prerequisites; escalate unresolved critical issues to the Mission Lead.

• Coordinate short-term Health, Mental Health, and MEAL Scale-Up Advisors with national technical teams through agreed assignments, practical deliverables, mentorship, and documented knowledge transfer.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning**

• Work with MEAL and sector leads to plan and oversee baseline data collection, assessments, and indicator definitions covering population needs, inputs, service performance, financial and other operational resource requirements.

• Ensure consistent results of monitoring, accurate service statistics, data-quality checks, indicator tracking, field verification, learning reviews, and evidence-based corrective action.

• Coordinate the review and improvement of pharmaceutical reporting requirements with the Mission Lead, Health, Supply Chain, and MEAL teams, including joint analysis of stock, consumption, traceability, and reporting gaps.

• Strengthen programmatic data systems, DHIS2 and other applicable registers, internal and external referral tracking, and safe use of sensitive beneficiary information.

• Ensure accountability to affected populations through accessible feedback mechanisms, inclusion, community participation, timely follow-up, and appropriate escalation of safeguarding concerns.

**Budget, Grants & Resource Management**

• Monitor program budgets, spending projections, burn rates, implementation variances, and resource utilization in coordination with Finance and designated budget holders.

• Align technical requirements with procurement and supply plans; anticipate commodity shortages, import and distribution delays, and resource gaps that could disrupt service continuity.

• Contribute to budget revisions, grant modifications, proposal development, donor reporting, and new funding opportunities in collaboration with grants, technical, Finance, and senior management colleagues.

• Ensure timely, accurate and audit-ready programmatic reporting and documentation in accordance with donor agreements and organizational requirements.

**Team Management, Representation & Coordination**

• Supervise assigned program staff, establish performance objectives, provide coaching and feedback, and strengthen national leadership and cross-sector collaboration.

• Work with the Mission Lead, departments, technical advisers, and partner organizations to facilitate joint planning, capacity strengthening, and effective decisions.

• Represent Project HOPE in relevant technical coordination forums, sector clusters, and meetings with stakeholders when delegated by the Mission Lead.

• Promote a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and results-oriented working culture that supports staff well-being and learning.

**Risk Management, Safeguarding & Accountability**

• Maintain programmatic risk monitoring and contingency arrangements, including access and security constraints, service disruptions, supply interruptions, diversion risks, and changing community needs.

• Ensure compliance with Project HOPE policies and applicable laws, humanitarian principles, donor regulations, anti-corruption safeguards, child safeguarding, PSHEA, data confidentiality, and do-no-harm standards.

• Escalate significant safety, programmatic, fiduciary or compliance concerns through established organizational channels; respect the independence and authority of Security, Finance, and Compliance functions.

• Support responsible transitions and close-out processes, ensuring continuity of care, safe case handover, evidence of results, and appropriate retention of program records.

Other duties as assigned, consistent with the role and organizational requirements.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

• Advanced university degree in Public Health, International Development, Humanitarian Affairs, Health Systems, or a related field preferred; a bachelor’s degree with substantial equivalent senior leadership experience may be considered.

• At least 10 years of progressive experience in humanitarian or development programming, including at least 4 years in senior program management, Head of Programs, or comparable multisectoral leadership roles.

• Proven experience leading integrated health, nutrition, WASH, protection or related humanitarian interventions in conflict-affected, access-constrained, or rapidly changing settings.

• Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, operational scale-up, project start-up, service quality assurance, budget management, risk mitigation, and institutional donor reporting.

• Strong grasp of humanitarian coordination mechanisms and standards, including Sphere, CHS, and relevant technical guidance; familiarity with safeguarding and accountability to affected populations.

• Experience with program management and planning tools, log frames, indicator tracking, Gantt charts, implementation of work plans, and financial monitoring.

• Excellent leadership, communication, analytical and problem-solving skills, with proven ability to mentor national technical teams and engage diverse stakeholders.

• Fluency in written and spoken English is required; Arabic is a strong asset. Previous experience in Gaza or comparable emergencies is desirable.

• Relevant professional certification in project/program management (e.g., Project DPro, PMD Pro, PMP) is an advantage.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

The physical demands and working conditions described below are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform those functions.

**Physical demands:**

• Ability to work in office and field settings, communicate effectively in verbal and written form, and use standard office equipment.

• Ability and willingness to travel as necessary, subject to security assessments, movement approvals, access conditions.

**Work environment:**

• The position will require deployment and work in resource-constrained, insecure, stressful and austere humanitarian environments.

• Working schedules and field movements may change rapidly in response to humanitarian needs, security constraints, and operational priorities.

  
Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks job applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries, we receive, only candidates who have met the required experience & qualifications for this position will be considered. **No phone calls please.** However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

title: Oficial de Finanzas - Caracas
body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Finanzas** altamente calificado con sede en **Caracas, Venezuela.**

**Acerca del trabajo**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, Zulia y La Guaira. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Propósito general del puesto**

El Oficial de Finanzas tendrá la tarea de apoyar las operaciones financieras para cumplir con los requisitos internos, externos y reglamentación legal, así como velar por el cumplimiento de los criterios de Donantes. El Oficial de Finanzas deberá estar familiarizado con la preparación de presupuestos, seguimiento presupuestario, actividades contables y procedimientos de auditorías externas.

**Responsabilidades principales**

**Gestión Financiera y Contable**

- Asegurar que todas las transacciones financieras sean registradas de manera oportuna, precisa y conforme en el sistema ERP de DRC.
- Realizar conciliaciones bancarias y de caja de forma mensual, asegurando la consistencia y exactitud de la información financiera.
- Garantizar el adecuado manejo contable de acuerdo con las leyes locales, políticas internas y procedimientos organizacionales.
- Mantener debidamente organizada y archivada la documentación soporte, asegurando su trazabilidad y disponibilidad para auditorías.
- Asegurar el cumplimiento oportuno de los cierres contables dentro de los plazos establecidos.

**Monitoreo Presupuestario y Reportes**

- Realizar seguimiento a la ejecución presupuestaria de los proyectos y presupuestos asignados a la oficina nacional.
- Identificar desviaciones presupuestarias y alertar oportunamente a la gerencia.
- Apoyar en la preparación de informes financieros para donantes, garantizando el cumplimiento de sus lineamientos y requisitos.

**Cumplimiento, Control Interno y Auditoría**

- Verificar que los gastos cumplan con los criterios de elegibilidad, razonabilidad y correcta imputación presupuestaria.
- Garantizar el cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos de DRC y los requisitos de los donantes.
- Apoyar la coordinación y atención de auditorías internas, externas y revisiones de donantes.
- Fortalecer los controles internos para minimizar riesgos financieros y asegurar la transparencia en la gestión.

**Tesorería y Gestión de Efectivo**

- Gestionar y monitorear el flujo de caja, asegurando la disponibilidad de fondos para la operación.
- Preparar solicitudes de fondos conforme a la planificación financiera.
- Realizar transacciones bancarias de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos.
- Asegurar el adecuado manejo y control del efectivo conforme a las políticas de DRC.

**Procesos de Pago y Soporte Operativo**

- Revisar y procesar pagos a proveedores, personal y terceros, asegurando la correcta documentación y autorizaciones.
- Verificar la disponibilidad presupuestaria antes de la ejecución de pagos.
- Apoyar los procesos financieros relacionados con adquisiciones, en cumplimiento con las políticas organizacionales.

**Coordinación y Apoyo Administrativo**

- Brindar apoyo financiero a los equipos operativos y de programas.
- Apoyar en la gestión documental financiera y administrativa requerida para el funcionamiento de la oficina.
- Coordinar con otras áreas para asegurar la adecuada implementación de los procesos financieros.

**Colaboración y Cumplimiento Organizacional**

- Cumplir y promover las políticas internas, incluyendo el código de conducta de DRC.
- Colaborar en el cumplimiento de las normas de seguridad y procedimientos operativos.
- Contribuir al trabajo en equipo y a la mejora continua de los procesos financieros.

**Experiencia y competencias técnicas:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia laboral con una ONG internacional en un rol similar.
- Manejo avanzado de Microsoft Office
- Conocimiento en Microsoft Dynamics
- Ingles Básico - Intermedio
- Competencias elevadas en el manejo de herramientas tecnológicas.
- Experiencia trabajando con ERP
- Dominio básico en PowerPoint y Word.
- Buena capacidad de comunicación y organización documental.

**Educación**:

Titulo universitario en Finanzas / Administración de Empresas / Contabilidad o su equivalente en experiencia

**Idiomas:**

Fluidez en español e inglés escrito y hablado.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: Actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

title: Venezuela: Asistente Administrativo de Proyecto (Caracas)
body:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria, de carácter voluntario, que forma parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Medialuna Roja. Su compromiso es prestar ayuda en todo momento y en todo lugar, promoviendo el bienestar integral de las comunidades para que sean menos vulnerables, con basamento en sus Principios Fundamentales: Humanidad, Neutralidad, Imparcialidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad; y sus valores humanitarios, como el respeto a la dignidad de la persona, la solidaridad, la no discriminación, movilizando con eficiencia, mística y calidad su capital humano, conformado por su personal voluntario.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades

El/La Asistente Administrativo de Proyecto tendrá como responsabilidad principal apoyar a la coordinación financiera y logística en la gestión eficiente y transparente del proyecto asignado, asegurando la ejecución presupuestal y operativa con calidad. Esto incluye el monitoreo, análisis y cumplimiento de procedimientos, así como la adecuada administración de recursos financieros y humanos, provisión oportuna de bienes y servicios, y la generación de informes financieros y técnicos que respalden la toma de decisiones estratégicas, en línea con los lineamientos institucionales y de los donantes. Adicionalmente, deberá apoyar al Oficial de Administración en la organización de documentos financieros y contables, y colaborar con el Oficial de Logística en el proceso de compras, organizando la información correspondiente a las adquisiciones del proyecto, manteniendo comunicación con proveedores, y garantizando la entrega y registro en inventario de los bienes y suministros específicos para las actividades del proyecto.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

· Apoyar al Oficial de Administración en la organización y archivo de documentos financieros y contables del proyecto.

· Apoyar al Oficial de Logística en el proceso de compras, organizando la información de adquisiciones, manteniendo comunicación con proveedores y verificando la entrega de bienes y servicios conforme a las especificaciones.

· Elaborar informes financieros interinos y reportes de rendición de cuentas para donantes y la coordinación financiera de la Sociedad Nacional.

· Revisar, consolidar y validar justificativos de gastos y facturas efectuados por coordinadores y personal de las filiales, asegurando su conformidad con los lineamientos institucionales y de los donantes.

· Gestionar y monitorear los valores transferidos a las seccionales para la ejecución de proyectos, confirmando una ejecución mínima del 80% antes de solicitar nuevos fondos.

· Coordinar con las áreas de compras y logística para verificar pagos a proveedores y garantizar la correcta codificación y registro de las adquisiciones.

· Monitorear la solicitud y ejecución de pagos de nómina del personal nacional de proyectos, asegurando su cumplimiento en tiempo y forma, incluyendo la incorporación de nuevo personal al sistema de pagos.

· Hacer seguimiento al plan de compras junto con el Oficial de Finanzas y el Oficial de Logística, asegurando el cumplimiento de los tiempos y procedimientos establecidos.

· Asegurar el pago oportuno de servicios y gastos operativos de las sedes, así como la adquisición de materiales de oficina y suministros vinculados a las actividades del proyecto.

· Mantener actualizada la documentación digital y física relacionada con compras, inventarios y justificativos de gastos, garantizando la trazabilidad de la información.

· Solicitar documentación faltante a las áreas pertinentes para garantizar el cumplimiento de los procesos administrativos y financieros.

· Coordinar con equipos administrativos, financieros, logísticos y operativos para asegurar la correcta ejecución de actividades y la entrega oportuna de bienes y servicios.

· Facilitar reuniones de seguimiento con donantes, equipos internos y aliados estratégicos para la gestión y control de fondos y adquisiciones.

· Apoyar en el monitoreo y control de la ejecución mensual del proyecto, identificando desviaciones y proponiendo medidas correctivas relacionadas con la gestión logística y financiera.

Reporte

El/La Asistente Administrativo de Proyecto le reportará al Oficial de Finanzas y Oficial de Logística del proyecto.

Equipos

Es altamente deseable que cuente con equipos suficientes para el desempeño de su función de manera remota: laptop y/o computadora, buena conexión a Internet, entre otros.

Lugar de trabajo

Caracas, con posibilidad de viajar a otros lugares del país donde se implemente el proyecto.

Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:

· Título universitario en Administración, Logística o Contaduría; también se considerará otra formación académica con experiencia comprobada en compras.

· Mínimo tres (3) años en planificación, seguimiento y análisis presupuestal de proyectos, preferiblemente en el ámbito humanitario o de desarrollo.

· Experiencia comprobada en elaboración de informes financieros para donantes internacionales, conciliación de saldos en múltiples monedas y cumplimiento de lineamientos financieros de organismos internacionales.

· Experiencia comprobada de trabajo en el sector humanitario y/o ONGs

· Mínimo dos (2) años gestionando pagos a proveedores, nóminas y gastos operativos.

· Experiencia mínima de dos (2) años trabajando en equipos multidisciplinarios, colaborando con áreas de logística, compras y operaciones.

· Experiencia en logística y/o compras, incluyendo coordinación con proveedores, gestión de adquisiciones y control de inventarios vinculados a proyectos.

· Producción de informes narrativos y financieros.

· Excelentes habilidades de redacción y comunicación.

· Manejo de paquetes informáticos (Office, Adobe, etc.).

· Habilidades analíticas y orientación a soluciones.

· Atención al detalle y cuidado en la ejecución de tareas.

· Capacidad para trabajar en equipo multicultural y bajo presión.

· Discreción, neutralidad y confidencialidad.

· Interés en trabajar en un entorno humanitario e internacional.

title: Fuel Monitoring Assistant
body:
**Location:** Tshopo Province with travel within or to other provinces as necessary

**Length of contract:** 3 months with possibility of extension

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

Under the supervision of the GORS Fleet Officer for work planning, execution, and performance, the Ebola Fuel Monitoring Assistant will report daily on activities, weekly on data, on monthly full report.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

Fuel Monitoring Assistant will monitor and report on fuel supply needs and utilization, ensuring strict adherence to all fleet, procurement, and finance protocols

*The Fuel Monitoring* Assistant *will:*

Fuel Supply Needs

- In its allocated area, report to the Fleet Officer on fuel levels and needs for the GORS program staff and partner

Logbooks

- Train drivers on the logbook systematic utilization, with an emphasis on the link between supply and usage report
- Verify logbooks, taking corrective action and reporting on underutilized logbooks or falsified records
- Communicate with distant driver to receive logbook picture by phone, track drivers who did not report the weekly logbook, report on them
- Register data in Excel tracking document and report on a weekly basis to the Fleet Officer
- Check and control the logbook record, and attach the report to the rental vehicle invoice

**Required Position Qualifications**

- At least 2 years of fleet experience, in humanitarian program or private sector.
- Demonstrate the management of a medium-size fleet at country or regional level
- Demonstrate knowledge on how to work with a fleet of ambulances in outbreak or emergency settings.
- Strong understanding of fleet management, quality assurance, and chain of custody.
- Ability to work in a difficult environment and work under pressure.
- Fluent communication in French, English is an asset.
- Ability to use Excel and word as an advance user, designing complex excel sheet
- Motorbike driving license

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travels**

The Fuel Monitoring Assistant will travel within the province and to other provinces in the Eastern region of the DRC for an agreed period according to operational needs, when required.

**Working Conditions**

Working hours will be scheduled within the contracted 40-hour weekly allocation, with hours aligned to DRC GORS operations. Emergency support will follow agreed activation and backup arrangements. The Fuel Monitoring Assistant adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

body:

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The ICT and Office Support Officer is responsible for preparing, administering, and managing the assets of the GORS program, and for ensuring that ICT equipment (laptops, printers, Starlinks, mobile phones, etc.) and security equipment (satellite phones, tracking devices, etc.) are maintained in optimal condition. The ICT and Office Support Officer will also manage travel requests, ensuring that UNHAS flights are booked on time, hotel reservations are made, and travelers are informed of their bookings or any changes immediately.

- Maintain the access to the internet, the Wi-Fi and wired network in working order.

*Security Equipment*

- In collaboration with the Security Team, ensure that Starlink, satellite phones and GPS trackers are cleaned and maintained in operational condition so that they are ready for use at any time.
- At the end of a field mission, print the call and data reports and report any misuse of the data and airtime packages.

*Office*

- Keep printers functioning and cartridges in stock, tracking cartridge usage.
- Maintain Office stationaries in stock and deliver stationaries request using a logbook

*Travel requests*

- Receive travel requests and resolve any questions before processing them.
- Manage the UNHAS booking system for in-country flights, ensuring flights are booked as soon as possible, reporting any issues back to the requester, and proposing solutions.
- Manage hotel reservations for travelers.
- Always maintain the travel request for each traveler with up-to-date information.

- At least 2 years of ICT experience, in humanitarian program or private sector.
- Demonstrated capacity to organize his/herself
- Demonstrated knowledge on how to work with a range of ICT equipment and other technological communication and security devices.

- Fluent communication in French, English is an asset.
- Ability to use Excel and word as an advance user, designing complex excel sheet

**Travels**

The ICT and Office Support Officer may travel within the province and to other provinces in the Eastern region of the DRC for an agreed period according to operational needs, when required.

**Working Conditions**

The ICT and Office Support Officer will work from Kisangani. Working hours will be scheduled within the contracted 40-hour weekly allocation, with hours aligned to DRC GORS operations. Emergency support will follow agreed activation and backup arrangements. The Fleet Officer adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.
