title: CHARGE-E DE PROJET POLE RESSOURCES - FRANCE
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

La ou le chargé de projet pôle ressources contribue à la définition et assure la mise en oeuvre de la stratégie d'accompagnement et d'appui des partenaires opérationnels de la Mission France à Marseille   
Plus précisément, vos missions seront de :  
Contribuer à la définition de la stratégie et des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires de la base Marseille-PACA  
Participer à l'identification, au développement et à la rédaction des nouveaux projets  
Représenter ACF à l'échelle locale et nationale.  
 Assurer le déploiement et le suivi des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires   
Développer les outils et méthodologie d'accompagnement des partenaires et d'ingénierie de projet (protocole d'intervention opérationnel et/ou en sécurité alimentaire, suivi et évaluation dont diagnostic ; coordination et maillage ; animation et formation...).  
Appuyer la capitalisation et la remontée des informations de terrain à des fins de reporting, de communication et de plaidoyer  
Assurer la collecte, l'analyse, la valorisation et la diffusion des données qualitatives et quantitatives issues des activités du pôle ressource, notamment celles issues des enquêtes de terrain   
Manager et superviser son équipe et participer à la vie de la base et la mission

  

Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master en sciences politiques, développement local et territorial, coordination de projet, sciences humaines, design social, économie ou statistiques.  
Vous disposez d'au moins 4 ans en gestion de projet dans l'un des domaines suivants : action sociale, sécurité alimentaire et lutte contre la précarité alimentaire, suivi et évaluation, protection et accès aux droits.  
Vous avez la capacité à mobiliser des réseaux d'acteurs (associations, institutions, collectivités, structures de quartier) et à créer et entretenir des relations de confiance.  
Vous avez des compétences relationnelles et en terme d'intelligence collective d'accompagnement des réflexions, d'animation multi-acteurs.  
Vous avez une connaissance et une compréhension des dynamiques politiques et institutionnelles en France, et une connaissance fine et appliquée du tissu associatif et institutionnel marseillais.  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDI - Temps plein  
Lieu : Marseille   
Rémunération :  
De 37K à 43Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Prime d'ancienneté à partir de 3 années de présence au siège   
Avantages:  
25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail  
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up):Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros  
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)   
Télétravail :  
Possibilité d'exercer certaines missions en télétravail   
Déplacements terrains : Intra-PACA, possibles déplacements de représentation et coordination hors région PACA.  
  
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

title: Country Support Officer - West & Central Africa (national applicants only)
body:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO West & Central Africa services**

Since 2013, INSO has supported the humanitarian community across the region and is looking to establish a regional presence for West & Central Africa services at the request of the NGO community. This position is based in Dakar, Senegal, and reports to the Regional Director under the technical guidance of the HQ technical referents.

**Job Summary**

Join INSO Senegal as our Country Support Officer and play a key role in keeping our operations running smoothly and effectively.

Working closely with the Regional Director and supported by HR, Finance, and Operations specialists, you will oversee the country office's core support functions, including finance, HR, administration, logistics, and procurement.

In this role, you will help safeguard the financial health and operational integrity of the programme by ensuring compliance with INSO policies and procedures, supporting audits and reporting requirements, and providing reliable data that informs strategic decisions. You will also guide and support colleagues on financial, HR, and administrative processes, helping the team deliver impact in a well-managed and accountable environment.

**Main Responsibilities**

*Finance Management*

- Manage petty cash, bank payments, reconciliations, and cash flow requests.
- Maintain accurate financial records and ensure timely month-end closures and SUN Systems reporting.
- Prepare budgets, donor financial reports, and monthly budget variance analysis (BVA) for management.
- Ensure compliance with INSO financial procedures, reporting requirements, and audit recommendations.
- Authorize transactions within delegated authority levels.
- Lead statutory financial reporting and compliance with Senegalese legal requirements.
- Strengthen internal controls and support continuous financial risk management.

*Human Resources Management*

- Lead implementation of INSO HR policies and ensure compliance with national labour legislation.
- Maintain accurate personnel records, HRIS data, and secure HR documentation.
- Coordinate and support payroll processes for national and international staff.
- Manage onboarding, inductions, safeguarding awareness, and employee lifecycle processes.
- Support recruitment, contracting, probation reviews, and offboarding activities.
- Contribute to salary benchmarking and compensation reviews.
- Liaise with legal counsel and HQ on employment, compliance, and registration matters.

*Administration, Legal and Compliance*

- Ensure compliance with registration, statutory reporting, taxation, and other legal obligations.
- Coordinate visas, work permits, and residency documentation for staff.
- Arrange business travel and provide administrative support for missions and deployments.
- Maintain organized and secure legal, administrative, and contractual records.

*Facility and Asset Management*

- Oversee office facilities, leases, service providers, and workplace operations.
- Maintain the asset register, including asset tracking, inventories, and periodic verification exercises.
- Ensure facilities and assets are managed in line with INSO safety, security, and asset management standards.

*Procurement and Logistics*

- Manage procurement processes in compliance with INSO procedures and donor requirements.
- Maintain procurement records, supplier databases, and contract documentation.
- Implement controls to mitigate fraud, corruption, and sanctions-related risks.
- Manage supplier relationships and conduct regular market assessments.
- Coordinate logistics for trainings, workshops, meetings, and team events.

**Confidentiality**

- Observe and maintain confidentiality and safety of any documentation or procedures as outlined by INSO Policies.
- Observe and maintain confidentiality and safety of all NGO information.

**Lines of Communication**

The Regional Director is your point of contact.

The above duties are not exhaustive; flexibility is expected as you may be assigned any other duties that may not be listed above to meet the needs of the programme.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

*Essential*

- Minimum 5 years of progressive professional experience in managing supporting services: HR, finance logistics, facilities and procurement.
- Proficient use of MS Office suite, financial and HR database management.
- Fluent spoken and written French language skills and professional English communication skills
- Experience working in an international NGO or similar environment
- General knowledge of donor procurement regulations.
- Strong organizational and multitasking abilities.

*Nice to Have:*

- Experience in SUNSYSTEM and Q&A reporting tool
- Knowledge of INSO and affinity with its mission.
- Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements in the country.
- Prior field experience in Senegal in a similar position is a plus.

**Competencies**

- Financial & risk management:Ensures sound financial planning, budget oversight, and compliance with internal policies and donor regulations while mitigating financial risks.
- Operational efficiency & resource management:Oversees logistics, procurement, finance, HR and administrative functions to ensure smooth and cost-effective operations in complex environments.
- Regulatory compliance & governance: Ensures adherence to local labour laws, donor requirements, and internal policies, maintaining transparency and accountability.
- Strategic planning & problem-solving:Anticipates operational and financial challenges, develops solutions, and supports long-term sustainability and efficiency.
- Leadership & stakeholder coordination: Manages and develops teams, fosters collaboration across departments, and engages with internal management and external partners to support INSO’s mission.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

Position open to national candidates only. 12-month renewable contract. 1521000 F CFA per month salary, 2.5 calendar days of annual leave per month.

title: Senior Communications Officer- Government and Multilateral Donors
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

The International Rescue Committee is among the world’s leading nonprofit humanitarian relief and development organizations. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. The organization is on the ground in more than 35 countries, providing emergency relief and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through over 30 regional offices across the United States, we also help refugees resettle in the US and become self-sufficient.

We’re striving to build an organization that is a supportive, kind and inspiring place to work. We encourage bold leadership, innovation, creative partnerships and accountability to those we serve.

  
The Awards Management Unit (AMU) is a global unit with teams in New York, Washington DC, London, Nairobi, Berlin, Brussels, Stockholm and Amman with staff presence in many other locations around the world. Its purpose is to lead IRC’s work to engage and influence government donors, secure funding, and enable compliant and effective program delivery for our clients. The AMU sits within IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department, alongside IRC’s international country programs, emergencies unit and technical teams.

  
The role will work to deliver excellent government and multilateral donor communications on behalf of CRRD, working closely with the Global Public Affairs and Communications Department, which will provide technical and strategic support.

**Job Overview:**

The Senior Communications Officer will help to position the IRC as a thought leader and partner of choice with government and multilateral partners and donors, shaping how they see IRC programs, solutions, and evidence. The role will lead the development and implementation of external communications strategies that build IRC’s profile with target donors and highlight the impact of key government and multilateral-funded programs.

  
The Senior Officer will be responsible for developing messaging, content, and media that showcase IRC programs and solutions and that connect IRC expertise to donor priorities. The role will ensure that our program-specific visibility obligations for key donors go well beyond minimum standards to highlight the innovative and impactful work IRC is doing with the support of these key organizations.

The role will sit in the Global Business Development Team, with a technical reporting line into the Global Public Affairs and Communications Team. The role will work closely with each priority donor’s engagement lead to ensure communications are aligned with donor engagement strategies and priorities.

The ideal candidate will bring experience of developing messaging and talking points, writing opeds, and creating thought leadership content that is focused on donor-funded priorities, will possesses a strong understanding of the humanitarian and development donor landscape, and be familiar with how to use media and digital channels to reach donor audiences.  
  
**Major Responsibilities:**

**Communications Planning**

- Develop and implement tailored Donor Communications Plans for a diverse set of public donors (initially World Bank and UNOCHA), designed to position IRC’s impact, technical expertise and innovations in line with donor strategic priorities.
- Identify, plan and manage ongoing communications that promote the IRC and our work, including around moments and events with relevant donor engagement leads.
- Advise IRC teams on donor communications and visibility requirements, prioritizing countries and programs that matter most to each donor and where going beyond visibility requirements will build the strongest case for future funding.

**Developing and Delivering Communications Content**

- Work with our Global Content and Creative Studio team to develop global communications materials and impact stories such as case studies, brochures, videos and other materials that showcase IRC projects and demonstrate IRC’s credentials as a reliable and impactful partner.
- Partner with country teams to meet and exceed strategic relevant donor communications and visibility requirements.
- Build a bank of stories and content that showcases IRC’s evidence, results, and impact from donor-funded projects and other programs that positions the IRC for future funding, working with country and technical teams to identify relevant evidence and content.
- Work with the Digital Engagement team to deliver content on social channels most relevant to each donor, particularly LinkedIn, and track which content reaches and engages donor audiences.
- Pitch and secure earned media coverage of IRC’s solutions and innovations in the outlets that donor decision-makers read, working with the Global Public Affairs media team and market comms leads.
- Draft, place and promote op-eds and bylined pieces from IRC leaders and technical experts that connect IRC’s evidence to donor priorities.
- Pursue joint content and speaking opportunities with donor communications teams that raise IRC’s profile as a trusted expert voice.
- Provide flexible, additional support as requested by colleagues in AMU for communications around other strategic projects in the IRC portfolio.

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience:**

- Strong professional experience in communications, international affairs or related field.
- Experience across communications strategy development, media relations and digital communications, with a track record of securing earned media and placing op-eds.
- Experience leading communications work internationally, adapting strategy and messaging for different countries, cultures and audiences.
- Experience translating complex information, programme evidence and results into clear, engaging communications for external audiences.
- Experience in communications planning and delivery.
- Experience leading projects and collaborating with multiple teams and individuals.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Excellent creative abilities, with a track record of having proactive, creative communications ideas and seeing them through to completion.
- Excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills, with the ability to produce clean, engaging, and jargon-free content tailored to different audiences, channels and institutional contexts.
- Ability to translate technical evidence, data and cost information into clear, accurate content for different audiences.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to establish positive working relationships and collaborate effectively with colleagues across a wide range of teams and functions.
- Proactive approach to problem solving to meet organisational demands.

**Desirable:**

- Experience living or working in a development or humanitarian programming context.
- Experience with and understanding of key institutional humanitarian or development organizations, particularly government or multilateral donors, especially OCHA and/or the World Bank.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard office working environment
- Some international travel as needed, up to 20%

**Recruitment Process**:

The expected recruitment process for this role will include:

- HR screening call online
- Technical panel interview online (potentially with a short pre-prepared presentation)
- Final round interview online

Candidates must have the right to work within the country they are applying. IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.  
  
**Compensation:** (GBP 46,780 - GBP 55,552) Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Training Assistants
body:
## **Call for expression of interest: Training Assistants (Consultancy)**

**Location:** Nairobi or Athi River

**Contract type:** Individual Consultant / Contracted Trainer

**Duration:** 9 months, with approximately 22 days training days per month, subject to final programme requirements.

**Expected start date:** February 2027

**About the opportunity:**

Sightsavers is seeking Assistant Trainers to support the delivery of the Digital Futures Programme across four Physical Digital Skills Academies in Kenya. Working alongside Lead Trainers, the consultants will provide practical classroom, laboratory, assignment and assessment support so that learners with disabilities can strengthen their technical competence and complete the academy successfully.

The Digital Futures Programme supports young women and men with disabilities to gain relevant digital skills, prepare for employment and build sustainable livelihoods. Training is residential and instructor-led, using industry-accredited curricula and equivalent programmes across employer-identified technical areas.

Technical areas: software development; data analysis and visualisation; cloud computing; cybersecurity; artificial intelligence; and other programme-approved disciplines. Allocation will depend on competence, certification and programme needs.

This call for expressions of interest is for the Kenya Assistant Trainer consultancies, not a general roster. Submitting an EOI or completing references, checks, an interview or an assessment does not guarantee a contract.

**Purpose:**

The Assistant Trainer will provide day-to-day technical, academic and practical support to Lead Trainers and learners. The role will help learners participate fully in practical sessions, complete assignments, prepare for assessments and build credible, work-relevant digital skills while maintaining an inclusive, accessible and safeguarding-conscious learning environment.

**Key responsibilities include:**

- Working with the Lead Trainer to review the curriculum, learner profiles, training calendar, facilities, equipment, software and accessibility arrangements.
- Preparing session resources, technology setups, practical exercises, laboratory guides, learner handouts and assignment-tracking tools.
- Providing hands-on support during demonstrations, guided practice, laboratories, projects, troubleshooting exercises, peer learning and assignment clinics.
- Offering timely clarification and guided practice without completing assessed work on behalf of learners.
- Supporting diagnostic, formative, practical and summative assessments, including accessible arrangements and reasonable adjustments.
- Helping learners create authentic portfolios, capstone projects, laboratory records and other evidence of competence.
- Monitoring attendance, participation, assignment completion and practical progress, and escalating barriers or support needs promptly.
- Contributing technical input to learner CVs, portfolios, professional profiles, interview preparation and progression opportunities.
- Maintaining accurate records and contributing to progress updates, quality-assurance meetings and final reporting.
- Following safeguarding, professional conduct, confidentiality, data-protection, health and safety and academic-integrity requirements.

**Trainers will be engaged for one or more of the below technical areas:**

Assistant Trainers will support one or more of the following areas, depending on their competence, certification and programme needs:

- Software development and related programming disciplines.
- Data analysis, data management and data visualisation.
- Cloud computing and cloud administration.
- Cybersecurity and secure digital practices.
- Artificial intelligence.
- Other market-relevant digital disciplines approved by the programme.

**Deliverables:**

- A session-support plan agreed with the Lead Trainer before training begins.
- Prepared practical exercises, laboratory guides, troubleshooting notes, assignment trackers and accessible learner-support materials.
- Weekly attendance, participation, assignment, accessibility and learner-support records.
- Monthly or agreed progress updates covering learner participation, practical skills, assignment completion, risks, barriers and follow-up actions.
- Assessment and portfolio-support records during assessment periods.
- An end-of-cohort Assistant Trainer report, submitted within two weeks of cohort close, including lessons learned, learner-progress observations, accessibility issues and recommendations.

**About you:**

You will be a technically credible and supportive professional who enjoys helping others put learning into practice. You will be able to explain complex concepts clearly, guide learners through practical challenges and work collaboratively under the direction of a Lead Trainer. You will bring patience, sound professional judgement and a learner-centred approach, while respecting the dignity, autonomy and individual choices of persons with disabilities.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- A relevant diploma, degree, professional or industry certification, or equivalent practical experience demonstrating your technical competence in the proposed subject area.
- Current, verifiable competence in your proposed technical area, with relevant vendor or industry certification where applicable.
- Relevant professional or practical experience in the assigned technical area.
- Experience supporting adult learners, graduates or early-career professionals.
- Demonstrated ability to support practical exercises, laboratories, assignment clinics, learner troubleshooting and project-based learning under the guidance of a Lead Trainer.
- Evidence of recent industry practice, consulting, technical project delivery or continuing professional development.
- Strong facilitation, communication, coaching, organisation, documentation, digital-literacy and learner-management skills.
- Experience supporting diverse learner groups. Experience working with persons with disabilities or applying universal-design and reasonable-accommodation principles is highly desirable.
- Fluency in written and spoken English. Kiswahili or another relevant language would be an advantage.
- Availability for the full preparation, delivery, assessment, reporting and close-out period.

This is a highly varied and involved consultancy position, and the above is not an exhaustive list of deliverables or required professional skills. Please see the [Terms of Reference](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQDH5OxgxnJyT6ylDSJcahbUAVtzBnyTC_HTwnvsI0_dBwM?e=ax6BtM) for full details.

title: Manager, Principal Giving East
Logistics Coordinator (f/m/x) – Italy – MSF Belgium
body:
## **CONTEXT**

MSF has maintained a longstanding presence in Italy. Currently, MSF Operational Center Brussels (OCB) runs two projects in Sicily: one assisting people on the move in Agrigento and another supporting survivors of ill-treatment in Palermo. In 2027, MSF OCB plans to expand its search and rescue (SAR) capacity at sea by adding an OCB SAR vessel alongside the existing OCA vessel. While the logistics needs of the Palermo and Agrigento projects are managed by the current project teams, starting the SAR activities will require significant coordination and hands-on guidance from the Logistics Department.

As **Logistics Coordinator**, you will initially be based mainly at the OCB vessel’s shipyard in Trapani, Sicily, to support the start-up of SAR activities. After this initial period, Rome will become your permanent base.

## **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Lead the Logistics Dept. within the Italy Country Coordination Team, taking overall responsibility and accountability for its activities
- Plan and manage the Department’s annual budget and activities, including Vessel Management, which represents a significant part of the workload
- Design and propose the most appropriate logistics setup for the programme and project teams, adapting it to changing needs
- Maintain a flexible approach by reducing barriers and adjusting the setup and procedures to ensure operational continuity in a changing context
- Support and develop the Logistics Managers in Agrigento, Palermo and SAR through functional management, capacity building, coaching and mentoring
- Coordinate technical matters with the project teams and, for SAR, among the onshore team, maritime crew and external Technical Superintendent (TSI)
- Enable the OCB vessel to conduct continuous and safe search and rescue activities
- Oversee security measures across the programme and support the Captain, who holds final responsibility for security on board, with MSF expertise and resources
- Ensure that bases, vehicles and the vessel provide safe environments for all staff members
- Analyze reported data to improve the quality and efficiency of the Department’s activities
- Strengthen safeguarding across the Department by identifying and reducing risks beyond those covered by safety and security measures
- Integrate DEI into all processes, including recruitment

**Vessel Management**

- Oversee the overall management of the SAR vessel
- Define the most appropriate fleet management model
- Integrate input from the maritime crew and external Technical Superintendent into the annual Vessel Management plan and budget
- Define internal and external technical support needs, draft Terms of Reference, organize tenders and contract the most appropriate service providers
- Coordinate vessel needs and non-operational periods across departments, including planned maintenance and dry docks, to support programme-wide planning
- Coordinate IT and telecommunications needs and identify appropriate solutions
- Control Vessel Management costs in line with the Authorization Table
- Oversee all Port Agent matters related to supplies and services, delegating tasks to the project team where appropriate, and liaising with relevant counterparts on legal compliance matters such as customs and duties
- Facilitate coordination among the Logistics Managers, maritime crew and Vessel Management Technical Superintendent
- Provide the Country Management Team and functional manager in Brussels with technical planning information, including ordinary and extraordinary maintenance
- Report on all matters related to Vessel Management

## **REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Degree in engineering or mechanics is desirable
- Previous experience with MSF or other INGOs, including at least 12 months as Logistic Manager, is mandatory
- MSF experience is a strong asset
- Experience in fleet management is strong asset
- Experience in emergency responses and emergency preparedness is an asset
- Experience in strategic engagement with authorities is an asset
- Knowledge of the Italian context is an asset

**Languages**

- Proficiency in **English and Italian**, both written & spoken is mandatory

## **CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: **As soon as possible**
- Location\*: based in **Rome, Italy**

***\*Candidates must already have the legal right to work in Italy, either as an Italian/ EU citizen or by holding a valid residence/ work permit that authorizes employment in Italy, with unrestricted access to the Italian labor market***

- Mobility: Frequent stays at the shipyard in Sicily until April 2027, followed by regular travel to projects
- Contract type: Fixed-term contract – full-time
- Contract duration: **12 months (extendable)**
- The contract will be a local contract, under labour Italian legislation; with salary according to MSF **Italy Programmes Country Based** salary grid
- Family position not possible
- ***Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment***
- ***Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments***

**Deadline for applications: 6th of December 2026**

title: General Coordinator (Head of mission) (F/M) - Myanmar
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Myanmar**

MdM has been operating in Myanmar since 1994. Its strategic objective is to increase access to Harm Reduction and Sexual and Reproductive Health services by addressing health, social, legal and normative barriers though a community-led approach and partnerships. MdM aims to further strengthen its partnership-based approach and advance localization efforts across Myanmar.

In Kachin, MdM works closely with and strengthens a local civil society organization (CSO) to deliver essential PHC and SRH services through dedicated clinics for conflict-affected populations in the context of protracted crisis.

In other parts of the country, MdM - in partnership with 3 CBOs - aims at complementing Harm Reduction intervention in integrating Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) for supporting high-risk groups of people to prevent STIs and GBV.

*Whenever required and possible, MdM could also respond to disaster-related crisis and launch tailored relevant response*.

**About the role**

As General Coordinator, you oversee a range of sites within the country, ensuring that the programmes meet operational, administrative, financial, human, material, safety and organizational objectives by coordinating and leading a team. You ensure the deployment of MdM frameworks, policies and procedures. You lead the implementation of MdM projects in each area by integrating it into a socio-political context. Whenever possible, you lead and develop advocacy work and partnerships.

**What you’ll do**

In close collaboration with the Desk Manager in HQ, the General Coordinator is responsible for:

Strategic and program management: program planning and implementation in accordance with 2027-2028 Country Strategy document, strategy reviews and strategic planning on regular basis.

Human Resources: Support the mission in its changes and defining human resources needs in line with operational requirements. Support all coordinators in their role as managers. Direct management of a multi-level team composed of Coordinators, Manager and Advisor (defining objectives, conducting appraisals…).

Donor relationship: Explore new funding opportunities, representation with donors, negotiations regarding proposals for ongoing and new and/or renewed contracts, copying with major changes in programming including force majeure.

Partnership strengthening: reinforce pre-existing partnerships and encourage the identification of new potential partners to consider progressive handover of MdM activities to partners or health authorities.

Provides technical support to the MdM team: in-country (trainings, workshops, etc.) and using MdM resources globally, linking with Technical Department in HQ and technical Groups.

Security and safety management: be responsible for security management; updating the security guidelines on bi-annual basis; ensure constant monitoring and analysis on contextual geopolitical and security issues.

Administrative, Financial and Logistics: As budget holder, ensure proper use of funds allocated, reporting to donors, yearly budget construction and review. Ensure that appropriate logistics, administrative and financial structures and procedures are maintained in accordance with MdM rules and/or donors’ guidelines.

Reporting: Supervise timely and quality proposals and report submission to donors, submit mission coordination reports to HQ.

**Who you’ll work with**

Based in Yangon, under the supervision of the Regional Desk Manager, you will be the direct line manager of one Deputy General Coordinator, one Medical Coordinator, one Liaison Advisor, one Project Coordinator, one Training Manager and one Field Coordinator located in Kachin State.

You will manage a team composed of 1 expatriate, and more than 50 national staff.

You must liaise with all departments and services located at MdM Headquarters to ensure smooth mission management.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree level, ideally with a background in Public Health and/or in Human rights, political science
- Have a successful coordination experience in development/humanitarian context of minimum 7 years, having already been Country Director/Head of Mission during minimum three years
- Have a past experience in sexual and reproductive health and/or harm reduction related interventions
- Have a proven experience with localization of aid and partnership approach, it will be a strong asset
- Have a past experience in Myanmar, it will be is a strong asset
- Have proven your ability to coordinate, plan, anticipate in collaboration with HQ counterparts
- Are praised for your ability to mobilize around a common project/strategy
- Are recognized for your strong problem solving and organizational skills
- Have proved your leadeship with good listening and diplomacy skills
- Have a good command of the MS Office Suite
- Have an extensive experience in project cycle management, with an excellent konwledge of the donor’s landscape
- Are described as a good team manager with a strong leadership and representation skills
- Have experience in communicating via INGO forum and bilaterally
- Have a solid experience in leading organizational changes, transition processes (program and Human Ressources)
- Are talented in negociating partnership development agreements with local authorities, local Civil Socialty Oorganizations and INGOs
- Are perfectly fluent in English (writing/speaking)

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- Are not flexible and not able to cope with last-minute changes
- Are not capable to work and to live in a multicultural environment

title: SYRIA - Field Coordinator - (M/F) - Aleppo
body:
- **Référence :** SRH06852
- **Statut :** Salarié
- **Domaine de compétence :** Coordination régionale / Direction pays
- **Type de poste :** Missions
- **Type de contrat :** Salarié - CDD
- **Pays :** Syrie

## About us

**Desired start date:** 15/01/27  
**Duration of the mission:** 6 months  
**Location:** North-West Syria (NWS) Base, Aleppo

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International operates in Syria since 2013 with a very diversified programs portfolio in Hassake & Raqqa (NES), Aleppo and Idleb (NWS) governorates. To achieve its humanitarian objectives the mission employs 350 staffs and developed meaningful partnerships with international and local NGOs.

In NES, SI is one of the leading agencies in the WaSH sector, responding to emergencies, protracted situations and recovery needs. The strategy is complemented with a significant FSL component, addressing market rehabilitations, business development and agriculture.

In NWS, SI operates in Idleb and Northern-Aleppo with large WaSH programs, with a focus in camps settings for IDP populations, and rehabilitation programs, especially after the earthquake. SI also responds to new emergencies, including regular displacements, natural disasters and epidemics.

SI is also heavily involved in humanitarian coordination, both at strategic and technical level with relevant fora and stakeholders, including key donors.

Since regime's change, SI is redefining it operational model as well as its geographical scope and programmatic priorities. The organizational set up is being deeply reviewed with a Damascus-based coordination office, the reshaping of the base level structure. Assessments are being carried out in new areas including rural Damascus, South, Aleppo and Hama and new partnerships are being envisioned. This is to ensure relevance and efficiency, maximize impact through secured access and more generally ensuring the mission remains fit for purpose in a quickly evolving environment.

## About the job

GENARAL OBJECTIVES :

The NWS Field Coordinator has the role of delegated from the CD for NWS.  
He/she proposes an area strategy according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated.  
He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures  
He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management.  
He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.  
He/she is the Country Director’s direct contact and representative.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGE :

Management of short-term and unpredictable funding streams: Ability to prioritise and adapt programming under predominantly one-year grants, with frequent changes in scope and funding continuity risks.  
Ongoing mission restructuring and shifting ways of working: Capacity to lead teams through organisational changes (structures, roles, decision-making lines), maintaining clarity, accountability, and team cohesion.  
Unpredictable geopolitical and security environment: While day-to-day security may appear stable, the broader context remains volatile; requires strong anticipation, scenario planning, and contingency thinking.  
Maintaining operational continuity under sudden context shifts: Ability to rapidly adjust programmes, access approaches, and team deployment in response to political or security developments.  
Balancing delegation and control in a changing leadership setup: Ensuring effective oversight while empowering managers, particularly in a context of evolving team composition and responsibilities.  
Access and stakeholder management in a fragmented environment: Navigating multiple authorities and stakeholders, maintaining acceptance, and ensuring principled humanitarian action.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Lead base-level right-sizing and restructuring efforts – Conduct rapid review of structure, staffing, and costs; propose and initiate adjustments in line with funding and priorities, ensuring fair and compliant HR processes.  
Stabilise teams through structured change management – Provide clear communication, role clarification, and prioritisation to maintain continuity and reduce disruption.  
Align base systems and ways of working with Country Office standards – Ensure operational, programmatic, and support processes are consistent with CO objectives and procedures.  
Strengthen delegation and accountability within the base team – Clarify roles, reinforce ownership at manager level, and reduce unnecessary escalation.  
Ensure continuity and quality of programme implementation during transition – Maintain oversight of WASH, FSL, and CVA activities to ensure compliant and relevant delivery.  
Reinforce planning and anticipation capacity – Strengthen HR, supply, and activity planning tools to improve predictability and reduce last-minute issues.  
Maintain strong coordination, access, and external engagement – Sustain stakeholder relationships and preserve access conditions during transition.  
Success indicator – Clearer and leaner structure, improved role clarity, and base systems functioning in line with Country Office expectations.

SECURUTY CONTRAINTS :

Recent political and contextual shifts in Syria have brought significant changes to the security dynamics in the NWS region. While Aleppo is currently experiencing a relative calm, the situation remains fragile. The city is now fully under central government control, following agreements with various OAGs that had been active in the area. However, criminal activity persists, though often underreported. As such, continuous vigilance and heightened alertness are necessary in the city.

## Your profile

DIPLOMAS : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

EXPERIENCE IN HUMANITARIAN SECTOR: 5 years

EXPERIENCE IN SILILAR EXPERIENCE : 0 - 2 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

1\. Experience of multi-department team management

2\. Experience in security management in unstable contexts

3\. Excellent understanding of sub-office management, including financial, HR, log and project cycle management

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

1\. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, together with the capacity to remain calm under pressure and not lose sight of strategic priorities. Must be organised and efficient.

2\. A sound understanding of the importance of gender.

3\. Sensitivity to cultural differences and the ability to work in a wide variety of cultural contexts.

LANGUAGES :

1\. English necessary

2\. Arabic would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions** : All international staff based in Aleppo will be accommodated in the SI guest house. The telecommunications network is generally good, though it may vary depending on the specific location within the city. Electricity blackouts are common during the day. Staff will have access to local restaurants and markets. A curfew may be implemented depending on the security situation.

title: Regional Director, Asia Ministry Team
body:
**Job Title:** Regional Director, Asia Ministry Team

**Department:** Asia Ministry Team (AMT)

**Reports To:** Chief Program and Implementation Officer

**Status:** Full-Time, Exempt

**Location:** An approved World Renew country of operation in Asia (Laos, Cambodia, Bangladesh, Thailand, Lebanon, Syria)

**Salary Level:** 86,467.94 - 97,275.62 USD

**PURPOSE:**

The Regional Director, Asia, provides strategic, spiritual, and operational leadership for World Renew's work across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and West Asia.

As a member of Senior Leadership, the Regional Director leads Country Directors and regional staff, strengthens local partnerships, and ensures a coherent portfolio of high-quality, partner- and community-led development, humanitarian, resilience, justice, and peacebuilding programs. The role advances World Renew's global strategy, Christian identity, Theology of Development, localization commitments, organizational sustainability, and impact across diverse operating models, including fragile, conflict-affected, and politically restricted contexts.

The Regional Director ensures a clear, contextually relevant regional strategy and operating footprint, strengthening leadership, accountability, performance, and development across country and regional teams. Working with partners, donors, governments, and regional networks, the role strengthens trusted and equitable relationships and promotes safeguarding, community accountability, learning, and measurable impact.

The Regional Director also oversees the regional funding pipeline and portfolio, aligning resources with strategic priorities and ensuring financial, operational, security, safeguarding, compliance, and reputational risks are actively managed and communicated. The role leads country and regional transitions responsibly, with appropriate consultation, communication, and care for staff and partners.

***We do not discriminate based on disability, culture, ethnicity, or gender, and welcome and encourage***

***people from diverse backgrounds to apply.***

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**:

**A. Regional Strategy, Program Quality and Impact**

- Set, communicate, and adapt a clear regional strategy and operating footprint aligned with World Renew’s global strategy and country contexts.
- Ensure regional, country, and program plans form a coherent portfolio that responds to changing humanitarian, development, political, climate, and conflict dynamics.
- Ensure programs reflect World Renew’s Christian faith, Theology of Development, humanitarian mandate, and commitment to Integral Mission.
- Promote partner- and community-led approaches, strong program quality, safeguarding, and accountability.
- Champion the use of evidence, learning, and community feedback to continuously improve decisions and results.

**B. Partnerships, Representation, and Resource Mobilization**

- Represent World Renew credibly with churches, local partners, communities, governments, donors, networks, and peer organizations.
- Build equitable strategic partnerships and strengthen local leadership and organizational capacity.
- Position World Renew as a trusted implementer, convener, intermediary, and advocate.
- Lead a diversified regional resource-development strategy and cultivate institutional and philanthropic funding relationships.
- Work with country and global teams to develop competitive multi-country and country-level opportunities.
- Align resources with strategy and strengthen the financial sustainability of programs, partnerships, and operations.

**C. People and Culture Leadership**

- Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and ongoing support to Country Directors and Regional Staff, strengthening accountability, and effectiveness.
- Build a Christ-centered, inclusive, accountable, learning-oriented, and high-performing team culture.
- Promote staff wellbeing and spiritual formation by fostering a supportive, Christ-centered work environment that encourages healthy practices, connection, reflection, and spiritual growth.
- Ensure effective performance management, leadership development, succession planning, and onboarding.

**D. Operational Leadership and Organizational Change**

- Ensure Country Offices and partners receive appropriate programmatic, technical, operational, financial, safeguarding, security, and people support.
- Lead changes to country presence, structures, partnership models, and ways of working through sound analysis, consultation, communication, and change management.

**E. Risk, Compliance, Safety, and Safeguarding**

- Maintain effective oversight of enterprise and program risk, humanitarian standards, donor and government compliance, safeguarding, staff safety and security, crisis readiness, and asset protection.
- Ensure risks are identified, managed, escalated, and reported, particularly in fragile, conflict-affected, sanctioned, or restricted environments.

**F. Financial Stewardship and Accountability**

- Oversee regional budgets, forecasts, financial performance, audits, authorizations, and corrective action in collaboration with the Chief Program and Implementation Officer and Chief Financial and Information Officer.
- Hold senior leaders accountable for program performance, responsible stewardship, and compliance.

**G. Organizational Leadership**

- Contribute regional perspectives and leadership to World Renew-wide strategy, committees, communities of practice, and cross-functional priorities.
- Strengthen collaboration between country, regional, humanitarian, technical, fundraising, communications, finance, and people functions.

**Additional Responsibilities**

- Perform other duties as assigned.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

This position will supervise Country Directors and designated regional staff and provide matrixed oversight to other country and regional positions.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

1. An actively practicing Christian who participates in a local Christian community, demonstrating a strong personal commitment to Christ. Understands that this role serves the mission of His Kingdom and is dedicated to embodying and promoting Integral Mission in all aspects of the work and context.
2. Demonstrated strategic leadership and judgment, with the ability to set direction, lead organizational change, make decisions amid uncertainty, and manage a complex multi-country portfolio.
3. Demonstrated servant leadership, coaching, performance management, team development, and culturally intelligent leadership across diverse and distributed teams.
4. Deep understanding of partner-led and community-led development, localization, equitable partnership, participatory methods, and the role of churches and civil society in holistic transformation.
5. Strong knowledge of integrated humanitarian and development programming, including fragile and conflict-affected settings, disaster risk reduction, resilience, peacebuilding, and the humanitarian development and peace nexus.
6. Sound understanding of program quality, monitoring, evaluation, research and learning, safeguarding, community accountability, humanitarian principles, the Core Humanitarian Standard, and evidence-informed decision-making.
7. Proven ability to build influential relationships and represent an organization with donors, governments, churches, partners, networks, and senior stakeholders in politically and religiously sensitive settings.
8. Demonstrated resource-mobilization capability across institutional, bilateral, multilateral, foundation, philanthropic, church, and private funding sources.
9. Strong financial, operational, compliance, risk, safety, and security oversight, including experience supervising annual budgets exceeding USD $10 million.
10. Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation, diplomacy, conflict-management, and cross-cultural collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a global matrixed organization.
11. Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, belonging, gender equality, justice, safeguarding, and respectful leadership.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:**

- A Master’s degree in or equivalent advanced degree in fields like international development, humanitarian studies, economics, social sciences, organizational development, public administration, project planning or a related field is required.
- Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible leadership in humanitarian and development work, including substantial regional or multi-country oversight.
- Significant cross-cultural leadership experience in Asia, preferably in at least two countries in South or Southeast Asia. Experience in the Middle East and in fragile or conflict-affected states is a strong asset.
- Experience in one or more of World Renew’s core programming areas, including food security, sustainable livelihoods, maternal and child health, disaster risk reduction, humanitarian response, peacebuilding, and justice.
- Prior experience in humanitarian and emergency contexts, including program design, response management, and implementation, is a strong asset.
- Previous Country Director experience is preferred; Regional Leadership experience would be a strong advantage.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**

Fluency in English, with excellent written, verbal, presentation, and advocacy skills. Knowledge of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or West Asian language is an asset.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Extended time spent in front of a computer screen using electronic mail, writing proposals, reviewing data, and reports, and meeting teams virtually across multiple time zones.

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This role is expected to operate on an in-office schedule of at least 2 - 3 days within the Regional Director’s country office location, in coordination with the Country Director to ensure consistent on-site leadership coverage; the position also requires periodic travel to countries within the region on a planned and recurring basis.

title: Senior Core Services Caseworker
body:
***This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.***

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview:** The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Client Intake, Assessment & Planning**

- Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
- Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
- Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.

**Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination**

- Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
- Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
- Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.

**Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management**

- Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
- Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
- Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
- Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
- Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.

**Home Visits & Community Integration**

- Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
- Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.

**Financial Assistance & Budgeting**

- Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
- Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
- Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.

**Documentation & Reporting**

- Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
- Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
- Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.

**Collaboration & Relationship Building**

- Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
- Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
- Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.

**Client Education & Workshops**

- Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
- Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.

**Supervision & Volunteer Engagement**

- Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
- Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.

**Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety**

- Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
- Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
- Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.

**Transportation & Logistics**

- Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
- Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.

**Job Requirements:**

**Preference:** Bilingual or multilingual candidates are strongly preferred. Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the client population is a plus.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- **Required:** Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the human services field.
- **Preferred:** Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant communities.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- **Relationship Building & Networking:** Proven ability to build and maintain effective internal and external relationships through strong diplomacy, communication, and collaboration skills.
- **Cross-Cultural Communication:** Demonstrated success in working and communicating in a multicultural environment.
- **Initiative & Problem-Solving:** Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of managing multiple tasks, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines efficiently.
- **Detail-Oriented:** Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
- **Digital & Technical Skills:** Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and skilled in using the internet and digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving.
- **Transportation:** Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $24.10-$25.37/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Consultoría Veterinaria para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en el Sur del Lago, estado Zulia– DRC Venezuela
body:
**1. Antecedentes**

El Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una organización humanitaria internacional que trabaja en más de 40 países. Brinda protección y asistencia a personas refugiadas, desplazadas internas, retornadas, migrantes y comunidades de acogida, siguiendo los principios humanitarios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

DRC Venezuela opera desde Caracas y cinco bases: Maracaibo, Guasdualito, Carúpano, Sur del Lago y La Guaira. En el estado Zulia, DRC implementa acciones de preparación frente a los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño en los municipios de Colón, Catatumbo y La Guajira, donde la agricultura y la ganadería constituyen medios de vida fundamentales. Los análisis climáticos y las consultas comunitarias realizadas en 2026 evidencian una disminución de las fuentes de agua, el deterioro de los pastizales, el aumento de la salinidad (Guajira) y mayores dificultades para mantener la producción agropecuaria, generando riesgos para la seguridad alimentaria y los ingresos de los hogares rurales.

Las comunidades identificaron una afectación creciente sobre los rebaños bovinos, ovinos y caprinos, reflejada en pérdida de condición corporal, reducción de la producción y mayor vulnerabilidad a enfermedades asociadas al estrés hídrico y nutricional. En respuesta, DRC desarrollará acciones anticipatorias para fortalecer la salud animal mediante campañas de vacunación y desparasitación, suplementación vitamínica y mineral, evaluación sanitaria de rebaños y capacitación para reducir los efectos negativos del niño sobre sus ganados y animales traspatio, con el fin de proteger los activos productivos y la resiliencia de las familias más expuestas a los efectos de la sequía.

**2. Objetivos**

**Objetivo general:**

Fortalecer las capacidades de los hogares productores de los municipios Colón y Catatumbo del estado Zulia para la protección y manejo adecuado de sus activos pecuarios, mediante acciones de asistencia técnica, formación e implementación de medidas preventivas de sanidad animal que contribuyan a la sostenibilidad de sus medios de vida frente a los efectos de la sequía.

**Objetivos específicos:**

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario**, mediante diagnósticos de campo que permitan determinar la elegibilidad de los hogares y el estado sanitario de sus animales, de acuerdo con los criterios establecidos por DRC.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva**, dirigido a pequeños productores u hogares que poseen cría de animales para la subsistencia (auto-consumo), abordando temas relacionados con alimentación animal en condiciones de sequía, suplementación nutricional, vacunación, desparasitación, bioseguridad y otras medidas para la protección de los medios de vida pecuarios.
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio**, incluyendo actividades de evaluación sanitaria, vacunación, desparasitación y orientación técnica a productores, contribuyendo a mejorar la salud animal y la capacidad de recuperación de los hogares frente a los impactos de la sequía.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**, que documente la implementación de las actividades, los principales logros alcanzados, las mejoras observadas en las capacidades de los hogares participantes y las recomendaciones para el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de los medios de vida pecuarios frente a eventos climáticos adversos.

**3. Alcance del trabajo**

La consultoría cubre los siguientes componentes:

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario.** Meta: Evaluar al menos a 110 hogares, para seleccionar 90 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base). Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva.** Meta: 1. Diseñar un programa formativo de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo. 2. Brindar formación a al menos 3 grupos de 30 personas, para un total de 90 personas formadas. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar la formación
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio.** Metas: Brindar jornadas veterinarias a los 90 participantes seleccionados en el programa. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para la formación de los participantes.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**.Metas: 1. Aplicar una línea de salida a los participantes (74 encuestas) 2. Elaborar 1 informe técnico de resultados. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio para realizar línea de salida puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes

Nota: la persona consultora no tendrá que cubrir los costos de traslados a las comunidades ni la adquisición de materiales formativos, toda vez que serán cubiertos por DRC.

A su vez, la lista de personas pre-identificadas a diagnosticar será proporcionada por el equipo de Recuperación Económica de DRC.

**4. Productos esperados**

Los productos se entregan de forma progresiva durante el contrato, según las prioridades que fije el Líder de recuperación económica con el Gerente de base. Los plazos y productos son indicativos y se cuentan desde la firma del contrato.

1. Diagnóstico inicial y plan de trabajo con estimación de horas por componente. Semana 1.
2. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario. Semanas 2-4.
3. Diseñar un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva de forma general y con énfasis en situaciones de altas temperaturas a fenómenos asociados (El Niño). Semanas 5-6.
4. Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio. Semanas 6-8.
5. Impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Semanas 9-12.
6. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados. emanas 13-16.

**5. Dedicación, modalidad y supervisión**

- **Período:** desde la firma del contrato, prevista para noviembre de 2026, hasta febrero de 2027. Puede extenderse por enmienda según necesidades y presupuesto.
- **Dedicación:** por horas, según las necesidades del Gerente de base y Líder de Recuperación Económica. El total no puede superar **640 horas**, DRC no garantiza un mínimo de horas.
- **Modalidad:** Presencial. El consultor deberá trasladarse con el equipo de DRC a las comunidades de intervención del proyecto, en el cronograma acordado con la oficina de la base de DRC.
- **Supervisión:** Gerente de base. La coordinación diaria es con la Líder de equipo de Recuperación Económica. También habrá coordinación con Supply cuando aplique\*\*.\*\*
- **Recursos que aporta DRC:** acceso a la documentación interna necesaria, costos de traslado a comunidades y material didáctico requerido. La persona consultora usa su propio equipo y conexión, así como la propiedad intelectual del desarrollo de las formaciones.

**6. Perfil requerido**

Requisitos obligatorios

- Profesional universitario en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería en Producción Animal, Biología o carreras afines relacionadas con la producción pecuaria y la sanidad animal.
- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional comprobable en el diseño, implementación o acompañamiento de proyectos vinculados a la sanidad animal, producción pecuaria, extensión rural o fortalecimiento de medios de vida agropecuarios.
- Experiencia en la ejecución de jornadas veterinarias preventivas, incluyendo vacunación, desparasitación, evaluación sanitaria y manejo de especies pecuarias como bovinos, caprinos, porcinos, ovinos y aves de traspatio.
- Experiencia en el desarrollo e implementación de procesos de formación y asistencia técnica dirigidos a productores agropecuarios, organizaciones comunitarias o promotores locales.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en enfoques de adaptación al cambio climático y gestión de riesgos en sistemas productivos agropecuarios, incluyendo medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de los medios de vida rurales frente a eventos climáticos extremos.
- Experiencia de trabajo de campo con comunidades rurales, poblaciones vulnerables, personas desplazadas, migrantes, refugiadas y/o comunidades de acogida.
- Capacidad demostrada para facilitar procesos participativos, relacionarse con diversos actores comunitarios e institucionales, coordinar actividades en terreno y trabajar de manera efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Habilidades para la elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de resultados y presentación de recomendaciones derivadas de procesos de diagnóstico, capacitación y asistencia técnica.
- Disponibilidad para iniciar en noviembre de 2026 y trasladarse a las comunidades de los municipios indicados, de preferencia en horarios de la mañana.

Requisitos deseables

- Experiencia previa de trabajo con organizaciones humanitarias, agencias de cooperación internacional o programas de recuperación temprana y resiliencia.
- Conocimiento de los sistemas productivos pecuarios predominantes en el estado Zulia o en otras zonas rurales de Venezuela.

**7. Contenido y presentación de la oferta**

Las ofertas deben incluir:

1. **CV** de la persona consultora, con tres referencias profesionales verificables.
2. Propuesta de contenido formativo (preliminar), detallando la siguiente información: - Número de módulo, - Nombre de la sesión, - Contenido a abordar propuesto, - Horas requeridas, - Total horas, -Material didáctico requerido.
3. **Oferta financiera:** tarifa diaria en USD, **todo incluido** (honorarios, impuestos, equipo, conexión y cualquier otro costo), por una jornada de 8 horas.
