5\. Voice for health equity – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

• Lead and manage the Procurement Team, setting priorities, allocating responsibilities, overseeing performance and providing technical guidance and support to ensure effective and timely delivery of procurement services in line with WHO policies and Country Office priorities.  
• Lead procurement planning and strategic sourcing, analysing programme and operational requirements, consolidating forecasts and developing procurement plans and sourcing strategies that consider available resources, market conditions, delivery timelines and operational risks  
• Provide professional procurement advice and guidance to programme and requesting units on procurement strategies, specifications, sourcing options, evaluation criteria and procurement methods, including for complex and time-critical requirements.  
• Oversee the procurement cycle, ensuring transparent, competitive and compliant processes. Lead or provide technical oversight of complex, high-value, sensitive or time-critical procurement exercises, including market assessments, solicitations, evaluations, negotiations and recommendations for award, within delegated authority.  
• Coordinate procurement operations with programme, finance, logistics and other relevant functions at all three levels (Headquarters, Regional Office, Country Office) to ensure alignment of requirements, funding, approvals and delivery arrangements. Facilitate the resolution of procurement-related operational issues and provide technical oversight of procurement of services undertaken by other units, as assigned.  
• Monitor supplier and contract performance, address delays and non-conformities, maintain records of corrective action and escalate material performance, integrity or operational risks.  
• Provide procurement advice during emergency response and other time-critical operations while safeguarding competition, transparency, value for money, quality and compliance.  
• Ensure procurement governance, risk management and performance monitoring, promoting compliance with WHO policies, internal controls, ethical standards and delegated authorities. Monitor performance and risks, maintain audit-ready records and ensure follow-up on audit and oversight recommendations.  
• Promote procurement capacity and continuous improvement through guidance and knowledge-sharing with team members and requesting units, and contribute to regional and global procurement initiatives and standardization efforts.  
• Contribute to regional and global procurement networks, category strategies, standardization initiatives and continuous improvement of procurement processes.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A first university degree (Bachelor's level) in business administration, management, public administration, procurement, logistics, supply-chain management, law, economics, or a field relevant to the functions of the position.

**Desirable:** Advance university degree (Master's level) in one of the above, or Professional procurement certification, such as CIPS or an equivalent internationally recognized qualification; additional training in contract management, category management, logistics or emergency supply operations.

### Experience

**Essential:** At least five years' experience, some of which in an international context, working in the area of procurement and logistics services.

**Desirable:** Experience in the United Nations system, another international organization, government or a large multinational organization; experience in emergency or fragile settings; experience procuring health commodities, medical equipment, infrastructure, vehicles or related services.

### Functional Skills

• Excellent knowledge of procurement principles, competitive sourcing, tendering, contracting and supplier management in public-sector or international organizations.  
• Sound knowledge of procurement planning, market and cost analysis, contract administration and procurement risk management.  
• Ability to manage complex and time-critical procurement activities, exercise sound judgement and ensure compliance, including in emergency settings.  
• Strong analytical, drafting, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills, including proficiency in ERP and e-procurement systems.  
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multicultural environment. Emotional intelligence and the ability to identify and manage one’s own emotions while supporting constructive working relationships with others.

### Other Skills (e.g. IT)

Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office applications. Practical proficiency in ERP/e-procurement systems, data analysis and procurement tracking tools is highly desirable.

### WHO Competencies

Teamwork  
Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences  
Communication  
Moving forward in a changing environment  
Creating an empowering and motivating environment

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - Procurement Specialist (2605119)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2605119&tz=GMT%2B02%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

title: Administrateur terrain H/F – Tillabéry - NIGER
body:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées surla proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

- Le patient et la patiente d’abord
- Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
- Responsabilité et liberté
- Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
- Faire confiance
- L’intelligence collective
- La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER - ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Ethiopie, Haïti, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Sénégal, Mauritanie et Soudan.

**TYPOLOGIE DU POSTE**

**CONTEXTE DU PROJET :**

**Description du projet :**

Fondée en 2009, ALIMA est présente au Niger aux côtés de son partenaire local l’ONG nigérienne BEFEN « le Bien Être de la Femme et de l’Enfant au Niger » depuis sa création. En effet, le tout premier projet d’ALIMA a été mis en œuvre au Niger, dans le district de Mirriah, région de Zinder. ALIMA possède une grande expérience dans la réponse aux épidémies (Diphtérie, Méningite, Rougeole, Choléra et COVID-19), la nutrition, la santé primaire et maternelle, les VBG (violences basées sur le genre) ainsi que le WASH (eau, assainissement et hygiène).

Il s’agit de :

1\. Un projet en consortium avec plusieurs ONG - ALIMA/ BEFEN met en œuvre le volet Santé Nutrition, ACF met en œuvre les activités WASH ; Agriculture et sécurité alimentaire et l’ONG DIKO le volet protection).

Dont l’objectif est : D'améliorer l'accès aux soins de santé communautaires, primaires, secondaires et nutritionnels pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que pour les femmes enceintes et allaitantes parmi les personnes déplacées et les communautés d'accueil, touchées par la crise dans les districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré.

En résumé : projet consiste en la mise en œuvre d’un programme de 30 mois qui se concentre sur la fourniture d'une réponse multisectorielle adaptée aux besoins les plus urgents des personnes déplacées et des communautés d'accueil vivant dans les zones d'intervention ciblées, tout en garantissant un environnement sûr pour tous.

Cette intervention met en œuvre des activités dans les secteurs de la Santé ; Nutrition ; WASH ; Agriculture et sécurité alimentaire ; pratique de réduction des risques de catastrophes (DRPP) ; et Protection. Toutes les interventions sont menées dans les mêmes zones définies dans le cadre du projet afin de garantir la multisectorialité de chaque action. La protection est intégrée dans l'ensemble de l’intervention afin de garantir une approche "sans préjudice". Les bénéficiaires sont constitués des populations déplacées et hôtes dans les zones d'intervention, avec une attention particulière pour les secteurs de la santé, de la nutrition et de la protection des enfants de moins de cinq ans et des femmes enceintes et allaitantes.

Objectif général : Contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité des populations hôtes et déplacées dans la région de Tillabéry (districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré) par une réponse d'urgence intégrée

**Objectifs spécifiques :**

Améliorer l'accès aux soins de santé communautaires, primaires et secondaires pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que pour les femmes enceintes et allaitantes parmi les personnes déplacées et les communautés d'accueil, affectées par la crise dans le district de Say, Téra et Bankilaré.

Améliorer l'accès à des soins nutritionnels de qualité pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans affectés par la crise dans les zones d'intervention de ce projet.

Durée du projet : 30 mois (Initialement 24 mois avec 6 mois Cost Extension obtenue à compter de Août 2025)

Zone d’intervention : les Districts Sanitaires de Téra (4 aires de santé), Say (6 AS et 1 HD) et Bankilaré (2 AS et 1 HD) – Région de Tillabéry

Bénéficiaires : 212 199 bénéficiaires directs (population hôte et déplacée interne)

Partenariat : 3 ONG ALIMA-BEFEN (Santé- Nutrition), ACF (WASH, SAME et Nutrition com) et DIKO (Protection)

Mots clés : soins de santé primaire et secondaire, Nutrition, PCIME-co

2\. Un projet de Réponse d’urgence pour l’accès et l’amélioration des soins de santé des populations affectées par un choc et la contribution à la réduction de la morbi-mortalité infantile dans les régions de Tillabéry (Abala, Banibangou et Ayerou), Tahoua, Maradi et Zinder

**En Résumé :**

Ce projet a pour objectif de réduire la morbi-mortalité des populations hôtes et déplacées affectées par les crises humanitaires dans les districts sanitaires (DS) d’Abala, Ayorou, Banibangou, Tchintabaraden, Tilia et Tassara, Guidan Roumdji et Madarounfa, à travers 3 axes :

I) Le renforcement du mécanisme de veille humanitaire et sanitaire et une réponse rapide, gratuite et de qualité, aux crises et urgences, adaptée aux besoins évalués dans le cadre des interventions RRM (R1)

II) Un renforcement de l’accès aux soins et une prise en charge (PEC) médico-nutritionnelle gratuite et de qualité via un appui ponctuel aux CSI, le soutien aux HD, et le déploiement de cliniques mobiles (R2)

III) Une évaluation et une réponse d’urgence immédiate et gratuite, en cas de crise sanitaire et humanitaire soudaine dans des zones couvertes et/ou non couvertes par le projet (R3)

**Objectif Spécifique :** Assurer un accès gratuit et de qualité aux soins de santé à travers un mécanisme de réponse rapide, un support aux structures de santé primaire et secondaire, incluant l'accès à la prise en charge MAS, aux populations déplacées et hôtes affectées par les conflits des DS de Abala, Ayorou, Banibangou, Tassara, Tillia, Tchinta, Madarounfa, Guidan Roumdji et de Matameye et tout autre district ayant subi un choc.

**Durée de l'action (en mois) :** 36 mois

**Zone d’intervention :** Tillabéry : 3 HD, 5 CSI et 2 cliniques mobiles. (Abala : 1 HD, 3 CSI, et 1 clinique mobile, Ayorou : 1 HD, 2 CSI et 1 clinique mobile, Banibangou :1 HD)..

**LIEU DU POSTE :** TILLABERI

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

**Niveau 3 :** Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

- Il/elle rend compte au Coordinateur de Terrain (responsable hiérarchique), et au coordinateur finances et RH (responsables techniques).
- Il/elle encadre des assistants administrateur des terrains (AYIROU ABALA et Manibangu ).

**MISSION PRINCIPALE**

L’administrateur terrain a pour objectif général d’assurer la gestion des ressources humaines, financières et de mettre en place les éléments de gestion utilisés sur les projets.

Il/elle est responsable d’une part, d’organiser la gestion administrative du personnel (national et international) et d’en superviser la gestion qualitative, et d’autre part, de décliner, valoriser et gérer les moyens financiers nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des décisions opérationnelles.

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

L’ administrateur trice projet doit , avant tout, doit:

- agir en lien avec le mandat d’ALIMA, les principes humanitaires et le principe de “do no harm / ne pas nuire”.
- Respecter la stratégie opérationnelle définie avec les autres coordinateurs (collaborer avec les autres acteurs humanitaires, internationaux et gouvernementaux présents dans la zone d’intervention.

**Comptabilité**

- Mise en œuvre des procédures : sécurité de l’argent (gestion des caisses, des transferts, des avances), engagement des dépenses (procédures d’achats, validation et organisation des paiements, suivi des paiements réguliers)
- Mise en œuvre du guide d’imputation pays (codes comptables, projets et axes analytiques, codes bailleurs
- Gestion des caisses et banques de son projet
- Enregistrement comptable (en propre ou délégué à un assistant administrateur), classement des pièces comptables, Checker/Comparer les écritures comptables par rapport au tableau d’affectation et réalisation de la clôture terrain mensuelle, envoi en capitale
- Réception des comptabilités corrigées par la capitale, analyse des écarts, actions correctives.

**Gestion de la trésorerie**

- Suivi des soldes bancaires et caisses sur le projet
- Connaissance du circuit d’approvisionnement, analyse des risques
- Anticipation des dépenses et demande de trésorerie mensuelle.
- Proposition des soldes minimum nécessaires sur chaque caisse et banque du projet

**Gestion générale des moyens**

- Gestion adéquate des structures (choix, organisation, contrats, intendance, assurance,).
- Participation à l’élaboration du cadre d’approvisionnement pour ses terrains.
- Récolte et analyse des informations de gestion non budgétaires (activités, consommations, donations, etc.).
- En lien avec les coordinateurs, création et analyse d’indicateurs de gestion des ressources.
- Tenue à jour de l’archivage administratif de la mission.

**Gestion budgétaire**

- Récolte, pour chaque activité définie, de toutes les informations nécessaires concernant les activités et les ressources
- Participation, sous la responsabilité du Coordinateur Finances et RH et du Coordinateur Terrain, à la mise en forme et la traduction budgétaire des éléments de gestion de ressources
- Analyse, en lien avec le Coordinateur Terrain, des suivis budgétaires mensuels généraux et spécifiques (axes analytiques), alertes éventuelles, propositions d’actions correctives, et reporting auprès du Coordinateur Finances et RH.
- Élaborer le prévisionnel de son projet par contrat de financement et suivre, Alerter le Coordinateur en cas de Gap.

**Gestion administrative du personnel national**

- Suivi et mise à jour de la paye et des dossiers du personnel (Homère).
- Veille, sous la responsabilité du coordinateur Finances et RH à la diffusion des documents, de référence RH au personnel et en assure le respect des principes, (règlement intérieur, procédure de gestion des abus…)

**Gestion qualitative du personnel**

**Composition des équipes**

- Mise à jour des organigrammes.
- Aide à la réalisation des descriptions de postes et s’assure de leur mise à jour.

**Bilans individuels**

- Planification des bilans.
- Mise à disposition des équipes des documents nécessaires pour la réalisation des bilans.
- Elaborer un planning de congé annuel de son projet
- Elaborer un plan de formation de son projet

**Communication interne et représentation du personnel**

- Diffusion de l’information du personnel sur l’association et la mission.
- Organisation des réunions du personnel.

**Recrutement**

- Soutien aux coordinateurs concernant le recrutement (processus, entretien, etc.).

**EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES**

 **Expérience**

- Expérience préalable à un poste équivalent en ONG Internationale.
- Expérience préalable dans contextes d’urgence.
- Une qualification dans la gestion RH et administrative est un atout
- Expérience préalable en gestion d’équipe multiculturelle.

**Compétences**

- Capacité d’écoute et empathie.
- Communication facile.
- Animation et motivation d’équipes.
- Capacité à identifier et anticiper les problèmes et les risques.
- Esprit orienté vers la résolution de problèmes.
- Organisation des rôles et délégation de tâches au sein d’une équipe.
- Capacité à définir des priorités.
- Établissement de réseaux de contacts et capacité à maintenir une posture neutre face à des acteurs opposés dans le cadre d’un même conflit armé.
- Autonomie.
- Sens des responsabilités.
- Capacité de prise d’initiative et de décision.
- Bonne gestion du stress.
- Flexibilité.
- Maîtrise de l’outil informatique (GSuite et pack office).

**Langues :**

- La maîtrise orale et écrite du français est indispensable

**CONDITIONS**

**Durée et type de contrat** : CDD de droit français de 6 à 12 mois renouvelable

**Prise de poste** : asap

**Salaire** : Selon grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem

ALIMA prend en charge :

- Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
- Les frais d’hébergement
- La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de
- Mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
- L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droits

title: Consultant en accompagnement technique et institutionnel des partenaires nationaux
body:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a pour objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociaux les plus vulnérables.

## **Introduction et conditions de la mission**

**Dans le cadre de ses engagements stratégiques pour la "Localisation de l'aide humanitaire", et grâce au financement crucial octroyé par le Sahel Regional Fund (SRF)**, INTERSOS a initié et s'est engagé de manière résolue dans un processus structuré et progressif de transfert de compétences, de connaissances, et, surtout, de leadership aux acteurs et organisations de la société civile locale au Tchad. Cet engagement vise à renforcer l'autonomie et la pérennité de l'action humanitaire menée par les entités nationales.

Ce processus de renforcement se base sur un diagnostic conjoint et les besoins exprimés par chaque partenaire, qui a permis d’élaborer des plans de renforcement des capacités (PRC) sur mesure établis et validés conjointement. Ces plans constituent la feuille de route du projet *ResiSila*, lequel a été officiellement lancé en juillet 2025.

Trois organisations nationales clés ont été sélectionnées pour ce partenariat stratégique :

1. **SECADEV** (Secrétariat Catholique pour le Développement), reconnue pour son vaste réseau communautaire et son expérience dans les domaines de la sécurité alimentaire, de la santé et de l'eau, hygiène et assainissement (EHA).
2. **ADESOH** (Association pour le Développement Social et Humanitaire), spécialisée dans la résilience et la protection des populations vulnérables.
3. **ACCCIA** (Association Tchadienne pour la Coordination et la Coopération Internationale des Actions Humanitaires), un acteur clé dans la lutte contre le changement climatique et l'insécurité alimentaire à l’est du pays.

L'objectif à terme de *ResiSila* est de permettre à ces partenaires d'assumer pleinement la direction et la mise en œuvre des programmes, garantissant ainsi une réponse humanitaire plus pertinente, plus efficace et durable, en parfaite adéquation avec les principes de Grand Bargain et de la localisation de l'aide.

### **Modalités de soumission :**

- **Condition de candidature**. Les candidatures, qu’elles soient présentées par des consultants individuels ou des cabinets, doivent couvrir l'ensemble des objectifs du projet et être en mesure d’assurer une expertise sur l’ensemble des thématiques. Les binômes incluant expertise internationale et locale seront les bienvenus.
- **Approche combinée :** Bien que certaines sessions de formation puissent être conjointes pour favoriser l'apprentissage mutuel, l'accompagnement doit impérativement être adapté aux besoins spécifiques et individuels de chaque organisation.
- **Méthodologie d'impact :** Le consultant/le bureau des consultants doit dépasser le cadre de la formation classique en intégrant des techniques d'autonomisation durable telles que le partage, adaptation et implémentation d'outils et politiques, le mentorat et le coaching de proximité.
- **Présence géographique :** Le travail peut être conduit soit exclusivement en présentiel soit alterné (à distance et sur place), dans ce deuxième cas le consultant/le cabinet des consultants, devra expliquer dans l’offre technique comment l’appui sera structuré et la durée envisagée de la présence physique ou à distance. Les interventions en présentiel se dérouleront dans les bureaux de **N'Djamena** et dans la **province du Sila**.
- L’offre technique devrait préciser les besoins en matière de dispositions logistiques nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des activités, notamment lorsque ces dispositions doivent être organisées ou prises en charge par l’organisation et ne peuvent être assurées directement par les consultants.
- **Durée :** L’appui pour les TDR doit s'étendre sur une durée **minimale de 8 mois et maximale de 12 mois**.

## **Objectifs de la consultance**

 Afin de renforcer les capacités institutionnelles des organisations, l'accompagnement s'articulera autour de trois thématiques prioritaires: la gestion des subventions et de la collecte de fonds, la gestion du cycle de projet, ainsi que le suivi, l'évaluation, la redevabilité et l'apprentissage (MEAL). Le parcours de renforcement devra couvrir l'ensemble de ces trois volets, tout en adaptant le niveau d'accompagnement au profil et aux besoins spécifiques de chaque organisation partenaire.

### **Objectifs liés à la gestion des subventions et collecte de fonds**

- Développer une stratégie de levée de fonds structurée et diversifiée pour réduire la dépendance aux financements uniques.
- Renforcer la maîtrise des exigences de conformité des bailleurs de fonds.
- Améliorer les outils de reporting financier et le suivi rigoureux des subventions.
- Appuyer les partenaires dans l’identification d’opportunités de financement et dans la soumission de propositions compétitives (minimum 2 par organisations).

### **Objectifs liés à la planification et gestion du cycle de projet** 

- Améliorer les systèmes de planification, de suivi d'implémentation et de pilotage stratégique au niveau central.
- Renforcer les capacités des chefs de projet sur toutes les étapes du cycle de vie des projets (conception, risques, suivi financier).

### **Objectifs liés à suivi, évaluation, redevabilité et apprentissage (MEAL)**

- Développer des outils standardisés pour collecter, analyser et utiliser les données de manière autonome.
- Intégrer les retours des parties prenantes (redevabilité) dans la gestion programmatique.
- Améliorer l’analyse et l’apprentissage sur la base des leçons apprises.

## **Méthodologie et livrables**

Dans le cadre de cet accompagnement, le consultant/cabinet des consultants sera chargé de contribuer à l’ensemble des objectifs à travers les missions suivantes:

- Analyse du portefeuille actuel et des lacunes en mobilisation et gestion
- Analyse de la coordination inter-départementale actuelle
- Diagnostic des systèmes de gestion des données existants.
- Identification de solutions adaptées et accessibles selon le profil et niveau de chaque organisation

**Livrables :** À l’issue de cet accompagnement, le consultant/le bureau de consultants sera amené à produire les livrables suivants:

- Stratégie de levée de fonds formalisée par partenaire, outils de suivi de conformité, fiches bailleurs, propositions soumises avec l’accompagnement du cabinet/consultant
- Outils de pilotage (type PAT - Project Appraisal Tool - modèle partagé par INTERSOS) adoptés, guides de gestion de projet internes, et plans de suivi centralisés
- Base de données fonctionnelle, outils MEAL (Kobo, tableurs) créés, et procédures de collecte établies.

## **Profil du consultant ou du cabinet des consultants**

Les candidats devront justifier de l’ensemble des compétences et expertises suivantes:

- Spécialiste en accompagnement de OSC dans la mobilisation de ressources (**min. 5 ans d'expérience**) avec une connaissance approfondie des bailleurs internationaux (ECHO, UE, Agences ONU).
- Spécialiste en accompagnement de OSC dans la gestion de projets, ou gestionnaire de programme senior avec une expertise prouvée en outils de pilotage stratégique et coordination.
- Spécialiste en accompagnement de OSC dans la gestion de systèmes de Suivi et évaluation ou spécialiste MEAL avec une maîtrise des outils numériques de collecte et d'analyse.

## **Calendrier et modalités (8 à 12 mois)** 

Le consultant/le cabinet des consultants proposera son propre chronogramme, en précisant pour chaque activité si celle-ci sera réalisée en présentiel ou à distance. Le chronogramme devra ainsi distinguer clairement les activités en présentiel des activités à distance.

## **Budget:**

Le budget total disponible pour cette prestation est plafonné à **30 000 euros**. Les candidat(e)s / cabinets sont invité(e)s à soumettre une proposition financière détaillée (incluant les honoraires, frais de déplacement, per diem et autres coûts logistiques) n'excédant pas ce montant.

title: Endline Evaluation Consultant
body:
**Background Information on Plan International**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child, but this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination, and its girls who are most affected. Working together with children, young people, our supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges facing girls and all vulnerable children.

We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood, and we enable children to prepare for – and respond to – crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge. We have been building powerful partnerships for children for over 80 years and are now active in more than 75 countries.

Read more about Plan International's Global Strategy: 100 Million Reasons at [https://plan-international.org/strategy](https://plan-international.org/strategy)

**Summary of the Requirement**

The ASPIRE Project intends to conduct an Endline Evaluation in Bauchi and Sokoto states. The evaluation will use a mixed-methods approach to establish endline values for approved project indicators (see table ToR) and assess the project’s relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence, impact and sustainability. The evaluation will measure progress against the project’s approved results framework, assess key achievements and lessons learned, and examine the contribution of project interventions to outcomes in sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender equality, mental health, child protection and women’s empowerment.

The findings will provide evidence on the overall performance of the ASPIRE Project and support accountability, organisational learning, future programme design and the potential scale-up of successful approaches.

**Overview**

The ASPIRE Endline Evaluation will assess the project's contribution to improving SRHR, gender equality, mental health, child protection, and women's empowerment outcomes among adolescents and young people in Bauchi and Sokoto States. Using a mixed-methods approach, the evaluation will measure progress against project indicators, document key achievements and lessons learned, and assess the effectiveness, sustainability, and impact of interventions such as Champions of Change, School Health Clubs, MHPSS groups, VSLAs, Fathers' Forums, advocacy initiatives, and health system strengthening efforts. Findings will inform future programming, accountability, and scale-up of successful approaches.

**Project Description**  
ASPIRE is a five-year (from December 2021 to October 2027) Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (ASRHR) project implemented by Plan International Nigeria in partnership with respective governments and local Nigerian organizations, including Life Helper’s Initiative (LHI), Planned Parenthood Federation of Nigeria (PPFN), Women’s Rights Organizations (WROs), and Ministries of Health, Education, Women’s Affairs, Religious Affairs, and Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs. Aspire is supported by Plan International Canada and funded by Global Affairs Canada and individual Canadian donors.  
With the ultimate outcome of improving the realization of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW), including vulnerable populations, in Bauchi and Sokoto states, the project aims to reach 877 868 direct beneficiaries in ten LGAs of Bauchi and 23 LGAs in Sokoto state.  
The ASPIRE project adopts a feminist, rights-based, and multi-sectoral approach to address the interdependent pillars of demand, supply and accountability to improve the SRHR of adolescent girls and women. It uses tested modalities at the individual, community, and institutional levels to increase girls' agency and decision-making around SRHR, enhance the demand for and their utilization of Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services, and strengthen institutional accountability towards their rights. This will be achieved through three intermediate outcomes, as follows:  
1\. Demand: Increased individual and collective agency of women and adolescent girls in their diversity to exercise their SRHR and access to gender and adolescent responsive and inclusive Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services  
2\. Supply: Strengthened health systems to provide gender and adolescent-responsive, inclusive, integrated and innovative SRHR and protection services for women and adolescent girls  
3\. Accountability: Improved responsiveness of local stakeholders to provide evidence-based, integrated, accountable and equitable policies, legal frameworks and SRHR and protection services.

**Study Objectives**  
The consultancy firm will conduct a mixed-methods study to establish endline values for approved project indicators (see table 1 below) and assess the Aspire project’s relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, coherence, impact and sustainability, with a focus on accountability, learning and future programme design.  
Child Rights, Gender and Inclusion  
In line with Plan International’s values and organisational ambition, the evaluation should seek to prioritise a focus on child rights, gender and inclusion. As a minimum, this requires:

1. the disaggregation of all data points from the survey by age, sex, disability, marriage status and state,
2. the development of an ethics protocol that safeguards children, youth and vulnerable adults.

Endline findings will primarily be used:  
1\. By Plan International to demonstrate accountability for the funding received to the donor (Global Affairs Canada) and project beneficiaries  
2\. By partners and stakeholders in Nigeria such as government departments/ministries, local authorities, civil society organizations (CSOs), women right organizations (WROs), Youth led organizations (YLOs), service providers and communities to inform the wider understanding of AG&YW rights to SRHR, gender equality, and protection in the targeted LGAs.  
3\. By Global Affairs Canada that provided funding to the project, to ensure accountability and communication of its Global Impact.

**Scope of Work for the Consultancy**  
The consultancy firm under this ToR will act as the lead on all components of the endline study. In this role, the consultancy firm will be responsible for:  
1\. Obtaining research ethical approvals as per national and state guidelines, including paying special attention to the unique ethical considerations of doing studies/research with and about children and young people in general, and on highly sensitive topics (i.e. child protection issues including GBV, and ASRHR)  
2\. In consultation with Plan Canada and Plan Nigeria technical advisors, finalizing inception/design and sampling methodology, including verifying underlying data on the size of target groups.  
3\. In consultation with Plan Nigeria and Plan Canada develop secondary data collection and qualitative interview tools  
4\. Developing high-quality data collection guidelines and protocols  
5\. The review and implementation of baseline quantitative data collection tools on a digital platform, including supplying the required mobile devices and data collection platform storage server (such as ODK or Kobo). The consultancy firm should clearly state the proposed platform for data collection.  
6\. Translation of all tools into Hausa language and pilot test to ensure conduct content validity  
7\. Carrying out all recruitment, training, deployment and supervision of enumerators/data collectors, field supervisors required to complete the assignment efficiently.  
8\. Ensure high-quality research design and implementation with respect for child safeguarding principles; This includes working with Plan International to assess risks to children and young people and mitigating those safeguarding risks with integrated measures (i.e. in data protection strategies, in tool development, etc.)2  
9\. Leading the implementation of high-quality data collection with adequate field testing and supervision of all data collection and data entry. This includes working with Plan International to ensure quality data collection includes safeguarding approaches and measures in line with the Do No Harm principle and regularly communicating progress and sharing raw data throughout the data collection period.  
10\. Analyzing the collected data  
11\. Facilitating the validation of the evaluation results by making presentations to Plan staff and partners (separately)  
12\. Writing draft and final reports, as well as a short field report, and soliciting and incorporating all feedback from Plan International Nigeria and Plan Canada  
13\. Ensuring strict adherence to Plan International’s Global Safeguarding and PHSEA policies, procedures and guidelines at all stages of the study.  
14\. Ensure all training materials, original data collection forms, and hard copies of raw data are securely maintained and submitted to Plan International Nigeria with the final dataset;

**Methodology**  
This study includes a quantitative household survey of adolescent girls and young women (AG&YW) aged 15-24 in target LGAs of Bauchi and Sokoto state as well as a short checklist for health facilities in sampled study areas. The study also includes qualitative KIIand FGDs to assess the project’s effectiveness, impact, expected sustainability, and lessons learned. Plan Nigeria will provide the quantitative survey tools and will work in close collaboration with the consultancy firm on the development of qualitative tools. The consultancy firm will be responsible for proper adaptation, translation, field testing and preparation of final tools as part of the design of the complete study inception as described in this document.  
A high-level description of protocols of the study components is provided as follows.

**Project Indicators**  
Data for the indicators below will be collected from adolescent girls and young women (aged 15-24 years) through a household survey within project areas, as well as from sample health facilities. Plan International will provide a template for all data frequency and analysis tables.

**Sampling Methodology and sample size**  
The endline will employ a stratified random sampling strategy, with a sample size of AGYW 15-24 that is statistically powered for both age and state disaggregation (AGYW 15-19 and 20-24 in 10 LGAs in Bauchi and 23 in Sokoto). The total sample size is expected to be approximately 1800 AGYW (900 in Bauchi and 900 in Sokoto), though the consultancy firm will be required to verify estimated population figures and validate sample sizes to ensure that the sample is of a sufficient size to allow reasonable levels of certainty that the findings are generalizable of the target groups. This will include obtaining the most recent Nigeria population census numbers or official projections to estimate the proportion of AGYW in the above age brackets and estimate the likely distribution of a random sample of AGYW 15-24, into age brackets of 15-19 and 20-24. The same estimation should be made for marital status, though the study is not expected to be statistically powered for marital status.  
The qualitative study should include AGYW and to a lesser extent ABYM who participated in key interventions such as Champions of Change, School Health Clubs, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support groups, VSLAs and WGs; parents, and husbands of young women who participated in interventions such as Fathers’ Forums; health providers and administrators in PHCs with adolescent corners; local leaders and duty bearers; and other key intermediaries. The qualitative portion will primarily look at impact, effectiveness and expected sustainability, with a focus on lessons learned. In addition, the consultancy firm is expected to collect qualitative data on the experience of AGYW with disabilities, to better capture successes and lessons learned around inclusion.

The consultancy firm will be expected to help finalize the methodology, sampling approach and data collection tools, in close collaboration with Plan international Nigeria and Plan Canada technical advisors, coordinators and program managers to ensure alignment with donor expectations and comparability with baseline measurements.  
In addition, the endline study will require secondary data collection to support the interpretation of findings and to provide additional context. The consultancy firm should factor and plan for undertaking these reviews and include them into the report in collaboration and consultation with Plan International Nigeria.

**Ethics, Safeguarding and Data Protection**  
The consultancy firm is required to ensure that the endline meets all national and Global Ethical standards, such as protection of any vulnerable groups (including adolescent girls in this case). By Global Ethical Standards, this necessarily includes the special ethical considerations for doing research with or about children (under age 18) and young people (age 18-24), for example, as set out by UNICEF Innocenti’s ERIC (Ethical Research Involving Children) guidelines.  
The consultancy firm must coordinate with Plan International Nigeria to obtain and adhere to research ethical approval processes from a relevant authorized body from Sokoto and Bauchi states, as well as national level research ethics bodies where necessary, before commencement of data collection. The consultancy firm must clearly articulate all costs, timelines and deliverables associated with ethical submissions in the proposal.

Use age-appropriate informed consent and assent procedures, private and safe interviewing arrangements, and clear referral pathways.  
• Complete safeguarding and security risk assessments, including risks of distress, disclosure, retaliation, stigma, community backlash and re-identification.  
• Apply role-based access, encryption, secure transfer, retention and deletion arrangements, and immediately report any data breach or safeguarding concern through approved channels.  
• Ensure reasonable accommodation for participants with disabilities and safe participation of marginalised groups.  
• Declare any use of AI-assisted tools and provide evidence of data protection, human oversight, validation, bias checks and prohibition of uploading identifiable or sensitive participant data to unapproved services.

**Disclosure and Ownership of Information**  
It is understood and agreed that the consultancy firm shall, during and after the effective period of the contract, treat as confidential and not divulge, unless authorized in writing by Plan International Nigeria, any information obtained in the course of the performance of the Contract. Information will be made available for the consultants on a need-to-know basis. All required field visits will be facilitated by Plan International Nigeria staff.  
All ownership and copyright for final data collected and report produced during the endline study is held by Plan International. The consultancy firm shall treat as confidential and not divulge, unless authorized in writing by Plan International Nigeria, any information obtained during the performance of the assignment during and after the effective period of the contract. All raw, processed and analyzed data, including coded qualitative datasets, must be handed over to Plan International Nigeria and Plan Canada before the end of the contract.

Obligations regarding non-disclosure of information and intellectual property rights will be specified in the contract for this consulting mandate.

**Key Roles, Responsibilities and Management**  
The consultancy firm will report to a designated person (MERL Coordinator, project manager or project coordinator) at Plan International Nigeria.5 The consultancy firm will keep the designated person continually informed on the progress of the assignment through updates via in-person meetings, email and calls. The consultancy firm will also collaborate closely with the Plan International Canada M&E advisor or other key focal person, who will input and review design, data collection tools, data quality protocols and procedures to guide data collection6 and entry. Additionally, Plan International will provide feedback on raw data and guidance on data analysis, and will review and provide feedback on the draft data tables and the draft baseline report.  
The specific roles and responsibilities of the consultancy firm are as follows:  
• Validate the proposed sample sizes for the AG&YW survey and present an overall sampling methodology/strategy and timeline for data collection at the HH level.  
• Review relevant documents, including the PMF, the baseline study, detailed indicator analysis frameworks, key project reports and relevant secondary data sources  
• Review and refine quantitative data collection tools  
• Draft qualitative data collections tools and revise them based on feedback from Plan Nigeria and Plan Canada until there is an agreed upon version  
• Submit draft endline inception document to Plan International Nigeria, including all tools, workplans, data collection and verification protocols and gender, child protection, and safeguarding protocols.  
• Work closely with Plan International Nigeria and Plan International Canada teams to incorporate input and feedback on the inception report, including conducting virtual meetings as necessary.  
• Lead the completion of all ethical approval application documents, submissions and follow up with the research ethics boards at state and national levels (as necessary) until approval of the submission, working closely with Plan International Nigeria for any required input and support.  
• Recruit translators, enumerators/data collectors and field supervisors (as necessary), and data cleaning and quality assurance operators.  
• Arrange all logistics for transport of enumerators and field supervisors.  
• Design survey tools with digital (mobile) data collection technique using an appropriate platform to ensure quality, accuracy and timeliness of data collection, as well as data security  
• Prepare and conduct enumerator training, with support from Plan International Nigeria and the project team, including co-facilitation of a gender equality and child safeguarding component, ensuring that enumerators understand the safeguarding risks to child research participants and their role and responsibility in preventing and responding to any safeguarding concerns/issues. This includes ensuring that all members of the consultancy firm, data collectors, enumerators and supervisors sign the Plan International Nigeria safeguarding code of conduct.

Ensure all training materials, original data collection forms, and hard and soft copies of raw data are maintained and submitted to Plan International Nigeria with the final dataset.  
• Ensure all tools are translated into local languages and piloted prior to enumerator training. Any changes required to the tools post-piloting must be submitted to Plan International Nigeria and Plan Canada with final revisions subject to approval.  
• Oversee data collection including piloting, supervision and spot checking.  
• Ensure that all data collection activities are inclusive, gender responsive, adolescent friendly and respect child safeguarding principles.  
• Provide daily detailed updates to Plan International Nigeria on progress in data collection, including sharing raw data, and where necessary giving access to the data collection server/platform.  
• Cleaned data is expected to be submitted within one week of the end of data collection for feedback from Plan International Nigeria and Plan Canada, with all data corrected and cleaned within another week.  
• Establish data entry protocols and oversee data entry as per agreed upon software.  
• Review data entry and transcription to ensure data quality and consistency, and take corrective actions, where necessary  
• Submit final data for validation with Plan Nigeria and Plan Canada M&E coordinators/advisors  
• Submit frequency/analysis tables and coded qualitative files and translated transcripts as per Plan Nigeria and Plan Canada guidance for approval prior to the draft report  
• Present key results to the Plan Internation and Plan Canada teams before submission of the draft report for additional feedback  
• Submit draft report  
• Liaise with the Plan International Nigeria and Plan International Canada offices for technical support throughout the process, and integrate feedback provided.  
• Submit final report, incorporating all feedback from Plan international Nigeria and Plan Canada, for approval, along with all training materials, raw, processed, coded and analyzed data (in excel as well as other formats as relevant)  
• Once all raw, analyzed, coded and transcribed qualitative and quantitative data has been confirmed received by Plan International Nigeria and Canada, including the submission of any paper forms, the consultancy is expected to retain the data for 12 months and then delete.

**Timing of key deliverables**  
This consultancy will follow a two-phased approach. Given the upcoming election, the tools and inception report should be finalized and all necessary ethical approvals submitted by the end of 2026. Enumerator training and data collection are expected to take place in March-April, with a staggered approach (likely commencing with Bauchi). Final, clean quantitative data is expected by May15th, and final, clean, transcribed and coded qualitative data by June 1st, and the final report, incorporating all feedback from Plan International Canada and Plan Nigeria, is due July 1st. The consultancy firm is expected to provide a detailed workback schedule incorporating all activities with the proposal.

**Expected Qualifications of the Consultant**  
The consultancy firm will possess the following skills and experiences:  
• Demonstrated experience as a firm in coordinating and administering baseline/endline studies in Northern Nigeria, with a strong focus on gender  
• Previous experience in (or capacity to) design and implement research/studies with or about children and adolescents, including on sensitive topics (i.e. ASRHR, CP, GBV etc.). It will be considered a strong asset if the consultancy firm has previous experience in child or adolescent-centered methods for doing studies/data collection.  
• Demonstrated experience in training, facilitation and supervising survey enumerators and data entry operators to collect and enter data as per high-quality standards.  
• Demonstrated ability to mobilize a strong team of enumerators and supervisors in Northern Nigeria required, with Bauchi and Sokoto considered an asset  
• Experience with mobile data collection, including building mobile tools, is required  
• Demonstrated experience in quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis.  
• A consultancy firm with an assigned level of effort for a data analysis expert to lead quantitative and qualitative analysis is required  
• Knowledge and experience with the Health, Child Protection and Education sector studies and ASRHR issues, policies and services systems in Nigeria is an asset. It will be considered a strong asset if the consultancy firm has an assigned level of effort for a specialist in ASRHR in the Nigerian context to participate in some qualitative data collection activities as well as results analysis and discussion.  
• Knowledge of and experience in gender equality issues is highly preferred.  
• Fluency in both English and Hausa (spoken and written) is mandatory.  
• Ability to produce high-quality work under tight timeframes is required.  
• Ability to work collaboratively with Plan International Nigeria and Plan International Canada and integrate feedback as required.  
• Experience with GAC project evaluation and Plan International Nigeria is an added advantage.

**Applications**  
Applications for the consultancy must include the following components, to a total of no more than 25 pages (not including appendices, CVs, etc.):  
A. A detailed human-written (non-Ai) technical proposal clearly demonstrating a thorough understanding of this ToR and including the following:  
1\. A brief summary of the consultancy firm’s previous experience in coordinating and administering studies of a similar nature.  
2\. A description of the consultancy firm’s approach to designing and implementing an adolescent friendly and inclusive research/study that covers sensitive topics (i.e. ASRHR, CP, GBV etc.)  
3\. An outline of the overall approach to the endline, including methodology, an elaboration on the sampling strategy provided, along with software and platforms to be used.  
4\. A detailed table proposing the number of qualitative kii and FGDs by project participant type/stakeholder. This should include AGYW and to a lesser extent ABYM who participated in key interventions such as Champions of Change, School Health Clubs, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support groups, VSLAs and Women’s Groups; parents, and husbands of young women who participated in interventions such as Fathers’ Forums; health providers and administrators in PHCs with adolescent corners; local leaders and duty bearers; and other key intermediaries.  
5\. A proposed workplan and gantt chart with proposed number of enumerators, size of teams and total numbers of days in the field, including adequate consideration for timing of surveys, travel per team of enumerators, supervision of enumeration teams and quality control. The workplan should also include time for document review, data analysis and draft report reviews and feedback (with at least 2 drafts per report).  
6\. Data protocols, including all necessary considerations to ensure quality data collection and data management, considering aspects such as screening and non-response  
7\. Proposed steps to be taken for enumerator training  
8\. Proposed risk management plan to ensure the successful delivery of the required outputs of this consultancy, on time, within budget and of a high quality. This should include risks, mitigations and protocols, including all ethical considerations related to the respondents, the data and the enumerators  
9\. Either a declaration that the consultancy firm will not use Ai for any of the design, preparatory, implementation, analysis or reporting, or a detailed explanation of how Ai will be used, including detailed security and quality protocols  
10\. Consultancy firm team composition (including sex-disaggregation), role within the consultancy (clearly indicate who will be responsible for report writing, data cleaning, data analysis, training content, digitization of tools, etc), and level of effort of each proposed team member. Please note spoken/written languages as well.

**Please note that considerations for gender should be incorporated throughout the proposal**

Further information, including access to **all relevant annexes and the full Terms of Reference**, is available via this link - [**https://tinyurl.com/zwn74v7k**](https://tinyurl.com/zwn74v7k)

title: Tupande Contract Management Specialist (Fixed-Term)
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

The main purpose of this role is to structure and lead medium-complexity procurement and commercial work across the full procurement lifecycle. The role will have a strong focus on contract lifecycle management while providing senior oversight of procure-to-pay activities for assigned work. Working with minimal manager support, the Specialist will guide procurement from an approved business need through supplier selection and contracting, then oversee delivery through payment and close-out. The role will ensure clear ownership, timely decisions and compliance throughout the process. Contract management will remain the primary focus. However, the role will operate as a senior procurement generalist and may lead other procurement categories or improvement projects as business priorities change.

## **Responsibilities**

Procurement Planning and Delivery

- Structure and lead medium-complexity procurement projects from approved need through delivery, with minimal manager support.
- Translate business plans and forecasts into sourcing priorities, working with relevant owners to confirm requirements.

Sourcing and Supplier Management

- Lead market engagement and supplier selection, including local or international sourcing where required.
- Evaluate proposals, lead commercial negotiations and recommend the best option within approved policies and budgets.
- Manage supplier performance to deliver agreed commercial value and delivery outcomes.

Contract and Procure-to-Pay Management

- Lead assigned contracts from development and approval through performance, renewal or close-out.
- Maintain visibility of contractual obligations and commercial risks, escalating material issues.
- Ensure contract commitments remain aligned with purchasing and payment activities.
- Resolve process exceptions and maintain accurate supporting records.

Performance and Leadership

- Use procurement and contract data to improve performance and lead process improvements.
- Represent Procurement independently in cross-functional work and supplier engagements.
- Guide team members and contribute to their professional development, including managing direct reports where assigned.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Knowledge: Deep understanding of commercial contracting, procurement processes, contract administration, and risk identification
- Skills: 
    - Skills:Technical: Contract redlining, negotiation, risk assessment, data/process analysis, and utilization of AI drafting tools.
    - Soft Skills: Effective communication, proactive problem-solving, stakeholder engagement, organizational skills, and collaborative teamwork.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kakamega, Kenya (Flexible)

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

2 Years

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

17 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Expert Legal & Compliance
body:
The position is to be filled for 01.02.2027 , with a contract duration of two years as a parental leave cover. Employment location will be Bonn, Germany.

We are looking for a motivated Expert to join our Legal & Compliance Unit. In this role, you will have the opportunity to work on a diverse range of legal and compliance matters and contribute to strengthening Welthungerhilfe’s internal processes and standards. Your responsibilities will include reviewing standard contracts, working with our compliance database, preparing compliance reports, and conducting and overseeing smaller compliance investigations. You will also take ownership of our anti-terrorism and financial sanctions screening processes, ensuring their effective implementation and continuous improvement. Working closely with colleagues in Germany and across our international offices, you will gain valuable insights into the diverse legal and compliance challenges of an international humanitarian organization while making a meaningful contribution to our mission.

## Your responsibilities

- Review standard contracts from a legal perspective and communicate with our Country Offices under the guidance of the Senior Legal Counsel.
- Take ownership of, manage, and continuously improve our financial and anti-terrorism sanctions screening process, including working with our screening software and investigating and resolving potential screening matches.
- Develop and maintain legal and compliance-related databases, particularly our compliance case reporting tool, and prepare regular compliance reports.
- Conduct and oversee smaller compliance investigations and coordinate with our Country Offices under the guidance of the Senior Compliance Manager.
- Support the registration of Welthungerhilfe in new project countries by coordinating and preparing registration documents in collaboration with local attorneys and maintaining communication with them.
- Contribute to the maintenance and updating of internal policies and process descriptions.
- Support the development and maintenance of contract templates.
- Keep the Legal & Compliance intranet site up to date.
- Provide additional support to the Legal & Compliance Unit as required by management.

## Your profile

- You hold a bachelor's degree in Law, Business Law, or a related field, obtained in Germany or abroad. A master's degree would be an advantage.
- You have at least two years of relevant professional experience.
- You are highly self-motivated, flexible, and able to work independently with a solution-oriented mindset.
- You have a structured and well-organized approach to work.
- You are proficient in MS Office and Microsoft 365 applications.
- You are able to quickly familiarize yourself with a wide range of legal and compliance-related topics while effectively managing multiple tasks simultaneously
- You can recognize the growing value of data in your field and are eager to build your awareness and skills to incorporate data-informed approaches into your work.
- You have strong communication skills and enjoy collaborating with colleagues in Germany and across our international offices.
- You have excellent written and spoken English and German skills. Knowledge of French would be an additional asset.

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Work-Life Balance: Enjoy flexible working arrangements to support a balanced lifestyle.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which are listed under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-employees-in-germany/).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

title: Regional Housing Ecosystem & Partnership Associate Director
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

PEO Worker

**Summary:**

The Regional Housing Ecosystem & Partnership Associate Director (focus: Ukraine) is a key technical and strategic position responsible for strengthening Habitat's role in the development of inclusive, resilient, and sustainable housing systems in Ukraine and across the Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) region. The role combines housing ecosystem development, partnership building, policy dialogue, and program design to support Habitat's strategic positioning and growth in a highly relevant and evolving housing and recovery context.

Approximately 60% of the role is dedicated to Ukraine, with a strong emphasis on building a robust pipeline of fundable opportunities and strategic partnerships that can translate Habitat's housing ecosystem approach into scalable programs. The Associate Director supports the identification, design, and advancement of donor-aligned concepts, fosters relationships with public, private, and institutional stakeholders, and helps position Habitat as a credible partner in housing recovery, basic services, and longer-term systems change.

The remaining 40% of the role contributes to the advancement of the CEE regional strategic program pillar focused on adaptive reuse and the "Empty Spaces to Homes" approach, ensuring strong linkages between Ukraine programming and broader regional affordable housing priorities. The role is expected to generate cross-regional synergies, support innovation in program design, and contribute to the development of partnership and funding pathways that reinforce Habitat's regional strategic objectives.

In addition, the position serves as the Europe and Middle East (EME) regional focal point for Habitability and Basic Services, providing thought leadership, technical input, and coordination support to strengthen program quality, regional learning, and strategic coherence.

**Key Responsibilities:**

1\. Strategic Planning and Program Support for HFHI's program in Ukraine and CEE region

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Support HFHI Ukraine and its partners in developing, implementing, and aligning national and subnational

housing strategies with HFHI’s vision for a strengthened housing ecosystem

• Lead analysis and integration of market systems, policy frameworks, and partnership opportunities

across the housing value chain

• Conduct research and provide technical recommendations on innovative, inclusive, and climate-resilient

housing solutions, including integration of energy systems, green construction practices, and circular

economy approaches relevant to Ukraine’s recovery context

CEE REGIONAL FOCUS

• Act as focal point for technical construction and spatial aspects of the regional ‘empty space to homes’

i.e. HFHI's "50 Cities strategy" development, implemention and drive project-level initiatives with cities across the CEE region;

• Liaise with demonstration project donors and partners in the NOs, CEE region and western/southern

Europe on promoting ‘empty space to homes’ initiatives, research and funding.

• Conduct contextual research and provide technical recommendations on appropriate, innovative, and

climate-resilient basic services solutions for housing projects.

2\. Support HFHI's Housing. Construction and adaptive reuse technical capabilities across the CEE region (Housing Systems Strengthening and Adaptive Reuse)

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Provide technical and strategic support to local partners, municipalities, and selected private-sector actors in Ukraine to integrate sustainable, inclusive, and resilient housing solutions into wider housing ecosystem development, local governance frameworks, and recovery planning.

• Support the design and delivery of targeted capacity-building initiatives, technical guidance, and knowledge products, including manuals, toolkits, policy briefs, and practical methodologies, to strengthen national and local capacities for housing systems development, partnership-based delivery, and scalable implementation in Ukraine.

• Provide ongoing technical assistance on project oversight, quality assurance, and performance monitoring for housing, neighborhood, and habitability interventions in Ukraine, ensuring alignment with national standards, sustainability objectives, donor expectations, and HFHI’s resilience, inclusion, and people-centered housing principles.

• Lead or support the documentation, synthesis, and dissemination of lessons learned, promising practices, and operational models emerging from Ukraine programming, with particular attention to housing ecosystem development, public-private collaboration, post-disaster and recovery settings, and the integration of energy-efficient and climate-resilient construction approaches.

CEE REGIONAL – Empty Spaces to Homes

• Provide technical and strategic advice to the regional program team and National Organizations engaged in Empty Spaces to Homes demonstration projects, including support on feasibility assessments, adaptive reuse options, life-cycle thinking, renovation pathways, and delivery models suited to local housing markets.

• Serve as a regional focal point for technical guidance and quality support to demonstration projects under the Empty Spaces to Homes agenda, helping ensure that practical pilots contribute to scalable models and evidence generation for Habitat’s 50 Cities by 2030 strategy.

• Support the development of tools, technical guidance, training modules, manuals, and reference materials that strengthen internal and partner capacities to design, implement, and scale adaptive reuse interventions under the Empty Spaces to Homes approach.

• Contribute to the strategic positioning of Empty Spaces to Homes within the wider CEE affordable housing agenda by helping connect demonstration projects to the 50 Cities by 2030 vision, city-level partnerships, municipal engagement, and broader housing ecosystem opportunities.

• Support the CEE program team and National Organizations in identifying and leveraging construction product donations, technical partnerships, and in-kind contributions that can strengthen the implementation, visibility, and replicability of Empty Spaces to Homes demonstration projects.

3\. Serve as Habitatibility and Basic Services contact point for EME regions

• Ensure regional housing programs incorporate habitability, accessibility, and safety standards in

alignment with HFHI housing quality frameworks.

• Provide guidance related to basic services provision in renovation projects (heating, ventilation,

WASH, fire safety, digital readiness).

• Capture and disseminate knowledge on habitability and service integration within HFHI.

4.Coordination, Representation, and Learning

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Actively engage in HFHI’s regional and global communities of practice and represent HFHI in Ukraine in

technical and policy forums

• Represent HFHI in Ukraine in national and international coordination platforms, working groups, and

forums related to housing, social infrastructure, and energy efficiency.

• Promote HFHI’s technical leadership and facilitate learning exchanges with donors, ministries, and

industry partners

• Provide a technical support to the Ukraine team in leading the development and nurturing of strategic

partnerships with government, financial institutions, private sector, and NGOs to advance affordable

housing, housing finance, and resilient urban development in Ukraine

CEE Regional Focus

• Represent the Area Office in regional and sub-regional technical forums, working groups, and

stakeholder engagements related to 'empty space to homes’ initiatives.

• Build partnerships with external organizations, donors, and networks engaged in housing technology,

climate change adaptation, and disaster risk reduction.

• Participate in relevant HFHI communities of practice, technical initiatives, and cross-departmental

coordination.

5.Supporting Fundraising

• Collaborate closely with Fundraising, Partnership, and Program team of Ukraine Program to position

Habitat’s housing ecosystem and partnership agenda to donors

• Contribute to proposal design, donor engagement, and project development processes, ensuring

technical quality, strategic alignment, and compliance with HFHI and donor standards

• Support in reviewing technical proposals, promoting donor compliance and the implementation of

technical standards in relation to ‘empty space to homes’ demonstration projects.

**Minimum Requirements**

• Master’s degree (or equivalent experience) in housing, architecture, urban development,

civil/environmental engineering, economics, or related field. Strong background in housing systems,

market-based approaches, and/or policy reform preferred.

• Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in housing, shelter, urban development,

market systems, or development programming, including at least 5 years in partnership management or

ecosystem development

• Proven experience in affordable housing, incremental housing processes, or climate/disaster-resilient

housing solutions.

• Background in humanitarian assistance, development sector, shelter or energy related projects

• Familiarity with humanitarian and development sector trends, principles, standards (e.g., Sphere, Core

Humanitarian Standard, WHO guidelines), and country specific standards.

• Strong analytical, facilitation, and advisory/consultancy skills.

• Proficient in MS Office; familiarity with GIS software and construction management tools preferred.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a matrix organization and multicultural

environments required.

• Active support of HFHI Values:

Humility - We are part of something bigger than ourselvses

Courage - We do what's right, even when it is difficult or unpopular

Accountability - We take personal responsibility for Habitat's mission

• Safeguarding

HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

This role requires 30% of international travel.

\#LI-DNI

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.
