title: Grants Coordinator (National / International)-Damascus
body:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 350 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country to date provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, in order to respond to the new realities, with a greater focus on resilience and recovery initiatives. Alongside this, the IRC also It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

Since 2012, the IRC has been at the forefront of providing lifesaving healthcare, protection, and economic recovery support across Syria. From hospitals and mobile clinics to specialized protection services and pioneering cash assistance, our programs serve the most vulnerable with dignity and care. We are also proud to nurture early childhood development through the "Ahlan Simsim" program, supporting families affected by conflict. Join us in making a lasting impact where it’s needed most. The IRC is currently funded by GFFO, BHA, ECHO, FCDO, GAC BMZ among other donors and working local organizations to ensure organizational delivery of quality and impactful services across Syria.

**Job overview:**

The IRC Syria Grants Coordinator will report to and work with the Deputy Director of Programs (DDP) for the Syria Country Program to maintain quality grants coordination. Reporting to the DDP, this position will work closely with all departments and staff including Program Coordinators, technical coordinators, finance, and operations, on compliance, donor relations, business development, and reporting. The Coordinator sitting in Damascus will supervise a team of 3 Grants Managers and Officers located in different locations.

The IRC Syria Grants Coordinator will additionally liaise with the Middle East Regional office in Amman, as well as IRC Headquarters colleagues in NY, Germany and the UK.

**Responsibilities**

**Program Design & Proposal Development**

- Support the DDP in cultivating donor relationships in Syria and the Region.
- Track upcoming opportunities by priority sectors in the country program
- Support the update and management of the BD strategy for Syria
- Support the DDP and technical leads in comprehensive business development and develop funding proposals, appropriate to the context and aligned with the country-level Strategic Action Plan.
- Lead proposal development initiatives, providing overall coordination function between HQ IRC’s global technical advisors, partners, finance, operations, HR, and program focal points to ensure smooth and timely proposal development processes.
- Serve as team lead for all proposals, working with and /or overseeing other key roles (e.g. regional support team, consultants) when needed and as resources are available to support them.
- Ensure proposals are tracked with standard IRC tracking tools (e.g. OTIS, Internal tracker)
- In collaboration with MEAL Coordinator, utilize needs assessments contextual analysis results to inform project design
- Monitor major donor trends (policies, strategic directions, etc.) and funding opportunities through regular research and monitoring of information on relevant websites and/or other sources.
- Support program growth aligned with strategic priorities through liaising and collaborating with respective technical units in program design, researching context, gaps, needs assessments, and viable new funding opportunities.
- Ensure the identification, appraisal, and mapping of partners is carried out in a constructively and consistently, and that strategic partners are appropriately engaged in pre-positioning and proposals development processes.
- Interpreting donor solicitations and donor-specific rules and regulations to ensure a responsive and compliant proposal design
- Support proposal budget develop and ensure responsiveness and that it matches the technical narrative.
- Consolidate written inputs into a cohesive proposal narrative; write non-technical sections such as the management and past performance sections.
- Edit full technical proposal and budget narrative for coherence, length, uniformity, and responsiveness to the solicitation.
- Ensure timely submission of quality proposals

**Grants Management and Compliance**

- Review and negotiate donor contracts and agreements
- Review any request for extension and amendments in coordination with the DDP and maintain a tracker for IRC and partners payments and expenditure per each grant
- Manage and provide overall oversight of the grants portfolio and regularly update the grants tracker for dissemination internally and to Awards Management Unit
- Ensure open, timely and accurate information flow within the Grants Unit and between the Unit and relevant departments
- Ensure the submission of timely and high-quality reports (including narrative, financial and MEAL) to donors, including the development and update of regular funding and reporting trackers and schedules for dissemination to relevant staff
- Maintain strong oversight of the portfolio and pipeline, including grant opening and closing dates to ensure timely submission of all related deliverables
- Provide technical guidance on IRC and donor regulations to ensure compliance within operations, program implementation and reporting
- Raise compliance issues proactively with program staff and the DDP, and SMT for timely action and keep senior management informed of any projected inabilities to meet contractual obligations, reports submission and of spend rates/signification budget variances.
- Manage and/or support all agreements reviews, revisions, amendments, and budget realignments, including relevant approvals
- Leads the Grants Unit to coordinate closely with finance teams and review project spending plans and financial health to ensure effective spending amendments, and closeout activities
- In coordination with DDP, conduct project lessons learned meeting during project closeout phase

 ***Staff Performance Management, Learning & Development***

- Develop and implement remote management capacity-building approaches to build the strengths of the teams in Syria.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting annual performance objectives, providing regular and timely positive and constructive performance feedback, and providing documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Approve and manage time, attendance and leave requests to ensure adequate departmental coverage; ensure monthly, accurate timesheet submission and carry out probationary reviews.
- Hold high-quality meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, minimally on a monthly basis.
- Provide a measurable development plan including on-the-job learning with the aim of strengthening technical capacity, exchanging knowledge within the team and providing guidance on career paths.
- As required, identify staff performance issues and work with Human Resources to document and address these in accordance with the National Staff Employment Policies.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth, where appropriate
- Adhere to and act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures and communicate through word and example a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies.

**Partnerships**

- Contribute to achievement of goals related to the SAP partnerships ambition including identification and onboarding of Strategic Partners
- Embody and model IRC values related to partnerships (partner as equals, partner first) and facilitate this approach in implementation of IRC programs
- Support development and maintenance of strategic partnerships.
- Support negotiation of partner sub award agreements in coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator, Award Management Unit and Compliance Unit

**Representation and Advocacy**

- In coordination with the DDP, actively develop and maintain effective working relationships with stakeholders including local communities, donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs, and other relevant actors.
- Liaise with county and national governments, donors, NGOs, and other operational partners in Syria via attendance at meetings, consultations and other forums.
- In coordination with the DDP, assist in organizing donor visits by supporting staff in the smooth design and running of field visits.

**Country Program Management and Strategic Planning**

- Actively participate in and contribute to strategy discussions, including SAP revision processes
- Stay updated on new IRC priorities, policies, or process updates and ensure Grants & Partnerships and MEAL units are informed of any changes.

**Job Requirements:**

 **Education**

A degree in International Studies, Development, or a related field is required. Alternatively, a Bachelor’s degree combined with substantial experience in grants management and excellent writing skills may be considered. Equivalent experience in a similar role may also be accepted in place of formal education.

**Work Experience**

- At least 8 years of demonstrated field-based experience with humanitarian grants management, possibly including experience working with sub-grantee partners to build their capacity to access and account for resources. 5 years of this experience should be working in relief and development contexts.
- At least 3 years in a managerial position, including staff management

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Excellent writing skills and experience in writing proposals/concept notes.
- Strong understanding and knowledge of USAID, PRM, FCDO, UN SIDA, FCDO, USG, GFFO, EU, ECHO and private donor rules and regulations.
- Proven competency with program design, M&E, proposal writing (including logical frameworks) and building budgets.
- Excellent management and coordination skills.
- Solid ability to provide team- building, coaching, and development for staff as well as encourage cross-functional collaboration and cooperation.
- Ability to work independently while being a strong team player.
- Excellent relationship-building, interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively represent IRC at forums and with donors.
- Full professional competency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
- High attention to detail and excellent time management skills
- Excellent leadership and management skills including coaching, mentoring and managing teams
- Politically astute, with well-developed diplomatic and negotiating skills.
- Superior oral and written communication skills, with ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively with senior internal and external stakeholders.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and other international and private donors.
- Established capacity to deal with ambiguity in stressful situations.
- Strong commitment to IRC’s vision, mission and core values.
- Proven ability to design and lead training engagements with staff and partners to enhance skills and adapt to changing program demands

 **Language/Travel:**

**Travel**: minimum 10% percent travel

**Language**: Fluency in English, written and spoken is mandatory, and Arabic is desirable

**Key Working Relationships:**

***Position Reports to***: Deputy Director for Programs, with close working relationships with Technical Advisors

***Position directly supervises***: Grants Managers

***Internal contacts:*** Awards Management Unit, MEAL, Program Coordinators, Supply Chain, Finance, HR, Partnerships Research Evaluation and Learning Technical Unit

***External***: Clusters and working group

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

title: Regional Analyst - West & Central Africa region
body:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO West Africa and Lake Chad Basin**

Since 2013, INSO has supported the humanitarian community across the region and is looking to establish a regional presence for West Africa at the request of the NGO community. This position is based in Dakar, Senegal, and reports to the Regional Director, under the technical guidance of the Global Analysis Team at Headquarters.

**Job Summary**

As Regional Analyst, you will assist NGOs working in, but not limited to, the Central Sahel, the West African Coastal States, and parts of the Lake Chad Basin through analysis of broader trends and dynamics, such as regional or contextual developments that shape humanitarian safety and access in the region.

**Major** **Responsibilities**

*Service Delivery*

- Prepare and produce reports to help NGO partners assess prevalent regional conflict dynamics and their impact on humanitarian safety and access.
- Initiate delivery of regional services, designing outputs in line with partner requirements and priorities.
- Manage and deliver ad hoc products on emerging regional challenges to humanitarian safety and access.
- Contribute to other countries’ office products and inform decision-making at the regional level.
- Offer a responsive, tailored analysis service directly to INSO’s NGO partners upon their request.
- Convene and contribute to regional NGO coordination meetings and fora with humanitarian counterparts to discuss regional safety and access.

*Local acceptance*

- Build a network of partners and interlocutors working on humanitarian activities in West Africa and Lake Chad, including NGOs, UN agencies, government representatives, and other actors involved in security coordination and information sharing.
- Establish a clear role for INSO within the humanitarian security architecture in West Africa.

*Representation*

When requested and in coordination with the Coastal Countries CD

- Represent the organization at the country and regional levels, and ensure adherence to INSO mission, policies, and principles.
- Build and maintain strong networks with government agencies, NGOs, the UN, Red Cross, donors, embassies, humanitarian coordination platforms, and security bodies while maintaining independence.
- Proactively seek opportunities to represent INSO at relevant events and forums
- Effectively represent and protect INSO’s principles of independence, impartiality, and neutrality; promote INSO as an integral member of the humanitarian community.
- Stay updated on political, security, and humanitarian developments in West Africa and Lake Chad Basin region, and provide regular strategic analysis.

*Program strategy and management*

- Assist the Country Director in the development of a regional strategy through consultation with internal and external stakeholders.
- Liaise and coordinate with INSO’s Global Analysis Team to enable analytical capacity building in the countries’ offices when needed.

**Requirements**

- A minimum of 5 years of work experience in an analytical capacity, preferably working on conflict or post-conflict contexts in West Africa and the Lake Chad region
- Experience working in NGOs, international organisations, consultancy, or journalism
- Exemplary command of French and at least professional fluency in English is required.
- Proven ability to provide operationally relevant analysis to a wide-ranging audience
- The administrative ability to travel to all countries in West Africa
- Demonstrable understanding of humanitarian safety practices and their application
- Excellent networking, diplomatic, and representative communication skills
- Graduate-level education in political science, history, or humanitarian studies, or a related field, or equivalent work experience

**Nice-to-have**

- Experience delivering a partner-focused advisory service
- Experience designing and delivering products based on close partner engagement
- Existing regional experience and/or information networks
- Experience in insecure/conflict-affected environments
- Experience in staff capacity development and training
- Detailed understanding of INSO’s mandate & services

**Core Competencies**

- Critical Thinking - Ability to analyse complex situations, question assumptions, and develop sound, practical solutions through logical reasoning.
- Communication - Ability to convey information clearly, build positive relationships, and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
- Organisation - Ability to plan, prioritise, and manage tasks efficiently while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
- Autonomy - Ability to work independently, take initiative, and make informed decisions while remaining accountable for results.
- Teamwork - Ability to contribute positively to team objectives through reliability, collaboration, cultural awareness, and mutual support.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable contract, based in Dakar, Senegal. €5000 per month salary, 4 calendar days of annual leave per month and 3 days of R&R every 3 months without allowance, global medical coverage (excluding USA) and AD&D insurance.

title: Feasibility & Baseline Study (Multi-Country, East Africa)
body:
*Request for Proposal (RFP)*

**Procurement of Consultancy Services for Feasibility & Baseline Study** - ReSCALE (DC-GP27.01)

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. is announcing an open tender procedure for a Feasibility Study and a Baseline Study in Marsabit & Isiolo (Kenya), Teso Region/Soroti (Uganda), Kamonyi District (Rwanda).

*Planned Timetable*

- **Date of Tender Publication:** *18th November 2026*
- **Closing Date for Questions:** *26th November 2026* at 11:59 am (CET)
- **Publication of Clarifications latest by:** *27th November 2026 (latest COB)*
- **Deadline for Submission of Bids:** *4th December 2026* at 11:59 am (CET)
- **Interviews** *(shortlisted candidates only): Estimated: 9th – 11th December 2026*
- **Selection of Winning Bid:** *Estimated: 15th December 2026*
- **Award of Contract:** *Estimated: 16th December 2026*
- **Contract start:** *Estimated: 16th - 18th December 2026*

## Introduction

**Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V.**

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is a Christian-motivated organisation for human rights, humanitarian assistance and development cooperation. From its base in Constance, Germany, Sign of Hope is committed to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

**Project Context**

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with ARDE/Kubaho (Rwanda), Soroti Catholic Diocese Integrated Development Organization (SOCADIDO / Uganda), Caritas Marsabit (CM), Merti Integrated Development Programme (MID-P) – hereinafter collectively called the “ReSCALE consortia” in the following - being the local implementing partners.

The programme strengthens climate-resilient sanitation and food security for approx. 5,500 households (directly) in UGA, KEN, and RWA. It addresses the lack of access to safe sanitation systems, inadequate faecal and waste management, and the impacts of climate change that exacerbate health risks and food insecurity—particularly for women and children. The programme combines WASH, nutrition, and climate resilience in an integrated approach at the micro, meso, and partially at macro levels. Innovative sanitation and circular economy solutions are piloted and implemented in collaboration with communities. At the same time, the programme strengthens local institutions and community structures. The programme supports SDGs 2, 3, 5, 6, and 13.

**The Purpose of this RFP**

It is the intent of this RFP to procure consultancy services to conduct a feasibility study (FS) and a baseline study (BS). While the FS shall be conducted before the submission of the final project proposal, the BS shall be done prior to the start of the project. On the one hand, the FS is a mandatory requirement of donor, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and shall confirm the feasibility of the planned project and deliver relevant information to further enhance the proposal. The BS on the other hand shall collect and analyse data from field visits, provide a MEAL framework and contribute to the development of the logframe (baseline and target indicators). Find more information in the attached Terms of Reference. *Note:* A division into lots is not applied for economic & efficiency reasons (e.g. level of familiarity; technical expertise) as both studies will be conducted prior to the official launch of the project and partially build upon each other.

## Tender Documents

The Bidder is expected to examine all instructions, forms, terms, and specifications in the tender documents prepared for the selection of a qualified Bidder. Failure to furnish all information required as per the Tender documents or to submit a Bid not substantially responsive to the Tender documents in every respect will be at the Bidder’s risk and may result in Bid rejection.

The Tender documents include the following documents:

- The Request for Proposal (this document)
- The Terms of Reference (Annexe A)
- Feasibility Assessment Areas and Guiding Questions (Annexe A2 (to the ToR))

**Clarification of Bidding Documents**

A prospective Bidder requiring clarification of the Tender Documents may notify SoH in writing at procurement@sign-of-hope.org. The request for clarification must reach the SoH not later than on *26th November 2026* at 11.59 am (CET). SoH will respond by providing clarification on the Tender documents no later than on *27th November 2026* at 2.00 pm (CET). Written copies of SoH’s responses (including an explanation of the query but without identifying the source of inquiry) will be added to the Tender Documents as a separate file. Clarifications will be collected, clarifications consolidated and uploaded at the above-mentioned date.

## Preparation of Bids

**Cost of Bidding**

The Bidder is responsible for all costs associated with the preparation and submission of its bid, and SoH will in no case be responsible or liable for those costs, regardless of the conduct or outcome of the Bidding process.

**Language of Bid**

The Bid and all related correspondence and documents exchanged between the Bidders and SoH must be written in English. Any printed literature furnished by the Bidder and written in another language must be accompanied by an English translation of its pertinent passages, in which case, for purposes of interpretation of the bid, the English version will prevail.

**Documents Comprising the Bid**

The submitted Bid must include the following information. Failure to provide all requested information or to comply with the specified formats may disqualify the Bidder from consideration.

*Submit only required documents clearly separated into Eligibility, Technical, and Financial documents:*

**Eligibility documents** that will be checked before Technical Evaluation (Preliminary Evaluation)

- Valid Certificate of (Business) Registration
- For consulting firms: Audit certificates certifying audited books of accounts for the past three years (2023, 2024, 2025), for self-employed consultants the tax clearance certificates are considered as equivalent)
- Bank statements for the last 3 months (August, September, October 2026)
- A list of projects/studies completed in the last 5 years, with a minimum of 3 assignments of similar scope. For each project, provide the project name, client, total budget, and choose 2 sample reports or extracts demonstrating relevant experience.

**Technical Documents:**

- A detailed technical proposal, limited to 15 pages, responding to the Terms of Reference (Annexe A & A2).
- A technical profile of the firm or consultant, limited to 2 pages. Additional information may be provided as annexes, including sample copies of relevant evaluation or other work.
- Proposed team composition and roles of each team member. The CV for all proposed consultant team members should be attached as annexes.
- A detailed implementation plan describing the proposed approach to fieldwork and analysis. This should include the estimated number of staff days, fieldwork plan, and a schedule of key activities presented in a clear timeline format such as a Gantt chart.
- References and/or documents (e.g. university/training certificates) proving the relevant expertise in the fields of WASH (particularly sanitation/FSM), food security and climate resilience and M&E.

**Financial Documents:**

- A detailed and costed financial proposal with clear justification. The budget must cover all costs associated with the assignment. A clear distinction shall be made between the feasibility study and the baseline study.

**Bid Prices**

The prices quoted by the Bidder must clearly indicate the unit price of the items. Furthermore, the financial proposal must separately present all additional expenses (e.g. taxes, deliveries, logistics etc.) as well as any potential discounts. For improved comparability of received Bids, please split into specific categories: staff, travel, material, and equipment. All incurring costs must be included in the ultimate Bid price. Any expenses exceeding the Bid price will not be covered.

**Currency**

The currency of the Bid must be in EUR.

**Period of Validity of Bids**

Bids must remain valid for 4 weeks after the date of the Bid submission deadline prescribed by SoH in this RFP. A Bid valid for a shorter period may be rejected by SoH as non-responsive.

In exceptional circumstances, SoH may request the Bidders to extend the period of validity. The request and the responses thereto will be made in writing by e-mail. A Bidder agreeing to the request will not be required nor permitted to modify his Bid.

**Format and Signing**

The original Bid must be signed by the Bidder or by a person or persons authorised to bind the Bidder to the contract. Financial proposal pages of the Bid must be initialled by the person or persons signing the Bid and stamped with the Bidder’s company seal.

Interlineations, erasures, annotations, or overwriting are valid only if they are initialled by the person or persons signing the bid.

**Alternative Bids**

Alternative Bids will not be accepted.

## Submission of Bids

See Section "How to apply" below.

## Bid Opening and Evaluation

SoH will examine the Bids to determine whether they are complete, whether any computational errors have been made, whether required sureties have been furnished, whether the documents have been properly signed and whether Bids are generally in order.

Where errors, omissions, or inconsistencies are identified, SoH may, at its sole discretion, request clarification from the Bidder or determine that the Bid will not be considered further.

**Evaluation**

Bids determined to be substantially responsive will be considered and evaluated according to the following scoring criteria:

**Evaluation Criteria - Eligibility** (Weight - yes/no)

- Valid Certificate of (Business) Registration
- For consulting firms: Audit certificates certifying audited books of accounts for the past three years (2023, 2024, 2025), for self-employed consultants the tax clearance certificates are considered as equivalent)
- Bank statements for the last 3 months (August, September, October 2026).
- A list of projects/studies completed in the last 5 years, with a minimum of 3 assignments of similar scope. For each project, provide the project name, client, total budget, and choose 2 sample reports or extracts demonstrating relevant experience.

Only bids that meet all eligibility requirements will proceed to the next stage of the evaluation process.

**Evaluation Criteria - Technical Evaluation** (Weight (%))

- **Relevant expertise & competencies (20%)**
    - Past experiences in WASH, climate resilience and food security, experience in evaluating multi-country projects and competencies of the team will be assessed on relevance. Provided references might be contacted.
- **Methodology & sample size (10%)**
    - Preciseness, degree of detail, suitability and clarity of the proposed methodology & sample size.
- **Implementation Plan (10%)**
    - The implementation plan will be checked on completeness, relevance and compared to expected duration of the assignment.
- **Interview Performance (20%)**
    - Short-listed candidates will be invited to a short interview (20-30 minutes) including a bidder presentation (max. 10 minutes) and a round of questions (max. 20 minutes).

Only bids scoring at least 70% of the maximum technical score will be eligible for financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criteria - Financial Evaluation** (Weight %)

**Financial Proposal (40%)**

The financial evaluation will be based on the total price proposed by each Bidder. The Bid with the lowest evaluated price will receive the maximum financial score, and all other bids will be scored proportionately:

Points for Financial Proposal = Lowest Evaluated Proposal Price / Bidder’s Proposal Price

If the weighted final scores of Bidders are equal, priority will be based on the total scores that were given for the Technical Evaluation: The contract will be awarded to the Bidder that has received the highest Technical Evaluation Score. If this does not lead to a distinction, the ranking will be determined by the drawing of lots.

## Contracting

As a result of this tender process, SoH anticipates to issue a Consultancy Agreement with the successful Bidder(s).

The contract will be awarded to the successful Bidder(s) whose Bid is determined to be substantially responsive to the requirements of the solicitation and represents the best value based on the evaluation criteria, including price and performance factors, provided that the Bidder is deemed qualified to enter into an agreement and to perform its contractual obligations satisfactorily. The contract will furthermore include a termination clause for the baseline study in case the contracted consultant (firm) does not deliver satisfactory results during the feasibility study.

The contract will be concluded and paid in EURO.

SoH reserves the right to cancel this procurement process, to reject all bids, and to award any contract based on the first and non-negotiated proposal.

## Ethical Operating Standards

**Code of Conduct**

- SoH requires all consultants and service providers who will interact with beneficiaries, communities, implementing partners, government counterparts or any other project stakeholders to sign and comply with SoH's Code of Conduct, available at [https://www.hoffnungszeichen.de/en/about-us/transparency/acting-responsibly](https://www.hoffnungszeichen.de/en/about-us/transparency/acting-responsibly).
- SoH requests that suppliers sign and adhere to the SoH Supplier Declaration to be found at [https://www.hoffnungszeichen.de/en/about-us/transparency/acting-responsibly](https://www.hoffnungszeichen.de/en/about-us/transparency/acting-responsibly).

**Research and Data Handling**

- The winner of this award will adhere to high ethical standards consistent with SoH policies and internationally accepted evaluation ethics.
- The winner will ensure that all participants provide informed consent before participation. Information about the purpose of the Evaluation, voluntary participation, confidentiality, and the right to withdraw will be clearly explained in appropriate languages.
- Confidentiality and anonymity of respondents will be strictly maintained. No personally identifiable information will be included in reports or shared datasets. Qualitative data will be anonymised during transcription and analysis. Data collection will be conducted in safe and appropriate settings, with particular care when engaging adolescents, survivors of violence, refugees, and persons with disabilities.
- The consultant will comply with SoH safeguarding requirements. Any disclosures of violence or protection concerns during data collection will be managed in line with established referral pathways and protocols, in coordination with SoH and relevant service providers.
- All data will be securely stored and accessed only by authorised members of the evaluation team. Ethical considerations and risk mitigation measures will be clearly described in the inception report.

**Conflict of Interest**

Bidders must avoid any situation that could result in an actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest in relation to this procurement process. This obligation applies equally to the bidder's employees, officers, consultants, agents, affiliates and subcontractors.

Where a conflict of interest exists, arises or is reasonably perceived to exist, the bidder must promptly disclose the matter to SoH in writing, providing full details of the circumstances. Such disclosure must include any personal, professional, financial or other relationship that could influence, or be perceived to influence, the impartiality of the procurement process or the performance of any resulting contract.

SoH reserves the right to determine whether a conflict of interest exists and to require appropriate corrective measures. Failure to disclose a conflict of interest may result in disqualification from the procurement process or termination of any resulting contract.

title: RFP-SDN-KRT-26-037-SIDA consultancy
body:
**Terms of Reference (TOR) for Building Resilience and Supporting Solutions to Displacement in Central Darfur**

## Who is the Danish Refugee Council?

Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement-affected people and communities. DRC works throughout displacement: in acute crises, during displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, and upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included in host societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence

## Purpose of the consultancy

The Danish Refugee Council based in Sudan seeks proposals from a consultant to assess Housing, Land and Property (HLP) Issues and Civil Documentation Needs Affecting Durable Solutions in Central Darfur, with a Focus on Reintegration and Access to Secure Housing for Vulnerable Populations in Nertiti, Golo and Um Dukhun Localities

## Background

Danish Refugee Council (DRC), Save the Children (SC), and Mercy Corps (MC) are jointly implementing the Second Phase of the Building Resilience and Supporting Solutions to Displacement in Central Darfur project in Nertiti, Golo and Um Dukhun localities, Central Darfur, Sudan, with funding from Sida and SDC, implemented from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2027. The project is implemented in a consortium led by DRC, with Mercy Corps and Save the Children as implementing partners. The second phase builds on the achievements and learning of Phase I (2024–2025), continuing efforts to strengthen resilience, address priority needs, reduce aid dependency, promote early recovery and create pathways towards durable solutions for people affected by displacement.

In Central Darfur, the pursuit of durable solutions takes place against a backdrop of decades of conflict and accumulated economic, social and institutional vulnerabilities, compounded by the October 2021 political crisis and the outbreak of conflict in April 2023. Continued insecurity, displacement and population mobility have further constrained access to stable livelihoods, public services and natural resources, while complex land and property issues remain difficult to resolve. In this context, comprehensive and sustainable durable solutions cannot be achieved immediately in many locations. The project therefore adopts an **early solutions and resilience-building approach**, addressing practical and legal barriers and strengthening the capacities, assets and relationships that can contribute to longer-term solutions as conditions evolve.

The project brings together three interconnected components. First, **ongoing analysis, monitoring and learning** inform adaptive and conflict-sensitive programming, including solutions analysis to identify realistic pathways towards durable solutions in the evolving Sudanese context. Second, **participatory needs assessment and community-led planning** enable communities to define priorities and shape interventions. Third, **integrated implementation** addresses barriers to accessing services and natural resources, including land and water; strengthens livelihood opportunities and early recovery; improves the protective environment and community safety; and enhances community capacity for peacebuilding, social cohesion and conflict resolution.

## Objective of the consultancy

The purpose of this consultancy is to The purpose of the consultancy is to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the existing formal legal and customary institutions, systems, and processes governing Housing, Land and Property (HLP) issues—including access modalities and tenure arrangements, dispute resolution mechanisms, and inheritance—as well as civil documentation requirements in Nertiti, Golo, and Um Dukhun localities, Central Darfur, Sudan. The assessment will seek to:

a) understand the current HLP and civil documentation landscape,

b) identify how existing frameworks and practices enable or hinder durable solutions, including reintegration and secure tenure over housing and land for vulnerable populations, and

c) provide practical, evidence-based recommendations to inform DRC’s programming and strengthen HLP-related interventions in support of durable solutions.

The assignment will be composed of one assessment which will identify the key national, traditional and international actors and stakeholders, current capacities of legal and customary systems and perceptions of legitimate HLP rights and civil documentation requirements to support durable solutions, the main issues and challenges being faced by the affected community and the main opportunities and constraints, including protection risks, for HLP and legal programming and assistance.

The consultancy will develop a roadmap and plan for appropriate HLP and civil documentation programming within targeted localities, in order to provide both short- and long-term solutions to some of the key challenges that are prohibiting durable solutions, adopting a conflict-sensitive and protection-focused approach.

The HLP and civil documentation assessments in targeted localities will identify gaps in the national and international response and needs in the access to civil documentation challenges, HLP intervention and will provide recommendations and guidance for further activities on civil documentation, HLP rights in Nertiti, Golo and Um Dukhun localities and other humanitarian actors. Building on DRC’s ongoing LAAF (Legal Aid Analytical Framework), the assessment will identify of legal and customary frameworks in Nertiti, Golo and Um Dukhun localities; specific support on access to land tenure for women. The Assessment will also include practical steps on what needs to be addressed for women to fully participate on an equal basis in the HLP and civil documentation process and claim their rights. The assessment will also include questions around access to arable land in Nertiti, Golo and Um Dukhun localities for the local community and for the internally displaced population (IDP).

The assessment will include comprehensive suggestions outlining the aforementioned factors and setting clear operational guidelines/next steps for the suggested DRC HLP and legal programmes in targeted locations.

The close cooperation between the consultant and the implementing partners and their Protection and legal staff (and other sectors involved in supporting livelihoods, HDP or shelter) will increase the knowledge of key consortium staff in Central Darfur, inform programming and possibly contribute to and influence discussions around HLP. Moreover, a final post-fieldwork workshop presenting and discussing the preliminary findings and recommendations of the report, and an in-person training for the consortium staff will improve the capacity of contextual understanding of the main HLP and civil documentation obstacles to durable solutions.

## Scope of work and Methodology

The consultancy will focus on the desk and field assessment and data collection for the actor mapping, and HLP and Civil documentation mechanisms analysis in Nertiti, Golo, and Um Dukhun localities to address institutional/process analysis, practice analysis, and protection analysis pertaining to locality-level formal systems; customary/traditional HLP mechanisms; community-level dispute resolution; state/local authorities; humanitarian/legal actors; and linkages between these systems.

The deliverables of the assignment consist of an assessment report identifying Housing, land, and property (HLP), and civil documentation barriers and programming options to support durable solutions, including reintegration and access to housing and land with secure tenure for vulnerable populations. It is anticipated that this would involve around 21 days of consultancy time (indicative- depending on the technical proposal and work plan submitted as part of the application process from the consultancy) and is expected to be finalized by December 2026.

### Key tasks

1. Develop an inception report for the assessment, including the civil documentation and HLP/legal analysis/actor mapping methodology.
    1. Conduct a desk review and identify gaps in available assessments

Under the technical supervision of the DRC Country Protection Manager, the consultant will coordinate closely with the ongoing LAAF (Legal Aid Analysis Framework) consultancy, building on its findings and outputs where relevant. The consultant will engage with relevant stakeholders and develop an inception report, ensuring clear complementarity between the two processes and avoiding duplication or overlap. The two consultancies should be implemented in close coordination to maximize synergies and ensure consistency in analysis, recommendations, and deliverables.

1. HLP and personal documentation field data collection

For this purpose, the selected consultant/group of consultants is expected to:

- Develop a research protocol , including engagement with communities, implementing agencies, and other key stakeholders. Ensure all key stakeholders’ perspectives are taken into consideration through multiple FGDs, KIIs, and other tools.
- Work closely with the consortium and DRC teams, particularly with the Area Manager, Consortium Manager, Protection Manager, and Safety and Access Manager, and other sector leads such as EcRecc, CCM and HDP on methodology and implementation of the assessment, as well as consult the Head of Programmes, MEAL Coordinator, and Country Protection Manager.

1. Compile and analyze field assessment data in a clear manner and format.
    1. Provide a one-day training workshop for DRC, MC, and SC staff

Provide an online one-day capacity-building workshop to consortium partner field staff on identified HLP concerns, legal and customary structures, and processes in place, and conflict-sensitive approaches to HLP (notably HLP due diligence) and legal programming. This should be in the form of a capacity-building session on issues and concerns identified by the assessment.

### Reporting

1. DRC Durable Solution Consortium Manager will lead coordination to present preliminary findings to key DRC, MC, and Save the Children staff (presentation of findings through validation session/workshop)
    1. Share draft assessment report with DRC and the relevant consortium partner staff
    2. Incorporate the partners' feedback into the final reports.

Submit final assessment report that should include: i) provision of prioritization elements with input from consultant's experience/recommendations, good practices, programme guidelines outlining opportunities and constraints, ii) roadmap and plan for appropriate HLP and civil documentation programming within targeted localities, in order to provide both short- and long-term solutions to some of the key challenges that are prohibiting durable solutions, adopting a conflict-sensitive and protection-focused approach.

## METHODOLOGY

The methodology should include an initial desk review of key literature available, combined with qualitative interviews with key informants and household-level interviews and FGDs. Attention should also be given to ensure perspectives from women and from marginalized groups are taken into account, and confidentiality procedures should be in place to ensure the safety of informants. Care will be taken to ensure that the different stakeholders are free to express their views without interference or concerns of reprisals.

The precise methodology will be agreed upon between the consultant and DRC before assessment activities commence, with the methodological outline provided by the consultant as per this tender and in the Inception Report. However, a mixed-method methodology is preferred for this type of assessment.

The partners will provide copies of relevant internal documentation deemed essential for effective assessment. The methodology shall include a review of other civil documentation and HLP initiatives around the country, to ensure that the methodology and terminology used are in line with ongoing Protection cluster and Shelter, Land and Site Coordination cluster efforts, analysis and recommendations in relation to civil documentation and HLP concerns in Sudan.  
6\. Deliverables  
The Consultant will submit the following deliverables as mentioned below:  
Phase Expected deliverables Indicative description tasks Maximum expected timeframe  
Phase 1  
Review Inception Report (assessment Methodology and Assessment Plan) Provide a desk review of available information provided by DRC, including a review of the assessment methodology. Provide a detailed overview of the assessment process including but not limited to:  
1\. Introduction (context/ background)  
2\. Objective of the assessment and Scope of Work, including assessment Questions  
3\. Assessment Approach and Data Collection Methods  
4\. Deliverables and Work Plan 5 working days  
Phase 2 Preparation Assessment Methodology Design The consultant is expected to prepare draft questionnaires ready for DRC approval 5 working days  
Phase 3 Implementation Data Collection Implementation of data collection based on the agreed methodology and tools 15 working days  
Phase 4 Analysis Raw Data & Clean Database The consultant is expected to clean the database and provide both raw and clean data. This is an opportunity to share and discuss outliers with the DRC team 4 working days  
Phase 5 Reporting Final Assessment Report, Assessment Presentation, and Infographics Prepare first draft report  
Feedback from DRC and Sida to be incorporated prior to submission of the final report  
Preparation of the presentation and infographics 10 working days  
Phase 6 Presentation Oral Presentations Present findings and recommendations to DRC staff and Sida representatives (and other relevant stakeholders as agreed), allowing space for discussion and clarification. 1 day

7\. Duration, timeline, and payment  
The total expected duration to complete the assignment will be no more than 35 days. The consultant shall be prepared to complete the assignment no later than a date to be agreed upon in Feb 2027  
The payments will be in two instalments, 30% after submission of the Inception Report, and 70% after the completion of the task and submission of final acceptable report to DRC

8\. Proposed Composition of Team  
The following is a recommended structure subject to amendment and negotiation upon realisation of the consultant’s existing team structure:  
• Analysist/ Reporting  
• Enumerators (either through third party or in-house)

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

**Examination Criteria**

**Bidder qualification criteria**

Bidders must meet the Essential Criteria below for this tender. Failure to comply with the criteria will result in the disqualification of the bid. Submitted offers will be reviewed on a “Pass” or “Fail” basis to determine compliance with the below formal criteria/ requirement:

**Requirements**

1\. The consultant must possess authorization to work in Sudan and/or have the necessary permissions for travel and data collection within Sudan and/or have access to an authorized third party with permission to collect data and operate in Sudan.

2\. The designated Project Manager / Lead Consultant must possess a master’s degree in international development or related social sciences.

3\. The consultant(s) or consultancy firm must have a minimum of 5 years of research and/or academic work with experience in conducting research within the fields of displacement and durable solutions as well as in difficult contexts.

**Technical Assessment Criteria**

To be technically acceptable, the bid shall meet or exceed the stipulated requirements and specifications in the RFP. A Bid is deemed to meet the criteria if it confirms that it meets the conditions, procedures and specifications in the RFP without substantially departing from or attaching restrictions with them. If a Bid does not technically comply with the RFP, it will be rejected.

For all bids deemed technically compliant as per the specification stipulated in Annex – Terms of Reference (ToR), DRC will give a weighted combined technical and financial score. The weighted score will determine the contract award.

The technical criteria for this RFP and their weighting in the technical assessment are:

**Technical criteria**

**Weighting in technical assessment\[Total 50%\]**

**1 Qualification and Language proficiency of personnel dedicated to the consultancy 10%**

1.1 The consultant's qualifications and experience, including their academic background, research, and practical work in challenging displacement environments, are relevant and extensive. Experience in displacement and durable solutions work/research is desirable.

1.2 The consultants must be fluent in English, and the enumerators must be in fluent in Arabic

1.3 Suitability and qualifications of the suggested team, consisting of professionals like Team Leader, Analyst/Reporting Specialist, Project Manager, Assistant Project Manager, and Enumerators.

**2 Proposed Methodology and Assessment %20**

2.1 Development of an extensive mixed-method project assessment approach, complete with definitions, criteria, and assessment questions.

**3 Previous experience in similar context 15%**

3.1 Demonstrated experience in conducting large-scale external assessment within fragile/emergency contexts.

3.2 Detailed knowledge and practical experience in designing and implementing research cycles in the humanitarian sector, specifically for impact measurement.

**References 5%**

4.1 Positive references from other institutions, preferably from NGOs/INGOs related to similar scope of service

4.1 Familiarity with durable solutions programming

4.2 Strong understanding of the difference between emergency support and development work

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified.

Bidders who pass the technical evaluation will be invited for an online panel interview. The interview will be evaluated per the following criteria:

**Panel Interview criteria**

**Weighting in technical evaluation \[Total 50%\]**

1-Previous experience in similar data collection, analysis and research projects

2-Clarity of proposed process

3-Demonstration of understanding of challenges and best practices across various contexts

4-Spoken fluency in English

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified

## Technical supervision

The selected consultant will work under the supervision of:

- Durable Solutions Consortium Manager / CMU (Lead) - Evans Agola Owino, evans.owino@drc.ngo
- Country Protection Manager - Blerta Mano blerta.mano@drc.ngo
- MEAL Manager (colead)
- PDQ Manager (Support)

## Location and support

**Address of Consultancy:**

Danish Refugee Council, House No. 14, Manshia B, Al Manshiya Neighborhood, Khartoum State, Sudan

The Consultant will provide her/his own computer and mobile telephone, including required software for data collection, analysis, and reporting.

## Travel

Travel within the country will be required to facilitate data collection and support teams. Presentation of the report can be online if required.

The consultant is solely responsible for the travel/permit and other related costs.

## Submission process

Proposals should include:

- Curriculum vitae detailing previous experience on related assessments within humanitarian assistance projects/contexts; references of previous related assignments done, or samples of work accomplished;
- Technical proposal including the assessment design and methodology, data collection and analysis, activities (e.g., development of tools), as well as a confirmed timeline considering contextual limitations and proposed team structure, including enumerators' qualifications and language proficiency;
- Financial proposal for the assessment. All costs related to the assessment without exceptions should be figured into the financial plan of the proposal, including (but not limited to) consultancy fees, travel, accommodation, interpreters, enumerators, data entry, logistics, etc. Please, note that no per diem will be paid to the engaged personnel on top of the overall fee;
- Three references, of which two should be from previous surveying experience.

Please refer to the Invitation Letter for detailed instructions on the submission process for your proposal.

## Evaluation of bids

Please refer to the related section of the RFP Invitation Letter.

title: Private Sector Partnerships Coordinator

body:
**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures, and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.  
**Greening strategy:**  
Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities: Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan. Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles. Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming  
standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes  
**Acted PSEAH Policy:**  
The Private Sector Partnerships Coordinator has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). And has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. The Private Sector Partnerships Coordinator carry out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.  
**Location:** Damascus – Syria  
**Start Date:** ASAP

**CHAIN OF COMMAND**

Under the authority of: Deputy Country Director – Programs

Responsible for: Consultants (if any)  
**WORKING RELATIONS**

Internal Relations:

- Country Director
- Deputy Country Director - Operations
- Area Coordinators
- Project Managers
- Project Development Department
- MEAL Department
- Technical Coordination Unit (including FSL, Water and Environment and Economic Recovery & Resilience TC)
- Acted Global Technical Staff

External Relations:

- Private sector actors: companies, investors, business associations, regional and diaspora business networks
- TVET institutions, training centers and relevant authorities
- Financial service providers and microfinance institutions
- Donors and financing institutions (institutional, blended and development finance)
- Other I/NGOs, UN agencies and relevant cluster and sector working groups.

**Job PURPOSE**

The Private Sector Partnerships Coordinator is responsible for developing and managing Acted Syria’s engagement with the private sector as a core pillar of its funding strategy alongside institutional and climate funding, co-investment and support for community-centred programming. The Coordinator builds mutually beneficial business-oriented partnerships that help companies operate and grow in Syria, in line with Acted’s 3ZERO strategy. The Coordinator develops partnerships with multinational and local companies, offering business-oriented solutions that help them operate and grow responsibly in Syria. Working through service agreements or other collaboration models, the Coordinator leads Acted’s engagement with the private sector on areas such as community engagement, local hiring and skills, supply chains, and the local services and infrastructure that company operations depend on. Where private actors wish to implement positive projects in the areas where they operate, the Coordinator also supports them to build community acceptance, while mobilizing resources and strengthening local skills systems and economic opportunities. :. He/She leads strategic planning, business development, partnership negotiation and technical guidance in this area, and works closely with the Program Teams, the Project Development and MEAL departments, and Acted’s FLATS functions. He/She proactively contributes to fundraising by identifying and converting private sector opportunities and by proposing new project ideas, approaches and strategies within his/her area of focus, in line with Acted’s policies and principles.  
**OBJECTIVES**

1. To develop and implement a private sector engagement and resource mobilization strategy for Acted Syria that clearly sets out what Acted offers (community acceptance and trusted access, conflict-sensitive implementation, skills and employment expertise) and what it seeks in return, and that raises Acted’s profile as a credible, principled partner for responsible business in Syria.
2. To secure private sector funding, co-investment and in-kind support by building and managing a pipeline of partnerships that deliver a win-win for communities and for private partners.
3. To strengthen TVET systems and skills-to-jobs pathways in Acted’s areas of, define coherent implementation modalities, tools and methodologies, provide technical support to economic recovery and climate finance projects involving private partners, and build the capacity of relevant staff.
4. To ensure every private sector partnership is community-anchored, conflict-sensitive and compliant, protecting Acted’s independence and in line with Acted’s policies and principles.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Private Sector Partnerships and Resource Mobilization**

**1.1 Strategy Planning**

- Lead the development, and annual update, of Acted Syria’s private sector engagement strategy in collaboration with the Country Director, the Deputy Country Director – Program, aligned with Acteds strategic priorities and with the sector strategy on economic recovery and employment pathways.
- Map and prioritize target sectors and companies and analyze each actor’s interests, risks and expectations.

**1.2 Business Development and Fundraising**

- Own the private sector pipeline from first contact to signed agreement: identify, approach, qualify and track prospects, and report regularly to Country Director and Deputy Country Director – Programs.
- Develop tailored pitches, concept notes and partnership proposals that show how a project serves both community needs and the partner’s interests.
- Identify and pursue funding structures that combine private and institutional resources (co-financing, blended finance and development finance instruments).
- Contribute to institutional donor fundraising for the economic recovery and development portfolio (in coordination with the relevant Technical Coordinators) by identifying new funding opportunities and proposing project ideas, approaches and strategies.

**1.3 Due Diligence, Risk and Compliance**

- Conduct and document due diligence and screening of prospective partners (ownership, reputation, human rights and conflict-sensitivity, sanctions and legal compliance)

**2. External Positioning and Project Development**

**2.1 External Relations**

- Act as a key Acted representative with private sector actors, TVET institutions, financial service providers and relevant authorities, and in business economic development vis-a-vis project stakeholders, including donors and partners.
- Ensure effective coordination and collaboration with NGOs, civil society organizations, community groups and government counterparts working on topics relevant to Acted programming, including TVET and skills development, MSME and enterprise development, financial inclusion and market systems development.
- Identify opportunities to collaborate with other organizations, research institutions, learning platforms and formal and informal networks.

**2.2 Project Development**

- Collect, analyze and disseminate primary and secondary data on labor markets, market systems and private sector development in Syria, including employer skills demand and company investment interests, to support evidence-based project development and anticipate new trends and needs. This includes mapping companies’ CSR and ESG commitments, corporate foundations, and the Gulf, Turkish and diaspora investors now entering Syria, as well as private pooled funds (e.g., CoAction’s PSHA) and development finance institutions (e.g., the World Bank and IFC).
- Provide technical inputs into the design of needs assessments led by program field teams and/or MEAL teams, in coordination with relevant Technical Coordinators.
- Develop and maintain standard partnership tools, including MoU and partnership agreement templates, pitch decks to enable consistent and timely engagement with private sector partners.
- Ensure alignment with Acted’s private sector engagement strategy, coordinating regularly with HQ private sector colleagues on approaches, tools and partnership opportunities.

**3. TVET Systems Strengthening and Technical Leadership**

**3.1 Employer-led TVET and Skills-to-Jobs**

- Lead Acted Syria’s approach to TVET systems strengthening, placing private sector demand at its center: apprenticeships and work-based learning, recognized certification, placement and local hiring pathways.
- Build partnerships between TVET institutions, training centers and authorities on one side and the private actors that need skilled labor on the other, linking each partnership to community priorities and to access for vulnerable groups.
- Ensure TVET interventions integrate decent work and employment pathways and gender inclusion, and meet recognized standards.

**3.2 Technical Leadership**

- Identify the needs of existing businesses, such as skills, local hiring, suppliers and local services, and respond with tailored business solutions, including service contracts with local companies and multinationals.
- Work closely with the FSL Technical Coordinator, who leads Acted’s wider TVET programming, so that company needs identified by this role feed into TVET projects where relevant.
- Ensure that service contracts and business solutions are delivered with sound targeting, participant selection, progress monitoring and results reporting to partners, in close collaboration with project managers and MEAL staff.
- Provide technical support for implementation modalities and methodologies of projects with TVET, enterprise development, MSME or market systems components (technical specifications, geo-targeting, registration and selection of beneficiaries, support provision schemes, progress monitoring and impact evaluation), in close collaboration with project managers and MEAL staff.
- Provide technical guidance on access-to-finance where they link to private partners, such as matching grants, revolving funds and links to microfinance institutions and financial service providers.
- Lead on investor-backed revolving fund models, where programme activity generates cash that is reinvested to expand the programme, as part of Acted’s private sector engagement.Coordinate with the FSL and Recovery & Resilience Technical Coordinator on linkages to climate adaptation, sustainable agriculture, food systems and climate finance.
- Facilitate the planning and integration of sound employment and economic development strategies into Acted’s area-based programming, in coordination with relevant Technical Coordinators, to strengthen local economies and employment opportunities.
- Disseminate tools, research, best practices and lessons learned internally and externally through publications, networks, working groups, events and conferences.

**4. Internal Coordination and Staff Capacity Building**

**4.1 Coordination**

- Lead Acted Syria’s private sector engagement approach as part of the country strategy, ensuring every business partnership and service contract is guided by the 3ZERO lens (zero exclusion, zero carbon, zero poverty) and benefits communities inclusively.
- Work closely with the FSL/Livelihoods TC and the Resilience & Recovery TC so that business needs and opportunities identified with companies feed into our TVET, small business and market systems programming, and so that our programming can respond to them.
- Organize regular coordination with Technical Coordinators, Project Development and Area Coordinators to share private sector leads, align on approaches and agree who leads on each opportunity.

**4.2 Staff Capacity Building**

- Brief and train project managers and area coordinators on private sector engagement, partnership standards and TVET good practice, drawing on Acted Global and external sources.
- Collect, review and validate existing guidance and training materials, and develop new tools as needed (e.g. pitches, due diligence checklists, SOPs, and ToRs for consultants and evaluators).

**KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

- % annual budget increase/decrease in the private sector portfolio as compared to previous year
- Number of quality concept notes and proposals submitted, and conversion rate to signed agreements
- Number of technical documents and tools produced (strategies, guidance, checklists, methodologies), number of staff trained, and % of trained staff with improved capacity
- % of projects with private sector components meeting implementation targets (timeliness, quality and target achievement)
- Number of active strategic partnerships with the private sector and % change as compared to previous year
- Number of staff trained on private sector engagement and partnerships development.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Bachelor’s degree required and above; Master’s degree in international development, business, economics, public policy or a related field is an advantage
- Fluent English and Arabic (written and spoken);
- Excellent writing and communication skills;
- At least 6 years’ relevant professional experience in development, early recovery or social impact work, including at least 4 years in private sector engagement and partnership building;
- Demonstrated experience in project proposal development and private sector engagement
- Strong knowledge of TVET systems strengthening, including employer engagement, apprenticeships and work-based learning, curricula and certification, preferably in fragile or transitional contexts
- Proven external engagement expertise: stakeholder mapping, pitching, negotiation and representing an organization to external audiences, including businesses, donors and government counterparts
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and coordination architecture, and ability to understand donor and governmental requirements;
- Experience providing technical guidance, capacity building and training to program teams;
- Direct experience in access-to-finance / financial inclusion programming or private sector partnership building is an advantage;
- Previous work experience in Syria and/or the MENA region is an advantage;
- Ability to work under pressure in a high-pace and multi-cultural environment;
- Good organisational and prioritisation skills;
- Strong interpersonal skills;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint);
- Ability to travel across Acted's areas of operation in Syria as required;

title: Data Entry Operator (Syria - Lattakia)
body:
**Job Title: Data Entry Operator**

**Job location: Syria – Lattakia**

**Work Type: Full Time**

**Reports to: Program Coordinator**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Data Entry Operator is the focal point for nutrition data. The role enters, cleans, and reports nutrition data, tracks CMAM cases with the technical team on a daily basis, follows up on scheduled follow-up visits and records, alerts the team to upcoming visits, and organizes reviews between the technical team and the data team to ensure accurate and timely data.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Nutrition data focal point and CMAM case tracking:**

1\. Act as the focal point for nutrition data in the assigned area, and link the technical team with the data team.

2\. Track CMAM cases (SAM and MAM) with the technical team on a daily basis, from admission to discharge, including outcomes (cured, defaulter, referred, non-response).

3\. Maintain the follow-up schedule, alert the team to upcoming follow-up visits, and follow up on missed visits and defaulters with the team.

4\. Ensure that registers, beneficiary cards, and records are complete, accurate, and up to date.

5\. Organize regular data reviews between the technical team and the data team to resolve errors and queries.

**Data entry and data quality:**

6\. Enter and update nutrition data in the relevant databases (Excel and KoBo) on time.

7\. Clean and verify nutrition data by identifying and correcting errors, duplicates, missing data, and inconsistencies.

8\. Compile the required data from all centers according to the reporting schedule.

9\. Compile nutrition supply stock data periodically from stock reports, and reconcile it with distribution records and nutrition technicians.

10\. Store hard and electronic copies of data in an organized way for easy retrieval.

**Reporting and data tools:**

11\. Prepare weekly and monthly reports on caseload, case outcomes, and data quality, and submit them to the Program Coordinator on time.

12\. Develop and maintain data tools (such as Excel trackers, KoBo forms, and dashboards) to improve data quality and case follow-up.

13\. Support the team on data-related technical issues, such as data collection tools and forms.

**Other:**

14\. Comply with MedGlobal policies, data protection rules, and child safeguarding standards.

15\. Participate in all trainings and orientation meetings, which may sometimes be held during weekends.

16\. Perform other related tasks assigned by the line manager.

**1QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

**Requirements (essential):**

1\. University degree or student in nutrition, health, computer science, statistics, or a related field.

2\. Minimum 2 years of experience in data management or reporting.

3\. At least one year of experience in community nutrition or CMAM programs in Syria.

4\. Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Excel and KoBo.

**Requirements (desired):**

1\. Experience in CMAM case tracking and follow-up.

2\. Knowledge of Power BI.

3\. Experience coordinating with field teams.

4\. Strong communication and organizational skills.

5\. Close attention to detail and the ability to work under pressure.

**ABOUT MEDGLOBAL**

MedGlobal is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

MedGlobal Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to MedGlobal employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

title: Data Entry Operator (Syria - Homs)
body:
**Job Title: Data Entry Operator**

**Job location: Syria – Homs**

**Work Type: Full Time**

**Reports to: Program Coordinator**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Data Entry Operator is the focal point for nutrition data. The role enters, cleans, and reports nutrition data, tracks CMAM cases with the technical team on a daily basis, follows up on scheduled follow-up visits and records, alerts the team to upcoming visits, and organizes reviews between the technical team and the data team to ensure accurate and timely data.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Nutrition data focal point and CMAM case tracking:**

1\. Act as the focal point for nutrition data in the assigned area, and link the technical team with the data team.

2\. Track CMAM cases (SAM and MAM) with the technical team on a daily basis, from admission to discharge, including outcomes (cured, defaulter, referred, non-response).

3\. Maintain the follow-up schedule, alert the team to upcoming follow-up visits, and follow up on missed visits and defaulters with the team.

4\. Ensure that registers, beneficiary cards, and records are complete, accurate, and up to date.

5\. Organize regular data reviews between the technical team and the data team to resolve errors and queries.

**Data entry and data quality:**

6\. Enter and update nutrition data in the relevant databases (Excel and KoBo) on time.

7\. Clean and verify nutrition data by identifying and correcting errors, duplicates, missing data, and inconsistencies.

8\. Compile the required data from all centers according to the reporting schedule.

9\. Compile nutrition supply stock data periodically from stock reports, and reconcile it with distribution records and nutrition technicians.

10\. Store hard and electronic copies of data in an organized way for easy retrieval.

**Reporting and data tools:**

11\. Prepare weekly and monthly reports on caseload, case outcomes, and data quality, and submit them to the Program Coordinator on time.

12\. Develop and maintain data tools (such as Excel trackers, KoBo forms, and dashboards) to improve data quality and case follow-up.

13\. Support the team on data-related technical issues, such as data collection tools and forms.

**Other:**

14\. Comply with MedGlobal policies, data protection rules, and child safeguarding standards.

15\. Participate in all trainings and orientation meetings, which may sometimes be held during weekends.

16\. Perform other related tasks assigned by the line manager.

1\. University degree or student in nutrition, health, computer science, statistics, or a related field.

2\. Minimum 2 years of experience in data management or reporting.

4\. Excellent proficiency in Microsoft Excel and KoBo.

**Requirements (desired):**

1\. Experience in CMAM case tracking and follow-up.

3\. Experience coordinating with field teams.

4\. Strong communication and organizational skills.

5\. Close attention to detail and the ability to work under pressure.
