Coordinate with logistics teams to ensure availability of medicines, PPE and IPC supplies.

Monitor stock levels and support appropriate use and storage of supplies.

Medical Doctor, Nurse or other recognised health qualification.

Experience supervising health staff and implementing health programmes.

Good computer and reporting skills.

Good written and spoken French.

Qualification in Public Health, Infectious Diseases or Tropical Medicine.

Humanitarian NGO experience.

Experience in Ebola, outbreak response, surveillance or IPC programmes

## Behavioural Competencies

Strong servant leadership and teamwork skills.

Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Flexible, resilient and able to work under pressure.

Strong organisational and prioritisation skills.

Commitment to quality and continuous learning

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

title: CELL INTERN – Desk 4
body:
## Join MSF OCG as a CELL INTERN – Desk 4!

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 9 months at 100%

### Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

### Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The Cell Intern provides operational and administrative support to the Cell Team with an additional objective of working on at least one Medico-Operational dossiers during the period of employment. The Cell Intern function can be part of an academic course (cursus intra or extra-academic’) or a federal program on professional integration. For this reason, most placements as Cell Intern require a 3-party convention with the academic institute concerned.

### Tasks & Responsibilities

*Operational Support*

- Supports the cell in the organization of meetings (i.e. the weekly cell meeting (Mini Desk), Plan of Action discussions with field teams) including the preparation of agendas, taking minutes and the archiving of meeting documentation.
- Supports the cell in the management of information such as cell archiving, is the focal point for the online platforms such as Kompas and Share Point and manages the key tools for the organization of the cell (i.e. presence, field visit preparation).
- Supports the preparation of key Operational documents and Presentations for either internal or external use.
- Provides support to the RLO (Logistic Referent) of the cell: follow up of material to be sent to missions, ordering of maps via the GIS center.
- Provides support to the FINOP (Finance Referent) to prepare Power of Attorney for mission teams, follow up of contracts and partnership agreements, and the management of information related to audits.
- Provides adhoc support to the Directorate of Operations such as management of meetings, minute taking and the coordination of operational and planning documents (portfolio reviews, emergency updates).
- Monitors the news update and different reports on the context of the countries followed by the cell in collaboration with the advocacy department.
- By delegation from the RP can be asked to provide operational updates to the HQ (Point Info).

*HR and Administrative Support*

- Ensures the updating of the international staff tracking table (HR Update) (mission dates, job openings, obtaining documents)
- Follows up with international staff on documents required for their departure (informed consents (BIC), proof of life)
- Organizes briefings/debriefings of international staff with the cell members
- Consolidates, monitors and updates pre-departure briefing materials for international staff
- Welcome international staff on departure, introduce them to current operations and ensure they have the necessary documents
- Compiles a table of the cell's mission positions to be opened, on a weekly basis
- Participate in monthly meetings to open positions and present the cell's operational news
- Files the job descriptions of international staff as soon as a position is required by the unit's missions
- Files documents for anticipated returns
- Follows up on other specific HR procedures as needed
- Develop HR statistics with the assistance of the RHOP

*Medico Operational Dossiers*

- Each Cell Intern, during the period of employment (from 6 months to 9 months) is expected to work on a Medico Operational Dossier. The dossier selected should combine (a) the operational needs of the Cell / Missions (b) academic requirements such as the need to complete a thesis and (c) if possible, a link to the future career of the Cell Intern.
- The topic needs to be selected within the first month of employment and agreed with the RP, ensuring that there is a clear deliverable (written report, thesis, …).
- The final deliverable MUST be presented to the Operations Department at the end of the period of employment.

### Your profile

*Education*

- Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Political Science, Humanitarian or Development Studies, or other relevant degree in prgoress

*Experience*

- No specific requirements in terms of work experience, but having had some form of employment in the past is considered an advantage.

*Languages*

- Fluent English and French (written and spoken).

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Capacity of analysis and synthesis;
- Planning and organization;
- Knowledge of key issues of the humanitarian environment;
- Excellent writing skills;
- Excellent knowledge of the MO environment (Powerpoint, Excel, Word)

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Team player; ability to coordinate with numerous stakeholders;
- Ability to work autonomously;
- Pro-active and solution-oriented
- Flexible and capacity to adapt quickly

### Terms of employment

- A tripartite internship agreement is mandatory.
- 6 to 9 months, according to internship agreement.
- Full time (40h/week).
- Based in Geneva, Switzerland
- Start date : 15th of February 2027
- Gross monthly remuneration 2'000.- CHF

title: Chargé(e) Protection et Cohésion Sociale
Public Health Medical Referent - Infectious Diseases (ID) Apply
body:
**MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people.**

**We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect.**   
  
At the moment MSF-OCA is looking for a:  
  
**Infectious Diseases (ID) Public Health Medical Referent - OCA Public Health Department**

The OCA Public Health Department is seeking an experienced Infectious Diseases professional to support clinicians working in Ebola Treatment Centres (ETCs) and other Viral Haemorrhagic Fever (VHF) contexts. The position focuses on strengthening the quality of patient care through technical support, coaching, mentoring, and field accompaniment of clinical teams.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Provide technical support, coaching, and mentoring to clinicians working in Ebola and other VHF contexts.
- Brief staff prior to deployment and provide ongoing remote and field-based support.
- Conduct regular field visits to strengthen clinical practice and quality of care.
- Support quality improvement initiatives through activities such as mortality reviews and rational prescription analysis.
- Strengthen systems and structures to improve quality of care in this and future VHF responses.
- Ensure clinical teams are guided by the latest best practice and evidence-based recommendations.
- Collaborate with relevant referents, including the current Infectious Diseases Advisors, to strengthen palliative care approaches.
- Act as a VHF technical resource for the Staff Health Unit regarding IMS and LHS Ebola-related health concerns.
- Analyze patient outcomes and programme data from OCA-run and OCA-supported treatment centres to identify opportunities for improving clinical care and patient pathways.
- Contribute to training and capacity-building initiatives for MSF and Ministry of Health staff.

**We are looking for a candidate who has:**

- Previous experience working in an Ebola response or other VHF context.
- Strong NGO field experience, preferably with MSF.
- Demonstrated experience of coaching and mentoring clinical teams.
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate clinical findings into improved patient care.
- Excellent collaboration and communication skills.
- A minimum French language level of C1.

**Deployment and Contract Conditions**

The position requires approximately 50-60% field deployment, with the remaining time dedicated to technical support, analysis, coordination, and mentoring activities.

Amsterdam or London are the preferred duty stations. Nairobi and Berlin may also consider suitable candidates. Flexibility regarding headquarters presence may be required depending on operational, travel, visa or quarantine constraints.

Please note: Accommodation is provided during field deployments only. Candidates are responsible for arranging and funding their own accommodation at their duty station when not deployed.

The anticipated start date is as soon as possible. The initial contract duration is 6 months, with the possibility of a 6-month extension.

title: Finance Coordinator
body:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organisation that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **TERMS OF REFERENCE**

- **Job Title:** Finance Coordinator
- **Code:** SR-28-10345
- **Duty station:** Kabul
- **Starting date:** 01/01/2027
- **Contract duration:** 12 months
- **Reporting to:** Head of Mission
- **Functional Supervisor:** Regional Finance Coordinator
- **Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

## **GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE CONTEXT**

Over the past few years, Afghanistan has witnessed a relative improvement in security and stability across much of the country. This has allowed humanitarian actors like INTERSOS to maintain uninterrupted access and expand services in areas that were previously hard to reach. Despite this progress, the humanitarian situation remains critical, with millions of Afghans continuing to face acute vulnerabilities due to prolonged economic hardship, natural disasters, and limited access to essential services.

In 2025, more than half of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance, with food insecurity, child malnutrition, and displacement remaining key concerns. Natural disasters, such as floods and recent earthquakes, have further compounded the needs of already struggling communities.

INTERSOS continues to operate through a community-based approach with field bases in Kabul, Kandahar, Zabul, Helmand, Herat, Nimroz delivering primary healthcare, nutrition, and protection services with a focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities. The organization enjoys strong community acceptance and collaborates closely with relevant national authorities, including maintaining the full participation of female staff in all activities.

While the operational environment is largely stable and conducive, funding shortfalls and systemic barriers such as restrictions on financial flows and administrative bottlenecks continue to impact the scope and scale of humanitarian response. Sustained support is crucial to ensure the continuity of life-saving services and to address the urgent needs of Afghanistan’s most vulnerable populations.

## **GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE POSITION**

Define, coordinate and monitor the implementation and management of finance strategies, policies, internal control and all financial administrative in the mission, in line with the context and operational challenges and INTERSOS protocols, standards and procedures, and with the Regional Finance Coordinator’s directions, in order to provide accurate, transparent, timely and reliable financial information to the organization and third parties on the allocation of resources in the projects.

## **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS**

**Strategy and budget**

- As an active member of the Senior Management Team, participate in the definition of the missions’ objectives and strategies planning, implementing and monitoring the financial operational and budget needs, anticipating changes and challenges and planning accordingly, in order to ensure budget is appropriate
- Define the financial strategy for the mission and the country, assessing and mitigating the financial risks of the mission, and the project economic and financial plan together with the Head of Mission and linking with the Project Managers
- Provide regular and adequate indicators to monitor the financial position of the mission and provide relevant cost analysis, regularly monitor of expenses vs budget, analyse variances and suggest corrective actions when needed
- Provide support to the Head of Mission and Programme Coordinator on drafting new projects and budget preparation, ensuring the collaboration of other support Departments (HR, Log, Security)

**Accounting and Treasury**

- Ensure the accounting process is efficient and accurate, foreseeing an adequate level of verification and segregation of duties based on the dimension and the staff of the mission. The accounting database must be compliant with the INTERSOS’ standard accounting practices, reconciled on a monthly basis following the standard internal control mechanisms and enforce an effective monitoring of payment of suppliers, social/tax institutions and staffs salaries
- Coordinate the efficient management of the treasury including to ensure the smooth running of operations and maintain control on security risks. This includes among other things, definition of minimum levels of cash, cash-flow forecast for projects and NGO, management of local bank accounts, bank/cash reconciliation, transfer of funds to field bases, relations with banks and/or other financial institutions at mission level, identify in advance the financial issues and cash crunch
- Ensure proper implementation and respect of INTERSOS policies and guidelines and compliance with donors procedures, ensuring they are aligned with legal requirements and within the national legal framework, and designing or adapting relevant local policies, procedures and tools for optimized management of the mission's financial resources
- Sensitize key executive staffs as coordinators, budget holders and relevant management on financial risks and the extent of their financial responsibilities
- In collaboration with Regional Finance Coordinator manage the funding agreements with donors e.g. coordinating and preparing proposals and financial reports and managing donor contracts
- Ensure the implementation of a relevant mission organizational set up and a reliable internal control system, in order to meet all financial obligations while keeping financial ethics respected within the mission and making use of the New Accounting Information System, or when not available, using the tools and templates provided by the procedural protocols

**Administration and HR**

- Is responsible for mission administrative-accounting documents and all finished project documentation. Submit to the Regional Finance Coordinator and the HQ Finance Director the accounting reports and the supporting official documentation on individual projects and contracts
- Collaborate with HR department to accomplish the administrative requirements related to staffs related matters
- Coordinate and oversee the monthly and yearly closing of accounts guarantying that the statement reflects the financial reality of the mission

**People management**

- Is responsible for the management, supervision and development of the finance team, including coaching, training, motivating and ensuring their capability, detecting potential conflicts and finding solutions when necessary
- Participate to the HR processes (recruitment, training, briefing/debriefing, evaluation, potential, detection, staff’s development and internal communication) in order to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required for the activities he is accountable for.

**Logistics**

- In collaboration with the Logistics Coordinator ensure the proper execution of goods, works and services procurement processes in conformity with INTERSOS and donors’ guidelines

## **REQUIRED PROFILE AND EXPERIENCE**

### **Education**

- Essential degree in Economics/Finances

### **Professional experience**

- Essential 4 years’ experience in budget management and in team management
- Desirable previous experience with NGO’s in developing countries

### **Professional requirements**

- Essential computer literacy (word, excel, finance DB and internet)

### Languages

- Fluent English (spoken and written)

### **Personal requirements**

- Strategic vision
- Leadership
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Behavioural flexibility
- People management and development
- Service orientation
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles

## **GENERAL CONDITIONS AND BENEFITS**

- **Salary range:** 12 - 3.690€ - 4.245€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** INTERSOS staff required to work for extended periods at duty stations under hazardous, stressful and difficult conditions are granted a regular and mandatory period of Rest and Recuperation (R&R). This is due to protecting their health and well-being and ensuring optimal work performance upon the resumption of their duties, while, at the same time, preserving the operational readiness of the Organisation. R&R benefits are not financial compensation for the degree of hardship and insecurity of a duty station. Eligibility: staff members recruited as international field staff whose contract states one R&R Duty Station as the main Duty Station and whose contract duration is equal to or longer than 4 calendar months. R&R: 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance; reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.

title: Chargé(e) Gestion de l’Information
body:
**Titre du poste : Chargé(e) Gestion de l’Information**

**Supervisé par : Chief of Party**

**Responsable hiérarchique technique : Spécialiste Protection et Cohésion Sociale**

**Lieu d’affectation : Garoua-BoulaÏ, Région de l’Est, Cameroun**

**Zone d’intervention : Territoire du Cameroun**

**Période considérée : 12 mois (possibilité d’extension)**

**Type de contrat : Contrat national**

**Salaire & Avantages : Non-Management, band H**

**INTRODUCTION**

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC, pour Danish Refugee Council) porte assistance aux réfugiés et aux personnes déplacées à travers le monde. Nous fournissons une aide d’urgence à ces personnes, défendons leurs droits et renforçons leurs opportunités pour un meilleur avenir. Nous travaillons dans les zones affectées par les conflits, le long des routes de déplacement ainsi que dans les pays où les réfugiés s’établissent. En coopération avec les communautés locales, nous nous efforçons de trouver des solutions responsables et durables. Nous œuvrons en faveur d’une intégration réussie des communautés vulnérables et, lorsque cela est possible, à la réalisation de leur souhait de retourner chez elles.

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC) a été fondé au Danemark en 1956 et est depuis devenu une organisation humanitaire internationale comptant plus de 7 000 employés et 8 000 volontaires. Son siège est établi à Copenhague et l’organisation est présente dans 40 pays. DRC est une organisation non gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, politiquement neutre, indépendante et non confessionnelle.

Notre vision est celle d’une vie avec dignité pour toutes les personnes déplacées dans le monde. Tous nos efforts reposent sur notre boussole morale : l’humanité, le respect, l’indépendance, la neutralité, la participation, l’honnêteté et la transparence.

**1. CONTEXTE**

Nous recherchons un(e) **Chargé(e) Gestion de l’information**qualifié(e) ayant expérience en gestion et analyse des données. Le candidat sélectionné travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l'Unité de gestion du consortium. Sous la supervision hiérarchique du Chief Of Party, technique des Spécialistes MEAL UGP et DRC et en étroite collaboration avec l’Unite de Gestion du Consortium (UGP).

**2. OBJET**

L’objectif général du poste est d’assurer la gestion du système d’information du programme, notamment des outils numériques de collecte, des bases de données, de la qualité, de la sécurité, de l’analyse et de la visualisation des données. De plus ce dernier (e) devra être disponible pour toute autre activité de DRC au cours de son contrat rentrant dans le cadre de son poste.

**3. RESPONSABILITES**

**1. Conception et gestion des systèmes d’information**

- Concevoir, développer, adapter et maintenir les outils numériques de collecte et de gestion des données, en fonction des besoins du programme et des équipes opérationnelles.
- Développer et administrer les formulaires de collecte, les bases de données et les outils de suivi des bénéficiaires et des activités.
- Structurer les bases de données et définir les flux de collecte, de traitement, de stockage et de partage de l’information.
- Assurer la mise à jour régulière des bases de données et veiller à leur disponibilité et à leur bon fonctionnement.
- Mettre en place des systèmes de suivi permettant de centraliser et de consolider les données provenant des différentes zones d’intervention et des partenaires.
- Contribuer à l’interconnexion des outils et des bases de données du programme, dans le respect des procédures et des exigences techniques applicables.

**2. Gestion de l’information de Protection (PIM)**

- Développer et administrer les bases de données de protection, en assurant la documentation et la structuration des informations issues du monitoring et des mécanismes communautaires, notamment les alertes et les risques de protection identifiés.
- Assurer la consolidation des informations de protection provenant des différentes sources et zones d'intervention, en maintenant la traçabilité des données et de leurs sources.
- Appuyer la mise à jour des bases de données sur les services et prestataires de protection, ainsi que sur les mécanismes d'orientation et de référencement.
- Élaborer des cartes, tableaux de bord, snapshots et autres produits de visualisation des informations de protection afin d'identifier les zones prioritaires et de faciliter le partage et l'utilisation des données, aussi bien en interne qu'avec les acteurs concernés, dans le respect des protocoles de confidentialité.
- Réaliser des analyses spécifiques à la protection portant notamment sur les tendances des risques, les profils de vulnérabilité, les incidents rapportés et les lacunes dans la disponibilité ou l'accessibilité des services.

**3. Qualité, sécurité et protection des données**

- Définir et appliquer des procédures de contrôle, de nettoyage, de validation et de vérification de la cohérence des données.
- Effectuer des contrôles réguliers afin d’identifier les doublons, les données manquantes, les erreurs de saisie et les incohérences.
- Accompagner les équipes et les partenaires dans l’amélioration de la qualité des données collectées et transmises.
- Mettre en œuvre les mesures de protection des bases de données, notamment la gestion des droits d’accès, la confidentialité, les sauvegardes, l’archivage et le contrôle des transferts d’informations.
- Veiller au respect des procédures institutionnelles relatives à la protection et au partage des données, particulièrement celles portant sur les informations sensibles et personnelles.
- Documenter les bases de données, les règles de validation, les procédures de nettoyage et les modifications apportées aux outils.

**4. Analyse, visualisation et diffusion des données**

- Traiter, consolider et analyser les données issues des activités de suivi, des enquêtes et des autres mécanismes de collecte du programme.
- Produire et actualiser des tableaux de bord, des graphiques et des outils de visualisation permettant de suivre les réalisations, les résultats et les indicateurs du programme.
- Élaborer des rapports analytiques, des fiches d’information, des notes de synthèse et d’autres produits d’information destinés aux équipes de mise en œuvre et aux parties prenantes.
- Identifier les tendances, les écarts et les éventuelles anomalies dans les données, et contribuer à leur interprétation avec les équipes MEAL et opérationnelles.
- Appuyer l’organisation de séances d’analyse et de partage des données afin de faciliter leur utilisation dans le pilotage du programme et la prise de décision.
- Fournir, dans les délais requis, les données et les produits d’information nécessaires au reporting interne et externe.

**5. Renforcement des capacités et assistance technique**

- Former et accompagner les équipes du programme et les partenaires dans l’utilisation des outils numériques de collecte, des bases de données et des systèmes de gestion de l’information.
- Fournir un appui technique aux utilisateurs pour résoudre les difficultés liées à la collecte, à la transmission, à la saisie et à l’exploitation des données.
- Élaborer et actualiser les guides d’utilisation, les fiches pratiques, les procédures opérationnelles et les supports de formation relatifs aux outils de gestion de l’information.
- Apporter un accompagnement technique aux équipes de terrain lors du déploiement ou de la modification des outils de collecte.
- Identifier les besoins de renforcement des capacités des utilisateurs et proposer des mesures adaptées pour améliorer leurs pratiques de gestion des données.

**6. Coordination et appui à la mise en œuvre**

- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les spécialistes MEAL UGP et DRC, l’UGP, les équipes sectorielles et les partenaires de mise en œuvre afin de garantir la cohérence des systèmes et des données du programme.
- Apporter un appui technique aux partenaires dans la structuration, la consolidation et la transmission des données relatives aux activités et aux bénéficiaires.
- Contribuer, en coordination avec le MINAS et les autres acteurs concernés, à la préparation, à la vérification et à la transmission des données destinées au Registre social unifié (RSU).
- Participer à l’harmonisation des outils, des formats de collecte et des procédures de gestion de l’information entre les différentes parties prenantes.
- Apporter un appui technique à la conception et à l’adaptation des questionnaires et des outils numériques utilisés dans les enquêtes, les évaluations et les exercices de collecte spécifiques.
- Participer aux missions de terrain nécessaires au déploiement des outils, au contrôle de la qualité des données et à l’accompagnement des équipes.
- Contribuer aux réunions techniques, aux cadres de coordination et aux exercices de partage d’informations liés à la gestion des données du programme

**4. QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES**

**Expérience et compétences techniques**

- Avoir une expérience professionnelle d’au moins 3 ans, pertinente et prouvée dans la gestion des données ;
- Maitrise des applications de collecte de données (Activity info, Kobo Collect, Odk, etc.) ;
- Expérience et compétences avérées dans les logiciels d'analyse et de visualisation de données tels que Kobo Collect, Power BI, R, Tableau, Qgis/ArcGIS, etc. ;
- Expérience de travail avec les ONG internationales ;
- Capacité à travailler en équipe et à communiquer de manière fluide ;
- Capacité à travailler sous pression.

**Qualifications souhaitables**

- L'achèvement d'une formation en gestion de l'information (IM).
- Une expérience en Microsoft Power Platform et Microsoft Fabric est un atout.

Une expérience dans la conception de sites Web et le développement de logiciels est un atout.

**Formation :** (y compris certificats, permis, etc.)

Diplôme universitaire en technologies de l'information, démographie, statistiques ou Formation spécialisée sur les systèmes de gestion de l'information (statistiques, science des données, Système d’Information Géographique (SIG), sciences juridiques, sciences sociales ou dans un domaine proche.

**Langues :**

- **Français : Maîtrise professionnelle**
- **Anglais : Bon niveau**
- **Connaissance d'une langue locale (Gbaya, Fulfulde, Sango, etc…) est un atout**

**5. REGLEMENTATIONS GENERALES**

- L’employé doit respecter les instructions et politiques de DRC en matière de sécurité, de confidentialité et d’éthique, y compris le Code de conduite et le cadre de responsabilité humanitaire ;
- L’employé ne doit exercer aucune autre activité rémunérée pendant la durée de son contrat avec DRC sans autorisation préalable, conformément aux politiques applicables ;
- L’employé ne doit s’engager dans aucune activité susceptible de nuire à DRC ou à la bonne mise en œuvre des projets pendant la durée de son contrat ;
- L’employé ne doit accorder d’interviews aux médias, publier des photos liées aux programmes de DRC ou partager des documents appartenant à DRC sans autorisation préalable ;
- L’employé doit restituer tout équipement mis à sa disposition par DRC pour l’exercice de ses fonctions à la fin de son contrat ou à la demande de DRC.

**6. COMPETENCES ET QUALITES EXIGEES**

À ce poste, le/la titulaire doit démontrer les cinq compétences essentielles de DRC :

- **Viser l’excellence :** se concentrer sur l’obtention de résultats tout en garantissant un processus efficace. S’efforcer de produire un travail précis, approfondi et professionnel, avec une utilisation optimale du temps et des ressources ;
- **Collaborer :** coopérer avec les parties concernées et les impliquer dans les processus pertinents, rechercher activement leur contribution et partager les informations clés. Soutenir les autres et favoriser un environnement propice au feedback ;
- **Prendre les rênes :** assumer la responsabilité de son travail et le prioriser en fonction de la vision et des objectifs généraux de DRC. Prendre des initiatives face aux défis et rechercher des solutions appropriées et innovantes ;
- **Communiquer :** communiquer de manière efficace, honnête et adaptée au contexte, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit. Pratiquer l’écoute active et favoriser le dialogue ;
- **Faire preuve d’intégrité :** respecter et promouvoir les normes les plus élevées en matière de conduite éthique et professionnelle, conformément aux valeurs et au Code de conduite de DRC, notamment en matière de prévention de l’exploitation, des abus et du harcèlement sexuels.

Le/la titulaire doit également démontrer :

- Capacité à travailler efficacement dans un environnement multiculturel ;
- Proactivité et approche coopérative et collaborative ;
- Excellentes capacités de communication, d’écoute active et de collaboration ;
- Bonnes capacités organisationnelles et attention aux détails ;
- Sens élevé de l’éthique et de l’intégrité professionnelle ;
- Capacité à travailler efficacement en équipe ;
- Flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation dans un environnement de travail dynamique.

title: CELL INTERN – Desk 2
body:
## Join MSF OCG as a CELL INTERN – Desk 2!

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 9 months at 100%

### Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

### Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The Cell Intern provides operational and administrative support to the Cell Team with an additional objective of working on at least one Medico-Operational dossiers during the period of employment. The Cell Intern function can be part of an academic course (cursus intra or extra-academic’) or a federal program on professional integration. For this reason, most placements as Cell Intern require a 3-party convention with the academic institute concerned.

### Tasks & Responsibilities

*Operational Support (50%)*

- Supports the cell in the organization of meetings (i.e. the weekly cell meeting (Mini Desk), Plan of Action discussions with field teams) including the preparation of agendas, taking minutes and the archiving of meeting documentation.
- Supports the cell in the management of information such as cell archiving, is the focal point for the online platforms such as Kompas and Share Point and manages the key tools for the organization of the cell (i.e. presence, field visit preparation).
- Supports the preparation of key Operational documents and Presentations for either internal or external use.
- Provides support to the RLO (Logistic Referent) of the cell: follow up of material to be sent to missions, ordering of maps via the GIS center.
- Provides support to the FINOP (Finance Referent) to prepare Power of Attorney for mission teams, follow up of contracts and partnership agreements, and the management of information related to audits.
- Provides adhoc support to the Directorate of Operations such as management of meetings, minute taking and the coordination of operational and planning documents (portfolio reviews, emergency updates).
- Monitors the news update and different reports on the context of the countries followed by the cell.
- By delegation from the RP can be asked to provide operational updates to the HQ (Point Info).

*HR and Administrative Support (30%)*

- Ensures the updating of the international staff tracking table (HR Update) (mission dates, job openings, obtaining documents)
- Follows up with international staff on documents required for their departure (informed consents (BIC), proof of life)
- Organizes briefings/debriefings of international staff with the cell members
- Consolidates, monitors and updates pre-departure briefing materials for international staff
- Welcome international staff on departure, introduce them to current operations and ensure they have the necessary documents
- Compiles a table of the cell's mission positions to be opened, on a weekly basis
- Participate in monthly meetings to open positions and present the cell's operational news
- Files the job descriptions of international staff as soon as a position is required by the unit's missions
- Files documents for anticipated returns
- Follows up on other specific HR procedures as needed
- Develop HR statistics with the assistance of the RHOP

*Medico Operational Dossiers (20%)*

- Each Cell Intern, during the period of employment (from 6 months to 9 months) is expected to work on a Medico Operational Dossier. The dossier selected should combine (a) the operational needs of the Cell / Missions (b) academic requirements such as the need to complete a thesis and (c) if possible, a link to the future career of the Cell Intern.
- The topic needs to be selected within the first month of employment and agreed with the RP, ensuring that there is a clear deliverable (written report, thesis, …).
- The final deliverable MUST be presented to the Operations Department at the end of the period of employment.

### Your profile

*Education*

- Master’s degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, Political Science, Humanitarian Or Development Studies in progress

*Experience*

- No specific requirements in terms of work experience, but having had some form of employment in the past is considered an advantage.

*Languages*

- Fluent English and French (written and spoken).

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Capacity of analysis and synthesis;
- Planning and organization;
- Knowledge of key issues of the humanitarian environment;
- Excellent writing skills;
- Excellent knowledge of the MO environment (Powerpoint, Excel, Word)

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Team player; ability to coordinate with numerous stakeholders;
- Ability to work autonomously;
- Pro-active and solution-oriented
- Flexible and capacity to adapt quickly

### Terms of employment

- A tripartite internship agreement is mandatory.
- 6 to 9 months, according to internship agreement.
- Full time (40h/week).
- Based in Geneva, Switzerland
- Start date : 18th of January 2027
- Gross monthly remuneration 2'000.- CHF

title: Regional Senior Research Officer for Middle East & Asia - Global, based in Amman
body:
## We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to join our Research Quality Assurance Unit in Amman, Jordan (IMPACT’s Multi-country office for Middle East and Asia)

**Division:** HQ Programs, Communications and Research

**Reporting to:** Manager of HQ Research Quality Assurance Unit

**Location:** Amman, Jordan

**Duration:** 9 months (with potential for extension)

**Start date:** December 2026/January 2027.

## **POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Programmes, Communications and Research (PCR) teams at IMPACT HQ were established to ensure the organisation continues to deliver high-impact, high-quality, research programmes through user-centered design, implementation of core quality standards, country implementation support, and amplifying impact through effective communications and advocacy. This is supported by robust internal systems for data, GIS and MEAL.

Within this set-up, the Research Quality Assurance (RQA) Unit acts as a “guardian” of research quality, ethics, and compliance within IMPACT. This means:

Ensuring that all IMPACT teams (global and country) have the knowledge, tools and capacities for the consistent production of rigorous, credible, and responsible evidence across different contexts; and

Continuously strengthening research methods, tools, processes through a learning-based approach.

Through these functions, the RQA Unit will contribute towards achieving *Objective 2 - Pioneering Research Excellence -* within [IMPACT’s 2030 Strategic Framework](https://www.impact-initiatives.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/IMPACT-Strategic-Framework-2025-2030_VF.pdf). To help achieve this, the Senior Research Officer will play a key role in ensuring research implementation is meeting or exceeding IMPACT’s quality standards, providing country teams with technical guidance, peer review support, and learning support across different stages of the research implementation cycle.

The Senior Research Officer will be based in Amman, Jordan - IMPACT’s Multi-country office for Middle East and Asia - and will be focusing their support for country operations within this regional portfolio. This could involve occasional travel to the countries, to work directly with specific teams, as and when requested.

### **CORE TASKS & RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Support implementation of research standards, especially for IMPACT’s country operations in Middle East and Asia;***

- i.e. implement quality control processes and provide technical backstopping and learning support for research implementation, to ensure all teams are complying with established standards, as defined within IMPACT’s Research Toolkit. This includes:
- Act as the HQ RQA Unit focal point for the Middle East and Asia region and provide day-to-day support and advice to country teams on different stages of research implementation, while ensuring proper documentation of all key outputs
- Support the transition to more streamlined and decentralised quality assurance processes at the country level, including the development of reviewer tools and training, and any other required capacity strengthening or mentoring support
- \[In collaboration with Global Programme teams\] Provide technical guidance and support for research planning and methodology design, primarily for quantitative research
- \[In collaboration with Global Programme teams\] Provide peer review support for research design, quantitative data processing and analysis, and narrative information products
- Flag and discuss relevant risks with Unit Manager in a timely manner
- Provide other research implementation support as needed, including temporary in-country deployments (“surge support”) to country teams *– this could represent up to 25% of the total working time under this contract.*

***Strengthen research standards through a learning-based approach*** i.e. implement internal learning processes to continuously strengthen IMPACT’s research methods, tools and outcomes. This includes:

- Support with the development, maintenance of relevant learning solutions (e.g. guidance notes, online courses, quarterly webinars, tailored training sessions) to ensure uptake and application of the Research Toolkit across all teams, primarily within the Middle East and Asia region
- \[In collaboration with MEAL team\] Contribute to the regular review and consolidation of research-related lessons learned and best practices, including in the implementation of regular ‘Quality Monitoring’ exercises to identify, address key gaps vis-à-vis IMPACT’s Research Quality Framework
- Identify and integrate required improvements to research processes and guidelines
- \[On an ad-hoc, by need basis only\] **Support research implementation in other regions / countries** as directed by Unit Manager and based on the team’s workflow and/ or organisational priorities.

## **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- **Work experience:** At least 3 years of relevant work experience in designing and implementing primary research programmes, preferably in humanitarian or international development contexts
- **Academic qualifications:** Master’s degree or equivalent in relevant discipline (e.g. Social Research, Economics, Data Science, Statistics, Anthropology, International Development, or similar)
- **Language requirements:** Fluency in English.

## **REQUIRED TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES**

In addition to the seven Core Competencies expected from all IMPACT staff (i.e. Integrity, Learning, Resilience, Interpersonal Skills, Collaboration, Producing Quality Results, Problem Solving), the Senior Research Officer is also required to demonstrate the following technical competencies for this role:

- Quantitative Methodology Design *i.e. ability to develop clear and appropriate quantitative research methodologies, including indicators, tools, sampling, and analysis strategies*
- Quantitative Data Processing and Management *i.e. ability to clean, process data while ensuring data quality*
- *Research Cycle Management, i.e. ability to ensure the research meets all minimum requirements and stated objectives throughout the research cycle.*
- Responsible Data Management *i.e. awareness and application of data privacy and ethical considerations in data collection and analysis*
- Statistics *i.e. ability to apply statistical concepts across the research cycle for rigorous research and analysis.*
- Programming *i.e. ability to use programming languages like Python or R, for data processing, cleaning, analysis, and visualization.*
- Overseeing Research Quality *i.e. ability to ensure all research meets required minimum standards.*

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of 400 USD *NB – IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.*
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction – 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Web Designer & Digital Communications Consultant (Only Ugandan Based Females) Previous applicants should not reapply.
body:
**About Bodmando Consulting Group**

Bodmando Consulting Group is a feminist international consulting firm registered in **Uganda** and **Kenya.** As a women-led social enterprise, Bodmando operates at the gender and climate nexus, driven by the vision of a world free from intergenerational poverty, gender inequality, and social injustice. Our work is anchored in intersectional analysis, systems thinking, and human-centred design, ensuring that every solution we craft is both inclusive and transformative. With a multidisciplinary core team spanning Africa, South Asia, and the MENA region, we deliver high-impact research, evaluation, capacity strengthening and strategic advisory services that blend contextual understanding with global best practices.

We further leverage a global consultancy network of over 1,000 technical experts, allowing rapid mobilization of specialized skills for complex, multi-country assignments. Through thought leadership, north-south collaboration, and co-creation, Bodmando continues unlocking value and generating evidence-based, scalable solutions that advance equity, sustainability, and impact. To date, we have successfully implemented more than 65 projects across 31 countries, empowering governments, donors, civil society organizations, and communities to design, implement, and learn from transformative interventions. ***Learn more about our work at*** [***www.bodmando.org***](http://www.bodmando.org)***.***

**Back ground**  
Bodmando Consulting Group is seeking a creative, technically competent and proactive Female Web Designer & Digital Communications consultant to manage and strengthen the organisation’s digital presence. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring that our website and social media platforms remain functional, current, professional and aligned with modern digital standards.

**Work location**

Kagoma, Wakiso district, Uganda

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The consultant will:

- Manage, maintain and regularly update the Bodmando Consulting Group website, including content, pages, images, project information, publications and other resources.
- Monitor website functionality, performance, security and user experience and promptly address technical issues.
- Continuously improve the website to ensure it remains modern, responsive, user-friendly and consistent with state-of-the-art web design practices.
- Manage and regularly update the organisation’s social media platforms, particularly **LinkedIn and X (formerly Twitter)**.
- Develop, design and publish professional digital content highlighting Bodmando’s projects, research, evaluations, achievements, opportunities and other organisational activities.
- Ensure consistent organisational branding and messaging across the website and social media platforms.
- Monitor digital engagement and periodically provide basic analytics on website and social media performance.

Applicants should have:

- A diploma or bachelor’s degree in Web Design, Information Technology, Computer Science, Digital Communications, Multimedia, Graphic Design or a related field.

title: Spécialiste Partenariats, Subventions et Reporting (Recrutement Interne et Externe)
Human-AI Collaboration Designer
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International works toward a world where everyone has a decent place to live. Achieving that vision requires both direct support to families and changes in the housing systems that shape whether low-income households can access affordable, appropriate, and resilient housing. Within Habitat, the Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter (TCIS) leads market systems and innovation efforts that influence private-sector, public-sector, and civil-society actors to improve housing outcomes at scale. TCIS identifies constraints within housing systems and works with partners to test, refine, and scale solutions across areas including housing finance, construction products and services, and enabling policy environments. As Habitat advances its 50 for 50 strategy, TCIS is also strengthening how its expertise, evidence, tools, and approaches can be accessed and applied across teams, geographies, and the wider Habitat network.

The Human-AI Collaboration Designer helps Habitat for Humanity redesign how work is performed by integrating human expertise, organizational knowledge, applied research, systems thinking, and emerging AI capabilities into practical, scalable workflows. Working across technical, operational, learning, research, and programmatic functions, this role analyzes existing processes, identifies opportunities for improvement, and design solutions that strengthen efficiency, decision-making, knowledge sharing, learning, and organizational effectiveness.

The position leads the design, testing, implementation, and continuous improvement of AI-enabled workflows, digital assistants, knowledge systems, learning tools, and collaborative work practices that augment human expertise and relationships. Through facilitation, workflow analysis, prototyping, user testing, and continuous learning, the Human-AI Collaboration Designer supports the responsible adoption of AI while maintaining a strong focus on human-centered design and mission impact. A key focus of the role is helping TCIS scale market systems development, housing systems analyses, technical assistance, learning, and innovation efforts by redesigning workflows and knowledge systems that enable teams to deliver greater reach and impact without proportional increases in resources.

The role serves as a bridge between subject matter experts, end users, and technology platforms, translating complex expertise into accessible tools, processes, and learning experiences. It strengthens the capability of individuals, teams, and partner organizations to adopt new ways of working, apply AI responsibly, and make more effective use of organizational knowledge.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Human-AI Collaboration Designer**

### **Help Shape the Future of Human-AI Collaboration at Habitat for Humanity!**

**Are you passionate about harnessing the power of artificial intelligence, human creativity, and innovative thinking to drive meaningful change?**

Habitat for Humanity International is seeking a forward-thinking and collaborative **Human-AI Collaboration Designer** to help transform how people, knowledge, and technology work together.

This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of **AI innovation, human-centered design, organizational learning, and systems thinking** while contributing to Habitat’s mission of building a world where everyone has a decent place to live.

If you thrive on solving complex challenges, designing practical solutions, and empowering others to embrace new ways of working, we invite you to explore this opportunity!

This position is ultimately focused on business transformation and organizational capability, combining strategic leadership with human-centered AI product design, evidence gathering and analysis, facilitated learning and systems thinking. It is not a technical specialist or IT role; rather it requires strong interpersonal skills and a deep understanding of how people work, learn, collaborate, and adapt to change. It is about designing better ways of working through human-AI collaboration.

- **Human-AI Workflow Design and Transformation (30%)**
    - Analyze, map, and evaluate existing organizational workflows, processes, and decision-making practices.
    - Identify opportunities to improve workflows through human-AI collaboration
    - Design and implement workflow improvements that increase efficiency, quality, scalability, user experience, and consistency.
    - Develop future-state operating models that integrate human expertise, organizational knowledge, and AI-enabled capabilities
    - Support teams in adopting redesigned workflows and practices
- **AI-Enabled Solution Design and Implementation (20%)**
    - Design, develop, test, deploy, and continuously improve AI-enabled tools, agents, digital assistants, knowledge systems, and workflow solutions
    - Translate business, technical, and learning requirements into practical solutions
    - Design human oversight, validation points, and quality-assurance processes within AI-supported workflows.
    - Prototype, test, and refine solutions based on user feedback and evolving organizational needs
    - Support adoption and continuous improvement of AI-enabled solutions across teams and functions.
- **Organizational Learning and Knowledge Systems (15%)**
    - Design and maintain approaches that make institutional knowledge more accessible, reusable, and actionable.
    - Convert technical expertise, applied research, methodologies, and lessons learned into practical tools, resources, and learning experiences.
    - Promote continuous learning and knowledge sharing across teams.
    - Contribute to the development of repeatable tools, playbooks, and resources that support organizational effectiveness.
- **Facilitation and Change Enablement (15%)**
    - Facilitate workshops, workflow design sessions, systems mapping processes, simulations and learning experiences.
    - Engage stakeholders to identify needs, prototype solutions, gather feedback, and support implementation.
    - Support change management efforts that enable sustainable adoption of redesigned workflows and technology-enabled solutions.
- **Strategic Innovation and Market Systems Enablement (10%)**
    - Support TCIS strategic priorities by applying housing systems, affordable housing, housing finance, climate-resilient housing, and market systems expertise to workflow design and capacity building efforts.
    - Identify opportunities where human-AI collaboration can improve TCIS’ ability to support market systems development and expansion including through the MicroBuild Impact and Innovation Hub.
    - Monitor emerging technologies, methodologies, and practices and identify opportunities to strengthen learning, knowledge management, and organizational effectiveness.
    - Contribute to the development of scalable approaches that can be adapted across multiple teams, countries, and contexts.
- **Partnership and Cross-Functional Collaboration (10%)**
    - Serve as a connector between subject matter experts, program teams, operational functions, and technology stakeholders.
    - Collaborate across regions, departments, and technical disciplines to co-design solutions that address organizational challenges.
    - Build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders involved in innovation, learning, and organizational improvement initiatives.
    - Support cross-functional projects that advance organizational priorities and objectives.

**n**

- - Bachelor's degree in Organizational Development, Human-Centered Design, Learning and Development, International Development, Public Policy, Knowledge Management, Information Systems, Business Administration, Social Sciences, or a related field required.
        - Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred
- - Minimum of 7-10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in organizational development, innovation, process improvement, knowledge management, learning and development, digital transformation, international development, or a related field.
        - Experience analyzing and redesigning complex workflows, processes, or organizational systems
        - Experience designing, implementing, and scaling technology enabled solutions, AI enabled workflows, digital assistants, or knowledge systems.
        - Experience facilitating workshops, stakeholder engagement processes, and collaborative problem-solving sessions.
        - Experience translating complex technical, operational, programmatic or research content into practical tools, guidance, and learning resources.
        - Experience working across multiple teams, functions, cultures, or geographic regions.
        - Experience supporting organizational change and adoption of new processes, tools, or ways of working
- - Experience working within Habitat for Humanity's global network or within a similarly distributed, federated, or matrixed organization.
        - Experience applying systems thinking, human centered design, market systems development, organizational learning, or process improvement methodologies.
        - Experience supporting international development, social impact, research, learning, innovation, or technical assistance programs, particularly with local civil society organizations in developing and emerging economies
        - Experience building capability through facilitation, coaching, mentoring, or organizational learning approaches.

### **Why Join Habitat for Humanity?**

At Habitat for Humanity, innovation is about more than technology—it’s about empowering people, strengthening collaboration, and creating lasting impact.

As a Human-AI Collaboration Designer, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape how emerging technologies and human expertise come together to support meaningful organizational transformation.

**Ready to turn innovation into impact?**

Join Habitat for Humanity International and help us advance smarter, more collaborative ways of working as we build toward a world where everyone has a decent place to live.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$73,500.00 USD

\-

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.
