The song may be shared with applicants who wish to listen to it before submitting their technical proposal, so that they can assess the track and evaluate their interest in and ability to promote it to the media.

To access the song, applicants must request it by email from PIRAC and attach the confidentiality agreement included in the appendix to these Terms of Reference, duly completed and signed (electronic signatures are accepted).

The track is provided solely for listening purposes in connection with this tender. Any distribution, reproduction or sharing with third parties is prohibited.

title: Consultant for SPRINT II Final Evaluation (Indonesia and Timor-Leste)
body:
**About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center:**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is a non-profit, autonomous, regional organization, international in status and non-political in management, staffing and operations, organized for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes, with the vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster reduction, and the objective of reducing the impact of disasters on communities and countries in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as a regional technical center, ADPC is governed by its Charter, signed by its nine Founding Members: Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Thailand. With its seat in Thailand and governed by a Board of Trustees, ADPC has evolved into a leading regional organization supporting countries to reduce disaster and climate risks through evidence-based, innovative, and inclusive approaches.

ADPC Strategy 2030, approved by the ADPC Board of Trustees in July 2024 and operationalized through the ADPC Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030, guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific. Under the Strategy, ADPC delivers programs across 15 Priority Areas of Action, which contribute to three strategic **goals and nine Result Areas measured through 27 strategic indicators,** through three technical departments (Preparedness and Climate Actions; Risk Analytics and Climate Services; and Risk Governance and Financing):

- Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics
- Policy and Institutional Systems
- Effective Localization for Resilience
- Climate Services
- Resilient Planning and Implementation
- Preparedness and Anticipatory Action
- Nature-based Solutions
- Financing for Resilience
- Resilient Recovery
- Food and Water Security
- Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance
- Health Risk Management
- Urban and Infrastructure Resilience
- Private Sector Engagement
- ADPC Knowledge Academy

These priority areas are reinforced by ADPC’s **cross-cutting themes**, which are advanced across all programs and operations:

- Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)
- Innovations
- Regional and Transboundary Cooperation

ADPC supports countries in implementing global frameworks including the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Paris Agreement/UNFCCC, the New Urban Agenda, and the agenda of the 2016 World Humanitarian Summit, while contributing to national and regional policy advancement on resilience. Through multi-sectoral partnerships, technical advisory services, capacity development, and program implementation across multiple countries, ADPC works to strengthen systems, institutions, and communities to better manage disaster and climate risks.

For additional details, please visit: **http://www.adpc.net/**

**Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Actions (PCA) Department of ADPC advances ADPC Strategy 2030 by strengthening disaster preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response, resilient recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. In line with the Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030, including its localization priority area of action, PCA works with governments, NGOs, the private sector, academes and communities. It focuses on:

- Ensuring frameworks and implementation plans for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery are in place before disaster strikes.
- Strengthening institutional systems and community capacities to prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters.
- Promoting locally led DRR and climate resilience interventions through multi-stakeholder partnerships.

**Statement of Intent**

The “Strengthening Partnerships for Community Resilience in Indonesia and Timor-Leste (SPRINT)” Phase II project aims to support the development of disaster-ready communities in selected provinces of Indonesia and Timor-Leste through inclusive, integrated, and multidisciplinary approaches for disaster risk reduction (DRR) at local levels so that suffering and dependence on outside support will be reduced with faster recovery from future disaster events.

SPRINT II is being implemented from April 2025 to March 2027 in four communities in Lampung Province, Indonesia, and four communities in Ainaro Municipality, Timor-Leste. Building on SPRINT I, the second phase has continued to strengthen community disaster management institutions, local CSOs/CBOs, participatory risk assessments and action plans, early warning and preparedness arrangements, and community-led Priority Implementation Projects (PIPs). The program also promotes inclusion, local leadership and links between community preparedness and local government systems. SPRINT II contributes to ADPC Strategy 2030 and the Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030, in particular Priority Area of Action 11 (Effective Localization for Resilience) and Priority Area of Action 12 (Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions), both of which list Indonesia and Timor-Leste as priority countries, and the cross-cutting theme of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion.

The five objectives of SPRINT II are to:

1. Build and improve the capacity of community members for integrated and inclusive disaster risk reduction.
2. Strengthen the capacity of local CSOs/CBOs to support community-based disaster risk management.
3. Develop and update inclusive, participatory community action plans.
4. Support communities to implement selected actions and Priority Implementation Projects.
5. Promote learning and South-South knowledge exchange.

**Purpose, Evaluation Framework and Methodology**

The final evaluation will assess SPRINT II's achievements against its five objectives and examine how the program has contributed to advancing community disaster readiness in Indonesia and Timor-Leste. The evaluation will also consider the progression from SPRINT I to SPRINT II, recognizing that the program has worked with the same communities over successive phases. Findings will also inform ADPC's implementation of Strategy 2030 and the Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030, particularly its localization priority, and will feed into the 2028 mid-term review of the Strategic Action Plan.

The evaluation will be guided by the six OECD DAC criteria (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability) and by two results frameworks. First, each target community will be assessed against the ten Margaret A. Cargill Philanthropies (MACP) Disaster-Ready Community (DRC) short-term outcome indicators and their Low/Medium/High rubrics, as defined in the MACP DRR-I Outcome Indicator Reference Sheets, covering four outcomes: (A) a knowledgeable, inclusive and self-organized DRR leadership group; (B) inclusive preparedness plans, household risk reduction measures and early warning systems that are implemented, maintained and updated; (C) connection with local government for technical assistance and funding; and (D) diffusion of good practices and uptake in non-target communities. Second, the evaluation will assess SPRINT II's contribution to the ADPC Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030 Institutional Strategic Indicator Framework, in particular Result Area 2 (local actors' influence), Result Area 4 (capacity strengthened through training, knowledge exchange and learning), Result Area 5 (regional cooperation), Result Area 6 (multistakeholder engagement), Result Area 7 (marginalized groups' influence) and Result Area 9 (actions amplified through partnerships). It will adopt a mixed-methods and participatory approach, drawing on project documents, stakeholder consultations, field observations, household surveys or representative samples where feasible, and observation of drills or recent early warning events. Available SPRINT I and SPRINT II baseline and monitoring data will be used to assess change over time, and endline values for the relevant SAP strategic outcome indicators will be reported using ADPC's standardized M&E tools.

**Suggested evaluation questions include:**

1. To what extent has SPRINT II achieved its objectives, and at what rubric level (Low, Medium or High) does each target community now stand against the ten MACP DRC short-term outcome indicators?
2. How relevant and coherent has SPRINT II been to community priorities, the needs of women, persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups?
3. What changes have occurred between SPRINT I and the end of SPRINT II in community capacities, preparedness practices (including household risk reduction measures and timely action on early warning information), inclusion and local ownership?
4. How effectively have local partnerships, CSO/CBO capacities, and implementation arrangements supported these changes?
5. To what extent are the community institutions, preparedness systems and PIPs supported by SPRINT II likely to be sustained after the project ends, to what extent have community plans been recognized by, qualified for or received resources from local or national authorities, and what roles can local government, community financing and other local resources play in sustaining them?
6. What factors have enabled or constrained progress in low-attention and hard-to-reach communities, and what lessons, including from South-South knowledge exchange, can inform future programming?
7. To what extent have SPRINT II practices, tools and lessons been systematized and disseminated to local government and non-governmental actors, and taken up by non-target communities?
8. How and to what extent has SPRINT II contributed to the ADPC Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030 Result Areas, particularly the influence of local actors and marginalized groups in decision-making, and what does this imply for ADPC's localization and preparedness programming?

The consultant will develop the detailed evaluation framework, questions, methodology, sampling plan and participatory assessment tools during inception. Findings will be shared with the relevant stakeholder groups to inform evidence-based, practical recommendations.

**Expected Outputs:**

Under the guidance of the program team, the consultant shall be responsible for the delivery of the following outputs:

**Deliverable 1 :** Inception Report

**Expected Content :** Evaluation methodology, questions and matrix (mapping the MACP DRC indicators and relevant ADPC SAP strategic indicators to data sources and tools), sampling approach, work plan, data collection tools, participatory assessment approach and case-study template

**Timeline:** December 2026

**Deliverable 2 :** First draft of evaluation report

**Expected Content :** First draft of the evaluation report

**Timeline:** February 2027

**Deliverable 3 :** First draft of case studies

**Expected Content :** First draft of the four case studies, two per country

**Timeline:** February 2027

**Deliverable 4 :** Validation of findings

**Expected Content :** Draft evaluation findings for validation

**Timeline:** February 2027

**Deliverable 5 :** Final evaluation report and case studies

**Expected Content :** Final report with methodology, findings, conclusions, recommendations and supporting annexes, including a community-by-community MACP DRC rubric scoring table, endline values for the relevant ADPC SAP strategic indicators, and anonymized datasets and tools

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Deliverable 6 :** Presentation of findings

**Expected Content :** Concise presentation summarizing the methodology, process, key findings, and recommendations with photographs and supporting evidence.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

The consultant will be responsible for:

1. Developing the evaluation methodology, tools, sampling approach and work plan in consultation with ADPC.
2. Reviewing relevant SPRINT I and II documentation and available monitoring evidence.
3. Conducting field consultations and participatory assessments in coordination with local implementing partners.
4. Assessing project performance, community readiness against the MACP DRC short-term outcome indicators, sustainability, institutional linkages and contribution to the ADPC SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas.
5. Comparing available evidence across project phases and explaining differences in community progress.
6. Preparing four case studies (two per country) based on verified findings.
7. Conducting a focused validation process with ADPC, partners and relevant community and local stakeholders.
8. Preparing and finalizing the evaluation report and presentation.

ADPC and local implementing partners will facilitate access to relevant documents, stakeholders and project sites. The consultant will maintain independence in analyzing evidence, interpreting findings and developing recommendations.

**Working Principles:**

**Supervision and Reporting:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities indicated above, the consultant will work under the supervision of the relevant country-level CBDRR Specialists in the two countries and the SPRINT II Program Manager, with overall guidance from the Unit Head, Climate Actions and Impact of the Preparedness and Climate Actions (PCA) Department of ADPC.

ADPC will review the inception report, draft deliverables and final outputs. The consultant will coordinate with implementing CSOs/CBOs in Indonesia and Timor-Leste for fieldwork arrangements and stakeholder consultations.

**Participation and independence**

The evaluation will encourage the participation of community members and local stakeholders in assessing progress and validating findings. The consultant must ensure that participation is voluntary, inclusive and based on informed consent, that data are disaggregated by sex, age and disability where feasible, and that confidentiality, do-no-harm and safeguarding standards are upheld, while maintaining independence in the final analysis and recommendations.

**General Requirements:**

The consultant must operate within all ADPC Guidelines & Procedures/Policies and within the specific program needs.

**Qualifications:**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

- At least a master’s degree in disaster management, emergency management, development studies, public policy, evaluation or a related discipline.
- At least ten years of relevant professional experience, including evaluation of development, disaster risk reduction or community resilience programs.
- Demonstrated experience with mixed-methods evaluation and community-based or participatory assessment approaches, including rubric-based outcome assessment and familiarity with the MACP Disaster-Ready Communities model or comparable community resilience results frameworks.
- Good understanding of CBDRM, locally led resilience, local institutions and sustainability of community interventions.
- Experience working with local CSOs/CBOs and government counterparts
- Strong analytical, reporting and communication skills in English.
- Familiarity with Bahasa Indonesia and/or Tetum for field consultations.
- Prior evaluation or program experience in Indonesia or Timor-Leste would be an advantage.

**Duty Station:** Home-based with travel to project sites in Lampung Province, Indonesia, and Ainaro Municipality, Timor-Leste.

**Duration:** December 2026 – March 2027

title: Tupande Zone Supervisor - (Ntmaru and Oldanyati )
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

Seeking an exceptional people leader with strong commercial and analytical skills to drive sales, repayment, and operational excellence while maximizing farmer impact across Tupande’s zones.

## Responsibilities

- Achieve the assigned sales, repayment, customer, impact, high value crop, crop buying, tree and poultry targets for the zone.
- Lead weekly zonal team meetings to review results, address challenges, provide training and develop and manage clear weekly work plans for Tupande Agents and Duka Assistants, ensuring that priorities and individual targets are understood, executed and tracked.
- Move regularly across all assigned territories to monitor performance and farmer engagement, identify challenges, and coach and support your staff to consistently achieve individual and zone targets.
- Support recruitment, onboarding, training and managing Tupande Agents, Duka Assistants, staff supporting aggregation activities and short term contract staff, including setting expectations, providing feedback and addressing performance gaps.
- Oversee Duka performance and ensure that Duka Assistants manage daily customer service, sales, stock, product display, data entry and cash handling according to company procedures.
- Review Duka controls and records regularly, investigate differences or concerns and ensure that corrective action is completed.
- Step into Duka or Buying Center operations when necessary to resolve an issue, manage an exception or provide temporary support.
- Oversee all high value crop activities within the zone, including farmer enrollment, planting, farm visits, crop monitoring, harvesting, quality checks, collection and buying.
- Oversee farmer training and crop buying activities, including production and post harvest practices, collection planning, staffing, weighing, handling, record keeping, quality grading and payment tracking, while resolving or escalating farmer concerns.
- Oversee tree nursery and poultry brooding operations and at the Stawi station, working closely with the owner, including production planning, seedling and chick care, inventory, quality, survival rates and readiness for distribution while ensuring that problems are identified and addressed promptly.
- Ensure that Stawi Station records are complete and accurate, and that production, monitoring and distribution remain on schedule.
- Support the planning and delivery of local sales campaigns, farmer meetings, product demonstrations, marketing and other activities that create sales opportunities.
- Work closely with the Area Coordinator and other teams to resolve operational challenges and deliver a consistent experience for farmers across the zone.
- Maintain accurate records and submit complete and timely reports on zone performance, operations, risks and required support.
- Ensure compliance with organization policies and procedures including but not limited to customer protection, staff management, cash, inventory, data, organizational property, crop quality and payments.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Diploma and higher from a recognized institution.
- At least three years of experience in sales, agriculture, retail operations, customer service or team supervision.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly throughout the assigned zone and work closely with small scale farmers.
- Ability to use computers, tablets, Google Workspace and the applications required for the role.
- Experience managing a team and supporting individuals to achieve clear performance targets.
- Ability to interpret sales, repayment, inventory, production and crop buying information and use it to guide team performance.
- Ability to follow established work plans and procedures while maintaining a strong focus on achieving set targets.
- Strong problem solving and decision making skills, including the ability to resolve or escalate issues promptly.
- Excellent spoken and written communication skills, fluency in the relevant local language and strong connections to the farming communities served.
- Strong organization, record keeping and attention to detail.
- Basic knowledge of agronomy is preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Ntmaru, Kenya or Oldanyati, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

03 February 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

- Support product modelling for other One Acre Fund countries during the off-season

General Risk & Scenario Analysis

- Own the credit risk scoring model and lead repayment risk scenario analysis for OAF Zambia.
- Evaluate how weather and yield shocks impact farmer repayment and portfolio performance.

Microinsurance Strategy & Market Entry

- Contribute to market assessments and advise on farmer-centric financial protection products.
- Help navigate initial partner conversations and shape long-term microinsurance strategy in Zambia.

- Demonstrated actuarial modelling experience with R or Python for pricing, statistical modelling, and portfolio analysis.
- Direct experience with credit scoring models and repayment risk scenario analysis.
- Ability to use remote sensing applications, such as QGIS, for spatial and weather-index analysis.
- Strong project management skills with a proven ability to maintain clear documentation across complex multi-stakeholder workstreams.

title: Senior Accounting Specialist
body:
## **About IDinsight**

*We're a global data and evidence advisory, working with governments, philanthropies, and non-profits to improve lives at scale, using technology and AI where they can deliver the most impact.*

IDinsight is a global nonprofit that equips leaders with the data, evidence and technology to improve lives at scale. We partner with governments, NGOs, multilaterals, and funders to support decisions at every stage of their impact journey – from bold pilots to nationwide scale-ups. Our teams bring rigorous evidence and practical insights so leaders can make informed decisions that truly change lives. With our partners, we are pioneering the next frontier of social impact, where data and technology accelerate progress for millions. We help leaders overcome the three main barriers to impact:

1. Figuring out what works
2. Learning and improving
3. Reaching and operating at scale

We work in multiple countries across Asia and Africa. Our work spans a wide range of sectors, including agriculture, education, health, governance, sanitation, financial inclusion, and other areas.

We have expertise in a variety of rigorous approaches and methodologies, which we tailor to each client depending on their needs and constraints. To achieve a positive social impact we:

- Support our partners with the full ‘data and evidence’ value chain – from primary data collection to data systems, monitoring evaluation and learning tools, and data science
- Inform funding decisions – toward high-impact initiatives and away from less effective programs or approaches
- Create cutting-edge AI-for-good products that make the delivery of social interventions and learning tools more cost-effective and scalable

Our diverse, growing team of roughly 250 outstanding colleagues operate in nearly two dozen countries around the world. Learn more about our mission, values, and principles at [www.IDinsight.org](http://www.idinsight.org/).

## **Joining IDinsight at this moment**

IDinsight is entering an exciting new phase of growth. As demand for rigorous evidence and AI-enabled solutions accelerates across the sectors and geographies we work in, we are actively investing in our teams, deepening our regional footprint, and expanding the frontier of what data and technology can do for social impact. This is a moment of real momentum for IDinsight. We're looking for people who want to use data and evidence to improve lives at scale; who are energized by taking on problems without a playbook; and who want a hand in shaping what IDinsight becomes as we grow.

## **About the Senior Accounting Specialist role**

The Senior Accounting Specialist is a core member of IDinsight's global finance team, responsible for maintaining the integrity of financial records across the organization's multi-entity structure. This role combines technical accounting rigor with cross-functional collaboration, supporting day-to-day transaction review through to global audits and consolidated statutory reporting. The role serves as institutional knowledge anchor for accounting operations,, including leading finance process improvements, supporting ERP transformation, and building team capability through training. This is a global accounting role housed under IDinsight India, with a strong technical understanding of multi-jurisdictional compliance frameworks, global financial consolidation across all IDinsight entities, and the ability to navigate diverse regulatory environments spanning USA, Asia, and Africa regions.

## **Responsibilities**

The Senior Accounting Specialist will deliver and support the following areas:

**1. General Ledger, Journal Entries & Balance Sheet Reconciliation**

- Review and upload journal entries in the accounting system, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and proper supporting documentation.
- Verify that entries comply with internal controls and IDinsight's accounting policies prior to posting.
- Coordinate multi-entity postbacks across India, US, South Africa, Kenya, Zambia, Morocco, Senegal, and other entities during monthly close.
- Prepare and review monthly balance sheet reconciliations across all accounts.
- Investigate and resolve variances; maintain reconciliation schedules as audit-ready documentation.
- Manage intercompany reconciliations, including lease accounting, software cost allocations, prepaid journals, and insurance accruals across entities.

**2. Revenue Reconciliation & Accounts Receivable**

- Own the full revenue reconciliation process, tracking AR aging across all entities, matching receipts to invoices in the ERP, flagging mismatches with FP&A and project teams, and resolving intercompany income items.
- Confirm completeness and accuracy of income recognition in line with IDinsight's revenue recognition policies.
- Review and provide oversight on transfer pricing (TP) invoices, ensuring accuracy and compliance with intercompany agreements; train relevant team members on TP invoice processes.

**3. Global Audit Support & Statutory Compliance**

- Support the organization's global audit by preparing audit schedules, responding to auditor queries, and compiling supporting documentation.
- Coordinate with country office admin teams to gather required information within agreed timelines.
- Act as the primary point of contact for multi-country audit requests (e.g., South Africa HLB audit), managing outstanding items through to closure.
- Support statutory compliance requirements across all IDinsight entities, with a strong technical understanding of global VAT, GST, WHT (Withholding Tax), PAYE (Pay As You Earn), EPF (Employees' Provident Fund), TDS, advance tax, and other region-specific tax and regulatory obligations.
- Lead multi-country tax compliance tasks across IDinsight's entity footprint, including payroll-related filings (e.g., SARS/EMP statements for South Africa), Kenya ETR invoices, and related vendor and government portal coordination. Ensure technical compliance with regional frameworks such as India GST/TDS, South Africa VAT/PAYE, Kenya WHT/VAT, Zambia NAPSA, Morocco IR/TVA, Senegal TVA, and US federal/state filings.
- Maintain organized records and compliance schedules across entities.

**4. Global Consolidated Financial Statements & Form 990 Preparation (USA)**

- Prepare global consolidated financial statements for quarterly and annual reporting across all IDinsight entities (India, US, South Africa, Kenya, Zambia, Morocco, Senegal, and others), including intercompany eliminations, multi-currency translation, and consolidation adjustments in compliance with applicable accounting standards.
- Ensure financial statements are accurate, complete, and delivered within reporting deadlines.
- Coordinate global consolidation schedules across entities, ensuring alignment of chart of accounts, elimination entries, and reporting packages for group-level reporting.
- Assist in the preparation of Form 990 for IDinsight's US entity, ensuring accurate and timely filing in line with IRS requirements and nonprofit regulatory standards.
- Maintain organized records and supporting schedules for all 990-related disclosures.

**5. Program BVA & Utilization Reporting**

- Provide requested data for Program BVA (Budget vs. Actuals) utilization reporting to FP&A and project teams within agreed timelines.
- Support project-level financial tracking by reconciling program expenditures against approved budgets and flagging variances for management review.
- Collaborate with project managers and FP&A to ensure accurate and timely BVA data is available for donor reporting and internal decision-making.

**6. Employee Advances & Full and Final Settlement**

- Manage the end-to-end process for employee advances, including issuance, tracking, aging analysis, and recovery across all entities.
- Oversee the full and final settlement of departing employees by validating sub-ledger balances, clearing outstanding advances, reconciling leave encashment, gratuity, and other terminal benefits, and ensuring timely closure in the ERP system.
- Ensure compliance with local labor and tax regulations (e.g., TDS on settlements in India, PAYE in Kenya/South Africa) during the settlement process.

**7. ERP Management & Process Improvement**

- Serve as the institutional knowledge anchor for Unit4 (current ERP), including maintaining internal controls around user roles and access, chart of accounts integrity, and system troubleshooting.
- Support the organization's ERP transition (Microsoft Business Central) by contributing to workflow design, process documentation, user acceptance testing, and team onboarding.
- Collaborate with Finance, FP&A, and Systems teams to identify automation opportunities and configure accounting workflows in the new ERP environment.
- Proactively identify inefficiencies in accounting processes, particularly during monthly close, audit cycles, and cross-entity reconciliation, and propose and implement solutions.
- Lead or contribute to finance automation and standardization initiatives, including building shared trackers, improving close checklists, and streamlining intercompany workflows.
- Document standard operating procedures for key accounting processes to support team resilience and knowledge transfer.

**8. Team Training & Capability Building**

- Lead internal training sessions on financial accounting operations, ERP usage, and accounting best practices for the finance team.
- Train team members on TP invoice review, revenue reconciliation processes, and close procedures.
- Expand and maintain SLA reporting to track finance team performance and accountability.

## **Qualifications**

The ideal candidate brings deep technical accounting expertise, multi-jurisdictional experience, and a track record of process ownership.

**Experience & Skills**

- Minimum 5 years of progressive accounting experience in a global or multi-entity setup, with hands-on exposure to multi-currency and multi-geography accounting operations.
- Demonstrated experience in handling financial accounting across multiple jurisdictions spanning USA, Asia, and Africa, including intercompany transactions, foreign currency translations, and consolidation adjustments.
- Well-versed with IFRS, US GAAP, or relevant regional GAAP standards, with the ability to apply appropriate accounting treatments across diverse regulatory environments.
- Strong working knowledge of reporting frameworks, including consolidated financial statements, management reporting, and donor/funder reporting requirements.
- Proven track record of managing stakeholder relationships by providing accurate, timely, and reliable financial information to internal teams, leadership, auditors, and external partners.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, data validation, conditional formatting, and financial modelling.
- Experience with ERP systems (e.g., Unit4, Microsoft Business Central, SAP, or similar) in a multi-entity accounting environment.
- Technical understanding of global tax and regulatory compliance frameworks (VAT, GST, WHT, PAYE, EPF, and other regional obligations)
- Experience supporting or leading statutory audits, tax compliance filings, and regulatory reporting across multiple countries.

**Key Competencies**

- Technical accuracy and accounting rigor
- Initiative and process ownership
- Cross-functional and cross-cultural collaboration
- Structured problem-solving and variance investigation
- Ability to translate institutional knowledge into training and documentation
- Adaptability during system transitions and change management
- Strong global consolidation and multi-currency accounting skills

**Education & Certifications**

- Chartered Accountant (CA) from ICAI or equivalent international body.
- Certified Public Accountant (CPA) from AICPA or equivalent.
- Company Secretary (CS) with relevant financial accounting experience.
- Cost and Works Accountant (CWA) / Cost and Management Accountant (CMA).
- Any other globally recognized accounting certification (e.g., ACCA, CIMA, CGA, or equivalent).
- MBA in Finance (with a strong emphasis on core financial accounting and reporting).

## **Professional development**

Skill and career development are core to IDinsight's values and long-term impact strategy, and have been noted highlights of teammates’ experiences. IDinsighters receive significant mentorship from IDinsight leadership, support from talented peers, and are given considerable autonomy when ready. They maintain professional development plans and are given "stretch" opportunities designed to strengthen a variety of skills. Real-time feedback is embedded in our culture and formal structure enables maximum professional growth. Additionally, teammates have access to an annual professional development stipend that they are encouraged to utilize to explore their career interests and develop their skills.

## **Nuts & bolts**

### **Location**

This position is based in IDinsight's Delhi, India office. This position is not eligible for remote work.

### **Start date**

We are looking for candidates who can join immediately or at the earliest possible date. We expect a minimum 2-year commitment,, with regular professional development conversations and potential for a long-term career at IDinsight.

### **Compensation**

Compensation and benefits are commensurate with the qualifications and experiences IDinsight is hiring for, and competitive within the global development sector.

### **Work authorization**

IDinsight is not able to sponsor work authorization for this role. Successful candidates will not require IDinsight to sponsor their work authorization in the office in which they'll be based.

### **How to apply**

This application includes several questions and requires a CV (one to two pages) covering your professional and personal experience as well as academic qualifications. Please omit headshots, parental details, birth dates, marital status, and similar personal information — these aren't relevant to our review.

More information, including details on [I**Dinsight’s hiring process**](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/the-idinsight-hiring-process/)and [**frequently asked questions**](http://idinsight.org/about/careers/frequently-asked-questions/), can be found online at [IDinsight Careers](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/). Any questions should be directed to careers@IDinsight.org.

## **IDinsight’s commitment to reducing power asymmetries**

IDinsight is committed to [**reducing power asymmetries in the social sector**](https://www.idinsight.org/about/careers/reducing-power-asymmetries-in-the-social-sector-an-idinsight-organizational-priority/). Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion reflects our understanding of the need for the sector to abandon unhealthy practices of the past. We wish to be part of a new generation of international NGOs who are honest about this history and transparent about our role in the present. Our commitment is also aligned with the impact of our work.

We seek a workforce that is inclusive of a variety of perspectives that will help us refine and improve our methods and relationships, and strengthen the services we provide our clients and their communities or constituencies. The following commitments represent our vision for the IDinsight team:

1. IDinsight will have greater representation from the **populations with whom we work** and **clients we serve**.
2. IDinsight will have greater representation from the **countries in which we work**.
3. Across all countries in which we recruit, we will seek **greater representation from historically excluded communities**.
4. IDinsight will foster an **inclusive work culture that empowers a diverse team** to do their best work.

IDinsight is committed to non-discrimination in our recruitment, employment practices, and organizational culture, regardless of people’s age, disability, gender, gender identity, national origin, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable law.

title: Country Safety Access and Liaison Manager
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunities for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfillment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, and honesty and transparency.

**DRC Syria**

**DRC has been operating in Syria since 2008**, initially responding to the Iraqi refugee crisis before pivoting to a full-scale response to the Syria crisis from 2011 onwards. Our work encompasses the full cycle of displacement—responding to **life-saving humanitarian needs** and supporting community recovery until **durable solutions can be achieved**. DRC Syria takes an area-based approach to supporting internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities across our key sectors: Economic Recovery and Resilience, Protection, WASH, Shelter and Infrastructure, and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action).

With an established rapid response mechanism, DRC can **rapidly respond to emerging crises and shocks** to meet **acute emergency needs**. Recognizing the significant need for **early recovery and resilience programming** to ensure dignified, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions for fragile communities, DRC’s programmes foster resilience for individuals and communities in situations of protracted displacement and during the initial stages of post-conflict recovery, towards a **durable solution of their choice**. With active portfolios in the neighboring countries of Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye and Iraq, DRC offers a **cross-border, regional response** to the Syria crisis, through cross-border protection monitoring, advocacy, and trends analysis.

**Overall purpose of the role:**

The Safety Access and Liaison Manager oversees the implementation of DRC’s Safety Risk Management System (SRMS) , as well as access and Liaison with relevant stakeholders in Syria.

This encompasses monitoring the safety situation at DRC’s operational hubs across the country, implementing effective safety risk management solutions, analysing safety-related developments and conducting regular Security Risk Assessments. In addition, the Safety, Access and Liaison Manager is responsible for delivering context-specific safety and access training, maintaining strong engagement with staff and key stakeholders, and providing the Country Director with regular updates on safety, security, access and liaison matters, including relevant analysis, recommendations and proposed courses of action.

The successful candidate will supervise, manage and provide oversight to the Liaison/Access Specialist, and two field-based Officers, ensuring coordinated and effective engagement with relevant stakeholders on matters related to visas, registration, and access.

The Safety Access and Liaison Manager also plays an important role in strengthening capacity sharing with DRC’s local partners.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

**Safety Risk Management:**

- Oversee the implementation of the Safety Risk Management System (SRMS) and corresponding tools, procedures, and mitigation measures in consultation with the Regional Safety Coordinator.
- Ensure Safety-related procedures are presented in a comprehensible manner to DRC Syria staff to enforce a Safety culture that is accepted and appreciated by employees.
- Facilitate Safety Risk Assessments (SRAs) on regular and ad hoc basis.
- Drive the design and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) related to the safe implementation of program activities in coordination with Area Managers, Head of Programme and Head of Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action).
- Maintain relevant safety documentation, data, and records for the areas of concern.
- Be responsible for the implementation of context-specific Minimum Operating Safety Standards (MOSS) and regularly assess the physical safety of DRC facilities and accommodations.
- Apprise the Safety Level System (SLS) in coordination with the two Officers
- Consolidate and maintain the Critical Incident Management Plan (CIMP), ensuring that all staff are familiar with its procedures and understand their roles and responsibilities in the event of an incident.
- Monitor the evolving situation in the area of DRC programming in coordination with other actors and other DRC staffs.
- Management and tracking of DRC staff movements (domestically and internationally) in coordination with other DRC staffs including the Admin Team Leader.
- Provide safety risk analysis during project development process, expansion of activities and reduction/restructuring phases.
- Provide safety briefings and orientations to all new and visiting DRC staff as well as other key stakeholders visiting DRC programmes.
- Advise on the procurement of Safety-related equipment, facilities and other resources.
- In close coordination with the Administration team, ensure the effective and compliant safety management of staff accommodation, office facilities, and guesthouse arrangements.

**Coordination, Supervision, Training and Incident Response:**

- Coordinate Safety, access and liaison operations in DRC’s areas of operation and synchronize the work of all country-based Safety professionals in close coordination with the Area Managers.
- Actively participate in DRC internal coordination forums to address Safety, Access, and Liaison components, including, but not limited to, Extended Senior Management Team (ESMT) meetings, grant review sessions, kick-off meetings, and Go/No-Go decision processes etc…
- Represent DRC at external Safety, security and liaison coordination meetings with INGOs, UN agencies and other humanitarian and development actors.
- Monitor and track the movement and status of DRC staff in the field.
- Mentor and provide technical supervision to all dedicated DRC Syria Safety, access and liaison employees as well as part-time Safety and access focal Points.
- Provide demand- and policy-driven Safety advice and training.
- Participate in regional training initiatives in coordination with the Regional Safety Coordinator.
- Be an essential part of DRC Syria ’s critical incident management, provide timely and accurate incident high level reports/analysis, and support organizational lessons learned.
- Direct immediate responses to incidents and support staff in the process.
- Provide briefings to IMT members on their roles and responsibilities, and ensure that alternate members are identified, properly briefed, and fully prepared to assume their duties when required.
- Develop the capacity of Incident Management Teams by regularly conducting drills.
- Maintain a DRC Syria communication tree, including but not limited to WhatsApp Safety alert messages and ensure members are aware of their roles and responsibilities.
- Ensure smooth and effective internal coordination with relevant colleagues, including Area Managers and HR and Administration teams, Fleet team, Supply Chain team and lead follow‑up on cross‑cutting issues.
- Provide briefings to SMT members on security analysis and contextual updates.

**Partnership:**

- Coordinate with partners to ensure structured and inclusive capacity strengthening, in line with equal‑partnership and localisation principles. This includes
    - - reviewing partners’ safety, access, and liaison policies and procedures;
            - proposing relevant revisions and adaptations;
            - documenting findings and developing action plan
            - delivering tailored training and Training‑of‑Trainers (ToT) support;
            - and promoting two‑way capacity sharing to learn from partners’ expertise and contextual knowledge.
- Provide support to partners in incident management processes.
- Assist partners in implementing joint activities, ensuring alignment with safety and access requirements.

**Quality assurance of safety-related policies, protocols, procedures, and regulations, including:**

- Regular SRA, MOSS & SLS audits of all Programme areas.
- Assess the implementation of physical and asset protection protocols and regulations
- Ensure that appropriate access controls are in place for all DRC facilities as per the SOPs
- Conduct regular site assessments and advise on mitigation measures and action plan

**Liaisons - Access**

- Ensure the organization remains informed of new regulations, procedures, and policy changes affecting operations.
- Supervise the Liaison and Access Specialist and serve as the secondary focal point for obtaining visas, residence permits, work permits, and other documentation required for DRC staff and visitors, in close coordination with relevant staffs.
- Monitor the visas record and follow up with the team to request or renew visas.
- Support the Country Director to ensure that MoUs and other sub-agreements are processed in a timely manner and that all documentation and process requirements relating to DRC’s registration are effectively met.
- Establish a network of contacts with relevant government offices, Immigration and other units, represent DRC and actively participate to related meetings.
- Coordinate with Area Managers for governorates level authorities for high level meetings.
- Managing the road travel for Expats travelling inside and outside the country (in coordination with neighbouring countries’ Safety staffs) and act as the main focal point during emergency such as evacuation.
- Build strong required relations with government entities and local authorities to ensure safe and smooth implementing interventions.
- Receive documents and communications from authorities, in collaboration with liaison and safety staff, and share them with the Country Director for review and follow-up.
- Raise up to CD’s attention any requests from local authorities for a discussion and feedback.
- Draft and assisting in finalizing projects reports, annual reports and submission to the relevant donor when needed and stakeholders in timely manner.
- Support the update of the Risk Register in collaboration with SMT Members.
- Carry out other activities as requested by the Country Director.

**Required Qualifications**

- To be considered for this position, candidates must have a minimum of 5 years of experience in a security-related field, with at least 3 years in a management position as a Security, safety or Access Manager or Advisor for an NGO in a high-risk context.
- Proven experience in context and security analysis, advising humanitarian personnel, and developing and updating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and contingency plans is essential.
- Candidates should also have experience in incident and crisis management, conducting safety training for both international and national staff, and capacity building and strengthening of staff and partners.
- The ability to provide timely, clear and concise written analysis, prioritize tasks under pressure, and work effectively with minimal supervision is required.
- Proficiency in common software packages, map design and the ability to mentor and guide team members and partners in safety, security and liaison issues are also necessary.

**Education**:

Essential qualification

- Master's degree or equivalent, alternatively: bachelor's degree with vast work experience.
- Participation in Safety training (HEAT, Safety management, first aid, TOT, etc) and corresponding certificates will be viewed favorably.
- Excellent skills in MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
- Previous experience in safety & security within a humanitarian field is required.

**Languages:**

- Arabic (native speaker)
- English (fluent)

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract Length**: 1 year (Renewable, based on performance and fund availability).
- **Salary Level**: Management – F level 1 (Based on DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Syria, Damascus.
- **Expected Start date**: As soon as possible

title: Partnerships Manager
body:
**The position is for an initial two year period, with the possibility of extension, and will be based in Canberra, Australia, or potentially elsewhere in Australia.**

**Program Background**

Partnerships for Infrastructure (P4I) Phase 2 is an Australian Government initiative to support quality infrastructure development that drives inclusive growth in Southeast Asia. P4I-2 is a 10-year initiative to April 2036, with an initial period of five years from May 2026 to April 2031.

P4I works with partners to strengthen policy and regulatory frameworks related to infrastructure development. It also addresses obstacles to project development, including through advice on financing strategies, with an emphasis on mobilising private finance. P4I works closely with the Australian Government and industry to help bring relevant solutions to Southeast Asia’s infrastructure development challenges, in line with Australia's Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040.

P4I currently works in four sectors: land transport resilience, maritime decarbonisation, integration of renewables into energy systems, and telecommunications. P4I incorporates inclusion, including gender equality, disability and social inclusion, and climate mitigation and adaptation across these four sectors.

P4I is a multi-country program that also works directly with ASEAN and its secretariat. P4I works in Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. P4I will increase engagement in Timor-Leste given its entry into ASEAN and retains flexibility to support activities in Indonesia, as requested by Australia’s bilateral program to Indonesia.

The P4I Program Office in Bangkok provides strategic direction and program management, with close engagement with P4I-funded locally engaged DFAT staff at Posts. A P4I Program Executive team oversees implementation, led by the delivery partner Team Leader (Executive Director), with strategic direction provided by the DFAT Strategic Director and Deputy Strategic Director.

More information about P4I is available at [www.partnershipsforinfrastructure.org](https://www.partnershipsforinfrastructure.org/).

**The Role**

Partnerships with Australian and other organisations, across both the public and private sectors, will continue to be a major feature of how P4I delivers on its objectives. Reporting to the Partnerships Director, the **Partnerships Manager** will support the oversight and management of P4I’s partnerships portfolio, including ensuring that appropriate systems, processes and structures are in place to enable effective partnership management.

The Partnerships Manager will support coordination with DFAT and Australian partners, including government agencies, academic institutions and industry, as well as stakeholders across P4I including DFAT Posts and Canberra, Country Engagement Managers and Sector Leads. The role will provide cross-portfolio coordination and support to promote strategic coherence and consistent approaches to the management of partnerships.

The position is for an initial **two year period, with the possibility of extension**, and will be based in **Canberra, Australia, or potentially elsewhere in Australia**.

**Responsibilities**

The Partnerships Manager will:

- Develop and refine procedures and templates for managing partnerships, including activity development, partnership agreements and workplans, activity delivery, travel and event coordination, briefings and reporting.
- Support the management of relationships with Australian Government and other institutional partners in close collaboration with DFAT and relevant Sector Leads.
- Coordinate the development of new partnerships under the direction of the Partnerships Director, including supporting research into partner mandates and capability in the context of P4I priorities and sector and country strategies.
- Support longer-term partner engagement through formal partnership agreements, where required, along with workplans and budgets.
- Coordinate activity-level partner engagement across Country Engagement Managers, Sector Leads, delivery teams, DFAT Canberra and Posts.
- Provide general briefings on P4I and support the development of preparatory materials covering Southeast Asian country priorities, context, key actors and relevant programs.
- Lead and oversee logistics service provision for government-to-government partners, including travel, per diems and event coordination.
- Maintain a clear pipeline of partnership activities and a forward plan/calendar of partner activities in Australia and across the region.
- Monitor and analyse the progress of the partnership portfolio, including data management, budgets, risks and issues, approvals, record keeping and reporting requirements.
- Provide briefings to the Program Executive and DFAT on the partnership portfolio as required.
- Coordinate with DFAT, the Strategic Communications team and partners to support effective internal and external communication of partnership activities and impact.
- Contribute to the development of program systems and processes, particularly those relating to partnership activities and the activity lifecycle.

Click on the link or copy and paste it to access the full Position Description for this position: https://tinyurl.com/3uv54fws

**About You**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- Tertiary qualifications in a relevant discipline.
- Ideally, an understanding of Australian infrastructure institutions, with experience working in or for Australian partner organisations.
- Strong project management experience, including coordinating multiple stakeholders, preferably within a P4I-focused sector.
- Ideally, an understanding of Southeast Asia, including ways of working and the institutional context.
- Demonstrated capacity to exercise sound judgement and make timely decisions in situations involving risk, uncertainty or competing priorities.
- Strong capability to analyse complex problems and identify linkages to achieve program impact.
- Exceptional organisational skills, with the ability to work under tight deadlines, respond to shifting priorities and effectively utilise available systems and processes.
- Demonstrated ability to produce program results in a complex and dynamic environment, collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary and multicultural teams operating in multiple locations.
- Proven ability to take responsibility for outcomes, including setting clear plans, meeting commitments, proactively managing and communicating risks and issues, and following through without close supervision.

Level 3: the post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process staff.

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

Organization guards are responsible for the safety and protection of the organization's property through procedural and physical security measures, while maintaining awareness of the surrounding local community.  
**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

Reports to: Security focal points officer/coordinator in Damascus and Aleppo

Staff reporting to this post: None

(delete is not applicable)  
Direct: Security Team  
Indirect : Security Director   
Budget Responsibilities: none  
Role Dimensions: Responsible for maintaining the safety and security of the organisation’s premises, personnel and assets through access control, surveillance, regular patrols and facility inspections. Ensure effective emergency response, report security incidents and breaches, and support staff protection and evacuation procedures.  
**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**   
• Do not allow strangers to enter the center.  
• Do not permit armed individuals to enter the premises.  
• Operate and shut down the generator outside working hours; ensure it is maintained and report any mechanical failures.  
• Switch electrical breakers to supply power to all guesthouses and guard posts, and report any technical faults.  
• Record the entry of staff and visitors at all times.  
• Maintain fire extinguishers and report any expired or soon-to-expire devices.  
• Conduct random patrols inside the building to inspect electrical panels, generators, and the overall condition of the premises.  
• Safeguard the organization’s property against damage, theft, or vandalism.  
• Receive and inspect any packages or mail sent to the center and deliver them to the intended recipient if deemed non-suspicious.  
• Reduce the likelihood of theft or attacks on the center or its staff through physical deterrence.  
• Conduct regular inspections of the center’s interior and exterior (where possible), paying special attention to suspicious packages, materials, or vehicles, particularly near vegetation or debris.  
• Maintain a good understanding of the local community and living patterns, and be alert to unusual circumstances.  
• Monitor the surveillance system (CCTV cameras).  
• Minimize the impact of any attacks on the organization's site by warning staff, requesting assistance, supporting evacuation procedures, and taking other necessary actions.  
• Report any incidents or breaches of the organization's policies.  
**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)**  
Accountability:  
• holds self accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values  
• holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.  
Ambition:  
• sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same  
• widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others  
• future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.  
Collaboration:  
• builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters  
• values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength  
• approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.  
Creativity:  
• develops and encourages new and innovative solutions  
• willing to take disciplined risks.  
Integrity:  
• honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity  
**QUALIFICATIONS**

• Literate.  
• Preferably a resident of the local area.  
• Minimum of three years' experience in a similar role with other organizations.  
• Good character.  
• Physically fit.  
• Self-confident and polite.  
• Committed to the organization's policies and principles.   
**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**  
• Previous experience in security, coordination, or related fields.  
• Basic knowledge of English (spoken and written) desired.  
• First aid experience.  
**Additional job responsibilities**  
The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.  
**Equal Opportunities**   
The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.  
**Child Safeguarding:**  
We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.  
**Safeguarding our Staff:**  
The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy  
**Health and Safety**  
The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.
