title: Area Manager Maradi Niger
body:
**Background**

The humanitarian crisis in the Central Sahel remains severe, complex and fast evolving, driven by conflict, displacement, climate shocks, food insecurity and shrinking operational space. In Niger and Burkina Faso, millions of people continue to require humanitarian assistance; while underfunding, insecurity and access constraints place sustained pressure on principled humanitarian action and programme quality.

Niger continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by insecurity, climate-related events, and chronic poverty, disrupting livelihoods for families and communities. Nearly one million displaced people, including refugees and internally displaced persons, are living in Niger, many of them in the regions of Tillabéri, Tahoua and Diffa.

NRC is currently working in Niger, with staff dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict. Its humanitarian interventions are based on programming expertise in core competencies including Education, WASH, Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence, and Shelter to vulnerable displaced people.

Within the Central Sahel Multi-Country Office (MCO) model, Burkina Faso and Niger are managed under a unified structure led by the Central Sahel MCO Country Director, while maintaining strong Area Office delivery hubs.

The Area Manager – Maradi is responsible for leading NRC’s area operations in the Maradi / Tillabéri / Dosso / Tahoua area, ensures high standard of project delivery and contributes to multi-country coherence through participation in the Multi-Country Management Group (MCMG).

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The purpose of the Area Manager position is to ensure high quality and cost-effective programme/project implementation in the Maradi, Tillabéri, and Tahoua Regions of Niger. The Area Manager supervises several field offices/antennas – Tillabéri, Tahoua, Dosso (non-exhaustive).

**What you will do**

- Overall responsibility of managing the Maradi / Tillabéri Area Office including potential sub offices, with close supervision of the Field Manager in Tillabéri
- Responsible for overall staff security, including completing security risk assessments for the area and possible new areas of intervention
- Support needs assessment in the region, ensure the implementation of all projects active in the area in line with the agreed standards and donors’ requirements; this includes ensuring that NRC’s data collection systems are in place and information is properly stored and analyzed
- Support the team in identifying the gaps for further programming and development, and participate in assessments for new areas of operation, possible areas of intervention, aiding the development of program strategy for implementation.
- Lead on access strategy and its implementation in hard-to-reach areas, in close collaboration with CD and relevant colleagues at the country level. This includes contextualizing, adapting, and implementing SOPs and procedures to ensure effective provision of assistance to hard-to-reach areas
- In conjunction with Country Office, liaise with donors on new funding and operational areas of programming, liaise regularly with local authorities (political and security), donors and humanitarian actors in the operational area. This includes support in the development of concept notes, project proposals, and budgets for scale-up of post emergency activities
- Represent NRC at coordination platforms at area level and provide regular feedback and input to advocacy initiatives
- Overall responsibility for staff management. Recruitment of qualified staff for the area office, in close collaboration with HR and support team in the Country Office, lead by example the teams on the ground on NRC’s core values (dedication, innovation, inclusion and accountability). Ensuring training is provided to all staff and capacity building initiatives are in place, work and development plans are completed by all staff in the operational area, and performance feedback sessions are conducted on a minimum quarterly basis
- Ensure sound financial management, including the Master Budget is covered and up to date, reflecting cost-efficient use of the available funding

Please download the detailed job description to learn more about the [JD Area Manager Maradi-Tillabéri Niger .pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBHy7h6uVMuQ6WNdVjh2jUiAXcbCfRs-sXSEBD6a1lIVN4?e=3ZheyZ)

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum 3-5 years of experience working as a Senior Project Manager / field manager in a humanitarian and recovery context
- Previous experience working in complex and volatile contexts
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in French and proficiency in English, both written and verbal

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the context in West Africa and Niger in particular
- Experience working in insecure / hard to reach locations
- Experience managing safety and security
- Competencies in humanitarian and access negotiations

**2. Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environments
- Strategic thinking
- Empowering and building trust
- Managing performance and development
- Managing resources to optimise results
- Coping with change

***Leadership profile***

- Building meaningful relations
- Acting with integrity
- Empowering people
- Delivering results

**What we offer**

- **Duty station**: Maradi,Niger
- **Contract**: Fixed term for 12 months with possibility of extension
- **Salary&Benefits**: Grade 10 on NRC’s National salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

**Female Applicants are Highly encouraged to Apply**

title: Global Safeguarding Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The Global Safeguarding Manager is a senior technical specialist in AKF’s global safeguarding team, working closely with and under the supervision of the Global Safeguarding Lead. The postholder leads the day-to-day delivery of investigations and case management, provides hands-on technical support to Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points in AKF units, and turns learning from cases into practical improvements across AKF and, where applicable, the wider integrated AKF.

**Hybrid working, based in our London office, with an expectation to attend in person on a regular basis. This global role reports to HQ in Geneva, Switzerland, with regular international travel (approx. 20%), including to fragile contexts.**

**Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK; AKF will not sponsor visa applications.**

**4. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND CORE TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES**

**4.1 Investigations and Case Management (approximately 50%)**

- **Intake and Triage:** Manage the intake, triage and risk assessment of concerns received by the global function.
- **Investigations:** Plan and conduct complex and sensitive investigations into sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH), bullying, harassment, discrimination and related workplace misconduct, producing clear, evidence-based reports.
- **Oversight of Investigations:** Scope, commission and quality-assure investigations carried out by unit and external investigators, and develop the internal investigator pool.
- **Case Management:** Manage the global case register and ensure cases are handled in a survivor-centred, fair and confidential way, with outcomes followed through with HR and management.
- **Case Support to Units:** Provide case supervision to unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points and support units, in person or remotely, in responding to serious incidents.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Prepare routine incident notifications to donors and regulators, and analyse case trends to recommend improvements.

**4.2 Technical Support, Capacity Building and Policy Development (approximately 40%)**

- **Technical Advice:** Advise and support unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points, on site and remotely, to put global safeguarding standards into practice in their context, such as risk assessments, safeguarding in programmes and community-level safeguarding and reporting mechanisms.
- **Capability Building:** Identify capability gaps among unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points and provide mentoring, coaching and technical learning.
- **Training and Awareness:** Develop training content and lead awareness and capacity building for staff across AKF, including specialised training for different stakeholder groups, to reinforce a culture of integrity and ethics.
- **Policies and Procedures:** Lead the review and improvement of safeguarding policies, procedures, guidance and practical tools, drawing on case learning and sector, donor and regulatory standards.
- **Partners:** Advise on safeguarding due diligence and capacity strengthening for partners and contractors.

**4.3 Assurance (approximately 10%)**

- **Assurance Support:** Support delivery of the safeguarding assurance framework, including unit reviews and follow-up of improvement actions.

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive, and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties that align with their skills and experience.

**5. QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE, BEHAVIOURS, ATTRIBUTES**

**5.1 Qualifications:**

- Degree in law, criminology, social work, psychology, human rights, international development or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- Recognised investigation qualification, such as CHS Alliance IQTS Tier 3 or equivalent (essential).
- Ethics and compliance certification, such as CCEP or ISO 37301/37002 (desirable).

**5.2 Experience:**

- At least seven years’ safeguarding, ethics and compliance or workplace investigations experience in international development, humanitarian or comparable multi-country organisations, covering both technical support and investigations (essential).
- At least five years leading complex, high-risk investigations into SEAH, bullying, harassment, discrimination or related workplace misconduct, including cases involving senior staff, and quality-assuring investigations by others (essential).
- Demonstrated experience of providing technical support on general safeguarding to country or field teams, such as risk assessments, safeguarding in programmes, community reporting mechanisms and partner safeguarding (essential).
- Proven experience of designing and delivering safeguarding training and capacity building for different audiences, and of mentoring safeguarding staff across countries (essential).
- Experience of developing practical safeguarding procedures, guidance and tools (essential).
- Experience in ethics and compliance, speak-up/whistleblowing programmes or workplace investigations, including in corporate, public or regulated sectors (desirable).
- Donor and regulatory reporting; experience in humanitarian, development, health, education or child-focused settings (desirable).

**5.3 Knowledge and Skills:**

- Expert knowledge of safeguarding and PSEAH frameworks and sector standards (e.g. IASC Six Core Principles, CHS, Keeping Children Safe), survivor-centred practice and procedural fairness.
- Excellent investigative interviewing, analytical and report-writing skills, and sound judgement under pressure.
- Ability to coach, influence and constructively challenge colleagues at all levels and across cultures.
- Fluent English essential; French, Portuguese, Russian, Dari, Urdu, Arabic or Swahili an asset.

**5.4 Behaviours:**

- **Politically aware & discreet:** Navigates complex, multicultural environments with strong stakeholder awareness, sound judgment, and a high level of confidentiality and discretion.
- **Clear & effective communicator:** Communicates complex information with clarity, adapts messaging to diverse audiences, and ensures timely, transparent communication.
- **Collaborative & low-ego mindset:** Builds strong relationships, works seamlessly across teams, and adopts a hands-on approach with a focus on collective outcomes over hierarchy.
- **Reliable execution & accountability:** Takes ownership to ensure cases and agreed actions move forward with local management in each country, manages multiple priorities with strong attention to detail, and follows through consistently.
- **Agile & resilient under pressure:** Adapts to changing priorities and organisational contexts, operates effectively in high-pressure environments, and remains solution oriented.

**6. KEY RELATIONSHIPS**

**Internal Relationships**

- Global Director of Operations
- Global Safeguarding Coordinator
- Global HR, Procurement, Programmes, Finance
- Unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points
- Unit leadership and HR teams
- Safeguarding counterparts in AKDN agencies

**External Relationships**

- External investigators and consultants
- Survivor support and referral services
- Implementing partners
- Inter-agency safeguarding networks
- Institutional donors and regulators

**7. APPLICATION DETAILS**

- Send a CV and a supporting statement (max. one side of A4) on why you want the role and how you meet the essential requirements, with your preferred salary and notice period.
- Application link: [PLEASE APPLY HERE](https://krb-xjobs.brassring.com/TGnewUI/Search/home/HomeWithPreLoad?partnerid=30025&siteid=5750&PageType=JobDetails&jobid=2299513#jobDetails=2299513_5750)
- Closing Date: **6TH December 2026**
- Salary commensurate with experience + benefits
- Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK; no visa sponsorship.
- Selection may include a written technical exercise.

*AKF recruitment and selection procedures reflect our commitment to equal opportunity and protecting children and at risk adults from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH).We will do everything possible to ensure that only those who are suitable to work with children and at risk adults are recruited to work for us.* *In the process of recruitment, selection and appointment AKF implement a range of procedures and vetting checks including criminal records disclosures to ensure everyone associated with AKF is kept free from harm and abuse is prevented.*

*By sharing their cover letter and resume with AKF in response to this job application, applicants consent for AKF to keep this information on file for recruitment and human resources management purposes.*

title: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist (80%)
source: The Global Community Engagement and Resilience Fund
body:
**Vacancy Announcement**

Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

**(REF. 2026-12)**

Position title: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist

Team: Performance and Impact

Required FTE: 80%

Required travel: Some travel, up to maximum 10% of time

Reports to: Head – Performance and Impact

**Scope of the role**

Violent extremism is a direct threat to international security, economic growth, and development. GCERF works to prevent violent extremism by investing in people. As the only global fund dedicated to preventing violent extremism (PVE), we connect local communities to global resources and support grassroots initiatives that are often out of reach for international donors. We fund community-centric initiatives led by civil society organisations to address the local social, economic, and political drivers of violent extremism.

The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will be part of GCERF’s dynamic and high-performing team of Monitoring and Evaluation experts. This role is responsible for ensuring the quality of monitoring, evaluation and evidence across assigned grants, including results frameworks, assessments, and evaluations. Provides technical support to the Performance & Impact unit in line with the role holder’s expertise.

**Principal accountabilities and ownership**

**Grant-management:** Responsible for ensuring M&E quality throughout the management of assigned grants, including oversight of results frameworks, and capacity building needs. Coordinate with the P&I Associate on routine results reporting, data quality and related monitoring processes, providing technical review and guidance as required.

**Assessments and Evaluations:** Responsible for planning, managing or advising on assessments across assigned grants, including baselines, endlines, evaluations and third-party monitoring (TPM). Ensure the methodological quality of assessments and support the use of findings for programme and grant management.

**Coordination:** Liaise and coordinate with Portfolio and Finance teams within each Country/Regional Team.

**P&I support:** Contribute to Performance & Impact unit priorities in areas aligned with the role holder’s technical skills and expertise, including technical analysis, methodological support, development of tools and guidance, and other technical inputs as required.

**Knowledge/Experience/Qualifications**

- Fluency in English and Russian; working knowledge of French is an advantage (B2-level).
- Strong, proven monitoring and Evaluation experience, specifically assessment experience, is required, as well as project management or applied research. We expect this to require at least 6 years of progressively responsible experience in a similar role. At least two years’ professional experience in one of GCERF’s partner countries or similar contexts.
- Master’s degree in Economics, Data Science, Statistics, International Relations, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Previous experience or demonstrated interest in the prevention of radicalisation to violent extremism will be an advantage.
- Programming and/or impact evaluation (especially quasi-experimental designs) experience is an asset.
- Detail-oriented, excellent coordination skills, must be able to work independently and have a keen interest in seeking tech solutions to improve efficiency.

**Values**

Demonstration of alignment with GCERF’s key values is a critical component of the selection process:

Make a difference

Achieve together

Uphold integrity

Respect yourself and others

Learn and improve

Be Kind

**Personal attributes based on GCERF competencies**

Be proactive

Work collaboratively

Be accountable and drive for solutions and results

Communicate effectively

Embrace learning and entrepreneurial spirit

**General information**: Our office is located in Geneva, Switzerland. Swiss residency or work eligibility is not a requirement.

GCERF values diversity, equality and inclusion, and we hire globally. We are committed to hiring qualified candidates irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, national origin, family status, sex, gender identity or expression, physical characteristics, race, religion, spirituality or sexual orientation. GCERF has a zero tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of discrimination or harassment. GCERF stands by its commitment to welcoming persons of all backgrounds into a safe work environment.

All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference checks and anti-terrorism screening.

Contract: 1 year, renewable. Part-time 80% (32 hours per week). The arrangement of days and hours worked is flexible.

GCERF allows a limited number of remote working days per week.

Competitive compensation package.

title: Director, Cause Marketing and Workplace Giving

**Develop fundraising strategy and pipeline to steward current donors and grow the portfolio (35%)**

· Develop and execute strategies to increase partner engagement and revenue in cause marketing initiatives, workplace giving and other sources of unrestricted revenue, including leveraging partners’ employees and customer spheres of influence to fundraise on behalf of HFHI.

· Lead and expand the fundraising and execution of “Home is the Key”, Habitat’s annual cause marketing platform and rollout of a multi-channel, integrated national cause marketing platform that appeals to existing partner portfolio as well as new industries including retail, CPG, QSR and others to broaden the base of HFHI support.

· Lead and support team in development of account-specific strategies that deepen partner engagement with Habitat and foster mutually beneficial, sustainable, mission-centered partnerships.

· Develop and execute strategies to increase partner participation in workplace giving campaigns; rollout toolkits and other support materials.

· Stay current on opportunities, trends, and best practices in cause marketing, retail, digital, corporate sponsorship and workplace giving; convert insights into actionable programs and new revenue streams and identify potential prospects for cultivation.

**Carry a personal portfolio and lead/coach staff on key partnerships (15%)**

· Develop and deliver creative and powerful presentations and proposals for corporate partnership opportunities; ensure organizational leadership involved in pitch are briefed and prepared for meetings.

· Ensure 100% partner satisfaction through thoughtful stewardship and best-in-class customer service.

**Collaborate cross functionally within Habitat to work on continuous process improvement and partnership development (20%)**

· Serve as cause-related marketing and workplace giving subject matter expert across the organization; ensure compliance with all applicable charitable sales promotion regulations; provide on-going training and support to Resource Development team.

· Provide leadership to team regarding structuring/managing their cause marketing partnerships and advancing global multi-national partnerships.

· Collaborate with HFHI leadership to develop relationships with key stakeholders at multiple levels across partner organizations.

· Partner with HFHI Marketing and Communications, key Resource Development teams and other organizational stakeholders to create and implement sound cause marketing strategies that beneficially advance HFHI fundraising and brand awareness goals and priorities.

· Establish strong relationships with HFH affiliate Executive Directors and resource development teams as well as HFHI regional staff; support the collaborative development efforts among Habitat for Humanity entities including the identification of opportunities to share prospects with HFHI resource development colleagues and local Habitat affiliates, as appropriate.

**Lead and coach the team (20%)**

· Through regular communication, and a strategic, forward-looking approach, work with each member of the team to create development plans that enhance their skill sets and achieve revenue goals. Lead the strategy for engaging new partners in cause and workplace activities / campaigns and ensure the proficiencies of the team.

**Administration, Reporting & Analysis (10%)**

· Oversight of deal terms and collaboration with HFHI legal and finance teams to ensure compliance.

· Maintain systems for metrics tracking, analytics, and knowledge sharing.

· Provide accurate activity and pipeline reports including situational analysis, revenue and expense forecasts as required.

· Maintain current prospect and partner records in donor management system.

**Other duties as assigned by supervisor**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

· Education: Bachelors Degree or equivalent experience

· Years of Related Experience: 6-10 years of related experience; 3-5 years in leadership capacity.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

· Experience in securing complex, six-and seven-figure cause marketing commitments from Fortune 500 companies.

· Experience leading a team and collaborating across a complex organization.

· Working knowledge of principles of corporate social responsibility, cause marketing, employee engagement and sponsorship.

· Superior skills in project management, metrics, analytics and reporting.

· Highly collaborative; optimistic personality with winning relationship skills to build internal and external partnerships.

· Creative, quick thinker who thrives in brainstorm sessions and who can think past obstacles to achieve a bigger vision.

· Highly proactive and autonomous, capable of driving projects through in a complex and layered organization.

· Outstanding oral and written communication skills with excellent interpersonal, presentation and negotiation skills.

· Solution-oriented with commitment to delivering excellent internal and external customer service.

· Ability to complete multiple projects concurrently while balancing competing priorities; ability to meet deadlines.

· Ability to effectively manage HFHI resources including travel expenses and unit budget.

· Computer literate; able to use word-processing, spreadsheet, database and project software.

**Preferred Requirements:**

· Knowledge of and passion for Habitat's worldwide mission preferred

· Established media relationships and deep knowledge of media and entertainment sector; track record of building media partnerships.

· Experience with international partnership strategy and development.

**Culture and Values**  
At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:

**\*Humility:** We are part of something bigger than ourselves.  
**\*Courage:** We do what is right, even when it is difficult.  
**\*Accountability:** We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.  
**\*Safeguarding:** We protect the rights, dignity, and safety of all people we serve and work alongside.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$116,600.00 USD

\-

Annual

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. title: Senior Specialist - Management & Operations Expertise Hub
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Job Summary

Are you ready to make an impact in the world? Join Habitat for Humanity’s Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub as we multiply Habitat’s impact in the United States.

Habitat for Humanity International’s U.S. Expertise Hubs are teams of subject matter experts and collaborative thought partners that – in partnership with local affiliate staff and leaders from across the country – create, connect and curate resources, trainings, and promising practices along dedicated practice areas in support of capability building within the U.S. affiliated network. The Management and Operations Expertise Hub drives the aggregation and exchange of practice-based knowledge and application among affiliates and other subject matter experts in nonprofit management and operations, including topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics.

The Sr. Specialist will manage and support the development, delivery/facilitation, evaluation and socialization of new and refreshed resource/training content, services, and support within the Management and Operations Expertise Hub to maximize the management and operations of U.S. Habitat affiliates. The role supports the thoughtful and intentional curation of existing content/expertise from both the Habitat community and external partnerships to advance promising practices. The role must collaborate closely with HFHI affiliate-facing learning professionals to ensure that hub content is packaged and delivered in the most accessible and useful way to be relevant and accessible to Habitat’s diverse network, and is responsible for that delivery and facilitation.

**Key Responsibilities:**

## **Senior Specialist – Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub**

**Help strengthen the organizations that help families build a better future.**

Bring your expertise in nonprofit management, learning, and relationship building to Habitat for Humanity International. In this role, you’ll turn knowledge into practical tools, connect affiliate leaders with promising practices, and facilitate learning experiences that strengthen Habitat’s impact across the United States.

**Work setting:** Remote/home office (may work in-person or hybrid if desired and near an HFHI office and space is available)  
**Domestic travel:** 20%

### **Essential Duties**

#### **Product and Services Development, Delivery, and Evaluation (60%)**

- Lead and/or contribute to the review, refresh, development, design, testing, delivery, and evaluation of quality, relevant, and timely content, products, and services (e.g., templates, toolkits, websites, webinars, peer learning and connection experiences, trainings, and other innovative learning approaches) aligned with hub topic areas for affiliate capability/capacity building and organizational/departmental standards and processes
- Collaborate across applicable HFHI departments, including affiliate learning consultants, external subject matter experts, and the affiliated network to ensure that resource content and support aligns with best practices, mission, values, and guiding principles.
- Design, coordinate, and facilitate Communities of Practice, Peer Connection Chats, and other training experiences for the affiliate network, applying strong project management practices, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
- Stay informed on nonprofit management and operations trends, risks, and opportunities (e.g. topics such as governance and board management, finance, human resources, information technology, administration, compliance and risk management, and other day-to-day operational topics) to ensure content, resources, and services are relevant, timely, and impactful for the US affiliate network.
- Support other key initiatives, as directed, through project management, stakeholder engagement, subject matter expertise, and effective use of data and content curation tools.

#### **Network Outreach, Engagement, Relationship Building, and General/SME Support (40%)**

- Provide high-quality service and support to the affiliate network, answering inquiries, identifying needs, and creating opportunities for peer-to-peer learning and community building.
- Collaborate on marketing, communications, knowledge management, and outreach efforts to elevate the hub as a go-to resource for affiliate leaders, including leveraging and supporting MyHabitat, Viva Engage communities, regional and Affiliate Support Organization events and offerings, Affiliate Support Center inquiries, practitioner cohorts, and other opportunities for building awareness, usage, and satisfaction through subject matter expertise
- Foster engagement (in Viva Engage communities and other innovative approaches) by identifying common needs, sparking conversations with and among affiliates, aggregating promising practices from the field, and integrating insights into content and services.

#### **Performance Expectations**

- Successful completion of annual goals connected to Expertise Hubs and Division Objectives
- Annual network engagement/customer service metrics successfully met
- Annual quality and satisfaction metrics successfully met
- Measurement of additional expectations based on Annual Job plan
- Active demonstration of living out HFHI’s core values and being an active, cooperative team member

### **Cross Functional Capabilities**

- Employees in multiple divisions with different skillsets work together to achieve Habitat for Humanity International’s mission and common strategic goals.
- Key aspects of cross-functional responsibilities in a global non-profit include: Strategic planning, program design and implementation, communication and branding, monitoring and evaluation, and compliance and risk management.
- Strong understanding of business management and operations, including board governance, financial management, and risk prevention, particularly within non-profit organizations - Proficient
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, and results-driven environment. - Proficient
- Proven project management skills, including prioritization, time management, and delivering impact amidst competing demands. - Proficient
- Experience coordinating and facilitating training sessions, webinars, and group/team meetings. - Proficient
- Ability to develop, organize, and deliver content, tools, and resources to support programmatic and/or operational application, implementation, improvement and socialization. - Proficient
- Outstanding interpersonal skills, including emotional intelligence, relationship building, and the ability to influence and motivate others without authority Proficient
- Ability to navigate ambiguity by defining success, establishing systems, and driving clarity in complex situations. - Proficient
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to quickly gather, synthesize, and summarize information for diverse audiences. - Proficient
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor communication for different stakeholders and audiences. - Proficient
- Demonstrated commitment to excellent customer service and stakeholder engagement. - Proficient
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and comfort using digital platforms (e.g., Smartsheet, SharePoint, Salesforce, other CRMs, online meeting tools). - Proficient

### **Preferred Requirements**

- Experience with Habitat for Humanity, other federated nonprofit organizations, or membership organizations
- Experience presenting or leading trainings (virtual and in-person)
- Project management experience
- Understanding of the HFH mission
- Active support of HFHI Values:
    - Humility – We are part of something bigger than ourselves
    - Courage – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular
    - Accountability – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission
- Safeguarding: HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

**Ready to put your expertise to work for Habitat’s mission? Apply to join our Management and Operations U.S. Expertise Hub.**

Please note that applications for this position will be accepted through December 11, 2026. Interested candidates are encouraged their applications before the deadline.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$63,900.00 USD

title: Project Manager
body:
?Our organization is an international NGO operating in 41 countries, committed to addressing global challenges through international cooperation projects. We work with an impact-oriented approach, collaborating with local and international partners to respond to humanitarian emergencies and promote sustainable development.

We are looking for a dynamic and passionate individual to join our team in Burundi as **Project Manager.**

**Aim of the position**: The main role of the **Project Manager (PM)** is to provide overall project management with technical expertise to all activities relating to the implementation of the project “**ENGAGER** – Renforcer l’ENGAGement de la société burundaises pour un Reele développement local participatif et inclusif de la Province de Butanyerera”. The **PM** has the key responsibility of coordinating and ensuring the successful implementation and targets’ achievements of the project.

**? Duty Station:** Bujumbura (with field travels)

**? Starting** **Date:** January 2027

**⏳Period:** 12 months (extendable)

**Language:** English

**Reporting to:** Country Program Coordinator (1st Supervisor) and Country Representative (2nd Supervisor).

?**Main tasks and responsibilities:**

- Supervise and have the final responsibility for the implementation of all the project activities in accordance with the projected/approved proposal, budget, financial planning and time schedule
- Be responsible and the main interlocutor between AVSI and donor in the Country
- Ensure adequate and regular coordination between AVSI Burundi and the thematic expert and focal points at Regional and Global level
- Be responsible for the achievement of all project targets and key performance indicators
- Contribute to the recruitment, orientation and training of the projects’ staff
- Ensure timely submission of narrative and financial reports to the donor in coordination with AVSI Senior Management Team and thematic focal points
- Coordinate projects staff, strengthen their capacity, autonomy and sense of responsibility; and contribute to their further professional development
- Be responsible for the application of AVSI logistic and administrative procedures for the assigned projects portfolio in concert with Operations Manager, Country Representative
- Ensure quality and sustainability of project(s) results through strategic and operational planning, monitoring, evaluation and learning (continuous improvement)
- Promote nexuses and synergies with other national and international projects, programs, interventions
- Elaborate narrative reports as per donor procedures and proactively support the preparation of financial reports including the collection and verification of the relevant project documentation
- Elaborate any other reports as required by AVSI, local authorities and/or donor
- Maintain and develop proactive relationships with partners, local authorities and with all stakeholders involved
- Periodically interact with HQs focal points for coordinating and sharing new strategies, innovations, lessons learnt, criticalities, trainings, workshops etc.
- Share within AVSI worldwide network the most significant experiences and lessons learnt together with the thematic focal point
- Represent AVSI in relevant sectorial coordination structures and other meetings
- Represent AVSI for project or thematic related meetings at provincial/national level, and district level if the situation requires
- Identify new funding proposals also with other donors and program
- Carry-out any other duties and/or responsibilities assigned by the supervisor
- Support and supervision of the implementation and application of AVSI policies (PSEAH, code of conduct, Whistleblowing, among others).

?**Essential Requirements**

- Bachelor’s degree in Rural Development, Economics, Management, Entrepreneurship, Development Studies, Political Sciences or other related fields
- Master’s degree in relevant field would be an added advantage
- Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in managerial position, preferably within INGOs, multinational organizations, private sector, or complex operational environments.

? **Other required skills and experiences:**

- Experience and well-developed skills in staff management, supervision, and capacity building
- Strong planning, management and coordination skills, with the ability to organize a workload comprised of varying and changing tasks and responsibilities
- Demonstrated strong ability to coordinate and manage multiple teams, partners and maintain strong relationships with government entities, donors, and other stakeholders
- Solid understanding of sub-granting procedures and contractual arrangements
- Strong experience and familiarity of working with M&E systems and approaches
- Computer skills: Strong knowledge of the main IT tools
- Patient, adaptable, flexible, able to improvise and remain responsive and communicate clearly and effectively under pressure
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Fluency in French and English, written and spoken
- Valid international driving license.

?AVSI reserves the right to request information from previous employers regarding any disputes, safeguarding concerns, investigations, or disciplinary actions, and to require the candidate to provide criminal and civil records, for the purpose of assessing the worker’s professional suitability for roles involving contact with vulnerable individuals, including children and adults.

?AVSI applies the principle of inclusiveness and non-discrimination in its selection process, ensuring equal opportunities regardless of sex, age, ethnicity, nationality, sexual orientation, gender, marital status, religious belief, disability, or belonging to protected classes.

title: Protection from Violence Programme Development Manager Ethiopia Addis Ababa
body:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a dynamic and strategic **Protection from Violence (PFV) Programme Development Manager (PDM)** to provide technical leadership and drive the growth, quality and impact of its Protection from Violence programming.

In this role, you will lead the technical development and strategic direction of the PFV Core Competency, spearhead programme development and fundraising initiatives, and ensure high-quality programme delivery across the operation. You will also strengthen technical capacity through staff mentoring, training and coaching, while providing oversight of programme quality, MEAL, budget management and procurement to ensure effective implementation and accountability.

We are looking for a leader who can translate protection priorities into impactful programmes, build strong technical teams and drive sustainable programming that responds to the needs of people affected by displacement and violence.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

- Develop and implement the Protection from Violence strategy for NRC Ethiopia including Macro Log frames that are aligned with country and global strategies priorities.
- Develop technical standards, SOPs, guidance documents for PFV across NRC Ethiopia, under the guidance of NRC’s PFV Global Advisers
- Promote the rights of conflict- and displacement-affected people in line with the advocacy strategy. Undertake Protection Advocacy initiatives.
- Contribute to fundraising, develop and revise funding proposal, budgets and donor reports.
- Overall technical management and mentorship of project staff across NRC Ethiopia
- Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff, in approaches including cash-based interventions and market-based programme
- Oversee PFV project(s) implementation across NRC Ethiopia, including development and oversight of Community Feedback Mechanism
- Lead the localization agenda of NRC Ethiopia for PFV. Identify meaningful partners for strategic cooperation aiming to advance PFV portfolio across Ethiopia.
- Follow up on compliance with contractual commitments within PFV, ensure high technical quality products
- Ensure that key learnings are extracted from Protection from Violence implementation, and incorporate them in Protection from Violence and staff development processes
- Represent NRC in relevant forums/clusters, including with national authorities and donors

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAt92z8Iv4rSqzgkeTdghASAZNyyCLKN07CJRmwR94cBx8?e=poxnT3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Graduate degree with minimum 5 years of relevant experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations
- Detailed knowledge of humanitarian and protection principles and guidelines for humanitarian assistance
- Good understanding of Protection Cluster coordination mechanisms
- Strong coordination, representation skills and inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Self-motivated and excellent observer of protection issues
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets
- Strong experience in programme development and management
- Experience in training facilitation and capacity-building
- Experience in Ethiopia mandatory
- Willingness to spend a significant period of time at NRC’s Area Offices
- This position is open to Ethiopian nationals only.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

title: [Pipeline Position] Program Implementation and Performance Manager (Africa Regional Office) [Based in Kigali]
body:
## ***\*\*\*This is a pipeline position created to prepare for anticipated hiring needs. Final hiring decisions will be made following internal review processes.\*\*\****

## **We are seeking a Program Implementation and Performance Manager for 2-year-regular position (renewable) to work within Africa Regional Office at the International Vaccine Institute in Kigali, Rwanda. (Duty station: Kigali, Rwanda)**

**Job Description**

This role is responsible for the technical implementation of VEA4A, working with the Program Director, participating institutions and other partners to translate programme objectives into activities and apply technical expertise throughout implementation. Its responsibilities also include institutional readiness, programme performance, monitoring, evaluation and learning, inclusion, safeguarding coordination and implementation learning for VEA4A. It also encompasses the day-to-day management and coordination of programme implementation, including planning, resource and budget monitoring, risk management and reporting, to support the delivery of agreed commitments on time, within budget and to the required quality standards. The role works with the Program Director, participating institutions and other partners to monitor progress and inform programme adaptations.

**Key Roles & Responsibilities**

**1. Institutional readiness assessment and programme performance monitoring**

- Lead HEI readiness assessment, institutional-strengthening monitoring and readiness recommendations with the Training Lead and HEI teams.
- Lead the MEL framework, indicator definitions, data-quality arrangements, performance dashboards, quarterly reviews, learning briefs and programme reporting.
- Integrate evidence from training, HEIs, participants and employment pathways and recommend adaptations to the Program Director.
- Facilitate narrative and performance reporting to the Foundation and ensure timely technical, budget and partner inputs.

**2. Programme planning and implementation**

- Manage day-to-day implementation in accordance with IVI Project Management Guidelines, monitoring progress against the approved workplan, timeline, quality requirements and budget.
- Translate the approved proposal, workplan and budget into integrated annual, quarterly and detailed implementation plans.
- Own the master workplan, critical path, milestones, dependencies, resource plan and consolidated delivery calendar.
- Coordinate routine implementation across ARUA, HEIs, IVI technical teams, functional units, providers and all programme workstreams.
- Manage scope, schedule, deliverables, risks, issues, decisions, changes, assumptions and corrective actions through documented project controls.
- Monitor partner deliverables and programme commitments and ensure that delays or performance concerns receive timely action.
- Chair routine implementation meetings and act for the Program Director on operational matters when formally delegated.

**3. Budget tracking and programme document preparation**

- Monitor programme expenditure and support budget phasing and forecasting, working with the Project Administrator and relevant colleagues to identify and communicate variances against the approved budget.
- Contribute to the preparation of programme-related agreements and contracts with participating institutions, service providers and other partners, in coordination with relevant IVI functions.

**4. Systems oversight and safeguarding & inclusion facilitation**

- Lead data-quality arrangements for programme monitoring and reporting.
- Oversee programme-wide digital operations, including the relationship among applications, LMS, participant records, course records and reporting systems.
- Facilitate the implementation of safeguarding, inclusion and data-protection requirements across the programme, working with IVI specialist functions and partners\*\*.\*\*

**Job Requirements and Qualifications**

**1. Education Requirements**

- Advanced degree in health sciences, public health, project management, development, education, social sciences or a related field.

**2. Related Field Work Experience**

- 8+ years with Master’s degree

**3. Technical and Professional Skills / Knowledge**

- Substantial experience managing complex, multi-partner and donor-funded programmes, preferably across more than one country.
- Demonstrated knowledge of project planning, scope and change control, risk management, partner performance, budget monitoring and donor reporting.
- Experience in monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), data quality and institutional-capacity assessment.
- Understanding of safeguarding and inclusive programme delivery.
- Experience in workforce development, higher education, health training or vaccine-related programmes is desirable.
- Integrated project and programme management.
- Analytical problem-solving and prioritisation.
- Programme performance monitoring and use of evidence.
- Cross-functional coordination and collaboration.
- Donor reporting and concise writing.
- Risk, safeguarding and data-governance awareness.
- Ability to move between strategic context and operational detail.
- Ability to travel internationally.
- Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is desirable.

**4. Key Competency**

- Client Orientation
- Communication
- Commitment to Continuous Learning

**5. Language Proficiency**

- Fluent in English (spoken, written)

**\*\*\*IVI welcomes applications from all sections of the community. We encourage women to apply, especially from countries that are currently under-represented within IVI.\*\*\***

title: Thailand Project Director, AFGHS
body:
***About FHI 360 and AFGHS-FHI 360***

FHI 360 is a nonprofit human development organization dedicated to improving lives in lasting ways by advancing integrated, locally driven solutions. Our staff includes experts in health, education, nutrition, economic development, youth, research, technology, communication, and social marketing—creating a unique mix of capabilities to address today’s interrelated development challenges. FHI 360 serves more than 60 countries and all U.S. states and territories.

The **America First Global Health Strategy – FHI 360 (AFGHS-FHI 360)** project is initially a 13-month project (2026 – 2027) with the ability to be extended for up to five years (though 2031). Funded by the United States (US) Department of State (DOS), AFGHS-FHI 360 is a global fixed amount award (FAA) and operates in approximately 50 countries, addressing key public health challenges such as HIV/AIDS, global health security (GHS), maternal and neonatal child health (MNCH), malaria, tuberculosis (TB), polio, supply chain (SC) and health systems strengthening (HSS). In Thailand, AFGHS-FHI 360 will continue to build off the country’s progress to date to future strengthen the country’s health systems responses to HIV/AIDS, GHS, and malaria. AFGHS-FHI 360 is recruiting a Project Director located in Bangkok, Thailand. This position is open to Thai nationals only.

***Job Summary:***

The AFGHS-FHI 360 Thailand Project Director provides overall leadership, management and strategic direction of the AFGHS-FHI 360 project in Thailand. The Project Director will oversee the implementation of the AFGHS-FHI 360 HIV/AIDS, GHS, and malaria portfolio in Thailand with a focus on health systems strengthening. They will ensure that project goals and objectives are achieved within the prescribed project milestones, time frame and funding parameters. They will serve as the primary point of contact for AFGHS-FHI 360 activities in Thailand and provide technical and management leadership to the country project and ensure successful implementation of the work plan to achieve project milestones, monitoring of expenditures in lines with the approved budget, achievement of the project’s targets and goals, and identification, mitigation and escalation of risk. They will be required to coordinate and work with a diverse group of organizations and stakeholders, such as the Ministry of Health, senior government officials, country health staff, international and national development partner organizations, and the United States Government (USG) donor representatives.

Reporting to the Regional Director, the Project Director works in close collaboration with the AFGHS-FHI 360 headquarters (HQ) team, planning and directing project implementation, milestone success, and monitoring budget/spending from startup through closeout. Under a matrixed structure, they lead the country project team in the planning of project activities ensuring completion of the project on schedule and within budget constraints.

***Accountabilities:***

- Direct overall project vision, design, planning and implementation; ensures that goals and objectives are accomplished within prescribed time frame and contractual parameters.
- Ensure internal management systems for contracting, recruitment, and delivery; move rapidly to respond to the demands for service delivery on the ground.
- Foster innovation and new ideas for better targeted, and more cost-efficient and effective strategies to reach project beneficiaries and retain them in services, as applicable to scope.
- Develop, manage, and strengthen strategic relationships with government entities, implementing partners, local organizations, and other stakeholders to advance project objectives and foster collaboration.
- Ensure achievement of contractual targets, milestones, and deliverables by leading effective milestone and performance management processes, monitoring progress, mitigating risks, and ensuring activities remain on schedule, within budget, and compliant with donor requirements.
- Identify and pursue opportunities to leverage complementary donor, governmental, and organizational resources through strategic partnerships, collaboration agreements, and aligned programming.
- Provide leadership and management to project staff within a matrixed management structure, ensuring clear priorities, effective teamwork, staff onboarding, performance management, professional development, and accountability for the timely delivery of high-quality project results.
- Work closely with AFGHS-FHI 360 HQ on the development of annual work plans, milestone plans and budgets for timely submission to and approval by USG to implement those plans.
- Serve as the primary contact to the global AFGHS-FHI 360 HQ project team.
- Serve as the primary liaison with the Regional Strategic Assistance Section (RSA)/DOS Thailand staff, maintaining strong donor relationships and ensuring effective communication, responsiveness, and coordination between the project team and donor representatives.
- Oversee technical and management reviews, to identify and escalate risks, address performance challenges and highlight accomplishments to ensure the program moves forward in a compliant manner.
- Oversee monitoring and evaluation systems, ensuring that program is adequately monitored, and that evaluative thinking is incorporated appropriately into the program wherever possible.
- Guide technical and organizational capacity building initiatives with local partners and senior staff to ensure delivery of high-quality training, technical assistance, and reports.
- Represent the project in advancing evidence-based and innovative strategies and approaches on a global, regional and local level.
- Coordinate closely with other FHI 360 project teams in country to ensure a “One FHI 360” approach and avoid duplication of efforts between projects, as applicable.
- Serve as a member of the FHI 360 Thailand Senior Leadership Team and provide input and assistance to the management of the country program, develop country program strategy, business plans, operational plans and budgets.
- Research sources for potential funding and contribute to proposal development, as requested.
- Responsible for creating, promoting, and maintaining safe and equitable work environments for all personnel, including a harassment- and violence-free work culture, and systems for safeguarding project participants.
- Support performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching, and career support.
- Potentially serve as FHI 360’s Country Representative (CR) for the country depending on current country project portfolio.
- Other tasks as appropriate to the position.

***Applied Knowledge & Skills:***

- Comprehensive knowledge of theories, concepts and practices with project management, process development and execution.
- Excellent and demonstrated project management skills.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills.
- Strong consultative and negotiation skills.
- Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to plan, organize, and manage resources for successful completion of projects.
- Ability to motivate, influences, and collaborates with others.
- Ability to build positive local working relationships with local communities, government officials, and donor representatives.

***Problem Solving & Impact:***

- Decisions and actions have a significant impact on management and division operations.
- Problems encountered are complex and highly varied.
- Exercise judgment to meet business strategies and develop objectives that align with organizational goals.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

***Education: \*\****

- Master's Degree or its International Equivalent • Communication and Social Marketing, Economic Development, Education, Health, Nutrition, Research, Technology and Youth or a Related Fields.
- Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.

***Experience: \*\****

- Typically requires 10+ years of relevant experience with projects management principles and practices (including 5+ years of line management experience).
- Proficient with applicable rules, regulations, and policies associated with international development and non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
- Experience in managing large, complex and high-quality health projects, with demonstrated expertise in health systems strengthening and at least one of the following technical areas: HIV, GHS, malaria.
- Experience in leadership in establishing and maintaining positive working relationships and partnerships with major stakeholders including governments, donor agencies, partners, and community networks in at least one of the three technical areas.
- Experience in overseeing all aspects of international donor-funded projects, with a preference for USG-funding, including program and financial management, human resources, compliance, and quality assurance.
- Experience with fixed price mechanisms (e.g., fixed amount awards, fixed price contracts, etc.)
- Demonstrated strategic planning, staff development and capacity building experience under a matrixed structure.
- Proactive in managing multiple tasks, managing and working in the virtual work environment, and flexible and open to managing time for working with different teams in different time zones as needed.
- Excellent interpersonal, organizational, communication, coordination and collaboration, team building and management, and problem-solving skills.
- Must be able to read, write, and speak fluent English and Thai.
- Experience operating in insecure environments.
- Experience working in a non-governmental organization (NGO).

***Typical Physical Demands***\*\*:\*\*

- Typical office environment.
- Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
- Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
- Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.

***Technology to be Used***\*\*:\*\*

- Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

***Travel Requirements:***

- 10% - 25%

\*\*Or an equivalent combination of relevant education and/or experience sufficient to successfully perform the key responsibilities of the job. This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time.
