title: CRM Platform Specialist (Cluster)
body:
## **Your mission**

The Platform Specialist (CRM) plays a key operational and strategic role in ensuring the availability, reliability, security, and ongoing improvement of War Child Alliance’s Salesforce platform as a business-critical global service. The role is responsible for the administration, delivery, maintenance, and optimization of the Salesforce environment, ensuring the platform remains stable, secure, scalable, and aligned with evolving organizational needs. This includes hands-on administration, configuration, implementation, release management, access control, integrations, incident resolution, documentation, and continuous service improvement.

In addition to Salesforce, the role provides technical administration and service ownership for a portfolio of smaller SaaS applications used across the organization, applying the same structured and service-led approach. The position ensures these systems are effectively governed, supported, maintained, and continuously improved, while also strengthening the integration and alignment between business applications, workflows, and data flows across the organization.

Working within War Child Alliance’s wider enterprise systems landscape, including Salesforce, Unit4 Business World, and other cloud-based tools, the Application Platform Lead (CRM) ensures that business-critical platforms operate as a stable and integrated ecosystem. The role works closely with business stakeholders, suppliers, and internal IT colleagues to ensure that Salesforce and related SaaS platforms are implemented in a scalable and supportable way, operated as managed services, and enhanced over time to meet changing operational and organizational needs.

The role is ideally to be staffed in within a Country Office, in line with War Child Alliance’s wider strategy to increasingly co-locate global resources closer to program and operational delivery. Embedding Salesforce platform administration within a Country Office environment will help strengthen adoption of the Salesforce platform by ensuring closer alignment between the global solution and operational realities in country programs. This will also provide greater insight into how the platform can be better configured, deployed, and supported to meet both global and country-level needs.

**What you will do:**

- Own and lead the end-to-end administration, delivery, support, and continuous improvement of the Salesforce platform as a business-critical service. The Salesforce platform includes multiple instances of Salesforce Cloud and multiple third-party applications integrations.
- Drive and deliver implementation and enhancement cycles, including requirements gathering, solution design, configuration, testing, deployment, and release management.
- Translate and priorities business requirements into scalable, secure, and sustainable Salesforce and SaaS solutions aligned with organizational needs.
- Administer and optimize the Salesforce environment, including user management, roles, permissions, workflows, automation, data models, and platform configuration.
- Own and manage ITIL service management processes for the platform, including incidents, service requests, problems, changes, releases, and escalation pathways.
- Monitor and proactively improve system performance, reliability, service levels, and user experience through root cause analysis, KPI tracking, and issue prevention.
- Lead continuous improvement by identifying process enhancements, automation opportunities, and roadmap priorities across Salesforce and supporting SaaS applications.
- Ensure accountability for system integration, data flows, data integrity, and alignment across Salesforce, Unit4, and other connected business systems.
- Provide ownership and oversight of user support, adoption, documentation, training, and resolution of recurring issues through sustainable solutions.
- Coordinate and manage internal stakeholders, vendors, and implementation partners to ensure timely delivery, alignment of expectations, and accountability for outcomes.

**ROLE-SPECIFIC OR CONTEXT RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Maintain and safeguard core applications, ensuring system performance, stability, and effective alignment with user and business needs.
- Safeguard and maintain data accuracy, consistency, and application logic across integrated systems, ensuring alignment with business processes and controls.
- Coordinate and support application testing, system upgrades, and change deployments, including documentation updates and user readiness activities.
- Deliver first- and second-line support for core applications, resolving incidents and liaising with vendors where required to ensure timely resolution.
- Collaborate with IT colleagues to maintain system interfaces and ensure seamless data exchange between applications and external platforms.
- Provide and maintain user training, guidance, and support materials, including manuals, FAQs, and system documentation in collaboration with process owners.
- Identify and propose system and process improvements, supporting implementation of enhancements aligned with organizational priorities.
- Establish and monitor user access and authorization structures, ensuring compliance with internal controls, security requirements, and safeguarding standards.
- Participate in cross-functional and multidisciplinary teams focused on improving digital workflows, systems integration, and organizational processes.
- Uphold and embed War Child safeguarding and data protection principles in all application administration, support, and system management activities.
- Maintain and operate ITIL-aligned change, release, and service management processes across supported applications and platforms.
- Evaluate and support adoption of new system features and application capabilities where they improve efficiency, usability, or service delivery.

## **Your profile**

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

- HBO+ (Bachelor’s level or higher applied education) working and thinking level in IT, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
- Relevant certifications in Salesforce Administration and Platform Management are highly desirable.
- Certifications in ITIL, Agile, or service management frameworks are an advantage.

**Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of hands on experience in Salesforce administration, configuration, and implementation.
- Strong experience with Salesforce configuration, including roles, profiles, permission sets, flows, automation, and data models.
- Proven experience managing systems as operational services, including ownership of reliability, performance, and support.
- Experience with ITIL-based service management practices, including incident, problem, change, and release management.
- Experience with release management processes, structured deployments, and controlled system changes.
- Experience administering and supporting SaaS platforms and cloud-based business applications.
- Experience supporting or managing system integrations and data flows between applications.
- Experience working with external vendors, implementation partners, and service providers.
- Experience working in multi-system environments, ideally including enterprise platforms such as Salesforce and ERP systems.
- Experience in NGO, humanitarian, or international development organisations is an advantage.
- Familiarity with Agile and/or Waterfall delivery methodologies.
- Strong experience in stakeholder engagement and translating business needs into technical solutions.
- Strong communication experience across technical and non-technical stakeholders in multi-location environments.

**Languages**

- English, mandatory
- Dutch, French, Spanish or Arabic, desirable.

**(Technical) Knowledge**

- Strong knowledge of Salesforce administration and configuration, including automation, data structures, and user management.
- Strong understanding of service management (ITIL) principles and operational IT service delivery.
- Knowledge of SaaS platform administration and lifecycle management.
- Understanding of system integrations, APIs, and data exchange principles.
- Understanding of data management, data quality, and governance principles.
- Knowledge of release and change management processes.
- Understanding of cloud-based application environments and enterprise systems ecosystems.
- Familiarity with Agile and Waterfall methodologies.
- Awareness of information security, access control, and data protection principles.
- Experience with support and ticketing systems for incident and service management.

**What we offer**

- **Location :** We work with global teams with team members being based in different locations. War Child currently operates in: Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Colombia, DR Congo, Jordan, Lebanon, the occupied Palestinian territory, South Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine (soon to be registered), and Yemen. Preference is given to applicants who reside and have valid working permits. War Child does not offer relocation.
- **Type of Contract :** Local contract with salary and secondary labour conditions based on the in-country salary scale, local T&C's will apply.

**Why You Should Apply**

- **Meaningful Impact :** Contribute directly to improving the lives of children and families affected by conflict through quality education and long-term, sustainable change.
- **Professional Growth:** Join a dynamic organisation that values learning, innovation, and professional development, with opportunities for capacity building and growth through the role and War Child’s global network.
- **Global Reach :** Play a key role in scaling a ground-breaking programme across multiple conflict-affected contexts worldwide.
- **Collaborative & Inclusive Culture :** Work alongside passionate, mission-driven colleagues in a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace that prioritises safety, fairness and equal opportunity for all.

title: National Non-Technical Survey/ Explosive Ordnance Risk Education Manager
body:
**Who are we?**

The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunities for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfillment of the wish to return home. The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, and honesty and transparency.

**DRC Syria**

DRC has been operating in Syria since 2008, initially responding to the Iraqi refugee crisis before pivoting to a full-scale response to the Syria crisis from 2011 onwards. Our work encompasses the full cycle of displacement—responding to life-saving humanitarian needs and supporting community recovery until durable solutions can be achieved. DRC Syria takes an area-based approach to supporting internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities across our key sectors: Economic Recovery and Resilience, Protection, WASH, Shelter and Infrastructure, and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (including Humanitarian Mine Action). With an established rapid response mechanism, DRC can rapidly respond to emerging crises and shocks to meet acute emergency needs. Recognizing the significant need for early recovery and resilience programming to ensure dignified, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions for fragile communities, DRC’s programmes foster resilience for individuals and communities in situations of protracted displacement and during the initial stages of post-conflict recovery, towards a durable solution of their choice. With active portfolios in the neighboring countries of Jordan, Lebanon, Türkiye and Iraq, DRC offers a cross-border, regional response to the Syria crisis, through cross-border protection monitoring, advocacy, and trends analysis.

**Overall purpose of the role**: The NTS/EORE Manager leads and oversees DRC’s Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Community Liaison (CL), and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) activities in Syria, ensuring full compliance with International Mine Action Standards (IMAS), national standards, and DRC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

The role is responsible for the planning, implementation, quality management, and continuous improvement of NTS/EORE operations, while contributing to the strategic development of DRC’s Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) programme. This includes developing and adapting SOPs, tools, and methodologies in line with the evolving operational context.

A key function of the role is to ensure strong integration of NTS/EORE with DRC’s broader recovery portfolio, including HLP, livelihoods, shelter, WASH, and protection, so that mine action activities directly enable safe, sustainable, and area-based recovery outcomes.

The NTS/EORE Manager ensures that DRC effectively maps EO contamination through systematic identification, recording, and analysis of hazardous areas, while delivering targeted EORE to reduce risk-taking behavior among affected populations.

This is a twelve-month, country-wide role designed to support the scale-up, consolidation, and standardization of NTS/EORE operations across Syria. The position offers a unique opportunity to shape operational approaches, systems, and tools during a critical phase of programme expansion.

**Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities:**

**Technical Management and Implementation**

- Lead the planning, implementation, and oversight of NTS, CL, and EORE activities in assigned areas
- Ensure activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in line with IMAS, national standards, and DRC SOPs
- Oversee tasking, deployment, and daily management of NTS/EORE teams
- Ensure systematic integration of NTS/EORE outputs into clearance prioritization and broader HMA programming
- Ensure that NTS/EORE activities are aligned with and support DRC’s recovery interventions, including livelihoods, shelter, infrastructure, WASH, and protection
- Lead the development, revision, and contextualization of SOPs, guidelines, and tools for NTS, CL, and EORE
- Develop and refine data collection tools, prioritization tools, and methodologies
- Ensure alignment of operational tools with IMAS and evolving national standards
- Promote continuous improvement and adaptation of approaches based on operational learning
- Develop monthly team workplans linked to project targets, locations and available resources; coordinate implementation with Technical Field Managers and Area Managers and escalate delivery gaps to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Ensure deployment readiness in accordance with approved safety, communications and medical procedures; suspend unsafe activities and immediately report concerns to the HMA Operations Manager.
- Lead EORE needs assessments, adapt and pre-test messages and materials for different at-risk groups, and work with MEAL to assess understanding and safer behavior.

**Strategy and Programme Development**

- Contribute to the strategic development and expansion of DRC’s HMA programme in Syria
- Provide technical inputs to proposal development, concept notes, and donor engagement
- Actively promote area-based and nexus approaches, ensuring mine action enables and is integrated with recovery and development outcomes
- Identify operational gaps and opportunities for scale-up and cross-sector collaboration

**Staff Management & Capacity Development**

- Line manage and supervise NTS/EORE team leaders and field teams
- Design and deliver initial and refresher training in NTS, CL, and EORE
- Lead capacity development of national staff, including substantial training, mentoring and on-the-job training
- Lead EORE/ NTS capacity development of national authorities (e.g. NMAC) and relevant stakeholders

**Quality Management, Monitoring & IM**

- Ensure strong quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) of all NTS/EORE activities
- Oversee data collection, verification, and analysis related to EO contamination
- Track progress against targets and indicators
- Ensure data is accurately captured, stored, and shared with relevant stakeholders (e.g. SNMAC, MA AoR)
- Strengthen linkages between operations and Information Management (IM)
- Document QA findings and non-conformities, assign corrective actions and deadlines, and verify closure.
- Coordinate with IM and MEAL on indicator definitions, disaggregated beneficiary reporting and prevention of double counting; protect personal and sensitive information and share it only through approved procedures.

**Coordination & External Liaison**

- Liaise with Mine Action AoR, relevant working groups and other operators to ensure alignment and avoid duplication
- Engage with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination forums as required
- Support coordination on tasking, prioritization, and information sharing

**Budget Management, Reporting & Compliance**

- Manage EORE/NTS budgets and track expenditures against targets as well as progress
- Prepare and oversee high-quality internal and donor reporting (weekly, monthly, and ad hoc)
- Ensure timely submission of field reports and data
- Contribute to donor reports with technical inputs and analysis
- Exercise budget responsibilities within delegated authority, coordinating expenditure forecasts and procurement planning with the HMA Operations Manager and the Head of HDP

**Integrated Programming and Housing, Land and Property (HLP)**

- Strengthen operational linkages between NTS/EORE and DRC's Protection, HLP, Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH programmes, ensuring that contamination data and risk assessments inform integrated, area-based interventions.
- Facilitate joint assessments, operational planning and referral pathways with other DRC sectors, enabling mine action to support safe access to land, infrastructure, essential services and livelihoods.
- Act as the HMA technical focal point for a HLP consultancy, supporting the development, field-testing and operationalization of harmonized HLP due diligence guidance, tools and procedures for Syria's mine action sector.
- Ensure HLP considerations, including land ownership, tenure, access, competing claims and potential land-related disputes, are systematically integrated into NTS, community liaison, prioritization and land release planning.
- Coordinate with DRC's HLP specialists, the HLP Technical Working Group, Mine Action AoR and relevant national stakeholders to support the adoption of harmonized HLP approaches and their potential integration into National Mine Action Standards.
- Promote conflict-sensitive approaches to survey and land release, ensuring that HMA interventions do not inadvertently exacerbate land disputes, exclusion or community tensions.
- Refer land disputes and legal questions to qualified HLP specialists; provide operational input to HLP processes within the manager’s technical competence and delegated authority.

**Safeguarding, Inclusion and Accountability**

- Ensure compliance with DRC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse requirements; report concerns through designated channels.
- Ensure inclusive participation and accessible community complaints and feedback channels, and coordinate appropriate referrals with Protection and Accountability colleagues.
- Undertake any other tasks as required by HMA Operations Manager and Head of HDP.

**Experience and technical competencies:**

- Minimum 5 years of experience in EORE and NTS within humanitarian mine action (HMA) programmes
- At least two years of experience supervising teams or managing EORE/NTS activities.
- NTS and EORE qualified
- QMS qualified (is an asset)
- Demonstrated experience in managing and training NTS, Community Liaison (CL), and EORE teams, including capacity development of national staff and authorities
- Strong knowledge of IMAS and SOPs applicable to NTS, CL, and EORE, including quality management (QA/QC)
- Proven experience in developing, adapting, and implementing SOPs, tools, and methodologies
- Solid understanding of EO contamination patterns and operational context in Syria or similar environments, including familiarity with military tactics and their impact on contamination
- Knowledge of land release processes, including NTS–TS–clearance linkages, and familiarity with clearance methodologies and equipment
- Experience integrating HMA with other humanitarian and recovery sectors, particularly HLP, including an understanding of land tenure risks, conflict sensitivity and the role of NTS in supporting integrated, area-based programming (desirable).
- Experience with information management and data analysis, including IMSMA and GIS tools (e.g. QGIS, ArcGIS, Garmin/BaseCamp or similar)
- Experience contributing to programme development, reporting, and donor engagement
- Strong coordination and representation skills, including engagement with national authorities, UN agencies, and other operators.

**Education**:

- Relevant university degree or technical qualification, or substantial directly relevant professional experience in lieu of a formal academic qualification.
- Documented NTS and EORE training and demonstrated technical competence remain essential.

**Languages:**

- Strong working English, both spoken and written.
- Fluent in Arabic, both spoken and written.

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating**: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating**: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity**: You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract length**: 12 months (Extension based on performance and funds)
- **Salary Level**: MF2 (in accordance with the DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Rural Damascus
- **Expected Start Date:** As soon as possible

title: Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education
body:
**BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education**

**Job Location:** **Kenya** ***(This position is local to Kenya, thus only Kenyan Nationals are encouraged to apply)***

**Application deadline: 28 November, 2026**

**About the Role:**

BRAC International (BI) is seeking a Senior Manager, Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE) who will provide technical, programmatic and strategic support to present and future ECD and Education interventions in Africa. A key strategic focus for BI will be delivering more integrated development programmes that address multi-dimensional issues of poverty and this implies working in close collaboration with other sectors in BI. Responsibilities also include supporting country teams in developing strong Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Monitoring and Learning systems and tools in an effort that ECDE interventions are of quality, address multiple barriers, and result in impact. S/he will also play a key role in assisting country offices and BI in mobilising additional resources, including supporting new business development and ensuring ECDE or integrated projects in countries under their purview are documented and learnings are disseminated, internally and externally. Furthermore, S/he will also actively participate in developing and supporting integrated programmes.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Programme and Strategy Development**

- Support country teams in the design, implementation of quality ECDE interventions in Africa and as required beyond.
- Work closely with country teams and other sector teams in designing scale-up plans for ECDE and integrated programmes;
- Participate in the project design process (both proactive and in response to calls for proposals), involving country programme teams, especially leveraging an integrated approach
- Support country management in setting strategic directions for ECDE and integrated programming.

**Technical Assistance in Quality ECD and Education Project / Programme Implementation**

- Support quality implementation of ECDE interventions in BI countries in Africa and as requested beyond.
- Collaborate with country teams to develop ECDE specific or integrated SOPs, curricula, training guides, monitoring and learning tools;
- Support the recruitment and onboarding processes of new ECD/Education and other programme staff as needed.
- Conduct field visits to ensure fidelity and impact of ECDE or integrated development interventions and provide capacity strengthening support based on needs.
- Regularly support the assessment of project performance to ensure early identification of implementation challenges and timely guidance and support with appropriate solutions.

**Business Development for Resource Mobilisation**

- Support opportunities for fundraising, and ensure high quality technical support to all ECDE specific or integrated related fundraising within the organisation.
- Write/edit technical parts of the concept note/proposal, review other sections to ensure alignment with the call for proposals, and incorporate experience, learnings, and achievements from past projects.
- Review the scope and requirements of any funding opportunity, check the alignment of the funds/calls with the respective programme strategies, and assess its fund size, scale, strategic importance, and the technical capacity of the country and programme team to design and deliver the project.
- Review of the proposal and project budget to ensure all programme activities in the design are well-resourced, as well as ensuring all costs of the programme team support (salary, travel, capacity building) are captured in the project budget.
- Participate in various meetings with potential donors and partners to present BI’s programme strategy, approach, achievements, and learnings as required.
- Lead or support the project design (as described in the programme development section), review the relevant programmatic sections of the proposal drafted by the country/GRP team and provide their technical inputs.

**Grants Management**

- Participate in and support country teams in Africa (and as required beyond) during grant kick-off meetings for new projects or programmes.
- Regularly participate in grants review meetings that include ECD or Education grants and proactively contribute to issues of concerns and solutions.
- Support countries in budget reviews, monitoring reports review and developing action plans, coordination with other units as per ECDE operation modality.
- Regularly review and provide solution-oriented feedback to donor reports.

**Capacity Strengthening**

- Foster an environment conducive to learning and impact, by supporting the establishment of processes that promote a culture of excellence, learning and knowledge sharing.
- Contribute to country-wise capacity needs assessment, and develop a capacity-building plan for ECDE, in collaboration with country offices, other sector teams, and the Learning & Effectiveness team.
- Plan, organize and facilitate effective capacity strengthening activities in program design, quality implementation, monitoring and knowledge management of ECDE involving the provision of advice, technical assistance, training workshops, seminars and meetings or setup of a community of practice.
- Promote collaboration among team members and with the wider Programme Team and with other relevant functions in the organisation.
- Organize/support the cross-country and cross-sector experience sharing, facilitate exchange visits to enhance the capacity of the programme staff.

**Partnerships, Learning and Advocacy**

- Support country teams in Africa (and as required beyond) in the development and maintenance of strong relationships with key government, donors, partners, and other stakeholders in the area of ECDE as needed.
- Support the establishment of BI as a thought leader in the ECDE space, promoting and showcasing innovation and impact.
- Contribute to advocacy agendas aligned with programme and country strategies.
- Support country and BI ECDE team to develop program-level learning-sharing and advocacy materials.
- Represent BI ECDE as required at select forums, networks, conferences and meetings.
- Support in development and execution of ECDE learning agenda and specific project learning plans, M&L frameworks and TOC development.
- Assist the Learning and Effectiveness and country M&L teams in developing tools to collect ECDE relevant output and outcomes data, review research/evaluation reports, process documentation reports, and other learning reports, and provide inputs for finalization.
- Work with the learning team in the project/programme design stage to formulate project/programme-specific learning questions and ensure adequate budgeting.
- Contribute to the development of research agenda, study designs and coordinate study areas in collaboration with implementation team and research team;
- Coordinate where/when needed external teams to conduct research/studies and ensure fulfillment of research objectives and methodologies.
- Contribute to developing and implementing appropriate monitoring frameworks for the ECDE programmes.

**Safeguarding responsibilities**

- Implement programme decisions keeping the safety and dignity of programme participants/clients at the center, mitigate safeguarding risks and contribute to a safe working environment where staff are respected and feel confident to voice concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Receive mandatory training on the safeguarding policies and reporting channels and have access to policies.
- Participate in discussions on the safeguarding agenda in monthly meetings and actively voice concerns without fear.
- Report safeguarding incidents witnessed or experiences to the Safeguarding department. For known cases, maintain neutrality, be sensitive and non-judgemental to victims/survivors, and cooperate with organisational investigations providing accurate information as needed.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Minimum Bachelor’s degree preferably in Early Childhood Development/ Education/ Social Studies/ Development studies/ Public health/ relevant discipline.

**Experience Requirements:**

- At least 05 years of experience in working directly in Education and/or Early Childhood Development in different African country contexts.
- Overall, 5 to 7 years of working in project management/ implementation/ technical assistance/ research in the development sector.
- Experience in monitoring and evaluation of ECD and/or Education approaches, including TOC design, mixed method research, data monitoring and analysis) and ability to interpret data for decision-making
- Experience in capacity strengthening approaching, including developing and facilitating training, mentorship, and coaching on ECD and/or Education approaches across country teams
- Experience in managing projects and budgets
- Experience of working in multicultural environment will have an added value

**Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:**

- Strong knowledge of international standards and best practices on ECD and/or Education
- Sound and up to date knowledge of policies, trends, evidence-based practices/ approaches with regards to Education and Early Childhood Development, especially in Africa and Asia
- Well informed about the literature pertaining to education and child development issues in low-income countries, particularly where BRAC International operates
- Knowledge of systems, sector priorities, learning resources available, stakeholders and networks with regard to the ECD sector in BI countries
- Ability to work strategically with multiple stakeholders
- Capable of working independently and as part of team(s)
- Ability to lead the development of monitoring, research and learning plans and agenda in relation to ECDE
- Excellent interpersonal skills and demonstrated success engaging with key stakeholders to improve education/ECD programming and funding
- Strong analytical skills, strategic thinking and conceptual clarity
- Proficient in proposal development and budgeting and project management
- Strong editing, reporting skills and solid planning and organising skills
- Ability to prioritise and deal with competing demands to deliver results
- Ability to work under pressure and manage tight deadlines
- A high degree of personal resilience, flexibility and ability to adapt to changing circumstances
- Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, negotiation, facilitation and presentation skills)
- Excellent in problem solving and decision making
- Excellent networking skills
- Fluent in English (verbal and written communications) and desirable fluency in one of the local languages in Liberia or Sierra Leone.
- Proficient in computer operations including MS Word, MS Excel, Power Point, Email and various internet search engines and web-based platforms
- Flexibility to travel globally and work in different time zones as needed
- Possess high ethical and moral standards.

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 14 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit [www.bracinternational.org](http://www.bracinternational.org)

**Our Core Values:**

**Integrity:** We approach our work with honesty and integrity.

**Innovation:** We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.

**Inclusiveness:** We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most

**Effectiveness:** We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty

title: Assistant administratif et financier
body:
## 1. Contexte

La Société de Développement International (SDI) INC. est un organisme de conseil spécialisé dans l’appui aux projets et programmes de développement. En prévision de la mise en œuvre d’une mission d’une durée de douze (12) mois dans le Sud de Madagascar, financée par un bailleur de fonds international, SDI constitue une équipe pluridisciplinaire et recherche à cet effet des professionnels qualifiés et expérimentés.

La mission vise à améliorer durablement les connaissances, les attitudes et les pratiques des ménages agricoles, des élèves et des communautés rurales en matière de nutrition, d’hygiène et d’agriculture sensible à la nutrition. Elle comprendra notamment la promotion de jardins familiaux et scolaires, de cultures biofortifiées et de l’arboriculture fruitière, l’éducation nutritionnelle et les démonstrations culinaires, la formation de relais communautaires, la transformation et la conservation des aliments, ainsi que des campagnes de communication pour le changement de comportement. Les dimensions genre, jeunesse et changement climatique seront intégrées dans l’ensemble des interventions.

## 2. Lieu d’affectation et durée

Les postes sont basés dans le Sud de Madagascar, avec des déplacements fréquents dans les communes rurales d’intervention des régions Androy et Anosy. La durée prévue de l’engagement est de douze (12) mois à compter du démarrage de la mission.

## 3. Postes à pourvoir

Au total, quatorze (14) postes répartis en neuf (9) profils sont à pourvoir. Pour chaque poste, le profil requis et les principales responsabilités sont présentés ci-après.

### 3.8. Assistant(e) administratif(ve) et financier(ère) (1 poste)

**Profil requis**

- Être gestionnaire ou comptable de niveau BAC+3 au minimum en gestion ou en comptabilité.
- Justifier de plus de trois (3) années d’expérience professionnelle en administration ou comptabilité au sein de programmes ou de projets, ou en collaboration avec eux.

**Principales responsabilités**

- Assurer la gestion administrative et financière, la tenue de la comptabilité et l’archivage.
- Collaborer avec le responsable financier du client, et assurer le suivi ainsi que le rapportage financiers de la mission.

## 4. Atouts communs à tous les postes

- Une expérience de travail dans les régions du Sud de Madagascar et une bonne connaissance du contexte local.
- Une expérience confirmée en développement rural, de préférence dans le cadre de projets financés par des bailleurs de fonds internationaux.
- La maîtrise du français et du malgache ; la pratique des parlers locaux du Sud sera appréciée.
- L’adhésion aux principes d’intégrité et de prévention du harcèlement, de l’exploitation et des abus sexuels.

title: Country Director
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The mission of the IRC is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future.

**IRC Chad strategy**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of Darfur refugees into eastern Chad, starting with the Ouré Cassoni refugee camp. Today, the IRC supports Sudanese refugees and host communities in 14 camps and host villages in the east, and since April 2023 has expanded its response to assist refugees fleeing the conflict in Sudan. Services in the east include health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), economic recovery and development, women’s empowerment and protection. The IRC also works in Guéra province to address malnutrition and in the Lac region to respond to the Boko Haram crisis, with projects in health, nutrition, protection and response to gender-based violence. Across the country, IRC Chad combines humanitarian, nexus and development responses to help the most affected populations exercise their rights with dignity and access quality basic social services that meet their needs.

IRC Chad’s strategy focuses on three outcome areas: health (nutrition, child health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and climate-resilient WASH), safety (high-impact targeted individual assistance) and economic wellbeing (food security, basic needs, early recovery and resilience). It is underpinned by commitments to gender equality, diversity and inclusion, cash and voucher assistance, and investment in partnerships with relevant ministries and local partners.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director will provide the strategic vision and leadership for the country program with the primary focus on ensuring IRC Chad’s programs meet the expressed needs of the beneficiaries we serve. S/he is responsible for ensuring the delivery of quality programs, maintaining/expanding donor and government relations, engaging strategic local organizations, fundraising and budget management, security and operations management, and developing a motivated and professional team.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary leadership abilities who deploys strong communications and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will enjoy developing networks to build partnerships and diversify program resources. Given the operating environment, the Country Director is expected to be attentive to risk management. S/he will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design and deliver responsive, high-quality programs; ensuring efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance and focused, timely reporting; and oversight of financial management and compliance systems.

Reporting to the Regional Vice President, this position receives support from regional and headquarters staff in the areas of program quality, new business development, safety and security management, finance, operations management, and external affairs. The Country Director is additionally expected to actively participate in defining the IRC’s public advocacy positions.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Provide exemplary leadership by fostering a strong team spirit, open communication, and an inclusive and empowering work environment.
- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with: Chad Government authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private); UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups.
- Position IRC as a key partner for major international donors and seize opportunities to promote IRC’s work.
- Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Initiate and sustain strong, mutually beneficial, and authentic partnerships with Chadian organizations.
- Seek out and pursue opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Chad, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Development***

- Ensure that the country program’s strategic vision and direction are aligned with the IRC’s strategy to serve populations through responsive, high-quality, and accountable programming, and secure the necessary resources for its implementation.
- Ensure the country program’s alignment with the IRC strategy and the implementation of the strategic action plan.
- Ensure program quality through rigorous design, M&E, and accountability processes, and investments in staff development and partner capacity sharing.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure country program alignment with and involvement in meeting regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities to expand programming and ensure continuous contextual monitoring.
- Oversee the development and submission of competitive, high-quality proposals; lead partnerships with local civil society organizations in line with PEERS standards, lead negotiations with donors; and build relationships with Chad Ministries.

***Safety Security and Access Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Oversee the management of all security issues, including appropriate response to emergency situations as they arise.
- Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including trainings and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation and contingency plans up to date and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety & Security Director on safety security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.

***Staff Performance Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide constructive feedback and counsel on appropriate career paths and professional development for IRC staff.
- Oversee the management, coaching and development of all staff to build a cadre of skilled, committed and motivated personnel.
- Pursue nationalization of senior management positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Undertake regular reviews of labor laws, and salary markets in Chad for the purpose of enhancing the competitiveness of the IRC’s overall compensation package for team members.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to comply with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure appropriate support for all departments (HR, Finance, Supply Chain) and the consistent implementation of the IRC Way.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Chad country program’s financial position.
- Ensure rigorous budget monitoring of grants and discretionary funds and identify opportunities for operational optimization

***Communications***

- Model and encourage active practice of the principles of the “IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct” throughout the Chad country program.
- Maintain a healthy and empowering office environment that encourages open, honest and productive communication among IRC staff and with partner organizations.
- Maintain open communication with regional management staff, regional technical advisors, and HQ departmental staff.

**KEY REPORTING RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**The position reports to**: Regional Vice President, WACAR

**The position directly supervises:** Deputy Director Programs, the Deputy Director of Finance, the Deputy Director Field Management, the People and Culture Coordinator, Humanitarian Access and Security Coordinator, Communication and media coordinator, Safeguarding and Compliance Coordinator.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

- Graduate degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience
- At least seven years of progressively responsible international work experience, including at least three years in a leadership role at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment.
- Experience of building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization
- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in a cross-cultural setting, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and international development donors.
- Experience of managing security in a fluid environment
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations. Experience with organizational capacity strengthening and partnership building helpful.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities
- Established capacity to deal with ambiguity in stressful situations.
- French and English fluency
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Previous experience working in Chad or in the West and Central Africa region preferred.

This position is based in N’djamena and is fully accompanied with an estimated 33% of the Country Director’s time spent in other locations in Chad and the region.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**CONTEXTE**

L’International Rescue Committee (IRC) répond aux pires crises humanitaires du monde et aide les populations à survivre et à reconstruire leur vie. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC apporte des soins vitaux et une aide qui transforme des vies, notamment auprès des réfugiés contraints de fuir la guerre ou les catastrophes. Présente aujourd’hui dans plus de 40 pays, l’IRC rétablit la sécurité, la dignité et l’espoir pour des millions de personnes qui luttent pour leur survie. Sa mission est d’aider les personnes dont la vie et les moyens de subsistance ont été brisés par les conflits et les catastrophes à survivre, à se relever et à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir.

**Stratégie de l’IRC au Tchad**

L’IRC a lancé ses opérations au Tchad en 2004 pour répondre à la crise humanitaire provoquée par l’afflux de réfugiés du Darfour dans l’est du pays, en commençant par le camp de réfugiés d’Ouré Cassoni. Aujourd’hui, l’IRC soutient les réfugiés soudanais et les communautés d’accueil dans 14 camps et villages d’accueil de l’Est et, depuis avril 2023, a élargi son intervention pour venir en aide aux réfugiés fuyant le conflit au Soudan. Les services fournis dans l’Est comprennent la santé, la nutrition, l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement (EHA), le relèvement et le développement économiques, l’autonomisation des femmes et la protection. L’IRC intervient également dans la province du Guéra pour lutter contre la malnutrition, et dans la région du Lac pour répondre à la crise liée à Boko Haram, avec des projets en santé, nutrition, protection et réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG). Dans l’ensemble du pays, l’IRC Tchad combine réponses humanitaires, approches de nexus et actions de développement afin d’aider les populations les plus touchées à exercer leurs droits dans la dignité et à accéder à des services sociaux de base de qualité répondant à leurs besoins.

La stratégie de l’IRC Tchad s’articule autour de trois domaines de résultats : la santé (nutrition, santé de l’enfant, santé et droits sexuels et reproductifs, et EHA résilient face au changement climatique), la sûreté (assistance individuelle ciblée à fort impact) et le bien-être économique (sécurité alimentaire, besoins de base, relèvement précoce et résilience). Elle repose sur des engagements en faveur de l’égalité de genre, de la diversité et de l’inclusion, de l’assistance en espèces et par coupons, ainsi que sur l’investissement dans des partenariats avec les ministères concernés et les partenaires locaux.

**PÉRIMÈTRE DU POSTE**

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays assure la vision stratégique et le leadership du programme pays, avec pour priorité de garantir que les programmes de l’IRC Tchad répondent aux besoins exprimés par les bénéficiaires que nous servons. Il/elle est chargé(e) de veiller à la qualité des programmes, d’entretenir et d’élargir les relations avec les bailleurs et le gouvernement, de mobiliser des organisations locales stratégiques, d’assurer la levée de fonds et la gestion budgétaire, de superviser la sécurité et les opérations, ainsi que de constituer une équipe motivée et professionnelle.

La réussite à ce poste exige une personne dotée d’un leadership exemplaire, capable de mobiliser efficacement de solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, tant en interne qu’en externe. Le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) devra développer des réseaux afin de bâtir des partenariats et de diversifier les ressources des programmes. Compte tenu du contexte d’intervention, le/la Directeur(trice) Pays doit porter une attention particulière à la gestion des risques. Il/elle est directement responsable de la coordination d’ensemble et de l’orientation stratégique du programme pays ; assure la supervision et le coaching des cadres supérieurs qu’il/elle encadre directement ; dirige les équipes du programme pays dans l’identification, la conception et la mise en œuvre de programmes réactifs et de grande qualité ; veille à une gestion efficiente des subventions publiques et des fonds privés, axée sur les résultats, la conformité et la remise de rapports ciblés dans les délais ; et supervise les systèmes de gestion financière et de conformité.

Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays, placé(e) sous l’autorité du/de la Vice-Président(e) régional(e), bénéficie de l’appui du personnel régional et du siège en matière de qualité des programmes, de développement de nouvelles opportunités de financement, de gestion de la sûreté et de la sécurité, de finances, de gestion des opérations et d’affaires extérieures. Il/elle est en outre appelé(e) à participer activement à la définition des positions de plaidoyer public de l’IRC.

**RESPONSABILITÉS SPÉCIFIQUES**

***Leadership et Représentation***

- Faire preuve d’un leadership exemplaire en favorisant un fort esprit d’équipe, une communication ouverte et un environnement de travail inclusif et valorisant.
- Développer et entretenir des relations stratégiques avec : les autorités gouvernementales tchadiennes à différents niveaux ; les bailleurs de fonds (institutionnels, non institutionnels et privés), dont l’Union européenne ; les Nations Unies et les autres organisations internationales ; les ONG internationales et locales ; ainsi que les réseaux tels que les mécanismes de coordination des ONG internationales et les groupes de travail pertinents.
- Positionner l’IRC comme un partenaire clé des grands bailleurs de fonds internationaux et saisir les occasions de promouvoir son action.
- Acquérir et maintenir une connaissance approfondie des priorités des bailleurs et des financements qu’ils prévoient.
- Nouer et entretenir des partenariats solides, authentiques et mutuellement bénéfiques avec des organisations tchadiennes.
- Rechercher et saisir les occasions de mieux faire connaître le travail de l’IRC et de ses partenaires au Tchad, ainsi que les conditions de vie et les besoins des personnes que l’IRC s’efforce de servir.

***Orientation Stratégique, Qualité et Développement des programmes***

- Veiller à ce que la vision et l’orientation stratégiques du programme pays soient alignées sur la stratégie de l’IRC afin de servir les populations à travers des programmes réactifs, de grande qualité et redevables, et mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre.
- Veiller à l’alignement du programme pays sur la stratégie de l’IRC et à la mise en œuvre du plan d’action stratégique.
- Garantir la qualité des programmes grâce à une conception rigoureuse, à des processus de suivi-évaluation et de redevabilité, ainsi qu’à des investissements dans le développement du personnel et le renforcement des capacités des partenaires.
- Se tenir informé(e) des enjeux nationaux et régionaux qui touchent le programme pays et les partenaires, et élaborer des stratégies adaptées afin de pouvoir poursuivre la mission de l’IRC de manière appropriée en cas d’évolution du contexte.
- Veiller à ce que le programme pays soit aligné sur les objectifs régionaux et contribue à leur réalisation.
- Identifier les possibilités d’extension de la programmation et suivre en continu l’évolution du contexte.
- Superviser l’élaboration et la soumission de propositions compétitives et de grande qualité ; piloter les partenariats avec les organisations locales de la société civile conformément aux standards PEERS ; mener les négociations avec les bailleurs ; et nouer des relations avec les ministères tchadiens.

***Gestion de la sûreté, de la sécurité et de l’accès***

- Assumer la responsabilité principale de la gestion globale de la sûreté et de la sécurité du programme pays.
- Superviser la gestion de toutes les questions de sécurité, y compris la réponse adaptée aux situations d’urgence au fur et à mesure qu’elles surviennent.
- Créer et entretenir, au sein du programme pays, une culture de sensibilisation à la sûreté et à la sécurité, notamment par des formations et des séances d’information qui préparent l’ensemble du personnel à prévenir les incidents de sécurité et à y répondre.
- Tenir à jour les plans de sécurité, d’évacuation et de contingence, et les rendre accessibles au personnel du programme pays.
- Maintenir une coordination et une communication étroites avec le/la Directeur(trice) régional(e) de la sûreté et de la sécurité au sujet des préoccupations en la matière et des évolutions susceptibles de nuire au personnel ou aux opérations de l’IRC.

***Gestion de la performance et développement du personnel***

- Encadrer et accompagner les collaborateurs placés sous sa responsabilité directe, notamment en communiquant des attentes claires, en fixant des objectifs de performance, en leur donnant régulièrement et en temps utile un retour sur leur performance, et en conduisant des évaluations semestrielles documentées.
- Donner au personnel de l’IRC des retours constructifs et des conseils sur son parcours de carrière et son développement professionnel.
- Superviser la gestion, le coaching et le développement de l’ensemble du personnel afin de constituer un vivier de collaborateurs compétents, engagés et motivés.
- Poursuivre la nationalisation des postes d’encadrement supérieur.
- Promouvoir et suivre la prise en charge et le bien-être du personnel. Montrer l’exemple en matière d’équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée. Soutenir les interventions adaptées aux besoins de bien-être identifiés, tant pour le personnel national que pour le personnel international.
- Examiner régulièrement la législation du travail et les niveaux de salaire pratiqués sur le marché au Tchad afin de renforcer la compétitivité de l’ensemble du dispositif de rémunération de l’IRC pour les membres de l’équipe.

***Gestion responsable des ressources et des opérations***

- Promouvoir l’excellence opérationnelle afin d’atteindre une efficience et un rapport coût-efficacité optimaux dans l’ensemble des fonctions et opérations du programme pays.
- Superviser l’élaboration, le déploiement et l’utilisation de politiques, procédures et systèmes financiers et opérationnels conformes aux exigences de l’IRC et des bailleurs.
- Assurer un appui adéquat à l’ensemble des départements (RH, Finance, Chaîne d’approvisionnement) et veiller à la mise en œuvre cohérente de l’IRC Way.
- Assurer une supervision rapide et efficace de la situation financière du programme pays du Tchad.
- Assurer un suivi budgétaire rigoureux des subventions et des fonds discrétionnaires et identifier les possibilités d’optimisation opérationnelle.

***Communication***

- Incarner les principes de « l’IRC Way – Normes globales de conduite professionnelle », et en encourager activement l’application dans l’ensemble du programme pays du Tchad.
- Maintenir un environnement de travail sain et valorisant, qui favorise une communication ouverte, honnête et productive entre les membres du personnel de l’IRC et avec les organisations partenaires.
- Maintenir une communication ouverte avec l’équipe de direction régionale, les conseillers techniques régionaux et le personnel des départements du siège.

**PRINCIPALES RELATIONS HIÉRARCHIQUES ET FONCTIONNELLES :**

**Le poste est rattaché à** : Vice-Président(e) régional(e), WACAR

**Le poste encadre directement :**le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Programmes, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Finances, le/la Directeur(trice) adjoint(e) Gestion du terrain, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Personnes et Culture, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Acces Humanitaire et Sécurité, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Communication et médias, le/la Coordinateur(trice) Sauvegarde et Conformité

**Principaux contacts internes :** Équipe régionale WACAR ; Gestion des subventions, Opérations et Stratégie, Finance, Qualité des programmes, Plaidoyer, Département juridique, Éthique et Conformité ; autres Directeurs(trices) Pays de la région WACAR ; personnel des départements du siège, selon les besoins.

**Principaux contacts externes :** Organisations partenaires, représentants du gouvernement du pays d’accueil, agences de bailleurs publics et privés, ONG internationales et nationales, agences des Nations Unies, gouvernements étrangers.

**EXIGENCES DU POSTE**

- Diplôme de niveau master (bac+5) dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience équivalente.
- Au moins sept ans d’expérience internationale à des postes de responsabilité croissante, dont au moins trois ans à un poste de direction de niveau Directeur(trice) Pays, à la tête d’opérations multisites et multisectorielles dans un environnement d’intervention complexe.
- Expérience dans la constitution de réseaux personnels de haut niveau, ayant permis d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives à l’organisation.
- Expérience avérée de leadership et de gestion d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire en contexte interculturel, avec un mentorat et un coaching actifs.
- Expérience avérée de supervision, à un niveau approprié, d’un portefeuille de projets complexes de grande envergure financés par des bailleurs.
- Solide expérience de représentation et de levée de fonds, y compris auprès de bailleurs européens, américains et d’autres bailleurs internationaux du développement.
- Expérience en gestion de la sécurité dans un environnement instable.
- Capacité avérée à négocier et à collaborer avec des organisations partenaires. Une expérience en renforcement des capacités organisationnelles et en développement de partenariats est un atout.
- Solides compétences en supervision budgétaire et financière.
- Capacité confirmée à gérer l’ambiguïté en situation de stress.
- Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans les délais impartis, tout en produisant des résultats de grande qualité.
- Une expérience préalable au Tchad ou en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre est souhaitée.

Ce poste est basé à N’Djamena, en statut accompagné. Le/la Directeur(trice) Pays consacrera environ 33 % de son temps à des déplacements dans d’autres localités du Tchad et de la région.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

title: Oficial de Preparación de Desastres - Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia
body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Preparación de Desastres** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**:

Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Base / Líder de Equipo de Preparación para Desastres (DP), el/la oficial de DP estará directamente involucrado y velará por la ejecución diaria de las actividades de DP, especialmente en las áreas de intervención. Apoyará al Líder de Equipo en la facilitación de actividades de DP, elaboración de materiales de información, apoyo en las comunicaciones y sensibilizaciones a personas con necesidades específicas. El/la oficial de DP apoyará al líder de equipo con las actividades de Acción anticipatoria y respuesta ante desastres.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

- Apoyar al líder de equipo a identificar las necesidades de evaluación ralacionadas a DP en los desplazados internos y las comunidades de acogida en Zulia y en cualquier otra zona.
- Apoyar la identificación y selección de los beneficiarios con la ayuda de las autoridades locales y otras derivadas de los equipos de protección, Recuperación Económica y WASH. Además, contribuir que se establezcan los informes correctos de entendimiento con los proveedores de servicios relevantes/partes interesadas.
- Implementar los proyectos de DP utilizando las herramientas adecuadas para garantizar los entregables a tiempo, dentro de presupuesto y con la calidad esperada.
- Tomar en cuenta las vulnerabilidades de las comunidades con Riesgos de protección y participar en cada uno de los ciclos de proyectos relacionados con las actividades de DP.
- Participar en las capacitaciones sobre DP, Acciones Anticipatorias y también apoyar las actividades de preparación y respuesta ante emergencias de WASH.
- Contribuir a la elaboración de materiales de formación y orientación. Documentar los resultados y las lecciones aprendidas de la implementación del programa de DP y Acciones Anticipatorias, incluida la preparación y respuesta ante emergencias, para promover el intercambio de conocimientos con las contrapartes y las partes interesadas en materia de DP.
- Apoyar con el enlace con otros actores/ONG relevantes, administradores locales y líderes de desplazados internos para los esfuerzos de colaboración, entre otros.
- Asegurar que todas las partes interesadas relevantes tengan información sobre los antecedentes, el programa, los objetivos, las áreas de trabajo, la duración de los programas y las actividades en el campo de la organización.
- Completar los formularios y la documentación adecuada del sector DP para los proyectos de intervención, incluido el transporte de coordenadas GPS y el mapeo de las actividades/áreas del proyecto, entre otras.
- Contribuir con la planificación de contingencias para una posible respuesta de emergencia en materia de DP.
- Apoyar el proyecto de DP con la estrecha coordinación del Gerente de Programa y el especialista de DP.
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el equipo de DP.
- Desarrollar/apoyar con simulacros y ejercicios de preparación para garantizar la eficiencia del equipo.
- Contribuir en el desarrollo e implementación de planes integrales de preparación ante desastres.

**EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia en el campo de DP, Acciones Anticipatorias y otros.
- Excelente comprensión de la capacitación básica en programación de DP, métodos de capacitación participativa, movilizaciones comunitarias y creación de redes.
- Licenciado en Trabajo Humanitario, Licenciatura en Administración de desastres, Ciencias Políticas, Ciencias Ambientales y otras carreras afines o similares. Los estudios superiores agregan valor para el proceso de selección.
- Implementación efectiva y oportuna de todas las intervenciones descritas en el proyecto y cualquier otra actividad programática relacionada con DP.
- Experiencia laboral y conocimiento del lugar de destino local.
- Capaz de adaptarse a situaciones cambiantes según sea necesario.
- Capaz de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.

Deseable:

- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de Protección, WASH o Recuperación Económica.
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de liderar un equipo y crear buen ambiente de equipo;
- Manejo del inglés
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

  
**DRC como empleador**  
Al trabajar en DRC, te unirás a una fuerza laboral global de alrededor de 6000 empleados en 30 países. Nos enorgullecemos de nuestro:

- Profesionalismo, impacto y experiencia
- Enfoque humanitario y el trabajo que realizamos
- Propósito, significado y contribución personal
- Cultura, valores y liderazgo sólido
- Compensación justa y desarrollo continuo

title: Regional Coordinator, Maestral MENA Office
body:
**About Maestral International**

Maestral International, LLC is a globally recognized consulting firm dedicated to strengthening systems that protect, support, and empower vulnerable children and youth. We work across more than 100 countries with multilateral, bilateral, governmental, philanthropic, and NGO partners. Our technical work spans child protection systems strengthening, care reform, social service workforce development, public finance for children, and child and adolescent wellbeing.

Grounded in evidence and guided by a commitment to children’s rights, Maestral helps clients and partners translate policy into practice, strengthen national systems, and build sustainable, responsive services for children and families. Learn more at [www.maestral.org](http://www.maestral.org)

Maestral established its new MENA regional office in Amman, Jordan, in 2026 to expand its support to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Building on previous and ongoing work in the region, Maestral has developed partnerships across MENA countries as well as through multi-country regional programmes. This office coordinates regional partnerships, supports the management and development of ongoing and future projects, and contributes to global initiatives. As a small office within a small global organization, all team members are expected to collaborate across functions and contribute to both regional and global work. The MENA office also serves as a regional hub, connecting Maestral’s global expertise with locally grounded knowledge, partnerships, and opportunities across the region.

**Position Description**

The Regional Coordinator, MENA, ensures the smooth functioning of the regional office and provides essential support to business development, project coordination, budgeting, financial processes, and administrative operations.

This role requires a high level of coordination between Maestral’s International team and the MENA regional team to ensure that opportunities are effectively identified, pursued, and coordinated, and that projects are aligned and implemented smoothly across global and regional teams.

The Regional Coordinator will initially support both global and MENA business development, operations, and project delivery, while gaining structured training in Maestral’s systems and processes as the regional project portfolio develops. As the MENA office grows, the responsibilities will transition toward primarily MENA-focused projects, operations, and business development support.

This position is a core operational and program support position in a small, dynamic office that requires initiative, organization, collaboration, and a willingness to support multiple functions.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Business Development***

The Regional Coordinator will work closely with the MENA Regional Director and Maestral’s HQ team to support business development across both global and MENA portfolios. The role will provide broader BD support to Maestral HQ, with responsibilities gradually shifting toward primarily MENA-focused business development as the regional portfolio grows.

- Assists the MENA Regional Director in the development, revision and refinement of the MENA business strategy, and ensuring alignment with Maestral’s overall strategy and priorities.
- Conducts market research to identify opportunities in both global and MENA portfolios.
- Supports preparation of Expressions of Interest, proposal packages, CVs, partner documents, and submission materials.
- Maintains opportunity, partner, and proposal tracking systems for both global and MENA pipelines.
- Assists with coordinating input from consultants and partners for technical proposals.
- Provides BD support across the organization during the office’s early phase, scaling back global BD responsibilities as the MENA portfolio expands.
- Supports the development and strengthening of existing strategic partnerships with a diverse range of partners across the MENA region.

***Project Support and Monitoring (Primarily MENA)***

- Maintains project timelines, workplans, and calendars, and supports monitoring progress against agreed deliverables, milestones, and deadlines.
- Oversees project operations and administration; including travel and compliance, keeps financial records, oversees the hiring of additional project support roles (i.e., translators, copy editors, etc.)
- Develops and processes project contracts (client and team) and amendments
- Supports implementation of compliance, safety, security, and safeguarding processes for MENA-based projects, ensuring documentation is complete and aligned with organizational standards.
- Coordinate the collection of end-of-project feedback from clients and team members and maintain summaries for organizational learning.

***Financial Management & Budgeting***

- Supports development and monitoring of project budgets for MENA-based work.
- Processes consultant invoices, vendor payments, and project expenses in collaboration with an external accounting firm.
- Maintains accurate financial records and documentation in accordance with donor and organizational requirements.
- Tracks budget performance and expenditure across MENA-based projects.

***Operations & Office Administration***

- Manages daily operational needs of the MENA office, including procurement, vendor coordination, document management, onboarding, and office logistics.
- Maintains organized systems for files, data, and documentation to support smooth office operations.
- Supports compliance processes in collaboration with HQ Operations & Compliance, including safety, security, legal and safeguarding documentation.
- Supports the MENA Regional Director and HQ team in strengthening Maestral’s visibility, focused MENA communication materials and events, and profiles across the region.

***Cross-Functional Global Support***

- Supports global BD, operational tasks, and project administration as needed to ensure consistency across the organization.
- Participates in team meetings, working groups, and/or initiatives that strengthen Maestral’s global systems.

**Key Relationships**

*Internal*

- Reports to the Regional Director, MENA.

- Supports consultants and project teams across global and regional portfolios.

*External*

- Works closely with Maestral’s regional accounting firm.
- Interacts with vendors, partners, consultants, and service providers supporting regional operations.
