**Requirements**

*Education:*

Master's degree in international development, Public Administration, Business, Social Sciences, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience of at least 15 years.

*Experience:*

- Experience working in the MENA region, humanitarian and development contexts.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining partnerships with diverse stakeholders, with experience supporting business development, opportunity identification, and proposal development.
- 10+ years of experience in project coordination, program support, business development, financial tracking, or office administration.
- Experience managing budgets, invoices, and financial documentation.
- Familiarity with international development, child protection, social policy, or related sectors preferred.

*Skills and Competencies:*

- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Arabic and English.
- Strong budgeting and financial tracking ability, with proficiency in Excel.
- Ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Teams, SharePoint, Planner, Excel, Word).
- Ability to rapidly learn new systems and apply consistent processes.
- Professional judgment, discretion, and problem-solving skills.

*Work Style and Values:*

- Proactive and self-directed; able to work independently in a small, start-up office environment.
- Collaborative team member, comfortable supporting multiple workstreams.
- Commitment to integrity, equity, and child safeguarding principles.
- Flexibility and adaptability in a shifting organizational environment.

*Other Requirements:*

- Must be legally eligible to work in Jordan.
- Must sign and uphold Maestral’s Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy Package.
- Ability to travel regionally and internationally, as required.

*\*This role may require occasional regional travel, as well as some global travel to attend Maestral Board Meetings and/or convenings.*

title: Grants, Partnerships and Communication Coordinator
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

***Fluency in both English & Spanish required***.

***Funding until September 30, 2027, potential to extend***.

**BACKGROUND**

Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.

In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.

The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

**Purpose of the role:** IRC Colombia and Venezuela is seeking an experienced business development, grants, and partnerships professional for the role of Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator. This role is responsible for leading resource mobilization and the timely production of high-quality funding proposals, modification requests and donor reports; playing a lead role in the full award management cycle, including compliance; facilitating partnership development and management processes; leading the communications strategy that positions the IRC’s work with donors, partners and the public and protects the organization’s reputation; and coordinating grants management-related capacity building efforts among IRC staff and partners. The Grants, and Partnerships Coordinator ensures the quality of and efficient processes for proposal development and grants management, and manages the delivery of the IRC’s partnership ambitions while supporting program coordinators and country leadership to ensure that IRC Colombia and Venezuela lives up to the partnership principles of responsibility, results-oriented approaches, equality, transparency, and complementarity.

The postholder will need to work under tight deadlines and deal with competing and changing priorities. The postholder will need to gather inputs by influencing other functions and roles while submitting quality and timely deliverables, will work with diverse country, region and headquarters-based teams, and will need to ensure adherence to organizational and donor compliance requirements. The position will be based in Bogota with frequent visits to field sites in Colombia and Venezuela.

**Scope and authority:** The Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator will lead a team of 15 members (both direct and indirect) divided in three sub-teams: grants, partnerships, and communications. The postholder will line manage 6 direct reports.

**Key Accountabilities & responsibilities:**

***Business Development and Resource Mobilization:***

- Lead the development and annual update of a resource mobilization strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country Strategy Action Plan, with clear targets by donor, sector and geography.
- Manage the funding pipeline: investigate and track funding opportunities, maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker, and regularly report on its status to country leadership.
- Lead the Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, assessing strategic fit, competitiveness, implementation capacity, risks, cost recovery and compliance requirements, and facilitate timely decisions with country leadership.
- Drive donor diversification and positioning beyond traditional institutional donors, including pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund), multilateral agencies and development banks, the private sector and foundations, and funding dedicated to localization and to partnerships with local organizations.
- Lead program design workshops for new business development opportunities with relevant IRC staff, and partners’ staff where applicable.
- Develop, lead, and track proposal development processes, including consortium proposals, directly coordinating and managing the development of proposals and concept notes in collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders; write sections of proposals and conduct final reviews, editing, and polishing of proposal documents for accuracy and quality control.
- Assist in compiling and editing proposal budgets and ensure communication and coordination between all departments (finance, programs, and operations) in drafting of budgets, bringing a strategic and competitive lens to the process.

***Grants/Sub-Grants Management:***

- Ensure that IRC awards and sub-awards in Colombia and Venezuela are well-administered and implemented in compliance with the relevant donor regulations and IRC procedures throughout the full award cycle.
- Lead award start-up, including grant summaries and kick-off meetings (pre-award and opening meetings) with programs, finance, operations and partners, so that all teams understand donor requirements from the outset.
- Lead the review and negotiation of grant and sub-grant agreements, in coordination with the Awards Management Unit, finance and other relevant departments.
- Coordinate award modifications, including cost and no-cost extensions, budget realignments and changes in scope, ensuring timely submission and donor approval.
- Take the lead on internal and external reporting in coordination with programs, MEAL, and finance, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and IRC requirements. Maintain close collaboration with all relevant departments in preparation of donor reports.
- Maintain award tracking systems, including the grants tracker, reporting and deadline calendars and award dashboards, ensuring that information is accurate and available to budget holders and senior management.
- Supervise the GPU in the coordination and facilitation of project cycle meetings.
- Lead award close-out processes, ensuring that final reports, financial reconciliation, asset disposition and documentation are completed on time.
- Coordinate the preparation for and follow-up of donor audits, verifications and monitoring visits, including the implementation of their recommendations.
- Play a significant role in efforts to strengthen and maintain country program project management capacities.
- Ensure that sub-grantees are being monitored for donor compliance and progress against objectives, and that key compliance monitoring information and learning are documented.
- Assist program technical leads, operations staff, and partners with understanding the reporting and other compliance requirements on their grants and sub-grants.
- Proactively identify compliance risks throughout the portfolio and advise programs, operations, finance and senior management on necessary actions.

***Partnerships Management:***

- Play a lead role in stakeholder analysis and potential partner mapping and vetting.
- Working closely with other senior staff, play a lead role in identifying, liaising on, and negotiating teaming arrangements with potential partners; collaborate with other departments as needed to verify and issue various types of partnership agreements.
- Ensure and coordinate adherence to IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) in the selection and management of IRC Colombia and Venezuela’s partnerships.
- Co-lead the review of the performance of different partnerships, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Support country leadership in promoting an enabling environment for effective work in partnership.
- Provide a quarterly Partnership Management Report to the CD, incorporating input from technical coordinators and operational leads as appropriate.

***Staff management and capacity building***

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of donor policies, regulations, and procedures and build this knowledge among grants team members.
- Build grant management capacity of field staff, and provide supportive supervision in report writing, budget management, indicator tracking, IRC-specific tools, and other topics as/if needed.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Maintain documentation of institutional knowledge and program activities in coordination with relevant sector coordinators and department leads.

***Communications***

- **Communications strategy:** Lead the development and implementation of a communications strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country strategy, resource mobilization priorities and IRC regional and global communications.
- **Brand management and visibility:** Ensure consistent and appropriate use of the IRC brand across materials, events, field sites and partner activities; provide advice on donor visibility requirements and proactively engage with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility.
- **Creation of communication materials:** Lead Colombia and Venezuela’s efforts in designing, writing and editing key communication materials (factsheets, capacity statements, stories from the field, digital content or special reports on IRC’s activities) in coordination with DDPs, program leads, and sector and field coordinators.
- **Crisis communications and reputational risk:** Develop and maintain protocols for crisis communications and reputational risk management, and advise the CD and senior management on sensitive issues, including security, data protection and the political context in Colombia and Venezuela.
- **Internal communications:** Promote clear and timely internal communication across offices and teams in Colombia and Venezuela, so that staff are informed about the country program’s priorities, results and key decisions.
- **Media:** Support media and communications activities in coordination with IRC regional and global communications teams, ensuring the safety, dignity and informed consent of clients.
- **Advocacy:** Support the CD and DDPs as needed.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Country Director, Colombia and Venezuela

**Position directly supervises:** Grants, Partnerships and Communications Unit staff

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Venezuela Country Manager and Venezuela senior management team, with whom the postholder works closely on the Venezuela portfolio; Colombia/Venezuela Deputy Directors of Programs and leads of programs, Finance and Operations, Budget Officers/Managers, HR Lead, Access & Security Department; MEAL Unit; Awards Management Unit (Regional), regional partnerships advisor, regional and global communications teams, and Technical Advisors.

**External:** Donors and pooled fund managers, consortium partners, local partner organizations, UN agencies and humanitarian coordination mechanisms, other NGO counterparts and media, as needed and indicated by Country Director, Country Manager or Deputy Director of Programs.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline, Master’s degree desired.
- At least five years international work experience in humanitarian and development programs; experience in a similar position/role is desired.
- Demonstrated, successful experience in program design and writing proposals for public and private donors.
- Solid knowledge of donor rules and regulations, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, UN agencies and OCHA-managed pooled funds; knowledge of other European, multilateral and private donor requirements is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience managing the full award cycle, including compliance, modifications, audits and close-out, and in managing partnerships with local organizations.
- Experience in communications, brand management or external relations in a humanitarian or development organization is desirable.
- Demonstrable understanding of project planning and management cycles.
- Highly organized, close attention to detail, and ability to effectively prioritize tasks in a fluid environment.
- Demonstrable high-level performance management and team-working skills, and well developed negotiation skills.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence and represent the organization with external organizations and stakeholders.
- Effective people- and program-management skills in acute emergency contexts: can train and lead staff productively under stressful circumstances.
- Flexible, focused and reliable, with the ability to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures in an environment of changing demands.
- Experience in the region is an asset; knowledge of the Colombian and Venezuelan contexts is strongly desired.
- Digital literacy and strong computer skills: MS Word, Excel & email applications required.

**Language Preference**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish, with high quality copywriting and editing skills in both languages.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate around: 10,051,500 COP/monthly). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Oficial de Ayuda Legal - Santa bárbara del Zulia
body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Ayuda Legal** altamente calificado con sede en **Santa Bárbara, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**:

El objetivo principal del Oficial de Ayuda Legal es implementar las actividades legales en el marco del programa de Protección de DRC. Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección implementará las actividades de ayuda legal y es responsable de brindar asesoría legal y gestión de casos para restablecer los derechos de refugiados, migrantes y retornados en materia civil, administrativa y constitucional. Es responsable para la implementación de sesiones informativas sobre temas legales en estrecha colaboración con el equipo de protección.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Principales Responsabilidades**

Este rol tiene un enfoque de área y garantiza el cumplimiento de los objetivos de asistencia/asesoría legal bajo los procedimientos y las pautas de DRC dentro del área. El rol contribuye al desempeño de los planes de acción y proporciona apoyo y orientación técnica para operaciones legales en el terreno.

- Trabajar en estrecha cooperación con el equipo de protección de DRC y responder a las necesidades legales documentadas;
- Implementar las actividades de asesoría y servicios legales conforme a los objetivos meta de los proyectos;
- Elaborar documentos de asesoría y servicios legales, determinando la mejor estrategia para los casos de beneficiarios bajo la supervisión del Gerente de Protección;
- Implementar asesoría y servicios legales en las zonas de intervención seleccionadas por el programa según el plan mensual establecido;
- Planear y proporcionar citas individuales para el asesoramiento jurídico a las personas de interés, según sea necesario.
- Recopilar información de los beneficiarios gestionando archivos de manera confidencial y completa; trasferir diariamente las informaciones relevantes en la base de datos legales para permitir el seguimiento de los casos legales identificados o remitidos.
- Proporcionar asesoramiento individual en temas de protección incluyendo protección internacional, reunificación familiar, registro civil y nacionalidad, afiliación en el sistema de seguridad social, acceso a salud, educación y vivienda y otros casos de derecho civil y administrativo que requieran asistencia jurídica;
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario;
- Apoyar a la Gerencia de Protección en la elaboración de estrategias y procedimientos estándares para facilitar la implementación de las actividades legales.
- Mantener buenas relaciones con las entidades e instituciones públicas pertinentes para que la coordinación y la articulación sea fortalecida.
- Proporcionar información para informes semanales según sea requerido.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas

**Responsabilidades sectoriales**:

- Incidencia sobre los derechos de las personas de interés en el contexto de su desplazamiento, asesoría legal y gestión de casos para restablecer los derechos de refugiados, migrantes y retornados en materia civil, constitucional y administrativa.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades legales en terreno.
- Abordar las necesidades de asesoría y servicios legales de los beneficiarios.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 2-3 años de experiencia relevante como abogado/a.
- Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos.
- Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal, seguimiento de casos y litigio.
- Optimas habilidades de escritura informes.
- Optimas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Optimas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.
- Experiencia con los procedimientos y directrices estándar.
- Alta ética profesional.

**Nivel educativo:**

- Pregrado en Derecho, con experiencia en derecho constitucional/derecho de los refugiados/derechos humanos. Experiencia demostrable en definición de estrategia legal, seguimiento de casos y litigio

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

title: Officer, Planned Giving - South
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee's (IRC) External Relations (ER) department enables the IRC to respond to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Within ER, the Philanthropy team leads on the organization’s work with High-Net-Worth Individuals and planned giving donors.

**Job Overview**:

The Officer, Planned Giving, will work with donors and prospects in an assigned geography across the Southern U.S. to support an increased number of legacy gift commitments and a growing and engaged legacy society. They will support the securing and sustaining of planned gifts by working directly with prospects and donors and Philanthropy colleagues to help ensure a healthy financial future for our humanitarian work. This may entail following up on new leads; soliciting donors for planned gifts; building positive relationships to steward legacy donors; carrying out cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies, set with the Senior Director, to connect with and inspire planned giving donors and prospects; supporting colleagues on collaborations; and reporting results of efforts.

The Officer will be expected to understand the needs of older donors and prospects, communicate and connect superbly with colleagues and supporters, use knowledge of various gift planning instruments to assist colleagues and donors, continue to learn about IRC programs, and maintain accurate donor records to support the IRC’s donor relationships and prospecting with high wealth individuals and families.

Additionally, the Officer will be expected to work directly with other development officers, ER colleagues, and local area leadership to increase awareness about planned giving, support education opportunities, and support planned giving conversations and asks for appropriate donors across Major and Principal Giving portfolios.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Manage an assigned portfolio of planned gift prospects and donors.
- Provide timely follow-up to new marketing leads to educate prospects, creating new planned gifts for the IRC.
- Implement meaningful engagement opportunities for planned giving donors and prospects, in line with the team’s stewardship plan, to deepen their understanding of the mission and the benefits of legacy giving and gifts of complex assets.
- Execute regional donor trips, with travel plans approved by manager, maximizing geographic clusters of donors and prospects
- Focus on significant interactions during in person visits, events, and digital and mail communications.
- Support engagement with the IRC legacy society (Changemakers) to recognize and retain committed donors, including an annual in-person recognition event in NYC and other regional market events.
- Partner with Major Gifts and Principal Gifts colleagues on planned gift conversations for appropriate prospects within their portfolios, with strategy set by senior staff
- Contribute to internal education across ER teams and IRC regional office leadership (RAI) on planned giving’s role and process with the organization, using materials developed by the team
- Successfully meet individual goals for significant interactions, prospect conversions, lead identification, and outright giving, in alignment with overall team goals.
- Review donor file data (Salesforce) to flag prospects and bring portfolio balance recommendations to manager
- Timely and accurately input opportunity data into Salesforce to drive pipeline activity, report on progress towards goals, and find areas of improvement.
- Promote and practice inclusive behavior and demonstrate a willingness to learn about the IRC’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion.

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience:**

- 3-5 years of experience working with individual donors, preferably in major gifts, annual giving, or planned giving.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of or familiarity with planned giving vehicles and benefits preferred;
- Ability to communicate effectively with older donors about the IRC’s mission and planning tools;
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines, in consultation with manager;
- Effective collaboration with colleagues at all levels across the organization;
- Proficient with Microsoft Office; experience with CRM databases such as Salesforce or Raiser’s Edge preferred;
- Outstanding attention to detail and commitment to timeframes;
- Commitment to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor information;
- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization.
- Driver’s license and ability to travel up to 25% of the time, including overnight travel, is required.

**Working Environment:** This role is remote and ability to travel to see donors and prospects required. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $77,600-$93,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Director of Finance
body:
PATHWAYS INTERNATIONAL

**Director of Finance**

**About us – what do we do?**

At a time of unprecedented forced displacement and system disruption, we are reforming the global system of safe and legal routes to protection. Our world-class team works closely with leaders and innovators from across sectors in over 20 countries. Together we design, launch, and expand safe and legal routes for displaced people. Together we pilot bold new ideas aimed at making the entire global system of safe and legal routes stronger and more sustainable.

**How we do it**

- We build and lead powerful partnerships and networks.
- We provide trusted advice.
- We accelerate operational delivery.
- We generate and share insights.
- We inspire change.

**About the role – what will you do?**

The Director of Finance manages Pathways International’s day-to-day finance operations across our entities, making sure they are accurate, compliant and on time. Over time, the role will also oversee our HR and IT operations.

This is a senior role in a small team, and a hands-on one. You’ll set direction and supervise, but you’ll also do the work yourself when needed, whether that’s reconciling an account, posting journal entries, running a payroll cycle or rebuilding a grant report. We’re looking for someone who genuinely enjoys both.

The role is designed to expand in time. In the first months you’ll learn our entities, funders and systems alongside the CFO, then take ownership of core processes step by step. As Pathways International evolves, the scope of the role will evolve with it.

**Key responsibilities**

- **Financial operations:** Lead the monthly close, reconciliations and consolidated reporting across our entities and currencies, and keep the general ledger accurate and well-structured.
- **Grant finance:** Partner with programme teams on grant budgets, monitor spending, and prepare funder financial reports.
- **Payroll and compliance:** Oversee payroll and statutory compliance across multiple jurisdictions, including provider and employer-of-record relationships.
- **Audit and tax:** Manage the statutory, tax and audit calendar, and act as day-to-day contact for external auditors.
- **Planning and reporting:** Contribute to budgets and forecasts, and prepare financial information for leadership and Boards.
- **Controls and systems:** Maintain strong internal controls and documented procedures, and keep improving our systems and processes.
- **Administration:** Over time, oversee HR operations and IT, coordinating specialist support, contract and onboarding processes, and systems and access across the organization.
- **Team:** Supervise and develop a small finance and administration team.

**About you – who are we looking for?**

You are a highly organized, detail-oriented finance professional who enjoys both leading and rolling up your sleeves to do the work. You are comfortable building and running processes with limited direction. You are able to work across a varied and evolving portfolio of entities, currencies and jurisdictions. You are comfortable in a fast-paced environment with recurring deadlines, while keeping sensitive financial and personnel information fully confidential. You also bring a high degree of professionalism, discretion, sound judgement and responsibility.

- You have a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in accounting, finance, business administration or a related field.
- A professional accounting designation (e.g. CPA or equivalent).
- You have at least eight years of relevant work experience, including senior responsibility for the month-end close, financial reporting and audit. Experience in a non-profit or grant-funded organization is a strong asset.
- You have a strong command of accounting fundamentals, including consolidation, multi-currency transactions and fund or grant accounting.
- You have experience managing restricted funding: budgets, spending oversight and financial reporting to institutional and private funders.
- You have a working knowledge of payroll, tax and statutory compliance in more than one country. Experience with employer-of-record providers or international payroll is an asset.
- You are hands-on and comfortable working directly in the books, the payroll and the spreadsheets, with strong attention to detail.
- You have a sound understanding of internal controls, segregation of duties and documentation, and you build processes that others can follow.
- You have experience supervising and developing staff.
- You learn new entities, systems and regulatory environments quickly, and you are comfortable in a role whose scope will grow and change over time.
- You have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and can explain financial information clearly to non-finance colleagues, leadership and Boards. Proficiency in other languages, in particular Spanish, Italian, or Portuguese, is an asset.
- You have excellent interpersonal skills and have experience collaborating with people from different backgrounds, countries, cultures and languages.
- You are proficient with cloud accounting systems (e.g. QuickBooks Online) and advanced Excel, and comfortable using Zoom, MS Teams and SharePoint. You are open to using new tools, including AI, to improve how the team works.

**Location:** This is a full-time remote position within the range of Eastern Time (ET) to Central European Time (CET). The candidate must be available for flexible working hours, including meetings in CET and ET.

title: Head of IT Operations - HQ
body:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**Job Summary**

As Head of IT Operations, you’ll own INSO’s IT infrastructure and make sure it is secure, reliable, and efficient. You’ll report to the Director of Operations and lead the IT team, set its goals, and hold it to high standards. You’ll also lead the secure and responsible use of AI and automation across INSO’s operations. The technology you run helps keep humanitarian workers safe in some of the world’s most difficult environments.

**Major Responsibilities**

*Strategy and policy*

- Set and maintain INSO’s IT vision, strategy and roadmap, aligned with organisational goals and operational needs
- Write and maintain IT policies and standards that comply with GDPR, the EU AI Act and ISO/IEC 27001
- Advise HQ departments, projects and Country Offices on infrastructure, systems and technology, including evaluating and integrating new software
- Agree a clear IT ownership and governance model with HQ Directors. IT is accountable for identity and access management, security standards, licensing, technical integration and architecture
- Manage software licences across HQ and Country Offices for compliance, cost and fit
- Review existing systems to keep them secure, resilient and fit for purpose
- Assess emerging technologies, including AI, for their operational, security, compliance and financial impact, and recommend what to adopt
- Manage strategic relationships with global technology vendors and partners to get the best service, value and innovation

*AI in IT infrastructure and support systems*

- Contribute to INSO’s AI strategy and lead its implementation within IT operations
- Own the AI acceptable use and security policy (approved tools, data handling, access and compliance), developed with DTL
- Lead AI integration into infrastructure and support systems such as Microsoft 365, finance, HR and IT service management
- Advise on and review the infrastructure, security and compliance (GDPR, ISO/IEC 27001) side of AI features in INSO-developed software and programme platforms, which DTL owns and leads
- Identify and manage AI and automation projects in support processes (finance, HR, logistics and administration) across HQ and Country Offices, working with system owners and referring programme-related opportunities to DTL
- Lead staff training on the safe use of INSO-approved AI tools and the AI policy, coordinating with DTL on training for the AI solutions it builds for programmes
- Track and report on the adoption, cost and benefits of AI tools to inform reviews of the AI strategy

*IT risk*

- Identify, assess and reduce risks to the security, resilience and availability of INSO’s IT
- Keep the IT and information security entries in the INSO Risk Register up to date, including mitigation measures, risk owners and residual risk
- Lead IT risk management, including data classification and protection, data loss prevention, incident response, business continuity and disaster recovery, cybersecurity awareness
- Monitor new threats and regulations, and put the right controls in place
- Build and test a disaster recovery framework (policies, plans, testing and procedures) so critical systems can be restored quickly
- Report regularly on risk exposure, how well controls are working and significant security incidents

*Leadership*

- Lead, manage and mentor the IT team, building a culture of collaboration, accountability and growth
- Plan, prioritise and delegate work so projects and support are delivered on time
- Own the IT budget, making sure resources are used well and give value for money
- Take on other duties as needed

**Requirements**

*Essential*

- At least 8 years of progressive IT management experience, including in humanitarian or NGO settings.
- Proven experience of managing IT, delivering projects together with service and supplier management.
- Experience administering Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, and Azure environments.
- Experience deploying, managing, and governing AI tools (e.g. Microsoft 365 Copilot) and business process automation solutions.
- Demonstrated ability to analyse information critically, evaluate risks and opportunities, develop effective solutions, and manage multiple priorities while consistently meeting deadlines.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field.

*Desirable*

- Solid project management skills related to organisational development projects and international, cross-functional, and integrated teams with a proven history of delivering results.
- Working knowledge of information security and data protection frameworks, such as ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR and the EU AI Act.
- Experience of working within a matrix organisation structure.
- Working knowledge of either French, Arabic, Dutch, or Spanish.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

This is a full-time, fixed-term (renewable) position based in The Hague, Netherlands, with office presence required. The full-time package, based on 40 hours a week, is €6700 gross per month, 8% vacation pay, and 2.5 days of annual leave per month. INSO provides Basic Premium ONVZ health insurance for the staff member and dependents. The position is eligible for a Highly Skilled Migrant visa and relocation. **Be aware that INSO’s employment terms do not include transport and pension benefits.** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

title: Technicien.ne data / BI
body:
**Date de début de contrat :** 01/02/2027

**Type de contrat** : Contrat à durée déterminée jusqu’au 30/09/2027

**Localisation** : Montreuil (93) / France (télétravail possible en France métropolitaine)

**QUI SOMMES-NOUS ET QUE FAISONS-NOUS…**

La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi connue sous l’appellation « hulo », est la première coopérative humanitaire fondée en juin 2021. Dirigée par des organisations humanitaires et intégrant de nouveaux membres régulièrement, hulo a pour objectif d'améliorer l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant la collaboration et la mise en place de projets communs dans ses pays d’intervention. Chez hulo nous sommes convaincus que le partage et la mise en commun de ressources et d’expertises entre organisations contribue à augmenter la performance de la logistique humanitaire et de la chaine d’approvisionnement

Notre action s’appuie sur une approche collaborative et participative, l’intelligence collective et l’animation d’une communauté de pratiques. Toutes nos activités sont structurées autour d’un objectif commun, impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes autonomes et interdépendantes, qui coopèrent de manière horizontale. Le pilotage y est distribué, fondée sur la concertation, la co-responsabilité et l’engagement volontaire.

Dans nos 7 pays d’intervention répartis dans 3 régions nous mettons en place des initiatives mutualisées dans les domaines des achats, des ressources humaines et de l’environnement. En support aux organisations humanitaires nous coordonnons des initiatives de transport international humanitaire mutualisées à destination des crises humanitaires les plus graves. Enfin nous développons constamment des solutions digitales au service de la communauté humanitaire.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez consultez le rapport annuel 2026 en cliquant sur le lien [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE**

Sous la supervision directe du Data Scientist, le/la technicien.ne data / BI contribuera à la gestion, la visualisation, l’analyse, et la protection des données recueillies au sein de l’organisation. Il/elle apportera un support clé dans la création et la maintenance des bases de données, des rapports BI, ainsi que dans la préparation des rapports d'analyse. Il/elle veillera à ce que les données soient traitées en conformité avec les règlements de protection des données et les normes internes de l'organisation.

**MISSIONS PRINCIPALES**

**\#1 : Collecte et traitement des données**

- Assister la collecte et le nettoyage des données provenant des différentes équipes et partenaires.
- Contribuer à la conception et à la mise en place d'outils de collecte de données tels que des questionnaires, des formulaires en ligne, ou des tableurs structurés.
- Participer à des exercices de vérification de la qualité des données pour identifier et traiter toute anomalie.

**\#2 : Gestion des bases de données**

- Assurer la création et la documentation des modèles de bases de données.
- Maintenir à jour les bases de données de l'organisation, et mettre en place un suivi régulier de la qualité des bases de données.
- Gérer la sécurité et les accès des bases de données.

**\#3 : Protection des données et conformité**

- Veiller au respect des règles de protection des données en vigueur (RGPD, CNIL, etc.).
- S'assurer que les processus de collecte et de stockage des données sont conformes aux politiques internes et aux exigences des bailleurs.
- Assurer la gouvernance, la sécurité et la gestion des accès

**\#4 : Visualisation des données**

- Créer et améliorer les rapports BI sur les plans fonctionnel, visuel et technique
- Améliorer les performances et la fiabilité des rapports BI lorsque cela est nécessaire
- Documenter les rapports finalisés et les principaux choix techniques.
- Appuyer le processus de développement, de validation et de publication des rapports.
- Assurer la gestion des versions et de suivi des modifications
- Identifier et prototyper des usages pertinents de Microsoft Power Platform pour automatiser certaines tâches ou étapes du processus BI

**\#5 : Analyse des données**

- Analyser les données collectées et fournir des rapports synthétiques à l'équipe.
- Identifier des tendances, des écarts ou des points d’amélioration à partir des données analysées.

**\#6 : Support opérationnel et collaboration**

- Appuyer la gestion de la plateforme analytique.
- Apporter un support ponctuel aux équipes dans la gestion de leurs données et besoins analytiques.
- Collaborer avec les autres départements pour répondre à leurs besoins en matière de données.
- Assurer l’accompagnement et formation des utilisateurs sur la gestion data / BI
- Participer aux formations organisées par l'organisation pour développer ses compétences techniques.

**VOTRE PROFIL**

**Expérience et formation :**

- Formation niveau Bac+5 en Data Engineering, Data Analysis et/ou Data Visualisation.
- Une première expérience professionnelle (stage, alternance, bénévolat) dans le secteur humanitaire ou à forte composante internationale est appréciée.

**Compétences Techniques et transversales :**

- Collecte et traitement des données
- Analyse de données
- Construction de Rapports Power BI
- Management de bases de données
- Connaissance des principes de protection des données
- Capacité à interpréter et à présenter des résultats analytiques
- Capacité à travailler avec différentes équipes
- Maitrise obligatoire de Power BI, SQL, Excel Avancé, Python
- Maitrise de Spark, MS Fabric, Azure est un plus
- Anglais indispensable, Espagnol est un plus

**HULO VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES :**

Un poste salarié temps plein

title: Responsable administratif du bureau (GS-7)
body:
Le bureau du représentant résident du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) en Côte d’Ivoire souhaite recruter un(e) responsable administratif du bureau hautement qualifié(e) pour rejoindre son équipe, de préférence dans le courant du mois d’avril 2027.

Le poste est proposé dans le cadre d’un contrat local d’un an, avec possibilité de renouvellement pour des périodes successives pouvant aller jusqu’à trois ans, sous réserve du maintien des besoins et de performances satisfaisantes.

Pour que leur candidature soit prise en considération, les candidats doivent être ressortissants ou résidents de Côte d’Ivoire, ou être en mesure d’obtenir par leurs propres moyens un permis de travail valide avant leur prise de fonctions au FMI. Un justificatif de nationalité, de résidence et/ou d’autorisation de travail sera exigé avant la prise de fonctions. Le FMI ne prendra pas en charge les démarches d’obtention d’un permis de travail et n’apportera aucune assistance à cet égard.

**Résumé du poste**  
Le responsable administratif du bureau assume seul la responsabilité de l’organisation, de la gestion et de la prestation de l’ensemble des services d’appui du bureau, et dispose de l’autorité nécessaire à cet effet. Il prend en charge tous les aspects des tâches qui lui sont confiées, en agissant de manière autonome et professionnelle et en favorisant la collaboration, la qualité du travail et le développement de l’équipe. Il adopte une approche stratégique et contribue activement à la mise en oeuvre du programme du chef de bureau. Le responsable administratif du bureau rend compte au chef de bureau. Sous la supervision du chef de bureau, la personne retenue contribuera à la réalisation du programme de travail du bureau en prenant en charge la gestion des flux de travail, de la charge de travail et des systèmes d’appui de la mission résidente. Elle sera en contact avec les employés à tous les niveaux du bureau, les missions du FMI en visite, les hauts responsables internes et externes, les donateurs, la société civile, les milieux universitaires, le secteur privé et les autres missions résidentes.

**Fonctions et responsabilités**  
Dans les limites des pouvoirs qui lui sont délégués, le responsable administratif du bureau exerce les fonctions et responsabilités suivantes :

- Fournit un appui administratif et exécutif complet au chef de bureau.
- Oriente et conseille les employés du bureau sur les questions administratives et ponctuelles.
- Veille au bon fonctionnement des activités et systèmes de fonction support du bureau. Gère et encadre les employés de fonction support du bureau.
- Fait office de point focal pour la sécurité et assume la responsabilité de toutes les questions de sécurité et de sûreté des employés.
- Supervise et gère la préparation et la coordination de tous les aspects logistiques liés aux déplacements nationaux et internationaux, aux conférences, aux ateliers, aux réunions d’examen de documents, etc. Cela comprend l’interprétation des règles et règlements applicables à toutes les formes de déplacement ainsi que l’appui logistique aux missions en visite, notamment les programmes des missions, l’organisation des déplacements et la mobilisation des chauffeurs.
- Assume la responsabilité principale de la coordination des technologies du bureau et de leur utilisation ; identifie un large éventail de problèmes technologiques et contribue à leur résolution (matériel, logiciels et communications). Facilite l’échange d’informations informatiques au sein du bureau.
- Aide les employés du bureau à examiner régulièrement et à recueillir les informations provenant de journaux, de communiqués de presse, de bulletins d’information, de services de revue de presse et de sources médiatiques concernant le FMI, ses activités ou ses politiques.
- Établit et entretient un réseau de contacts efficace avec les responsables gouvernementaux, les donateurs, la société civile, les milieux universitaires, le secteur privé, le siège et les autres missions résidentes. Collabore avec les employés du département de la communication (COM) à la création et à la mise à jour du site internet du représentant résident du FMI pour le pays.
- Sert de premier point de contact pour les hauts responsables, tant internes qu’externes, dans le pays d’affectation.
- Coordonne et gère des programmes de réunions complexes, résout les difficultés de planification et répond aux demandes des hauts responsables gouvernementaux.
- Gère les activités liées aux ressources humaines (RH), notamment le recrutement et la formation, et participe, selon les besoins, à l’élaboration des plans des employés et au processus d’évaluation de leurs performances.
- Joue un rôle moteur dans la planification et le suivi du programme de travail du bureau, du budget, des procédures administratives et des employés. Traite toutes les questions budgétaires et en assure le suivi, notamment les contrats de consultants, l’organisation des déplacements et les demandes de paiement.
- Gère tous les paiements imputés au budget du bureau. Cela comprend la gestion des informations relatives aux employés et aux fournisseurs dans le système Corporate Banking Solution (CBS), la vérification de l’exactitude des coordonnées bancaires et la saisie des demandes de paiement dans le CBS pour approbation par le chef de bureau et traitement par le département financier (FIN), en veillant au respect des délais de paiement, à l’exactitude du calcul des montants et à la présence de pièces justificatives adéquates.
- Assure le suivi du compte bancaire en veillant à ce que tous les paiements effectués par l’intermédiaire des comptes locaux soient enregistrés en temps utile dans le système comptable du Fonds, à ce que les soldes des comptes concordent avec les écritures du Fonds, à ce que les frais facturés par la banque locale soient conformes au barème prévu par la convention bancaire signée, et à ce que le solde soit suffisant pour couvrir les paiements à venir tout en maintenant une réserve pour les imprévus.
- Gère la petite caisse du bureau. Cela comprend le respect des contrôles relatifs à la manipulation des espèces, le comptage mensuel de la petite caisse et le rapprochement avec les écritures correspondantes dans le système comptable du Fonds.
- Prépare les pièces d’achat et de paiement et en assure le suivi ; contribue également à la préparation des offres dans le cadre d’appels d’offres et à l’évaluation des fournisseurs.
- Apporte son concours aux audits financiers périodiques des documents comptables et réalise des analyses financières ponctuelles.
- Assure la liaison entre la direction et les autres employés.
- Exécute toute autre tâche qui lui est confiée.

**Qualifications**  
Un diplôme de licence ou un diplôme équivalent est requis. Une expérience d’au moins sept ans dans les services administratifs, la finance, la comptabilité, l’audit, les ressources humaines ou un domaine similaire est exigée. Une expérience au sein d’une institution internationale, d’une ONG, d’une organisation similaire ou de l’administration publique constituerait un atout. Une expérience en comptabilité et en finance constituerait également un atout.

**Compétences :**

- Maîtrise approfondie de l’interprétation des politiques, procédures et pratiques pertinentes.
- Compétences relationnelles : capacité à bien travailler avec les autres.
- Connaissance des systèmes financiers et budgétaires.
- Excellentes compétences informatiques : expérience avérée des logiciels courants, tels que la suite Microsoft Office (notamment Word, Excel et PowerPoint).

**Exigences linguistiques**  
Une parfaite maîtrise du français, à l’oral et à l’écrit, est exigée. La maîtrise de l’anglais est un atout.

body:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts.

INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. title: Consultancy - Economic and Financial Analysis - Central Asia
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
body:
**Background:**

Acted is an independent, international organization headquartered in Paris, France. Founded in Afghanistan in 1993, Acted now supports 20 million people across 43 countries worldwide in pursuit of its triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development actor in response to the triple planetary crisis.

Acted has been operating continuously in Central Asia since 1996, working to address the region’s main challenges and, as a result, has long standing partnerships with communities, government agencies, and development partners. In line with Acted's global "3Zero" [Strategy](https://www.3zero.org/): Zero Exclusion, Zero Poverty, Zero Carbon, Acted works across a broad range of sectors to foster inclusive and sustainable development, including Natural Resource Management (NRM), Climate Change Adaption (CCA) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) through its STREAM approach.

Acted is an accredited GCF entity preparing a Full Funding Proposal (PAP) for Fin-Fergana, targeting submission January 2027. The programme addresses climate-driven water insecurity in the Fergana Valley.

**Objectives:**

Acted seeks an external consultant to: (i) conduct a societal-perspective cost-benefit analysis (CBA) with positive Economic Net Present Value and Benefit-Cost Ratio > 1; (ii) develop institution- and beneficiary-perspective financial analyses with and without GCF, assessing minimum concessionality; (iii) build a formula-driven Excel model using GCF official Annex 11 templates; and (iv) write the Annex 11 narrative to GCF submission standards.

## Qualification requirements

**Essential:** Advanced degree in economics, finance or agricultural economics; ≥7 years' experience in economic CBA and/or financial analysis for development or climate projects; at least one approved GCF Full Funding Proposal EFA (Annex 11) — eliminatory criterion; experience with blended finance and lending through financial intermediaries; proficiency in multi-sheet Excel modelling (P&L, cash flow, DSCR, WACC, IRR); CBA experience in water or agriculture; excellent technical English.

**Desirable:** Experience in Central Asia; agricultural microfinance; FX risk; gender-disaggregated economic analysis.

## Duties

**Economic analysis (CBA).** Societal perspective; shadow prices; 15-year analysis period; SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Quantify costs from the approved budget (Annex 4) and benefits for both outcomes: water savings, productivity gains, non-market co-benefits (Outcome 1); incremental farm-level gains and revolving-lending multiplier (Outcome 2). Calculate ENPV, EIRR and BCR per outcome and in aggregate. Sensitivity analysis on discount rate, cost drivers, climate scenario and portfolio performance; disaggregation by country and beneficiary group.

**Financial analysis.** Market prices; institution/beneficiary perspective. Outcome 1: O&M affordability assessment; cost-effectiveness analysis where full CBA is not feasible. Each lending facility (Oxus KG; Uzbekistan PFI(s)): P&L, cash flow and balance sheet projections; DSCR, NPV, IRR, payback; model the revolving mechanism and recycling multiplier; with- and without-GCF comparison; WACC and minimum concessionality via GCF Grant Equivalent Calculator (GCF/B.21/24, GCF/B.23/19); FX risk and hedging. Farm-level analysis for at least three representative investment cases. Sensitivity and scenario analysis throughout.

**Model and narrative.** Consolidated GCF Annex 11 Excel model with central parameters tab; facility-level and aggregate views; no hard-coded values. Annex 11 narrative covering methodology, results, sensitivity and distributional analysis, cross-referenced with Annexes 3, 4, 12 and 13.

## Conditions

Submit to kyrgyzstan.tender@acted.org by the deadline to be communicated. Subject line: EoI — GCF EFA — Fin-Fergana — \[Name\]. Include: (1) CV(s) highlighting GCF EFA, CBA and financial modelling experience; (2) technical proposal (max. 5 pp) with methodology and work plan; (3) at least one GCF EFA example or equivalent sample; (4) financial proposal with total fixed fee (USD) broken down by deliverable; (5) two references. Evaluation: 70% technical (GCF EFA experience 30%, methodology 25%, qualifications 15%) / 30% financial (value for money 20%, person-days 10%). Applications without at least one approved GCF FP EFA will not be evaluated.

**Key Reference Documents**

Annex 11 [template](https://www.greenclimate.fund/document/economic-and-financial-analyses-templates-annex-11) and [guidance](https://www.greenclimate.fund/document/guidelines-preparing-economic-and-financial-analysis-annex-11-pap-proposals).

Provided on contract signature: draft Feasibility Study (Annex 2).

## About company

Acted is committed to the promotion of a 3Zero world of Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty. Acted has been active in Central Asia since 1996, helping to address the region’s main development challenges and fostering opportunities for sustainable and inclusive development, especially in rural and remote communities. This includes a special focus on civil society development and transparent and effective governance.
