title: Gender Officer
body:
**The Africa Enterprise Challenge Fund**

**About Us**

AECF is a leading African-based development organization that leverages the power of the private sector to address systemic issues of rural poverty and employment across the continent. We find and fund innovative, game changing commercial businesses in the agribusiness and renewable energy sectors that transform the lives of low-income households. By catalyzing funding, we help companies surface and commercialize new ideas, business models, and technologies that increase agricultural productivity, expand energy access, and alleviate poverty, particularly where these efforts impact women and young people. AECF works in frontier markets, fragile contexts, and high-risk countries where few mainstream financing institutions go. We back bold enterprises to tackle climate risk, expand opportunity for women and youth, and build resilience in fragile contexts so rural and marginalized communities can rise out of poverty

Since 2008, we have deployed over US$290 million, leveraged $916 million in additional capital, provided funding to 698 businesses in 27 countries – impacting 36 million people.

**About the Programme**

AECF is implementing Investing in Women’s Entrepreneurship for a Greener Economy in Benin and Burkina Faso, a six-year gender equality and economic inclusion programme funded by Global Affairs Canada. The programme provides investment capital and technical assistance to women-owned and women-led enterprises, financial institutions, cooperatives and associations operating in climate-positive sectors. It also works with women’s rights organisations and other local actors to address structural barriers, strengthen women’s agency and advance policy advocacy and social norm change at community and national levels.

**About the Role**

This role supports implementation of AECF’s current Gender Lens Investing Strategy through the Investing in Women Benin and Burkina Faso programme (IFEV-Benin and Burkina Faso). The role will lead and coordinate gender-responsive activities, help the programme achieve its gender equality and women’s economic empowerment targets, and ensure that gender considerations are integrated across investment, technical assistance, advocacy, learning and results measurement.

The successful candidate will work closely with women entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises, agricultural cooperatives and farmer associations, financial institutions, women’s rights organisations, gender champions and other programme partners.

The incumbent will be based in Burkina Faso. This role will report to the Programme Manager, Benin/ Burkina Faso.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of gender equality and women’s economic empowerment activities across the programme, in accordance with the programme management framework, approved workplans, budget and results framework.
- Assess the gender capacity of programme investees and provide tailored technical assistance that enables enterprises, cooperatives and micro-finance institutions to adopt gender-responsive business practices, inclusive workplace policies, climate-smart solutions and products or services that better meet women’s needs.
- Design of gender tools, and guides for portfolio companies in ensuring inclusive climate-smart practices and policies.
- Design and supervise the delivery of women empowerment and norm-shifting activities by women’s rights organizations, and other local community-advocacy groups.
- Strengthen the capacity of gender champions to influence formal and traditional institutions, promote women’s voice and decision-making, and advocate for women’s social and economic empowerment in target communities in Burkina Faso.
- Work with the programme and impact teams to monitor gender equality and women’s economic empowerment indicators, analyse sex-disaggregated and other relevant data, and document outcomes, lessons, case studies and participant stories.
- Deliver quality programme reports outlining gender activities, insights and impact created during donor reporting cycles.
- Lead in the development of evidence-based policy briefs, advocacy frameworks and other materials that champion women’s empowerment in Burkina Faso, together with the women rights organizations.
- Support the larger IFEV-Burkina Faso programme team on gender integration across the investment process.
- Build a network of gender champions, allies and actors that can collaborate with the IFEV-Burkina Faso programme to advance gender equality in Burkina Faso.
- Support the development of knowledge products and organize knowledge sharing events
- Contribute actively to AECF’s Gender Department by sharing programme learning, supporting the development of institutional tools and approaches, and contributing to cross-programme gender equality priorities.

**Suitable candidates should possess:**

- A bachelor’s degree in Gender Economics, Gender Studies, Development Studies, Economics, Development Finance, or other relevant fields of study.
- A minimum of five (5) years of post-training experience in one or more of the following areas: gender economics, social entrepreneurship, impact investing, management consulting, private sector development, renewable energy. agribusiness, SME finance, rural financial services and/or renewable energy and adaptation to combat climate change.
- Hands-on experience in the agribusiness sector is preferred.
- A strong understanding of climate-smart agriculture and solutions.
- Previous experience working with women rights and gender advocacy organizations is strongly preferred.
- Strong experience/ interest in the international development field.
- Experience working in an international team and proven ability to deliver in a complex environment with multiple, divergent stakeholder interests.
- Be fluent in English and French.

title: Head of Programmes CARE Ukraine
body:
## **Is this you?**

**Contract Start Date**: early 2027, no later than 1 March, 2027  
**Contract Duration:** 1 year  
**Duty Station:** Kyiv (Ukraine)

As a member of the Senior Management Team, reporting directly to the Country Director, the Head of Programmes leads the development and implementation of high-quality programmes in Ukraine, ensuring delivery against scope, time and budget, and overseeing quality management and impact across the portfolio. The role line-manages the Programme Implementation Lead, Technical Advisors and Coordinators, and MEAL Coordinator, while ensuring close cross-departmental coordination. It places particular emphasis on programme quality and strengthening partners’ technical capacities in relevant sectors. Working closely with the Country Director, Programme Development Lead, Partnership Coordinator, Advocacy Advisor and department heads, the Head of Programmes contributes to strategic direction, programme implementation and partnership development.

## **Your mission**

## Overall Programme Implementation and Quality

- Provide inclusive and cohesive leadership to CARE Ukraine’s programme teams, ensuring coordinated, high-quality implementation in line with the Country Strategy.
- Maintain a strong understanding of Ukraine’s social, political and economic context, initiating assessments to identify emerging needs and opportunities for programme expansion.
- Ensure projects are delivered on scope, time and budget, with day-to-day oversight delegated to the Program Implementation Lead and technical guidance provided by relevant teams.
- Regularly review programme priorities against the Country Strategy, adapting them based on contextual changes, evidence, learning and priorities identified with partners.
- Ensure effective coordination between programme implementation, technical teams, MEAL and Program Development to address challenges, strengthen cross-sector integration and inform new initiatives.
- Oversee strategic programmes and initiatives, ensuring their contribution to CARE Ukraine’s long-term objectives.
- Mainstream gender equality, protection and inclusion across all programmes, ensuring consistent application of CARE’s programme quality standards.
- Lead regular programme review meetings covering progress, quality, risks and monitoring findings, ensuring follow-up on agreed actions.
- Resolve operational bottlenecks between the Programme Department and other Country and Area Office departments.

## Oversight and Management of Programme Implementation and Budget

- In collaboration with the SMT, define and oversee an effective, efficient and sustainable programme implementation model, clarifying the roles of CARE and its partners and ensuring appropriate SOPs and systems are in place.
- Support the Partnership Coordinator in overseeing partner due diligence, capacity development plans and partnership agreements, ensuring compliance with CARE requirements, including PSEA.
- Ensure effective use and follow-up of project management tools, including Detailed Implementation Plans, MEAL Plans and monitoring reports, through the Program Implementation Lead and MEAL Coordinator.
- Ensure programmes are responsive to communities, particularly women and girls, and comply with CARE’s principles, values, strategic plans and CI procedures.
- Act as overall budget holder for all programmes, delegating day-to-day budget management to the Program Implementation Lead while retaining accountability for expenditure and donor compliance.
- Oversee financial forecasting, expenditure monitoring and corrective actions, ensuring budget risks and variances are addressed and resources are aligned with programme priorities, in coordination with Finance and Operations.
- Provide direction on significant budget adjustments and resource allocation, and directly oversee specific grants where required.

## Programme Quality, Technical Support and Learning

- Maintain and adapt CARE Ukraine’s programme quality framework in line with CARE International and humanitarian standards, including the Core Humanitarian Standard.
- Guide technical leads in ensuring compliance with minimum technical standards and consistent application of appropriate tools, guidelines and SOPs, providing the necessary support to Programme Managers and partners.
- Promote coherent and integrated technical approaches across sectors, particularly regarding gender equality, protection and inclusion.
- Lead regular programme quality reviews with technical teams, MEAL and the Program Implementation Lead, ensuring gaps, risks and improvement actions are identified and addressed.
- Oversee MEAL and information management systems through the MEAL Coordinator, ensuring reliable and timely evidence on programme quality and outcomes and addressing significant system and capacity gaps.
- Set priorities for needs assessments, evaluations, external monitoring and research, ensuring their quality and relevance to programme effectiveness and changing needs.
- Lead the development of a research and learning agenda with MEAL and technical teams, ensuring evidence, implementation experience and good practices inform technical approaches and programme adaptation.
- Ensure learning and recommendations are shared with CARE teams and partners, translated into improvements and reflected in programme strategy.
- Oversee CARE Ukraine’s accountability mechanism, ensuring community feedback informs programme reviews and adaptations in line with CARE standards.
- Ensure partner capacity strengthening addresses identified quality gaps and its effectiveness is regularly reviewed with technical leads and the Partnership Unit.

## Business Development

- Support the Country Director in developing and adapting the funding strategy, diversifying donor engagement in line with CARE Ukraine’s Country Strategy.
- Coordinate technical inputs to new programmes, proposals and reports with the Program Development Lead, Program Implementation Lead, technical teams and MEAL Coordinator, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities and quality standards.
- Ensure programme design builds on contextual analysis, monitoring findings, lessons learned and priorities identified with communities and partners.
- Promote the meaningful participation of partners and communities in programme design, including the development of logical frameworks, activities and budgets, ensuring proposals address identified needs and include appropriate MEAL components and resources.

## Representation and Networking

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with strategic and implementing partners and peer organisations.
- Maintain strong links across CARE International and its membership to mobilise technical expertise and resources in support of the Country Strategy.
- Engage with UN agencies, humanitarian clusters and sector working groups to inform strategic priorities and operational planning, share programme evidence and learning, and fulfil CARE’s coordination commitments, including co-leadership responsibilities.
- Provide programme evidence and technical input to advocacy and communications strategies, working closely with the Advocacy Advisor and Communications Coordinator to promote the visibility and uptake of programme learning.

## Team Management and Coordination

- Manage the performance and development of direct reports in line with CARE policies, providing coaching, mentoring and training to strengthen leadership and team effectiveness.
- Oversee recruitment, training and promotion of programme staff, ensuring that key functions are adequately staffed.
- Foster a collaborative and respectful team environment, promoting staff resilience and well-being in challenging contexts.
- Identify staff capacity development needs in collaboration with Human Resources.
- Supervise managers and technical leads, ensuring coordinated implementation of workplans and budgets.
- Lead safeguarding prevention and response across CARE Ukraine’s workplaces, programmes and communities, ensuring compliance with CARE standards and policies on PSEA-CP, Gender Equality and CARE Performance Standards, in coordination with the CARE DE Safeguarding Focal Point and CARE Ukraine HR Manager.

## **Your profile**

**Essential**  
**Experience and Technical Expertise**

- At least 7 years’ experience in humanitarian and/or development work with national or international NGOs, including 5 years in senior management roles and significant field operations experience.
- At least 2 years’ experience living and working in an emergency or conflict setting.
- Master’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences or a relevant discipline.
- Good understanding of at least one of CARE’s key programme sectors (Protection, WASH/Shelter, SRH or Livelihoods).
- Strong knowledge of international humanitarian and development systems, institutions and donors.
- Proven project management skills, including knowledge of accountability frameworks and substantial experience in financial and budgetary management.
- Demonstrated expertise in gender equality and gender-transformative programming.
- Sound understanding of MEAL systems and experience using data, evidence and learning to assess programme quality, adapt implementation and inform programme design.
- Experience in partnership-based approaches, civil society development and strengthening the capacity of local partner organisations.

**Leadership and Management Skills**

- Proven ability to lead, motivate and develop teams through coaching, mentoring and capacity building, including cross-functional teams.
- Strong results orientation, with the ability to challenge existing approaches and drive improvements.
- Excellent analytical and strategic thinking skills, including the ability to assess information, evaluate options and plan effectively.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, negotiation and influencing skills.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Ability and willingness to work flexible hours and operate in environments with security restrictions.
- Strong commitment to CARE’s mission, values and principles.
- High levels of political and cultural sensitivity, patience, tact and diplomacy.
- Strong sense of responsibility, integrity and trustworthiness.

**Desirable**

- Significant experience designing and supporting partner-led programmes.
- Strong and up-to-date knowledge of the humanitarian context in Ukraine.
- Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or other relevant regional languages.
- Experience in training and capacity development.
- Proven representation and networking skills, including the ability to represent CARE effectively in external forums.

## **Why us?**

CARE Ukraine is a country office which comes under the management of CARE Germany. It has been operating in Ukraine since March 2022.

CARE prioritizes a locally led response and is partnering primarily with Civil-Society Organizations (CSOs), National NGOs, local authorities, and when needed, INGOs with a longstanding presence in the country and access to hard-to-reach areas. CARE Ukraine deliberately and strategically prioritizes partnerships with local and national Women Led and Women Rights organizations (WLO’s/ WRO’s), in accordance with Gender in Emergencies (GiE) principles.

CARE Ukraine’s FY25 portfolio was approx. EUR 13 million, funded by GFFO/ BMZ, ECHO, DANIDA, Czech MOFA, ADA (Austrian Development Agency), AFD (Agence Francaise de Developpement), LDS (Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints) and others. We implement primarily humanitarian programs, in the protection/ GBV, SRH, integrated humanitarian response and WASH/ shelter sectors. Some 10-15% of our programs are recovery/ response, primarily in livelihoods, WASH and womens empowerment sectors. The focus of most programming is the frontline oblasts of Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, and Dnipropetrovsk oblast. We also have some programming in Odesa. The country office is in Kyiv, with a support office in Lviv and field offices in Dnipro and Kharkiv. We plan to phase out the Lviv support office in the second half of 2026.

CARE Ukraine currently partners with 12 local/national organizations, almost all of which are WLO’s/WRO’s. We channel some 80% of our funding through local/national partners. Through the activities that have been implemented so far, CARE Ukraine has been able to reach over 750,000 people, including IDPs and affected populations in hard-to-reach areas.

## **General information**

CARE values equal opportunities and diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability.

**Accountability within CARE**  
A commitment to CARE values and CARE’s integrity framework is critical to working with CARE. Any candidate offered a job with CARE will be expected to adhere to the following key areas of accountability:  
\- Comply with CARE’s policies and procedures with respect to safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, confidentiality, do no harm principles and unacceptable behavior protocols.  
\- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.  
\- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior of a CARE staff or partner.

**Safeguarding**  
Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with CARE as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that CARE shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Gender equality**  
CARE is committed to meeting the standards of the CARE International Gender Policy (2019). Through this policy, CARE seeks to promote the equal realization of dignity and human rights for girls, women, boys and men in all diversities, and the elimination of poverty and injustice. Specifically, this policy seeks to improve the explicit incorporation of gender in programmatic and organizational practices.

## **Our offer**

- Competitive salary
- Housing allowance
- Risk allowance
- Relocation package
- Vacation according to the country office policies, plus additional days off on public holidays
- Generous R&R policy
- 24/7 group accident insurance
- Health insurance
- Coverage of relevant training and development opportunities

We are looking for highly motivated team members who identify with CARE’s goals and values. We offer a varied role with numerous employee benefits within a supportive, international team.

## **About us**

**About CARE Germany**  
Founded in 1980 and based in Bonn, CARE Germany is a member of the CARE International confederation—a global humanitarian network dedicated to fighting poverty and delivering life-saving aid in times of crisis. We work with communities to promote sustainable development, gender equality, and resilience, addressing the world’s most pressing challenges from climate change to conflict-driven displacement.  
At CARE Germany, our staff are the cornerstone of our humanitarian efforts. Committed to the principles of CARE International and working tirelessly to uplift disadvantaged communities worldwide. Whether based in our headquarters or in our Country Offices in the Balkans, Ukraine, Iraq, or Libya, each team member plays a vital role in delivering aid, supporting long-term recovery, and advocating for those most in need. Regardless of their role, all staff contribute to a collective mission—one rooted in solidarity, compassion, and impactful action.

title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Flying Manager - Nigeria - M/F
body:
**THE ALIMA ASSOCIATION**

**ALIMA’S ETHOS:** *ALIMA’s purpose is to save lives and provide care for the most vulnerable populations, without any discrimination based on identity, religion or politics, through actions based on proximity, innovation, and the alliance of organizations and individuals. We act with humanity and impartiality in accordance with universal medical ethics. To gain access to patients, we undertake to act in a neutral and independent manner.*

**Our CHARTER defines the VALUES and PRINCIPLES of our action:**

1. Patient First – Patient centered medical care
2. Revolutionizing humanitarian medicine through research
3. Responsibility and freedom: encourage decision-making by those closest to patients
4. Commitment to a dynamic of continuous quality improvement
5. Creating a climate of trust among colleagues
6. Collective intelligence
7. Environmental liability

**CARING - INNOVATING - TOGETHER:**

Since its creation in 2009, ALIMA has treated more than 13 million patients and today deploys its operations in 15 countries. In 2023, ALIMA cared for 2.8 million patients, including over a million children under the age of 5, received 157,393 people for mental health consultations, assisted 67,617 births, carried out 64 projects in 14 countries. Whenever possible, we work in partnership with local NGOs to ensure that our patients benefit from the best and most relevant expertise wherever it is, whether within their own country or in the rest of the world. In addition, to improve the humanitarian response, we are carrying out operational and clinical research projects, particularly in the field of the fight against malnutrition and viral hemorrhagic fevers.

**ALIMA’S TEAM:** More than 2000 people currently work for ALIMA. The field teams, as close as possible to the patients, receive their support from the coordination teams generally based in the capitals of the countries of intervention. These receive support from the 4 desk teams and the emergency and opening service team based at the operational headquarters in Dakar, Senegal. The Paris and New York teams are actively working on fundraising as well as representing ALIMA. The rest of the ALIMA Galaxy includes individuals and partner teams who work on behalf of other organizations such as medical NGOs BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, research organizations PACCI, INSERM, Universities of Bordeaux or Copenhagen, the NGO Solidarités International and many others.

**COUNTRIES WHERE WE WORK IN 2021:** Mali, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Democratic Republic of Congo, Cameroon, Guinea, South Sudan, Mauritania, Senegal, Sudan, Ethiopia and Haiti.

**THE WORK WE DO** covers: Primary and Secondary Health Care, with a main focus on children and women - including treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition, maternal health, mental health, response to epidemics (Ebola, Cholera, Measles, Dengue, Lassa Fever), surgery, displaced populations, and gender based violence, Covid 19.

**ALIMA IN NIGERIA** : ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) has been active in Nigeria since 2016, with interventions guided by a regional strategy addressing health and nutrition emergencies, maternal-infant care, mental health, epidemic response alongside operational research to enhance health outcomes for vulnerable populations—particularly internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities.

The organization operates across several states: North-East: Borno (MMC and Jere LGAs) and Yobe (Bade, Yusufari, Nguru and Karasuwa LGAs) North-West: Katsina (Kaita, Batagarawa, Batsari and Katsina LGAs) , South-West: Ondo (Owo LGA).

**PROTECTION OF BENEFICIARIES AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS**

Level 3: As part of his/her duties, the incumbent will visit programs and come into contact with children and/or vulnerable adults. Therefore, a criminal record check or a certificate of good character will be required. In situations where a criminal record check or character reference is not possible, a declaration of honor will be requested.

**FUNCTIONAL AND HIERARCHICAL LINKS**

- He/she reports to the Medical Coordinator (line manager), and to the Mental Health referent at HQ (technical manager).
- He/she manages the mental health team
- He/she works in close collaboration with the coordinators (medical, logistics and projects).

**MAIN MISSION**

The Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Activity Flying Manager (MHPSS) is responsible for the mental health strategy and the implementation of the psycho-social support for patients, their families, the community and the teams. He/she ensures the functioning of the mental health pole on the Nigeria projects.

1. **Implementation of ALIMA programs**

- Contribute to Implement and evolve the mental health care strategy, care circuit and referral in each intervention site;
- Ensures the implementation and monitoring of psychological support for beneficiaries in the various projects, patients or isolated people and families
- Organize the mental health department in collaboration with the Mental Health project teams, Medical coordination and HQ.
- Ensures and follow the psychological support for the team in the fields and in the mission
- Supervise the organization of the psychological first aid sessions for patients and victims;
- Supervise and sharing time of practices on specific situations
- Ensures the effectiveness of mental health and psychosocial support activities in accordance with the defined action plan and according to the minimum package of mental health activities vs. the complete package, with a focus on psychological first aid, prevention and management of psychotrauma;
- Ensures the development of partnerships for the management, orientation and referral of severe or chronic cases of mental disorders and/or psychosocial problems.
- Collaborate with partners to ensure the continuity of patients care
- Assure the drafting of training modules and be in charge of training of trainers in the mental health department according to identified needs.
- Collected information on vulnerable audiences and ensured the establishment of focus groups and discussion groups.

1. **Monitoring, analysis and reporting**

- Participates in external meetings and reports relevant information to the Medical coordinator
- Conducts a weekly summary of mental health activities and reports to the medical coordinator and feedback on the mental health activities to the Mental Health managers of the projects.
- Follows the issues and recommendations of the cluster
- Produces a mission report and recommendations

1. **Representation, coordination with other teams**

- Ensures networking with the various partners,
- Participates in meetings related to his/her field of intervention on the instructions of the head office mental health referent;

1. **Management of the mental health team**

- Supervise the organization of the duties and schedules of the mental health team.
- Ensures the proper transmission of information, provides clinical supervision of teams
- Ensure regular formative supervision for the teams.
- Analyse and put into action the data collected for the department of mental health monitoring and activity report

1. **Capacity building and team facilitation**

- Support the sets up a mental health team in collaboration with the project coordinator (the recruitment, training and reinforcement)
- Ensures that the skills of the mental Health staff are updated according to the evolution of the technical platform and the protocols made available to the mission
- Defines and update job profiles and performance objective plans for team members and participate in the same documents for medical coordinator
- Carries out the assessments of its team in an approach of professional course
- Identify the skills that team members need to acquire to master their positions and organize training to reinforce them
- Ensure trainings in accordance with ALIMA's minimum package of mental health activities, and if necessary according to the complete package (psychological first aid, psychosocial activities, psychological support in the practice of medical care, mental health staff, prevention and management of psychotrauma, the relationship between caregivers and patients, and other needs identified upstream).

1. **Team health**

- Supervise the organization of the briefing sessions / He/she supports the teams in case of critical incident
- Ensures the implementation and follow-up of the psychological support of the teams on the different projects
- Evaluates and validates mental health referral structures with the project's medrefs and medco.

**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**

**Experiences**

- Professional Master's degree in clinical and/or health psychology or equivalent
- Previous experience in humanitarian work
- Experience working with vulnerable people in an intercultural context
- A minimum of 3 years of Proven experience at psychological scope
- Proven experience of conducting of training

## **Qualities of the candidate**

- An ability to problematize and summarize the main psychological issues and be able to set priorities
- Good teamwork and delegation skills
- A good deal of autonomy and the ability to create one's own position in line with the association's objectives and resources
- Good writing skills
- A good knowledge of psycho-trauma

## **Languages**

- English fluent
- Nigeria local languages could be are an asset

**CONDITIONS**

**Contract term**:

- Contract term: contract under French law, contract length: 6 months (renewable, based on funding availability and performance)
- Position to be filled: ASAP

**Salary**: depending on experience + per diem

ALIMA pays for :

- travel costs between the expatriate’s country of origin and the mission location
- Accommodation costs
- medical cover from the first day of the contract to a month after the date of departure from the mission country for the employee
- Evacuation of the employee

title: Senior Procurement Specialist and Procurement Specialist - Fiji and Pacific Region
body:
## Job Brief

Open to Fiji and other Pacific Region applicants

**DT Global** invites applications for the following positions for in international donor funded program in Fiji: **Senior Procurement Specialist and Procurement Specialist.** The Program is expected to focus on strengthening physical, economic, and social infrastructure and the expected duration of the Program is for a period of six years.

**Senior Procurement Specialist**

**Duties and Responsibilities:** The Senior Procurement Specialist will plan, manage, execute, and coordinate tasks related to the procurement of goods, services, and civil works for the Program. The Senior Procurement Specialist will provide advice on the procurement activities and provide contract administration services.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- 12 years of experience working as a public procurement professional
- Extensive knowledge of international development partner institutions’ procurement guidelines and procedures
- Demonstrated understanding of best practices in procurement procedures, and in project and contract management
- Experience and demonstrated ability in the development of procurement documents, i.e. bidding documents, evaluation reports, contracts, etc.
- Prior experience conducting procurements and contract administration of civil works. Prior experience with FIDIC-based work contracts
- Experience working on two or more of donor funded project such as the World Bank, African Development Bank, USAID
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills and ability to work with high-level government officials

title: Director, UNRWA Representative Office, Washington, DC, D1
source: UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East
body:
**Posting Title : Director, UNRWA Representative Office, Washington, DC, D**1

Job Code Title : Duro - Wdc Department/ Office : UNRWA - Commissioner-General Office - Headquarters Amman

Location: WASHINGTON

Posting Period : 9 November 2026-6 December 2026

Job Opening number : 26-PCL-Commissioner-General Office-287851-R WASHINGTON (R) Staffing

Exercise : N/A

United Nations Core Values: Integrity, Professionalism, Respect for Diversity

**Org. Setting and Reporting**

UNRWA, the largest United Nations operation in the Middle East with over 25,000 staff and complementary personnel across five areas of operation, is looking for highly committed personnel wishing to make a change. If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you. The incumbent reports to the Commissioner-General (USG) and reports administratively to the Chief of Staff. The incumbent works closely with the Deputy Commissioner-General for Operational Support (ASG).

**Responsibilities**

Leads and directs UNRWA's strategic engagement and promotes the interests of UNRWA vis-à-vis the U.S. government (with particular reference to the U.S. Congress, State Department and National Security Council), Canada (including the Canadian Parliament and Global Affairs Canada) and their non-governmental entities, think tanks, press, and diplomatic corps; advances understanding of UNRWA's role with these policymakers in the context of the regional issues of the Middle East, the Agency's operations, and the plight of Palestine refugees in the five fields.

Serves as the principal adviser to the Commissioner-General, Deputy Commissioner General for Operational Support and Chief of Staff on political, legislative and policy developments in the United States and Canada affecting UNRWA's mandate, operations, funding environment and reputation; provides strategic analysis and recommendations to inform Agency-wide decision-making and risk mitigation

Shapes stakeholder understanding of UNRWA's mandate, strategic priorities and challenges through targeted political engagement, strategic communications and high-level advocacy; promotes awareness of UNRWA programmes, initiatives and institutional practices, particularly in the areas of neutrality, impartiality and independence.

Monitors relevant development in the U.S. and Canadian political spheres, with a view to formulating and leading the implementation of outreach and awareness-raising strategies dedicated to optimizing UNRWA's relations with U.S. and Canadian policy makers; promotes strengthened bilateral support both politically and financially with U.S. and Canadian stakeholders.

In close coordination with the Department of External Relations and Communications (ERCD), supports the implementation of UNRWA's resource mobilization and strategic communications frameworks in the United States and Canada.

Advises on the development of media and communications messaging for U.S. and Canadian audiences, provides timely responses to queries from media and other entities; including through press and public appearances.

Represents UNRWA at public engagements in the U.S. and Canada (except those related to the activities of UNRWA Representative Office, New York).

Leads the drafting, preparation and presentation of materials required for briefings by the Commissioner-General and other senior UNRWA staff for U.S. and Canadian officials, entities, the media, and other governmental and non-governmental agencies.

In close consultation with ERCD, and working in tandem with the Director, UNRWA Representative Office, New York, builds and sustains partnerships with international organisations headquartered in the U.S. and Canada, the private sector, national and local non-profit institutions, including UNRWA-USA, and high value individuals, amongst others; maintains awareness and support through special events requiring dedicated support, speaking engagements and informational outreach.

Leads UNRWA's Representative Office and the team in Washington, DC. through providing strategic leadership and management of the Office, ensuring effective planning, operational oversight, resource management, compliance, staff performance and delivery of results in support of Agency priorities.

**Competencies**

UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default.

-Entrepreneurial Thinking.

-Persuading and Influencing.

-Coping with Pressure and Setbacks.

-Deciding and Initiating Action.

 -Managing Complexity and Change.

-Creating and Maintaining Impact and Partnership.

-Political Awareness and acuteness.

-Empathy, and coaching skills.

-Thought leadership to support innovation, learning and knowledge sharing towards capacity development.

**Education**

An Advanced university degree (master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in political science, public or business administration, or a related field.

**Job Specific Qualifications**

**Work Experience**

An Advanced university degree (master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in political science, public or business administration, or a related field is required.

At least fifteen years' experience in political or administrative affairs is required.

At least five years in a leadership or managerial capacity is required.

At least five years' experience in governmental affairs and outreach with Washington, DC-based U.S. government, non-governmental agencies or entities is required.

Unless already serving as an international staff member in the UN Common System, at least two continuous years of relevant international experience should be outside UNRWA and outside the country of primary citizenship is required.

Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A "yes" answer doesn't necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired.

Familiarity with political affairs in the Middle East, with emphasis on Palestine refugees' issues is desirable.

Experience in a large governmental or international organisation is desirable.

Experience with appropriations processes with the U.S. or Canadian government is desirable.

Experience in, or in close association with, a United Nations organisation is desirable.

**Languages**

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat.

For this job opening, English is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details).

**Required Languages**

Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking

 English UN Level III UN Level III UN Level III UN Level III

**Assessment**

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interview.

**Special Notice**

The appointment against this position is limited to the UNRWA - Commissioner-General Office - Headquarters Amman.

Type of Contract and duration: 1 year, with the possibility of further extension.

The incumbent will occasionally travel to UNRWA's area of operations and various venues in the United States as required.

Only applications that have been fully completed in UNRWA's online e-recruitment system Inspira will be considered and no late applications will be accepted. The Personal History Profile (PHP) should be completed with full work experience under the experience tabs as per the requirements in the Job Opening.

All university degrees must also be stated, where applicable. UNRWA personnel must ensure adding their contract type and grade level. Given the large pool of applicants, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment.

Providing incorrect or misleading information on an application form will result in the immediate disqualification of the candidate.

UNRWA has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNRWA, including sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment, racism/racial discrimination and other forms of conduct, including but not limited to discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment. To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for all recommended candidates and those placed on a roster to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s), employment history, ClearCheck and INTERPOL, as well as certification of non-conviction, where available. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check. By applying for a position with UNRWA, candidates acknowledge and consent to these verification processes.

 Advertisements published in English will only accept applications in English; other language submissions will not be considered.

UNRWA is committed to achieving gender balance in its workforce. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

UNRWA welcomes applications from qualified candidates with disabilities.

A roster may be created from the selection exercise, and successful candidates may become eligible for appointment to the same post or a similar post, when the need arises.

Equivalency:

A first level university degree in combination with additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of an advanced university degree.

NB: work experience alone or formal qualifications with no relevant work experience are not considered an acceptable combination.

The Agency disqualifies applicants whose name appears on the UN Sanctions List or a UN database of staff separated for reason of misconduct or of staff who separated while a misconduct process was pending. UNRWA shares investigation and misconduct information with other UN Agencies, and past and prospective employers about staff members who have been separated for misconduct, or who have separated while an investigation and/or disciplinary process for misconduct is underway; and those individuals may be prohibited from employment with the United Nations.

UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions from UN member states, regional bodies, business foundations and individual contributions. The mission of UNRWA is to help Palestine refugees achieve their full potential in human development under the difficult circumstances in which they live.

For more details on UNRWA, please visit: [https://www.unrwa.org/](https://www.unrwa.org/)

**United Nations Considerations**

Staff members are subject to the authority of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA and to assignment by him or her.

UNRWA is committed to achieving gender parity at all levels of staffing under the current UN-wide gender agenda and strongly encourages applications from qualified applicants from under-represented groups.

At UNRWA, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. UNRWA is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application.

**UNRWA Considerations**

UNRWA staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, competence, neutrality, impartiality and integrity. This includes respect for and commitment to human rights, diversity and non-violent means of dealing with all kinds of conflict. Only persons who fully and unconditionally commit to these values should consider applying for UNRWA jobs. Candidates will not be considered for employment with UNRWA if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. The Agency may disqualify applicants who have separated for reason of misconduct, who left a UN Agency while misconduct processes were pending, or who appear on the UN Sanctions List.

UNRWA is a non-smoking work environment.

Applicants are urged to follow carefully all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira. For more detailed guidance, applicants may refer to the Manual for the Applicant, which can be accessed by clicking on "Manuals" hyper-link on the upper right side of the inspira account-holder homepage.

The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines.

Applicants must provide complete and accurate information pertaining to their personal profile and qualifications according to the instructions provided in inspira to be considered for the current job opening. No amendment, addition, deletion, revision or modification shall be made to applications that have been submitted. Candidates under serious consideration for selection will be subject to reference checks to verify the information provided in the application.

Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date.

**No Fee**

THE UNITED NATIONS RELIEF AND WORKS AGENCY FOR PALESTINE REFUGEES IN THE NEAR EAST (UNRWA) DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE OR REQUEST MONEY FROM CANDIDATES AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT AND ONBOARDING PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING, ONBOARDING). title: Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) - GUARD
body:
**PROGRAM SUMMARY**

GUARD America (Global Urgent Activation for Response to Infectious Diseases) is an International Medical Corps-led consortium funded by the U.S. Department of State Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD) to support rapid outbreak activation and response, early detection and containment, operational coordination, and stronger national and subnational outbreak-response systems. GUARD is currently supporting the BVD response in DRC, while retaining a broader platform and consortium structure that may support additional country responses as activated.

International Medical Corps is implementing a large and evolving Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with additional regional and multi-country programming. The response spans multiple projects and funding streams and includes case management through Ebola Treatment Centers and transit/triage structures; surveillance, alert management and community-based surveillance; infection prevention and control (IPC) and WASH; risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); mental health and psychosocial support; and continuity of essential health services. The scale and complexity of the response requires a coordinated M/E approach that harmonizes indicators, tools, data systems and reporting across projects while meeting government, donor and internal requirements.

The Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation (M/E) - GUARD will provide senior technical M/E leadership and oversight for International Medical Corps' global project team for GUARD. The role will augment, not replace, the existing country M/E team and leadership. The role will also provide targeted M/E support to the GUARD consortium, including management of the results framework and indicator tracking, donor reporting, consolidation of partner results, and coordination with consortium partners on M/E standards and requirements. As GUARD's response remit evolves, the position is expected to transition to a broader multi-country or global GUARD M/E role.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The role of the Senior Specialist is to support better performance and greater accountability by implementing evidence-based project management at the field level, to guide and improve performance. The Senior Specialist will lead the design of methodologies and tools to ensure the availability of clear and accurate information at the project level. The Senior Specialist also plays a vital role in data management, surveys and quality by designing an M/E system that adheres to the International Medical Corps (IMC) M/E Global Guidelines, the M/E Minimum Standards for Quality, and the guiding M/E policies and procedures, among others. The Senior Specialist, M/E will provide technical support to the project and build capacity in the country mission through strengthening learning and knowledge sharing across the IMC and with the wider humanitarian community.

For this assignment, the Senior Specialist will provide senior technical M/E leadership and oversight for IMC's highly infectious disease responses led by GUARD, providing technical direction to the country M/E team to ensure coherent monitoring, data quality, analysis and reporting across multiple projects and funding streams, while also supporting GUARD consortium-level performance monitoring, reporting and partner M/E coordination.

**REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

- The country-based M/E lead will have a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Senior Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation, for technical direction and oversight, while keeping their solid-line reporting relationship to country leadership.
- Sets the technical scope, standards, methods, tools and quality expectations for M/E across the Ebola response and GUARD-supported activities. Provides technical guidance, review and capacity building to the country M/E lead and team.
- Country leadership keeps line management of the country M/E team, including day-to-day work assignments, deadlines, performance management, and hiring and separation decisions. The Senior Specialist gives technical input to these processes as appropriate.
- Where GUARD operates in countries with an existing IMC mission, the same model applies. Country M/E leads reports to the Senior Specialist on a dotted line for technical matters, and country leadership keeps solid-line management and operational accountability.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation.

**MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**IMC's policies, guidelines, and procedures**

- Mainstream the Global M/E Guidelines across all related M/E activities at the field level and ensure the guidance notes for monitoring and evaluation are functional at the field level.
- Apply and adapt existing Global M/E Guidelines, tools, and templates at the relevant stages of the project cycle.
- Actively promote the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards within IMC and amongst its beneficiaries.
- Contribute to the creation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organization, notably through the application of the Code of Conduct, ethics, values, and standpoint with regards to internal and external actors.

**Ebola Response and GUARD M/E Leadership**

- Provide senior technical leadership and oversight of M/E for IMC's Ebola response in DRC across multiple projects and funding streams, providing technical direction to the country M/E lead and team to ensure that project-specific requirements are met within a harmonized response-level M/E approach.
- Maintain and strengthen the consolidated Ebola response M/E framework, including harmonization of indicators, definitions, data collection tools, reporting flows and performance tracking across projects and implementation areas.
- Lead routine review of response performance, data quality and indicator achievement, working with program, technical and field teams to identify discrepancies, implementation gaps and required corrective actions and to strengthen the use of data for operational decision-making.
- Coordinate donor and internal M/E deliverables for the Ebola portfolio, including M/E plans, indicator tracking tables, performance reports, data calls and other quantitative reporting requirements, ensuring consistency of results across submissions.
- For GUARD, maintain and update the project results framework/log frame and indicator tracking systems; coordinate consolidation and quality assurance of results reported by IMC and consortium partners; and contribute M/E evidence and analysis to GUARD donor reporting, reviews and planning.
- Provide M/E guidance and capacity strengthening to GUARD consortium partners as required, including clarification of indicator definitions, reporting requirements, data-quality expectations and supporting documentation.
- Ensure that GUARD country-response monitoring is integrated with existing Ebola response systems to the extent feasible, avoiding unnecessary duplication of indicators, tools, databases and reporting processes.
- Coordinate closely with the Information Management/Data Manager, epidemiology staff, country M/E staff, technical leads and relevant HQ technical teams to establish clear responsibilities for data collection, management, analysis and reporting.
- Support adaptation of M/E systems for additional GUARD-supported country responses if activated and be prepared to assume a broader multi-country/global GUARD M/E remit as the program evolves.

**Project design and planning**

- Lead or support the development and updating of project and response-level results frameworks, theories of change, log frames, M/E plans and indicator tracking tables, including harmonization of indicators across Ebola response projects and GUARD.
- Identify the budget/resources needed for M/E activities of the project.
- Support project planning processes related to M/E aspects (M/E work plan and budget). M/E system
- In coordination with the implementation Team and M/E field Focal Points, establish a reliable participatory M/E framework according to donors' requirements for the project to ensure quality.
- Follow full M/E procedures and operating plans within the project and develop harmonized data collection tools involving the different stakeholders (project team, partners).
- Establish M/E system in line with donors and project requirements and ensure donors' requirements are followed through the project management life cycle.
- Develop and maintain data gathering strategies and clear data and reporting flows across projects, implementation sites and, for GUARD, consortium partners.
- Oversee the collection and timely reporting of data and statistics from the service delivery points.
- Consolidate and reconcile results across technical sectors, projects, geographic areas and relevant implementing partners, ensuring consistency between project-level and response-level reporting.
- Implement DHIS2 where appropriate and applicable, control and manage DHIS2 data entry and management.
- Collaborate with the M/E and DHIS2 teams at HQ to develop and maintain the data management system, including updating, troubleshooting and promptly addressing all problems as they arise
- Lead the implementation of Satellite-based Tracking and Remote Monitoring (STARM) system
- Conduct regular site visits or when required to monitor service provision and ensure data quality.
- Support project team to organize regular review and planning meetings to assess project progress.
- Set project monitoring system for the project (monitoring plan, monitoring tools and strategies) and disseminate all monitoring tools within project.

**Data quality management**

- Collaborate with technical staff on data quality maintenance and routine monitoring of project.
- Assess the quality of data collected for the indicators and ensure that data pitfalls and issues are mitigated.
- Coordinate routine data quality audits conducted in different sites, compile results at the level of a project, and develop action plans to implement corrective measures.
- Manage tools and methods for assessing data quality and security.
- Ensure ethical practices are followed in the collection and management of all data; informed consent practices are used in all interviews, and privacy risks are mitigated in the storage and transfer of data.
- Identify and locate back-up documentation for reporting against indicators.
- Maintain data at the mission level according to IMC's data protection protocols.
- Work closely with Information Management and epidemiology colleagues to establish interoperable reporting flows and clearly delineated responsibilities for epidemiological/surveillance data, routine program monitoring data, case-management data and donor performance reporting, minimizing parallel data systems and duplicate data collection.

**Sampling techniques**

- Use proper sampling (probability and non-probability) techniques considering desired power, type of survey or evaluation (e.g., single point or multiple points; baseline vs endline), the objective of the survey or evaluation (e.g., testing for change or getting the point prevalence), and budget limitations.
- Review the sampling approach proposed by an expert/consultant (if applicable).
- Develop the sampling frame and calculate the sample size for surveys, including implementation of donors’ recommendations for the surveys. Qualitative and quantitative techniques:
- Develop and use different qualitative and quantitative methods of data collection, including structured/ semi-structured interviews, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, group discussions, focus group discussions, and direct observations as an M/E tool.
- Conduct training on quantitative and qualitative techniques for data collection for M/E, project, and interviewers.
- Keeping the social dynamics in mind, manage errors/bias, and strategize to minimize them and to ensure the data collected is representative of populations without power (avoiding over-dependence on community leaders, local authorities, and/or government authorities as primary sources for defining communities' needs and preferences).
- Coordinate the logistics of data collection, data management, and ensure adequate resources are available.
- Develop questionnaires for monitoring purposes and apply the different interview techniques (structured/semi-structured).
- Develop database structures to store and manipulate quantitative data.
- Implement appropriate and recommended survey guidelines
- Conduct regular site visits or when required to monitor and assist partners in the data collection process to ensure data quality.

**Mobile and manual data collection**

- Determine the appropriate data collection tool based on the purpose, advantages, and disadvantages of mobile data collection techniques.
- Design simple and complex questionnaires using XLS or form builder (Kobo form builder, Ona form builder, etc.)
- Support in installing and configuring mobile data collection tools (ODK collect, Kobo collect, CommCare, etc.) on smartphones or tablets and managing data on mobile servers
- Increase the capacity of other staff in developing XLS forms and setting up mobile data collection.

**Data analysis, including use of statistical software**

- Apply standard methodologies for the analysis of data to allow for comparison and aggregation across time and different areas.
- Support M/E and the implementation team on conducting statistical analysis, including descriptive (univariate and bivariate data analysis) and inferential analysis using statistical software.
- Perform qualitative textual analysis and develop topical outlines (coding).
- Triangulate findings from several qualitative and quantitative sources.
- Interpret statistical data for use in decision-making and synthesize quantitative and qualitative information for write-up/reports and decision making.
- Support development and maintenance of response dashboards, analytical products and routine performance summaries that integrate programmatic and epidemiological information where appropriate for operational decision-making.

**Evaluation design**

- Support in developing Terms of Reference (TOR) for internal and external baseline surveys, mid-term evaluations, final evaluations, and frame the different types of study questions such as barrier analysis, market analysis, and Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Surveys (KAP).
- Identify the needed resources for evaluation, such as information, expertise, personnel, instruments, and budget.
- Manage the administrative and logistic process of evaluations involving external evaluators.
- Support in training and supervising data gathering of internal performance evaluation and design and synthesize the findings from participative evaluation techniques (actively involving affected communities in the evaluation exercises).
- Support operational and implementation research and other studies using appropriate epidemiological, quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods approaches, in coordination with HQ research, epidemiology and relevant technical teams.

**Presenting information**

- Write full narrative reports (internal reviews, progress reports, survey reports) and executive summaries.
- Present information and tell the story of the project to multiple audiences and decisionmakers based on the findings from the analysis and monitoring.
- Verify reports' accuracy and presentation of information, including the use of appropriate graphs and tables.
- Disseminate qualitative and quantitative results using the established dashboard or system as per agreed frequency.
- Report and share evaluation findings with stakeholders.
- Generate past performance sheet with updated trend analysis of the key project indicators

**Capacity development and training**

- Provide coaching/mentoring of staff and on-the-job training to improve the skills of the staff in M/E.
- Provide training and on-the-job learning to project staff and volunteers based on required skills for M/E activities
- Support project staff with additional training and mentoring on routine monitoring procedures and surveillance techniques.

**Knowledge management learning:**

- Support in developing Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) mechanisms and processes for the project while ensuring these mechanisms are in line with IMC's guidelines.
- Establish basic learning systems and framework that incorporate project studies' findings, lessons learned, achievements and gaps, and develop all the tools required to support learning practices.
- Facilitate review and lessons learned exercises, including data collected through assessments, surveys and other participative forms of community engagement and feedback collection.
- Collect and document project Most Significant Change Stories (MSCSs) from direct beneficiaries. Community-based feedback and response mechanism:
- Lead the implementation of methodologies to consult communities on their preferences based on the operational context.
- Contribute to planned and ongoing operational research, implementation research, learning and other evidence-generation initiatives related to Ebola and broader outbreak preparedness and response, in coordination with technical, epidemiology, research and program teams. This may include contributing to study design and protocols, development of data collection approaches and tools, data quality and analysis, interpretation of findings, documentation of lessons learned, and translation of evidence into program adaptation and learning.
- Support systematic documentation and synthesis of evidence across GUARD activations and the wider Ebola response, including after-action reviews, implementation learning, operational lessons and cross-country learning, and support dissemination and uptake of findings as appropriate.

**Cross-cutting themes**

- Support project staff to mainstream critical concepts around sex, age, disability protection, and conflict sensitivity by supporting dedicated sex, protection, and conflict sensitivity analyses as may be required by project.
- Integrating the collection of information related to demographic vulnerabilities and contextual risks (sex, age, disability, environment, etc.) into all M/E exercises to provide an evidence base.
- Following up with implementation teams to utilize findings and strengthen activities in line with sex, protection, and conflict-sensitive approaches.
- Coordinate M/E with consortium and implementing partners, including agreement on indicator definitions, reporting timelines, supporting documentation, data-quality expectations and consolidation of partner results; lead relevant M/E coordination meetings and represent IMC as required.
- Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Typically, a bachelor’s degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development, with experience or background in M/E, epidemiology, public health, and health information management. Master's level or a higher degree in social sciences, public health, statistics, or international development preferred. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.
- Typically, 10+ years of applied experience in the humanitarian or international development sector, including 7+ years designing, implementing and overseeing monitoring and evaluation systems in relevant sectors.
- Demonstrated experience providing technical leadership and capacity building to M/E teams in complex programming, including leading staff through matrixed or dotted-line reporting relationships.
- Significant international humanitarian field experience, preferably including outbreak or emergency health response; willingness to be based in DRC, with the potential to transition to a multi-country/global remit.
- Experience with M/E approaches for key donors such as US Dept of State, USG, OFDA, ECHO, EU, DfID, UN, etc. Strong experience with U.S. Government-funded program monitoring and reporting; Department of State experience strongly preferred.
- Experience in database design and other tools for information and data management such as DHIS2
- Experience in the use of qualitative and quantitative software for data analysis.
- Experience with mobile data collection platform
- Able to identify gaps in staff knowledge of M/E concepts and skills and provide training in these topics.
- Ability to write full narrative reports (needs assessments, internal reviews, progress reports) and executive summaries.
- Demonstrated understanding of data protection and confidentiality as part of data collection and management practices and ability to respect and maintain confidentiality.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint and Teams.
- Competency in statistical analysis software; proficiency in R/RStudio, Python, or another programming language for data management and analysis is strongly preferred. Broader data science skills are an asset.
- Possess skills in qualitative data analysis, with or without software
- Possess skills in mobile data collection software such as Ona, Kobo, ToolBox.
- Communicate the organizational goals to the team.
- Support innovation and organizational change when needed.
- Have analytical, conceptual, and strategic thinking skills.
- Build collaborative relationships and foster teamwork.
- High-level English proficiency (Speaking – Reading – Writing).
- High-level local language proficiency preferred (Speaking – Reading – Writing).

## Ethical Conduct at International Medical Corps

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

## Equal Opportunities

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

## Misconduct Disclosure Scheme

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

title: Supply Chain and Operations Manager - Sudan
body:
We are currently recruiting a **Supply Chain and Operations Manager** to join our **Supply Chain and Operations** team.

This is a **country-based position** in **Khartoum, Sudan**, with regular travel to field locations subject to access and security conditions.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks and enhanced due diligence**.

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

We work with local actors to deliver safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs. Relief International is an alliance of multiple international entities operating under a one-team approach with a shared mission and leadership structure.

**About the Opportunity**

This is a critical leadership role supporting Relief International's operations in one of the world's most complex humanitarian environments.

The Supply Chain and Operations Manager leads the delivery and continuous improvement of procurement, warehousing, medical supply logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and office operations across Sudan. Based in Khartoum and supporting teams operating in dispersed and often insecure locations, the role is responsible for ensuring country operations remain reliable, cost-effective, compliant and responsive to programme needs.

Working closely with Area Managers, programme teams, Finance, HR, Security, IT and global supply chain colleagues, you will strengthen systems, build the capacity of field teams, improve operational visibility and ensure supply chains continue to function effectively in challenging circumstances.

This is a hands-on leadership position requiring someone who has successfully managed complex field operations and can balance strategic oversight with practical problem-solving.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead and manage supply chain and operations functions across country and field offices, providing leadership, supervision and clear accountability for operational performance.
- Oversee procurement planning and implementation, ensuring timely, competitive and compliant procurement of goods and services while maintaining strong supplier relationships and value for money.
- Manage warehousing, inventory control and medical supply logistics systems, ensuring accurate stock visibility, quality standards, reconciliation processes and reporting.
- Lead fleet, transport, asset and office operations management across country and field locations, ensuring operational continuity, cost controls and compliance with organizational and donor requirements.
- Strengthen procurement, inventory, fleet and asset tracking systems through practical, user-friendly tools and reporting mechanisms.
- Produce regular operational performance reporting, identifying risks, bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement and ensuring corrective actions are implemented.
- Support cross-border supply chain activities and importation processes where required, including medical commodities and specialized programme supplies.
- Work closely with Finance and programme teams to strengthen controls, reconcile commitments and proactively address operational, compliance and fraud risks.
- Build and develop high-performing teams through coaching, mentoring, performance management and capacity strengthening initiatives.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- University degree in logistics, supply chain management, business administration or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Minimum seven years' experience in humanitarian supply chain, logistics or operations management, including at least three years in a senior management role within conflict-affected, post-conflict or similarly fragile environments.
- Demonstrated hands-on experience across procurement, warehousing and inventory management, medical logistics, transport and fleet management, asset management and multi-site operations.
- Proven ability to lead and support geographically dispersed teams operating in challenging and low-connectivity environments.
- Experience designing or improving practical operational tracking systems and using data to strengthen controls, decision-making and performance management.
- Strong knowledge of donor procurement compliance requirements, supplier management, inventory controls, operational budgeting and risk management.
- Excellent leadership, coaching and problem-solving skills, with the ability to simplify processes while maintaining effective controls and accountability.
- Strong written and spoken English and willingness to travel regularly to field locations.
- Arabic language skills would be an advantage.
- Previous experience in Sudan, Chad, Darfur or similar humanitarian contexts would be a bonus
- Experience supporting health and nutrition supply chains, emergency scale-ups and complex humanitarian donor-funded programmes is desirable.

title: Consultoría especialista de medios de vida pecuarios y pesqueros para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en los Municipios Cruz Salmerón Aco
body:
