title: Media Literacy and Countering Disinformation Advisor
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 15 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors.

One of the primary challenges facing Syria during this transitional phase is the fragile social cohesion within communities. Years of conflict and displacement have left Syrian society severely divided, with communities often split along political, ethnic, and sectarian lines. Trust between groups has been eroded, making it difficult for communities to come together and plan for a shared future. Women and youth having been left without meaningful avenues for civic and economic engagement, further marginalizing them from the reconstruction process.

To support the transition and address these challenges, the GIZ BRIDGE project “Strengthening the capacities of the Syrian civil society” plays a vital role. BRIDGE aims to strengthen the role of Syrian civil society in the ongoing transition. The project supports a broad range of activities, from providing capacity-building efforts, to empowering civil society to contribute meaningfully to the country's future, to support independent media in Syria. A key focus of the BRIDGE project is on strengthening social cohesion, with particular emphasis on the inclusion of women and youth in the rebuilding process. By working closely with local communities and civil society representatives, BRIDGE seeks to facilitate cooperation between civil actors and independent media, fostering a more inclusive and united approach to Syria's recovery.

**Your tasks**

- Designs capacity building strategies and activities tailored to the unique needs and challenges of media organizations in Syria
- Overseas and conducts organizational capacity development activities in media literacy and countering disinformation to local independent media and others, including developing and delivering training as needed
- Designs, develops, and manages activities related to promoting media literacy and addressing disinformation that are credible, accurate, and reliable for Syrian citizens
- Develops and maintains relationships with key media stakeholders and government officials at the national and local level, other donors and implementers, program beneficiaries, and other stakeholders
- Develops and maintains strong relationships with local partner organizations, overseeing technical activities and providing coaching to ensure a focus on relevant activities and achieving outcomes
- Contributes to monitoring, evaluation, and learning; project communications; and project reporting
- Develops documentations, manuals, reports, and guidelines related to the implementation of projects

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- University degree (Bachelor or Master) in Journalism, Media related field or other
- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in a similar position with an international or national organization or institution
- Highly-organised and detail-oriented, with strong ability to multi-task and deliver quality work on time under pressure
- Ability to keep track of and reconcile multiple data sources with minimum error
- Highly collaborative, team player and experienced in working in multi-cultural organizations and in a fast-paced environment
- Reliable with confidential information and materials
- Ability to work in an international multicultural team with loyalty, reliability and tolerance
- High motivation and ability to work independently and meet deadlines without compromising the quality of outputs
- Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic, knowledge of German is an asset.

title: M&E Specialist
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 15 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors.

To support this transition, GIZ is strengthening its Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) function to ensure that programme delivery is evidence-driven, accountable, and compliant with donor requirements. The M&E Specialist(s) will contribute to strengthening portfolio oversight, performance tracking and learning, ensuring that decision-makers have timely and credible information to steer implementation, manage risks, and demonstrate results.

**Your tasks**

- Support in ensuring consistent methodologies, tools, standards, and approaches across projects and partners.
- Work on the operationalisation of a portfolio-wide MEAL system, including results frameworks, indicator registries, monitoring plans, reporting templates, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- Ensure robust performance tracking through a maintained portfolio results tracker and dashboards, enabling routine management updates and decision-making products.
- Establish and enforce data quality standards, including verification protocols, documentation requirements, data quality assessments (DQAs), and follow-up on corrective actions with project teams and implementing partners.
- Coordinate routine monitoring cycles (field-based and remote, as applicable), including structured monitoring visits, partner reporting validation, and triangulation of results.
- Support the design and implementation of evaluations, assessments, and studies (e.g., baseline/endline, outcome reviews, third-party monitoring), including drafting TORs, reviewing methodologies, and quality assuring deliverables.
- Institutionalise learning processes across the portfolio, including after-action reviews, quarterly reflection sessions, lessons learnt documentation, and tracking of agreed follow-up actions.
- Ensure accountability to affected populations is integrated into monitoring and learning where applicable, including feedback mechanisms, response tracking, and safe handling of sensitive information.
- Provide structured MEAL inputs into donor reporting and internal reporting processes, ensuring consistency between narrative reporting, indicator tables, and underlying datasets.
- Deliver capacity building and coaching to programme staff and partners on MEAL tools, indicator definitions, data collection ethics, and reporting standards.
- Contribute to the wider Analysis & Research function by supporting evidence synthesis, portfolio performance analysis, and management briefings as requested.
- Where appropriate and reasonable, additional tasks upon request of the management.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- University degree in social sciences, statistics, economics, public policy, development studies, or a related field.
- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in MEAL/M&E, including demonstrated experience designing and rolling out MEAL systems and tools across multiple projects.
- Strong competence in quantitative and qualitative methods, including data collection design, sampling basics, data cleaning, analysis, and interpretation.
- Demonstrated experience with digital data systems and tools (e.g., KoBo/ODK/CommCare or similar) and strong Excel-based data management; experience with PowerBI or similar dashboards is an asset.
- Highly organised and detail oriented, with strong ability to multitask and deliver quality work under pressure and on time.
- Ability to keep track of and reconcile multiple data sources with minimum error, maintaining strong audit trails and documentation.
- Strong interpersonal and coordination skills
- Reliable with confidential information and sensitive datasets, with a strong commitment to ethical data handling.
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English and Arabic; knowledge of German is an asset.

title: Program Officer, Roving Direct Services, Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR)
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The headquarters Resettlement Team oversees the implementation and quality of services for refugees within their early resettlement period. The team supports IRC local office staff in implementing high-quality programs by providing technical assistance, training and monitoring. The Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), funded by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), coordinates placement and resettlement services to newly arriving refugee populations into the US.

The **Program Officer, Roving Direct Services, Program for Initial Resettlement**, supports local IRC offices by joining them on site or virtually to deliver high-quality PIR services to newly arrived refugees. This position is expected to travel up to 50% of the time to any IRC resettlement site to provide strengths-based, client-centered support, working side by side with local staff. The Program Officer also supports the quality of services through training, monitoring and reporting, using critical thinking and sound judgment to diagnose site-level challenges and recommending solutions tailored to each office’s context. The position reports to the Senior Program Officer, Roving Direct Services, in the Resettlement, Asylum, and Integration Department in the US, and works closely with the PIR team.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Support the overall management and implementation of the HQ Roving Direct Services team’s PIR deployments to local IRC sites.
- Conduct a needs assessment before arriving at each site to analyze available data and understand the office’s needs and the root causes behind them, agree on a plan of action, and identify the resources needed.
- Provide on-the-ground and/or virtual support for PIR service delivery in partnership with local site staff for extended periods of time. Support may include helping staff orient newly arrived refugees, complete intake and needs assessments, develop individualized plans, and connect clients to health care, housing, early employment and other community services.
- Support local staff with complex and medical cases by assessing risk, weighing options and prioritizing actions, and provide crisis intervention as necessary.
- Temporarily mentor and support local staff when needed.
- Maintain accurate records in electronic case files and required databases, and consistently protect the confidentiality of client information.
- Guide and support interns as appropriate and necessary.
- Complete post-deployment reporting to maintain high-quality data for the overall quality assurance of the program, and reflect critically on what worked, what did not and why to inform future deployments.
- Support the development of data tracking tools to better understand the outcomes and impact of Roving Direct Services deployments on PIR delivery at local sites.
- Develop and deliver training materials to new or seasoned staff on PIR program guidelines, policies and procedures.
- Support local offices in preparing for internal and donor monitoring through activities such as home visits, case file reviews (analyzing findings to identify patterns and systemic gaps), developing quality assurance tools, and helping staff become well versed in PIR program guidelines and policies.
- Analyze patterns and lessons learned from local offices and develop evidence-based recommendations for the PIR team to improve guidance, procedures, and support to the network.
- Other responsibilities as assigned, including the provision of direct services to clients when needed.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.

**Work experience:**

- Minimum 3-6 years of progressive non-profit experience, preferably in refugee resettlement or with the IRC’s Program for Initial Resettlement.
- Previous experience supervising case managers strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated skills and competencies:**

- Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of US Refugee Resettlement Programs.
- Demonstrated critical thinking and sound judgment: the ability to assess complex situations, interpret data, identify root causes, question assumptions, adapt guidance to local context, weigh trade-offs, and make well-reasoned recommendations and decisions, often with limited information and without on-site HQ oversight, escalating highly complex issues to the Senior Program Officer.

**Preferred experience and skills:**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, and an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; proven ability to prioritize and deliver on time.
- Strong critical thinking and analytic problem-solving skills, including the ability to question assumptions, adapt guidance to local context, and translate field observations into practical, evidence-based solutions.
- Resourcefulness and flexibility when working in different offices and communities.
- Ability to work both independently and in a dynamic, cross-functional team structure.
- Highly proficient in the Microsoft Office suite.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels.
- Familiarity with types of AI solutions for operational productivity and accuracy
- Ability to guide and coach others and work through change in a proactive and positive manner.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time at local sites to perform the responsibilities outlined above.
- Up to 50% domestic travel to IRC resettlement sites.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ***($80,000 - $85,000 - Annually).*** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
- Maintain accurate case notes and data entry in required systems; prepare employment vouchers and other documentation.
- Participate in program meetings, trainings, and professional development activities; follow all IRC policies including safeguarding and confidentiality standards.
- Perform other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, workforce development, or related field strongly preferred; equivalent work experience may be considered.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of case management, employment, job placement, or business experience in a social services setting.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).

title: Project Director
body:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

In Cambodia, GRC works with trade unions and civil society organisations to strengthen labour rights accountability in the garment and apparel sector. It supports garment workers and their representatives to document and monitor labour rights violations, and to use that evidence to secure remedy through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, and international accountability routes. Alongside monitoring, the project delivers awareness-raising, community building and tailored legal aid.

We are seeking a Project Director to join our team. The Project Director will lead the strategy and delivery of GRC’s worker-led monitoring and remedy programme in Cambodia’s garment sector and will be accountable for its quality and results. The role will shape and convene the programme’s multi-stakeholder platform, bringing together trade unions, civil society organisations, government, employers and international brands and make sure worker-generated evidence leads to remedy and to changes in sourcing practices. Alongside this, they will manage the in-country team, oversee partner relationships, budget and donor reporting and make sure the project is delivered safely for workers, partners and staff.

**Full / Part-time:** Full-time

**Location:** Remote (with regular travel to Cambodia)

**The Role**

- Develop and lead the strategy for the programme against its workplan and budget, adapting the approach as required.
- Represent GRC with government actors, including the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training, as well as suppliers, international brands and buyers, multi-stakeholder initiatives, donors and embassies.
- Lead cross-cutting work on responsible sourcing and labour rights, linking Cambodian evidence to brand due diligence and relevant regulation.
- Develop and facilitate workshops, multi-stakeholder events and training courses.
- Lead advocacy activities in-country, including launch events, roundtables and briefings.
- Set priorities for the team and make sure deliverables are completed on time and to a high standard.
- Oversee how documented cases are turned into remedy, whether through domestic mechanisms, supplier and brand engagement, or advocacy.
- Ensure the program complies with donor and GRC financial rules, working with GRC’s finance team.
- Lead the preparation of narrative reports, workplans and other donor deliverables.
- Build a robust understanding of the training needs, strategic plans and priorities of workers and workers' organisations.
- Lead the rollout of a bilingual documentation and monitoring tool in Cambodia with trade unions, CSOs and paralegals, including training, data quality and secure data handling.
- Provide leadership and support to the worker centres and worker monitors.
- Manage relationships with trade union and CSO partners, including any sub-grant or partnership agreements, capacity support and oversight.
- Mentor consultants and team members to help them perform to their full potential.
- Hold in-country responsibility for safeguarding, do-no-harm and security, including informed consent, protecting the identity of workers and union members, and reporting concerns under GRC policy.
- Monitor the political and civic space context, including retaliation risks to workers and unions, and maintain a project risk register and security plan.
- Make sure gender, including gender-based violence and harassment at work, is reflected in programme design and delivery.
- Identify opportunities for future work, collaboration, and funding in Cambodia and the region, consistent with GRC's strategic priorities.

**Your Background**

- 8+ years of experience in labour rights, business and human rights, or related legal practice.
- Qualified with a law degree, LLM or other postgraduate qualification in human rights, labour or international law, or equivalent is desirable.
- Practical experience addressing labour rights abuses in Cambodia, ideally in the garment and apparel sector.
- Knowledge of international labour standards and business and human rights frameworks and how they apply to the garment and apparel sector.
- Experience designing or convening multi-stakeholder processes involving unions, business and government, ideally in garment supply chains
- Practical experience working with trade unions, civil society organisations, businesses and government institutions on labour rights or corporate accountability.
- Experience engaging international brands and suppliers on labour rights, remediation and human rights due diligence.
- Experience developing programme or organisational strategy, including partnerships and funding models.
- A clear understanding of the risks facing workers and union representatives in Cambodia, and experience working safely and confidentially in a sensitive environment.
- Experience leading teams and managing donor-funded programs, including budget management.
- Experience designing and delivering training and workshops.
- Experience applying gender-responsive approaches, including on gender-based violence and harassment at work.
- Strategic and diplomatic, being able to hold the confidence of unions, brands and governments while keeping worker interests centred.
- Proactive and practical, anticipates problems, proposes solutions and can break a strategy down into workable steps.
- Flexible and willing to support deliverables beyond the core remit when needed.
- Well organised and able to manage competing urgent demands.
- Fluent in written and spoken English.
- Experience with worker-led monitoring, documentation or investigations, including handling sensitive data, is desirable.
- Experience coordinating multi-partner programmes, including indicator tracking and sub-grant management, is desirable.
- Experience engaging with international garment brands, suppliers and other business actors on labour rights violations, remediation and human rights due diligence is desirable.

title: Health Supply Chain Specialist
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**1. Job Overview**

The Health Supply Chain Specialist will provide integrated operational and technical leadership to strengthen supply chain performance across four critical health program areas, including but not limited to: Nutrition (with a focus on Ready-to-Use Food, or RUF), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH, covering Family Planning commodities and Postpartum Hemorrhage prevention and treatment supplies), Primary Healthcare (PHC, covering essential medicines and primary-level clinical supplies), and Infection and Disease Prevention and Control (IDPC). Focus will be on IRCs Impact at Scale ‘’go-big’’ designated country programs.

This is a project management and integration role embedded in Global Supply Chain (GSC), with a Management in Partnership (MIP) reporting line to Deputy Director, Health Unit (HU). The role translates health program priorities into optimized, scalable supply chain solutions, and directly advances the IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) objectives across all program areas.

Working in close collaboration with Country Programs, Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs), Global Procurement, Nutrition, SRH and IDPC Technical Leads, and external partners (including UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, other UN agencies and NGOs, and vendors), the Specialist will cover demand planning, forecasting, procurement coordination, and delivery across all four commodity areas, including essential medicines and IDPC commodities used in IRC health facilities and outbreak response. The role will also act as a key connector between field realities and global supply strategies — ensuring operational challenges are converted into actionable learning, system  
improvements, and scalable solutions.

**2. Key Responsibilities**

**2.1 Integrated Demand Planning and Forecasting**

- Develop and maintain a consolidated global demand plan covering RUF (Nutrition), IDPC and key SRH commodities (FP and PPH) for Go-big countries.
- Lead responses to specific commodity shortages and urgent projects across all countries.
- Analyze consumption data across programs (procured and Contribution in Kind -CIK) to inform forecasting and procurement decisions.
- Implement forecasts and supply chain plans for FY27 and FY28 for all Go-Big countries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.
- Regularly analyze and report on demand, stock, pipeline, and spend data at global and country levels, incorporating stockout data and mitigation actions.
- Proactively monitor global supply outlook for RUF, SRH and IDPC commodities and escalate alerts within program, supply chain and leadership.

**2.2 SRH Supply Chain Strategy and UNFPA Engagement**

- Lead scoping and stakeholder engagement to design and implement a UNFPA relationship strengthening strategy, including pre-positioning, CIK strengthening at global/country level, service and delivery improvements etc.
- Classify IRC country programs into operational SRHR supply chain profiles (e.g., PPH-focused, LARC-driven (long‑acting reversible contraception), UNFPA-dependent, emergency-only) to support differentiated supply chain strategies and prioritization.
- In alignment with country scale plans, support short-, medium-, and long-term improvement activities anchored to each country's operational profile and risk level.
- Engage with vendors like DKT, MSI, and other partners to leverage their in-country distribution networks and broad FP/PPH product portfolios.

**2.3 RUF SOP Implementation and Fraud Risk Management**

- Coordinate with Ethics and Risk and Compliance (R&C), and country focal points to strengthen fraud risk monitoring, incident review, and mitigation actions.
- Track RUF SOP adoption, compliance gaps, and corrective actions to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including travel to at least one country program.

**2.4 IDPC-Specific Supply Chain Strengthening**

- Assess the availability of key designated IDPC commodities and supply chain readiness against WHO IDPC minimum requirements at health facility level, and support country teams in developing corrective action plans.
- Support country programs in forecasting and pre-positioning key designated IDPC and essential medicine stocks for outbreak and epidemic preparedness and response.

**2.5 Supply Chain Strengthening and Capacity Building**

- Build country capacity, with a focus on pharmacists, in forecasting and demand planning, stock monitoring and stockout mitigation, and supply and sourcing strategies.
- Provide targeted technical support to address bottlenecks and operational challenges in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH programs.

**2.6 Stakeholder Engagement and External Representation**

- Cultivate strong relationships with UNFPA, UNICEF supply chain teams, WHO, DKT, MSI, and other key SRH, nutrition, and IDPC stakeholders.
- Represent IRC in relevant external supply chain and humanitarian coordination platforms, including the Global Health Cluster and IDPC technical working groups.
- Act as the global focal point for CIK deliveries in Nutrition, IDPC and SRH.

**2.7 Reporting, Data, and Knowledge Management**

- Document best practices and lessons learned to inform future improvements across all commodity areas.
- Produce a data-driven summary report linking supply levels to FY27 and FY28 I@S targets for Nutrition, IDPC and SRH Go-Big countries.
- Maintain an evidence repository (data, reports, learnings) for handover to Nutrition, SRH, IDPC and GSC teams.
- Lead the integration of Impact at Scale (I@S) priorities and core indicators into the Global Pharma Indicator (GPI) Dashboard, in collaboration with relevant I@S Leads, the Health Unit/Pharma Specialist, and Global Supply Chain teams. Ensure the dashboard tracks key pharmaceutical and nutrition supply chain performance indicators aligned with I@S objectives, enabling progress monitoring, gap identification, and evidence-based decision-making.

**3. Key Working Relationships**

**Reporting Line**

Position Reports to: Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain, with a Management in Partnership (MIP) line to the Deputy Director, Health Unit, and with strong technical engagement with the Global Practice Leads for Nutrition, SRH, Primary Healthcare (PHC), and Infection and Disease Prevention and Control (IDPC).

**Internal Relationships**

- Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs)
- Nutrition Technical Advisors, SRH specialists, and Health / PHC and IDPC Technical Advisors —
- Senior Pharmacy Specialist & Deputy Director for Pharma QA
- Country program teams and CP pharmacists —
- Global Procurement and Senior Procurement Manager for Health
- Risk & Compliance (R&C) and ECU
- Research and Nutrition/SRH/IDPC leads

**External Relationships**

- UNFPA, UNICEF, Hulo/EUHAB/Airlink, Vendors, WHO, INGOs,

**4. Job Requirements**

**Essential Qualifications**

- Degree in supply chain management, pharmacy, business administration, public health, nutrition, or related field — or equivalent additional experience.
- Minimum 4 years' experience in commodity procurement or supply chain management in humanitarian or development settings.
- Proven experience managing health commodities across at least two of the following areas: nutrition (therapeutic foods, RUF), SRH (FP, PPH supplies), primary healthcare (essential medicines), or infection and disease prevention and control.
- Demonstrated understanding of donor procurement regulations — particularly U.S. Department of State (formerly USAID/BHA), ECHO, FCDO, and UNFPA/UNICEF frameworks.
- Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills in supply chain optimization, forecasting, and risk mitigation.
- Familiarity with Nutrition supply chain challenges (RUTF/RUF, therapeutic food systems), SRH supply chain dynamics (FP method mix, PPH commodity management), primary healthcare essential medicines management, and IDPC commodity requirements.
- Experience with MEAL, ERPs, or Logistics Management Information Systems (LMIS); experience with Power BI or similar data visualization tools is an asset.
- Understanding of international freight (Incoterms), warehousing, transportation logistics, and last-mile delivery in humanitarian contexts.
- Knowledge of pharmaceutical management — vendor prequalification, quality assurance, cold chain, distribution, and pharmacovigilance — is an advantage.
- Exceptional interpersonal and stakeholder management skills; ability to engage credibly with country program staff, global leads, and external partners.

title: Development of Integrated M&E Data Management and Visualization System
body:
**Wildlife Conservation Society**

Term of Reference

Development of Integrated M&E Data Management and Visualization System

**Background**

The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a US non-profit established in 1895 that saves wildlife and wild places around the world. WCS runs four zoos and an aquarium in New York and has global conservation programs in more than 50 countries. WCS uses science to discover and understand the natural world. This knowledge helps us engage and inspire decision-makers, communities, and millions of supporters to take action with us to protect the wildlife and wild places we all care about.

In Africa, WCS operates in 13 counties and 15 protected or conserved areas. WCS Global Conservation Programs generate thus a large volume of heterogeneous data, including financial and human resources records, law enforcement and wildlife protection data, wildlife survey and ecological monitoring data, socio-economic surveys data, and spatial datasets.

WCS Africa Hub requires a robust, centralized, and automated system to manage its data for Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) purposes. Current processes rely on fragmented data sources, necessitating a unified platform that can translate raw data into actionable insights for performance and impact tracking.

**Objective of the consultancy**

The primary objective of this consultancy is to design, develop, and deploy across WCS landscapes in Africa an integrated data management and visualization system. This system will streamline the lifecycle of data—from ingestion and validation to spatial and statistical visualization.

**Scope of Work**

In strict collaboration with the Regional Technical Directors and other technical leads, the consultant will be responsible for the following key functional areas:

***A. Data Collation & Integration***

- **Multi-Source Ingestion:** Build connectors for spreadsheet-based data (Excel, CSV, Google Sheets), including developing application programming interfaces (API) depending on data source locations.
- **Geospatial Integration:** Ensure the system can ingest and process GIS files (Esri Shapefile, GeoJSON, GPX, GeoTIFF, etc.) to map impact, including processes for automated updated versions of key datasets as they are released (e.g.forest loss form Global Forest Watch).
- **Centralized Repository:** Establish a structured database to house historical and real-time MEL indicators and associated information. To maintain data integrity and institutional memory, the system must be governed by a rigorous data governance framework that incorporates standardized metadata (defining data lineage and ownership), a comprehensive indicator dictionary (providing clear definitions, calculation formulas, and units of measure), and robust version control to track all modifications to datasets and system configurations over time.
- **Offline Functionality:** The system must include features for offline data entry and local caching to ensure full functionality in low-bandwidth areas or sites with no internet connectivity, with automated synchronization once a connection is re-established.

***B. Validation & Processing***

- **Automated Quality Checks:** Implement scripts for data cleaning, identifying outliers, and ensuring consistency across reporting periods.
- **Transformation Logic:** Create workflows to process raw inputs into standardized performance and impact indicators, including geospatial processing.

***C. Dynamic Visualization & Dashboarding***

- **Interactive Dashboards:** Develop a user-friendly interface featuring charts, heatmaps, and trend lines.
- **Custom Aggregation:** Users must be able to filter and aggregate data dynamically by:
- **Variables:** Region, sector, demographic, project identity/ type, etc. Disaggregation variables are defined for each indicator.
- **Timeframes:** Monthly, quarterly, annual, or custom ranges.
- **Spatial Visualization:** Integrated maps that overlay MEL data onto geographic layers.

**Phased approach**

The work will be structured around a phased approach. The first phase will focus on developing and implementing the system architecture and processes required for site-specific M&E, with the aim of directly supporting adaptive management at the site level. The second phase will integrate thematic indicators across relevant programmatic areas, while the third phase will incorporate high-level, regional and Africa-wide indicators to enable regional aggregation, performance monitoring, and strategic decision-making.

**Technical Requirements**

The proposed system must adhere to the following:

- **Scalability:** Ability to handle increasing data volumes and new sites over time.
- **Interoperability:** Compatible with existing organizational software and databases.
- **Security:** Role-based access control to protect sensitive MEL data.
- **User Autonomy:** The system should allow non-technical staff to generate basic reports without coding.
- **Accountability and transparency:** The system must maintain a clear and navigable traceability chain (audit trail) that allows users to drill down from high-level dashboard indicators directly to the specific raw datasets and the document folders containing the original means of verification (MoV; e.g., reports, photos, participant lists, etc.).

**Deliverables**

- **Inception Phase:**
    - Deliverable: Technical Design Document
    - Description: System architecture, data flow diagrams (including offline sync logic), and UI/UX wireframes.
- **Development Phase:**
    - Deliverable: Beta Version (Prototype)
    - Description: Functional system with core data ingestion capabilities and basic dashboarding.
- **Testing Phase:**
    - Deliverable: Validation Report detailing
    - Description: Results of UAT (User Acceptance Testing), including connectivity stress tests and bug fixes.
- **Deployment Phase:**
    - Deliverable: Final System & Manuals
    - Description: Full rollout, including source code, admin manuals, and user guides.
- **Training Phase:**
    - Deliverable: Capacity building
    - Description: Training sessions for MEL staff and system administrators

**Consultant Qualifications and Experience**

The consultant should meet the following minimum requirements:

- Advanced degree in Information Systems, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field.
- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in data architecture and systems design.
- Proven track record in developing M&E systems specifically for international development or conservation organizations with impact tracking.
- Demonstrated experience in GIS integration and advanced data modeling from flat files (Excel/CSV).
- Evidence of ability to create dynamic, interactive dashboards with multi-variable filtering and time-series analyses for business intelligence.
- Strong communication skills and ability to translate technical concepts into practical guidance.

**Application and Selection Criteria**

Interested candidates are requested to submit:

- A technical proposal outlining understanding of the assignment and proposed approach, including relevant examples of similar assignments (80%)
- A financial proposal (20%)
- Qualifications and CVs of key personnel (Lead Architect, GIS Specialist, and Data Analyst).

A detailed workplan, timeline, and deliverable schedule will be agreed at contract inception.

WCS reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal and is not bound to select the lowest-cost offer.

title: Head of Support Services
body:
**Overall purpose of the role**: The HoSS ensures effective, efficient Finance, Administration, HR, IT and Supply Chain services across Syria, complying with DRC procedures and guidelines. As a Senior Management Team (SMT) member, the HoSS oversees programme support and timely achievement of annual support-function performance indicators, develops and implements country strategies, and improves operational systems, processes and policies supporting DRC’s mission. The role helps assess and implement global and regional organizational development and financial accountability initiatives. The HoSS ensures timely, appropriate communication with the Head of Program and support departments on finance, administration, supply chain and HR matters, proactively resolving differences and prioritizing time-sensitive tasks.

**Responsibilities**:

The key responsibilities outlined below are not exhaustive; additional duties, including ad hoc tasks, may be assigned to support the effective fulfillment of the role’s overall purpose.

## **Management**

- Lead and manage the Support service teams Managers and technically manage area support services teams (including people planning, performance, well-being and staff development).
- Manage, deliver and report on current operations programme support in geographic scope.
- Establish high performing support teams ensuring high-quality approaches are maintained.
- Develop and improve operational approaches, compliance, and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations.
- Ensure support for annual planning and review processes.

## **Operational Management**

- Oversee the operational support units for the country by providing strategic leadership and technical support to the areas under his/her supervision.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and transport systems.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation through frequent in-service training sessions and mentoring support.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives.
- Decentralization of support services functions and empowering area support teams to enhance the efficiency of support functions in country and area offices.

## **Workforce Planning and Operational Transitions**

- Lead workforce planning with Programme, HR, Finance and Area teams, forecasting staffing needs and costs against humanitarian priorities, funding scenarios and operational requirements.
- Develop and update country and field office organigrams, ensuring clear reporting lines, appropriate staffing structures and alignment with approved budgets.
- Coordinate support services readiness for operational scale-up and scale-down, including recruitment, redeployment and responsible staffing transitions, in line with DRC policies and applicable labour requirements.
- Lead coordinated support planning for new office setups, relocations and closures, covering staffing, budgets, premises, logistics, IT and administrative requirements to maintain operational continuity.

## **Strengthening Localization**

- Coordinate support services due diligence for new local implementing partners, assessing financial management, procurement, HR and internal control systems, and ensuring identified risks and capacity gaps are addressed before partnership approval.
- Oversee the timely review and verification of local implementing partners’ financial and support services reports, monitoring expenditure, supporting documentation and compliance with partnership agreements and donor requirements, and ensuring follow-up on discrepancies and corrective actions.
- Lead support services capacity building for local implementing partners through joint capacity assessments, tailored development plans, training and mentoring, strengthening systems, internal controls and reporting quality.
- Promote and develop a phased nationalization plan for the Syria operation with the Country Director, HR and relevant technical leads, incorporating succession planning, staff development, knowledge transfer and clear milestones while maintaining operational continuity and transparent, merit-based processes.

## **Policies and SOPs Development and Rollout**

- Lead the development, contextualization and regular review of support services policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs), ensuring alignment with DRC frameworks, donor requirements, applicable legislation and humanitarian operational needs.
- Coordinate updates with relevant technical leads, Programme and Area teams, securing required approvals and maintaining clear responsibilities, version control and accessible guidance.
- Oversee rollout across country and field offices through clear communication, staff briefings, training and practical tools to support consistent implementation.
- Monitor implementation and compliance, address gaps and incorporate staff feedback, audit findings and changes in the operating context into timely policy and SOP revisions.

## **Budget Management**

- Ensure that the Country Master Budget is updated on a regular basis and is used to adequately prepare project proposals or cost cutting measures.
- Ensure the timely completion of monthly budget follow-up meetings, financial reports and month-end closing processes, maintaining data accuracy and integrity.
- Develop country office support services budget including staff costs for all donor project proposals and track spending on regular basis to ensure budget is used according to plan.
- Implement Core cost project and other global initiatives related to Budgeting.

## **Risk Management**

- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team (SMT) in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit respectively.
- Supervise audits, controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area.
- Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Develop a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy. Support Senior Management to ensure risk register is up to date and action plans are implemented accordingly.
- Participate in audit kick-off and exit meetings and ensure cooperation at all time during every audit field works. Lead on providing management response on each audit report.

## **DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff.
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance.
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities.

## **Experience and technical competencies:**

- At least 10 years' management experience in relevant field.
- At least 5 years’ experience in playing similar role, preferably in an international NGO.
- Previous experience as Country Senior Management is essential.
- Previous experience of working in the Middle East and/or a fast-paced conflict setting is preferred.
- Proven leadership skills and competence in people management
- Proven operational experience in one or more of the following thematic areas: financial, supply chain, human resources, and information management.
- Proven experience managing the scale-up and scale-down of humanitarian operations in response to changing needs and funding levels.
- Experience working in an ERP system, including supply chain, finance, and HR systems.

## **Education:**

Master’s degree in finance, HR, Economics, business administration or related field.

## **Languages:**

- Fluency in written and spoken English required.
- Arabic language skills would be an advantage.

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:*

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with our vision and values.

**We offer:**

- **Contract Length**: 1 year (Renewable, based on performance and fund availability).
- **Salary Level**: Management – E level 1 (Based on DRC's salary scale)
- **Location**: Syria, Damascus.
- **Expected Start date**: January or February 2027

title: Request for Expression of Interest: Numeracy and Learning Institution or Organisation
body:
**Program Background**

**Education Quality for Inclusive Prosperity (EQUIP)**

The Education Quality for Inclusive Prosperity (EQUIP) is a critical component of Australia’s strategic partnership with the Philippines. It builds on over 30 years of investment by the Government of Australia into the Philippines’ education sector and supports the Philippine government’s commitment to improve the global competitiveness of the Philippine education and labour market. EQUIP reflects the collective interest of Australia and the Philippines to foster a robust and adaptive education system where learners and graduates can thrive in an increasingly digitalised economy.

EQUIP aims to support the Philippines’ inclusive economic growth ambitions by ensuring the labour force is well equipped with skills relevant to meet the needs of the country’s rapidly transforming economy. EQUIP aims to promote skills development in senior high school and enable a smooth transition to the labour force, whether immediately upon leaving school or after further education. It will also support Philippine Government agencies improve its policies and practices to support relevant skills pathways for senior secondary school learners.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**  
At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [DT Global](https://dt-global.com/)

**Background**

A significant proportion of learners in Grades 9–12 continue to experience difficulties in meeting expected proficiency levels in numeracy. Gaps in foundational and functional numeracy can affect learners’ ability to engage successfully with the secondary curriculum, apply mathematical concepts in real-world situations, and transition effectively to higher education, technical and vocational training, and employment.

Strengthening numeracy at the secondary level is therefore critical not only to improving academic achievement, but also to developing learners’ capacity to solve problems, interpret and use information, make informed decisions, manage every day and workplace situations, and participate meaningfully in further education, training, employment, and lifelong learning.

In response to this need, the EQUIP Program seeks to strengthen the foundational and 21st century skills of learners in Grades 9–12 through evidence-based, learner-centred, and context-responsive approaches. EQUIP is therefore seeking an experienced Philippine-based institution/organisation with demonstrated expertise in numeracy education, mathematics education, curriculum development, teacher professional development, and school-based instructional support to provide technical assistance in the design, development, and implementation of numeracy interventions in selected EQUIP pilot schools.

  
**Objective of the Engagement**

The overall objective of the consultancy is to support EQUIP in designing and implementing an evidence-based Numeracy Skills Development Package for Grades 9–12, with emphasis on strengthening functional numeracy, improving classroom practice, and building the capacity of teachers and schools to identify and address learner numeracy needs.

Specifically, the institutional partner will:  
• strengthen teachers’ knowledge and pedagogical practices for teaching and developing numeracy across learning areas;  
• support schools in using available learner assessment data to identify numeracy needs and target appropriate interventions;  
• develop practical, differentiated, and context-responsive numeracy intervention resources for Grades 9–12 learners;  
• promote the integration and application of numeracy in authentic academic, everyday-life, and workplace contexts;  
• provide school-based technical assistance, coaching, and implementation support; and  
• contribute to the generation of evidence and lessons to inform refinement, replication, and potential scale-up of effective numeracy interventions.

title: TO PROVIDE PSYCHOSOCIAL SERVICES TO HUMANITY & INCLUSION (HI) STAFF IN KENYA
body:
**CONTEXT**  
Handicap International Federation (HI), operating as Humanity & Inclusion, is an international organisation working alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations. In Kenya, HI operates from Nairobi and from field locations including Kakuma and Dadaab, where staff often work in demanding, remote and humanitarian settings that expose them to stress, critical incidents and workplace hazards.  
HI Kenya recognises that the mental health and wellbeing of its staff are central to delivering quality programmes and to caring for its people. Staff working in humanitarian and field settings may be exposed to prolonged stress, burnout and distressing events, and need access to professional, confidential support.  
To support this, HI is seeking a qualified service provider to offer psychosocial services for HI staff in Kenya

**DESCRIPTION OF THE EXPECTED SERVICE**  
The contracted service provider is to provide the following services: -  
**Specific objectives of the assignment**  
• To provide confidential, professional and accessible psychosocial support services that promote the mental health and wellbeing of HI staff in Kenya.  
• To provide timely psychological support to individuals and teams affected by critical incidents.  
• To strengthen the capacity of managers and Human Resources staff to recognize distress and support staff wellbeing.  
**Responsibilities and Tasks**  
The service provider will carry out the following activities: -  
a) Individual and Group Support  
• Provide confidential individual counselling sessions, delivered in person or virtually, by qualified and licensed counsellors or psychologists, with the number of sessions per staff member to be agreed with HI.  
• Facilitate group sessions and workshops on stress and burnout management, resilience, self-care and work-life balance.  
• Refer staff requiring specialised psychiatric or medical care to appropriate providers, with  
the staff member’s consent.  
b) Critical Incident Response  
• Provide psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing for individuals and teams following distressing events, such as accidents, security incidents or the loss of a colleague, within an agreed response time.  
• Provide a mechanism for urgent support outside normal working hours, such as an on-call counsellor or helpline.  
c) Manager and Human Resources Support • Orient managers and Human Resources staff on recognising signs of distress, supportive supervision and referral pathways.  
• Advise HI on staff wellbeing initiatives based on anonymised trends.  
d) Confidentiality and Inclusion  
• Ensure strict confidentiality and safe handling of records in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and professional codes of ethics. HI will not have access to individual counselling content.  
• Ensure services are inclusive and accessible, including for staff with disabilities, culturally sensitive, and available in English and Kiswahili.

**Scope and Target**  
The assignment covers HI Kenya staff based in Nairobi and in the field locations of Kakuma and Dadaab. The estimated number of staff eligible for the service is 59  
The scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:  
• Providing individual and group psychosocial support to HI staff throughout the contract period.  
• Providing psychological first aid and critical incident debriefing when required.  
• Providing urgent support outside normal working hours.  
• Referring staff to specialised care where needed.  
• Orienting managers and Human Resources staff on supporting staff wellbeing.  
• Preparing and submitting the reports and deliverables listed in this TOR.

**Profile of the service provider**  
The service provider will need to have the following capacities:  
• Registered business entity in Kenya with a proven track record of providing psychosocial or counselling services to organisations. Experience with NGOs or humanitarian organisations is an added advantage.  
• Counsellors and psychologists must be licensed by the Counsellors and Psychologists Board of Kenya, with experience in trauma, stress and burnout management and critical incident debriefing.  
• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and protect client data in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019.  
• Ability to deliver services in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab (in person or virtually), in English and Kiswahili.  
• Experience in or commitment to disability inclusion is an added advantage.

Duration and Place of Performance of the Service  
The contract will be for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of signing, renewable subject to satisfactory performance. Psychosocial services will be available throughout the contract period. The service shall be carried out in Nairobi, Kakuma and Dadaab, with virtual counselling options where appropriate.  
**Work Plan**  
Based on the proposed assignment, the timeline shall be agreed upon by the service provider and HI. The service provider shall submit a service delivery plan within one (1) week of signing the contract.

**Report**  
The service provider shall provide the following deliverables:-  
• Psychosocial service delivery plan  
• Quarterly psychosocial service report, with anonymised utilisation data, key themes and recommendations  
• Summary report (without identifying details) for each critical incident response  
• Final end-of-assignment report  
All reports shall be submitted in both editable electronic format and PDF format. Reports shall not contain information that identifies individual staff members.  
**Contact Person**  
During the performance of the service, the service provider will be assisted by the Human Resources Officer – Kenya in coordinating schedules and logistics with the field offices.  
**Appendices**  
Willingness to adhere to Handicap International's Federation institutional policies (Prevention and fight against corruption, Child Protection, Protection of Beneficiaries against sexual abuse and harassment). Available on the website: [https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.](https://hi.org/en/institutional-policies.)

**Evaluation**  
Application documents submitted will be evaluated in three (stages);  
**General Mandatory Evaluation Criteria**  
**For firms or institutions**

-Certificate of Registration  
-Trade license Certificate/ Business Permit  
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate  
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate  
-Personal Accident Insurance cover  
-Valid practising licences of the proposed counsellors and psychologists (Counsellors and Psychologists Board)

**For Individuals**

-National ID  
-Relevant certifications, professional licences and accreditations  
-PIN/VAT Registration Certificate  
-Current Tax Compliance Certificate  
-Personal Accident insurance cover

**Technical Capacity Evaluation**  
**(a) Profile and experience of the service provider:**

- The firm should have proven expertise and experience in providing psychosocial services. Attach three reference letters.
- Provide a list of assignments of similar scope of work undertaken within the last 2 years, along with names of clients (including contact person, email contacts, postal address and telephone numbers – this must include the three referees provided above)
    
    **(b)Professional/technical capacity/ capability:**
- The proposed counsellors and psychologists should have relevant experience and professional qualifications in the relevant field.
- The proposal should describe the proposed approach to service delivery and the measures to ensure confidentiality and protection of staff data.
    
    **Financial Evaluation**  
    \- At the Financial stage, the Lowest Competitive Evaluated bidder and within budget estimates will be considered for the award of the contract.
    
    **NB: Your Financial proposal should Include flights, meals, accomodation,communication and any other contigency / miscelleneous costs for Kakuma ,Dadaab and Nairobi.**

title: Technical Advisor MHPSS Services
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 15 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors.

The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Technical Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting partner organizations to provide MHPSS services for specific target groups as well as for the scientific accompaniment of those services and the dissemination of the findings to promote the application of effective approaches. You will be working on these tasks in close collaboration with another colleague in a project team of overall 8 staff.

**Your tasks**

- Identifying and contracting suitable MHPSS-partner organizations that work with the project’s target groups
- Technically and administratively accompanying and supporting the partner organizations in their planning and implementation of these services; identifying and addressing capacity development needs of the partner organization, if any
- Technically and administratively accompanying and supporting the research teams who are documenting and systematically evaluating the MHPSS-services offered
- Ensuring the quality of the research papers/ research briefs prepared by the research teams and supporting the dissemination of the findings, e.g. through presentations
- Coordinating between different service offers and research teams
- Where suitable, bringing in expertise and ideas into the other work streams of the project (mentioned above), which will be mainly covered by your colleagues
- Supporting with team-internal tasks, including monitoring and evaluation, reporting, preparation of team workshops etc.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- A completed post-graduate degree in mental health, clinical or general psychology, psychological counselling, psychiatry or a related field
- At least 4 years of professional experience in MHPSS in the humanitarian or development sector, preferably in the Middle East, particularly in/ for Syria
- Proven experience with and openness for non-traditional MHPSS-interventions, for example arts-based or sports-based interventions
- Proven experience with scientific work and methods combined with strong analytical thinking
- Experience with project and process management
- A good overview of the MHPSS-actor landscape in Syria (particularly civil society)
- Strong team work and communication skills
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- High degree of initiative
- Structured and meticulous working methods – even under time pressure
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is a strong asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

- A high degree of understanding of the cross-sectoral nature of MHPSS, its interactions and relevance for other sectors such as peacebuilding, transitional justice, education and disaster management and how to work in an MHPSS-informed way
- Experience in working on the development or revision of academic curricula and/ or experience with giving trainings in the field of MHPSS in a practice-oriented way
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria, particularly in its cross-sectoral nature
- Strong perspective-taking
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- Experience with clinical supervision is an asset
- An existing network of actors in Syria particularly in the fields of peacebuilding, transitional justice, education or disaster management is an asset
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is an asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

title: MHPSS Implementation Manager
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organisations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopened its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 15 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors.

The project “Strengthening the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) System in Syria” is due to start on 1. December 2026 for a duration of 3 years. Given the continued high demand for MHPSS services across Syria, the aim of the project is to strengthen the Syrian MHPSS system by

- supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and uniform quality standards for MHPSS services
- developing practice-oriented training and continuing professional development programs for MHPSS professionals and ensuring these are permanently established in local training institutions
- supporting partner organizations in offering MHPSS services for particularly distressed population groups, including survivors of torture, some of them through non-traditional (e.g. creative) interventions
- working with researchers to scientifically accompany and evaluate the MHPSS-services offered through the project and preparing the findings for professionals, thereby expanding target-group-specific knowledge and promoting the application of effective approaches
- training and advising professionals from the fields of education, peacebuilding, transitional justice and disaster risk management on how to work in an MHPSS-informed manner with people affected by crises and conflicts.

In this position as MHPSS Implementation Manager, you will have both managerial and technical tasks and will be overall responsible for the project’s implementation and its work packages as mentioned above. In addition, you will be supporting the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and standards for MHPSS-services in tandem with two other colleagues. You will be reporting to the head of project who is at the same time leading another GIZ project in the health sector.

**Your tasks**

- Overseeing and coordinating the project’s implementation across all abovementioned work packages
- Managing the MHPSS project team consisting of 5 national and 1 international MHPSS technical advisors.
- Technically supporting staff in their work regarding the abovementioned work packages
- Functioning as liaison person with governmental entities in Syria, particularly the Directorate for Mental Health within the Ministry of Health, the Council for Mental Health and Addiction, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management and the National Commission for Missing Persons
- Supporting governmental entities in strengthening MHPSS-systems and structures, including through the development of national strategies, regulatory frameworks and quality standards on MHPSS. This comprises for example providing continuous technical and process-oriented advisory services, capacity development measures, facilitating the coordination between different institutions, giving technical inputs etc.
- Representing the project towards actors in Syria

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- A completed post-graduate degree in mental health, clinical or general psychology, psychological counselling, psychiatry or a related field
- At least 3 years of experience in managing a team
- At least 7 years of professional experience in MHPSS, preferably in the Middle East, particularly in/ for Syria
- Experience in interacting with government stakeholders, particularly regarding the development of MHPSS strategies and standards
- Experience with strengthening national or sub-national MHPSS-systems and structures
- A high degree of understanding of the Syrian MHPSS system (governmental, civil society, and academic)
- Knowledge in the areas of peacebuilding, social cohesion, transitional justice and their interactions with the field of MHPSS
- A high ability to maintain an overview of encompassing projects and coordinate them, also under pressure, as well as good judgement and decision-making
- Strong teamwork skills
- High cultural-, context- and gender-sensitivity as well as sensitivity to inclusion issues
- High intercultural competence and diplomatic skills
- A high motivation to contribute to strengthening the MHPSS system in Syria
- Resilience and frustration tolerance
- Business fluency in Arabic and English
- An existing network of MHPSS actors (preferably governmental, civil society, and academic) in Syria is an asset
- Knowledge of and experience with GIZ procedures and policies is an asset
- Basic knowledge of German is an asset

title: UNE OU UN CONTROLEUR DE GESTION - FRANCE
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. Action contre la Faim focuses its actions on 7 main areas of expertise: Nutrition and Health - Mental Health, Psychosocial Support - Food Security and Livelihoods - Water, Sanitation and Hygiene - Advocacy - Climate - Research. In 2024, Action contre la Faim provided aid to more than 26 million people in 57 countries worldwide. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Responsable du Service Contrôle de Gestion, votre mission sera d'assurer la gestion budgétaire, le suivi des couts du siège et garantir le respect du cadre de gestion sur son périmètre. Accompagner les managers dans le suivi budgétaire de leur l'activité.

 Vous êtes titulaire d'une formation supérieure en gestion financière, et vous avez au moins 3 ans d'expérience en Contrôle de Gestion.

Une bonne maitrise de la Business Intelligence est un plus.  
Vous avez un niveau Excel avancé.

Travaillant dans un environnement international, vous maîtrisez l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.
