body:
**Lieu d’affectation :** Bureau National, N’Djamena, avec des missions régulières dans les bases terrain (environ 20 % du temps)  
**Rattachement hiérarchique :** Directeur National  
**Date de prise de poste :** début janvier 2027  
**Durée de l’engagement :** 1 an, renouvelable sous réserve de la disponibilité des financements et d’une performance satisfaisante

**À propos du JRS**

Le Service Jésuite des Réfugiés (JRS) est une organisation catholique internationale et une œuvre de la Compagnie de Jésus. Fondé en 1980, il accompagne, sert et défend les droits des réfugiés et des personnes déplacées de force dans plus de 50 pays.

Le JRS est présent au Tchad depuis 2006. Il y mène des programmes d’éducation, de protection de l’enfance, de cohésion sociale et de moyens de subsistance dans plusieurs régions qui accueillent des réfugiés.

**Objectif du poste**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) National(e) des Finances est responsable de la gestion budgétaire, financière, comptable et de trésorerie de JRS Tchad et de tous ses projets. Il/elle dirige le département Finances. Il/elle fait respecter les procédures internes et les exigences des bailleurs. Il/elle supervise l’Associé(e) Finances (Comptable) et l’Associé(e) Budget et Reporting.

**Relations de travail**

- *En interne :* le Directeur National ; l’équipe Finances du Bureau National et des bases ; les Directeurs et Chefs de projet ; les responsables Programmes, Logistique et RH.
- *En externe :* les bailleurs de fonds (UNHCR, UE, BPRM, etc.) ; l’administration fiscale, les banques et les institutions financières ; les auditeurs internes et externes ; les prestataires.

**Responsabilités principales**

*1. Pilotage stratégique, budget et management du département*

- Suivre et analyser la performance financière de JRS Tchad, et conseiller le Directeur National sur les choix stratégiques.
- Conduire la planification financière, préparer le budget annuel et répartir les ressources selon les exigences des subventions.
- Encadrer directement l’Associé(e) Finances et l’Associé(e) Budget et Reporting, et assurer le leadership technique de toute la filière Finances, y compris dans les bases.
- Renforcer le contrôle interne et suivre la mise en œuvre des recommandations d’audit.

*2. Comptabilité, trésorerie et conformité des subventions*

- Mettre en place des contrôles financiers internes solides et une méthode comptable rigoureuse, et respecter les délais de reporting.
- Gérer la trésorerie et suivre les soldes des projets pour éviter tout dépassement budgétaire.
- Veiller au respect permanent des exigences réglementaires, contractuelles, juridiques et financières des bailleurs.
- Garantir le bon paramétrage et la cohérence de la comptabilité dans le logiciel de gestion (Navision/ Business Central).

*3. Audits, reporting et coordination externe*

- Coordonner la préparation des audits annuels, internes et externes.
- Valider les rapports financiers internes et les rapports aux bailleurs.
- Préparer et réviser régulièrement les états financiers et les prévisions de recettes et de dépenses.
- Représenter le JRS dans les réunions sectorielles et inter-agences, et auprès des autorités financières.

**Profil recherché**

*Formation et expérience*

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+4/5 en comptabilité, finance, gestion ou administration des affaires. Une certification professionnelle (ACCA, CPA, DSCG ou équivalent) est un atout.
- Au moins 7 ans d’expérience en gestion financière dans le secteur humanitaire, dont au moins 3 ans à un poste de management dans l’humanitaire.

*Compétences techniques*

- Expertise en gestion financière, contrôle budgétaire et analyse financière en contexte humanitaire.
- Très bonne connaissance des procédures et exigences des bailleurs institutionnels (UNHCR, UE, BPRM, etc.).
- Maîtrise des logiciels comptables ERP (Navision/ Business Central, Sage) et d’Excel à un niveau avancé.
- Expérience confirmée en audit, contrôle interne et gestion des risques financiers.

*Langues*

- Maîtrise parfaite du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. Une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais est fortement souhaitée.

*Qualités personnelles*

- Adhésion aux valeurs du JRS et au Code de conduite.
- Leadership, vision stratégique et sens des responsabilités.
- Intégrité irréprochable, sens de l’éthique et respect de la confidentialité.
- Capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et de négociation.
- Résilience et bonne résistance au stress.

**Ce que nous offrons**

Le poste s’accompagne d’un ensemble d’avantages adaptés à une mission en contexte humanitaire :

- **Indemnité mensuelle :** un montant attractif, au niveau des standards des ONG internationales au Tchad.
- **Logement :** une **aide mensuelle au logement d’environ 990 € (650 000 FCFA)**, versée en plus de l’indemnité mensuelle.
- **Couverture santé internationale :** une assurance médicale avec **évacuation et rapatriement sanitaires**, prise en charge par le JRS.
- **Voyages pris en charge :** billet aller-retour entre votre pays d’origine et N’Djamena, au début et à la fin de l’affectation. Les missions de terrain (visa, transport, repas, hébergement) sont aussi couvertes.
- **Repos et récupération (R&R) :** une semaine de R&R après **3 mois de service**.
- **Congés annuels :** **24 jours par an** (2 jours par mois de service effectif), plus des jours de voyage.
- **Autres congés :** 5 jours ouvrables de congé pour raisons familiales et jusqu’à 3 jours par an pour une retraite spirituelle.
- **Accompagnement :** soutien régulier de la Direction Nationale et du Bureau Régional, et formations internes.
- **Une mission qui a du sens :** vous rejoignez une organisation présente dans plus de 50 pays, au service direct des réfugiés au Tchad.

**Engagement du JRS**

Le JRS applique une politique de tolérance zéro envers toute forme d’exploitation, d’abus ou de harcèlement, notamment sexuels. Avant tout engagement, les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s feront l’objet de vérifications préalables : références professionnelles, identité, diplômes et antécédents. Ils/elles devront signer le Code de conduite et les politiques de safeguarding du JRS (PHEAS, protection de l’enfance). **Les candidatures féminines sont vivement encouragées.**

title: Officer, Prospect Research & Management
Country Head of Programmes Tanzania
body:
**Position**:Country Head of Programmes Tanzania

**Reporting to**: Country Representative

**Collaborating with**: Head of Departments and Project Managers

**Location:** Dar es Salaam, with frequent field visits

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline:** 08/12/2026

**Family Duty Station**: YES

**R&R**: NO

**Contract Type**: Expatriate (International)

**Working Context**

Since 2010, WeWorld has maintained a strong operational presence in Tanzania, implementing multisectoral, school-centredprogrammes in Dar es Salaam and Ludewa District, reaching nearly 25,000 beneficiaries, primarily children, adolescents, parents, and school personnel. These interventions integrate education, health, nutrition, child protection, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalised children, including children with disabilities. Through an integrated, community-based approach, WeWorld seeks to improve children's access to quality education, enhance their wellbeing and protection, and strengthen the capacity of families, schools, and community care systems to respond to their needs.

WeWorld works in close collaboration with local civil society organisations, government authorities, and other development stakeholders to promote sustainable, locally owned solutions. As an active member of the Tanzania Education Network (TENMET), the organisation contributes to national efforts to advance inclusive and equitable quality education in line with the Education for All agenda. Between 2017 and 2022, WeWorld also supported the Bunju Multipurpose Centre in Dar es Salaam, providing integrated psychosocial, legal, medical, educational, and vocational support to vulnerable children and young people, alongside family reintegration services.

Building on its longstanding engagement in education and child protection, WeWorld has progressively expanded its programmatic portfolio to encompass civil society strengthening, human rights, peacebuilding, youth empowerment, and environmental sustainability. Between 2020 and 2022, the organisation implemented the European Union-funded SautiMpya project in Kigoma, Mbeya, and Mtwara regions, strengthening partnerships between civil society organisations and media actors to advance the rights and participation of women and young people.

WeWorld is currently implementing a diversified portfolio of programmes supported by the European Union and other institutional donors. These include Kijani Pemba, which promotes urban eco-resilience and environmental sustainability in Zanzibar; Kujenga Amani Pamoja, a regional initiative advancing peacebuilding and meaningful youth engagement across Kenya, Mozambique, and Tanzania; and Pamoja Tudumishe Elimu, a cross-border Kenya–Tanzania programme supporting the retention, participation, and access of vulnerable learners to quality primary education.

As WeWorld Tanzania continues to consolidate its operational presence and strengthen its programmatic portfolio, the organisation is prioritising enhanced programme quality, strategic coherence, operational effectiveness, and sustainable resource mobilisation. This requires stronger integration across projects and thematic areas, more effective programme oversight and accountability, and increased investment in national staff leadership, institutional partnerships, and country-level programme development.

**Purpose of the Role**

Under the direct supervision of the Country Representative, the Country Head of Programmes provides strategic, technical and operational leadership for WeWorld Tanzania’s programme portfolio, ensuring quality, accountability, donor compliance and effective programme implementation.

He/She leads programme development and resource mobilisation, contributing to the country strategy, identifying funding opportunities, strengthening donor and partner engagement, and overseeing the development of proposals.

The Country Head of Programmes leads and supports programme teams, strengthens national staff capacity, ensures effective coordination with support functions, and contributes to WeWorld’s institutional representation and strategic partnerships with government, donors, civil society and implementing partners.

**Main Functions and Duties**

**1. Programme and Quality Management**

- Provide leadership and oversight to ensure high-quality implementation of all programmes in line with WeWorld’s strategy and contextual needs
- Supervise and support Project Managers, Grants and Programme Advisors, and technical staff in planning, monitoring, and reporting of activities and results
- Ensure programme implementation complies with internal policies, donor regulations, national legislation, and international standards
- Coordinate with the Head of Support Services and Country Representative to oversee the financial management of the country programme portfolio
- Ensure timely and quality preparation of internal and external reports, donor submissions, briefing notes, and other reporting requirements
- Lead coordination and integration across programme sectors (e.g., education, protection, livelihoods, basic assistance, civil society)
- Lead the integration of cross-cutting themes such as gender, inclusion, climate resilience, and accountability
- Directly manage or support project implementation in the absence of a dedicated Project Manager, based on needs and guidance from the Country Representative
- Facilitate harmonization of tools, methodologies, procedures, and guidelines across projects
- Ensure quality criteria and indicators are monitored and used for evidence-based decision-making

**2. Strategic Planning and Fundraising**

- Collaborate with the Country Representative to define and implement the long-term country strategy
- Identify and assess programming and funding opportunities aligned with country priorities and WeWorld’s global strategy
- Lead and coordinate proposal development, engaging technical and support teams, and liaising with HQ technical coordinators and the regional unit
- Ensure proposals are competitive, technically sound, and responsive to donor requirements and contextual realities
- Promote synergies between humanitarian response and development programmes

**3. Representation and Institutional Relations**

- Represent WeWorld in strategic fora, donor meetings, technical working groups, cluster coordination mechanisms, and consortia
- Build and maintain relationships with institutional donors, UN agencies, INGOs, national and local authorities, and civil society actors
- Provide strategic input into communication and visibility activities, including documentation, lessons learned, and programme capitalization

**4. HR Management and Capacity Building**

- Line manageprogramme and technical staff, ensuring performance objectives are set and regularly reviewed
- Promote a supportive environment that encourages accountability, learning, and professional growth
- Identify capacity-building needs and coordinate appropriate training for programme teams
- Foster transparent, inclusive, and equitable recruitment and staff management in accordance with WeWorld policies and national labor laws
- Ensure strong internal communication and collaboration across departments (e.g., MEAL, Admin, Logistics, HR)
- Promote staff well-being and uphold WeWorld’s values and standards of conduct, emphasizing diversity and inclusion

**5. MEAL and Accountability**

- Oversee the design and implementation of MEAL systems across all projects
- Ensure monitoring tools are in place and data is used to inform programme planning and decision-making
- Coordinate with the MEAL Officer/Manager to support evaluations, learning, accountability mechanisms, and quality reporting

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in the field of Social or Political Science, Development Studies, Economics, International relations, Project Management, Agronomy, Business development.
- Knowledge of main donors’ policies and procedures (EU, UN Agencies, Italian Cooperation, ECHO)
- Fluent in written and spoken English
- Good computer skills, in particular MS Office package

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of relevant working experience in humanitarian or development settings
- At least 4 years of experience in Project Cycle Management
- Proven experience in project proposal writing

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong interpersonal relationships and good communication and leadership skills
- Ability to perform under stress conditions
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problem prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Integrity in line with the Humanitarian Principles and ethical standards
- Cultural, gender, religionsensitivity and adaptability

**DESIRABLE REQUIREMENTS**

- Previous experience in Tanzania and East Africa
- Previous experience in Development and Emergency programmes
- Knowledge of the Swahili language

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) months contract subject to verification (achievement of specific objectives); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first period of collaboration and depending on available funding.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy

Base Salary (3.190€ - 3.790€ monthly)+ Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Annual leave**: 2,5 days/month (working days).

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station).

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family Duty Station**: YES

**R&R**: NO

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

title: Regional Communications Officer – Central America Region
body:
**The Regional Communications Officer** is an execution-focused regional role responsible for translating the global communications and brand framework into high-quality communications products, content, storytelling, digital outputs and country-level communications support across Central America (El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras). The position coordinates regional communications delivery, production planning and operational requirements, while implementing the regional communications strategy established by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications. Indicative balance of time: 45% producing materials and content · 35% planning, coordination and managing demand across the three countries · 20% supporting country offices.

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Graphic Design, or a related field.
- At least three years of professional experience in communications or content production, preferably in the humanitarian or international development sector.
- Demonstrated anticipation: evidence of having identified what an organization would need and prepared for it before being asked. Candidates will be asked to demonstrate this during the selection process.
- Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite; Illustrator, InDesign and Photoshop, with a working command of output specifications for print and digital. Premiere Pro or equivalent for basic video editing. Canva is not a substitute.
- Practical field photography and video capture: interview framing, lavalier and directional audio, stabilization, exposure control and use of filters.
- Experience planning production against supplier lead times and working with procurement processes.
- Experience operating organizational social media accounts and reporting on engagement.
- Working proficiency in Spanish and English, written and spoken.
- Competence with collaborative planning tools; experience with Monday.com or equivalent is an advantage.
- Right to work in Guatemala, and able to attend the country office on a hybrid basis in line with regional policy.
- Experience driving standard 4WD vehicles in rough terrain. Valid driver's license.
- Ability to project and maintain a calm work environment while operating in a time and
- deadline-defined environment required by internal and external clients.
- Excellent interpersonal, relational, and communication skills, with a history of inspiring collaboration across multiple functions.
- Possessing a deep connection with the local context of communities in social risk conditions.
- Ability to adopt and promote a positive attitude towards processes of change, renewal, and transformation.
- Committed to creating a positive impact on the world with inspiration, passion, compassion, and a sense of service vocation.
- Ability to travel regularly to program locations, both nationally and internationally.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Oversight and Governance Responsibilities:**

- Ensure that all communications outputs produced in or for the region adhere to organizational policies, brand standards, safeguarding requirements and ethical storytelling standards.
- Identify and escalate to the line manager any reputational, brand or safeguarding risk arising from regional communications activity, including materials produced by implementing partners.
- Maintain complete consent and release documentation for all content produced in the region, and verify it is in place before any material is used or published.
- Ensure that country offices and implementing partners use the organizational identity only through the defined authorization process and report any unauthorized use.
- Maintain accurate records of production, suppliers and communications expenditure, and report them to the line manager.
- Support training and awareness for country staff and implementing partner staff on brand standards, consent and safeguarding in communications.
- Recommend improvements to communications processes and controls to strengthen consistency, accountability and quality across the region.

**Production of Communications Materials**

- Produce communications and visibility materials for the three countries: brochures, reports, IEC tools, banners, signage, event materials, staff identification and program collateral.
- Adapt global campaign materials for regional use, working from approved templates and brand assets.
- Specify materials correctly for their intended use, including application, resolution, color space, bleed, and finishing.
- Prepare supplier briefs and specifications, coordinate with Procurement and Finance on execution, and obtain a printer’s proof before any full production run, without exception.
- Maintain supplier and printer records for the region, with current lead times and costs.

**Content and Storytelling**

- Deliver an agreed monthly volume of approved success stories from the three country offices to the global repository, with complete metadata, working with country program staff to source them.
- Write and edit success stories and donor-facing content to the organization’s global voice and quality standards.
- Capture photography and short-form video interviews in the field to a professional standard, including framing, audio, stabilization and exposure control.

**Planning and Coordination**

- Develop an annual communications work plan jointly with the country office teams, setting out their planned activities, dates and material requirements for the year, so that needs are mapped early enough to be produced properly. Update it through the quarterly Requirements Report.
- Maintain the regional production calendar: record every communications deliverable with its material type, lead time, the date final artwork is required, and the date it must reach procurement. Reviewed monthly with the line manager.
- Submit a Regional Communications Requirements Report before the start of each quarter, listing, for each country, the commemorative dates, program milestones, partner events, and activities that will require communications support, along with the lead time each requires.
- Flag in writing, as soon as it is known, any activity whose timeline is no longer viable, and propose an alternative material or scope.
- Maintain the regional workstream board and keep the status of each item up to date.

**Regional Digital Presence and Media**

- Operate and administer the regional social media accounts: schedule and publish posts, stories, reels and short-form content approved within the global framework, maintain a content calendar one month in advance, and report engagement quarterly.
- Maintain an organizational media contact database for the three countries, held on the regional system and kept current. Personal contact lists are not a substitute.
- Liaise with local and regional media outlets to enhance visibility and maintain the regional media kit: organizational fact sheet, spokesperson protocol, and approved boilerplate.

**Country Office Support and Capacity**

- Train and support country program staff and implementing partner staff in interviewing, photography specifications, consent documentation, and the use of approved templates and brand assets.
- Operate the shared mechanisms through which program teams submit content and requests.
- Work with country teams to incorporate their communication requirements into the annual plan and propose the approaches most likely to work for each country and audience.
- Provide guidance to country offices on brand application so that materials start from approved templates rather than being corrected at approval stage.

**Brand Application and Partner Materials**

- Apply the organizational identity consistently across all regional outputs, and ensure that country offices and implementing partners work from the currently approved assets.
- Route every partner request to use the organizational identity on physical materials through the defined authorization process. The postholder does not approve partner use of the organizational identity.
- Produce final artwork for approved co-branded materials from organizational templates rather than amending partner-originated files.

**Service Standard**

- Acknowledge every internal and partner request upon receipt, and respond with a specific date within two working days.
- Where a request arrives without the information needed to act, obtain it from the requester rather than waiting.
- Report status by stage — not started, in design, pending approval, final artwork ready, with procurement, in production, delivered — never as a general assessment.

**Scope and Interface with Headquarters**

- Held by this post: regional adaptation of global campaigns, field capture, templated and routine production, supplier briefing and coordination, regional channels, local media liaison, and country office support.
- Routed to headquarters Creative Services: campaign concept development, complex design, finished video editing and institutional publications. The postholder is responsible for recognizing which is which and routing in good time.
- The postholder implements the regional communications strategy designed by the Vice President, Integrated Brand & Communications, within the global Marketing & Communications frameork.

title: Finance Manager (National Position)
body:
**Position: Finance Manager**

**Job location:** Kampala

**Starting date:** January 2027

**Vacancy closing date:** 24th November 2026

**Duration position:** 1-year renewable contract.

**Working hours:** Fulltime (40 hours per week)

**About ZOA**

***We are here for people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster.***

ZOA, as an international NGO, supports people who have lost everything due to armed conflict or natural disaster. Together, we can come to their aid in emergencies and remain faithful to communities as they recover – providing new opportunities for them to help themselves again. The work of ZOA is coordinated from the Netherlands. We are active in multiple countries in Africa, South America, the Middle East Region, and Asia. We work with approximately 900 employees worldwide and with (local) partners. We invite you to join our team of committed colleagues. In Uganda, ZOA has offices in Kampala, West Nile (Arua), Acholi (Gulu), and Karamoja (Amudat). ZOA Uganda works both in relief and recovery on the themes of food security & livelihoods, education, and conflict management with a special focus on land Rights.

**Your challenge**

The Finance Manager is to ensure that there is significant leadership provided to the team in the implementation of ZOA finance strategies and to ensure financial planning and management activities including budgeting & forecasting, a sound financial reporting systems, compliance and creation of value to support achievement ZOA’s strategic business continuity by having meaningful financial impact on the organisation.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

***Leadership and Team Management***

- Oversee application of ZOA Policy and Guidelines ensuring compliance.
- Communicate to the Finance team a clear and exciting vision for the work of ZOA and for the role of department in supporting the organisation.
- Responsible for induction, performance monitoring, training on the job and staff well-being of finance staff.
- Support team members to grow in their potential capacity and motivate them to grow in their performance e.g. by encouraging and praising good performance, coaching, assisting staff to prevent or resolve problems, providing resources, tools and equipment.
- Ensure gender and conflict sensitive approach to team management;
- Monitor the quality of financial and administrative operations of the field offices.
- Support country office and field offices in acquisition, purchase, contract management and tender procedures in accordance with ZOA internal systems;
- Periodic meetings with the field finance team for relevant accounting needs and deliverables.

***Risk Management and Compliance***

- Provide leadership, and financial insights to the finance and accounting areas of the organization, proposing and implementing improvements in operational management processes to increase efficiency.
- Support management in compliance to donor regulation, local government regulation and ZOA regulations.
- Support and oversee awareness measures for prevention of fraud, bribery and corruption; report any suspected misconduct to Manager of Operations and assist with periodic risk assessments and trainings.
- Advise both finance and non-finance staff over matters of internal control compliance periodically review the suitability of the existing controls to ensure they are adequate to minimise the risk exposure of ZOA and that they reinforce the proper implementation of programs.
- Ensure full compliance with Uganda Revenue Authority, NGO Board and returns requirements and be the key contact with bank support personnel, auditors and tax advisors.
- Coordinate and support the External and Internal Audits and follows on actions for management resolution/address.
- Collaborate with other contracted finance support teams, and lead finance functions, especially with the budget owners/manager/Operations team.

***Financial Reporting***

- Ensure accurate and timely financial reporting for decision making.
- Ensure the monthly budget balances report is up to date and shared with budget holders. Minimize the number of errors from the team reports through constant feedback.
- Confirm expense codes on all requests as they are received, correct where necessary through the budget manager.
- Prepare, analyze, and submit accurate monthly financial and management reports, including; income statement, balance sheet, budget and variance, projections and forecast, and cash flow.
- Coordinate the preparation of the audited financial statements and all tax returns.
- Prepare a variety of ad hoc financial scenarios as requested.

***Financial Control & Accounting***

- Observe and implement the accounting systems, payments, bookkeeping, statutory filing, revenue management, and improvement of payment systems.
- Ensure that all financial transactions are processed accurately, in a timely manner, in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles through the ERP system, identifying and correcting any variances.
- Maintain a system to track financial commitments and outstanding contract amounts by staff and third parties transacting with ZOA and ensure that they are diligently executed when due.
- Develop, implement, and maintain processes and controls that are current best practices related to transaction processing.
- Manage and process all the following transactions: payroll, taxes, accounts payable, revenue and expense, fixed assets, cash, bank reconciliations, and allocations.
- Responsible for periodic update of fixed assets register in ERP, collaborating with the logistics team to ensure accuracy of asset details.
- Perform month-end closing procedures, including account reconciliations, and updating schedules.

***Budget Management***

- Support budget managers to prepare periodic budgets and forecasts while providing clarity where needed.
- Prepare budgets for new proposals, budget modifications and the country year budget.
- Ensure budgets are entered into the ERP system.
- Share monthly and quarterly BVA reports with budget holders for ease of planning.
- Monitor the budget changes and update the approved budgets in ERP.
- Offer periodic training or refresher training to the teams aimed at improving financial management, discipline and accountability as stipulated in our policies and procedures.

**Your profile**

Identity

title: Tok Pasifika Project Adviser
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific peoples, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I)** collective delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The **Tok Pasifika Project Advisor** is responsible for the implementation, coordination and development of the Tok Pasifika project. This position works to improve the accessibility, quality and impact of Pacific language services, by enhancing the project’s visibility, strengthening and assisting the network of language service providers, supporting integration of language issues into SPC practices, and ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning as part of the project. The Project Advisor serves as Tok Pasifika’s point of contact with internal teams and external partners, using an inclusive, culturally appropriate approach that is aligned with the SPC’s institutional priorities.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Improving the Tok Pasifika project’s visibility and outreach**

- Develop a communication plan in collaboration with SPC’s Strategic Communications, Outreach, Publishing and Engagement (SCOPE) team, that takes into account stakeholders’ feedback; and update this plan annually.
- In collaboration with SPC teams, enhance use of existing communication materials and plan and coordinate production of new materials, as needed.
- Create a strong visual identity for the project, and regularly update and track project visibility tools such as the website, intranet page, etc.
- Develop and implement awareness-raising activities for SPC’s technical divisions and other external stakeholders.
- Use the information gathered through Tok Pasifika’s monitoring and evaluation system, take part in efforts to present SPC’s results in a view to raising the profile of Tok Pasifika’s work and results (e.g. drafting performance stories, communicating numerical outcomes).
- Participate in internal, local and/or international cultural events to represent and promote Tok Pasifika.
- Liaise with media outlets to publicise the Tok Pasifika project.

**Building the network of language service providers and improving the quality of the services provided**

- Manage contracts and external contractors, in particular by monitoring and updating the list of preferred service providers (contracts, deadlines, administrative compliance), in collaboration with the Procurement and Finance teams, and ensure that contractual documents are properly filed and accessible.
- Provide support and advice to SPC teams on managing requests for translation into Pacific languages.
- Engage the network on a regular basis (e.g. mailing list, newsletter, focus groups).
- Take part in drafting guidelines for providers and/or organise training sessions (e.g. webinars on translation techniques or administrative procedures, liaison interpreting workshops, etc.), in collaboration with members of the Conference and Languages unit.
- Hold annual meetings (face-to-face or on-line) with language service providers to discuss their needs, difficulties and successes.
- Set up and monitor a system for evaluating the performance of language service providers and their use by SPC teams, with a view to continuously improving the quality, relevance and effectiveness of the language services provided.

**Integrating language issues across SPC and boosting demand**

- Set up and facilitate a Tok Pasifika community of practice in order to strengthen internal coordination, information sharing and ownership of language services within SPC.
- Set up, in collaboration with a focal point within one SPC division, a pilot Pacific language translation project, and identify lessons from that project, in a view to providing better advice to teams and optimising their use of Tok Pasifika services
- Contribute to the integration of language issues from the project design stage, especially in terms of the key forms used, through the relationships established with various relevant SPC teams (SPL, PIRMO, HRSD, Procurement).
- Contribute to the development, adoption and dissemination of an SPC-wide language policy that explicitly recognises the value of Pacific languages and implements the guiding principles for their gradual integration into SPC activities.

**Mobilising project resources and ensuring their sustainability**

- Develop strategic partnerships with institutions, NGOs, universities or companies in the language sector.
- Assist in securing additional funding (grants, partnerships, regional/international calls for projects).
- Optimise existing resources (pooling with other projects, using tools that have already been developed).
- Ensure thorough budget monitoring for the Tok Pasifika project and produce regular financial reports to demonstrate the efficient use of resources and the actual results achieved.

**Monitoring, evaluation and learning**

- Identify and map the Tok Pasifika project’s key internal and external stakeholders and keep this list up to date.
- Undertake an internal assessment, by analysing Pacific language translation needs and carrying out surveys and interviews with the user divisions; and issue a comparison with the previous assessment.
- The approaches to conduct an external assessment are defined (analysis of the needs of SPC stakeholders).
- Develop, implement and refine a framework of indicators to monitor activities, service provider performance, service quality, demand and use of Tok Pasifika services.
- Produce regular monitoring, evaluation and learning reports and use the results and lessons learned to adjust the services Tok Pasifika proposes, as well as the project’s work approaches and communication strategy.
- Draft a project sustainability plan, to be updated annually, which contains the key points, possible project directions and recommendations for integrating multilingualism throughout SPC.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the **online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in project management; Pacific languages, linguistics or cultures; international relations; cultural studies; or a related field, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 10 years in the management of language-related, cultural or international cooperation projects, ideally in a regional or international institutional context
- Demonstrated project management skills and proficiency in project management methods and tools (planning, monitoring, reporting, coordination and partnerships)
- Experience in purchasing processes in private or public entities
- Experience in administrative and budgetary project management, funding-raising and project monitoring and evaluation

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communications skills
- Proficiency in one or more Pacific languages.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Very good knowledge of Pacific context and cultures
- Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This vacant position is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** The **Tok Pasifika Project Adviser** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 3727 to 4562 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 537,766 to 658,322 (USD 4994 to 6114; EUR 4506 to 5517). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale is based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for international staff employees based in New Caledonia** – SPC provides subsidised housing in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy

title: VA26P186V01 MRC Counsellor (M1)
source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
body:
MRAPP funded by the Government of the Netherlands, aims to strengthen migration prevention efforts and improve access to migration-related information, counselling, referral and reintegration services in Iraq. The project is implemented by ICMPD in close coordination with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement and other relevant governmental and local stakeholders, with a focus on strengthening and expanding the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) model.

The position will be based within the MRAPP project team and will report to the Project Manager, while working closely with relevant ICMPD colleagues, MRC staff, government counterparts and project stakeholders to support the effective delivery of project activities and results.

## Functional Overview

Working closely with the respective Migration Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator, the MRC Counsellor assists with the implementation of MRC activities and workplans, in support of effective communication, information and service delivery. They contribute to the organisation of events and outreach activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Coordinator and other Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures.

## Key Results

***Support to MRC Activities:*** Via various means and platforms such as face-to-face, phone and online, counselling, guidance, referral and information provided to a variety of clients (prospective or returning migrants, migrants, families of migrants, etc.) who visit or attend MRC activities, initiating and following up on referrals, linking them with relevant agencies depending on their needs, e.g. technical and vocational institutes to upgrade their skills or with the relevant authorities for the processing of their documents for overseas employment. Outreach activities supported via the use of media and social media and participation in online discussions, forums or symposiums, conferences, and other related events. In collaboration with the MRC Coordinator the MRC website and database, Facebook page and other social media accounts regularly updated.

***Support to Outreach Activities:*** In cooperation with relevant agencies both in the public and private sector, networks and contacts effectively established. Community events and outreach activities organised such as briefings in academic and training institutions, symposia with civil society, training of education or emigration consultancies, and the setting-up of booths, kiosks, or similar structures in public places to disseminate information and materials on safe, orderly, and regular migration, including on return and reintegration.

***Preparation of Information Materials:*** In collaboration with the ICMPD team and whenever applicable, with consultants or experts, research or mapping undertaken of available migration-related programmes, services, and activities of various stakeholders. Knowledge materials compiled on migration that are helpful in the full operation and functioning of the MRC. Additional knowledge products andinformation materials revised, prepared, or further developed, as necessary, such as brochures, handbooks, audio-visual products, web-based information documents, etc. Online discussions relevant to migration, regularly maintained and populated, initiating regular and timely responses to issues raised and information requested.

***Support to the MRC Coordination Activities:*** Assistance provided to the respective MRC Coordinator to ensure the timely, efficient, and effective implementation of MRC activities, and with the monitoring and updating of the workplans, as necessary, ensuring that outputs and outcomes are aligned and integrated with the national priorities and strategies of government partners, and of the projects. Substantive contributions provided to the preparation of relevant reports, responses to client feedback and monitoring and reporting to relevant agencies on any policy or programmatic recommendations. Information materials compiled and prepared for dissemination. The MRC database regularly updated recording relevant activities, events and outreach activities undertaken. Effective support provided to the MRC Coordinator in preparing weekly, quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity andmission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests on agreed formats, and other documentary requirements.

## Required Expertise

- ​Solid organizational, planning and prioritizing skills and abilities.
- Upon consultation with the supervisor, ability to make decisions in full compliance with ICMPD’soperational regulations and rules.
- Analytical thinking to gather, analyse and compile information, identifying critical relationships and patterns among data and proposing workable solutions.
- An understanding of migration dynamics in the country.
- Experience in the area of migration in the country.
- High sense of initiative and good judgement to be able to work independently with minimum supervision.
- Strong sense of client orientation and good understanding of effective service delivery, community engagement, outreach, and social work.
- Ability to work effectively with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds.
- Capability to establish effective relationships across the organisation at all levels.

## Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field. High school diploma or equivalent with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the bachelor’s degree.
- Minimum of 2 years of position-specific experience.
- Working experience with international organisations is an asset.
- Experience in office administration and management.
- Experience working with local authorities and businesses.
- Solid organizational skills.
- Proficiency in English, Kurdish and Arabic (verbal/written) is required.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

title: VA26P114V02 Junior ICT Officer - Service Desk (IP1)

body:
> Note: Please note that this vacancy has been republished. Applicants who have already submitted an application do not need to reapply.​

## **Functional Overview**

Within the Directorate of Management (MGT), and specifically the Information and Communications Technology (ICT) Unit, the Junior ICT Officer – Service Desk supports the organisation-wide ICT ticketing system (Service Portal) and contributes to the timely resolution of ICT incidents and service requests in accordance with established ICMPD/ICT procedures, service standards and continuous improvement processes. As an active member of the ICT Service Desk Team, the incumbent provides client-oriented and efficient first-level technical support to end-users across ICMPD, contributing to the smooth day-to-day operation of ICT services and the consistent application of ICT policies and guidelines.

The position is based in one of ICMPD’s regional offices and serves as the first point of contact for end-users at the assigned duty station. In line with the Service Desk’s centrally coordinated operating model, all incidents and service requests are logged and managed through the single Service Portal and assigned based on priority, workload and required technical expertise. While priority is given to requests originating from the assigned duty station, the Junior ICT Officer may also be assigned to handle service requests across multiple regions. Likewise, service requests from the regional office may be handled by other Service Desk team members, ensuring continuity and adherence to defined service levels.

The incumbent functionally reports to the ICT Team Lead – Service Desk, based at ICMPD Headquarters in Vienna, Austria, who provides technical guidance and performance supervision. Administrative supervision, including office presence and local administrative matters, is managed by the relevant management authority in the respective regional office.

The role also contributes to supporting organisational project teams in the effective use of Microsoft 365 collaboration tools, in particular Microsoft Teams and related document libraries, in coordination with the Knowledge Management function to ensure alignment with established organisational standards.

## Key Results

***Provision of Tier 1 Support and Incident Management:*** Basic hardware and software issues are resolved through troubleshooting, diagnosis and application of established solutions, ensuring minimal service disruption and user satisfaction. Reported issues are logged, categorised and addressed in accordance with defined procedures. Complex or unresolved cases are escalated to higher-level support as required. Local ICT needs across ICMPD duty stations are supported in coordination with on-site ICT experts. Common issues and standard solutions are documented to facilitate consistent handling of recurring incidents.

***Provision of Tier 2 Support for Specific ICT Services:*** Specific ICT services are supported through configuration and maintenance activities carried out in accordance with established procedures and under the guidance of senior ICT Service Desk team members. Basic ICT services, including mobile device and access rights management, are consistently monitored and maintained to ensure operational continuity. Troubleshooting steps and solutions are recorded and documented to support knowledge sharing and service consistency.

***Contributions to Additional Client and Project ICT Services:*** Basic ICT equipment, including workstations and mobile devices, is set up and maintained following standard procedures. User and device management tasks, such as account setup and configuration, are carried out in line with defined processes. Technical assistance is provided for virtual meetings and video conferencing. Software installations are implemented promptly, and the standard operating procedures, for frequently requested services are documented to streamline processes and improve service delivery.

***Support to Project Teams and Document Management:*** Project teams are supported in the day-to-day use of Microsoft Teams document libraries. Guidance is provided to users on standard document management and collaboration practices, including file sharing and co-authoring within the organisation, as well as secure collaboration with external users, in line with ICT security and information management guidelines.

## Required Expertise

- ​Ability to analyse technical issues and apply established solutions within the assigned area of work.
- Ability to adapt to changing priorities and manage multiple service requests.
- Ability to provide technical support to end-users, including problem identification, diagnosis and resolution within defined procedures.
- Working knowledge of basic network concepts (TCP/IP, Wireless, DNS, DHCP) and ability to support network device configuration under guidance.
- Working knowledge of operating systems, standard software applications, ICT services and hardware environments used within ICMPD.
- Basic understanding of Microsoft Teams and SharePoint Online, particularly document libraries and collaboration features.
- Ability to guide users in applying standard document management practices (access control, versioning, sharing and structure).
- Awareness of information security and data protection principles, particularly in relation to the management of shared document repositories.

## **Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills**

- ​Master’s Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field. A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Master’s degree.
- Minimum of one (1) year of relevant professional experience in an IT service desk or technical support environment.
- Experience with Microsoft Active Directory (user and group management) and remote support tools (e.g. Remote Desktop, LogMeln, Bomgar, TeamViewer or similar).
- Experience working with IT service management (ITSM) systems and related service desk technologies.
- Experience supporting Microsoft 365 tools, particularly Microsoft Teams and SharePoint Online, including cloud-based document management environments.
- ITIL Foundation certification and previous experience with SAP Business One are considered assets.
- Strong analytical, organisational, and communication skills with a client-oriented approach, and the ability to build effective working relationships and collaborate well within diverse, international teams.
- Proficiency in written and spoken English; proficiency in the language of the duty station is an asset.

title: ECHO Proposal Writing Consultant
body:
**Title:** ECHO Proposal Writing Consultant

**Type of contract:** Consultancy

**Duration:** 3-6 months in 2027, aligned with the ECHO HIP calendar; total 30-40 working days

**Location:** Home-based/remote, with possible travel to The Hague

**Reporting to:** Executive Director

## **Background**

The Dr. Denis Mukwege Foundation (MF), established in 2016, is an international, survivor-centred, rights-based organisation working to change the response to conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV). Through three interconnected strategies – Care, Voice, and Justice & Accountability – MF provides holistic care to survivors in the Central African Republic (CAR), Ukraine and Burundi, is developing its work in Ethiopia and Syria, and supports 19 national survivor networks across 10 contexts.

MF’s recent certification as a DG ECHO humanitarian partner opens access to funding for its work in emergency and protracted crisis settings, typically at a much larger scale than most of its current grants. In 2027, MF plans to submit its first proposals for ECHO humanitarian funding, either directly or as part of a consortium with experienced humanitarian partners. Priority contexts are those where MF already has presence, knowledge and partners and where ECHO priorities match survivors’ needs, such as CAR, Ukraine, Ethiopia and the Sudan regional response.

Humanitarian funding brings new demands: rapid start-up, shorter project cycles, strict compliance and reporting requirements, and work in insecure, fast-changing environments. To make the most of its first applications, MF wishes to engage an experienced humanitarian proposal writer with in-depth knowledge of ECHO formats, requirements and assessment criteria, while MF staff build the expertise to write future ECHO proposals in-house.

## **Purpose and objectives**

The overall purpose of this consultancy is to help MF submit competitive and compliant first ECHO proposals in 2027 and, in doing so, build lasting in-house capacity to develop future ECHO proposals independently.

Specific objectives – the consultant will:

- Map relevant ECHO Humanitarian Implementation Plans (HIPs) and Technical Annexes for MF’s priority contexts and advise on where and how MF should apply (directly or in consortium).
- Lead the writing of 1–2 ECHO proposals in close collaboration with MF staff in The Hague and country offices.
- Ensure MF’s survivor-centred holistic care model – including clinical management of rape (CMR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) and case management – is translated into a strong, fundable humanitarian intervention logic.
- Coach MF staff on ECHO formats, requirements and assessment criteria, and leave behind practical tools for future proposals.

## **Scope of work**

**A. ECHO opportunity mapping and planning**

- Review the HIPs and Technical Annexes relevant to CAR, Ukraine, Ethiopia and the Sudan regional crisis (including CAR, Chad and Uganda), and other MF contexts as agreed.
- Assess the fit between ECHO priorities (protection, GBV, health, MHPSS) and MF’s expertise, presence and partnerships.
- Recommend which opportunities to pursue, whether as lead applicant or consortium partner, and propose a calendar aligned with ECHO’s funding cycle.
- Where a consortium is recommended, advise on suitable ECHO-certified partners and on MF’s positioning as a specialist CRSV partner.

**B. Proposal development**

- Lead the drafting of the ECHO Single Form (or MF’s sections of a consortium proposal), including needs analysis, intervention logic, logframe with ECHO Key Results Indicators, risk analysis, localisation and partnership approach, and exit strategy.
- Work with MF’s Care team to integrate CMR, MHPSS and case management, building on MF toolkits developed for CAR, Burundi and Ethiopia.
- Ensure alignment with ECHO thematic policies and markers (e.g. GBV, protection mainstreaming, Gender-Age Marker), humanitarian principles and Do No Harm.
- Support MF Finance in preparing a budget and budget narrative consistent with ECHO eligibility rules.
- Review complete drafts against ECHO assessment criteria and support responses to ECHO requests for clarification after submission.

**C. Coaching and capacity building**

- Involve designated MF staff in each step of proposal development, so they learn by doing.
- Facilitate 2 practical training sessions for staff in The Hague and country offices on ECHO requirements, proposal writing, the Single Form, and reporting and visibility basics.
- Provide targeted feedback and coaching sessions to staff drafting sections.
- Flag gaps in MF policies or systems (e.g. safeguarding/PSEA, security, anti-fraud, partner due diligence, procurement) that could weaken a proposal, as input to MF’s humanitarian readiness plan.

Out of scope: project implementation, ECHO reporting on awarded grants, and the full revision of MF policies. These may be covered in a separate assignment.

## **Deliverables and indicative timing**

1. Inception note: approach, workplan, staff involvement and review process *(Week 2)*
2. ECHO opportunity mapping: HIP analysis per context, go/no-go recommendations, lead vs consortium options and proposal calendar *(Week 4)*
3. Submission-ready ECHO proposal 1 (Single Form or MF consortium sections, logframe, budget narrative input) *(Per HIP deadline)*
4. Submission-ready ECHO proposal 2, if applicable *(Per HIP deadline)*
5. Training sessions for staff in The Hague and country offices, with materials *(Spread across the assignment)*
6. ECHO proposal toolkit: annotated Single Form guide, submission checklist, and a library of reusable text on MF’s survivor-centred CRSV approach *(End of assignment)*
7. Short end-of-assignment note: lessons learned, remaining capacity gaps and recommendations for MF’s humanitarian readiness plan *(End of assignment)*

All deliverables will be in English, with French-language support for CAR or Chad where needed.

## **Timeline**

The assignment is expected to run for between 3-6 months in 2027, with an indicative 30–40 working days, concentrated around HIP deadlines. Exact dates will be agreed at inception, once the relevant HIP Technical Annexes and deadlines are known.

- **Inception and mapping**: Inception meeting, desk review of MF documents and HIPs, mapping and recommendations (5-7 days)
- **Proposal 1**: Drafting, internal reviews, budget support, finalisation (10-12 days)
- **Proposal 2 (if applicable)**: Drafting, internal reviews, budget support, finalisation (8-10 days)
- **Capacity building**: Training sessions, coaching, toolkit development (5-7 days)
- **Follow-up and closure**: Support with ECHO clarification requests; end-of-assignment note (2-4 days)

## **Management and reporting**

The consultant will report to the Executive Director, who will be the primary point of contact and coordinate internal reviews. A small internal working group – including Fundraising, the Care and Voice teams, Finance and the relevant country programme lead(s) – will contribute content, review drafts and take part in coaching. MF will designate 1–2 staff members as counterparts who will co-write with the consultant and lead future ECHO proposals.

MF will provide access to relevant internal documents (Strategic Plan, country strategies, care toolkits, policies, budgets and past proposals), make introductions to potential consortium partners and ECHO field contacts as needed, and give timely feedback on drafts. Final approval of any proposal rests with MF Management.

## **Consultant profile**

MF is looking for a consultant or small team with:

- At least 7 years of experience in humanitarian programme design and proposal writing, including a proven track record of successful ECHO proposals as lead writer.
- In-depth knowledge of ECHO’s funding cycle, HIPs, the Single Form, eligibility and budget rules, Key Results Indicators, and thematic policies and markers.
- Experience with protection, GBV and/or health/MHPSS programming in conflict settings; knowledge of CRSV and survivor-centred approaches is a strong asset.
- Experience with consortium proposals and localisation approaches.
- Familiarity with one or more of MF’s priority contexts (CAR, Ukraine, Ethiopia, Sudan regional response).
- Proven ability to coach and train staff with little humanitarian funding experience.
- Excellent written English; working French is a strong asset for proposals in CAR or Chad.
- Availability during the expected HIP proposal windows in 2027.

## **Location, logistics, budget and contractual terms**

The assignment is largely home-based. A few visits to MF’s office in The Hague, for example for a training session, may be agreed. Any travel costs will be agreed in advance and reimbursed separately from the fee.

The consultant is invited to propose a daily fee and an estimated total cost based on the indicative level of effort. Payment will be linked to deliverables and agreed in the consultancy contract. Because ECHO deadlines may shift, the contract will allow days to be reallocated between phases within the agreed total.

## **Confidentiality, safeguarding and ethics**

All information shared by MF, and all products developed under this assignment, are confidential and remain the property of MF. The consultant may not disclose or use them for any other purpose without MF’s prior written consent.

The consultant will sign and comply with MF’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding and PSEA policy, and data protection policy. No identifiable survivor data will be shared or used in proposals; survivor information will only be used in anonymised and aggregated form, in line with survivor-centred and Do No Harm principles.

title: Development Supervisor
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview**: The Development Supervisor leads corporate and community engagement efforts that generate financial contributions, sponsorships, in-kind resources, volunteer support, and long-term partnerships for IRC programs in Georgia and Florida. Reporting to the Development Director, this position develops and stewards’ relationships with businesses, civic and faith-based organizations, community leaders, and other supporters; advances local visibility and mission-aligned engagement; and translates these relationships into measurable fundraising and resource-development outcomes. The Supervisor directly supervises the Development Specialist and works collaboratively with program teams, local leadership, and IRC headquarters.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Corporate Partnerships, Sponsorships & Revenue Development**

- Identify, research, cultivate, solicit, and steward corporate and community prospects for cash gifts, sponsorships, workplace giving, matching gifts, cause-marketing partnerships, and other philanthropic support.
- Develop tailored sponsorship proposals and partnership opportunities for events, program priorities, and special initiatives; negotiate and fulfill approved partner benefits and recognition commitments.
- Build and support third-party fundraising opportunities led by businesses, civic organizations, community groups, and individual supporters; coordinate with the Development Director on approvals, messaging, and gift processing.
- Manage a defined portfolio of corporate and community relationships, maintain prospect pipelines and stewardship plans, and contribute to annual revenue and engagement goals established with the Development Director.
- Identify and refer major-gift, individual donor, corporate foundation, and institutional funding prospects to the Development Director and grants lead; collaborate on cultivation and introductions.

**Community Engagement, Advisory Council & External Representation**

- Manage, maintain, and expand relationships with faith-based organizations, civic groups, businesses, and community partners.
- Represent IRC Georgia and Florida at selected chambers, networking events, civic meetings, community forums, and presentations; proactively recommend engagements that support strategic visibility and resource development.
- Coordinate and help lead engagement of the IRC in Atlanta Economic Empowerment Advisory Council, including member cultivation, meeting preparation, partnership activation, and fundraising participation.
- Collaborate with leadership and program teams on mission-aligned community education and advocacy-related engagement, consistent with IRC policies and approved organizational positions.
- Work with Site Directors and program leads to coordinate event planning, partner orientations, and in-kind giving across Georgia and Florida.

**In-Kind Giving, Match & Volunteer Partnerships**

- Create and execute an in-kind acquisition strategy, from identifying needs and soliciting donors through stewardship, valuation, documentation, and outcome tracking.
- Work directly with program leads to identify priority client and program needs; coordinate drives and work with Supply Chain/Operations to track receipt, storage, and distribution in accordance with IRC and funder policies.
- Coordinate the office’s raising of Match support through eligible in-kind donations, volunteer time, and cash donations; prepare monthly Match Grant status reports and recommend strategies to address shortfalls.
- Lead the strategy and partner solicitation for seasonal and special-purpose giving drives, including Holiday Giving; oversee implementation with support from the Development Specialist and program/operations teams.
- Provide oversight and direction for volunteer engagement, including corporate group opportunities, while the Development Specialist supports recruitment, onboarding, scheduling, and day-to-day coordination.
- Administer AmeriCorps and fellowship partnerships across Georgia and Florida offices, including recruitment, onboarding, and funder reporting; confirm annual service-member targets and operational responsibilities with leadership.

**Campaigns, Events & Communications**

- Work with the Development Director and relevant headquarters/RAM teams to support annual and seasonal giving campaigns, including year-end, Give Miami Day, Georgia Gives Day, and other approved appeals.
- Work with the Development Director, Deputy Director of Programs, and Economic Empowerment Advisory Council to plan and execute Dinner Together and other fundraising events, with responsibility for sponsorship acquisition and partner engagement; event revenue goals are set annually with leadership.
- Plan and oversee donor-facing components of donation events, fundraising events, and partner activations, delegating event logistics to the Development Specialist as appropriate.
- Coordinate donor and partner communications, impact updates, testimonials, and stewardship materials with appropriate communications colleagues and headquarters teams; ensure accuracy, consent, and brand alignment.
- Coordinate with responsible communications staff to keep Georgia and Florida local web content and stories current, subject to IRC website governance and approvals.

**Data, Reporting, Collaboration & Supervision**

- Maintain accurate donor cultivation, solicitation, giving, and recognition records in Salesforce for cash and in-kind donors; analyze reports to inform donor moves and pipeline priorities.
- Track and report partnership activity, sponsorship revenue, in-kind support, eligible Match contributions, and other agreed-upon development metrics; prepare required partner and in-kind donor reports.
- Supervise, coach, prioritize work for, and evaluate the Development Specialist; establish clear division of responsibilities and support consistent volunteer, event, engagement, and data workflows.
- Collaborate with the Development Director and grants lead to identify funding opportunities and supply corporate/community introductions or partnership information for proposals.
- Liaise with IRC headquarters/RAM staff on national corporate, in-kind, and volunteer opportunities relevant to Georgia and Florida.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**: Bachelor’s degree in business and/or Communications or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field, fundraising, corporate partnerships, sponsorship sales, business development, community engagement, or related relationship-management work strongly preferred; prior supervisory or team-lead experience desirable. minimum of 2-5 years’ experience strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.
- Demonstrated ability to solicit financial support, build persuasive sponsorship proposals, steward partners, and manage multiple prospects toward measurable results.
- Comfort with public speaking, external representation, cross-functional coordination, and supervising/delegating work.
- Experience with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), donor data quality, reporting, and pipeline tracking.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, hybrid work (3 days office) and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional domestic (non-local) travel required; up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate starting at $60,131.30/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Director of Operations (f/x/m) – Brussels – MSF Belgium
body:
## CONTEXT

As Director of Operations, you will provide strategic leadership for the operational portfolio of MSF Operational Centre Brussels (OCB), ensuring that interventions remain relevant, responsive and accountable to the people we assist. You will lead OCB’s operational response in complex and rapidly changing environments, steering priorities and allocating resources across countries and over multiple years in line with OCB’s Strategic Ambitions 2026–2031.

OCB has two Directors of Operations (DOs), who jointly oversee and manage operations currently spanning 35 countries, with an annual budget of €400 million. Working closely with your fellow Director of Operations, the Medical Director and the wider leadership team, you will bring together humanitarian analysis, medical priorities and operational capacity to enable access to care, deliver effective programmes with an oversight of operational risks and opportunities.

You directly report to the General Director of MSF OCB and are member of the OCB CODIR (*Comité des Directeurs*), thereby actively contributing to the broader delivery of OCB Strategic Ambitions and leadership of the organization.

Together with the other Directors of Operations, you provide strategic operational leadership for the MSF movement, as part of MSF’s RIOD and in the Medical Operational platform (platform of the Operations & Medical Directors). You also represent MSF in external fora to negotiate, advocate and enable donor trust.

Both Directors of Operations (DOs) lead the Operations Department of MSF OCB.

The department consists of six managerial and technical teams called Cells, each in charge of a portfolio of countries and an Emergency Team (E-Pool) for the management of highly volatile emergency interventions. These teams are in Brussels, Abidjan and Rio. They supervise, empower and support Country and Project Teams to deliver MSF OCB medical humanitarian action.

The department also includes the Security Risk Management Unit (SRMU) and teams working on transversal management functions, including operational monitoring, information and knowledge management, and duty of care. These functions are coordinated and implemented through delegated responsibilities and dedicated support structures, ensuring coherent operational management, institutional learning and support to decision-making.

The DOs and operations department colleagues have a critical role in championing wider aspects of the quality of our social mission including bearing witness, safeguarding, climate adaptation, diversity, equity and inclusion, empowering teams and optimally and ethically collecting and using our data.

The DOs jointly manage the department and ensure operational continuity. Each supervises designated teams and leads agreed dossiers covering OCB issues, the MSF movement and external stakeholders. Team assignments may shift between DOs to balance workload.
