title: Consultance - Évaluation Programme DGD quiquennal - Bénin
body:
***Consultance externe pilotée et mise en place par Terres Rouges, merci de lire les informations ci-dessous et de ne pas postuler ici.***

[***Informations détaillées via ce lien***](https://jobpage.cvwarehouse.com/?companyGuid=14dacb70-fd86-419f-baa7-a286e0565aac&lang=fr-FR&job=405393&q=Consultance-Evaluation-Programme-DGD-quiquennal-Benin&api=false)

## Contexte de la mission

***Mission et vision de Terres Rouges***

Terres Rouges est une organisation non gouvernementale béninoise qui intervient depuis 2009 dans la protection de l’enfance, l’accompagnement psychosocial et la réinsertion sociale et professionnelle des enfants et jeunes en situation de vulnérabilité, particulièrement ceux vivant dans la rue, en rupture familiale ou exposés à différentes formes de violences, d’exploitation et d’exclusion sociale.  
L’organisation oeuvre pour une société dans laquelle chaque enfant et chaque jeune peut exercer ses droits fondamentaux, accéder aux services sociaux et sanitaires adaptés à ses besoins et bénéficier d’un environnement protecteur favorable à son développement, à son épanouissement et à son autonomisation.  
Son approche repose sur la participation active des enfants et jeunes à leur propre parcours d’accompagnement. Terres Rouges privilégie l’écoute, le respect des choix individuels, la valorisation des ressources personnelles, la réduction des risques et la recherche de solutions adaptées à chaque situation. Elle considère que les enfants et jeunes ne doivent pas uniquement être bénéficiaires des interventions, mais également acteurs des décisions qui les concernent.

## Objectif de l'évaluation

**Objectifs général et spécifique(s)**

L’objectif général de cette évaluation finale est d’apprécier, de manière indépendante, participative et objective, les résultats, les changements et les acquis du programme DGD 2022–2026 mis en œuvre par Terres Rouges au Bénin, afin de rendre compte de sa performance, d’identifier les enseignements tirés de sa mise en œuvre et de formuler des recommandations permettant de renforcer la qualité, l’efficacité et la durabilité des interventions futures en faveur des enfants et jeunes vulnérables et en situation de rue.

L’évaluation poursuivra une double finalité de redevabilité et d’apprentissage. Elle permettra à Terres Rouges de disposer d’une analyse documentée des résultats obtenus au regard des engagements du programme et de mieux comprendre les changements auxquels les interventions ont contribué. Elle devra également favoriser la capitalisation des expériences et l’identification de pratiques susceptibles d’être consolidées, adaptées ou reproduites dans les prochains programmes.

De manière spécifique, l’évaluation devra :

1. Apprécier le niveau d’atteinte des objectifs, des résultats et des indicateurs du programme au terme des cinq années de mise en œuvre, en identifiant les facteurs ayant favorisé ou limité leur réalisation.
2. Analyser les changements observés chez les enfants et jeunes bénéficiaires, notamment en matière de connaissance, d’exercice des droits et de mise en oeuvre des informations reçues en Réduction des Risques et en SDSR, de protection, de bien-être psychosocial, d’accès aux services, de réinsertion familiale, scolaire et socioprofessionnelle et d’autonomisation.
3. Examiner la contribution des approches développées par Terres Rouges, notamment le travail social de rue, la réduction des risques, les dispositifs d’accueil et d’hébergement, les écoles des parents, l’éducation par les pairs, la mobilisation communautaire, l’accompagnement psychosocial, la réinsertion et le plaidoyer, aux changements observés.
4. Apprécier le niveau d’appropriation et les perspectives de durabilité des acquis du programme, en particulier les compétences développées par les bénéficiaires, leur place dans le dispositif, les changements dans les pratiques familiales et communautaires, les mécanismes locaux de protection et les collaborations institutionnelles.
5. Identifier les bonnes pratiques, les difficultés, les enseignements tirés et les recommandations opérationnelles permettant de consolider les acquis et d’améliorer les interventions futures de Terres Rouges.

## **Profil recherché**

**Education**

- Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de deuxième cycle (Bac + 5) au minimum en sciences sociales, statistiques, santé publique, protection de l’enfance, gestion de projets, suivi-évaluation ou dans une discipline connexe. Une certification en évaluation de projets humanitaires ou de développement, ou l’appartenance à une association professionnelle d’évaluateurs reconnue, constitue un atout.

**Expérience**

- Justifier d’au moins cinq années d’expérience dans l’évaluation de projets ou programmes de développement, particulièrement dans les domaines de la protection de l’enfance, de la santé communautaire, de l’accompagnement psychosocial, de la réduction des risques, de la mobilisation communautaire ou de la réinsertion sociale. Disposer d’une expérience avérée des méthodes d’évaluation qualitatives et mixtes, des enquêtes sociales, des entretiens semi-structurés et des discussions de groupe. Une expérience dans l’évaluation de programmes financés par la DGD ou d’autres bailleurs institutionnels sera appréciée. Une bonne connaissance du contexte béninois et des dispositifs de protection de l’enfance est souhaitée.

**Qualité et justification de la méthodologie**

- Présenter une proposition technique claire, cohérente et adaptée aux objectifs et questions d’évaluation. Justifier le choix des méthodes, des outils de collecte et des modalités d’analyse. Démontrer une bonne compréhension de la théorie du changement, de l’analyse des résultats et des changements, de la triangulation des données et des approches participatives. Proposer un calendrier réaliste et une organisation de la mission compatible avec les délais et les ressources disponibles.

**Autres atouts**

- Avoir une excellente maîtrise du français et de solides capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et de rédaction. Disposer d’une expérience de travail avec des enfants et jeunes en situation de vulnérabilité et d’une bonne compréhension des principes éthiques de protection, de confidentialité et de prévention des abus. La connaissance des langues locales des zones d’intervention, ou la capacité à mobiliser des compétences linguistiques adaptées, constitue un atout. Une expérience de collaboration avec des organisations nationales et internationales de développement sera également appréciée.

## Budget 

Le budget de la consultance devra couvrir l’ensemble des dépenses nécessaires à la réalisation de l’évaluation finale externe du programme DGD 2022–2026 de Terres Rouges au Bénin.

Il devra inclure au minimum les éléments suivants :

- Les journées d’expertise du consultant ou des différents membres de l’équipe de consultance, couvrant la préparation, la revue documentaire, la collecte des données, l’analyse, la restitution et la rédaction des livrables ;
- Les frais de déplacement nécessaires à la réalisation de la mission, notamment les déplacements vers les sites d’intervention à Cotonou et dans la commune de Sô-Ava ;
- Les frais d’hébergement, de voyage, d’assurance et de séjour, lorsque ceux-ci sont nécessaires à la réalisation de la mission ;
- Les frais liés à la collecte et au traitement des données, notamment les communications, la reprographie, les supports de collecte et les éventuels besoins d’appui à la collecte ;
- Les frais annexes nécessaires à l’organisation des restitutions et à la production des livrables.

L’offre financière devra être présentée en franc CFA et en euros et faire apparaître clairement les honoraires, les frais opérationnels et le coût total de la prestation.

Le prix proposé devra être cohérent avec la méthodologie, le calendrier et les moyens humains mobilisés. Il devra couvrir l’ensemble des dépenses nécessaires à l’exécution de la mission, sans coûts supplémentaires non prévus.

**Le budget maximal disponible pour cette consultance s’élève à : 10.000 EUR.**

title: Senior Programme Manager
body:
**General Background**

GRC are policy makers, lawyers and development experts dedicated to promoting accountability and strengthening justice systems through the application of international law. With ongoing operations in some of the world’s most complex legal and security environments, Global Rights Compliance continues to provide specialised legal expertise, policy solutions, and strategic advisory services to uphold justice and strengthen the rule of law globally.

The legal response to the crisis in Ukraine has been supported by the Atrocity Crimes Advisory (ACA) Group, an international initiative assisting the Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG) and associated investigative bodies. Global Rights Compliance (GRC) operates as an implementing partner on the ground.

 Mobile Justice Teams (MJTs) are groups of local and international experts, and practitioners collaborating with, and in support of, local justice actors, such as Ukraine’s Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG) and Regional Prosecutor Offices (RPOs), to advance Ukraine's capacity to hold perpetrators accountable and pursue cases against high-ranking perpetrators. The MJTs are organised across regional and thematic areas to address context-specific and cross-cutting legal issues. The teams work in the most affected regions of Ukraine to provide advisory and case-building support, focusing on supporting prosecutors and investigators in their investigations and prosecutions.

We are seeking a Senior Programme Manager to join our team. This role is responsible for overseeing and coordinating GRC’s operations in Ukraine, ensuring effective and compliant project delivery, alignment with organisational goals, and a solutions-oriented approach to decision-making. The Senior Programme Manager ensures the effective day-to-day functioning of office operations, facilitates timely and informed decision-making, and upholds operational discipline across all levels.

**Full / Part-time:** Full-time  
**Location:** Ukraine, or Remote with a defined R&R / deployment cycle to Ukraine

**The Role**

- Programme leadership: Hold overall accountability for all Ukraine programmes ensuring they align with organisational priorities and donor requirements. Translate the Ukraine hub’s strategy into operational delivery plans with the Principal Legal Advisers, MJTs, Outreach Coordinator and security team. Oversee implementation against timelines, quality standards and impact goals.
- Outreach: Design & support prosecutorial and diplomatic outreach in line with programme objectives, working with relevant internal stakeholders.
- Donor reporting and compliance: Oversee all programme reporting, including monthly reports, donor quarterly and interim reports, risk registers, and final reports. Ensuring accuracy, consistency and strategic alignment, and that GRC complies with donor requirements, financial policies and audit standards.
- Budget oversight: Oversee programme budgets, forecasts and financial performance with the CFO, Treasurer and Programme Coordination Lead. Understand budget changes and their implications, and raise risks early.
- Growth and partnerships: Identify new programming and funding opportunities, and strengthen engagement with local actors and civil society organisations.
- External representation: Maintain strategic relationships with donors, Ukrainian authorities (including the OPG), civil society and international partners. Represent GRC in high-level meetings and act as liaison within the ACA framework.
- Governance and decision-making: Ensure the Executive Board are updated on all key developments. Maintain operational discipline and improve day-to-day systems and processes so decisions are made quickly and on good information.
- Operations, risk and security: Oversee the Ukraine office, security and GRC’s duty of care. Lead risk identification and mitigation with the Risk Manager.
- Cross-cutting coordination: Coordinate OSINT and M&E across the MJTs, and align priorities with the relevant functions.
- People and resourcing: Support resourcing, contracts and performance management alongside HR and the Treasurer, and lead objective-setting and feedback for the programme team.

**Your Background**

- 10+ years of operational management at a donor-funded international NGO or international organisation, including managing justice or humanitarian programmes in conflict-affected or high-risk environments.
- Ability to cope with and function effectively in high-stress, fluid environments.
- Proven people leadership & office / team management skills.
- Experience answering to, collaborating with, and supervising culturally/ethnically/geographically diverse teams.
- Experience with civil society / democracy / good governance/justice / human rights projects.
- Comfort with elementary cybersecurity principles, e.g. 2fa, whole-disk encryption, Account separation, end-to-end IM encryption.
- Fluency in English, both verbal and written skills, Ukrainian language would be highly beneficial.

title: Digital Workplace Platform Administrator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Candidate Verification Step:** As part of our application process, candidates are asked to complete a brief verification exercise. This will involve including a short cover letter with your application that answers the following question, written in your own words: Describe a recent AI or platform release you had to learn quickly. What did you do with it, and what happened? ***A cover letter is required for your application to be considered, and applications submitted without one cannot move forward.***   
**Why we’re asking:** This step helps us confirm that every applicant is a real person and keeps the selection process fair for all candidates. It is not part of your skills assessment, and it will take only a few minutes.

**Job Background / Overview**

The IRC is actively investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As the organization expands its use of AI platforms, including tools from Anthropic, OpenAI, and integrated data environments, the IT department is building dedicated technical capacity to keep these systems running reliably, securely, and effectively.

The IRC is investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As that investment grows, so does the need for someone to own the technical layer underneath it: the systems, integrations, and infrastructure that make AI tools work at scale.

The AI Platform Engineer is that person. This is a technical operations role, not a user-facing one. This role is responsible for keeping the IRC's enterprise AI environment running managing platform configurations and API access, building and maintaining integrations between AI tools and IRC systems, writing scripts and automations, and serving as the technical point of contact for data engineering and InfoSec. Day-to-day, this person is more likely to be reading logs, troubleshooting a broken pipeline, or pushing a configuration change than answering questions from end users.

The role works in close coordination with the AI Platform Support Director, who owns vendor relationships, licensing, and adoption strategy. This role owns the technical execution underneath that, ensuring the systems are reliable, observable, and properly connected to the rest of the IRC's data and operational environment.

**Major Responsibilities**

**AI Systems Administration & Operations (40%)**

- Serve as primary technical administrator across IRC enterprise AI environments, currently including Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI platform deployments
- Manage user access, API key governance, workspace configurations, and environment-level settings across AI platforms
- Monitor system health, usage patterns, and API performance across AI tools; triage and resolve operational issues as they arise
- Maintain and improve observability across AI systems
- Tracking uptime, error rates, token consumption, and integration reliability
- Oversee and document configuration changes, environment updates, and deployment procedures across managed platforms
- Support responsible use by flagging anomalous usage patterns and coordinating with InfoSec on policy adherence and access controls

**Integrations & Technical Implementation (35%)**

- Coordinate with the DevOps, SW Engineering and Data Engineering team(s) on deployment processes, environment access, and infrastructure dependencies required to build and maintain AI integrations
- Follow established change management procedures for all configuration changes, environment updates, and integration deployments, including documentation, testing, and appropriate approvals before pushing to production
- Develop lightweight scripts, connectors, and automations to support AI-assisted workflows across teams, primarily in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript
- Troubleshoot integration failures, data flow issues, and API connectivity problems across the AI ecosystem
- Collaborate with the data engineering team on AI/KM pipeline work, including vector store ingestion, retrieval configuration, and source data connections
- Contribute to technical design discussions with engineering partners, translating operational requirements into implementable solutions
- Maintain technical documentation for all integrations, including architecture notes, runbooks, and dependency maps

**Monitoring, Resource Optimization & InfoSec Liaison (15%)**

- Track and report on AI resource utilization across platforms, identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve cost efficiency in coordination with the AI
- Serve as the technical point of contact with the InfoSec team on matters related to AI system security, data handling, access controls, and compliance requirements
- Support risk assessments and security reviews for new AI tools or integrations by providing accurate technical context on system behavior and data flows
- Contribute to the development of technical SOPs and best-practice guidelines for AI system use, in coordination with the AI Platform Support Director and relevant stakeholders

**Stakeholder Support & Collaboration (10%)**

- Act as a technical resource for program and operations teams adopting AI tools, including answering implementation questions, supporting troubleshooting, and identifying configuration solutions
- Participate in rollout planning for new AI capabilities, providing grounded input on technical feasibility, integration requirements, and operational readiness
- Collaborate with the AI Platform Support Director on onboarding documentation and technical guidance materials for end users
- Contribute to sprint and project planning with accurate estimates on technical effort and dependencies

**Required Experience & Skills**

**AI & Cloud Platforms**

- Hands-on experience administering enterprise AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable tools), including API management, access controls, and environment configuration
- Familiarity with LLM application infrastructure: prompt pipelines, Model Context Protocol (MCP), other tool-calling integration frameworks, vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns, and embedding workflows
- Experience working with Databricks or comparable data/ML platforms is a strong plus

**Integration & Development**

- Proficiency in Python and/or JavaScript for scripting, automation, and lightweight integration work
- Experience building and maintaining REST API integrations, including authentication patterns, webhook handling, and error management
- Comfort reading and working within existing codebases without requiring significant architectural guidance
- Familiarity with version control (Git) and standard deployment practices for scripts and integrations

**Systems Administration & Monitoring**

- Experience monitoring distributed systems or SaaS platforms, including setting up alerting, reviewing logs, and diagnosing performance or availability issues
- Familiarity with usage/cost monitoring for cloud or API-based services
- Comfort operating in live production environments where reliability and data integrity are critical

**Security & Compliance**

- Working knowledge of information security principles as they apply to SaaS and API-based systems: access controls, credential management, data handling, and audit logging
- Ability to engage constructively with InfoSec teams, providing clear technical context to support reviews and risk assessments

**Collaboration & Communication**

- Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical colleagues and program staff
- Experience contributing to cross-functional teams alongside product, engineering, and operations stakeholders
- Strong documentation habits: runbooks, SOPs, architecture notes, and internal guides

**Working Environment**

This role is remote, with the possibility of in-person work depending on location. Stakeholders are located across multiple time zones (GMT-8 to GMT+3), which may require occasional early or late meetings.

**Compensation:** ($88,277 - $102,451/annual). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

 This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

 The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

 This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

 **Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

**Job Requirements:**

**Knowledge & Experience**

- 6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
- Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
- Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
- Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
- Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

**Personal Attributes**

- Spanish language proficiency
- Builds credibility quickly with leadership
- Comfortable holding ambiguity and structuring it
- Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate fluently between technical and program audiences

**Working Environment*****:***

This position is based in the US – Hybrid. The role may require travel to US and LATAM Offices as necessary.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $132,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Program Officer, Catalyst
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

Across the U.S. and Europe, IRC's Resettlement, Asylum, and Integration (RAI) department works to strengthen the systems that surround newcomers, building the capacity of service providers, governments, and communities to plan, coordinate, and deliver services more effectively. Over the past decade, this work has reached tens of thousands of learners through more than 50 projects across 13 countries and all 50 U.S. states.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer to support the implementation of Catalyst, RAI’s new systems strengthening identity. Catalyst draws on IRC's expertise in learning, research, programmatic excellence, partnerships, and AI-enabled delivery to help governments and organizations build stronger, more coordinated systems that deliver accessible, high-quality services to newcomers. Through systems strengthening work, Catalyst advances RAI's Impact@Scale priorities of Legal Services, Workforce Development, and Connected Communities.

This role will focus on project management and coordination of various Catalyst systems strengthening projects. The position will lead cross-team coordination among multiple contributors, support strategy and outreach efforts, manage deliverables using Switchboard’s project management tools, and ensure timely, high-quality completion of work across multiple initiatives. This role reports to the Senior Program Officer for Catalyst and will work closely with teams across Switchboard and the IRC.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Serve as the designated project manager for state-specific training and capacity-building initiatives.
- Manage projects across multiple teams, establishing clear processes, tracking progress, and ensuring deliverables meet internal standards, established deadlines, and funder expectations.

- Cultivate and manage relationships with internal teams and external partners, serving as a point of contact to sustain effective collaboration.

- Strong familiarity with relevant Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded programs and services, with an emphasis on state-administered programming
- Familiarity with grant-funded programming and federal funding requirements

*Skills and Competencies*

title: Health Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**APERÇU DU POSTE:** Le/la Coordinateur/trice Santé est le point focal pour l’ensemble des programmes de santé de l’IRC dans le pays. Il/elle assure le leadership stratégique et la supervision technique afin de garantir la mise en oeuvre de services de soins de santé primaires de haute qualité, y compris les services de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR), dans toutes les zones d’intervention.

Le/la titulaire du poste est responsable de définir l’orientation stratégique globale des programmes de santé lors des réponses d’urgence et d’accompagner la transition vers le relèvement et le développement à plus long terme. Il/elle joue également un rôle clé dans le développement des programmes, la mobilisation des ressources et le plaidoyer en faveur des interventions de santé de l’IRC, tout en veillant à leur conformité avec les politiques nationales et les normes internationales.

Le poste nécessite une présence régulière sur le terrain afin d’appuyer, d’accompagner et de renforcer les capacités des équipes. Le/la Coordinateur/trice Santé assure également la coordination et la représentation auprès des principales parties prenantes, notamment le Ministère de la Santé, les agences des Nations Unies et les ONG, tout en veillant à l’alignement des interventions avec les orientations stratégiques de l’IRC.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**Qualité technique et gestion des programmes – 25 %**

- Fournir, conjointement avec les partenaires de l’IRC, un leadership stratégique et technique pour les programmes de santé mis en œuvre en Haïti, en veillant à leur alignement avec les politiques organisationnelles, les normes nationales et les bonnes pratiques internationales.
- Veiller à la fourniture d’un paquet complet de soins de santé primaires intégrant une composante forte de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR), conformément au Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP).
- Superviser la conception, la mise en œuvre et la qualité des programmes de santé, de SSR et de nutrition des partenaires, en collaboration avec l’équipe Santé d’Urgence, le/la Directeur/trice Adjoint/e des Programmes (DDP) et les équipes de terrain.
- Veiller à ce que tous les programmes de santé financés par l’IRC atteignent leurs objectifs grâce à un suivi, une évaluation et une amélioration continue de la qualité efficace.
- Suivre la mise en œuvre des programmes par rapport aux plans de travail, aux indicateurs de performance et aux budgets, en veillant au respect des échéances et à la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives nécessaires.
- Veiller au respect des protocoles et directives cliniques standardisés définis par le Ministère de la Santé, l’OMS et l’IRC.
- Superviser et promouvoir l’utilisation rationnelle des médicaments et les bonnes pratiques de prescription dans l’ensemble des services de santé soutenus.
- En coordination avec les équipes des partenaires chargées du renforcement des capacités, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, de la pharmacie et de la logistique médicale, superviser la prévision des besoins, l’approvisionnement, la distribution et la redevabilité concernant les intrants médicaux.
- Veiller à la bonne supervision des systèmes de chaîne d’approvisionnement, notamment la gestion des stocks, les commandes en temps opportun, l’entreposage et l’utilisation appropriée des médicaments et consommables médicaux.

**Renforcement institutionnel et représentation – 5 %**

- Développer la programmation de l’IRC Haïti entièrement dirigée par les partenaires, en renforçant le rôle technique des partenaires nationaux et locaux en tant que co-responsables de la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Renforcer le rôle des partenaires nationaux et locaux dans l’évaluation et l’adaptation des programmes de santé existants afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des bénéficiaires et aux réalités du contexte.
- Renforcer et harmoniser la représentation des partenaires nationaux et locaux dans les instances stratégiques et les espaces de coordination avec les principales parties prenantes, notamment les bailleurs, les autorités gouvernementales et les agences des Nations Unies.
- Développer et maintenir des relations stratégiques avec les principales parties prenantes, notamment les bailleurs, les autorités gouvernementales, les agences des Nations Unies ainsi que les partenaires internationaux et locaux.
- Représenter l’organisation dans les mécanismes de coordination nationaux et infranationaux, notamment au sein du Groupe sectoriel Santé (Health Cluster) et des groupes de travail sur la santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR).
- Renforcer la collaboration et le partage d’informations entre les partenaires afin de garantir une réponse coordonnée, cohérente et efficace dans les domaines de la santé et de la santé sexuelle et reproductive.
- Promouvoir et défendre la qualité des programmes de santé et de SSR, conformément aux normes, principes et priorités humanitaires.

**Supervision et développement du personnel – 10 %**

- Assurer le leadership stratégique et la supervision des équipes de santé dans l’ensemble des zones d’intervention, afin de garantir une mise en œuvre de qualité des programmes.
- Assurer la supervision hiérarchique des cadres supérieurs de santé, notamment les Health Managers, en veillant à la gestion de la performance, au coaching et à la redevabilité. • Diriger la planification des ressources humaines et appuyer le recrutement des postes clés en santé en coordination avec les RH et la haute direction.
- Élaborer des stratégies de renforcement des capacités et veiller à la mise en œuvre de formations structurées, de mentorat et d’initiatives de développement professionnel.

 **Développement des programmes, gestion des subventions et rapportage – 15 %**

- Assurer la supervision stratégique de la mise en œuvre des subventions, en veillant à leur alignement avec les plans de travail, les plans de dépenses et les cadres de suivi-évaluation. • Veiller à l’intégration et aux liens entre la santé/SSR et les autres secteurs, notamment la Protection.
- Veiller au respect des exigences des bailleurs en étroite coordination avec les équipes Opérations, Finance et Grants.
- En coordination avec l’équipe MEAL, établir et renforcer les systèmes de supervision des programmes, de contrôle qualité et de reporting pour les programmes de santé.
- Veiller à la production dans les délais de rapports internes et de rapports destinés aux bailleurs, de haute qualité, portant sur les activités, les indicateurs et les résultats des programmes.
- Superviser le suivi budgétaire et des dépenses, notamment à travers la revue régulière des écarts entre budget et dépenses réelles en collaboration avec les équipes programmes.
- Diriger l’élaboration des stratégies des programmes de santé, en assurant une forte intégration de la SSR et un alignement avec le MISP.
- Contribuer à la stratégie globale du programme pays, en veillant à son alignement avec les priorités organisationnelles et les besoins du contexte.
- En complément de l’expertise des partenaires, identifier les opportunités d’expansion des programmes et diriger les évaluations et analyses techniques nécessaires à la conception conjointe de programmes fondés sur les données probantes.
- Diriger l’élaboration de notes conceptuelles, propositions et budgets de haute qualité, conformément aux priorités des bailleurs et à la stratégie de l’IRC.
- Coordonner avec les équipes Grants, Finance, Opérations et techniques afin de garantir la soumission dans les délais de propositions conformes et compétitives.

**Partenariats – 30 %**

- Promouvoir une culture de partenariats efficaces et respectueux et favoriser la programmation dirigée par les partenaires, conformément aux approches de l’IRC « Why not Partner? » et « Partner as equals ».
- Veiller à ce que les considérations liées aux partenariats soient intégrées dans le plan global de réponse aux urgences et à ce que les partenaires locaux participent activement à la conception et à la mise en œuvre des programmes.
- Participer à l’identification des partenaires potentiels et au processus d’analyse des parties prenantes.
- Contribuer activement aux sections pertinentes de l’analyse des capacités des partenaires (PCA) et à l’élaboration des plans d’appui aux partenaires qui en découlent.
- Diriger et/ou soutenir la conception collaborative des projets et des budgets avec les partenaires.
- Veiller à ce que chaque conception de programme définisse l’approche d’urgence de l’IRC en fonction de la manière dont l’organisation peut au mieux soutenir, renforcer et compléter les acteurs locaux.
- Veiller à une allocation budgétaire appropriée permettant à l’IRC de soutenir les partenaires conformément à la conception globale de la réponse et des programmes.
- Examiner et fournir des retours sur les outils techniques, rapports et données des partenaires, selon les besoins, et collaborer avec eux sur les adaptations et améliorations nécessaires.
- Participer activement au Partnership Working Group (PWG).

**Suivi et évaluation – 15 %**

- Assurer la supervision stratégique des fonctions de suivi et d’évaluation de l’ensemble des programmes de santé, en veillant à leur conformité avec les exigences de l’IRC et des bailleurs.
- Veiller à la production dans les délais de rapports internes et de rapports destinés aux bailleurs sur la performance des programmes, les indicateurs et les résultats.
- Superviser les processus de collecte et de reporting des données afin d’en garantir l’exactitude, l’exhaustivité et la cohérence.
- Orienter le développement et le renforcement des cadres, systèmes et outils de suivi-évaluation en collaboration avec les équipes MEAL.
- Promouvoir l’utilisation des données et des données probantes pour améliorer la qualité des programmes, éclairer la prise de décision et orienter la stratégie.

**Sauvegarde**

- Intégrer l’analyse des risques liés à la sauvegarde ainsi que les mesures d’atténuation appropriées dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Maintenir à jour la cartographie multisectorielle des services et les mécanismes d’orientation pour la réponse aux violences.

**Programmation sûre, inclusive et transformatrice (SIT)**

- Diriger et/ou conseiller sur l’analyse contextuelle adaptée aux besoins, notamment en matière d’intersectionnalité, de pouvoir, de bien-être et de barrières à l’accès, et utiliser les résultats pour orienter la conception des programmes et les mesures d’accès pour les groupes à risque.
- Soutenir la participation significative des personnes exposées aux risques d’exclusion dans la planification, la mise en œuvre et le suivi.
- Soutenir l’engagement avec les organisations représentatives et les approches communautaires.
- Promouvoir une mise en œuvre inclusive et, lorsque cela est pertinent, transformatrice, conformément aux standards IMPACT.
- Renforcer le suivi-évaluation afin de mesurer l’inclusion, le bien-être et les résultats pour les bénéficiaires.
- Contribuer aux données probantes et aux apprentissages du SIT Community of Practice.

**Autres responsabilités**

- Assurer une supervision régulière de la sécurité et de la sûreté des équipes de terrain, signaler rapidement les préoccupations ou incidents et coordonner avec les parties prenantes concernées.
- Veiller au respect des protocoles organisationnels de sécurité et de sûreté dans l’ensemble des activités des programmes de santé.
- Exécuter toute autre tâche assignée par le/la superviseur/e afin de soutenir la mise en œuvre efficace et le développement stratégique des programmes de l’IRC.

**Culture d’équipe**

- Diriger et favoriser une équipe de santé collaborative, redevable et performante dans l’ensemble des zones d’intervention.
- Promouvoir une culture de qualité, d’équité et de soins centrés sur le patient, en veillant à ce que les services soient fournis avec dignité et respect.
- Créer un environnement favorable à l’apprentissage continu, au mentorat et au développement professionnel du personnel.
- Faire preuve d’intégrité et de professionnalisme et respecter les principes éthiques et humanitaires dans tous les aspects du travail.

**Relations professionnelles clés**

- Supérieur hiérarchique : Directeur/trice Adjoint/e des Programmes (DDP)
- Supervision directe : Health Managers et Nutrition Managers
- Lien fonctionnel : Senior Technical Advisor
- Autres contacts : Départements sectoriels

**Qualifications requises**

**Formation:** Diplôme en santé publique ou qualification dans un domaine de la santé (médecine, soins infirmiers, maïeutique, etc.), avec une qualification de troisième cycle en santé publique ou dans un domaine connexe de préférence.

**Expérience professionnelle :**

- Minimum de 3 à 5 ans d’expérience progressive dans la programmation en santé, notamment en soins de santé primaires et en SSR.
- Bonne compréhension du Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) pour la santé reproductive en situation de crise.
- Expérience dans la conception de programmes, l’élaboration de stratégies et la préparation de propositions.
- Expérience en leadership d’équipe, notamment dans la supervision de cadres supérieurs et d’équipes multidisciplinaires.
- Expérience de la coordination avec les autorités gouvernementales, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG et autres parties prenantes.
- Expérience en gestion de subventions, reporting aux bailleurs et supervision budgétaire.
- Expérience de travail avec des équipes et communautés diverses, notamment les femmes, les jeunes, les personnes handicapées et autres groupes exposés aux risques d’exclusion.

**Compétences et aptitudes**

- Excellentes compétences informatiques, notamment dans MS Word, Excel
- Solides compétences en leadership et en gestion d’équipe, avec la capacité de diriger, encadrer et développer des équipes diverses.
- Solides compétences en coordination, représentation et gestion des partenariats.
- Capacité à analyser les données et à utiliser les données probantes pour la prise de décision et l’amélioration des programmes.
- Excellentes compétences en communication, rédaction de rapports et relations interpersonnelles.
- Capacité à travailler sous pression et à s’adapter à des environnements complexes et d’urgence.
- Intérêt et engagement démontrés en faveur de la collaboration et des partenariats avec les acteurs locaux dans les situations d’urgence.
- Engagement démontré en faveur de l’égalité de genre, de la diversité et de l’inclusion dans les contextes humanitaires.
- Capacité à identifier et à traiter les obstacles à l’inclusion des groupes marginalisés et sous-représentés dans les réponses d’urgence.
- Engagement en faveur de l’apprentissage continu et de la réflexion sur les biais personnels et organisationnels.
- Haut niveau d’intégrité, de professionnalisme et d’engagement envers les principes humanitaires.

**Langues**

Maîtrise du français et/ou d’autres langues requises.

**Égalité de genre**

L’IRC s’engage à réduire les écarts entre les femmes et les hommes dans les postes de leadership et met en place des mesures favorisant la participation des femmes à sa main-d’oeuvre, notamment des congés parentaux, des protocoles de sécurité sensibles au genre ainsi que d’autres avantages et allocations de soutien.

L’IRC est un employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances. L’IRC examine toutes les candidatures sur la base des compétences et du mérite, sans distinction fondée sur la race, le sexe, la couleur de peau, l’origine nationale, la religion, l’orientation sexuelle, l’âge, la situation matrimoniale, le statut d’ancien combattant, le handicap ou toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**COMMENT POSTULER**

Pour commencer le processus de candidature, les candidats sont tenus d'envoyer leur CV à : adminRH.haiti@rescue.org Les candidatures doivent être envoyées à l'adresse e-mail ci-dessus avec un CV et une lettre de motivation au plus tard le 15 octobre 2026.

Objet du mail indiqué comme : « HEALTH COORDINATOR » En raison du grand nombre de candidatures reçues pour tous les postes publiés, seuls les candidats présélectionnés pour un entretien seront contactés. IRC Haïti ne facture aucun frais à aucune étape du processus de recrutement. Toute sollicitation dans le processus de recrutement entraîne la disqualification.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Expression of Interest for Various Roles - El Niño Response
body:
**Work on a global humanitarian program contributing to saving lives and alleviating suffering.**

Australia Assists is an Australian Government program that deploys skilled humanitarian specialists to support multilateral agencies, governments, civil society and communities to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters and conflict. Australia Assists’ Goal is to: Save lives, alleviate suffering, and maintain human dignity during and in the aftermath of conflict, disasters and other humanitarian crises, and strengthen preparedness for the occurrence of such situations. The program’s Objective is: Targeted deployment of humanitarian expertise that meets the priorities and needs of Australia's multilateral, bilateral and civil society partners and advances Australia's international humanitarian priorities.

For more information [please visit our website.](https://www.australiaassists.org/)

**The Opportunity:**

- Location: Indo-Pacific – Remote support may also be required
- Duration: \[TBC – e.g. 1–6 months per deployment\], with availability to deploy at short notice (within 3–4 weeks)
- Contract type: Employment or Consultancy Agreements where applicable, with guaranteed inclusion to the Australia Assists Humanitarian Roster.

*Submitting an EOI and being assessed as suitable may result in inclusion in a pool of potential suppliers; however, **this does not guarantee paid work or engagement**. Future assignments will be offered as opportunities arise.*

**The Role:**

A very strong El Niño is now established in the Pacific and is forecast to persist into early 2027, alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole. Together these are expected to drive drought, water shortages, heat stress, food insecurity, fire and disease risk across much of the Indo-Pacific, while increasing the risk of localised flooding and tropical cyclones elsewhere. These hazards will compound existing vulnerabilities, and impacts are likely to persist well after the El Niño event peaks.

Through this EOI, we seek experienced technical specialists in:

- Water, Sanitation and Hygiene
- Drought Response and Management
- Hydrology and Hydrogeology
- Climate Resilience and Climate Services
- Food Security and Nutrition
- Climate Smart Agriculture and Livelihoods

Successful candidates will join our deployment roster. Roster members may be deployed to support partner governments, regional bodies, UN agencies and civil society organisations to:

- Rapidly scale anticipatory action and preparedness as well as possible response and early recovery
- Protect water, food and livelihood security for affected communities
- Embed climate risk information and resilience into response and recovery, so short-term action reduces longer-term vulnerability
- Strengthen local and national capacity through mentoring, co-design and knowledge transfer

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Provide technical advice and surge support to host partners in the deployees area of expertise
- Undertake rapid assessments and analysis to inform anticipatory action, response and early recovery planning
- Support coordination with national systems and cluster/sector mechanisms, and across sectors
- Strengthen local and national capacity through mentoring, training and co-delivery
- Ensure cross-cutting priorities (GEDSI, Climate Resilience, Localisation, First Nations) are integrated in all work
- Produce timely technical products, reports and recommendations
- Other tasks as specified in the tailored TOR

**Selection Criteria**

**All applicants must demonstrate:**

- Minimum 8 years' relevant technical experience, including preferably at least 2 years in disaster risk reduction, humanitarian, resilience or development contexts in low- and middle-income countries.
- Demonstrated experience applying technical expertise in drought, water scarcity, climate-related emergencies, disaster response, recovery, resilience programming or other relevant technical fields.
- Proven ability to work with and through national governments, local authorities, communities and local partners, with a strong commitment to localisation.
- Demonstrated experience in assessment, planning, implementation, monitoring and coordination of humanitarian, disaster response, recovery or resilience initiatives.
- Experience using evidence, data, monitoring systems, forecasting, risk analysis or technical assessments to support preparedness, decision-making and response activities.
- Experience working in remote, resource-constrained and culturally diverse settings, including in the Pacific and/or Southeast Asia.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, including the ability to translate technical information into practical guidance for decision-makers, communities and non-technical audiences.
- Relevant tertiary qualifications and technical expertise related to the nominated area of specialisation.
- Desirable: previous El Niño, drought or climate-related emergency response experience; experience working with National Disaster Management Offices (NDMOs), government technical agencies, UN agencies, coordination mechanisms or cluster systems.

**Applicants are only required to address the selection criteria relevant to their nominated technical area(s).**

There may be a need for other technical specialists beyond those identified here. If you have experience you believe may be relevant, please submit your profile. **Pacific and Southeast Asian nationals are strongly encouraged to apply.**

For a complete position description please click [here](https://intdev.tetratech.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/AA-PD-Various-Roles-El-Nino-Response.pdf).

title: Global Surge Team Roster: Emergency Deputy Director of People & Culture
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 30 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

The IRC’s Global Surge Team (GST) is a Roster of highly qualified humanitarian professionals who deploy on short notice to emergency and non‑emergency contexts to support the IRC’s mission. GST members provide specialized, time‑bound support where capacity gaps exist, typically for deployments of up to three months.

**The GST Roster is a flexible, OCCASIONAL employment opportunity. Deployment needs vary based on demand. Staff can take on additional deployments as opportunities arise and if they are interested.**

Deployment opportunities depend on organizational and operational requirements and may vary over time; as such, deployments cannot be guaranteed. Staff supporting emergency responses must be prepared to deploy within 72 hours as needs arise.

Members of the GST Roster who specialize in emergencies are deployed to support either existing country programs in their emergency response, or to initiate a new program in the crisis zone. The overall responsibility of the team is to design, develop, and manage the IRC’s on-site humanitarian response, allowing us to meet the immediate needs of the affected population rapidly and effectively.

**Job overview:**

The Emergency Deputy Director of People and Culture, Global Surge (Emergency DD P&C) leads all People and Culture (P&C) work in the assigned response during an emergency. The Emergency DD P&C is responsible for the overall leadership and supervisory management of the response’s P&C team, systems, and services, including workforce planning, policy compliance, staff care and well-being, safeguarding and GEDI commitments, performance management, and handover to sustainable country P&C operations.

In this role, you will be directly responsible for rapidly establishing and scaling P&C structures and a safe, inclusive workplace culture; serving as strategic advisor to the Emergency Country Director and the Senior Management Team; providing oversight for Country Program’s staff; leading emergency recruitment, onboarding, and employee relations in line with IRC policies and local labor law; ensuring accurate and timely payroll, people data, and reporting; and partnering with the Emergency Unit, regional, and global P&C teams to adapt policies and tools to the emergency context.

***The Emergency DD P&C is expected to be deployed in the field, either in an emergency or roving capacity, and must be able to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification, and for up to 12 weeks.***

**Major responsibilities**

**Emergency set-up and scale-up**

- Rapidly establish P&C structures, processes and tools for the response, including employment registration, labor law compliance, contract templates, national staff terms and payroll set-up.
- Conduct a quick review of the local labor and salary market, and recommend a competitive, compliant compensation approach for the response.
- Lead emergency recruitment and onboarding at volume. Coordinate with the Emergency Unit, regional and global P&C teams to deploy surge and roster staff and fill priority national and international positions quickly.
- Co-lead workforce planning and organizational design with the SMT, including rapid scale-ups and adjustments, in line with legal requirements and IRC policies.
- Set up a simple headcount, vacancy and recruitment tracker, and report to leadership on a regular, short cycle.

**Strategic leadership and management**

- Serve as strategic advisor to the Emergency Country Director and the SMT on workforce strategy, compliance and organizational culture, aligned with response priorities.
- Lead, supervise and support the P&C team, including deployed and national P&C colleagues. Remain accountable for the quality and timeliness of P&C services.
- Coach managers on supervision, performance expectations and difficult conversations in high-pressure conditions.
- Advise supervisors on disciplinary matters, act as an impartial mediator, and ensure fairness and compliance with labor regulations.
- Escalate code of conduct issues, and lead or co-lead investigations with the Employee Relations unit and, when needed, the Ethics and Compliance unit.

**P&C operations**

- Ensure context-specific practices in recruitment, compensation and benefits, employee relations, onboarding and offboarding, contract and leave management, and HR information systems.
- Implement IRC People and Culture policies across the response and adapt them to the emergency context, with Regional and Global Surge Team P&C support.
- Ensure accurate and timely payroll and compensation for all staff.
- Contribute expert input on staffing structures and position scoping to proposal design and grant review.
- Where partners are part of the response, provide technical P&C guidance in line with the PEERS framework.

**GEDI and safeguarding**

- Ensure inclusive, fair recruitment and onboarding, and promote a workplace free of discrimination, harassment, bullying and abuse of power.
- Integrate safeguarding into rapid hiring and onboarding, including delivery of the Safeguarding Minimum Standards.
- Ensure all staff receive orientation on the Safeguarding Policy and the IRC Way, with reporting channels visible in all offices in relevant local languages.
- Partner with global investigations teams and response leadership to implement recommendations from safeguarding investigations, particularly disciplinary actions, within two weeks.

**Duty of care and staff well-being**

- With the Duty of Care team, provide guidance on staff duty of care.
- Partner with Safety and Security to ensure best-practice aftercare following critical incidents.
- Develop plans to support the physical and psychological well-being of staff in high-stress, high-risk contexts, including R&R and rotation arrangements.
- Set up engagement and communication approaches suited to fast-changing, remote and insecure environments, including listening sessions.

**Transition and handover**

- Plan and deliver the transition from emergency to sustainable country P&C operations, including a documented handover to incoming long-term P&C staff.
- Coach national P&C colleagues so they can take over core processes.
- Contribute lessons learned to refine IRC emergency P&C policies, SOPs and toolkits.

**Other**

- Support the Emergency Country Director with ad hoc tasks as needed.
- Stay alert to irregularities in operational and administrative procedures and uphold organizational standards.

**Job Requirements:**

You should have strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and be able to communicate effectively, both internally and externally. You should enjoy building trusted relationships with leadership teams, colleagues and partners, and adapting P&C practice to fast-moving contexts.

- Graduate degree in HR management or a related field preferred.
- At least 10 years of progressive P&C experience, including leadership of a P&C function supporting small, medium and large scale Country Programs across multiple locations in an emergency Context.
- Experience working in conflict, post-conflict or disaster response settings, including rapid start-up or scale-up of P&C operations.
- Prior experience working within organizational structures in transition.

**Demonstrated technical skills:**

- Broad knowledge of P&C competencies: recruitment, compensation and benefits, employee relations, contract management, payroll, performance management and HR information systems.
- Working knowledge of international labor law and the ability to establish compliant employment practices quickly in a new country context.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding and deployment of surge and national staff at volume.
- Experience in handling employee relations, safeguarding and code of conduct cases, including coordination with investigations teams.
- Knowledge of duty of care and staff well-being practices in high-risk, high-stress contexts, and the ability to work with security teams on staff safety.
- Ability to use people data and analysis to inform decisions, producing simple, timely reporting.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel, Word and Outlook. Working knowledge of Workday or other HR information systems, and of file-sharing platforms such as SharePoint, is an advantage.

**Demonstrated managerial and leadership competencies:**

- Demonstrated experience advising senior leaders, such as Country Directors and SMTs, and building strong, trusted relationships.
- Demonstrated successful leadership of multi-disciplinary teams in cross-cultural settings, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Ability to build the capacity of national P&C colleagues and hand over systems and responsibilities effectively.
- Ability to supervise in matrixed, remote and fast-changing environments.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner, and to model and promote staff well-being.
- High levels of integrity, empathy and sound judgment on sensitive matters.
- Opportunity-awareness: a successful, innovative approach to unpredictable operational, staffing and funding contexts.
- Ability to represent the P&C context, constraints and successes clearly to senior internal and external audiences, including regulators and government authorities.

**Language and travel**

- English is required. French, Arabic, Spanish are highly desired.
- Ability to deploy within 72 hours of notification.

 **Working Environment**

IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

 **Gender Equality**: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

 **Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Coordinator for a Medical Project (Volunteer Coordination & Health Education)
body:
**Med’EqualiTeam** is a French non-profit organization, created in July 2018. Our aim is to provide free health care to displaced populations, who wouldn’t otherwise have access to it due to any kind of barriers or lack of physicians. We are a volunteer based NGO, with most of the staff coming for short period of term in order to support with their medical or translation skills.

We are running since December 2023 a [**project in Northern Greece**](https://www.medequali.team/en/projects/medical-help-thessaloniki/), with mobile medical units reaching out to different centers to provide medical consultations. We also run a Health Education program with first aid trainings and sessions about health topics designed for the community.

## *Job description*

This is a combined role of two coordination branches: Volunteer Coordination & Health Education Coordination.

### **1) Volunteer Coordination**

Are you someone with **great people skills**, **experience in the humanitarian sector**, and a (academic/professional) **background relevant to our medical project** in Thessaloniki e.g., medicine, public health, psychology, social work, etc.?

Then you might be our next *Volunteer Coordinator* managing our volunteer team on the ground in Northern Greece! This role focuses on recruiting qualified volunteers, composing a compatible medical team, supervising volunteer wellbeing, and managing the project’s HR tasks. This role is a great opportunity to gain project management experience in the medical humanitarian field and further hone your leadership skills.

*Job description:*

- Advertise new positions with recruitment partners
- Implement existing processes for recruitment and on-boarding of new (medical) volunteers; registration and evaluation of applications, holding interviews, composing the volunteer team, organising travel and accommodation logistics, conducting volunteer inductions on the ground, conducting check-in and exit chats, etc.
- Gather and implement volunteer feedback
- Coordinate the recruitment and onboarding of community translators
- Organise volunteer schedules in collaboration with the Medical Coordinator and Field Coordinator
- Look out for the wellbeing of volunteers and coordinate wellbeing activities
- Ensure professional behaviour and respect of MET code of conduct by all volunteers
- Ensure the safe storage and confidentiality of all HR data and information according to MET’s processes
- Be the on-site coordinator and manage the reception for approximately 1-2 clinics a week: register patients, coordinate clinic translation and medical volunteers, and manage on-site safety

### **2) Health Education Coordination**

Are you interested in improving the health of asylum seeker and refugee communities through education and empowerment? We are seeking a volunteer with an **interest in training** **and education** to coordinate the health education branch of our medical project in Northern Greece; where we provide first aid training sessions for NGO volunteers and health education sessions to displaced communities across Northern Greece. This role is a great opportunity to develop your coordination and education skills and use your medical experience to deliver preventative health measures.

*Job description:*

- Plan and coordinate first aid trainings and health education sessions with NGO partners across Northern Greece.
- Lead in developing and delivering sessions with support of the medical volunteer team; designing training materials (presentations, leaflets etc.), overseeing translations, conducting focus groups, etc.
- Work with the medical coordinator to shape the strategy of health education and training
- Implement service evaluation protocols by gathering and processing feedback from attendees of sessions to improve the service

*As a key position, we ask for a minimum of **9 months** commitment. The **starting date is 10th of January 2027** with 2 weeks of handover with the current coordinator.*

***This is a volunteer position with a stipend - we cannot facilitate entry into Greece or obtain a visa.***

## ***Required experience and skills***

- Fluency in English
- Minimum time commitment of 6 months
- Strong organizational and administration skills
- Strong communication and reporting skills
- Strong interpersonal and intercultural skills
- A high level of personal organization, flexibility and resilience
- Capable of working independently, while knowing your professional limits and asking for help if needed
- Commitment to humanitarian principles and to MET’s mandate
- A driving licence and experience driving a manual car
- Proficiency on computer (Office pack, PowerPoint, Canva)

## Desired experience and skills

- Experience in HR and in working with volunteers
- Healthcare professional (or student in a health field)
- Previous experience working or volunteering with displaced or vulnerable people
- Previous work experience in NGOs/INGOs
- Experience providing education/training sessions
- Knowledge of locally relevant languages (Greek, Arabic, Farsi, Turkish)

## Benefits of working with Med'EqualiTeam

- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- A highly rewarding and meaningful job
- Work in a multilingual environment
- Work in a highly adaptive NGO context to meet the medical needs of displaced people
- Contribute to improving the lives of refugees and vulnerable populations
- Accommodation in Thessaloniki in a shared flat, transport to the mission site and emergency health insurance provided.
- Please note that this is a voluntary position, which comes with a basic stipend to cover living expenses. Unfortunately, we cannot offer a salary.

title: Supply Chain intern
body:
## Join MSF OCG as a Supply Chain intern!

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 12 months at 100%

### Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women.
