title: Kiwa Regional Technical Assistance Coordinator
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Climate Change and Sustainability (CCS)** division strengthens and streamlines SPC’s actions on climate change by bringing together work already undertaken by the organisation under a coherent strategic and technical leadership. In addition, it leads the actions of SPC on climate change and sustainability, works with SPC’s regional and international partners and promotes the integration of these issues into all development activities conducted by its divisions.

The **Kiwa Regional Technical Assistance Coordinator** will coordinate SPC’s delivery of the Kiwa Initiative Phase II Regional Technical Assistance, providing overall coordination of programme activities, technical oversight for ecosystem and forest restoration interventions, and ensuring effective administration and financial management of the financing agreement. The position will work closely with SPC’s Land Resources Division to support the technical quality and implementation of restoration activities and liaise with the dedicated GEDSI Adviser within the Human Rights and Social Development Division to promote inclusive, equitable and socially responsive approaches across all activities.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Coordination & Financial Management**

- Coordinating SPC’s delivery of the Kiwa Technical Assistance, ensuring coherence across restoration, GEDSI, and knowledge-sharing components.
- Acting as focal point with the Kiwa Secretariat, AFD, SPREP, and other partners.
- Preparing and submitting progress reports, ensuring accuracy of technical and financial data.
- Overseeing the financing agreement, including budgeting, expenditure tracking, and audits.
- Coordinating with SPC’s Finance, Procurement, MEL, and Legal units to ensure compliance with SPC and donor standards.
- Ensuring timely responses to requests from AFD, the Kiwa Secretariat, and partners.

**Capacity Strengthening and Technical Oversight for Forest and Ecosystem Restoration**

- Providing technical oversight on ecosystem/forest restoration, in close partnership with LRD.
- Identifying specific needs from Kiwa’s grantees and partners.
- Guiding the design, delivery, and monitoring of the restoration-focused micro-qualification.
- Supporting targeted capacity building activities for Kiwa’s grantees and partners including national forestry/environment departments.
- Documenting lessons learned and best practices on restoration approaches.
- Ensuring restoration work integrates NbS principles and is scientifically sound and context-specific.

**GEDSI Integration**

- Working in collaboration with the GEDSI Adviser from HRSD.
- Ensuring GEDSI principles are systematically embedded across restoration and NbS activities.
- In collaboration with HRSD GEDSI Adviser, supporting Kiwa grantees to unpack, scale up, and mainstream GEDSI in their NbS projects.
- Facilitating the production of GEDSI-related tools, case studies, and knowledge products.
- Promoting inclusive participation and equitable access in all Kiwa-supported training and events.

**Stakeholder Engagement & Regional Knowledge Sharing**

- Fostering peer-to-peer learning and regional knowledge exchange on restoration and GEDSI.
- Coordinating the development and dissemination of case studies, knowledge products, and communication materials.
- Promoting Pacific-led restoration and inclusive NbS practices at regional and international events.
- Engaging with government agencies, NGOs, and training institutions to strengthen ownership and uptake.
- Ensuring alignment with SPC’s communications strategy and Kiwa visibility requirements.
- Identifying opportunities and supporting resource mobilisation to scale up restoration efforts in the Pacific.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Postgraduate degree in environmental management, forestry, natural resources management, climate change, or a related field, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 8 years of professional experience in forestry, ecosystem restoration, climate change adaptation, biodiversity conservation, or NbS programming.
- Experience in project management and coordination of multi-partner, donor-funded initiatives, including work planning, reporting, and budget oversight.
- Proven technical expertise in forest and ecosystem restoration, covering practical restoration practices (such as seed collection, nursery management, propagation, site preparation, and species selection in tropical and island ecosystems) as well as capacity building and applied training in Pacific or similar contexts.
- Experience engaging with government forestry/environment departments, universities, and training institutions in the Pacific.
- Experience coordinating cross-cutting functions such as GEDSI integration into technical programmes.
- Good communication skills across multicultural and multi-stakeholder environments.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in English (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Solid understanding of the Pacific region, including political, cultural, environmental, and socio-economic contexts.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted until 31 December 2029 and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Kiwa Regional Technical Assistance Coordinator** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,703‒3,379 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 8,354–10,442 (USD 3,623-4,528; EUR 3,269-4,086). Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

title: Yemen - Deputy Country Director for Operations - Aden
body:
**Desired start date : 15/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission : 6 months**  
**Location : Yemen mission - Based in Aden Coordination with regular travel to bases in Marib, West Coast (Al Mokha) and Taiz**

## **About us**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SI opened its mission in Yemen in 2017, establishing its coordination office in Aden. Since then, SI has expanded the geographical scope of its interventions, establishing three operational field bases in Al Mokha, Taiz and Marib, with additional operational presence in Hodeidah and Abyan Governorates. The mission has a forecast budget of approximately EUR 11 million for 2027 and comprises approximately 4 expatriate and 70 national staff.

The mission’s objectives for 2027 are to expand into hard-to-reach areas and deliver quality interventions responding to emergency and protracted needs, while enhancing its longer-term resilience and development portfolio to strengthen water and natural resource management, food systems and livelihoods.

SI is currently implementing 11 projects in Yemen, financed by ECHO, UN-OCHA, CDCS, SDC, DG MENA, FCDO and private donors. SI implements emergency and resilience WASH programmes, including water trucking, rehabilitation of water networks, construction of emergency latrines and showers, distribution of hygiene kits, hygiene promotion and cleaning campaigns. Under its FSL portfolio, SI provides unconditional, multipurpose cash assistance to IDPs and host communities and supports livelihoods through income-generating and CASH+ activities.

In 2027 SI intends to further strengthen and expand its longer-term, integrated development portfolio. It’s current development portfolio is supported by DG MENA and SDC funding, to strengthen water and natural resource management, job creation, agroecological practices, food production, financial inclusion and market access. SI will further strengthen its current partnership approach with national and international organisations, building on complementary expertise, local knowledge and shared objectives. This will include strengthening joint programme design and delivery, mutual capacity sharing and the role of national partners in shaping locally led, sustainable responses.

Reports to: Country Director.

Direct reports: Base Managers/ Head of Bases of all operational bases

Coordinates closely with programme and support departments and Security / Humanitarian Access;

Staffing numbers by base: Marib 12/ ALM 24 / TAIZ: 15

SI was among the first humanitarian actors to access the West Coast and continues to operate in hard-to-reach areas close to the frontlines in Marib, Hodeidah and Maqbanah. SI aims to maintain this operational positioning and further expand its presence to reach underserved communities.

## About the job

### **General objective:**

Lead SI operations in Marib, Al Mokha/West Coast and Taiz, ensuring quality implementation, resource management, compliance, accountability and follow-up of audits. Supervise Base Managers/Heads of Base and support operational planning. Coordinate closely with programme, support and security teams on access, risk management and programme continuity. Maintain strong security management and negotiation with authorities and tribes. Support partnerships, representation, country strategy and assess the potential opening of a new base in DFA-controlled areas in the North.

### **The main challenges:**

Marib, Taiz and Al Mokha face significant security risks due to proximity to frontlines and the presence of multiple armed groups. Each area is governed by different authorities, making stakeholder engagement and coordination essential. Strengthening and enforcing security management systems is a priority.

The bases benefit from experienced management teams, although some functions oversee multiple locations. Taiz is rapidly expanding its portfolio and operational footprint. For 2026-2027, the context requires a stronger nexus, resilience and consortium-based approach. Planned growth includes humanitarian, resilience and livelihood programmes funded by donors such as ECHO, EU, PRO, CDCS and potentially SDRPY and SDC. Localization remains a key priority, with four new local partners being onboarded and additional partnerships planned with universities and research institutions. Increasing access constraints due to shifting territorial control require sustained negotiations with conflict parties.

### **Priorities for the first 2-3 months:**

1. Review programme delivery, budgets, staffing, access challenges and key commitments across all bases; establish priority action plans and regular operational reviews.
2. Strengthen business continuity and access arrangements with the Country Director and Security/Humanitarian Access teams. Assess options for a potential DFA/northern base, including location, legal requirements, costs, staffing and feasibility.
3. Build staff capacity, particularly to support the nationalisation of Head of Base positions.
4. Expand local and international partnerships to improve access to new operational areas.

### **Security constraints:**

Security conditions are particularly critical in Taiz and Hodeidah, two active frontline areas hosting over 2 million displaced people, including nearly 300,000 recent IDPs. Strict security measures apply across Taiz, West Coast and Marib, with some areas inaccessible to international staff. Curfews generally run from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., with slight adjustments in Aden depending on daily security assessments.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCES :**

Diploma : Diploma (BA or MA) in relevant field (Political science, international relations or other)

Experiment in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experiment on similar positions : 0-2 years

**SKILLS :**

Technical skills :

1. Knowledge and experience of Yemen or Middle East appreciated
2. Leadership and. Management skills including: Multi-base operational leadership, project-cycle management, resource planning and programme quality; Managing and coacing staff
3. Security management, negotiation skills and Compliance management skills: Access negotiation, context and risk analysis, continuity planning and preparation of new bases, Internal controls and audit coordination

Transversal skills :

1. Multi projects and multi donors management experience
2. Strong interpersonal skills and problem solving capacity, anticipation and self-organization capacities
3. Great drive to achieve results and stress management capacities, willingness to work in complex and violatile environment

**Languages :**

1. Fluency in written and oral English mandatory
2. Arabic an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every two months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Living conditions – Accommodation is in SI rented guesthouse in Al Mokha and Taiz City, with offices being in the same location. Both offices are shard with other INGOs, IMC and MC. The guesthouses are fitted with large rooms – private bathroom/toilet and well air conditioned, including large living areas and sports equipment available. Kitchen and cook are available and a few restaurants are present in town, where staff can go eat out or order. Staff can organize for the meals to be prepared within the guesthouse kitchen or buy from restaurants which are close by. Reliable but limited internet is available in the GH and guarding services are present.

title: Myanmar - Deputy Country Director Operations & Partnership (M/F) - Yangon
body:
## About us

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. ## About the mission

SI has been in Myanmar since 2008, first responding to the devastating Cyclone Nargis. In 2011 and 2012, SI expanded to new regions focusing on Livelihoods, Food Security, Shelter, and WASH sectors. SI is currently mainly operating in Rakhine and in Kachin States with outreach emergency capacities through its local partners in other locations. The operations are supported by a Coordination team based in Yangon.

While continuing to support the vulnerable communities suffering from a long-term protracted crisis, SI is also developing a stronger and more responsive Emergency component, either directly or through local partners, to tackle the growing needs spreading across the country.

Projects are currently funded by FCDO, ECHO, CIAA, CDCS and UN agencies with potential for development in terms of geographical coverage and activities’ scope to address the emerging needs.

As of October 2026, SI has 13 international staff and more than 200 national staff working in Myanmar to implement projects focusing on Wash, FSL and Emergency response. Projects range from immediate life-saving response (Water Scarcity in Rakhine, Emergency response to new displacements etc.) to the search for more sustainable solutions to protracted crisis (handover to communities and local organizations, capacity-building, community empowerment etc.)

"Limited in Yangon

All operational bases in Myanmar are now presenting medium to severe security constraints."

Experiment in the humanitarian sector : more than 5 years

Experiment on similar positions : 3-4 years

1. Proven experience in partnership management or indirect implementation
2. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making

Transversal skills :

1. Cross-Cultural Communication & Adaptability: Proven ability to navigate diverse multicultural environments by actively observing local ways of working, adjusting interpersonal approaches, and fostering inclusive, collaborative relationships across diverse teams and institutional partners.
2. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts

Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

Internet and telephone network are sometimes lower quality and reliability when in Myanmar (overall OK in Yangon with specific internet restrictions by the authorities)

Restaurant & social life: When in Yangon, the social life scene has shrunk a bit since 2021, but there is still a community and a diversity of options for social and outgoing life."

title: SUDAN - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - KHARTOUM
body:
## About us

**Desired start date : 15/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission : 12 months**  
**Location : KHARTOUM**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SI has been present in Sudan for a long time, untill expulsion in 2009 and subsequent reopening in the early 2010s.

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.

Geneina base scaled up in 2024 and 2025 to deliver life-safing and recovery humanitarian assistance through WASH, FSL and Shelter interventions.

SI opened an office in Zalingei, Central Darfur in November 2024, North Darfur in 2024/5 and in Ed Daein and West Kordofan in 2026.

Today, thanks to the support of SIDA, SHF, CDCS, ECHO and UNDP, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, East Darfur, North Darfur, West Kordofan, Khartoum and Jazeera States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors. SI is also in the process of opening up activities in Blue Nile State.

Across the Darfurs and in West Kordofan, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH -from 1st line to 2nd line & beyond- with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, networks, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.

In West Darfur, SI remains one of the main WASH actors and has developped a strong technical and access capacity through the rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.

In Central Darfur, the activities mostly focus on WASH and FSL. SI also has an Emergency Response Team based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA).

In the Eastern part of the country, SI is present with Wash and FSL activities in Khartoum and Jazeera, under ECHO, CDCS, SHF and US funds. Activities in Blue Nile are being launched by the end of 2026.

Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, including 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.

Mission size around 45 international staff and 190 National staff across different bases

Base Size (5 International staff and 22 National across Khartoum and Jazira Base)

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Field Coordinator oversees the development of Solidarites International's (SI) presence and response in their area of intervention, in line with the Country Strategy and the organisation's mandate.

Delegated by the Country Director, they are SI's representative in the area to aid workers, local administrative, military and political authorities, civil society and the media.

They are responsible for ensuring the security of SI teams and assets in their area, as well as compliance with the organisation's ethical framework and values.

**The main challenges:**

\- Bureaucratic impediments in East Sudan are significant and have the potential to delay interventions and activities. A good communication style and patience are necessary for maintaining relationships and solving problems is high.

\- Coordination is moving to Khartoum in January 2027, the integration of Project and Coordination remains to be implemented.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\- Consolidating 2027 strategy based on needs and funding and ensuring an appropriate structure

\- Consolidation of opening of Blue Nile activities and base

**Security constraints:**

Both states are at level 2-3 and are safe. Social life is more active in Khartoum, but staff can move freely in both states.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3-4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Security and access management
2. Rapid need Assesement
3. Strong negociations skills
4. Conflict sensitivy skills

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Work under pressure
2. Adaptability
3. Strong initiative capacities and solution-finding attitude

**LANGUAGES**

1. Fluent English
2. Arabic would be an advantage
3. French would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Khartoum is recovering and life is returning to normal, with a lot of restaurants and shops. There are also a lot of internationals, both humanitarians and others, and there is opporunity to socialize. The international hotels are reopening allowing for increase in variety of activities that can be done.

title: Director, People Development- CRRD
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

**The Director, People Development is responsible for planning and implementing a variety of people development initiatives for the IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department. Partnering closely with the Global Learning & Development Team and P&C Partners across CRRD, the Director, People Development, will plan and facilitate workshops, peer learning groups, facilitate talent review processes, and support other talent management and learning efforts across CRRD. CRRD people development activities must build capability and competency to achieve CRRD's strategic action plans, leadership diversity targets, and the overall development, retention, and improved internal promotion rates of top talent across CRRD.**

**Duties/Responsibilities:**

- Serve as a member of CRRD People & Culture leadership team and contribute to its strategy development and establishment of L&D priorities connected to IRCs Strategy 100 and Delivery Letter goals.
- Build and maintain trusted partnerships with senior CRRD leaders, regional directors, and country directors to ensure sustained engagement and measurable adoption of people development programs across CRRD.
- Serve as the primary voice of CRRD within the Global Learning & Development team by participating in strategy and planning sessions to ensure globally implemented programming reflects the needs, contexts, and constraints of field-based staff and leaders.
- Translate CRRD's strategic priorities — including Strategy 100, leadership diversity targets, and retention goals — into scalable learning and talent development plans, providing guidance on how programs should be adapted to varying operational contexts across a complex, globally distributed humanitarian operation.
- Partner with CRRD P&C Partners to design and deliver new leader integration and country director onboarding experiences that accelerate effectiveness and cultural alignment.
- Contextualize, communicate and drive org-wide learning and development initiatives across CRRD.
- Design and implement people development programs — including, but not limited to, talent review, succession planning, manager capability building, and P&C capacity strengthening — that equip, engage, and retain CRRD staff, managers and leaders.
- Build CRRD's talent movement and capability-building infrastructure — including workforce planning and succession readiness pipelines.
- Maintain and deliver a strategic roadmap of people development initiatives in CRRD while also remaining agile and able to deliver against last-minute and unexpected needs that may arise.
- Identify and champion the responsible use of AI tools and technologies to enhance talent development and learning and development work — improving the personalization, efficiency, and scalability of programs across CRRD's globally distributed teams — in alignment with IRC's approved AI tools and governance standards.
- Establish and track key metrics to evaluate program effectiveness and report progress to CRRD and P&C leadership.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to**: Dual reporting to Senior Director, CRRD People & Culture and Director, Global Learning and Development  
**Position directly supervises**: N/A

**Key Internal Relationships**:

- Collaborate with colleagues across the People & Culture function including all CRRD Regional P&C Directors, Gender Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (GEDI), HR Operations, Compensation & Benefits, Global Learning and Development and others to achieve meaningful impact.
- CRRD Leadership and Country People and Culture teams.

**Qualifications:**

- Minimum 8–10 years of progressive experience in learning & development, talent management, or organizational development.
- Demonstrated experience designing and implementing people development programs across a complex, matrixed organization.
- Proven ability to design and facilitate leadership and manager development programs, talent reviews, and succession planning processes.
- Experience conducting learning needs assessments and translating findings into targeted, scalable development solutions.
- Proficiency in tracking and reporting on L&D metrics and using data to evaluate and iterate program effectiveness.
- Familiarity with instructional design methodologies and adult learning principles.
- Exceptional relationship-building and influencing skills, with demonstrated ability to partner effectively with senior leaders and stakeholders across functions and geographies.
- Strong in-person and virtual facilitation skills, with experience leading workshops, peer learning groups, and leadership programs across diverse, multicultural audiences.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and competing priorities, balancing a strategic roadmap with agile responsiveness to emerging needs.
- Deep understanding of the operational realities of field-based and humanitarian contexts, with the ability to design programs that are relevant and accessible across limited resource environments.
- Ability to work across multiple time zones and with globally distributed teams; willingness to travel internationally as needed.
- Some experience applying AI tools and technologies to talent development work — such as learning content design, program personalization, or talent/workforce analytics — preferred.
- English fluency. Proficiency in an additional core IRC language (French, Arabic, Spanish) strongly preferred.

**Compensation:** (GBP 65,785 - GBP 73,095). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Country Director, Yemen
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than twenty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

The IRC launched an emergency health response in Yemen in 2012. Since then, and despite continued instability and conflict, the IRC has extended its presence throughout the country, implementing a diverse, integrated program of health, nutrition, WASH, protection, and cash programs. These programs prioritize local partnerships with both public institutions and civil society, and span emergency response, humanitarian, and recovery modalities, while serving vulnerable Yemenis including IDPs and returnees, migrants and refugees, women, children, and youth.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

The Country Director (CD) sets the strategic direction, leads all programs, emergency response, financial and operational matters, and oversees humanitarian access and the adherence to and application of security measures, as well as external relationships and partnerships in Yemen. As lead of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the CD ensures accountability of the SMT for the overall leadership and supervisory management of approximately 120 IRC staff and more than 400 incentive workers, programming, and operations, including program quality and accountability, stewardship of resources, staff safety and security, performance management, and external representation, for which the CD remains accountable.

Success in this position requires an individual with exemplary, demonstrated leadership abilities who deploys strong communication and interpersonal skills effectively, both internally and externally. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong contextual analytical skills and an ability to translate the impact of geopolitical developments and rapidly changing humanitarian conditions into operational priorities and effective responses. They will build a network of partnerships, diversify program resources, and ensure organizational readiness to respond to emerging and escalating emergencies while maintaining continuity of critical humanitarian services. They will be directly responsible for the overall coordination and strategic direction of the country program; providing oversight and coaching for directly supervised senior managers; leading country program teams to identify, design, and deliver responsive, high-quality humanitarian, emergency response, early recovery, and development programs; ensuring the efficient management of public grants and private funds for results, compliance, and focused, timely reporting; and overseeing financial management and compliance systems.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Lead the country program by maintaining open and professional relations with colleagues, promoting a strong team spirit, and providing guidance, oversight, and resources to enable staff to perform successfully.
- Lead strategic representation and positioning with national and local authorities at various levels; donors (including institutional, non-institutional and private), European Union; UN and other international organizations; international and local NGOs; and networks such as INGO coordination mechanisms and appropriate working groups. Develop and maintain a high level of understanding of donor priorities and planned funding.
- Play a leadership role in efforts to improve humanitarian response coordination in Yemen
- Provide leadership for strong, mutually beneficial, and effective partnerships with Yemeni organizations.
- Seek out and pursue respectful and safe opportunities to raise the profile of the work of the IRC and its partners in Yemen, as well as the lives and the needs of the people the IRC seeks to serve.
- Lead country program collaboration with colleagues in the IRC’s MENAU region to deliver regional programming and advocacy.
- Ensure leadership and management processes enable the IRC to effectively adapt to contextual changes and fully leverage opportunities to expand humanitarian access and assistance.
- Collaborate closely with regional leadership and neighboring country programs to address cross-border and regional issues coherently and effectively.

***Strategic Direction, Program Quality and Growth***

- Set the strategic vision and direction of the country program is aligned with IRC’s strategy to serve more people with the most responsive and highest quality programming possible and secure the resources necessary to do so.
- Ensure the strategy action plan is of quality, implemented and guides decision making, to achieve IRC’s ambitions in Yemen and contribute to IRC’s strategic objectives globally.
- Ensure program quality through consistent use throughout the country program of rigorous assessment, design, and proposal development and review processes; comprehensive monitoring & evaluation, accountability and learning systems; staff development investments; and partner organization capacity strengthening.
- Actively seek out and pursue opportunities to expand, in line with the IRC’s mission, humanitarian, resilience and development programming in Yemen, in terms of populations and areas served.
- Develop a deep understanding of the geopolitical landscape and remain current on context analysis and develop responsive strategies to ensure the IRC mission can be carried out appropriately in case of contextual changes.
- Ensure timely submission of competitive, responsive, and high-quality proposals, and support colleagues in negotiations with donors.
- Lead implementation of IRC’s objective of expanding partnerships with Yemeni civil society organizations, and ensuring strong collaborative, principled partnerships that deliver effective and efficient program outcomes.
- Remain current on national and regional issues impacting the country program and partners and develop responsive strategies to changing contexts.
- Ensure the SMT delivers the leadership, management structures, staffing skills and approaches, and operational systems required to ensure a coherent “one IRC” approach to achieve Yemen and regional objectives.
- Identify opportunities for appropriate expansion and growth of programs, supported by the acquisition and investment of human resources.

***Emergency Response Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall strategic and operational emergency response readiness and action for the country program.
- Lead Country Context Analysis, Emergency Response Planning and Strategy Development as well as In-Country Emergency Response Teams
- Ensure the country program maintains robust emergency preparedness and response capacity, including crisis management structures, clear decision-making protocols, and surge readiness to enable rapid operational scale-up or adaptation in volatile contexts.
- Lead and oversee the management timely, well-coordinated, and principled responses to emergencies, including conflict escalation, displacements, critical incidents, and program disruptions.
- Engage with Regional and Global Emergency Response Teams prior to, during and post emergency response, in line with organizational Emergency Guidelines.
- Represent IRC with peer organizations, and other emergency response agencies operating in Yemen.
- Ensure coordinated emergency response in the event of cross-border/regional emergencies.

***Safety and Security Management***

- Take primary responsibility for overall management of safety and security for the country program.
- Lead and oversee the management of all security risks and incidents, ensure timely, well-coordinated, and ensure primacy of the wellbeing and security of our clients, staff and partners. Create and maintain a culture of safety and security awareness throughout the country program, including training and briefings that prepare all country program staff for security incident prevention and response.
- Keep security, evacuation, and contingency plans current and accessible to country program staff.
- Maintain close coordination and communication with the Regional Safety and Security Director on safety and security concerns and evolving issues that could adversely affect IRC staff or operations.
- Liaise with the regional office, with peer agencies and use the tools and information portals available to keep abreast of all security-related matters; In case of necessity, ensure adequate roll-out of emergency procedures.

***Staff Management and Development***

- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives and providing regular and timely performance feedback, and leading documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Provide direct oversight and guidance to multi-disciplinary teams across cross-cultural settings, ensuring performance excellence and alignment with strategic objectives.
- Effectively manage staff across various functions and locations, including setting clear expectations, performance monitoring, and accountability frameworks.
- Lead sensitive and complex staff-related conversations (e.g., performance issues, conflict resolution) with professionalism, empathy, and respect.
- Mentor and coach high-potential staff to support career progression and leadership development within the organization.
- Promote a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing across teams and departments.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.

***Stewardship and Operational Management***

- Drive operational excellence to achieve optimal efficiency and cost-effectiveness in all functions and operations of the country program.
- Oversee the development, deployment and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to deliver compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, especially in the areas of People and Culture, finance, and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the Yemen country program’s financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for grant funds and discretionary funds.
- Ensure a country-wide culture of safeguarding, grounded in accountability, transparency, and survivor-centered response. Provide strategic leadership to mainstream safeguarding across all country program operations and partnerships, in line with IRC’s Safeguarding Policy.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Regional Vice President - MENAU

**Position directly Supervises:** A senior management team responsible for Programs, Operations, Finance, People and Culture, Field Management, and Safety & Security and Compliance and Risk Management.

**Key Internal Contacts:** Country Program: All staff, Region: MENAU Regional Team, Head Office: Crisis Response and Recovery Department (CRRD), Ethics & Compliance, Operations and Strategy, Finance, Global Philanthropy & Partnerships, Technical Excellence and General Counsel.

**Key External Contacts:** Partner organizations, host country government officials, public and private donor agencies, international and national NGOs, UN agencies

**PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS:**

- Strong leadership abilities and interpersonal skills, and ability to deploy strong communications effectively, both internally and externally, and in emergency operational contexts. Ability to build networks, partnerships and diversify program resources.
- Experience in a leadership role in conflict settings and situations of constrained humanitarian access required.
- Graduate degree in a relevant field.
- At least 12 years of dynamically responsible international work experience, including leadership at the Country Director level of multi-site, multi-sectoral operations in a complex operating environment, with demonstrated responsibility for emergency preparedness, crisis management, and operational response. Preference for experience in the MENAU Region.
- Fluency in English is required. Arabic is a preferred asset.

**Demonstrated Technical Skills:**

- Superior communication skills, verbal and written.
- Experience in managing security in a complex and rapidly changing security context.
- Proven ability to negotiate and work with partner organizations.
- Strong budget and fiscal oversight capacities.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with both institutional and private donors.
- Established capacity to handle stressful situations in a healthy, constructive manner.
- Ability to respond to multiple priorities in a timely manner, producing high-quality outcomes.
- Prior work experience and a keen understanding of political complexities in Yemen and the Middle East and North Africa region is preferred.

**Demonstrated Managerial/Leadership Competencies:**

- Demonstrated successful leadership and management experience with a multi-disciplinary team in cross-cultural settings, including active mentoring and coaching.
- Analytical, strategic, and able to proactively develop solutions to complex challenges.
- Comfortable with ambiguity and decision making in a fast-paced environment.
- Effective in developing high-potential staff to achieve career growth and maximum contribution.
- Proven experience in managing high-quality programming that meets the needs of clients.
- Proven experience delivering appropriate levels of oversight of a portfolio consisting of a variety of complex, high-value donor-funded projects.
- Experience building personal networks at a senior level, resulting in securing new opportunities for the organization.
- Opportunity-awareness. A successful innovative approach to unpredictable programming, operational, and funding contexts.
- Ability to dispassionately represent program context, constraints, and successes to media, government, and other senior audiences.
- Highly resilient and comfortable working in an insecure environment with restricted personal freedoms.

**Ability to Travel: Position is primarily based in Aden, Yemen.** Approximately 5-10 % outside the region for workshops, representation, and conferences.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and giving them greater influence over program design and delivery.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC MENAU, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: SOUTH SUDAN - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIPS HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - JUBA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location : Juba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement, this year El Nino), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.

\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.

\- South Sudan has also been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of October 2026, more than 1,400,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).

\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may raise further division and tensions.

\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.

As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

SI sectors of intervention:

\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission

Areas of operation:

SI is present:

\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk, Malakal and Ulang (since 2025). The response has focused on cholera, response to acute food insecurity and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.

\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.

Size of operations:

In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 8 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up since 2025.

The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

The mission is currently in the last step of a scale up phase with approx 120 staffs, aiming at reaching 140 staffs. Coordination team will soon be around 30 staffs

The Grants department currently has 1 Grants & Partnership Head of Department Expat, 1 Grants Manager Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer Expat + 1 Reporting & Communication Officer National. With the mission scale up, the idea is to add Compliance Manager National. A Compliance coordinator supports the mission only part time and is therefore not in charge of audits.

## About the job

**General objective:**

\- The objectives of the position rely on donor engagement, financing and partnership strategy, preparation of project documents, contract management, partnership management, compliance and external audits, external communication, internal control.  
\- Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Grants & Partnership Head of Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. He/She supervises, adapts and optimises working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.  
The Grants Department validates contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.  
It plays a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). The Grants & Partnership Head of Department ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- SI has increased the number of consortium we lead/are part of and we need the Grants department to support better engagement with these partners.  
\- SI also needs to have more capacities to engage on the localization agenda.  
\- In the meantime, SI needs to build a strong Grants department supported by national staffs.  
\- The Grants & Partnership Department scale up should facilitate and lighten the work of the program teams on the ground who have to face an increasing number of reporting & proposal requests.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\- Support localization effort and engage with a couple of selected local partners.  
\- Support follow up of proposals submitted in the Dec-Jan period (notably ECHO)

**Security constraints :**

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates.  
The situation in South Sudan is volatile, please document yourself before applying. SI is adapting the set up in real time as context evolves  
There is one driver available on evenings and 2 on weekends for movements out of office hours.  
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).  
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are limited

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Master Degree in financial / accountancy studies

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years

Experience on a similar position : 0-2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Excellent writing skills & mastering of MS Office suite

2\. Donors rule understanding & knowledge: ECHO, CDCS, FIFSAN, Norway MoFA, FCDO, DoS, SSHF

3\. Donor platform technicities: APPEL, GMS, UNPP

4\. Contractual management

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Capacity building experience

2\. Department structuring knowledge

3\. Information management structuration is a +

4\. Networking capacities

5\. Very hands-on: not top senior management only: capacity to be a doer as well

6\. Attraction for the field

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Very good in English, written and spoken.

2\. French & Arabic are a +

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**   
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grants & Parternships Head of Department will be living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs. With the scale up, different options are being considered and some staffs may also be hosted at another NGO nearby.  
Individual room in the guesthouse, with electricity 24/7 and generator during specific time. NB: During field visits, living conditions are much more basic.  
Juba, as the capital of South Sudan offers a good variety of markets, supermarkets, restaurants, and bars.

title: Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services
source: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
body:
**Nature of Consultancy:** Independent Senior Technical Expert – Peacebuilding, Fragility & UN Strategic Advisory Consultancy Services

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment (with mission travel to Port-au-Prince and designated departmental hubs). Any required mission travel, including its dates, arrangements, security requirements, and reimbursement of agreed expenses, shall be specified or separately agreed in writing.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days/hours, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, deliverables, and estimated levels of effort agreed between COAR and the Consultant.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 01 December 2026 to 31 December 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed; it does not create an obligation to provide or accept assignments, guarantee a minimum workload, or require continuous availability. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated Haiti Team Lead, acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope. This role is for assignment coordination and does not confer authority to direct the Consultant's day-to-day working methods or exercise line-management authority over the Consultant.

**Overview:** This Scope of Work (SoW) outlines the specific senior technical consultancy assignment with the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant may be commissioned to provide specialist analytical and advisory services for an in-depth study examining the systemic, historical, and multidimensional crisis in Haiti. Commissioned in the context of UNDP and UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) strategic planning, the study is intended to establish an evidence-based baseline to guide conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and sustainable recovery initiatives across Haiti. The assignment may include the preparation of a comprehensive, formally published biennial report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks, accompanied by a strategic intervention approach for the United Nations system. The Consultant's responsibility shall be limited to the agreed research, analytical, drafting, advisory, and facilitation outputs. Decisions concerning publication, institutional endorsement, strategic adoption, and implementation shall remain with COAR and the commissioning institutions.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**About COAR:** COAR is an independent social enterprise that directly supports practitioners, policymakers, and donors by facilitating humanitarian and development interventions in complex, fragile, and high-risk environments. COAR delivers neutral and objective research and analysis, which identifies - but does not influence - local stakeholders, relationships, interests, and analyzes broader political, economic, social, and security dynamics and trends. COAR research leverages social media, personal networks, field research teams, and local experts in order to map and translate the local human context; COAR analysis synthesizes and studies this data in order to inform both programmatic and strategic decision-making, reduce security and conflict sensitivity risks, and increase the impact of humanitarian, development, stabilization, peace-building, and peacekeeping initiatives.

**Objectives**

For the specific study assignment, the Consultant may be commissioned to:

- Conduct an analysis of historical trends and trajectories of Haiti’s systemic, social, community, political, and economic crisis to develop a comprehensive understanding of underlying structural dynamics;
- Analyze the multidimensional drivers of fragility and crisis across national, departmental, and cross-border domains;
- Map crises and trace underlying drivers of distinct forms of violence (criminal, gang-driven, political, and gender-based) to elucidate crisis systems;
- Evaluate crisis dynamics through intersectional gender, generational, and social inequality perspectives, highlighting the contributions and protection of women and youth in conflict prevention and mediation;
- Review and assess past and ongoing conflict prevention and peacebuilding interventions supported by the UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) and key multilateral/bilateral partners;
- Propose a tailored intervention approach for the United Nations system anchored in conflict prevention and peacebuilding principles; and
- Where included in the agreed assignment, provide substantive input into the preparation of an inclusive multi-stakeholder validation workshop, including contributing to validation discussions and moderating specified panel sessions.

**Activities and Key Responsibilities**

The following activities describe potential services under the study assignment. The specific activities to be performed, their estimated effort, and the associated outputs shall be confirmed in writing before commencement.

1\. Analytical Framing & Methodological Design

- Develop an analytical framework and research matrix tailored to the Haitian operational context, integrating OECD DAC peacebuilding criteria and UN Integrated Strategic Framework (ISF) objectives.
- Formulate and calibrate qualitative and quantitative research instruments, including semi-structured Key Informant Interview (KII) guides, Focus Group Discussion (FGD) protocols, and secondary assessment templates.
- Incorporate strict Conflict Sensitivity, Do No Harm, and data protection protocols, reflecting localized security constraints and protection considerations in gang-controlled and fragile environments.

2\. Multidimensional Fragility, Violence & Hotspot Mapping

- Trace historical fault lines, institutional degradation, and economic patterns driving instability across Port-au-Prince and outlying departments (e.g., Artibonite, Nord, Grand'Anse).
- Document geographic conflict hotspots, illicit trade flows, arms proliferation corridors, and cross-border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Assess formal and informal mechanisms, social cohesion structures, customary dispute-resolution mechanisms, and local resilience dynamics fostering community stability.

3\. Intersectional Analysis & PBF Portfolio Assessment

- Analyze structural socio-economic inequalities, youth recruitment vulnerabilities, and gender-based violence (GBV) as systemic drivers of fragility.
- Conduct a focused desk review and stakeholder assessment of UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) projects and partner peacebuilding programming in Haiti, evaluating impact, lessons learned, and systemic gaps.
- Identify practical entry points and age- and gender-sensitive recommendations to strengthen the leadership of women and youth in peacebuilding architectures.

4\. Report Authoring & UN Strategic Intervention Approach

- Prepare and coordinate the analytical synthesis and drafting of the formal, publication-ready baseline report examining fragilities and peacebuilding risks in Haiti.
- Draft a pragmatic, forward-looking UN intervention approach that connects empirical research findings with strategic programming across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace (HDP) Nexus.
- Integrate technical review comments from COAR leadership, UNDP, PBF, and institutional counterparts into final publishable outputs to the extent that such comments are provided within the agreed review process and schedule. The Consultant shall identify and discuss any material changes to the agreed scope or analytical conclusions that arise during review.

5\. Stakeholder Workshop Coordination & Panel Moderation

- Where specified in the assignment, provide substantive recommendations on the agenda and content of the national multi-stakeholder validation workshop.
- Deliver technical presentations on analytical findings, methodological approaches, and strategic recommendations to UN leadership, civil society, and international partners, at agreed events or sessions.
- Moderate thematic panel discussions during inclusive consultations to cultivate national ownership and partnership consensus where the relevant sessions, preparation requirements, and expected level of effort have been agreed in writing.

**Expected Results and Deliverables**

The primary result of this assignment will be a publicly available, formally published large-scale report examining fragilities and risks related to peacebuilding and development in Haiti. The report serves three primary purposes:

1. Understanding Haiti’s Crisis: Deepening multilateral and national understanding of the systems, drivers, and trajectories underlying the crisis.
2. Strategic & Programmatic Decision-Making: Informing conflict prevention, peacebuilding, and HDP nexus resource allocation.
3. Advocacy & Dialogue: Supporting continuous, multilevel dialogue among national authorities, civil society, and international partners.

**Required Experience and Expertise**

- Education: Advanced university degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in Peace and Conflict Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, or a related discipline required.
- UN System Experience: Required minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience advising or implementing peacebuilding, conflict prevention, and stabilization programming within or alongside the UN System (e.g., UNDP, BINUH, DPO/DPPA, IOM, or UN Country Teams).
- Country & Contextual Expertise: Desired analytical or operational track record in Haiti, with nuanced understanding of Haitian political history, gang territorial dynamics, departmental socio-economic disparities, and border dynamics with the Dominican Republic.
- Analytical Capabilities: Proven track record conducting complex conflict analyses, fragility assessments, and intersectional studies focusing on gender, youth, and structural inequalities.
- Facilitation & Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue: Proven experience designing and moderating high-level validation workshops, roundtables, and policy panels involving government counterparts, UN leadership, and grassroots civil society organizations.
- Languages: Professional proficiency in both French and English (written and spoken) is required; fluency or working knowledge of Haitian Creole (Kreyòl) is a distinct asset.

**Safeguarding, Ethics, and Confidentiality**

In performing the Services, the Consultant shall comply with COAR’s Code of Conduct, any applicable Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA), and safeguarding requirements that COAR identifies in writing as applicable to external consultants and relevant to the accepted assignment. In light of the delicate security and protection environment in Haiti, the Consultant shall conduct agreed research and stakeholder interactions in accordance with Do No Harm principles, informant anonymity, data protection protocols, and UN standards on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client. The Consultant shall promptly notify COAR of any material ethical, safeguarding, data-protection, or security concern arising in the course of the assignment, while retaining responsibility for the independent professional judgment required to perform the Services safely and ethically.

All working drafts, field notes, and final deliverables remain the sole property of COAR Global and the commissioning client, subject to the terms of the applicable consultancy agreement, including any agreed provisions concerning pre-existing materials, third-party materials, research data, intellectual property, and permitted retention of records.

title: Mental Health Specialist
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**DESCRIPTION:**

The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad. Assistance to Sudanese refugees expanded to include the management of eleven camps in the east and one camp in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, IRC expanded its geographic coverage to Guéra Province, where the organization currently works in five health districts and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population, as well as family planning, response, and prevention activities related to gender-based violence (GBV). In May 2016, IRC established a presence in Lac Province to respond to the crisis caused by Boko Haram. In its 2022–2024 Strategic Action Plan, IRC Chad is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and line ministries in key sectors to ensure that IRC’s actions are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the initiatives undertaken.

**Job Description:**

Reporting directly to the Senior Health Coordinator, the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Specialist based in Hadjer Hadid will be responsible for the overall management and implementation of a high-quality mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) program in all of IRC’s areas of operation, and more specifically in refugee camps. The Mental Health Specialist will work closely with the Ministry of Public Health’s mental health program, UNHCR, IRC, HIAS, and all members of the mental health working group in Chad to facilitate the coordination of mental health interventions in the country and strengthen their integration into the minimum package of services provided in health centers and hospitals. The mental health and psychosocial support specialist will supervise health workers in providing prevention, diagnosis, and treatment services for patients with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders, using the guidelines of the WHO/UNHCR Mental Health Gaps Action Program (mhGAP), and will train new providers on the mhGAP model. She/he will develop standard operating procedures for providing psychological support and psychiatric care, as well as psychosocial support through group psychoeducation and community-based programs. She/he will represent IRC at all mental health working group meetings.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Program Coordination:
- Coordinate mental health needs assessments;
- Organize regular meetings on mental health with health program managers and the Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) team, in collaboration with other technical coordinators;
- Ensure that mental health and psychosocial support are fully integrated into the various sectors of the health program (primary health care, sexual and reproductive health, nutrition, environmental health) and other IRC programs (WPE and ERD);
- Coordinate the implementation of all interventions in the field of mental health and psychosocial support
- Contribute to capacity building for the MHPSS team to enable them to effectively carry out their duties and ensure a smooth transition;
- Participate in capacity building for local partners (Ministry of Public Health, NGOs, United Nations agencies, etc.) in the field of mental health and psychosocial support;
