L'objectif de cette enquête est d'évaluer la situation nutritionnelle des enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois dans le DS de Bouca, ainsi que le taux de mortalité rétrospective chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans, pour une meilleure planification des interventions dans l'avenir.  
Dans ce cadre, vos responsabilités seront:  
Assistance technique à la réalisation d'une enquête SMART nutritionnelle et coordination de l'activité avec les autorités locales et ONGs partenaire  
Planification, préparation des outils et supervision de l'enquête  
Elaboration du protocole d'enquête, préparation du matériel de formation et de tout autre outil de travail conformément aux normes d'enquête SMART  
Elaboration d'outils de collecte des données et de questionnaires prédéfinis dans des tablettes utilisant le logiciel Kobo Collect, ACF disposera de tablettes contenant l'application Kobo Collect  
Recrutement, formation (méthodologie d'enquête SMART), et sélection des staffs techniques et des agents communautaires devant conduire l'activité dans le District.  
Coordonner toute la collecte des données sur le terrain pour garantir une collecte de données de qualité  
Nettoyer les bases de données et analyser les résultats de l'enquête à l'aide du logiciel standard ENA et de tout logiciel supplémentaire (EPI-Info) requis pour les indicateurs  
Présenter les résultats préliminaires à ACF et à toutes les parties prenantes concernées pour obtenir des commentaires (verbaux et écrits) et formuler des recommandations.  
Sur la base des retours, finaliser le rapport avec des recommandations claires et pertinentes dans les délais impartis et présenter les résultats à un groupe plus large (coordination d'ACF, cluster nutrition et ministère de la Santé)

  

Profile :

 Vous êtes diplômé·e en nutrition, santé publique, médecine, soins infirmiers, épidémiologie, biostatistique ou dans une discipline connexe, avec de bonnes connaissances en méthodologie d'enquête et en recherche.  
Vous justifiez d'au moins 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la nutrition, de la santé publique ou de la santé maternelle, infantile et nutritionnelle.  
Vous avez une expérience confirmée dans la coordination, la mise en oeuvre et le suivi-évaluation de projets de nutrition, ainsi que dans la réalisation d'évaluations nutritionnelles et le monitoring des activités de santé et nutrition.  
Vous maîtrisez les statistiques, l'analyse de données, ainsi que les logiciels EPI Info, ENA for SMART, SMART+ et les outils informatiques associés.  
Vous êtes reconnu·e pour vos qualités de communication, votre capacité à animer des ateliers et à rédiger des rapports d'évaluation de qualité.  
La maîtrise du français oral et écrit est indispensable.  
La connaissance des langues locales et du contexte humanitaire en RCA constituera un atout apprécié.  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Contrat à durée déterminée d'usage de droit français : 1,5 mois jusqu'au 31/12/2026.  
Salaire mensuel brut : de 2130 à euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois  
Remboursement assurance retraite pour les citoyens non français : 16% du salaire mensuel brut  
Augmentation du salaire de base : 6% tous les 12 mois de contrat continu  
Per diem et frais de vie mensuels : 775euros nets, versés sur le terrain  
Allocation contexte mensuelle : 300euros  
Allocation enfant : 1500euros par an et par enfant présent dans le pays d'origine (plafond de 6000euros/an)  
Transport et logement : Prise en charge des déplacements et logement collectif  
Couverture Médicale : 100% de la prise en charge des cotisations santé et assurance rapatriement, de vos frais médicaux et ce jusqu'à 1 mois après la fin de votre contrat  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Congés et RnR : 25 jours par an de CP et 20 RnR par an ; prise en charge du billet avec plafond pour se rendre sur la zone de break choisie, et 215euros d'indemnité forfaitaire par RnRAccompagnement et formation  
Suivi et accompagnement parcours professionnel  
Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft  
Déplacements terrains : Ouham-Fafa, Ouham  
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

title: Coordinateur programmes Droits et Santé Sexuels et Reproductifs (DSSR) (F/H) - RCI
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## Médecins du Monde en RCI

Présente en Côte d’Ivoire depuis 1980, Médecins du Monde France (MdM) œuvre pour garantir un accès équitable à des services de santé de qualité, en plaçant les Droits et la Santé Sexuels et Reproductifs (DSSR) au cœur de son action.

Dans le cadre de sa stratégie 2027-2028, MdM met en œuvre une approche intégrée visant à renforcer durablement le système de santé et les capacités des acteurs communautaires. Cette approche combine la promotion des DSSR, la prévention et la prise en charge des violences basées sur le genre, le renforcement de la santé communautaire, ainsi que la promotion de l’égalité de genre et de l’autonomisation des femmes, des filles et des adolescent·e·s.

À travers ses programmes, l’organisation accompagne les structures de santé, les institutions publiques et les organisations de la société civile afin d’améliorer l’offre et la demande de services de DSSR. MdM contribue également au renforcement des capacités des différents acteurs, au développement de mécanismes favorisant l’accès aux soins des populations les plus vulnérables et à la transformation durable des normes sociales limitant l’exercice des droits sexuels et reproductifs.

Par ailleurs, l’organisation est engagée dans la prévention et la prise en charge du cancer du col de l’utérus, le plaidoyer en faveur des droits sexuels et reproductifs, ainsi que le développement d’approches innovantes visant à améliorer l’accès à des soins de santé de qualité pour toutes et tous.

## Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous

En tant que coordinateur programmes Droits et Santé Sexuels et Reproductifs (DSSR) (F/H), vous devez gérer et superviser la mise en œuvre du programme ainsi que l’équipe qui y est rattachée. Plus précisément, vous assurez la planification, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l’évaluation des activités, en veillant particulièrement à l’implication des partenaires ivoiriens, à la qualité des interventions, ainsi qu’au respect des exigences des bailleurs de fonds et des autorités locales.

## Vos missions

Plus spécifiquement, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes :

**Planification, mise en œuvre et suivi du programme**

- Assurer la planification stratégique et opérationnelle du programme avec les partenaires
- Coordonner la mise en œuvre des activités et veiller à l'atteinte des résultats attendus
- Superviser le suivi des indicateurs, le reporting et la qualité des données
- Garantir la qualité technique des activités et proposer les ajustements nécessaires
- Piloter les évaluations, enquêtes et exercices de capitalisation

**Relations avec les partenaires et les autorités**

- Animer la gouvernance du consortium et garantir l'implication des partenaires
- Développer et maintenir des relations avec les autorités et les parties prenantes clés
- Assurer une veille contextuelle et identifier des opportunités de partenariat
- Représenter MdM auprès des instances et réseaux pertinents

**Gestion financière, administrative et logistique des programmes**

- Contribuer à l'élaboration et au suivi budgétaire du programme
- Garantir le respect des procédures internes et des exigences bailleurs
- Superviser l'utilisation des ressources financières, matérielles et logistiques
- Identifier les risques et mettre en œuvre les mesures correctrices nécessaires

**Relations et négociations avec les bailleurs**

- Contribuer au développement de nouvelles opportunités de financement
- Superviser l'élaboration des propositions de projets et des rapports bailleurs
- Assurer le suivi des engagements contractuels et participer aux échanges avec les bailleurs

**Plaidoyer et communication externe**

- Représenter MdM auprès des partenaires institutionnels et techniques
- Contribuer à la stratégie de plaidoyer et à la valorisation des résultats du programme
- Participer aux espaces de coordination et de concertation sectoriels

**Management**

- Encadrer, accompagner et évaluer les membres de l'équipe
- Définir les priorités et assurer le suivi des performances
- Renforcer les capacités de l'équipe et favoriser un environnement de travail collaboratif
- Veiller au respect des politiques, procédures et valeurs de MdM

## Vos collègues

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du coordinateur de site, vous collaborez en interne avec l'équipe de coordination. Vous supervisez directement, deux médecins superviseurs, un chargé suivi évaluation redevabilité et apprentissage, un préparateur gestionnaire en pharmacie et un.e chargé.e de plaidoyer.

## Vous êtes la bonne personne si…

- Vous êtes diplômé.e d'une formation supérieure Bac+3 en en médical ou paramédical
- Vous avez obligatoirement une expérience préalable de deux ans minimum sur un poste similaire en ONG dans la coordination/gestion d’un portefeuille de programmes de différents bailleurs et en gestion des activités en consortium, idéalement en DSSR
- Vous avez une forte expérience en appui technique aux partenaires et en animation de consortium et une forte capacité à diriger une équipe de collaborateurs
- Vous êtes à la fois flexible et rigoureux.se
- Vous savez faire preuve de proactivité et savez être performant.e dans un environnement de travail sous pression

## Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si...

- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde
- Vous n'avez aucune connaissance des principaux axes de la DSSR
- Vous n'avez pas d'expérience de travail avec les populations clés (population réfugiée, adolescent.e.s)
- Vous ne savez pas faire preuve de patience, diplomatie et pédagogie

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un.e chargé.e de recrutement. Les entretiens, technique et managérial, auxquels des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés, auront lieu dans le courant du mois de novembre.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez !

## Vos conditions d’emploi

title: ESOL Instructor
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The ESOL Instructor is responsible for providing integrated English language instruction for non-native English speakers. The instructor must be able to successfully develop and tailor curriculum and materials to the needs of students enrolled into the program including the support of student recruitment, registration, attendance tracking, retention, progress, and assessment.

This is a part-time, approx. 7 hours per week, reporting to the Adult Education Specialist. Classes and registrations are held at the IRC Richmond office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Deliver integrated ESOL instruction
    - Plan and prepare curricula and lesson plans for mixed-level classes to meet the English language learning needs of students. Integrated ESOL combines English language lessons with job skills and workforce preparation, digital literacy skills, civics, and other life skills.
    - Tune lesson activities to meet student needs across a range of English proficiency levels, from the most basic through intermediate and advanced levels of speaking, comprehension, reading, and writing.
    - Utilize and oversee community volunteers as classroom assistants, managing the delivery of lesson plan activities through those assistants in breakout groups.
    - Document student progress with goal setting and conference notes and assist in recruitment and retention activities.
- Orient and conference with current and potential students, assisting students in completing necessary intake and enrollment forms, both virtually, using phone and web-based platforms, and in-person.
- Administer English language assessments to measure and track student progress and gains.
- Assist with record-keeping and data entry to support program administration and compliance with programmatic requirements. Document student progress by keeping accurate and timely attendance records, case notes, assessment data, program participant surveys, and observations of student progress.
- Maintain a positive learning environment. Facilitate student learning activities that build cultural and community knowledge and encourage collaboration and positive peer support.
- Maintain open and effective communication with adult education team members. Report regularly on program goals, client attendance, learning activities, student progress and any problems or concerns with clients or program.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (4-year) preferred.
- Completion of a certificate program in Adult Education, TEFL, TESL, and/or TESOL is preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant teaching experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with immigrants or refugees preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies**

- Strong desire to support vulnerable individuals and families and enthusiasm for working in a multi-cultural setting.
- Enthusiasm for adult education and language learning.
- An interest in immigrant and refugee and asylee issues and the resettlement process.
- Strong communication abilities, including the ability to lead classes and oversee community volunteers and adult learners.
- Detail oriented and comfortable working with online databases.
- Comfortable working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
- Ability to take initiative, work independently on projects, and follow through on critical tasks.
- Ability to work in a collaborative environment, co-teaching and facilitating learning through others.
- Strong time management skills and comfortability with computer and web-based office and communication platforms.
- Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities in a language spoken by an IRC client group are desired.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $22.75 - $24.20/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Mission France - Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Référent.e projet pluridisciplinaire migration pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Au sein du projet Migration de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, vous contribuez à définir, planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités médico-psycho-sociales et de protection. En lien étroit avec la coordination du projet et les référent·es techniques, vous veillez à la qualité des soins, à la bonne articulation des différentes disciplines et à une réponse cohérente, adaptée aux besoins des personnes accompagnées.

Vous supervisez les responsables des pôles santé somatique, santé mentale, travail social, ainsi que promotion et médiation en santé. Votre rôle est de faire vivre une approche pluridisciplinaire, qui prend en compte à la fois les situations individuelles et les besoins de santé des communautés.

**Principales responsabilités :**

**Piloter et suivre les activités du projet**

- Planifier, mettre en œuvre et suivre les activités sur le Littoral Nord : soins de santé primaires, santé mentale, protection, maraudes et activités post-traversée.
- Contribuer à l’évolution de la stratégie du projet selon le contexte et les besoins du terrain, et participer aux évaluations et missi Eons exploratoires si nécessaire.
- Suivre les indicateurs et les données d’activité, analyser les tendances et proposer des actions correctives pour renforcer la pertinence, la qualité et l’efficience des opérations.
- Participer à l’élaboration du plan annuel, des propositions de projet, des budgets et des rapports opérationnels et narratifs.
- Garantir une prise en charge pluridisciplinaire et centrée sur la personne
- Favoriser la collaboration entre les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de protection, notamment par des échanges professionnels adaptés et le respect du secret médical partagé.
- Organiser la gestion des situations complexes médico-psycho-sociales et de protection, en priorisant les besoins, en clarifiant les limites de prise en charge et en assurant des parcours de référencement et de suivi lisibles.
- Veiller au consentement des personnes avant tout partage d’informations, à la confidentialité et à la protection des données.
- S’assurer de parcours adaptés pour les personnes victimes de violences sexuelles et pour l’accès aux soins d’avortement sécurisé, avec des procédures opérationnelles claires.
- Intégrer les retours des personnes accompagnées et les besoins exprimés par les communautés dans l’amélioration des activités.

 **Encadrer, soutenir et développer les équipes**

- Superviser les responsables de pôles, clarifier les rôles et responsabilités et assurer un suivi régulier des performances.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et accompagner le développement des compétences, notamment en matière d’intégration de la protection dans la prise en charge médicale.
- Contribuer au recrutement, à l’intégration et à la formation des nouveaux membres de l’équipe, en coordination avec les ressources humaines.
- Promouvoir un environnement de travail collaboratif et respectueux, faciliter la coopération pluridisciplinaire et traiter les difficultés d’équipe.
- Gérer les ressources et veiller à la qualité et à la sécurité
- Veiller à la disponibilité et à la bonne gestion des médicaments, dispositifs, consommables et matériels médicaux, en coordination avec la logistique et le service approvisionnement.
- Suivre les consommations et préparer les commandes médicales, dans le respect des protocoles et des procédures applicables.
- Contribuer à l’application des mesures d’hygiène, de sécurité et de prévention des risques sanitaires pour le personnel, ainsi qu’au suivi des événements indésirables.
- Veiller à la sécurité des personnes accompagnées, au fonctionnement des mécanismes de plaintes et de retours, et au signalement des situations d’abus.

**Représenter MSF et travailler en réseau**

- Entretenir des relations de travail constructives avec les partenaires associatifs, les autorités sanitaires et les acteurs locaux, notamment l’ARS et les structures de santé pertinentes.
- Représenter MSF dans les réunions externes liées aux activités et contribuer aux actions de plaidoyer en coordination avec le·la coordinateur·rice de projet.
- Participer à l’analyse du contexte et à la mise en place des protocoles de sécurité adaptés aux opérations.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme de médecine ou diplôme paramédical obligatoire.
- Au moins 3 ans d’expérience en lien avec le diplôme et expérience antérieure sur le terrain avec MSF indispensables.
- Expérience de projets Migration indispensable.
- Expérience confirmée de gestion d’équipe et de management pluridisciplinaire, notamment dans les domaines de la santé mentale, des soins de santé primaires et de l’accès aux droits.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Leadership, vision stratégique, sens de l’organisation, capacité à développer les équipes, esprit de coopération, flexibilité et gestion du stress dans des environnements changeants et parfois difficiles, y compris la nuit.
- Permis B souhaitable.

**Langues et outils :**

- Français courant obligatoire et anglais maîtrisé à l’oral souhaité.
- La connaissance d’autres langues est fortement désirée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

 Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 598.40 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an.
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir : 4 janvier 2026**

title: ASSISTANTE OU ASSISTANT GESTION DE PROJET JEUNESSE - FRANCE
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

title: Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)
body:
arche nova - initiative for people in need (AN) is an independent, non-religious, non-profit and non-governmental organisation (NGO) from Germany working in the fields of humanitarian aid, rehabilitation and development. The primary focus of our activities lies in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH).

Since 2013, AN has been working in Mali, implementing humanitarian and transitional aid projects in the sectors of WaSH, Food Security & Livelihoods (FSL) and DRR. The activities in Mali are managed through the AN Bamako office in close collaboration with the arche nova’s headquarters in Germany.

We are currently looking for a

**Head of Mission Mali (f/m/d)**

**Position to be filled:** 15thof December 2026

**Duty station:** Bamako, Mali with travels to the project locations in Gao (Mali) and Niamey (Niger)

**Duration:** initial 12 months contract (extension desired) with 6 months’ probation period

**Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.**

**Overall Purpose of the Position**

The responsibilities of the **Head of Mission (HoM) Mali** include the overall operational, human resources and financial management of the mission Mali, ensuring programme quality, compliance, staff wellbeing, and the implementation of the country strategy. The responsibility also includes fundraising as well as communication and representation of arche nova e.V. towards relevant authorities and stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. General**

- Coordinate the general management of the AN Mali office and, in close coordination with headquarters (HQ), the further adjustment of the organisational structure.
- Ensure the strict application of arche nova's policies and procedures.
- Ensure all relevant and required reporting for authorities in Mali.
- Ensure that all operations are in line with laws of Mali.
- Implementation of AN Mali mission strategy in collaboration with the HQ in Germany and Senior Management Team.
- Ensure AN is represented in technical working groups in relevant sector clusters, ensure meaningful participation in advisory boards, steering committees, NGO consortia and other relevant meetings for Mali.
- Maintain strong relationships with authorities, donors, UN agencies, INGOs, and local partners.
- Ensure quality and timely communication and reporting with all relevant stakeholders.
- Close collaboration with and regular reporting to the different relevant departments at HQ level.
- Identify new funding opportunities and develop donor engagement plans.
- Ensure the promotion and visibility of AN through presentations, reports, and external communication.
- Fostering a positive and accountable work environment, as well as empowering and encouraging staff to take initiative
- Ensure safeguarding of AN’s assets and interests and protect from loss arising from fraud, waste, weak administration and poor value for money.
- Guarantee the correct, efficient, and effective use of logistical, financial and human resources.

**2. Programme & Grants Management**

- Oversee the management and quality assurance of all programmes and grants, ensuring compliance with AN policies and donor regulations in close cooperation with the Head of Programmes.
- Ensure that programme design reflects innovation, community participation, sustainability, and humanitarian principles.
- Supervise project implementation and provide regular support to programme staff and partners.
- Ensure MEAL systems, accountability mechanisms, learning processes, and safeguarding standards are implemented in close collaboration with the MEAL Officer.
- Lead and coordinate proposal development, ensuring strong technical input and alignment with donor priorities.
- Lead and strengthen existing consortia relations in close cooperation with the Desk Manager and the Head of Programmes.
- Approve and oversee external research, evaluations, audits, and rapid assessments of emerging crises.

**3. Human Resources, Administration & Capacity Building**

- Overseeing the HR management: development of programme staff structures, recruitment, performance monitoring, capacity building (including being the lead for any disciplinary procedures of AN staff, e.g. issuing warnings, terminations, suspensions, etc.)
- Promote staff wellbeing and duty of care, ensuring safe and enabling working conditions.
- Identify and support capacity-building needs for staff and partners.
- Ensure compliance with national labour laws, AN HR policies, safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and anti-fraud measures.
- Ensure harmonised and compliant administrative, procurement, and financial procedures.
- Ensure that internal review and exchange meetings are regularly conducted and documented

**4. Finance Management & Compliance**

- Oversee financial planning, budget management, expenditure monitoring, and forecasting.
- Ensure compliance with AN’s authority matrix, procurement rules, and donor financial regulations.
- Signatory of all contracts (i.e. employment, consultancies, contractors, PAs, etc.).
- Ensure compliance with AN, donor and governmental rules and regulations
- Support internal and external audits and ensure follow-up on audit recommendations.
- Monitor financial risks and advise HQ on sustainability and growth.

**5. Security Management**

- In collaboration with the HQ Global Security Advisor and the Security Focal Point, monitor the programme implementation environment, including security, political, development and personnel issues that may affect implementation of the projects, and provide updates to the Desk Manager (DM) and Team Lead Africa in a timely manner
- Ensure all security protocols, SOPs, contingency plans, and risk mitigation measures are up to date.
- Provide regular security briefings to HQ and ensure staff receive security training.
- Ensure appropriate response to political, operational, or natural crisis developments affecting programming.

**6. Operations, Logistics**

- Oversee logistics, procurement, fleet, warehousing, and asset management.
- Ensure transparent and efficient procurement in line with AN and donor standards.
- Oversee office registrations, legal compliance, and adherence to national regulations.
- Manage risk, prevent fraud, and safeguard AN’s assets and reputation.

**7. Partnership Management & Localisation**

- Strengthen partnerships with national NGOs, community-based organisations, and technical institutions.
- Lead due diligence processes, capacity-strengthening plans, and partnership compliance.
- Promote equitable partnerships and localisation principles.
- Where appropriate and feasible visit to project sites for monitoring purposes.

**8. Safeguarding (PSEA & Child Protection)**

- Ensure that safeguarding and PSEA policies are implemented across all offices and programmes.
- Deliver and monitor mandatory staff training on PSEA and child protection.
- Ensure there are confidential, safe, and efficient reporting mechanisms for safeguarding concerns.
- Promote a culture of protection, equality, and accountability among the staff and affected populations.

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree (or BA with substantial experience): in development and cooperation, humanitarian and international affairs, management of non-profits or other relevant fields.
- Minimum **5 years’ experience** in senior management roles in humanitarian or development settings.
- Strong experience in programme management, strategic leadership, HR oversight, and financial management.
- Firm understanding of donor compliance, reporting and proposal development (especially BMZ, German Federal Foreign Office, Europe Aid, ECHO)
- A broad understanding of the roles and responsibilities of international cooperation and humanitarian architecture including key actors, standards, clusters, donors
- Strong understanding of and experience in security management in complex environments.
- Excellent team leader skills, guidance and support to the team
- Fluency in written and spoken French; Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Bambara, is a strong asset.
- Sensitivity to cultural differences and the ability to work in a culturally diverse team
- High degree of intercultural competences and conflict-sensitivity, strong sense of integrity and sensitivity towards the needs of vulnerable groups
- Having the ability to work under pressure and changing project environment.
- Experience in West Africa, particularly Mali.
- Commitment to gender equality, safeguarding, and localisation.

Note: This position is only filled locally with a local contract (Mali). Applicants must hold a valid work permit.

We would like to encourage people with similar CVs, and especially women to apply.

**We offer:**

- Competitive salary
- 30 days of annual leave + public holidays
- Professional development and training
- An inclusive, respectful, and diversity-positive organisational culture

**Attention:** this is not a family duty station

However, arche nova is a family-friendly employer and allows for flexibility regarding children or care work.

AN is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment without attention to race, age, ability, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other factor. At AN we celebrate diversity and appreciate our employees for the people they are and their unique skills, backgrounds, and perspectives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply!

**Deadline for application:** 15.11.2026

title: Operational Research Advisor (f/m/x) specialized in Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)
body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international humanitarian aid organization that provides assistance in more than 70 countries to populations in distress, to victims of natural or manmade disasters and to victims of armed conflicts, without discrimination and irrespective of origin, religion, creed or political affiliation. Our actions are guided by medical ethics and the principle of impartiality, independence and neutrality.**

**To contribute to this work, MSF-Luxembourg is recruiting an**

## **Operational Research Advisor (f/m/x)** specialized in **Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)**

### **Context**

The Luxembourg Operational Research Unit (LuxOR) is part of the MSF-OCB Medical Department and supports evidence-based improvements to MSF operations through Operational Research. LuxOR is also coordinating Field Epidemiology activities, providing technical support to strengthen data quality, analysis, and operational decision-making across MSF projects.

We are looking for an **Operational Research Advisor** specializing in **Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Preventable Diseases (ID/VPD)** to support research activities ranging from outbreak documentation and epidemiological studies to clinical research and vaccine-related implementation studies.

**The successful candidate will combine strong scientific expertise with a pragmatic understanding of humanitarian operations and will work closely with medical, epidemiological, social science, and operational teams across MSF.**

### **Main responsibilities**

#### **Lead and support operational research activities**

- Guide research projects throughout the full research cycle, from question formulation to dissemination of results.
- Support the development of concept notes, study protocols, and ethical review submissions.
- Ensure methodological rigor, scientific quality, and adherence to ethical standards.
- Provide technical support to research teams and principal investigators.
- Contribute to manuscript writing, scientific publications, reports, policy briefs, and conference presentations.

#### **Research design, data analysis, and scientific support**

- Advise on study design, research methodologies, and data collection strategies.
- Support data management, statistical analysis, interpretation of findings, and evidence synthesis.
- Contribute expertise in infectious diseases, outbreak investigations, vaccination, and clinical research.
- Strengthen the use of research findings to inform operational decision-making and policy development.

#### **Capacity strengthening and collaboration**

- Mentor and support researchers and field teams.
- Contribute to training initiatives in operational research, epidemiology, and data analysis.
- Participate in field visits and provide direct support to projects.
- Promote collaboration across MSF departments and with external academic and public health partners.

#### **Support in advancing clinical research in the areas of ID/VPD in MSF in coordination with public health intelligence:**

- Contribute to advancing evidence synthesis and knowledge gaps in ID/VPD as one of the core activities of MSF activities.
- Information sharing, coordinate with social science teams, especially in areas like surveillance, outbreak response, and data analysis.
- Represent MSF in scientific networks, technical platforms, and international conferences.
- Support the translation of research evidence into operational practice and policy.

### **Profile**

- **Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment**
- **Adhere to the MSF Behavioural Commitments**

#### **Education**

- Postgraduate degree (Master's level minimum) in Medicine, Epidemiology, Public Health, Research Methods, Microbiology, or another relevant health-related discipline.
- PhD considered a strong asset.
- Certification in Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
- Additional training in epidemiology, biostatistics, or research methodologies is an advantage.

#### **Experience**

- Significant experience conducting operational, clinical, or biomedical research.
- Proven experience within MSF or another international humanitarian organization.
- Experience designing and implementing studies or clinical trials in low-resource and/or humanitarian settings.
- Experience in scientific writing and dissemination of research findings.

#### **Skills**

- Strong expertise in study design, epidemiology, biostatistics, and data interpretation.
- Excellent scientific writing and communication skills.
- Ability to work autonomously while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
- Strong commitment to research ethics, scientific integrity, and humanitarian principles.
- Proficiency with statistical software such as R and/or Stata,
- Knowledge of data management and data collection platforms (e.g., REDCap, Kobo).
- Knowledge of GIS and Health Information softwares are an asset (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS, HIS, DHIS2, etc)
- Excellent command of English (C1 level or higher).
- French is an asset.

### **What we offer**

- A unique opportunity to contribute to humanitarian medical research with global impact.
- Collaboration with multidisciplinary experts across the MSF movement.
- Exposure to innovative research in infectious diseases, vaccination, and outbreak response.
- Opportunities for field engagement, capacity building, and professional development.

### **Conditions**

- 1-year Full-time contract with possibility of extension
- Based in Luxembourg with frequent travels abroad
- Gross salary over 12 months from 63000 to 76200 € according to MSF experience
- 29 days annual paid leaves
- Possibility of teleworking 2 days per week
- Medical complementary insurance (including hospitalization)
- 18 Lunch vouchers each with a face value of 10,80 € (2/3 covered by MSF).
- Public transport allowance & relocation package (if applicable)
- **Expected starting date: Mid-January 2027**

title: Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors
body:
**Join MSF OCG as a Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

MSF Switzerland was created in 1981 and it is headquartered in Geneva. The Philanthropy Unit is one of the eight units at the Communications and Fundraising Department. To ensure a good geographical coverage of the Swiss fundraising market, the Unit is divided into two offices: Geneva and Zurich. The Unit’s mission is to strengthen MSF’s relationship with its private major supporters, including wealthy individuals, foundations, companies, and other philanthropic organisations. It also manages grants and donations from Swiss cantons and communes. Last but not least, it is also in charge of legacy fundraising, including management of heritages as well as contacts with potential legators and confirmed bequestors.

The Associate Philanthropy Advisor for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland is a key member of the Philanthropy Unit, ensuring an efficient and effective cultivation approach for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The mission is to secure and grow income for MSF from private major donors in German speaking Switzerland.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

*Strategy and action plan*

- Actively contribute to the implementation of the yearly plan

*Cultivation and stewardship*

- Manages a portfolio of Major Donors and potential Top Major Donors and, alongside the Team Coordinator, design and develop the donor journey for donors giving between CHF 10’000 and CHF 20’000 annually.
- Regularly reports to and consults with the Team Coordinator on the strategy for the pool regarding upgrading donors within this segment.
- Determine the best approach and journey for each individual donor depending on their wishes and level of engagement.
- Prepare and facilitate one-to-one meetings, calls, presentations and other meaningful interactions with major donors.
- Interact and collaborate with key spokespersons within MSF (President, General Director, Director of Operations, other management team members), as well as field staff, with the aim of bringing donors closer to the organisation to demonstrate our life-saving mission and work in the projects.
- Define, propose and organise visits to MSF offices and projects, in line with MSF criteria and guidance.
- Ensure that the nature / identity of donors is in line with MSF gifts acceptance policy.
- Ensure that the donor journey runs smoothly, and donors are thanked and stewarded promptly.
- Ensure the database is kept up-to-date.
- Draft engaging communication for the MDs about MSF projects.

*Solicitation/ask*

- In line with the yearly plan and past giving history of main donors, proactively present asks to selected donors for gifts (general and individualized asks) and consult with the Team Coordinator about the solicitation plan
- Ensure that the major donors journey strategy is followed and that major donors are solicited according to their motivations in a personalised way.

*Information and data management*

- Closely work with the System Support Team to ensure most efficient use of Customer Relationship Management Database.
- Support the Team Coordinator in income forecasting and quarterly analysis of results.

*Others*

- Participate in the Community of Practice for Individual Major Donors of MSF in particular with other German-speaking sections.
- Work proactively on projects as needed in the Unit, upon request by her/his supervisor.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing,
- Communications, Political Science, International
- Relations or other relevant areas

*Experience*

- First professional experience in the non-profit sector or in the fields of marketing/sales/communication or client relationship management

*Languages*

- German mother tongue & very good English
- French and Italian an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Proven excellent writing skills (drafting and editing)
- Excellent in oral public presentations
- Strong knowledge of the Windows environment (Word, Excel, Power Point) and tech-savvy
- Strong Analytical skills
- Knowledge of the humanitarian and development sector in Switzerland.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Service oriented
- Dynamic, proactive and autonomous
- Rigorous and good organizational skills
- Empathic, enthusiastic, optimistic
- Discretion
- Team spirit.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Zurich, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: As soon as possible
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 80’856.- to CHF 97’224.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

title: Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator - BU Support
body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
- The Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator will also perform any other duties as assigned by the manager.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong communication skills.
- Analytical Skills: Ability to apply logical thinking and problem-solving techniques to break down complex issues and reach sound conclusions.
- Data Analysis Skills: Proven ability to collect, analyze, and interpret large datasets to inform decision-making. Advanced proficiency in data manipulation and visualization tools, including expertise in Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, and Array formulas).
- Solid stakeholder management skills
- Strong working knowledge of process improvement tools and methodologies, DMAIC, 5Whys
- Supply chain risk management skills
- Commercial contracting skills
- Strategic sourcing skills
- Supplier relationship management skills
- Commercial negotiation skills
- Minimum 3 years of work experience in a demanding professional environment.
- Bachelor's degree in procurement, project management, business strategy, or related discipline. Candidates with higher diploma and extensive relevant experience may also qualify.
- Professional qualification e.g CIPS, CILT preferred
- Familiarity with procurement models, sourcing frameworks, and PR-PO systems such as Odoo or Power BI
- Language: Fluent in English and Kiswahili preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Grants officer (F/M) - Afghanistan
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing grants management, donor compliance, resource mobilization, and partnership and donor engagement for MdM in Afghanistan. In addition, you will be responsible for the mission's communication and will promote visibility on MdM works, particularly when it comes to ensuring implementation of donors’ communication requirements.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Proposal management:**

- Lead and coordinate concept notes and proposals
- Write the non-technical sections (context, needs analysis, cross-cutting)
- Ensure coherence between narrative, logframe and budget as well as alignment with MdM strategy and donor requirements

**Reporting:**

- Track all active grants and deadlines
- Coordinate donor and internal reports (including the monthly situation report)
- Ensure quality and consistency between programmatic and financial information

**Donor engagement:**

- Maintain donor mapping and a database of calls for proposals
- Train teams on donor rules, prepare meetings and briefing materials for the general coordinator
- Support audits and evaluations

**Partnerships:**

- Support the development of MoUs and partnership agreements
- Coordinate due diligence
- Manage collaboration with partners, including in a consortium

**Communication:**

- Develop communication products (factsheets, country profiles, success stories)
- Contribute to the visibility strategy, train staff on guidelines
- Collect field content, and manage social media in line with MdM and donor guidelines

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the program officer at HQ, the Institutional Funding Unit, the technical coordinators, the support coordinators, the MEAL team, and the communication teams at HQ and in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following or related field: Development, International Relations, Humanitarian Management
- Have at least two years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in coordinating and preparing strong narrative and financial reports for a variety of donors
- Have a strong understanding of donor compliance, especially for ECHO/INTPA, FCDO, BHA, GFFO
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in multi-donors’ budgets
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 069 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Climate Resilience and Adaptation Advisor
body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

**Summary:**

Position Summary

The Climate Resilience Advisor provides technical and advisory support to strengthen climate resilience of Habitat for Humanity’s housing and settlement work across Asia Pacific programs. The Advisor will work with the Asia-Pacific regional team to support Country Offices. This will include the implementation of strategic guidance, provision of technical assistance, design and delivery of capacity strengthening, supporting research, evidence-based implementation and knowledge management, advocacy and partnership development. This will include coordination with HFHI Global Program Operations, and specifically the Director-Climate Resilience (e.g., on development and implementation of the Global Climate Approach). The Advisor will work to ensure the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation into housing and settlement work and community development initiatives.

The Advisor will serve as the regional focal point for climate action, and in this capacity will support Country Offices to understand climate risks, and options to address/mitigate these risks to reduce vulnerability and build resilience of low- and middle-income households and communities across the Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Key Result Areas and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Alignment and Stakeholder Engagement (30%)**

Provide technical thought leadership to ensure climate resilient housing and settlement programming is aligned with the Global Climate Approach, with contextualized implementation across Country Offices in Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical leadership to support contextualized/localized implementation and monitoring of HFHI’s Global Climate Approach within the Asia Pacific region.
- Advise on current/recent sources of climate risk data and analyses, and options for integrating climate these risks into housing/settlement-focused project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Facilitate alignment and promote integration between climate resilience programming and broader disaster risk reduction/humanitarian programming.
- Serve as a technical resource and thought partner to Habitat Country Offices, supporting program design, implementation and learning.
- Engage with external stakeholders (HFHI’s global and regional partners, research institutions, NGOs, and networks) to strengthen technical positioning and partnerships opportunities around climate resilience and DRR.
- Represent HFHI and contribute to relevant regional and global forums, working groups, and coordination platforms, as required.
- Support strategic partnerships and collaboration opportunities that advance Habitat's climate resilience agenda.

**2. Capacity Building and Technical Support (25%)**

Strengthen the technical capacity of Country Offices and partners to design, implement, and scale high-quality climate resilience housing/settlement programming

**Key Responsibilities**

Assess in-country capacity, design and facilitate targeted capacity building initiatives (e.g., structured training, workshops, coaching) for National Organization staff on climate resilience.

Develop and maintain technical resources, tools, guidance documents, and learning materials.

Facilitate communities of practice, peer learning, and regional exchanges.

Promote organizational learning across countries, programs and operations.

**3. Technical Program Oversight (25%)**

Provide advisory support to Country Offices to help ensure the quality of climate-related program design, implementation and monitoring. considerations into program designs, projects—supporting Country Offices to scale impact, and cross-learning across the Asia Pacific Region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical input and advisory support to Country Offices to strengthen integration of climate risk data/analyses and evidenced-based approaches into climate resilient housing/settlements project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Advise Country Offices on context specific adaptation measures, including resilient construction techniques, site selection, safer land use, and community-based approaches.
- Where feasible, advise Country Offices on context appropriate mitigation measures, where feasible,
- Contribute technical input to concept notes, program proposals, and donor reports related to climate resilience (e.g., adaptation and mitigation).
- As requested, support donor engagement resource mobilization efforts.
- Collaborate with other Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and technical teams to ensure climate considerations are integrated into cross-sectoral programming.

**4. Research, Innovation, Learning and Knowledge Management (15%)**

Strengthen evidence generation, cross-learning and innovation, to improve climate resilient housing/settlement programming and support scaling of effective approaches.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support research design and implementation, the generation and synthesis of evidence, and institutional learning specific to climate resilient housing.
- Document and share climate resilient housing/settlement promising practices, case studies, and lessons learned.
- Contribute to integration of climate and DRR indicators into MEAL systems and contribute to regional and global learning agendas.
- Contribute to research, support innovation pilots, and partnerships related to climate resilient housing and settlements.
- Develop and disseminate technical resources, and guidance materials.
- Provide subject matter expertise and technical advisory support to other departments and initiatives within HFHI.

**5. Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery Support (5%)**

Provide advisory support to integrate climate risk reduction and resilience into disaster preparedness, response and recovery efforts

**Key Responsibilities**

Work with the Housing Disaster Risk and Resilience (HDRR) team on climate risk reduction measures in response and recovery

Provide technical input on risk-informed approaches to recovery planning and implementation

Support alignment of recovery interventions with long-term resilience objectives

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Risk Reduction, Urban Planning, Engineering, Development Studies, or a related field
- Minimum 5–7 years of relevant experience in climate resilience, DRR, or risk-informed programming, preferably in the Asia-Pacific region
- Demonstrated experience supporting multi-country programs and working with decentralized teams
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, and resilience approaches in housing, settlements, or community development
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, resilience, and mitigation approaches in housing, settlements, infrastructure, or community development.
- Experience in humanitarian, recovery, or nexus programming is an asset
- Experience in donor engagement, proposal development, or climate finance is an advantage

**Key Skills & Competencies**

- Strong technical expertise in climate adaptation and the built environment
- Sound understanding of climate mitigation, with the ability to understand where synergies and tradeoffs exist between mitigation and adaptation (especially where these impact affordability)
- Ability to translate technical concepts into practical, field-oriented guidance
- Proven advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English (regional languages an asset)
- Strong cross-cultural collaboration skills and ability to work in matrixed environments
- Willingness and ability to travel within the Asia-Pacific region

**Core Behavioral Competencies**

- Commitment to HFHI’s mission, values, equity, and safeguarding principles
- Collaboration and partnership mindset
- Learning oriented and solution focused
- Accountability and integrity

**Working Conditions**

- Regional role with frequent collaboration across multiple countries and time zones.
- Periodic travel to Country Offices and Country Offices, including fragile, climate-vulnerable, and disaster-affected contexts.
- Ability and willingness to travel within the Asia-Pacific region as required.

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

title: Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager
body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** will provide strategic and technical expertise in the design, development, governance, and deployment of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data systems, including databases, digital platforms, and AI-enabled solutions. Support evidence-based management and strengthen capacity across Pacific Island countries through innovative, standardised, and sustainable data systems.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Develop and maintain high-quality regional and national coastal fisheries and aquaculture databases and information systems and provide training in their use**

- Develops, maintains and updates the regional coastal fisheries (science, management and development) and aquaculture databases including training in the use of databases, data extraction and analysis
- Develops new web and mobile applications for the regional and national databases in line with country needs and the needs of the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff
- Develops and assists in maintaining national databases based on the regional databases and additional modules.
- Develops specific queries for data extraction and analysis as required by countries or the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff.
- Promotes and encourages the use of standard databases and information systems across the region for coastal fisheries and aquaculture data, and countries to providing the data they collect for back-up and storage at SPC.
- Identifies and develops linkages between the coastal fisheries and oceanic fisheries databases in collaboration with oceanic fisheries statistics and data collection section.
- Identifies ways to better use GIS and remote sensing products in relation to the analysis of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data.

**Practical assistance to members in the designing and targeting of appropriate awareness raising and educational information**

- Develops training materials on data entry, cleaning and extraction.
- Assists with developing and maintaining the website for the CFAP with the Information Unit to assist with the dissemination of information in general.
- Provides input to awareness raising and educational materials focused on coastal fisheries science and/or management or livelihoods and aquaculture

**Develop Artificial Intelligence based tools and models for data collection**

- Improves coastal fisheries and aquaculture data collection using photos and videos automatically processed by computer vision and artificial intelligence
- Develops and trains models to calibrate and reproject pictures for measurement from picture
- Develops and trains models to automate measurements of fishes and invertebrates for the various types of measurements
- Develops and trains models for species identification

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration in coastal fisheries and aquaculture**

- Develops links with other CROP agencies and NGOs in regard to database needs and design for coastal fisheries and aquaculture
- Advocates at global forums on behalf of the Pacific region sectoral interests
- Develops and promotes collaborations within the CFAP on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.
- Works closely with other sections of CFAP to ensure smooth implementation of projects.

**Administration and communication**

- Assists the CFAP Deputy Director and Section heads, to include information and database needs in the annual work plans and work plan reports for each Section, consistent with the strategic plan.
- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, and Divisional reports for CRGA.
- Produces reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity including technical reports and trip reports, and input to funding proposals, donor reports.
- Manage, develop and train direct report.
- Fills in for senior staff when they are on leave or duty travel, when required

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master’s in computer science, database development or a related field/discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ of demonstrated experience in database management, project management and software development associated with the successful implementation of medium- to large-scale web and desktop application systems.
- At least 8 years’ of demonstrated experience in the use of Microsoft products, both as a user and developer, in particular, (i) experience in software engineering, (ii) programming in client-server environments in C# with MS Visual Studio, (iii) ASP.NET Core and single page web applications with MS Visual Studio (C#, JavaScript and angularjs), (iv) database technologies (preferably SQL Server) and other database formats, (v) development of mobile application in C# (.NET MAUI).
- Demonstrated experience with (i) producing system and user manual documentation, (ii) user training and (iii) ongoing technical support for deployed applications.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills, detail orientation, and ability to multi-task.

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and negotiate with people from different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
