title: Gestor de casos de violencia basada en género (VBG) - Catatumbo
body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Gestor/a de Casos de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG)** altamente calificado con sede en **Catatumbo, Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Gerencia de Protección de la base, el/la Gestor/a de Casos de VBG apoyará la implementación en terreno del componente de respuesta y atención a la Violencia Basada en Género (VBG) en el marco de las intervenciones humanitarias de DRC Venezuela. La persona seleccionada será responsable de brindar atención individualizada directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG y personas en riesgo bajo el modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG, garantizando el cumplimiento de los principios rectores (enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, confidencialidad, seguridad, respeto y no discriminación).

Asimismo, integrará un enfoque diferencial de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), interseccionalidad y derechos humanos, asegurando el adecuado mapeo, articulación y derivación con servicios especializados (salud, legal, protección infantil, apoyo psicosocial) y actores institucionales locales (Consejos de Protección de NNA, Defensoría del Pueblo, Ministerio Público, Centros de Salud), contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de los entornos de protección comunitarios y a la calidad de la información del programa.

**RESPONSABILIDADES**

- Implementar el ciclo completo del modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG (evaluación, plan de atención, seguimiento y cierre), brindando Primera Ayuda Psicológica bajo principios de estricta confidencialidad y consentimiento informado.
- Elaborar planes de seguridad individualizados junto con las personas sobrevivientes para mitigar sus factores de riesgo.
- Gestionar derivaciones seguras y oportunas a servicios especializados (atención médica/atención postexposición, asesoría legal, atención en salud mental y apoyo psicosocial y/o alojamiento).
- Mantener actualizado el mapeo local de actores y rutas de atención (CPNNA, Fiscalía, Defensorías, centros de salud, etc.).
- Facilitar sesiones comunitarias de sensibilización sobre prevención de VBG, derechos humanos y rutas de atención, promoviendo la inclusión de mujeres, niñas, personas con discapacidad y población OSIEGD.
- Registrar de manera oportuna, segura y confidencial la información de los casos en las plataformas internas (KoBo, bases de datos), garantizando la entrega de insumos mensuales para reportes programáticos y donantes.
- Garantizar la aplicación transversal de la Política de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), la Rendición de Cuentas (AAP), el enfoque de No Hacer Daño (Do No Harm) y los estándares de Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS).
- Participar en reuniones de seguimiento técnico, supervisión de casos y coordinación interinstitucional según los requerimientos operativos de la base.

**REQUISITOS, EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

**Educación:**

- Pregrado / Titulación universitaria en Ciencias Sociales, Salud o Humanidades (Psicología, Trabajo Social, Sociología, Orientación o áreas afines).

**Experiencia laboral:**

- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia práctica relevante en atención directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG, gestión de casos de VBG o implementación de programas de protección de género/apoyo psicosocial.
- Experiencia demostrable en el trabajo con comunidades en situación de vulnerabilidad, población en movilidad/migración, comunidades rurales, indígenas o personas OSIEGD.
- Mínimo un (1) año de experiencia en contextos humanitarios o de cooperación internacional (deseable en el contexto venezolano).

**Conocimientos técnicos:**

- Dominio del modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG y de las Directrices del IASC para la integración de intervenciones contra la Violencia Basada en Género en la Acción Humanitaria.
- Conocimiento del marco normativo nacional venezolano (Ley Orgánica sobre el Derecho de las
- Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia, LOPNNA, entre otros) y de los servicios de atención institucionales y comunitarios.
- Manejo del enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, enfoque de derechos, interseccionalidad y diversidad (AGD).
- Conocimiento del contexto socio-humanitario específico de la base a la que postula (Apure/Guasdualito, Zulia/Maracaibo, Zulia/ Sur del Lago o Sucre/Carúpano).
- Manejo intermedio de herramientas ofimáticas (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint) y plataformas de recolección de datos (KoBoToolbox).

**Habilidades Personales:**

- Altas habilidades relacionales, comunicación asertiva, escucha activa, empatía y confidencialidad.
- Capacidad de resolución de conflictos y toma de decisiones en situaciones complejas.
- Capacidad de trabajo en equipo multidisciplinario y adaptabilidad al trabajo de campo/terreno en zonas de difícil acceso.

IDIOMAS:

- Español (obligatorio)
- Comprensión escrita de lenguaje inglés (es una ventaja)

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**

title: Caseworker
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Casework Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Mission France - Responsables des activités de santé mentale F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de santé mentale pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte:**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre action médicale, coordination opérationnelle et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration, vous assurerez la coordination, la supervision et le suivi des activités de santé mentale du projet.

Vous encadrerez les psychologues, garantirez la qualité des prises en charge et contribuerez à l’adaptation des interventions aux besoins identifiés sur le terrain.

Votre fonction associera **pilotage opérationnel, supervision clinique, management d’équipe et contribution aux orientations stratégiques du projet**.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

## **Définir et piloter les activités de santé mentale**

- Identifier et analyser les besoins en santé mentale des personnes accompagnées et contribuer à l’élaboration de la stratégie du projet.
- Planifier, organiser et adapter les activités de soutien psychologique et psychosocial, individuelles et collectives, en fonction des besoins et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir l’application des protocoles et standards MSF, ainsi que la qualité des interventions réalisées dans les structures de soins et sur les lieux d’intervention.
- Participer, avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration et le·la Référent·e du projet, à l’élaboration et à l’actualisation des protocoles, outils et supports techniques, conformément aux recommandations sanitaires applicables.
- Superviser la prise en charge des situations complexes et veiller à ce que les personnes nécessitant un soutien psychiatrique bénéficient d’une orientation et d’un suivi adaptés, y compris pour les traitements prescrits.
- Contribuer aux discussions stratégiques et opérationnelles afin d’adapter les interventions aux réalités du terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences des équipes**

- Encadrer les psychologues et organiser leurs plannings entre consultations, activités collectives et interventions d’« aller-vers ».
- Assurer, en collaboration avec les ressources humaines, le recrutement, l’intégration et l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant supervision, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Apporter un appui technique et organiser des formations en santé mentale pour les équipes pluridisciplinaires et les partenaires du projet.
- Veiller à ce que les médiateur·rices et les interprètes intervenant lors des consultations disposent des connaissances et des repères nécessaires pour assurer une communication adaptée.
- Favoriser la coopération, la communication interne et le respect d’une posture professionnelle neutre, indépendamment des convictions personnelles.

**Renforcer les parcours de soins et la coordination pluridisciplinaire**

- Favoriser une prise en charge globale des personnes en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, de travail social et de médiation.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires de gestion de cas et accompagner la recherche de solutions pour les situations complexes ou prioritaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie des services de santé mentale, des structures spécialisées, des associations et des partenaires du territoire.
- Renforcer les mécanismes d’orientation internes et externes, en tenant compte de l’accessibilité et des capacités de prise en charge des services existants.
- Entretenir des relations régulières avec les partenaires institutionnels, associatifs et sanitaires afin de faciliter la continuité des accompagnements.
- Identifier et documenter les obstacles à l’accès aux soins, notamment les insuffisances des dispositifs de prise en charge d’urgence après des événements traumatiques.

**Analyser les résultats et garantir la qualité des interventions**

- Superviser la collecte et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de santé mentale, en veillant à leur fiabilité.
- Définir et suivre les indicateurs, évaluer les résultats et produire les rapports d’activité nécessaires au pilotage du projet.

body:
**The Vacancy**

Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian relief and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world’s most vulnerable people. Established in 1984, with an active presence in over 45 countries, we strive to make the world a better and fairer place for those affected by poverty, conflict and natural disasters. IRUK’s focus is strengthening effective funding, mobilising for change through advocacy and awareness-raising, and strengthening programme development and delivery. IRUK works with various partners and institutions, from governments, non-governmental organisations and local authorities to grassroots communities.

Islamic Relief UK (IRUK) is actively recruiting for the position of Fundraising Admin Assistant to be based across one of the following regions: Glasgow, Manchester, Bradford, Leicester, Birmingham or East London.

**Job Purpose**

The Fundraising Admin Assistant will play an important role in supporting the successful delivery of regional fundraising activities across their designated area. The postholder will provide high-quality administrative support, assist with fundraising events and campaigns, coordinate volunteer involvement, maintain accurate financial and supporter records, and help ensure an excellent experience for donors, supporters and local communities. Working closely with the regional fundraising team, the role will contribute towards the achievement of regional fundraising objectives, particularly during busy campaign periods such as Ramadan. ​

**The successful candidate must have:**

- Experience in an administrative role.
- Experience of effectively maintaining electronic and paper administrative, financial and information systems.
- Proven experience of successfully working under pressure, with multiple demands and in a busy environment.
- Knowledge and understanding of the local region and community.
- Strong organisational and administrative skills.
- Good communication skills.
- The ability to work accurately under pressure and pay attention to detail.
- High standard of numeracy skills in accurately entering and recording financial data and other general calculations whilst working within defined procedures and regulations.
- Ability to represent Islamic Relief in a wide range of situations.
- Ability to work under pressure, be self-motivated and deliver to target.
- IT literacy with the ability to use Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Familiarity with social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter) and other digital channels.
- Strong motivation and empathy towards the aims and objectives of the organisation.
- A friendly, proactive and team-focused approach, with a willingness to support colleagues and volunteers when required.
- Willingness to work flexibly, including occasional evenings, weekends and travel as required.
- A full UK driving licence.

For more information, please click on the Documents tab above to view the full Job Description.

If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient and a highly motivated professional looking for a meaningful career, with a strong commitment to IRW’s mission and values of sincerity, excellence, compassion, social justice and custodianship, please apply by completing our online application form.

title: Coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H) - République Centrafricaine
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## Médecins du Monde en RCA

La République centrafricaine (RCA) demeure confrontée à des conflits armés récurrents, entraînant une crise humanitaire majeure et de nombreuses violations des droits humains et du droit international humanitaire.

Présente dans le pays depuis 2013, Médecins du Monde (MdM) France intervient auprès des populations les plus vulnérables à travers des soins de santé dans les zones reculées, des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive, la prise en charge des survivant·e·s de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et le déploiement de cliniques mobiles d’urgence. En 2025, ses interventions ont bénéficié à 278 113 personnes.

Récemment, MdM a renforcé sa présence opérationnelle avec le lancement, en novembre 2024, d’un projet à Batangafo dédié à la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants et des survivant·e·s de VBG. En mars 2026, une nouvelle base a été ouverte dans la sous-préfecture de Kabo, grâce au financement de la DG ECHO, afin d’appuyer six formations sanitaires, dont l’hôpital secondaire, pour une durée de seize mois.

Pour les prochaines années, MdM prévoit d’accroître ses activités, ses financements et sa couverture géographique, tout en consolidant son positionnement comme acteur de référence dans le domaine de la santé, notamment en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG. L’organisation poursuit également sa collaboration avec les autres ONG internationales afin de renforcer la coordination humanitaire, le partage d’informations et l’efficacité des interventions.

## Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous

En tant que coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H), vous aurez pour principales missions de piloter et de coordonner la stratégie et la mise en œuvre des programmes du consortium Fonds Humanitaire à Batangafo, Bouca, Kabo et Sido, en animant les équipes et les partenaires, en garantissant l'application des procédures MdM et en développant le plaidoyer et les partenariats.

Vous assurerez l’animation du consortium entre MdM et Solidarités International sur la base.

## Vos missions

Plus spécifiquement, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes:

## 1. Coordination, représentation et partenariats

- Représenter MdM auprès des autorités, acteurs humanitaires, bailleurs, partenaires techniques et forces présentes dans la zone d’intervention
- Participer aux mécanismes de coordination, ateliers, conférences et visites institutionnelles afin de renforcer le positionnement de MdM
- Assurer des relations régulières avec les partenaires et veiller à la cohérence des actions menées sur la zone

## 2. Pilotage stratégique et gestion du consortium

- Diriger le consortium, animer la gouvernance, coordonner les membres et garantir une prise de décision efficace et transparente
- Définir, suivre et actualiser les plans d’action, de contingence et de suivi-évaluation (MEAL), tout en veillant à la bonne utilisation des ressources
- Produire des analyses, recommandations et retours d’expérience permettant d’améliorer la qualité des interventions et la coopération opérationnelle

## 3. Supervision opérationnelle et suivi des projets

- Organiser et coordonner les activités de la base de Batangafo, y compris les projets, la construction des infrastructures et les relations avec les partenaires
- Piloter la planification des activités, suivre les indicateurs, les échéances contractuelles et l’exécution des actions afin d’assurer leur qualité et leur conformité
- Contribuer à la définition des orientations stratégiques, assurer le reporting opérationnel et capitaliser les enseignements tirés des interventions

## 4. Gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire

- Assurer une veille contextuelle et sécuritaire, collecter et partager les informations nécessaires à l’analyse des risques
- Élaborer, actualiser et faire appliquer les dispositifs de sécurité, tout en sensibilisant les équipes aux procédures et règles en vigueur
- Garantir l’accès humanitaire, gérer les incidents de sécurité et coordonner les réponses opérationnelles et les communications en cas de crise

## 5. Management des équipes et supervision des fonctions support

- Encadrer les équipes de la base : recrutement, intégration, fixation des objectifs, évaluation des performances, accompagnement et développement des compétences
- Favoriser la cohésion d’équipe, gérer les conflits, faire respecter les politiques internes et prendre les mesures correctives nécessaires
- Superviser les volets RH, financiers, administratifs et logistiques de la base, notamment le budget, le suivi des ressources et le respect des procédures internes

## Vos collègues

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du coordinateur général (F/H) basé à Bangui, vous collaborez avec l’équipe de coordination de MdM à Bangui et les chefs de base des ONGs membres du consortium ainsi le chef d’Antenne OCHA de Batangafo et tous les responsables des ONGs Internationales et nationales présente à Batangafo. Vous supervisez directement les responsables des équipes support et programmes.

## Vous êtes la bonne personne si…

- Vous êtes diplômé.e d'une formation supérieure en gestion de projet ou généraliste de l’Humanitaire
- Vous avez obligatoirement une expérience réussie de trois ans minimum sur un poste similaire de coordinateur terrain au sein d'ONGi en appui de programmes humanitaires financés par des bailleurs intstitutionnels
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en ouverture de base (fortement souhaité)
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en élaboration, conduite et évaluation de projet de santé d’urgence dans des pays et/ou zones en crise
- Vous avez une expérience réussie dans la gestion de la sécurité et de l'accès dans un contexte sécuritaire volatile
- Vous avez une expérience significative en management d'équipe
- Vous êtes capable d'arbitrer en cas de dilemme de manière structurée et méthodique
- Vous savez faire preuve de proactivité, d'organisation et de planification
- Vous parlez couramment le français et l'anglais
- Vous avez une bonne maîtrise du Pack Office et des outils de travail collaboratifs

## Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si...

- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde
- Vous ne vous sentez pas à l'aise pour vivre et travailler dans des conditions de vie relativement simples, voire spartiates
- Vous n'avez pas d'expérience de travail en équipe interculturelle et multidisciplinaire
- Vous ne savez pas faire preuve de patience, diplomatie et pédagogie

## **Les prochaines étapes**

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un.e chargé.e de recrutement. Les entretiens, technique et managérial, auxquels des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés, auront lieu dans le courant du mois de novembre.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez !

## Vos conditions d’emploi

**Contrat & statut :**

- Salaire brut mensuel 3 663 €
- CDD à pourvoir à partir du 1er novembre jusqu'au 30/08/2027 (non glissant)
- Départ seul

Cadre de travail :

- Poste basé à Batangafo
- Déplacements à prévoir sur la zone du projet (Sido, Batangafo Kabo et Bouca) et à Bangui

Les avantages :

- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime d’expatriation de 10% du salaire brut par mois
- Prise en charge du transport (domicile – mission), des visas, des vaccins
- Hébergement: vous serez hébergé.e en guest house (bon niveau de confort)
- Politique R&R: tous les trois mois
- Assurance santé (participation à 50% de MdM et 50% du salarié)
- Assurance rapatriement
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

Les indispensables :

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

Diversité et inclusion

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

- Garantir la fiabilité des données financières à travers le contrôle des imputations, des pièces comptables, des inventaires de caisse, de l’archivage et du respect des exigences légales et bailleurs
- Élaborer, consolider et suivre les budgets, prévisions financières et plans de trésorerie de la mission
- Assurer le pilotage des financements en optimisant l’allocation des ressources, le suivi des contrats bailleurs et l’analyse régulière des écarts budgétaires et risques financiers

- Assurer le suivi du parcours collaborateur (intégration, évaluation, départ) et accompagner les managers dans la gestion disciplinaire

- Assurer le pilotage financier des financements en élaborant les budgets bailleurs, en suivant le plan de financement de la mission et les engagements contractuels de MdM
- Produire les rapports financiers destinés aux bailleurs et contribuer aux volets financiers des propositions de financement et demandes de subventions

- Coordonner les audits financiers et bailleurs, assurer la relation avec les auditeurs et veiller à la mise en œuvre des recommandations issues des contrôles

title: Request for proposals : provision of WIBA plus and group personal accident insurance policy & employer’s liability insurance
body:
**Background**

Tdh is present in Kenya since 2011. Currently Tdh is providing protection services for children and families affected by migration, natural crises and poverty in Dadaab, Kakuma refugee camps, in Garissa and Turkana County respectively, and in Kiambu for child’s rights business in Kiambu County

## The Need/Purpose

TDH provides WIBA Plus & GPA insurance & Employer’s Liability coverage for its employees across the country. TDH is now soliciting detailed proposals from eligible insurance firms to provide WIBA Plus & GPA Insurance for its staff. **The staff number will be subject to change due to staff leaving and staff being hired**.

## Salaries and number of Staff

Details for number of staff as at October 2026 of staff is 52 at an accumulative gross salary of 11,029,041.22 broken down into below categories.

- **Category 1.** 48 Office Workers

Gross Salary Kshs 10,756,899.47

- **Category 2**. 4 Drivers

Gross Salary Kshs. 272,141.75

## Scope of Work/ Service Outcomes

TDH requires extensions provided to cover the following cases/incidents; and all proposals should provide limits on but not limited to the items below.

**GROUP LIFE**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 3 Times annual salary
- Permanent Total Disability - 3 Times annual salary
- Critical illness – 30% of sum Assured to a maximum of 10,000,000.00.
- Last Expense
    - Last expense Main Member – Kshs.300,000.00
    - Coffin and Hearse – Kshs.100,000.00
    - Dependent’s last expense - Kshs.100,000.00
    - Free Cover Limit Kshs 25,000,000.00

**WIBA/GPA**

- Accidental Death Benefit – 8 Times annual Gross salary
- Accidental/ Occupational Permanent Total Disability - 8 Times annual Gross salary
- Temporary Total Disability (Accidental) – Salary up to a maximum of 104 weeks
- Medical Expenses Reimbursement Benefit – Maximum Kshs.800,000.00
- 24 hour cover
- Death as a result of accident or natural causes
- Death as a result of pandemic (e.g COVID-19)
- Permanent disability as a result of accident or critical illness
- Temporary disability as result of accident or illness
- Medical expenses
- Mobility artificial appliances
- Repatriation of mortal remains
- Funeral expenses
- Extension to cover riots, strikes, civil commotions, burns and disfigurements
- Disappearance
- Terrorism extension (Death or Injuries)
- Exclusion of post-mortem report requirement.
- Worldwide Cover
- Inclusion of motor cycling as a driver or passenger but not as racing/sporting
- Inclusion of football, rugby, lawn tennis, badminton.

**EMPLOYER’S LIABILITY**

Limit of Liability

- Limit per person: Kshs. 10,000,000.00
- Any one event Kshs. 25,000,000.00
- Any one period Kshs. 50,000,000.00

## Note to Quote:

Please quote rate applicable for:

- Premium for year 2027 and proposal for 2027
    - Policy excess.
    - Short term Cover or pro rata premium calculation.
    - refund of premium when staff leave.
    - refund policy of medical expense incurred when staff use other medical providers.
    - Please quote any free rider or cover

## Timelines for compensation

The insurance provider upon being notified of applicable accident or scheduled disease shall submit all required documentation within two days and payment shall be made no more than One Month from the date of receiving all documentation submitted by TDH.

## Duration of Cover

The successful Company will enter into a contract with TDH for a period of TWO (2) years. This contract will be renewed based on performance and availability of funding.

**Reporting**

We expect a quarterly report to indicate number of accidents reported, those processed and those outstanding and any recommendations. We do expect minimal TDH staff involvement in processing claims and thus should have a dedicated account holder to help.

## Adding and deletion of Members

Staff who join during the policy year should be added on cover on a pro rata basis. Staff who leave the organization during the policy year should be deleted and reimbursement made for the remaining period.

**Criteria for Proposal Evaluation.**

**Technical Proposal**

Each bidder shall submit a technical proposal addressing the services required and clearly demonstrating how they will meet TDH’s needs.

The proposal will be evaluated according to the following criteria:

- Benefit coverage.
- Claim Settlement timeline.
- Technical support Competency
- Demonstrated Capacity to meet required deliverables.
- Quality of service (ng systems)

**Financial Proposal.**

The financial proposal shall be evaluated according to the price structure proposed.

**Other required Competencies/Skills.** The successful bidder should have.

- Extensive experience and a proven track record in the Life insurance business – List of top 3 clients in the last 3 years is required.
- Sound experience in servicing international organizations – Proof of association with an INGO in Kenya
- Ability to provide 24-hours service.
- Real time administrative support systems – Ability to assign an account manager.
- NO INSURANCE BROKERS

title: Tupande Local Sales, Retail & Market Development Lead
body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a commercial professional with 2+ years of FMCG experience to drive Tupande's market expansion in Kenya, get products onto major supermarket shelves, launch Animal Feed and BioChar, and secure high-value B2B sales for excess produce.

## **Responsibilities**

Business Development & Market Expansion:

- Identify, evaluate, and pursue new market opportunities and distribution networks for Tupande’s retail products (roasted macadamia and dried fruit), and animal feed products.
- Place products in major supermarkets, wholesale distributors, and key retail avenues
- Map local demand for excess produce and processing byproducts generated by export value chains.
- Develop direct-to-business (B2B) or alternative local sales channels to sell Biochar, Animal Feed, excess produce and processing byproducts from across Tupdande’s value chains.

Sales Management:

- Build, negotiate, and maintain strategic partnerships with B2B customers, retail buyers, distributors, and store managers
- Take full ownership of current customer relationships, ensuring consistent engagement, satisfaction, and retention.
- Drive the sales pipeline and close deals to achieve or exceed targets.
- Provide accurate revenue forecasting to department leadership.

Account Management:

- Maintain and grow strategic accounts by providing excellent service, understanding client needs, and offering tailored solutions.
- Ensure a high standard of customer experience at all times.

Strategy design and execution

- Design and execute the go-to-market strategies for Tupande Retail products, Animal Feed and Bio Char

Performance Monitoring:

- Track and analyze sales performance, provide regular updates, and implement corrective actions to meet objectives.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 2+ years of experience in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), or retail distribution (experience getting products onto major supermarket shelves is strongly preferred)
- Experience in selling at scale: managing a minimum recurring revenue of $5m personally, structuring commercial agreements, negotiating trade terms, managing credit risks, and international import/export regulations
- Experience in building new accounts.
- Proven track record of taking new products—ideally in food, agriculture, or animal nutrition—from concept to market launch.
- You can bridge market opportunities with on-the-ground operational capacities
- Strong ability to negotiate listing fees, payment terms, and margins with retail giants and commercial distributors.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Democratic Republic of Congo.

## **Application Deadline**

14 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

title: Iraq Country Director
body:
## IRAQ COUNTRY DIRECTOR

### FULL-TIME - ERBIL, IRAQ

#### ABOUT FREE TO RUN

Free to Run’s mission is to advance gender equity globally through running. We are a registered nonprofit/nongovernmental organization that has been operating community-led programs for adolescent girls and young women since 2014. We are known for delivering long-term, youth-led, progressive running, leadership, rights, and health programs directly to adolescent girls and young women living in protracted conflict zones. However, the longer-term impact of our work is building enduring social change - decreasing barriers to public participation, increasing women in leadership, and making power structures more equitable and inclusive. Free to Run identifies as an organization working at the intersections of feminism, human rights, development, and humanitarian interventions.

In 2027, we will begin to execute on a new three-year strategic plan which has the organization positioned to grow in a multitude of directions - programmatically, operationally, financially and geographically. The achievement of our mission will continue to be rooted in our work across three strategic pillars: direct service (EMPOWER), capacity building for local NGOs (EQUIP), and building a global movement of activists who are passionate about gender equity and running (MOVE).

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Iraq Country Director is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the organization’s work in Iraq – from big picture to the small details. The Country Director is responsible for building the Free to Run network in the country, with a specific focus on donor-relations to achieve fundraising goals and grow the organization’s profile. The Country Director reports directly to the (internationally-based) Executive Director.

**CORE ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1) Develop and Manage an Effective and Informed Iraq Country Strategy (10%)**

- Envision a high-impact Iraq strategy that aligns with Free to Run’s global strategy
- Develop and track key performance indicators related to strategy
- Participate in organizational strategic planning, budgeting and performance reporting activities

**2) Oversee Free to Run Programs (20%)**

- Oversee program development and design efforts for Iraq-based programs, with support of Senior Program Officer who will directly manage program cycles, currently designed to be operating in three provinces by 2023
- Ensure all programs are adequately staffed and resourced, support staff training and development
- Oversee safe and high-quality program implementation, monitor day-to-day activities of Program staff
- Ensure all programs are monitored and evaluated using standard instruments, work closely with the Executive Director to improve current data collection tools to provide more accurate and timely information on project indicators for success
- Lead program learning and analysis activities with staff, contribute to global learning practices
- Develop and maintain relationships with key local, regional and national stakeholders to ensure smooth operations
- Ensure program data and learning is shared with other relevant staff for program improvement, external reporting and communications

**3) Grow and Lead a High-Performing Team (30%)**

- Lead recruitment, interviewing, hiring and on-boarding/off-boarding of Iraq Free to Run team
- Manage Senior Program Officer and Finance and Operations Officer (others as deemed necessary for growth and as resources allow)
- Ensure the organization and employees comply with all relevant in-country employment laws and best practices
- Coordinate the bi-annual goal setting and performance review processes for all administrative employees and support a culture of constant feedback and learning through targeted coaching and mentoring organization-wide
- Support visits from international staff, Board members and volunteers

**4) Oversee Country-level Finances and Operations (20%)**

- Develop and manage organizational country budget and finances as well as program budgets for specific projects
- Work with bookkeeper to manage administration of expenses, handling of cash and procurement processes, and accounts payable and receivable
- Prepare timely, high-quality financial and narrative reports
- Ensure financial compliance with national and local laws, as well as Free to Run’s finance policies
- Ensure all office operations are functional, with support from Finance and Operations Officer
- Liaise with Executive Director on a regular basis to ensure financial cohesion
- Confirm all registrations and permits to operate as an NGO are up to date, secure licenses to operate in new geographies as needed

**5) Build Support for Free to Run in Iraq (20%)**

- Identify, cultivate and follow through on funding opportunities across sectors, including mapping potential funding opportunities, meeting with potential and current partners and developing funding proposals (with support from the Executive Director)
- Use strong storytelling and persuasion skills to build individual and community support for Free to Run in Iraq amongst key stakeholders
- Compile and prepare Iraq case studies and stories, provide regular input to Free to Run’s social media channels
- Communicate regularly with Free to Run’s community partners and coordinating their participation in events
- Represent Free to Run at influential events and speaking engagements locally, regionally and internationally
- Write press releases and editorial content for website and earned media opportunities

LOCATION

The Country Director position is based in Erbil (KRI) with an expectation of travel to other parts of Iraq regularly and international travel on occasion. Must have a passport and/or residency permit that allows for travel throughout (federal) Iraq and KRI.

**WORKING HOURS**

The Country Director position is a full-time role, estimated at 40 hours per week. Due to the nature of the organization’s business, hours may fluctuate outside regular core hours (Sunday–Thursday; 9AM-5PM), with the possibility of some nights or weekends, depending on the needs of the organization.

**COMPENSATION**

Based on experience. Aligned with market rate for a Country Director in Iraq. (Free to Run uses MSF Salary Survey as one of a handful of benchmarks for salary calculations in Iraq).

**EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES**

Below is what we are looking for as we evaluate applications. Candidates *don’t need to have all these experiences* *and competencies* but should be able to display strengths across multiple areas.

Free to Run seeks an experienced, values-driven leader with a demonstrated ability to mobilize resources, build strategic partnerships, and lead high-performing teams. The successful candidate will combine strong knowledge of Iraq's civil society and development landscape with a commitment to feminist leadership, human rights, and locally-led development. We recognize that strong leaders bring diverse professional and educational experiences.

**Education and Language:**

- Bachelor's degree in international development, human rights, women’s/gender studies, public health or MHPSS, nonprofit management, business administration, or a related field required. An advanced degree is preferred; equivalent relevant professional experience may be considered.
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English is required.
- Professional fluency in Kurdish (Sorani or Kurmanji/Badini) or Arabic required; proficiency in both is strongly preferred.

**Professional Experience:**

- Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in international development, humanitarian assistance, human rights, civil society, or related sectors, including at least three years in a senior management or leadership role.
- Demonstrated track record of successful fundraising and resource mobilization in Iraq and/or the wider Middle East region, including personally cultivating donor relationships, securing institutional or private funding, and developing successful funding proposals or partnerships.
- Established relationships with, and strong understanding of, the regional donor landscape, including bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, international NGOs, and private-sector funding partners.
- Proven experience leading, managing, and developing diverse teams, including responsibility for staff performance, professional development, organizational culture, and effective team collaboration.
- Experience managing organizational budgets, operational systems, and financial accountability, including compliance with donor requirements and applicable national regulations.
- Deep understanding of Iraq's political, social, cultural, and operating environment, including the Kurdistan Region, and demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder relationships.
- Experience engaging with government authorities, civil society organizations, institutional donors, and community-based partners.
- Experience working in women's rights, gender equity, youth leadership, refugee and displacement, or community-based development programming strongly preferred.
- Experience managing institutional grants and working within international NGO accountability, safeguarding, and compliance frameworks preferred.
- Experience working in collaboration with a global headquarters and other country-teams strongly preferred

**Skills, Leadership Approach and Competencies:**

Feminist and Rights-Based Leadership

- Demonstrated commitment to feminist principles, gender equality, and human rights, with the ability to translate these values into everyday leadership, management practices, and organizational decision-making.
- Proven ability to lead through an empowering, inclusive, and participatory management approach that shares power appropriately, encourages staff agency and ownership, values diverse perspectives, and creates opportunities for individual and collective leadership.
- Ability to foster a respectful, psychologically safe, and accountable working environment in which team members feel empowered to raise concerns, challenge ideas constructively, and contribute meaningfully to decisions.
- Strong understanding of power dynamics, discrimination, and structural inequalities, with the ability to apply intersectional and culturally responsive approaches to staff management, partnerships, and programming.
- Commitment to safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), non-discrimination, and the dignity and rights of staff, participants, and communities.

Fundraising and External Relations

- Excellent relationship-building, networking, and negotiation skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage senior government officials, institutional donors, private-sector partners, and civil society leaders.
- Strong fundraising and business development capabilities, including donor cultivation, strategic positioning, proposal development, and negotiation of funding partnerships.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including persuasive writing, public speaking, and the ability to represent Free to Run effectively with diverse audiences.
- Ability to identify and pursue strategic opportunities that strengthen Free to Run's financial sustainability, institutional credibility, and influence.

Strategic and Operational Leadership

- Strong strategic thinking and planning skills, with the ability to translate organizational priorities into achievable country-level objectives, operational plans, and measurable results.
- Demonstrated ability to balance strategic leadership with sound financial management, operational oversight, and organizational accountability.
- Strong judgment, integrity, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to make sound decisions in complex, politically sensitive, and rapidly changing environments.
- Ability to lead organizational change constructively, foster innovation, and build a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Strong cross-cultural communication, emotional intelligence, and conflict-resolution skills, including the ability to provide constructive feedback, address performance challenges fairly, and navigate difficult conversations with professionalism.
- Ability to collaborate effectively within a globally distributed organization, maintaining clear communication, mutual accountability, and alignment between country-level and global teams.
- Proficiency with standard digital collaboration, communication, and financial management tools, including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.

**PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES**

The successful candidate will demonstrate integrity, humility, resilience, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to Free to Run's mission. They will be a confident external representative and an empowering internal leader who understands that effective leadership is measured not only by organizational results, but also by the capacity, confidence, and agency developed in others.

*Free to Run is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don’t just accept differences — we celebrate, support and thrive on them for the benefit of our team, our programs, and our organizational strength. We are proud to be an affirmative action employer, committed to diversity, equity and inclusion of ALL people in our hiring and employment practices. We encourage applications from people who have non-dominant identities based on race, ethnicity, migration status, ability, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, etc.*

title: Technical Officer – Ocean Observations
body:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** will provide technical hands-on support for SPC’s regional ocean observation and monitoring activities, with a primary focus on wave monitoring systems. The role operates within SPC’s technical workshop capability, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and operational sustainability of wave buoys, while contributing to other in situ ocean observing systems (e.g. ADCPs, water-quality sensors, and multi-sensor platforms) across SPC member countries, including applications relevant to fisheries, maritime, and ocean and climate services.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Wave and Ocean Monitoring System – Deployment and Field Operations**

- Plan, coordinate, and participate in deployment, recovery, and redeployment of wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing instruments, in collaboration with SPC teams and national counterparts, including participation in diving operations where required.
- Undertake or contribute to site assessments, mooring design and deployment planning ensuring alignment with local environmental conditions and operational requirements.
- Lead or support offshore and coastal field operations, ensuring compliance with SPC safety and operational procedures, and alignment with mission objectives.
- Prepare mission plans, risk assessments, and field operation reports, documenting technical outcomes, issues encountered, and lessons learned.

**Maintenance, Troubleshooting and Technical Support**

- Provide technical maintenance and troubleshooting support for wave buoys and other in‑situ ocean observing systems, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and moorings, in collaboration with national counterparts, SPC teams and service providers.
- Plan and coordinate preventative and corrective maintenance activities, to ensure operational availability and longevity of observing systems.
- Diagnose technical faults, recommend corrective actions, and support their implementation by relevant SPC teams, service providers, or national partners.
- Maintain accurate maintenance logs, calibration records, and technical documentation to support asset tracking, audits, and knowledge transfer.

**Data Quality Assurance, Data Management Procedures & SOP Development**

- Support the application of agreed data management and data quality assurance procedures for wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing systems, in line with SPC and country arrangements.
- Support the timely and reliable ingestion of observation data from SPC‑supported systems into SPC and agreed national data management platforms.
- Work with national counterparts to support the sharing and integration of country‑owned observation data in accordance with agreed processes and data governance arrangements.
- Contribute to the development, maintenance, and application of standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering deployment, maintenance, data handling, and incident response.

**Procurement and Asset Management**

- Provide technical input to procurement processes for ocean observing equipment and services, including preparation of technical specifications, participation in evaluations, and engagement with suppliers, in line with SPC policies and procedures.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of ocean observing assets, including inventories, warranties, servicing requirements, and lifecycle status, to support effective planning, maintenance, and sustainability of observing systems.
- Coordinate logistics for ocean observing equipment, including shipping, customs clearance, insurance, and freight documentation, in collaboration with SPC logistics, procurement, and finance teams.
- Ensure asset and logistics documentation is complete, current, and accessible to support audits, reporting, and effective handover between staff and teams.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Degree in electronics, electrical engineering, marine science or technology, ocean instrumentation, or a closely related technical discipline or an equivalent body of knowledge and experience.
- Open Water Diving certification or equivalent occupational diving certification, and fitness to undertake work‑related diving activities.

**Technical expertise**

- Minimum 4-5 years’ progressive technical experience in marine, oceanographic, environmental monitoring, or related operational fieldwork.
- Demonstrated experience in the deployment, recovery, commissioning, testing, and validation of in situ observation systems, such as wave buoys, moorings, current meters (e.g. ADCPs), or multi‑sensor platforms.
- Practical experience maintaining and troubleshooting marine instrumentation, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and associated electronics.
- Experience supporting or applying preventative and corrective maintenance practices, including record‑keeping and technical documentation.
- Understanding of marine field operations, including site selection, environmental conditions, operational risks, and safety requirements.
- Experience delivering hands‑on technical training or mentoring to adult learners or technical counterparts.
- Proven ability to work effectively with government agencies, technical services, and regional partners.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **Until 30 June 2028** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** is a band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,146‒2,683 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 6,632–8,290 (USD 2,876–3,595; EUR 2,595–3,244). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

title: Team Leader, Syria Education Programme III (SEP III)
body:
**SYRIA EDUCATION PROGRAMME III (SEP III)**

Building on SEP I (2018–2022) and SEP II (2022–2027), which supported primary educatio in Idleb and Aleppo, FCDO plans to procure a new Technical Assistance (TA) contract, SEP III, to support the Syrian Ministry of Education (MoE) in implementing its nationally-led reform agenda, complementing the Ministry's wider reform programme, including support provided through the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Since December 2024, the MoE has begun to reunify a fragmented education system, but progress has been constrained by limited institutional capacity, a lack of data, weak policy development processes and the absence of a clear long-term strategy for recovery. Unlike earlier phases, which focused primarily on service delivery in northwest Syria, SEP III will work directly with the MoE and local Education Directorates, generally at national level and directorate level, in partnership with Ministry officials, to help the Ministry translate its policy and process reforms into practice through technical advice, capacity building, coaching and support to implementation.

SEP III has two components. The first, which is the subject of this contract, is politically informed TA to the MoE and Education Directorates to strengthen inclusive, effective and evidence-based policy making. The second is non-formal education (NFE) for returning refugees and internally displaced persons, which is outside the scope of this contract and will be delivered by a separate provider. The TA supplier will be required to work collaboratively with the NFE component.

The exact scope of the TA work will be determined jointly with FCDO and the MoE through a demand-led, co-designed and flexible approach. No reform priorities are set in advance; they will be identified with the Ministry during inception. The work is expected to focus on strengthening the education system to improve foundational learning outcomes for primary-school-aged children across Syria, delivered through: 1) Services and Analysis to inform TA and policy decisions; 2) Foundational Learning thematic TA (for example teacher development, coaching and supervision, safeguarding, learning data generation and use, and inclusive education); and 3) Education Systems Strengthening TA (sector planning and prioritisation, policy development, financial management, and monitoring and accountability). Given the difficult fiscal choices likely to shape the sector over the coming years, the programme is also expected to support the Ministry's public finance and value-for-money decision-making. Illustrative technical priorities include: supporting policy reform and Ministry-led coordination, standard-setting, and system strengthening; supporting the roll-out of child safeguarding and Codes of Conduct; improving the quality and consistency of teaching through professional development and a national Teacher Competency Framework; and data-driven planning, including through education management information systems (EMIS/SIMIS).

Given the fluid transition context, the programme will need to operate flexibly, respond quickly to changes, and seize windows of opportunity for reform as they arise. FCDO expects a politically informed, 'test, learn, adapt' approach rather than a fixed blueprint. Delivery must be aligned with government systems, avoiding parallel platforms and the substitution of government functions, and must be underpinned by gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and conflict sensitivity. This requires strong political judgement, including a clear understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, an in-depth understanding of the Syrian education system and its institutional actors, and the ability to sustain trusted relationships with the Ministry, FCDO, and other sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), and the World Bank.

The anticipated delivery model comprises i) a **Core Delivery Team** responsible for overall leadership, technical oversight, coordination, MEAL, governance and quality assurance, which should be predominantly Syrian and mostly based in Syria; and ii) a **demand-led TA Pool** of experts with education and governance backgrounds. The contract is expected to begin on 1 July 2027 with a six-month inception period, during which the supplier must mobilise rapidly, establish a presence in Damascus and operationalise its delivery systems. Details are indicative and will be confirmed in FCDO's Tender Notice.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Team Leader holds overall accountability for the design, rapid mobilisation, and delivery of SEP III, including leading the Core Delivery Team and overseeing the TA Pool, ensuring the programme is implemented in accordance with the contract, FCDO requirements, IRC policies and principles, and internationally recognised quality of assistance standards. The Team Leader is the primary point of contact with FCDO and, working closely with the ESS Technical Director and senior Ministry counterparts, provides strategic direction to support the Ministry's implementation of its reform priorities.

The Team Leader is responsible for the programme's overall management, including budget oversight and value for money, performance against contractual KPIs, and risk management (including fiduciary and reputational risk in a sensitive political environment), with the technical quality of the programme's workstreams assured by the ESS Technical Director. The postholder ensures the programme operates adaptively — using political analysis, evidence, monitoring data, and regular review points to prioritise, test, learn and adapt in response to a fast-moving political and institutional context — while maintaining the flexibility needed to respond to emerging windows of opportunity for reform.

The Team Leader maintains strong working relationships with the implementing team, consortium/delivery partners (if applicable), the MoE and Education Directorates, FCDO, the provider of the NFE component, and other education sector stakeholders, and represents the programme and IRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups, and policy dialogues. The postholder also oversees programme staffing, procurement, and administrative functions, and ensures robust communications and knowledge management, both internally and with external stakeholders, to share progress, evidence, and lessons learned.

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership**

● Provide overall strategic leadership for SEP III, ensuring the programme's support to the MoE and Education Directorates, led technically by the ESS Technical Director, is relevant to, and aligned with, the Ministry's evolving reform priorities and helps translate these priorities into practice.

● Lead the six-month inception period (July –December 2027), including establishing the Damascus presence, mobilising the Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, operationalising delivery systems, formalising ways of working with the MoE, developing the screening and prioritisation framework and Tasking Order criteria, and delivering inception milestones to FCDO's standard and timetable.

● Provide strategic oversight of the ESS Technical Director's technical leadership, ensuring the programme's technical direction remains aligned with strategic priorities and senior-level MoE relations.

● Ensure the programme operates flexibly and applies a 'test, learn, adapt' approach: agreeing clear reform objectives and decision criteria with the Ministry, co-designing and trialling options, using evidence and learning to decide whether to continue, scale, adapt, pause or pivot workstreams, and documenting adaptation decisions.

● Think and work politically, with a strong understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, drawing on strong contextual and institutional analysis to ensure these opportunities are identified early and acted upon in a timely way.

● Take explicit responsibility for reform sequencing, political economy analysis, and navigating institutional constraints, ensuring a regularly updated PEA and periodic political reviews inform programme design, prioritisation and delivery, and that support is prioritised and paced in line with the Ministry's capacity and the political space available for reform.

● Ensure delivery remains aligned with government systems, avoids parallel platforms and substituting for government functions, and is designed for sustainability and capacity transfer, while supporting coalitions of reform-minded actors within and beyond government.

● Champion evidence-based, gender-responsive, and inclusive approaches throughout programme design and delivery, including dedicated attention to the needs of girls and children with disabilities, and ensure conflict sensitivity is embedded throughout.

● Provide leadership on GEDSI, ensuring diversity and inclusion are reflected in team and partner selection, programme design and implementation, and programme reporting.

**Donor, Government and Stakeholder Relations**

● Serve as the primary point of contact and representational link with FCDO, ensuring high-quality, timely reporting through formal and informal debriefings, and annual and semi-annual reports.

● Build and maintain a trusted, politically informed working relationship with senior officials in the MoE and other relevant government counterparts, supporting the Ministry's stewardship of the education sector and complementing the ESS Technical Director's ongoing technical-level engagement with MoE and Education Directorate representatives at all levels to identify technical assistance needs and design and implement ESS interventions.

● Coordinate with sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, ECW, the World Bank, and other donors and implementing partners, to support coordinated reform efforts across government and development partners, and to ensure the programme complements ongoing initiatives and other TA investments and adheres to national and global standards.

● Ensure close coherence and collaboration with the provider of the separate NFE component of SEP III, including joint planning, information sharing and coordination of engagement with the Ministry.

● Represent the programme and IRC at national and international forums, including technical conferences and policy dialogues, sharing programme achievements and lessons learned.

● Champion accountability to affected populations, partners, and diverse stakeholders, ensuring that feedback and complaints mechanisms, transparent communication, and participatory approaches inform programme design, delivery, and adaptive management.

**Programme, Risk and Financial Management**

● Oversee overall programme and budget management, ensuring value for money across all components, informed by a sound understanding of the Ministry's public finance context, and robust compliance with FCDO and IRC financial and procurement requirements.

● Oversee the Tasking Order mechanism for the TA Pool, ensuring requests are screened and prioritised against agreed criteria, co-created with the Ministry and Education Directorates, approved by FCDO, costed transparently against the agreed rate card with clear milestones, and delivered to a high-quality standard.

● Lead on identification and management of programme risks, including fiduciary, safeguarding, political, and reputational risks associated with operating within Syrian government structures during a period of political transition.

● Develop, review, and monitor, in coordination with key programme staff, the annual work plan (updated quarterly) and performance plans, and ensure quarterly and annual reports are submitted in the agreed format and to the required standard, so that long-term and short-term priorities remain on track.
