**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2150 gross per month (2150 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

- The Grants Manager is living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs.
- Individual room, with electricity 24/7.
- Internet and Phone network available
- Restaurants and international food are available

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates  
There is one driver available on evenings for movements out of office hours, 2 drivers during weekends daytime.  
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).  
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are not permitted.

title: DMEAL Adviser - Pacific
body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **DMEAL Adviser - Pacific**, you will provide strategic and technical DMEAL support, capacity strengthening, and advisory services to World Vision’s four Pacific Field Offices within the SAPO region, promoting quality DMEAL practices, evidence use, and learning. You will provide technical leadership for grant DMEAL across SAPO, including non-Pacific Field Offices, through the DMEAL for Grants Community of Practice (CoP), strengthening grant DMEAL quality, capacity, and cross-country learning while developing evidence and impact briefs. You will also provide matrix supervision and technical guidance to the DMEAL leads in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands, as agreed with the respective Field Offices, and report to the Regional Evidence and Impact Senior Adviser.

**Technical Assistance**

You will support Pacific National Offices in applying DMEAL and programme quality standards, guidelines, tools, and methodologies, including reviewing programme designs, baselines, evaluations, Annual Impact Measurement (AIM), and programme reports. You will provide technical guidance on iMPAQ, monitoring and MEAL systems, data quality, analysis, reporting, and evidence-based decision-making. You will also help communicate programme impact for income and influence goals and promote knowledge sharing and lessons learned to improve programme and organizational performance.

**Capacity Building**

You will assess DMEAL staff competencies, processes, structures, and approaches, identify gaps, and develop capacity-building interventions for National Offices and partners. You will facilitate workshops, peer learning, and individual support, lead regional MEAL capacity-strengthening initiatives, support the regional M&E Community of Practice, and strengthen Field Office teams’ use of monitoring data and evidence for programme quality, adaptive management, learning, and reporting.

**Strategic Management Support**

You will support the development and refresh of Pacific Field Office strategies, ensuring DMEAL and programme quality priorities are integrated. You will support Partnership and DMEAL initiatives, strengthen collaboration with donors and Support Offices, contribute to organizational programme quality strategies and standards, lead the regional AIM process and support quality Annual Child Results Reports. You will also provide technical support to relevant Pacific Field Offices in developing and implementing Integrated Programme Frameworks (IPFs), including in Solomon Islands.

**M&E Leadership**

You will develop professional networks and partnerships with universities, private-sector organizations, donors, and non-profit entities, contribute to organizational M&E discussions and guideline development, and coordinate with Support Offices and major donors to align monitoring and evaluation requirements. You will also collaborate with the Regional Grant Acquisition team to provide DMEAL and programme quality inputs and support, including participation in grant Go/No-Go decision-making.

**Requirements include:**

- Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation at a national level (or large program level).
- Proven ability to facilitate working groups, communities of practice or other similar learning mechanisms
- Proven ability to collaborate with all levels of staff and to motivate and mobilize individuals outside their reporting line to achieve agreed strategic plans.
- Knowledge of the monitoring and evaluation requirements of one or more institutional donors (USAID, DFAT, DevCo, etc.)
- Bachelor’s degree and post-graduate certification or master’s degree in the social, statistic or related field.
- Qualitative and/or quantitative research and evaluation skills, including but not limited to study design, survey instrument design and use, establishing and measuring outcome and process indicators, sampling, data analysis plans, data cleaning, and statistical analysis.
- Demonstrated ability to report, present and communicate results, written and verbal in modern standard English.
- Master’s degree in social sciences, statistics or related field.
- Evidence of the ability to facilitate M&E capacity building approaches (workshop facilitation, 1:1 coaching, etc.)
- Business process improvement (Lean Six Sigma)
- Experience in working in pacific countries

title: NIGERIA - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIP HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - ABUDJA
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: ABUJA**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

**Solidarites International** launched its operation in Nigeria in 2016 as a consequence of the humanitarian needs of displaced populations and host communities caused by the current crisis with conflict and the ongoing violence in the North-East of Nigeria led by Armed Opposition Groups since 2009. The security situation and epidemics/outbreaks continue to affect millions of lives in Northeastern and North Western parts of Nigeria. As of June 2022, according to IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, an estimated 2.2 million people are displaced within Borno State which remains, for a major part, inaccessible to humanitarian actors.

The targeted sectors of intervention are WASH, Shelter, RRM, Food Security & Livelihoods. The annual budget of the mission is around 8.3 million euros in 2022.

The mission is organized with a coordination office in Maiduguri and 3 bases located in Ngala, Dikwa and Monguno managed remotely from Maiduguri for the North-East. In the North-West, Solidarites International is conducting activities on 3 bases located in Gusau, Anka and Taleta in Zamfara State. Abuja is the representative for the mission Nigeria.

Mission staff : 165  
The Grants and Partnership HOD will directly manage the Grants coordination team composed of :   
\- A Reporting & Communications Officer   
She/he will closely work with all Departmental Heads, Field Coordinators and Project Managers of the mission.   
The Grants and Partnership HOD will report to the Country Director and be in link with Grants & Partnership department in HQ.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Head of Grants and Partnerships Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. They supervise, adapt and optimise working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.   
They validate contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.   
They play a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). Ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- Access challenges and remote management due to security contraints in some areas of intervention  
\- Strategic positionning in a global trend of funding decrease   
\- Focus on partnership and localization in all areas of intervention. This requires adapted operational modalities and a support to local partners.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\*Support the programmatic strategy (2027-2032) and PROG 2027 implementation  
\*Monitoring of partnerships and capacity building plan in coordination with other Department (Programs, E & C, etc.)  
\*Follow up on the advancement of the financing contracts   
\*Finalize partnership management/localization strategy  
\*Coordinate proposals   
\*Continue developing relationship with donor representatives and engage internally/ externally with different interlocutors to identify new funding opportunities

**Security constraints:**

No walking policy everywhere in the country / Security situation calm in Abuja, level 2 (out of 5), Maiduguri is level 3 and level 4 in other bases/sub-bases.

## Your profile

**Diploma and Experience :**

Diploma : Bachelor or masters in a related degree: humanitarian response, international cooperation

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on similar positions : 3/4 years

**SKILLS :**

**Technical skills**

1. Excellent reporting, writing and proof reading skills
2. Strong knowledge of main donors (ECHO, French donors, SIDA etc) and their respective policies / guidelines
3. Previous experience and achievements in developing strategic partnerships with other NGOs (MoUs, negotiations, governance, capacity building ...)
4. Proven ability to deal with donors and operational partners

**Transversal skills**

1. Critical thinking skills and the ability to adapt to fast-paced environments, while working independently to meet tight deadlines with minimal supervision
2. Good knowledge of the humanitarian project cycle management;
3. Excellent communication, networking skills, organizational and prioritization skills, ability to multi-task, Capacity to adapt and show organizational flexibilit
4. External representation

**Languages :**

1. English (fluent - Mandatory)
2. French (an asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grant & Partnership HOD will be based in Abuja with frequent field visit expected in the regional offices (Maiduguri. Birnin Kebbi and potentially Gusau or Sokoto).   
In Abuja, living condition are good and all commodities and goods (local or imported) can be found (supermarket, restautant, cinema, sport centers ...). Abuja GH is Comfortable with private bedroom and bathroom, 24/7 electricity and internet. GH is located in the same estate as the office, avoiding taking the car every morning but still clearly separated from working area (not the same building). Estate where GH/Office is located is providing Gym room, Swimming pool and squash court.  
At base level, (Maiduguri, Birnin Kebbi and Gusau), the bases offers a comfortable environment, in spite of limited movements outside of the compound for security reasons. The Guest House offers good living conditions, with private bedroom and bathroom and shared & comfortable common spaces. Electricity and internet are available at the office and at the GH at all times. Ping pong, pool table and some gym equipment are available in the GH in Maiduguri. All essential good (food, hygiene etc..) can be bought locally in the small shops around the office, or in the pre-validated supermarket. Visits to other NGOs are possible, as well as some pre-validated places (hotel and restaurants).  
Occasional field visit in NE sub bases, to ensure a correct program overview depedning on the security context and validation. No Overnight are possible in NE sub bases, only daily round trip with UNHAS are possible.

title: Global Surge Team Roster: Emergency Grants Coordinator
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**IRC Global Surge Team:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, helping people survive, recover, and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC delivers life‑saving assistance and long‑term recovery services to people affected by conflict and disaster. Today, the IRC works in over 30 countries and 22 U.S. cities, restoring safety, dignity, and hope to millions worldwide.

The IRC’s Global Surge Team (GST) is a roster of highly qualified humanitarian professionals who deploy on short notice to emergency and non‑emergency contexts to support the IRC’s mission. GST members provide specialized, time‑bound support where capacity gaps exist, typically for deployments of up to three months.

**The GST is a flexible, occasional employment opportunity. Deployment needs vary based on demand. Staff can take on additional deployments as opportunities arise and if they are interested.** Deployment opportunities depend on organizational and operational requirements and may vary over time; as such, deployments cannot be guaranteed. Staff supporting emergency responses must be prepared to deploy within 72 hours as needs arise.

**French speaking candidates are currently being prioritized.**

**Job Summary:**

The **Emergency Grants Coordinator, Global Surge** plays a critical role in supporting emergency humanitarian responses by leading grant management, donor compliance, proposal development, and reporting functions in rapidly evolving crisis settings. As part of surge deployments, this position ensures the timely mobilization and stewardship of donor funding through the development of high-quality proposals, robust monitoring and reporting systems, and effective coordination with program teams, partners, donors, and headquarters. The role provides strategic guidance on donor regulations and compliance requirements, strengthens grants management capacity through staff training and mentorship, and supports strong information management practices to ensure accountability, program quality, and operational effectiveness. Working in complex emergency environments, the Emergency Grants Coordinator helps secure and manage resources that enable the delivery of impactful humanitarian assistance to affected populations.

**Responsibilities:**

- Ensure high quality and timely submission of funding proposals through development of timelines, coordinating technical and financial input, writing overviews, editing and formatting proposal documents, and liaison with HQ on approval and submission processes.
- Work with program and management staff to promote and ensure development of strong data collection andmonitoring & evaluation process, detailed collection and analysis of program data.
- Hire and train in-county grants staff as the need arises to efficiently support the scale and scope of the program
- Establish and ensure maintenance of comprehensive grant files and related information management processes including issuing reporting formats and schedules, maintaining donor and external contact information/files and protocols and establishing a photo library.
- Participate in and/or lead grant opening and review meetings; ensuring all required information is circulated in advance, meetings are fully documented and action items completed.
- Provide advice on donor grant compliance issues, visibility and reporting requirements; proactively engaging with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility
- Coordinate partner subgrant processes including preaward assessments, subgrant development, HQ review and approval processes, related partner reporting and compliance training to promote an encouraging and constructive relationship and effective oversight of subgrant activities and results.
- Prepare high quality and timely donor and management reports on grants and sector activities in close collaboration with program staff.
- Represent IRC and coordinate with other agencies, local government, donors and other partners to promote deliver of best practice humanitarian assistance and coordination of efforts.
- Support media and communications activities as requested by the emergency response team.
- Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program monitoring data and staff performance information.

**Requirements:**

- Significant experience in grants management, humanitarian program management, or a related field, including work in emergency and conflict-affected settings.
- Strong knowledge of major humanitarian donor regulations and compliance requirements, including UN agencies, USAID/BHA, ECHO/EC, and FCDO (formerly DFID).
- Proven experience coordinating donor proposals, grant management processes, reporting, and compliance across multiple stakeholders.
- Excellent English writing, editing, and communication skills; additional language skills are an asset (French fluency required).
- Strong understanding of monitoring, evaluation, and data management systems, with experience supporting program quality and accountability.
- Experience developing project budgets and working closely with finance teams on donor financial requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to build partnerships, facilitate collaboration across departments, and provide training and guidance on grants management and donor compliance.
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines in fast-paced environments.
- Ability to work independently, adapt quickly to changing circumstances, and perform effectively in high-pressure emergency response contexts.
- Willingness and ability to deploy internationally on short notice to support humanitarian emergencies.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Tax Site Coordinator
Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor
body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Background/IRC Summary:**  Each year the IRC in New York provides support to more than 1500 refugee, asylee and other humanitarian entrants seeking to start new lives in the New York City area. The IRC in New York aims to help these clients achieve self-sufficiency and adapt to and become engaged citizens of their new communities. The Education & Learning unit strives to serve the entire family unit, and the need all family members have for access to relevant educational opportunities in order to thrive in the U.S.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor coordinates educational programming for newcomer youth, including planning, implementation, and reporting for 2-4 Youth Education Programs, including but not limited to World Explorers, Youth ESOL, Mini-NYSA, and Tutoring. The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor collaborates closely with the other supervisors and Youth Education Manager to ensure all programs integrate best practices for teaching and tutoring English Language Learners and students with interrupted education, as well as social-emotional learning principles, and to ensure that IRC NY’s Youth Education goals and objectives are accomplished using a holistic, collaborative approach, in partnership with school staff, caregivers, and newcomer youth themselves.

In addition, the Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor will steward relevant partnerships for the Youth Education Department as needed to ensure program implementation. This will include coordinating with community-based organizations for collaboration and locations.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Oversee 2-4 youth programs including but not limited to Work Explorers, Youth ESOL, and other programs as needed.
- Develop logical framework and program design in alignment with IRC Outcomes and Evidence Framework for all programming in consultation with the M&E specialist
- Oversee recruitment of all staff, interns, and volunteers needed for programs
- Manage 2-3 Youth Education Coordinators and Specialists responsible for program implementation
- Ensure all programming follows all IRC policies and procedures, particularly concerning child safeguarding
- Design and implement opportunities for parent/caregiver engagement
- Oversee planning of all programs, including but not limited to space allocation and field trips.
- Manage participant recruitment, retention, attendance, and family engagement
- Oversee Monitoring and evaluation for all programs
- Manage program files and databases (enrollment, attendance, outcomes monitoring); maintain accurate and complete records according to IRC and funder policies
- Implement all programs in accordance with the IRC Multi-Tiered Systems of Support
- Serve as a school leader for the Newcomer Youth Summer Academy, responsible for planning, staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Supervise program Academic Lead Teachers, Classroom Culture Lead Teachers, SEL Teacher and Physical Education Teacher
- Oversee teachers to coordinate, plan and develop a 6 week culturally responsive and age-appropriate curriculum, lesson plans and assessment tools using student centered teaching methodologies for English Language Learners
- Ensure effective implementation of IRC’s Multi-tiered System of Support
- Design progress report and report card templates and coordinate related systems of data collection and dissemination
- Plan and coordinate caregiver and teacher conferences
- Conduct teacher observations and coaching using the IRC Framework for Effective Teaching
- Co-lead and plan weekly community events and student award ceremonies in collaboration with other Deans
- Provide technical assistance to internal IRC programs (such as mini academies, School Success Coaching) as well as to external subgrantee organizations
- Deliver workshops on supporting refugee and immigrant students to NYC schools and other community based organizations
- Coordinate with community based organizations as needed for program implementation with consultation with the Youth Education Manager
- Maintain existing partnerships as well as seek out new partnerships that align with Youth Education Department goals
- Prepare internal and external reports for programs supervised
- Ensure program data is consistently collected and entered in relevant databases
- Other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

- Master’s degree in education or related field required
- Must be available on Saturdays as needed to oversee youth programs
- A minimum of 2 years’ professional experience working with children and youth, specifically in the context of educational and social programs, required. Teaching certification and experience in the NYC public school system desirable.
- Experience as Head of Teaching, Instructional Coach, or School Leader, highly desirable
- Responsive Classrooms and/or Restorative Justice trained, highly desirable
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Proven success planning and delivering creative and engaging curricula for beginner to intermediate ELLs
- Cultural competency training experience, desirable
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives
- Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
- Fluent in MS Office applications, especially MS Excel
- Organized, responsible, and flexible: able to maintain responsibility for multiple tasks in the context of a diverse, fast-paced work environment and maintain composure under pressure
- Fluency in a second language highly desired (such as: Spanish, Dari, Pashto, Arabic, French, Haitian-Creole)

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, with the potential for remote work on a limited basis.
- Occasional weekend and/or evening work required.
- Staff are required to adhere to IRC’s COVID risk mitigation policies, which may include masking, physical distancing, enhanced hygiene practices, symptom screening, and isolation and quarantine when needed. IRC policies may be stricter than federal, state, or local level policies.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $72,700/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement
body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to humanitarian crises in over 40 countries and in communities across the United States and Europe, helping people whose lives have been shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures.

Global Procurement, within the Global Supply Chain function, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for the organization. As IRC continues to test and adopt new technology to support its mission, Global Procurement is establishing a dedicated Procurement Manager role to provide procurement capacity for emerging technology and digital innovation.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement supports fast-moving technology sourcing needs across IRC, with a focus on early-stage digital innovation, pilots, proofs of concept, trials, and emerging tools. The role helps teams test and evaluate new technology quickly while maintaining procurement discipline, vendor due diligence, risk review, documentation, and compliance.

For this role, “digital innovation” refers to early-stage, small-scale, fast-moving technology initiatives where IRC teams are testing a new idea, tool, platform, vendor, or digital approach before deciding whether to scale. The portfolio covers AI and generative AI tools where applicable, SaaS and digital platforms, automation, data and analytics, migration and testing tools, cybersecurity tools, collaboration platforms, digital service delivery tools, field and mobile technology, low-code and no-code platforms, and other emerging digital solutions.

This role is an execution-focused, hands-on individual contributor role. It enables IRC to move quickly on emerging technology and digital innovation requests without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as the day-to-day procurement focal point for these requests

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Sourcing Execution**

- Provide hands-on sourcing support for pilots, trials, proofs of concept, small-scale SaaS, emerging vendors, startup-style tools, and digital innovation requests across IRC.
- Execute sourcing activities in line with the IT category strategy and under the guidance of the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Conduct early market scans and market intelligence for emerging tools, vendors, pricing models, and digital innovation categories.
- Support requirements gathering, supplier identification, RFI/RFQ/RFP preparation, evaluation support, award recommendation, and contract finalization.
- Build supplier visibility for innovation and emerging technology vendors, including startup and niche providers that may later become larger enterprise solutions.
- Help bring new tools into proper procurement channels, reducing shadow IT, credit-card purchasing, and unmanaged technology spend.
- Support SaaS rationalization, renewal planning, demand management, and license optimization at the innovation and pilot tier.
- Help business teams translate technical needs into clear scopes of work, evaluation criteria, and vendor questions.

**B. Pilot, Trial, and Proof-of-Concept Procurement Frameworks**

- Build and maintain a lightweight, repeatable procurement pathway for pilots, trials, and proofs of concept.
- Develop checklists, decision tools, and methodology for short-term technology engagements.
- Define the minimum documentation required before a pilot, trial, or proof of concept can begin.
- Maintain clear approval checkpoints and escalation criteria so teams understand when a pilot can proceed and when it requires further review.
- Track emerging technology requests from intake through pilot, decision, and possible scale-up.
- Ensure required reviews and approvals are completed and all necessary checks are documented before tools are tested or used.
- Help document whether a pilot should end, continue, scale, or move into a formal sourcing process.
- Coordinate NDAs and pre-procurement documentation when teams need to test or evaluate multiple tools before selecting a vendor.
- Ensure pilots and trials are set up in a way that allows long-term success if IRC later moves to a larger phase or formal sourcing process.

**C. AI-Enabled and High-Risk Technology Procurement Support**

- Support sourcing for AI-enabled tools as part of the broader emerging technology portfolio, applied only when AI functionality is in scope.
- For AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC’s AI assessment requirements, including use-case risk classification, provider/deployer determination, GenAI tool checks, and required approvals.
- Coordinate with the AI Governance and Risk Committee and AI Department Focal Points when applicable.
- Identify and escalate sourcing requests that may involve high-risk technology, AI functionality, personal information, confidential data, client-facing tools, cybersecurity concerns, or unapproved tools.
- Support procurement documentation for AI-enabled tools, including evidence of approvals, vendor assessments, risk reviews, and contract requirements.

**D. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate required vendor risk assessments (VRA) and due diligence across cybersecurity, privacy and data protection, legal, donor compliance, sanctions and ATC screening, financial viability, implementation risk, integration risk, operational support model, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Coordinate with Information Security, Data Protection, Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance to ensure required reviews are completed before pilots, trials, awards, or contract signature.
- Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements that may affect technology, AI, data hosting, data residency, and vendor selection.
- Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.

**E. Tool and Vendor Visibility**

- Maintain or support a list of emerging technology tools and vendors, indicating status (under review, in pilot, approved, rejected, expired) and the approved use case for each tool.
- Document the business owner, contract status, contract dates, and renewal timing for each tool.
- Document what each tool is approved for and what use would require additional approval or new procurement action.
- Help connect business owners, end users, IT, Procurement, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance around emerging technology tools and vendors.
- Reduce situations where approved tools are used in non-approved ways, and flag misuse for review.

**F. Contracting and Commercial Support**

- Support commercial negotiation and contracting across the emerging technology portfolio, including NDAs, trial agreements, pilot agreements, proof-of-concept agreements, SaaS agreements, subscriptions, software licenses, cloud services, implementation services, and renewals.
- Review pricing models, including seat-based licensing, usage-based pricing, token usage, API calls, implementation fees, renewal escalators, and support fees, and provide commercial analysis.
- Coordinate with Legal, IT, Finance, and business owners to ensure contracts include appropriate terms on data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, incident reporting, termination, data return, and exit provisions.
- For AI-enabled tools, ensure contracts also address AI-generated outputs, model training restrictions, and AI-specific risk allocation.
- Support renewal planning and help prevent last-minute renewals or unplanned vendor commitments.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented procurement support to teams exploring new tools, pilots, digital services, automation platforms, AI solutions, or other emerging technology.
- Help stakeholders move through the procurement process without unnecessary delays, while maintaining compliance and risk controls.
- Coordinate between business owners, IT owners, Procurement, end users, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance to ensure tool usage remains aligned with approved scope, contract terms, procurement files, risk approvals, and any applicable usage guidelines.
- Reduce workarounds, shadow IT, and credit-card purchasing by making the correct procurement process easier to follow.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines for emerging technology procurement.
- Support early engagement with teams considering new tools, pilots, or digital approaches, before commitments are made to vendors.

**H. Reporting and Continuous Improvement**

- Track the emerging technology sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar, cycle time, savings, risk flags, documentation completion, and approval status.
- Track pilot outcomes (end, continue, scale, or formal sourcing) and capture lessons learned.
- Track user adoption issues, non-approved usage of approved tools, and other compliance signals, and surface these to the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Identify recurring issues in emerging technology sourcing and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.
- Contribute to knowledge sharing across Global Procurement on emerging technology, SaaS, AI, and digital innovation sourcing practices.
- Support the role’s value contribution by improving visibility over fast-moving technology spend, reducing duplicated tools, undocumented pilots, and audit risk.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Reports to:** Senior Category Manager, IT.
- **Internal:** Office of the CIO and IT teams; Senior Category Manager, IT; Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Finance; Airbel Impact Lab; Data and Analytics; External Relations; Country Program supply chain and innovation leads; program innovation teams; fundraising and digital teams; AI Governance and Risk Committee when applicable; Global Procurement peers.
- **External:** Emerging technology vendors and resellers; SaaS, cloud, cybersecurity, automation, data, and AI providers; startup and niche technology vendors; industry analysts; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, information technology, engineering, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- Minimum 5 to 7 years of procurement, sourcing, contract management, or vendor management experience.
- Of the required 5 to 7 years above, at least 3 years must be in IT procurement, SaaS and software sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, cybersecurity tools, data platforms, or similar technology categories.
- Experience supporting pilots, trials, proofs of concept, or other early-stage technology procurement activities.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and technology risk reviews, including cybersecurity, data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier evaluations, commercial analysis, and contract coordination.
- Good understanding of technology procurement risks, including data protection, information security, intellectual property, software licensing, vendor lock-in, and third-party risk.
- Ability to work effectively with IT, Legal, Information Security, Data Protection, Finance, and business teams.
- Demonstrated ability to work quickly while maintaining compliance, controls, and documentation standards.
- Strong stakeholder service orientation and ability to balance procurement standards with customer needs.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good judgment and ability to balance speed, compliance, risk, and stakeholder needs.
- Experience in an NGO, donor-funded organization, humanitarian agency, UN agency, or complex global organization.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements such as USAID/BHA, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Professional certification such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Flexible (IRC hub city preferred; remote considered). Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Lebanon, Germany, Kenya, Pakistan, and Jordan.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Senior Expert, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL), National Security
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**UK, London | Full-time**

The Senior Expert, MEL will join Integrity’s Services Team and play a key technical and management role in the design and delivery of our MEL portfolio. UK national security will be a primary thematic focus, including cybersecurity, countering information manipulation, economic security, resilience and preparedness, and emerging technology governance.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a leading role in technical design and delivery of MEL projects and proposals. The Senior Expert will develop and apply appropriate, innovative, and proportionate MEL approaches and methodologies in response to client needs, drawing where relevant on Integrity’s wider expertise in research, evidence, and analysis, and data analytics.

We are looking for someone with experience and expertise that include:

- At least 7 years’ experience in MEL and research, including experience working with UK Government clients.
- Proven experience designing complex MEL bids, preferably for UK Government clients, including developing technical approaches and methodologies, work and resource plans, and commercially viable budgets.
- Strong understanding of the UK national security policy and institutional context, and the implications for the design and delivery of MEL.
- Strong expertise in MEL design including developing theories of change, results frameworks, indicators and wider monitoring and learning systems.
- Strong project and relationship management skills, including experience managing complex projects and working effectively with clients, partners, consultants, and multidisciplinary teams.
- Strong applied research and analytical skills and experience of assuring the quality of MEL, research, and evaluation.

title: Regional Safety & Security Director
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Context**

The East Africa region supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges – conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation – through integrated, impactful approaches.

The region prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. EA focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

The EA region operates country programs in Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and Ethiopia.  
  
**Position Summary**

The Regional Safety and Security Director (RSSD) is one of the most senior leadership roles in the East Africa region and provides strategic leadership for safety, security, and humanitarian access across the region. They set and drive the implementation of a comprehensive strategy to anticipate, analyze, and mitigate risks, safeguard staff and assets, enable principled humanitarian access, and ensure the continuity of IRC’s operations and programs in complex and high-risk environments.

As the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the Regional Vice President (RVP), the RSSD works alongside the RVP on the decisions that shape IRC’s presence, access, and continuity across the region. They are a full member of the Regional Management Team and of IRC’s global safety and security (S&S) team. Within the Regional Management Team, the RSSD contributes as a senior leader to regional strategy, priorities, and decision-making, not only as the safety and security function, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices. They integrate Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) informed security risk analysis into strategic, operational, programmatic, and partnership decisions so that security considerations are embedded across IRC’s work.

Reporting jointly to the RVP and the Senior Director for Safety and Security (SDSS), the RSSD operates with significant autonomy and influence. Working in close partnership with Country Directors, they ensure that each country program has robust, context-appropriate protocols, systems, and capacities in place to address unique threats and challenges, while remaining agile to adapt to shifting environments.

The RSSD maintains in-depth knowledge of security dynamics across all EA countries, monitors early warning indicators, and deploys regularly, including at short notice, to support local teams. They play a central role in mentoring and building the capabilities of IRC staff and leaders to operate safely and effectively, thereby strengthening IRC’s ability to reach and serve the most affected and underserved populations.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Regional Management**

- As a member of the Regional Management Team, contribute as a senior leader to regional strategy, priority-setting, and decision-making, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices across the region rather than representing the safety and security function alone.
- Serve as the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the RVP, enabling timely, risk-informed decisions on humanitarian access, operational continuity, and duty of care, and jointly activating and leading crisis management when required.
- Partner with Country Directors to align safety, security, and humanitarian access with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs) and operational priorities, supporting their decision-making and accountability for risk.

**Security Risk Management**

- Lead and supervise the identification, analysis, and mitigation of S&S risks across the region, ensuring alignment with IRC’s global standards.
- Guide and support Country Directors and field leaders to adapt and implement context-specific security risk management strategies ensuring proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness.
- Review, monitor, and encourage compliance with the Security Minimum Standards (SMS) in all country programs providing follow-up and technical guidance where gaps are identified.
- Drive and champion the development, adaptation, and roll-out of global and regional initiatives on duty of care and safeguarding, embedding these into operational culture and practice.
- Shape and strengthen safety and security policies, procedures, and practices that fully integrate Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (GEDI) principles as well as Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) commitments.
- Extend IRC’s security capacity to partners, ensuring they receive tailored risk management support, access to systems, and benefit from IRC’s standards relevant to their operational contexts.
- Build and maintain an active network of IRC security focal points across country programs and cultivate strong external relationships with professional contacts, peer agencies, and security counterparts to enhance collective risk management.

**Humanitarian Access Management**

- Enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access across country programs, ensuring communities can be reached and served in line with IRC’s country Strategy Action Plans (SAP).
- Strengthen and expand humanitarian access teams and capabilities across the region, building skills, systems, and approaches that enhance operational reach and acceptance.
- Develop, adapt, and implement context-specific guidelines for humanitarian access and engagement with state and non-state actors, ensuring alignment with IRC policy, international humanitarian law, and standards.
- Advise and guide country programs in the design of operational and programmatic contingency plans ensuring preparedness for sudden shifts in political, security, or conflict dynamics.
- Collaborate with relevant IRC units to ensure prompt and appropriate follow-up to violations of IRC’s Code of Conduct and breaches of humanitarian principles, reinforcing accountability and ethical operations.

**Performance Management and Development**

- Lead and actively contribute to the recruitment and selection of key positions with S&S responsibilities, ensuring high-caliber talent and diverse representation.
- Co-manage and mentor direct-report staff (under the Management in Partnership (MiP) model with Country Directors), setting clear expectations, defining performance objectives, providing regular, timely feedback, and conducting documented performance reviews that drive accountability and growth.
- Promote and safeguard staff well-being, monitoring staff care across the region and supporting appropriate interventions to address the needs of both national and international staff.
- Directly supervise and develop the Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Coordinator, ensuring progressive and forward-looking S&S plans that align with regional priorities and organizational strategy.

**Learning & Development**

- Design, support, and supervise the implementation of regional capacity-building plans, ensuring effective delivery of IRC’s global S&S training programs across EA country programs.
- Embed gender-sensitive approaches into all capacity development and learning initiatives, addressing gender-specific risks and ensuring inclusivity in staff preparedness.
- Lead and facilitate critical incident management trainings and simulations, in close coordination with the global S&S unit to strengthen preparedness and response capacities across the region.

**Incident Management**

- Support country programs to ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality incident notification, reporting, analysis, and dissemination of lessons learned.
- Serve as a member of the Regional Incident Management Team actively supporting the RVP in the management and resolution of Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents.
- Facilitate After-Action Reviews ensuring that corrective measures are clearly defined, documented, and systematically implemented in line with established incident protocols.
- Oversee and monitor the SHIELD incident database producing quarterly trend analyses to inform strategic decision-making and strengthen regional risk mitigation.

**Key Working Relationships**

- Reports to: Regional Vice President, East Africa, and Senior Director, Global Safety & Security (matrixed reporting)
- Member of: Regional Management Team and IRC’s global Safety & Security team
- Partners closely with: the Regional Vice President, as principal safety and security advisor, and Country Directors on country risk, humanitarian access, and duty of care
- Manages: Regional Humanitarian Access & Security Coordinator; and, through Management in Partnership with the respective Country Directors, country Security Leads
- Collaborates with: fellow Regional Safety & Security Directors, the Director of Security Learning & Operations, the Global Duty of Care Director, People & Culture, and other members of the Regional Management Team; and, externally, with peer agencies, security networks, and relevant counterparts

**Qualifications & Requirements**

- At least 10 years’ experience in international humanitarian assistance, with proven ability to plan, organize, and lead security management operations.
- Prior experience in EA with strong knowledge of regional and country dynamics is essential.
- Fluency in English required; proficiency in a relevant regional language (e.g. Arabic, Amharic, Somali, or Swahili) is an asset.
- Demonstrated grounding in humanitarian principles, codes of conduct, NGO culture, and proven success in gender-sensitive security management and gender equality.
- Skilled at influencing without authority and building effective relationships across multinational teams, partners, and stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge through mentoring, coaching, and non-formal methods.
- Strong capacity to analyze and present complex security dynamics and incidents clearly and on short notice, highlighting implications for operations.
- Willingness and ability to travel up to 40% of the time.

**Work Environment**

This position is open to both national and international applicants, in the locations indicated as well as potentially other IRC locations open to hosting. We will, however, prioritize consideration of national candidates from the region and for which our highly competitive national salary scale and benefits will apply.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based, are currently located outside your home country, and possess over 4 years of international work experience, the IRC has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing, and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.  
  
**Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply for this role, and are committed to supporting them through flexible working arrangements, safety and duty of care planning tailored to the East African countries’ context, and a workplace culture that values the leadership women bring to humanitarian response.

In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: ICT Strategy & Digital Transformation Consultancy
body:
**Purpose & Scope of work**  
Afghanaid seeks to engage an independent ICT consultant or consulting firm to undertake a focused review  
of its ICT environment and develop a practical ICT Strategy and Digital Transformation Roadmap. The  
assignment will focus on strengthening operational resilience, cybersecurity, inter-office connectivity,  
systems integration, business continuity, and digital service delivery. The consultancy is expected to provide:  
a) Clear findings on the current ICT environment;  
b) Prioritised and practical recommendations;  
c) A high-level target ICT architecture and operating model; and  
d) A phased and costed implementation roadmap aligned with organisational priorities, capacity, and  
budget.  
The objective is to provide Afghanaid with an implementable roadmap that supports operational continuity,  
informed decision-making, and future ICT investment planning.  
The assignment will support Afghanaid in making informed and cost-effective ICT investment decisions by  
identifying priority areas for improvement, reducing operational and cybersecurity risks, strengthening interoffice connectivity, business continuity and organisational resilience, and ensuring that future ICT  
investments are planned, prioritised, and aligned with organisational needs and available resources. The  
resulting roadmap will provide a structured basis for budgeting, resource allocation, and medium-term  
planning.

**The Consultant shall:**  
a) Review Afghanaid's current ICT environment, governance, infrastructure, systems, service delivery,  
processes, and operational challenges;  
b) Identify risks, gaps, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities;  
Page 2 of 5  
c) Assess ICT asset lifecycle management, including device assignment, inventory management,  
maintenance, replacement planning, procurement governance, and end-user support processes.  
d) Develop a future-state ICT operating model and high-level enterprise architecture;  
e) Recommend priority for modernization, system integration, automation, AI adoption,  
cybersecurity, and data governance.  
f) Establish practical governance, service management, asset management frameworks to improve  
accountability, service quality and organization resilience;  
g) Prepare a phased and costed roadmap to support budgeting and decision-making.  
1\. Existing Strategic Decisions  
The following organisational initiatives are already approved and are not subject to strategic review:  
a) ERP modernisation (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central);  
b) CRM development and enhancement; and  
c) Website platform development.  
d) Odoo, CRM and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central integration.  
The Consultant shall focus on dependencies, risks, and alignment of these initiatives within the overall ICT  
roadmap rather than recommending alternative platforms. The assignment does not require detailed low  
level system design or implementation-level specifications.

**2. Current Landscape**  
Afghanaid operates across Afghanistan through a head office, provincial offices, district locations, and  
partner organisations. The organisation relies heavily on ICT systems to support programme delivery,  
financial management, fundraising, human resources, communication, monitoring and evaluation, and  
operational coordination.  
a) Over recent years, Afghanaid has invested in network infrastructure, collaboration tools, enterprise  
systems, connectivity, and digital capabilities. Core systems currently include:  
b) Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2013 (upgradation to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central in  
progress);  
c) Salesforce CRM;  
d) Odoo HRMIS;  
e) Google Workspace; and  
f) Microsoft Teams.  
While these systems support key business functions, they have developed over time with limited integration,  
creating challenges in data management, reporting, governance, operational efficiency, and service delivery.  
Key areas requiring improvement include business continuity, disaster recovery, cybersecurity, data  
protection, systems integration, service management, and operational resilience in low-connectivity and  
high-risk environments.

**3. Strategic Priorities and Transformation Drivers**  
Afghanaid operates in a complex and volatile environment characterised by security risks, political  
uncertainty, constrained connectivity, and periodic internet disruptions that may impact field operations.  
These conditions require ICT systems that are resilient, secure, and capable of sustaining operations under  
remote, low-connectivity, and high-risk scenarios.  
To support operational continuity, Afghanaid must strengthen its enterprise network architecture, inter office  
connectivity, collaboration tools to ensure uninterrupted communication between headquarters, provincial  
offices, and district-level structures, regardless of external disruptions. In parallel, the organisation must  
enhance its capability for secure remote working through the implementation of digitised workflow systems  
and standardised collaboration tools.  
There is also a critical need to strengthen cybersecurity controls, data protection mechanisms, and identity  
and access management, including improved governance of licensed software, online accounts, and  
password security. These measures are essential to mitigate evolving cyber threats and reduce organisational  
exposure to security risks. Continued investment in staff digital capacity is required to ensure effective system  
adoption and operational efficiency across all user groups.  
Afghanaid should also progressively expand and optimise the use of ERP capabilities across the organisation,  
where operationally and financially viable. In addition, the organisation must accelerate the digitisation of  
monitoring, evaluation, and needs assessment processes to improve data quality, timeliness, and decisionmaking.  
As Afghanaid’s digital presence continues to grow, its web and social media platforms must remain current,  
secure, and strategically aligned with organisational communications objectives. In parallel, there is a need  
to enhance donor management workflows to improve efficiency and accuracy.

**Key Priorities: The following strategic priorities have been identified:**  
▪ Network architecture, resilience, inter-office connectivity, and collaboration tools: This includes assessment  
and optimisation of enterprise network architecture, connectivity between HQ, provincial and district offices,  
and collaboration platforms to ensure secure, reliable, and uninterrupted communication under lowconnectivity, high-risk, and disruption-prone operating conditions.  
▪ Platform consolidation and standardisation: The parallel use of Google Workspace and Microsoft Teams  
increases exposure to phishing, account compromise, and unauthorised access. There is a need to standardise  
collaboration and communication platforms to strengthen governance, security, and operational control.  
▪ Digital transformation and automation: Develop a practical roadmap for digital transformation, workflow  
automation, AI readiness, and the controlled transition towards a paperless operating environment,  
supported by governance, change management, and user adoption.  
▪ Cybersecurity and resilience: Strengthening cybersecurity governance, technical controls, identity and access  
management, security monitoring, vulnerability management and organisational data protection, and  
business continuity frameworks is essential, particularly in the context of low-connectivity environments and  
operational risk exposure.  
▪ Data protection and ethical governance: Robust data protection, privacy, and ethical data governance  
frameworks must be established and enforced in line with international standards.  
▪ Business continuity and disaster recovery: Formalisation and strengthening of business continuity and  
disaster recovery capabilities is required to ensure operational stability under disruption scenarios.  
▪ Capacity development: Structured staff training and continuous digital capability development programmes  
are required to ensure sustainable adoption of systems and processes.  
▪ Information security and risk management: Strengthening enterprise-wide information security governance  
and risk management frameworks is required to support organisational resilience.  
▪ IT service management: Improvement of ICT service delivery, service desk operations, incident management,  
request fulfilment, problem management, and change management, support project managers and M&E  
staff, and operational governance is required to enhance efficiency, accountability, and user experience.  
▪ Digital alignment: ICT systems must be continuously aligned and integrated in line with evolving technological  
trends and the organisation’s operational and strategic priorities.  
Afghanaid therefore requires independent technical expertise to assess its current ICT environment and  
develop strategic, technically robust, and implementation-ready recommendations for a secure, integrated,  
and scalable digital ecosystem aligned with organisational needs.

**4. Duration of the Assignment**  
The consultancy shall be executed in accordance with an agreed project implementation plan, detailing clearly  
defined milestones, deliverables, and timelines. The overall assignment is expected to be completed within 4  
months from the date of contract signing, unless an extension is formally agreed in writing by both parties.  
The Consultant shall ensure timely delivery of all outputs in accordance with the approved work plan and  
shall report progress regularly to Afghanaid’s designated project manager or senior management.

**5. Consultant Qualifications**  
The consulting firm or individual consultant must demonstrate the following qualifications, expertise, and  
experience:  
• Experience in developing and implementing enterprise-wide ICT strategies and digital transformation  
plans.  
• Evidence of previous assignments of a similar nature with NGOs or grant funded organisations, the  
firm shall provide a list of relevant clients and references, including contact details “where available”.  
• Proven expertise in enterprise architecture frameworks and designing integrated ICT ecosystems.  
• Experience in aligning ICT architecture with operational, governance, and data management  
requirements.  
• Knowledge and practical experience with cybersecurity frameworks, risk assessments, vulnerability  
management, and mitigation strategies.  
• Familiarity with ISO 27001 or equivalent security standards.  
• Knowledge of GDPR and internationally recognised data protection and privacy standards.  
• Experience establishing data governance, privacy, and ethical information management frameworks.  
• Strong understanding of digital workflows, automation, AI applications, cloud solutions, and  
emerging ICT technologies.  
• Experience in implementing practical digital innovations that enhance operational efficiency and  
decision-making.  
• Ability to propose training programmes to ensure sustainable adoption of recommended systems and  
processes.

**6. Confidentiality and Data Protection**  
The Consultant shall treat all information, data, and documentation obtained or accessed during the course  
of this assignment as strictly confidential. This includes, but is not limited to, organisational records, financial  
data, donor information, programme details, and staff information.  
The Consultant shall:  
• Comply fully with Afghanaid’s data protection policies and all applicable data protection laws,  
including GDPR.  
• Ensure that all sensitive information is stored, transmitted, and processed securely, preventing  
unauthorised access, disclosure, or loss.  
• Use the information solely for the purposes of delivering the consultancy assignment.  
• Return or securely destroy all organisational data and materials upon completion of the assignment,  
unless otherwise agreed in writing.  
• Immediately notify Afghanaid of any actual or suspected breach of confidentiality or data security.  
The Consultant acknowledges that any breach of confidentiality or improper handling of data may result in  
legal liability and termination of the consultancy contract.

**7. Evaluation and Selection Process**  
Afghanaid will apply a structured, transparent, and competitive evaluation process to assess all eligible  
proposals. Submissions will be evaluated in two stages: (i) technical evaluation and (ii) financial evaluation.  
Only proposals that meet the minimum technical threshold will proceed to financial assessment.  
The technical evaluation will assess the bidder’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology,  
and compliance with the functional and technical requirements. Financial proposals will be evaluated based  
on overall cost-effectiveness and value for money. Proposals will also be assessed for clarity, completeness,  
and alignment with the scope of work. Technical and financial proposals will be weighted, unless otherwise  
specified, at 70% for technical and 30% for financial evaluation. The combined score will be used to determine  
the most economically and technically advantageous proposal.  
Afghanaid may request clarifications, conduct interviews, and require shortlisted bidders to present or  
demonstrate their proposed solution either virtually or in person as part of the evaluation process. Afghanaid  
reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal, in whole or in part, and may cancel the procurement  
process at any stage without incurring any liability.

title: Project Director, Virtual Services
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Project Director of Virtual Services at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of a national portfolio of virtual resettlement programs that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, particularly those living outside traditional service areas. The portfolio includes legacy resettlement programs, state-run programs as well as [ALMA](https://welcome.rescue.org/us/en/services/alma), an AI-powered virtual assistant that helps newcomers navigate essential resources and services. The Project Director also contributes to the Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department’s virtual and information services strategy.

The role oversees virtual program strategy, implementation, performance, and budget management. It also ensures compliance with award requirements through programmatic monitoring and rigorous direct assistance operations, and it oversees the case management and data systems that support reporting and evidence of impact. The Director leads a geographically dispersed team and cultivates partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders. A central focus of the position is developing and scaling innovative, technology-enabled service delivery models that strengthen operational efficiency and promote client self-sufficiency. This position reports to the Senior Director of Resettlement.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Program Implementation**: Lead the design, implementation, and scaling of a national portfolio of virtual programs (some examples include Program of Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, Preferred Communities) that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, leveraging innovative, client-centered service delivery models to reach underserved populations.
- **Interagency Collaboration:** Provide strategic leadership and oversight of interagency virtual services working groups, fostering collaboration and alignment across resettlement agencies to inform program strategy, coordinate implementation, and strengthen virtual service delivery.
- **People & Culture:** Build and cultivate an inclusive, impactful team. Support managers in their leadership of teams in line with IRC's People Manager Standards to ensure successful program delivery and a safe, supportive environment for clients and staff.
- **Monitoring & Compliance:** Design and enable effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on program services. Ensure a data-driven approach that informs program adaptation and provides further evidence of virtual services impact.
- **Budget & Financial Management:** Coordinate with HQ Finance staff to ensure compliance with donor and organizational requirements including financial planning, expenditure monitoring, caseload forecasting, and effective resource allocation.
- **AI Product Strategy and Management:** Lead the product strategy, development, and deployment of ALMA, IRC's AI-powered virtual assistant, in collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab and IRC's technical development teams. Oversee product roadmaps, iterative development, testing, and the rollout of new features and international adaptations, including expansion to Poland.
- **Client Engagement and Co-Design:** Lead IRC's Service Excellence Advisory Committee, creating structured opportunities for refugees and other newcomers to inform program design, implementation, and continuous improvement. Integrate client feedback and lived experiences into service delivery, technology development, and strategic decision-making.
- **Technical Expertise and Resource Mobilization:** Provide technical expertise and strategic input into the development of grant proposals, funding opportunities, and program designs that expand and strengthen virtual service delivery across IRC's resettlement network. Identify and apply for opportunities to advance virtual services.
