Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Coordinateur logistique voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d’urgence face aux crises, conflits, catastrophes naturelles, sont l’un des axes prioritaires d’intervention pour Médecins du Monde. Notre indépendance financière, la force de nos partenariats, l'implication et la flexibilité de nos équipes sont autant d’éléments clés pour apporter une réponse efficace à ces catastrophes.

Le mandat de la Cellule Urgence est d’intervenir en priorité sur les urgences et crises qui surviennent dans les pays où MdM est déjà opérationnel (30 pays). La réponse d’urgence dans les pays où MdM n’est pas présent est systématiquement considéré si l’accès au continuum de soins est interrompu et si les capacités du pays et des acteurs sur place sont dépassées.

MdM fournit également un appui et une expertise opérationnelle et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques sur leurs réponses d’urgences.

Vous faites partie de l’équipe voltigeur.euse.s de la Cellule Urgence qui est donc déployée dans les contextes d’urgence pour lancer de nouvelles interventions et/ou renforcer les équipes existantes. Vous pouvez également être déployé.e pour participer à des missions exploratoires, participer à l’ouverture de nouvelles missions et/ou de nouvelles bases, appuyer les opérations/missions existantes MdM à travers du « gap-filling » ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d’activités spécifiques liées aux activités logistiques (ex : formation, préparation, etc.).

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

- Piloter la stratégie logistique de la mission et en assurer la mise en œuvre
- Coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités logistiques : chaîne d’approvisionnement, parc de véhicules, gestion des stocks, équipements, bâtiments, infrastructures informatiques, moyens de communication et énergie
- Animer et renforcer les capacités de l’équipe
- Appuyer également le/la coordinateur·rice général·e dans le suivi des procédures de sécurité
- Veiller au respect et à la bonne application des procédures MdM et bailleurs, et contribuer à garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité des services logistiques au sein de la mission, tout en œuvrant à la prévention et à la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la Cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la coordinateur.rice général.e de la mission. Vous avez un lien fonctionnel avec le/la référent.e logistique basé.e au siège. Vous collaborez avec les coordinateur.rice.s support ainsi qu'avec le/la chargé.e d'accès humanitaire & risques et les équipes programme.

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si :**

- Vous avez une formation supérieure bac+2 type achat ou logistique
- Vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle de 5 ans (dont minimum 1 an sur un poste en coordination logistique dans le milieu humanitaire ou de minimum 2 ans d'expérience en tant que logisticien)
- Vous avez une solide résistance au stress et une capacité à vous adapter dans des contextes sécuritaires complexes
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous maitrisez l’anglais et le français couramment à l’écrit comme à l’oral

**Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité et l’adaptabilité ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe vous posent des difficultés
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, n’attendez plus, postulez !

## VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

**Contrat & statut :**

- CDD à pourvoir dès que possible et jusqu'au 31/12/2026
- Salaire brut mensuel de 3 392 €
- Statut : agent de maitrise
- Poste à temps plein

**Les avantages :**

- Télétravail ponctuel
- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime de déplacement terrain de 198,18€ brut/mois au prorata du temps de présence sur le terrain
- Au siège, tickets restaurants d’une valeur unitaire de 10€ (participation à hauteur de 60% de MdM, 40% salarié.e) et sur le terrain via une allocation forfaitaire de restauration fixée en fonction du pays
- Au siège, remboursement du titre de transport en commun à 50% (abonnement mensuel) et prise en charge à 100% des allers-retours siège-terrain
- Logement pris en charge sur le terrain à 100%
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé au siège à Saint-Denis (20% du temps) et sur les terrains internationaux (80% du temps)
- Déploiement sur le terrain pas avant 1 mois d’intégration
- Travail sur écran, en open space
- Communication orale et téléphonique
- Posture assise prolongée

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

title: MEL Lead (FCDO GOAL)
body:
**About the GOAL Opportunity**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is preparing to bid for FCDO's Girls and Out-of-School Children: Action for Learning Programme (GOAL) Long-Term Technical Assistance (LTTA) contract in Pakistan, following release of FCDO's Terms of Reference (ITT 7863). GOAL builds on more than a decade of UK-funded education reform in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), delivered through the Punjab Education Support Programme (PESP, 2013–2022) and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Education Sector Programme (KESP, 2012–2022), and on two live GOAL components: the Bridging Technical Assistance grant (B-TAG, ending March 2027) and the ILMpact remedial learning grant (ending September 2026), both of which the incoming Supplier will need to review and build on during inception.

The LTTA contract will run for up to 38 months (December 2026 – January 2030), comprising a 4-month inception period, a 32-month implementation period, and a 2-month closure phase, with a budget of up to £13 million and an extension option of up to £6.5 million and 18 months at FCDO's discretion. It will deliver systems-strengthening, politically informed technical assistance to provincial education departments in Punjab and KP, with Sindh included as a limited, capped scope (up to £1 million) focused on scoping, needs analysis and possibly Teacher Licensing support; the remaining budget is split equally between Punjab and KP.

The programme's three outcomes are:

- **Foundational Learning (30%):** strengthened provincial delivery of early and inclusive Foundational Learning.
- **Teacher Professionalisation (40%):** improved teacher professionalisation, including standards, licensing, and performance and support systems.
- **Education Financing Governance (30%):** improved governance and accountability of education financing, including public financial management and innovative financing.

The Terms of Reference place strong emphasis on systems thinking and a Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) approach, including a 'coalitions for change' lens that looks beyond government departments to civil society, philanthropy and the private sector, and on strengthening how provincial governments manage the rapid growth of outsourced and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schools across Punjab and KP. Equity, inclusion and safeguarding are cross-cutting requirements throughout.

FCDO requires a lean Core Team of a Project Director (the only role not required to be full-time; at least 20% of days in Pakistan), a Team Leader, a Technical Assistance Lead, two Outcome Leads (one covering teaching and learning, one covering PFM and innovative financing), and two Provincial Leads (Punjab and KP) from contract commencement, with a third for Sindh only if FCDO later approves a Sindh implementation phase. The named Table 1 Core Team positions must be full-time and exclusive to the contract; any additional Core Team positions a bidder proposes do not have to be full-time, but are still subject to the same exclusivity requirement while engaged. IRC is proposing to strengthen this structure with a dedicated MEL Lead. FCDO's Terms of Reference confirm that GOAL's programme-wide MEL component is not being separately procured, and para 13.5 explicitly invites bidders to propose additional Core Team expertise beyond FCDO's named positions — this role is IRC's response to that invitation, not a named Table 1 position.

**Background of the role:**

The MEL Lead is a core team position responsible for the production, budgeting and implementation of the programme's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) strategy. The MEL strategy must set out the approach to data collection, management and analysis; evidence use and generation; use of innovation and technology; Value for Money (VFM); and dissemination — and must align with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the overall GOAL programme.

The MEL Lead will report to the Team Lead, working closely with the Technical Assistance Lead to ensure MEL evidence informs technical decision-making, and with the GESI Specialist to ensure GESI-disaggregated data collection and analysis.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

- Lead production of the programme's MEL strategy covering data collection/management/analysis, evidence use and generation, use of innovation and technology, VFM, and dissemination, aligned with the Theory of Change, logframe and VFM monitoring for the wider GOAL programme.
- Propose and apply MEL methodologies and methods capable of capturing progress in systems thinking and Thinking and Working Politically (TWP) — for example Developmental Evaluation or Systems Thinking MEL, using methods such as outcome mapping or process tracing — rather than relying on conventional summative M&E alone.
- Lead development and updating of the programme's logframe and maintain the change log recording all logframe amendments throughout the life of the contract.
- Establish required quantitative and qualitative baseline data before the end of the inception period, in collaboration with SED Punjab, ESED KP and other GOAL component partners, drawing on existing B-TAG, ILMpact, DARE-RC and RSPN knowledge products rather than starting from scratch.
- Design monitoring activities that are real-time wherever possible, use community-driven modes of monitoring and appropriate technology, integrate into government systems rather than creating parallel ones, and remain accessible and easy to understand by all partners.
- Ensure the MEL system can track plausible contribution pathways to FCDO's wider education portfolio milestones — for example, the Foundational Learning milestone of a 5% increase in Grade 5 reading in Urdu and English in KP and Punjab by 2029 against the 2023 ASER baseline — using agreed indicators and available data sources including Annual School Census data, ASER and relevant provincial/national assessments.
- Propose an incremental, additive approach to evaluation that builds up a picture over the life of the contract, rather than relying on a single summative report at the end of the TA.
- Own the evidence base for KPI 5 (acting on lessons learnt), ensuring lessons from partners are systematically captured, analysed and reflected in quarterly reporting and adaptive management decisions; contribute quality-assured MEL and logframe products that support KPI 2 (quality of implementation deliverables).
- Lead preparation of the annual MEL Strategy document and annual Results KPIs reporting, and contribute the MEL sections of the Exit Plan (first drafted in the inception phase, updated annually, finalised January 2029) and of quarterly Progress Reports to FCDO and to SED Punjab/ESED KP/SELD Sindh.
- Ensure MEL data collection is disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography, working closely with the GESI Specialist to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- Track and report on Value for Money, supporting the Team Lead's quarterly financial and progress reporting and the programme's fee-retention/KPI-linked payment model.
- Build the MEL capacity of provincial government counterparts as part of the programme's systems-strengthening approach, consistent with the ToR's expectation that TA strengthens government routines rather than substituting for them.

**Qualification, experience and Skills will include:**

**Essential:**

- Advanced degree in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, social science, education, or a related field.
- Substantial senior MEL leadership experience (indicatively 8-10+ years) on FCDO- or similarly funded, complex donor programmes, ideally involving adaptive, politically informed programming.
- Demonstrated expertise in adaptive/developmental MEL methodologies (e.g. Developmental Evaluation, Systems Thinking MEL) and methods (e.g. outcome mapping, process tracing), rather than conventional logframe-only M&E.
- Strong experience developing and managing logframes, Theories of Change, and Value for Money monitoring frameworks nested within a wider programme logframe.
- Experience with KPI-linked, fee-retention payment structures and donor reporting requirements, ideally FCDO's.
- Experience with education data systems and sources (e.g. EMIS, Annual School Census, ASER) in Pakistan or a similar context strongly preferred.
- Experience building MEL capacity within government counterparts.
- Excellent written and spoken English; Urdu and/or other relevant regional languages an advantage.

**Collaboration with Other Team Members**

- **Team Lead:** provide regular MEL evidence and VfM reporting to inform programme management and donor reporting.
- **Technical Assistance Lead:** ensure MEL findings inform technical decision-making and quality assurance across outcome areas.
- **Outcome Leads (Teaching & Learning; PFM & Innovative Financing) and Provincial Leads:** coordinate data collection, monitoring and process evaluation across outcome areas and provinces.
- **GESI Specialist:** ensure MEL data and analysis are disaggregated by gender, disability, poverty and geography to identify and target the most marginalised children.
- **SED Punjab / ESED KP:** support provincial government counterparts to strengthen their own MEL and data systems, in alignment with DARE.

title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

**Working Environment:**  This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.

title: Grants and Reporting Coordinator
body:
**Country Programme:** Ukraine

**Contract Length:** 1 year with possible extension

**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Line Manager:** Head of Grants and Rerporting

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

## **About the Ukrainian Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) began operations in Ukraine in 2003 with human rights programs and expanded to humanitarian assistance in 2014. With the full-scale invasion in February 2022, we significantly scaled up our programming across the country. Since then, PIN has reached almost 4 million people, working with a network of local partner organizations.

Today, PIN has its offices and teams in 8 oblasts in Ukraine with more than 500 local and international staff working in Lvivska, Kyivska (head office), Sumska, Kharkivska, Dnipropetrovska, Mykolaivska and Khersonska, Zaporizka, and Donetska oblasts.

PIN's assistance addresses both immediate and longer-term needs of war-affected people, focusing on safe water and sanitation, shelter repairs, protection services, and education in emergencies. Our recovery programming delivers more systemic solutions, including support to district heating systems and renewable energy initiatives.

PIN also provides comprehensive assistance to veterans and their families, including business grants and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), strengthens the quality of education in schools, and advances systemic improvements in social care for the most vulnerable. Funding comes from a diverse range of institutional and private donors.

## **About the role:**

As a member of the Country Programme (CP) and specifically a team member of the Grants and Reporting Unit, with the support of the Head of Grants and Reporting (HoGR), the Grants and Reporting Coordinator (GC) will oversee assigned grants’ implementation progress, particularly in relation to approved proposal and in compliance with donor’s rules and procedures. The GC will report on their assigned project/s in close collaboration with relevant teams. The Grants and Reporting Coordinator will act as a Grants Focal Point (GFP) as assigned during the proposal development, will support or lead the proposal development and project modification processes, and may act as a focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums as assigned. Other tasks may be assigned by the HoGR as deemed necessary.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

**Program Coordination and Grants Management:**

- Maintains an internal tracking database of her/his assigned grants/donors, reporting timelines, project milestones/targets and modifications. Ensures comprehensive grant files, donor guidelines and resources are maintained, updated and available for use.
- Coordinates with Area Managers and Area teams, Programme Coordinators,
- MEAL, Technical Leads, as well as Advocacy and Communication, Procurement, Finance, Database, Partnership units, and Security department as well as Headquarters (HQ) focal points to ensure accurate tracking and reporting of programmatic adjustments throughout the project life cycle.
- Advises teams and partners, where needed, on donor’s compliance, rules and requirements in coordination with other relevant units.
- Prepares and leads the kick off, project review, and close out meetings, and participates in other project/grant-related meetings e.g. Lessons Learned meeting. Prepares documents and collects information from relevant Finance, Logistics/Procurement, Partnership (PI), MEAL, Comms and Advocacy, Security, Data and Programme teams in order to facilitate regular project review meetings.
- Prepares regular updates for key donors on project progress, achievement highlights and challenges as well as shares briefing notes, other project and communication materials with respective donors
- Provides information to relevant staff members on reporting timelines of the assigned project/s. Ensures relevant staff are provided with timely information and materials – including guidelines, templates and examples – to develop quality reporting contributions. Acts as a focal point for collection, compilation, review, quality control and editing of both quantitative and qualitative internal and donor reporting.
- Prepares all donor narrative reports and coordinates necessary clearances and submission of reports and necessary annexes; and flags inconsistencies, if identified to the Finance Department to ensure that financial and narrative reports are aligned.
- In collaboration with technical leads, ensures that all reports are in-line with the assigned donor/s requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues such as protection, gender, do no harm, and conflict sensitivity.
- Works with Data team to report on all quantitative figures; flags any discrepancies if identified, to Data team; utilises dashboards and databases as primary source of information, working with Area teams to provide qualitative information where dashboards have gaps.
- In coordination with the PI and Technical Leads, reviews all MEAL products that will be submitted to the donor to ensure alignment with reports and donor communication.
- Prepares Modification Request, No-cost Extension, and/or Cost Extension packages in coordination with relevant departments. Supports finalisation of relevant project-related documents prepared by other departments, such as Evaluation Terms of References (ToRs), Third Party Monitoring (TPM) plans, etc. and coordinates with TPM organizations contributing to planning monitoring visits.
- Undertakes regular field visits to gain in-depth understanding of the context and implementation.
- Coordinates donor-related field visits as needed.

**Fundraising and Resource Mobilization:**

- Proactively supports in monitoring and analysis of new funding opportunities for PIN in Ukraine through relevant open sources (donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals), clusters, and bilateral consultation and scoping with existing and potential donors.
- Working in close collaboration with Technical Leads, Programme Coordinators and Area teams, as well as other relevant units and departments, acts as a GFP and/or Proposal Lead, as assigned; supports preparation for Go-No-Go and proposal kick-off preparation meetings, proposal development workplan/timelines; leads development of concept notes, proposals (including supporting the design of logical frameworks, targets, and budgets); ensures updated and current templates are available for narrative, finance, and other parts or annexes.
- Leads proposal modifications and situation analyses – including modifications in logical frameworks, targets, and budgets.
- As assigned, creates and shares a folder on SharePoint for the internal proposal preparation, creates a Teams chat for relevant colleagues, and were helpful organizes sectoral design chats/discussions.
- As assigned, creates the [Resource Folder in ELO](https://elo.pinf.cz/ix-CZE/plugin/de.elo.ix.plugin.proxy/web/?useSSO=true#/archive/(A5A8F0FF-3B32-48C6-A732-71520F4FB7B6)/) (PIN’s internal system) and initiates the workflow.
- Follows-up on relevant action items from Ukraine Fundraising and Resource Mobilization meetings, as well as other meetings, ensuring timely completion of relevant tasks.

**Internal and External Coordination:**

- Communicates with relevant donors and represents PIN at the appropriate level of representation.
- Participates in meetings with HQ and other coordination meetings as requested by the line manager.
- Coordinates with focal points from Finance, Data team, MEAL, Programme Quality, and Area teams during proposal development and reporting periods as well as partners, as needed.
- Coordinates with communications team to ensure that relevant communication materials (human interest stories, videos, etc.) are developed for projects as per workplan and donors’ requirements; as well as ensures distribution of readily available communication materials to donors.
- Acts as the main project focal point for respective donors.

## **Requirements:**

- At least 3 years of experience working in a humanitarian and/or development organization, including at least 2 years of experience in grants development.
- Demonstrated experience leading the development and coordination of successful large-scale project proposals for key institutional donors, including DoS, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, BMZ, UN agencies, GAC, and others.
- Proven experience leading the preparation and submission of interim and final donor reports, with a strong understanding of donor requirements, compliance standards, and grant management processes.
- Strong knowledge of all stages of the project and programme cycle, including humanitarian programming quality standards, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), and data management.
- Experience working in complex and volatile humanitarian contexts. Familiarity with the humanitarian context in Ukraine is an advantage.
- Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize competing deadlines, and work effectively under pressure.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including outstanding report writing and editing abilities, and the capacity to collaborate effectively with internal teams and institutional donors. Knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian is an advantage.

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Starting Salary** based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies, between 2600-2800 EUR;
- **Additional allowances include**:
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Monthly Hardship Allowance of 400 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance up to 1000 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
    - Rest & Recreation (R&R) policy in place: 3x 5 days of leave per year with 350 Eur lump sum allowance per each leave.
- **Travel benefits:**
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT);

## **Security situation in Ukraine**

Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front-line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly. PIN security SOPs require PIN staff to proceed to shelter should the risk level be assessed by the Security Department as the highest (launch of missiles or drones) and remain there until the air raid siren is cancelled, which cumulatively can be several times a week, occasionally for several hours at a time (although shorter periods are as well occurring). While air strikes that were targeting energy, infrastructure have finished after winter, they have succeeded in reaching their goals and are likely to resume in late autumn/winter. At the moment military and civilian objects are being targeted, including the west of Ukraine. While Kyiv enjoys relatively strong air defence systems that are intercepting most of the missiles and UAVs, other regions are covered much less significantly which results in bigger damage. Outside of the areas in the vicinity to the contact line, services such as medical care, shops, public transportation as well as restaurants or leisure facilities remain operational.

title: Financial Capabilities Coordinator
body:
**Job Overview:** Under the supervision of the Senior Program Manager, the IRC seeks a Financial Capabilities Coordinator to support the development and implementation of career pathways services in its Economic Empowerment program for refugees and other immigrants in Tucson. This position is responsible for assisting clients in developing plans that help them reach their goals and achieve financial stability, and for ensuring IRC achieves program targets relating to enrollment, economic empowerment outcomes, and connection to community benefits and resources. The Coordinator is to tangibly connect working clients on their journey to a higher paying job to resources and certifications. It is expected to focus services in a one-on-one career counseling format in tandem with conducting classes and workshops on topics such as budgeting, credit building, banking, and financial products.

**Responsibilities: Include, but are not limited to:**

**Client Services:**

- Assist clients in assessing and resolving current financial challenges, while providing a wide lens on their financial health to shift the approach to proactive financial management
- Administer intake and assessment for enrolled participants and co-develop an Individualized Career Development Plan (ICDP) with each participant to guide training, employment, and follow-up activities.
- Coordinate case-managed wraparound supports, including interpretation, transportation and childcare stipends, work supplies, and emergency assistance, tied to each participant's documented barriers and ICDP.
- Connect participants to local occupational training, apprenticeships, or certification programs, and to employer partners for job upgrades or career-related employment.
- Conduct 6- and 12-month follow-up with participants and, when applicable, their employers to assess job retention, wages, advancement, job quality, benefits, and household financial stability.
- Ensure that changes (new job, new benefit, and change in credit score) are properly documented in relevant systems.
- Capture client success stories
- Develop workshop materials or tailor existing materials to meet the needs of the community. Workshop topics may include the following: budgeting, savings, banking products, credit building, and identity theft.

**Program Coordination:**

- Ensure compliance with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency.
- Ensure that information required for program eligibility for all career programs and reporting purposes is collected and that accurate records are maintained, including case files and client data entry.
- Work as part of a team to provide comprehensive strength-based services to IRC clients through coordination of cases and effective communication between team members and departments.

- Train, and supervise interns and volunteers providing career support services to clients enrolled in career programs;
- Participate in IRC network-wide initiatives to understand and share best-practices relating to career pathways programming;
- Build and maintain partnerships with community-based organizations, career service providers, and small business and corporate entities for advanced career opportunities;
- Coordinate corporate and employer engagement opportunities and events.
- Participate in program meetings and staff development activities.

- 2+ years of related professional experience in financial capabilities and/or career development

- Experience working in a diverse, and non-traditional setting with diverse staff and client base

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills and an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications

title: Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor
body:
**Country Programme:** Angola

**Contract Length:** 1 year, with the possibility of extension

**Base**: Luanda, Angola

**Starting date:** upon agreement

**Line Manager:** Country Director for Angola

**People in Need** (PIN) is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

**About the Angola Programme of People in Need:**

**PIN has been in Angola since 2006**, initially through education projects and subsequently expanding its programming across agriculture and livelihoods, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), community health and nutrition, gender, civil society strengthening, child protection and human rights. Over the years, PIN has worked across several provinces, including Bié, Huambo, Huíla, Namibe, Luanda, Uíge, Moxico and Kwanza Sul. Today, PIN’s work in Angola combines longer-term development and resilience building with support to communities affected by climate-related and other shocks, with particular expertise in climate-resilient livelihoods, WASH, nutrition, civil society strengthening and inclusive governance.

**PARS Programme**

PIN is the executing entity for the **PARS Angola project**, "**Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola**". A **five-year project** funded by the **Global Environement Fund (GEF)** and iimplemented in partnership with the **Angolan Ministry of Environment** and **UNIDO**. The project is part of the six-country GEN-funded PARS programme and aims to reduce climate vulnerability and strenghten the resilience of communities in Angola´s southern and coastal provinces by promoting innovation, technology transfer and private-sector-led adaptation solutions through support of Angolan MSMEs.

## **About the role:**

The Project Quality, Reporting and Implementation Advisor supports the effective and high-quality implementation of the **PARS Angola – Promoting climate adaptation and resilience through innovation and entrepreneurship for green jobs in Angola** project implemented by People in Need (PIN) in partnership with the Ministry of Environment of Angola and UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO).

The position provides dedicated support to the PARS Angola Project Management Unit (PMU), with a particular focus on **project cycle management, planning, monitoring of implementation, donor reporting, documentation and compliance**, complemented by operational support required for timely project delivery.

The Advisor works closely with the Project Manager to ensure that activities, outputs, targets, budget, procurement and implementation milestones remain aligned; that implementation progress and risks are systematically tracked; and that reporting to UNIDO is timely, accurate, evidence-based and compliant with the Project Document, Implementing Partner Agreement, Terms of Reference and Operational Guidelines.

The position also helps maintain effective coordination between programme, MEAL, finance, procurement, logistics and other support functions involved in project implementation.

## **Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

- **Project Cycle Management, Planning and Coordination**
    - Support the PMU in the day-to-day coordination and follow-up of project implementation across all PARS Angola components.
    - Support preparation and regular updating of Annual Work Plans, reporting-period workplans, implementation schedules and other project management tools.
    - Maintain an integrated project implementation tracker covering activities, deliverables, indicators, procurement and other milestones, responsible persons and deadlines.
    - Regularly follow up with technical and support teams on agreed actions, deliverables and implementation deadlines; identify delays, bottlenecks or non-compliance with agreed processes; seek timely clarification and corrective action from responsible colleagues; and escalate unresolved or recurring issues to the Head of Programmes and/or Country Director, as appropriate.
    - Support the organization and preparation of regular internal project coordination and review meetings.
    - Support preparation for bi-weekly coordination meetings with UNIDO and monthly implementation reviews, including consolidation of information on implementation progress, budget execution, procurement and recruitment, safeguards, risks and upcoming priorities.
    - Support preparation and follow-up of Project Steering Committee meetings, including background documents, presentations, minutes and agreed actions.
    - Support coordination across programme, MEAL, Finance, Procurement/Logistics and other relevant functions to ensure that implementation remains aligned with approved workplans and project requirements.
- **Reporting and Documentation**
    - Coordinate the internal process for preparation of project reports and ensure that inputs are requested, received and consolidated according to agreed internal deadlines.
    - Draft and/or consolidate technical sections of the **Kick-off Report, interim and annual technical progress reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), final report and other reports required by UNIDO and GEF**.
    - Work closely with MEAL colleagues to ensure that reported results are supported by up-to-date indicator data, monitoring evidence and appropriate means of verification.
    - Work closely with Finance to ensure consistency between narrative reporting, implementation progress, expenditure and financial reporting.
    - Verify that reports clearly describe progress against outputs, activities, indicators and targets and adequately explain delays, challenges, risks and corrective measures.
    - Coordinate internal review and quality assurance of reports before submission to UNIDO.
    - Maintain a structured repository of project achievements, lessons learned, case studies and other evidence that can feed into reporting and knowledge products.
- **Monitoring, Quality and Adaptive Management**
    - Support regular monitoring of implementation against the Project Results Framework, Annual Work Plan, milestones and contractual commitments.
    - Work with the MEAL team and technical staff to ensure that project monitoring data and supporting evidence are collected and available for management and reporting purposes.
    - Support the PMU in monitoring project risks and maintaining an up-to-date Project Risk Register.
    - Track agreed risk mitigation and corrective measures, follow up with responsible colleagues on their implementation, and escalate overdue or insufficiently addressed actions where they may affect project results, compliance, budget execution or contractual commitments.
    - Maintain a clear escalation pathway for significant or recurring implementation issues, including delays, compliance gaps, unresolved risks and deviations from approved workplans or project requirements. Ensure that such issues are documented, brought to the attention of the appropriate decision-maker in a timely manner, and followed up until a decision or corrective action is agreed.
- **Operational and Implementation Support**
    - Provide practical support to the PMU and technical teams in translating approved workplans into concrete implementation steps and timelines.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics and programme teams to follow the status of procurement processes required for planned activities and flag potential delays.
    - Support preparation and updating of procurement planning information required for Annual Work Plans and implementation reviews, while respecting the responsibilities of dedicated Finance and Procurement staff.
    - Support preparation of ToRs, scopes of work and other documentation for consultants, service providers and technical assignments.
- **Procurement Planning and Technical Procurement Support**
    - Support the preparation of procurement documentation required for project implementation, particularly for consultant recruitments, technical service contracts, studies, assessments and other specialized assignments.
    - Coordinate the provision of technical inputs required for procurement processes and ensure that Terms of Reference (ToRs), scopes of work, technical specifications and expected deliverables are prepared in a timely and high-quality manner.
    - Support programme and technical teams in the development and review of tender documentation and procurement packages in line with project requirements and PIN procedures.
    - Follow up with responsible colleagues to ensure that procurement processes are initiated sufficiently in advance and remain aligned with implementation timelines and workplans.
    - Participate in the technical evaluation of bids, proposals and consultant applications where relevant and support the documentation of evaluation processes.
    - Coordinate with Procurement/Logistics colleagues to monitor the status of key procurements and help address bottlenecks that may affect project implementation.
    - Ensure that procurement-related documentation and decisions are properly documented and accessible for project management, reporting and audit purposes.
- **Knowledge Management, Communication and Learning**
    - Support systematic documentation of project results, lessons learned, good practices and implementation experiences.
    - Contribute to preparation of project presentations, briefs, case studies and other knowledge products.
    - Support exchange of relevant information and learning with the PARS Global Coordination Project and other PARS country projects.

## **Main requirements:**

- At least **5 years of relevant professional experience** in project/programme management, reporting, programme quality, MEAL or a related area; experience with large institutional donor-funded projects is strongly preferred.
- Strong command of **English and Portuguese**, both written and spoken
- Demonstrated experience in donor reporting and preparation of high-quality narrative reports.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, work planning, monitoring and risk management.
- Experience coordinating inputs from programme, MEAL, finance, procurement and other functions is an advantage.
- Experience with UN agencies, GEF-funded programmes or other complex institutional donors would be a strong advantage.
- Experience in climate adaptation, private-sector/MSME development, green entrepreneurship or related programming is desirable but not essential.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deadlines and streams of information simultaneously.
- Excellent analytical, drafting and editing skills.
- Advanced user of MS Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Willingness to travel within Angola as required.

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization;
- *Salary & Benefits*: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3300 EUR super gross (based on experience).
- Additional allowances include:
    - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR;
    - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance;
    - *Time off and Rest:*
    - 25 days of holiday annually;
    - 10 sick days
- *Travel benefits:*
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
    - *Health and Well-being:*
    - 24/7 Medical Support available online;
    - Free psychological consultations available online;
    - *Professional Development:* Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities

title: COORDINATEUR.ICE PAIE ET ADMINISTRATION DU PERSONNEL TERRAIN (HOMERE)
body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Responsable de Service RH Régionales, votre rôle sera d'apporter un support aux RH des 21 pays d'intervention afin d'assurer le bon déroulement du processus de paie (logiciel Homère) et aux révisions de la rémunération, ainsi qu'un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationales.  
Plus précisément, vos missions seront les suivantes :  
Appuyer au déploiement et à la révision des processus de paie et rémunération en collaboration avec l'équipe RH Régionales et les Coordinateurs ou Coordinatrices Fonctionnelles SIRHAccompagner les Responsables RH dans la formalisation de leurs demandes de paramétrages du SIRH  
Appuyer les RH des Bureaux Pays à la formalisation de leur processus de paie et à son suivi  
Participer à l'appui technique sur aux outils d'administration à destination des utilisateurs dans les pays d'intervention en lien avec l'équipe SIRH  
Apporter un support au pilotage et au suivi des Ressources Humaines nationalesAppuyer à la création et la mise à jour des cadrages d'administration du personnel national et à leur dissémination  
Appuyer à la mise à jour des outils d'administration du personnel  
Appuyer le suivi des audits siège  
Assurer le contrôle interne sur la paie, la gestion administrative du personnel et la mise en oeuvre des politiques de rémunération  
Appuyer à la définition des indicateurs RH

  

Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme supérieur en Ressources Humaines (RH) et/ou en paie, vous une avez une solide expérience RH au sein d'une ONG international (siège ou terrain).  
Autonome et force de proposition, vous avez une bonne connaissance de la réglementation de la paie, des charges sociales et des méthodes de calcul des cotisations sociales et fiscales. Vous avez une appétence pour les chiffres, les fonctions avancées d'Excel et vous pouvez vous appuyer sur vos connaissances en paramétrage de paie.  
Vous êtes reconnu.e pour vos capacités à identifier, analyser les problématiques RH et formuler à vos interlocuteur·rice·s des recommandations, des alertes et/ou trouver des solutions.  
Doté·e d'un excellent relationnel, vous êtes capable de vous adapter aux problématiques nationales et internationales du secteur humanitaire. Vous êtes également capable d'animer une séquence de formation.  
Une expérience dans l'utilisation du logiciel Homère et une connaissance du logiciel NIBELIS (logiciel de paie) sont de vrais atouts.  
Vous maîtrisez le français et l'anglais à l'oral comme à l'écrit.  
Une expérience ACF est un atout.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
Statut:Cadre Intégré - CDD de 4 mois - Temps plein  
Lieu: Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)  
Rémunération :De 46K à 55Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience  
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT  
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF  
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail  
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up):  
Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros
